After all, Xie Yuanjing was who he was. And she had agreed to be his wife, wearing the name of the household's head mistress. If her conduct was careless or left her open to manipulation, it would reflect on both families.

Given his nature, he would likely not allow that kind of risk.

But she didn't want to give it up.

She didn't want to give up this place—or the girls who trusted the woman behind the operation. And she didn't want to give up what she loved.

So then. She would just have to try harder.

On the way back, Lu Huaixi sat curled in the carriage, head drooping.

Today had been genuinely exhausting.

Back at the courtyard, Yaoshu had prepared the evening meal and was waiting for her.

Lu Huaixi was still turning over how to bring up the subject with Xie Yuanjing when she heard footsteps outside—someone coming, it seemed, to deliver something.

Not long afterward, Yaoshu came in carrying two small books.

"What are these?"

"Miss, these look like... calligraphy copybooks."

"?"

Lu Huaixi's resistance was immediate. She frowned, already unhappy.

Then her gaze landed on the corner of the top book, and she pulled out the slip of paper tucked inside.

Bold, forceful characters leaped off the page—handwriting beautiful as the person who had written it, sharp and impossible to look away from.

"The writing is interesting. Practice the copybook or not as you please—consider it a reminder to write that piece for me."

Two books sent at once, and he called it "practice or not as you please." Clearly he thought her writing was awful.

Lu Huaixi pushed the slip back in and pretended she hadn't seen it.

chapters.title: Their Young Master Doesn't Care About the Marriage
chapters.content:
The days grew hot quickly as early summer arrived. After that day, Lu Huaixi spent another ten or so days looking through portrait scrolls—and decided she didn't want to leave the house.

It wasn't until Xie Yuanjing's mother sent an invitation—a flower-viewing gathering, under which guise she had invited the wives of both the first and second branches of the Lu family—that Lu Huaixi set foot outside again.

She still wanted to talk to Xie Yuanjing about matters after the wedding, but since their one chance meeting at the academy, the two of them had had no contact whatsoever.

This wedding was really happening.

Lu Huaixi stepped up into the carriage, saw that her mother was still a little displeased, and didn't dare pour more oil on the fire. She obediently sat down beside her.

"Today, Tangshu is coming along too. Since neither family has made this public yet, if you happen to see Xie Yuanjing at the marquis' household today, mind your manner."

Lu Tangshu was the legitimate daughter of the second branch, only a few months younger than Lu Huaixi.

The two of them weren't enemies—as children they had even shared a bed—but after the first branch gradually took on more of the Lu family's affairs, this younger cousin had grown increasingly distant.

Hearing her mother's words, Lu Huaixi almost said out loud, "Don't worry, I won't even see him"—but stopped herself, not wanting to give her mother unnecessary things to think about.

She pressed it down, and in the end just gave a nod.

"I understand, Mother."

The Chengen Marquis' household was an imperial-granted residence, a gift from the late emperor. Although the household had fallen somewhat out of favor, its foundation remained solid.

As Lady Liu and her daughter stepped down from the carriage, several elegantly dressed women were just being ushered inside the gates.

Xie Yuanjing's mother had been chatting with someone nearby, but the moment she spotted the Lu family's carriage, she ended the conversation and came over.

They were now, in a sense, family-in-law. Protocol required she not receive them coldly.

Lu Tangshu kept step with Lu Huaixi. This usually composed girl seemed, today, to have taken on a surprising liveliness.

Then again, it wasn't just today. It had been more or less since Lu Huaixi was forced to begin searching for a match—around that time, the second branch's legitimate daughter had started drawing closer to her again.

"The marquis' household is enormous."

Lu Tangshu looked around as they walked, and couldn't help murmuring in admiration. "People always say our Lu family's estate has a fine position—but I don't think it holds a candle to half of this."

Lu Huaixi didn't reply, though her gaze did pause for a moment.

"And I wonder why Lady Xie suddenly sent us an invitation. The day before yesterday, a friend of mine found out I was going with Mother to the marquis' household—and she came asking about their eldest young lord. I just don't know if we'll manage to see him today."

The reason Xie Yuanjing's name spread so widely—aside from his name and his methods—was naturally also because of that face.

If it were anyone else who had displeased the Emperor, people would have retreated long ago and avoided any connection. Yet this eldest young lord of the Xie family remained to this day someone many people asked after.

Lu Huaixi still didn't respond. She, more than anyone, had wanted to know whether she'd see Xie Yuanjing today—yet by his disposition and the current circumstances, she suspected she wouldn't.

A flower-viewing gathering, after all. He couldn't even be bothered about his own wedding. Why would he turn up for a gathering?

Lu Huaixi came back to herself. Less disappointment than worry.

Up ahead, Lady Xie led the Lu family women into the main hall. Though she hadn't made an announcement, there was a quietly perceptible attention she was paying to Lady Liu—and to the gentle, smiling girl following close behind.

More than a few of the assembled wives and matrons noticed, and their curiosity was stirred.

But no sooner had someone tried to approach than Lady Xie smoothly redirected their attention with a joke:

"No scaring the young ladies at my flower-viewing gathering."

She laughed as she spoke. "If you want to ask questions, do it on the quiet—or next time, how will I get them to come at all?"

With one remark, she had complimented every young woman in the hall, kept Lu Huaixi from becoming too conspicuous, and managed not to place her too high.

But Lu Huaixi was simply too lovely. Just sitting there, she drew eyes.

"The flowers outside are all in fine bloom. Those of you who can't sit still are welcome to wander the gardens."

The tea had only just been served when the soft strains of music began, and Lady Xie smiled as she spoke along to the gentle melody.

Lu Tangshu naturally wasn't going to step out at a moment like this. But Lu Huaixi couldn't stay a moment longer than she had to.

As if anticipating that she would go to view the flowers, a maidservant had been waiting outside. Seeing Lu Huaixi, she stepped forward and called out to her.

Lu Huaixi paused, then understood—it must be an arrangement Lady Xie had made.

"Second Young Miss Lu need not feel constrained. Lady Xie has instructed this servant to make sure Young Miss is well attended to. Any area within the first branch's grounds, Young Miss may freely visit."

Lu Huaixi had no mood for leisurely strolling. She smiled and waved a hand. "There's no need to go to so much trouble—I'll just walk around here."

"This servant would not dare be negligent. Lady Xie mentioned that today's gathering, while appearing to be a flower viewing, is mainly intended to let Second Young Miss familiarize herself with the household. Once the time is right, Lady Xie plans to invite Young Miss for a private meeting."

Hearing that, Lu Huaixi paused again.

Her marriage to Xie Yuanjing was only a performance. Yet somehow it was beginning to feel as though she was genuinely coming to take her place as the household's mistress.

But the confusion didn't last long. This was the marquis' household, after all—fully committing to a performance was nothing unusual.

"I'd rather leave that for next time. Today I'll just look around here."

"Yes, this servant will accompany Young Miss."

The maidservant fell in behind her, quietly narrating the layout of the estate's courtyards.

"...Beyond the gardens in this section, there is also one adjacent to Young Master's residence—though this servant and the others cannot enter the Young Master's area. Second Young Miss may visit next time."

Hearing the maidservant mention Xie Yuanjing, Lu Huaixi couldn't help but think of Shun'an Lane again.

She paused in thought, then turned her head.

"Is your Young Master at home today?"

"In reply to Second Young Miss, the Young Master took on an assignment a few days ago and left the city. Yesterday there seems to have been another delay. This servant has not yet heard that the Young Master has returned."

Well. As expected.

Lu Huaixi blinked.

The Shun'an Lane matter would have to wait for another opportunity. For now, she only hoped that when she returned home, her mother wouldn't be too displeased.

She couldn't quite help herself.

"Does your Young Master know there's a flower-viewing gathering at the house today?"

"He does. When Lady Xie settled the date a few days back, she mentioned it to Young Master."

"I see."

Lu Huaixi gave a small nod to show she had heard, said nothing more.

Today's gathering had invited several guests—but its main purpose was for the two families' matrons to have a quiet conversation without drawing attention.

Xie Yuanjing knew. But he had no intention of making an appearance.

Though Lu Huaixi had long expected it, she imagined her mother must still be hoping to meet him. Especially since today was the first visit to the marquis' household—even if his absence was due to an assignment, her mother would likely come away with a small, lingering dissatisfaction.

"Let's rest here for a while."

Lu Huaixi looked at what lay ahead, not wanting to continue the conversation.

This path had wound out of the garden. There was no one to be seen.

A few steps ahead, where the water curved, a covered pavilion looked out over a pond. Sitting there, you could just make out fish drifting by below—perfect for idle rest.

"Second Young Miss..."

Watching the Lu family's young miss say nothing for a while, lashes low over downcast eyes, lips lightly pressed as if lost in thought, the maidservant assumed she was unhappy about the Young Master not having returned.

Not daring to feel sorry for admiring the beauty, she began to feel uneasy inside.

Their Young Master really didn't care about the marriage.

Or rather—not just the marriage.

"Second Young Miss, please don't be upset. I'm sure Young Master is being held up by important matters..."

"Upset?"

Lu Huaixi looked over, half-amused and a little helpless. "Why would I be upset?"

Not seeing Xie Yuanjing today wasn't something that weighed on her. They were performing a role, after all. Lu Huaixi was clear-eyed about it.

She was only worried that her mother couldn't express her frustration at Xie Yuanjing and would redirect it at her instead.

Her mother's view—even in a pretense, both parties should carry respect for the arrangement.

"I'd like to feed the fish. Is that all right?"

Changing the subject, Lu Huaixi pointed toward the water's surface.

The maidservant gave an immediate nod.

"Of course—please sit a while, Young Miss, and this servant will go and fetch what you need."

Seeing the girl before her smile openly—brow curved, not the slightest hint of strain—the maidservant couldn't help but be briefly transfixed. Then she exhaled in relief.

Too lovely.

A young miss this lovely, and he didn't take notice. Truly didn't understand what their Young Master was thinking.

With that thought, the maidservant was about to withdraw—when she spotted someone approaching from ahead.

She recognized the person immediately, and a greeting nearly didn't make it out in time. She barely managed to swallow her shock before the figure was almost upon her. Head lowered, knees bent in a bow.

"This servant greets Young Master."

chapters.title: I Will Not Be Away
chapters.content:
Hearing the words "Young Master," Lu Huaixi didn't register them at first—she even began wondering just how many "young masters" there were in this household.

Only when Xie Yuanjing responded did she turn her head and stare.

"You were in the household after all."

"Surprised?"

"Yes."

Lu Huaixi nodded, and quickly at that.

Genuinely surprised—because in her mind, running into this man today had been the last thing she expected.

"You weren't here when you arrived."

There seemed to be a faint smile in Xie Yuanjing's expression, prompted by her blank-faced staring, and his tone shifted—oddly gentle. "Just got back."

That trace of a smile vanished almost instantly, so quickly that the maidservant preparing to withdraw had no time to be surprised before it was already gone.

"You wanted to feed the fish?"

"Yes. I wanted to sit here a while. I don't have to feed them if there's nothing to use."

"Then you shall feed them."

Seeing him step closer, Lu Huaixi was still a little at a loss.

The sudden appearance had slowed her thoughts, and the gaze she sent his way didn't seem to have any plans to leave—as if she were a little pleased, and a little incredulous.

Xie Yuanjing rarely encountered this kind of expression.

The people he had dealt with were all calculating and sharp. Someone like Lu Huaixi—standing in the full path of the wind, letting it carry the water-mist straight into her face and not caring—there was perhaps only one of her.

And even that heedless quality couldn't conceal how good she looked.

Standing in the full current of wind and spring light—her trailing skirt hem picking up a warmth like a painted scene—the girl inside the painting made all the flowers jealous.

"A few days ago there was an assignment. I wasn't in the capital."

"I know. I just asked one of the maidservants in your household."

"Mm. Looking for me?"

Lu Huaixi had almost nodded, but caught herself—bluntly saying yes to that felt odd somehow.

"There is something I wanted to speak to you about. I thought I wouldn't be able to see you today."

"You'll see me."

Xie Yuanjing stopped a short distance away and glanced at the freshly poured tea on the table before him. "Your Lady Mother and you—this is your first visit to the household. I shouldn't be absent."

"?"

Quiet fell around them. Lu Huaixi froze again, unable to find a reply.

So Xie Yuanjing was really this considerate?

Before she could dwell on it, Xie Yuanjing continued: "You had something to discuss?"

A cup of tea had just been poured—still giving off wisps of heat.

Not quite scalding, but Xie Yuanjing still knitted his brow, not inclined to reach for it.

Lu Huaixi noticed his reaction, and the tension from moments ago scattered. Something about it struck her as oddly funny.

Didn't like hot tea?

Rather different from the "old fox" her brother had in his head.

"There is something—"

Collecting herself, Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together and said: "The things you said before—about being able to come and go from the house freely afterward—does that still stand?"

"To wander around?"

Lu Huaixi considered, then shook her head. "Not entirely."

Some things couldn't be hidden. Even if she forced herself to hide them, now that she was connected to Xie Yuanjing, they would only become vulnerabilities later.

Lu Huaixi might not be one for studying or deep thinking—but she wasn't stupid.

"I bought a place a while ago and kept some people there."

"What kind of people?"

"Dancers."

The maidservant had arrived with the fish food by the time Xie Yuanjing still hadn't replied.

Lu Huaixi shifted from initial nerves to something more like—well, whatever, it is what it is—and relaxed.

The secret was out. Though she hadn't mentioned that she herself loved to dance, or that she had choreographed pieces for others—Xie Yuanjing was not dim. He would likely piece together her few and private joys from what she'd said.

Whatever came of it, she was keeping Shun'an Lane. She was keeping those dancers.

Having sorted out her mind, Lu Huaixi let her gaze drift to the surface of the lake.

"I just saw a golden fish—it looked enormous."

"There is one."

Xie Yuanjing didn't remain silent—he followed her lead and gave a nod. "A gift from the palace some time ago. Been raised a few years now."

"May I feed it?"

"You may. Though that fish is old—it doesn't come out much. Catching a glimpse of it is already rare. You'll likely not be able to feed it."

Watching Lu Huaixi's eyes widen, gaze fixed on the water with eager anticipation, Xie Yuanjing felt some of his tiredness ease.

He looked over alongside her. The place he had looked at a hundred times and found tedious—suddenly held a little more of interest.

Not wanting to dampen her eagerness, he still said plainly:

"That fish rarely surfaces. Even the servants who tend it here barely see it once. You're welcome to look at the others."

"Is that so? Still—I want to feed it. It's fine, it will come."

Hearing the certainty in her voice—the ringing confidence of a child making a bet—Xie Yuanjing turned his head and looked at her.

This girl had a mind that didn't like to dwell on things, yet she had just openly told him she kept a household of dancers somewhere.

Listening to music, watching dancing. All above board—no other dealings.

Genuinely startling, in a way. Difficult to know how to respond.

His thoughts wandered. Lu Huaixi grabbed a handful of fish food and scattered it across the water—her lashes blinking as she watched, lips moving in quiet murmurs.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze had just begun to drift from her eyes lower when she spun toward him, eyes bright, meeting his head-on.

"Look! There it is! It came out!"

Same fish food. Same spot.

But this time, the big golden fish flipped its tail and surfaced—rising exactly where it could be most clearly seen.

A rare glimmer passed through Xie Yuanjing's dark eyes. He didn't speak for a long moment.

When he finally did, it came with a quiet, helpless laugh and a small shake of his head.

"What I said before still stands."

"What?"

"You can come and go from the house as you please."

Xie Yuanjing watched that golden, glittering fish—which had suddenly grown lively again. "But each time you go to that place, you tell me first."

The fish food was quickly scattered across the surface.

The stillness of the lake was broken. The beautiful golden body carved a smooth arc through the water, and the droplets it kicked up caught the light like bright glass beads—scattering into small, prismatic rings.

Lu Huaixi watched, satisfied in the watching and satisfied in the feeding.

"All right. But if you're not in the household?"

"My guard will be."

Lu Huaixi gave a nod. She hadn't expected Xie Yuanjing to agree so easily, or for him to be this easy to talk to—as though the whole thing didn't concern him at all.

She had fretted over it for nothing.

Spent days worrying for no reason.

"I should go back to the front."

"Wait a moment."

Xie Yuanjing stopped her. "There is also something I want to raise—about the year after the wedding."

Up in the front hall, a maidservant who heard the footsteps startled with delight.

Lady Xie's eyes flashed with surprise she kept carefully concealed—she glanced once, without moving, toward the well-behaved Lu Huaixi sitting quietly nearby, and then, composed as ever, turned to the maidservant with a warm smile.

"How unusual. He's been so occupied lately, I could barely catch a glimpse of him—I thought he'd forgotten about the gathering today."

Lu Huaixi lowered her head over her tea without a trace of expression, giving nothing away.

Anyone watching would never have guessed she had already met Xie Yuanjing once—and spoken to him at some length.

Not long after, Lu Huaixi heard a soft exclamation from Lu Tangshu beside her, followed by a ripple of quiet voices.

She set down her teacup and looked up—only then did she see that Xie Yuanjing had come over to this side.

He didn't enter—perhaps mindful of the young women inside. He remained in the courtyard, simply having something delivered through a servant to the attendant nearby.

Before leaving, his gaze lingered for a moment on some point—but it lasted no longer than an instant before he pulled it away.

Then a maidservant came back inside, and behind her was a stand bearing a brilliant coral ornament.

"To have a son this thoughtful of his mother—Lady Xie really does make the rest of us envious."

"Don't be envious—who else has a son they can barely get a glimpse of once in ten days? Even when I want some motherly warmth and filial conversation, there's no one to be found."

Lady Xie dabbed the corner of her mouth with a handkerchief. Her words were complaints, but the joy in her eyes was plain to see.

The woman who had spoken knew she had hit the mark, and laughed with all the more warmth.

"Easy to fix—have your Young Master marry soon. Then Lady Xie will have someone to talk to morning to night, and once grandchildren come, the household will be even livelier. You won't be able to keep quiet if you tried!"

Lady Xie didn't take up the thread about "marrying," but her gaze drifted once more to Lu Huaixi—and she smiled with a nod.

The matrons seated nearby were waiting for that line about marriage to be picked up. A few of lower standing even hoped to use the moment to suggest their own daughters.

But the woman at the head of the table said nothing—only lifted her teacup and smoothly changed the subject.

Off to one side, Lu Tangshu had also been waiting.

She had been convinced all along that today's gathering was, essentially, a viewing occasion for Xie Yuanjing—so she had deliberately stayed put the whole time, hoping Lady Xie might take note of her, and hoping she might perhaps manage a glimpse of Xie Yuanjing.

And she had glimpsed him. A man of extraordinary presence—like jade and pine on a high mountain, unmatched in looks, cool and untamed.

Lu Tangshu couldn't help the lurch in her chest.

The way to position oneself well wasn't limited to family backing. Being pursued by a formidable man—even if nothing came of it—could still raise one's own standing.

chapters.title: Quite the Expert at Winning People Over
chapters.content:
Lady Liu caught sight of Xie Yuanjing outside a side room toward the end of the gathering.

The man who was not often warm toward others was waiting under the covered walkway—long robes, jade-pinned topknot, a cool arrogance in the set of his brow. Strikingly refined and handsome.

Lady Liu startled.

She glanced back at her daughter, saw the girl had gone momentarily still, and assumed she was just dazzled by Xie Yuanjing's looks.

Not having the heart to scold her, she simply gestured for Xixi to go back to the carriage first.

The second branch hadn't come out yet. Lu Huaixi glanced their way, then stepped up onto the mounting block.

The carriage inside was spacious, but the moment she lifted the curtain, a large object caught her eye.

A brilliant red coral.

"What is this?"

"In reply to Second Young Miss—this was sent over by the eldest young lord of the marquis' household, via a page boy. He said it was to bring some auspicious cheer to the Lady and Young Miss alike."

Coral had long been considered a symbol of good fortune. The larger pieces were especially rare and costly—which was precisely why when Xie Yuanjing had presented a fine coral to his mother at the flower-viewing gathering, every matron in attendance had praised and envied it.

And the piece before her now was clearly no lesser—a pair measured to the same standard.

Lu Huaixi said nothing more. She only stared at the coral in front of her, and slowly, slowly pressed her lips together.

She was taking back what she'd thought back there in the water pavilion.

An old fox was an old fox. Winning people over—he was quite the expert.

As expected, when Lady Liu returned and saw it, she was momentarily taken aback, barely managing to hold her composure. Once told Xie Yuanjing had selected it personally, she gave a satisfied nod.

"One really can't trust rumors."

Lu Huaixi knew exactly what that meant.

Rumors said Xie Yuanjing was difficult, his temperament unpredictable, his methods numerous and ruthless. That when he smiled at someone, it wasn't necessarily goodwill—there was even a chance he was about to wring their neck.

Lu Huaixi shifted to look at her mother, and moved her lips.

A moment passed, as if a thought had surfaced. She said quietly, "Not entirely to be trusted."

Seeing her mother glance over, Lu Huaixi pointed to herself: "Mother was saying the same thing before—that the rumors were right."

The second branch arrived home half an hour after Lu Huaixi.

Lu Tangshu followed her mother into her courtyard. Once the maidservants had withdrawn, she frowned and spoke.

"We stayed the extra time and still couldn't get a single word out of Lady Xie."

"And what word were you hoping for?"

Lady Lu of the second branch, née Luó, let her expression slip a fraction. With no outsiders present, she no longer watched her tongue.

"The Chengen Marquis' household hasn't been what it was. Right now all they have left is a bit of surface dignity. Once your standing is higher, that eldest son of theirs—he may not deserve you anymore!"

"Then why were you so warm to Lady Xie today, Mother?"

Lu Tangshu said flatly, without patience. Xie Yuanjing's image from the gathering kept reappearing in her mind.

"And besides—never mind how far the marquis' household has fallen. Where could it fall to? Let's not forget the Xie family has produced two empresses. And even now, even with the Marquis out of the Emperor's favor, Xie Yuanjing has never been stripped of any of his authority."

"Two empresses—what use are they now?"

Lady Luo had no interest in quarreling over that.

"If you truly like the Xie eldest son, wait two more years. Once Lu Huaixi's situation is resolved, let her elevate your standing a little. If the marquis' household rises, you'll be marrying into glory. If it doesn't rise—you can still make another choice."

Lu Tangshu didn't argue back.

She did have some feeling for Xie Yuanjing—but she also saw things clearly. Compared to marrying into a household that might never recover, having Xie Yuanjing drawn to her—even if nothing came of it—might serve her better.

But she didn't feel like thinking it through now.

There was something else that bothered her more.

"I still don't understand—why are you so set on getting Lu Huaixi into the palace? If she actually becomes a consort, I'd have to bow my head to her for the rest of my life. Why should she have that?"

"Why should she? Because the Lu family gains influence through it, and your standing gets lifted because of her."

"Grandfather always plays favorites—any influence the Lu family gains goes to First Uncle's branch. How much would actually reach us? And Lu Huaixi—she can't compose poems, can't paint, can't do any of it. Favored by the Emperor? Just because of her face?"

"I keep telling you that head of yours doesn't think—all these years and you've only learned the pretty surface of things."

Lady Luo shot a look at her daughter, pressing down her impatience.

"That face of hers is more than enough! The moment she earns favor, the Emperor's benevolence will extend to the Lu family—even a small gesture from the palace is imperial grace. People everywhere will come seeking to ingratiate themselves. Then you tell me who controls what inside the Lu family—it doesn't matter."

"And if she doesn't earn favor—if she dies in the palace?"

The word "dies" came out of Lu Tangshu's mouth with an odd savoring quality, a crease between her brows that somehow also held a strange anticipation.

"If she doesn't earn favor—"

Lady Luo smiled at her daughter.

"With the Lu family's backing, she'll earn favor. Dying is possible—but if she's killed by someone, then whoever is on the throne owes a debt, and the Lu family will still receive recompense. They still get elevated. Whatever the outcome, you come out ahead. Understand?"

Lu Tangshu understood.

Not only did she understand that Lu Huaixi simply had to enter the palace, she also understood that the moment Lu Huaixi became someone belonging to the Emperor—the Lu family would have only one legitimate daughter left.

And that would be her.

Any other Lu daughter would come below her in standing.

Anyone who wanted to attach themselves to the Lu family—even those seeking to flatter the first branch—would still have to consider her.

"Then... Mother, is it certain that Lu Huaixi will definitely enter the palace?"

"It is. Who else—who would dare make a match with her once the news is out? And another thing—why did you have that He family boy's portrait sent over? He's already engaged. If that caused a scene and your grandfather found out, there'd be trouble!"

"It was He Jianxing who asked me to do it."

Lu Tangshu pursed her lips. "I just wanted to give Lu Huaixi some grief. I won't do it again."

Afterward, she'd only be hoping for Lu Huaixi to enter the palace. And if she was lucky—

The thought surfaced, complicated with it, an unacknowledged darkness growing in her heart.

Though it troubled her, she had truly been thinking it: that Lu Huaixi might be killed by someone inside the palace.

"Killed? She won't be. With the Lu family there, she can't not earn favor."

Lady Luo rose, cutting off that line of thought, with no wish to dwell on it.

"She's still family. Use your head and keep up a close rapport with her. There's plenty of benefit ahead."

"I know, your daughter isn't foolish."

chapters.title: Who Would Marry You at a Time Like This?
chapters.content:
At the Chengen Marquis' household, Xie Yuanjing had been kept behind by his mother.

The hall held that eye-catching coral—brilliant red and festive.

"How did you end up coming back today? Wasn't the assignment complicated?"

His mother sipped her tea, watching her son summon someone to bring ice. She wanted to stop him—but in the end only let out a sigh.

"It really is past time to settle your marriage. At least then there'd be someone to look after you."

Xie Yuanjing gave a languid smile and reached to pour his own tea.

He filled it only halfway—leaving space.

"But you rushed into this engagement so suddenly, and you won't have a proper ceremony—I can't quite shake a feeling of unease. Tell me honestly: was this truly your own idea?"

On the day the arrangement with the Lu family was finalized, Xie Yuanjing hadn't even returned to the estate.

Lady Xie, unable to find him, had only heard the confirmed news from the Old Master himself.

She'd had no chance to say a word about the timing being too rushed before the Old Master instructed that the matter not be made public.

Even the wedding was to be handled discreetly. Lady Xie could not feel this was a happy event.

"The Lu second daughter has a lovely face—gentle and sweet, like a celestial being when she sits there. But—"

Lady Xie paused and chose her words carefully. "But she is truly quite young. A hasty marriage is not good for her."

"She is young—rushing into a wedding doesn't suit her. That's why the date on the betrothal contract was moved forward by a year. And after the wedding, I won't rush her into having children early. So Mother, please don't press on that."

Shortly, a maidservant brought in chipped ice. Xie Yuanjing took it and began nudging pieces slowly into his teacup.

"Mother, going forward, please don't lend your ear to rumors outside. She is marrying in—she will be family. There's no sense in repeating outsiders' gossip about one's own people."

"I'm not talking ill of her—I'm..."

Lady Xie couldn't help knitting her brow. "I'm only saying this to you. To outsiders—do you think I'd say anything so careless?"

"Mother should bear with it—don't say it to me either."

"You really are..."

Lady Xie's words were blocked back in her throat. She collected herself before saying, helplessly:

"Fine, fine. I won't say anything. But if you're truly going to shield that Lu girl so fiercely, then take this marriage seriously. Anyone looking at this household and seeing no hint of celebration, and then suddenly a wife appears—they'll assume your wife has no favor at all."

Something shifted in Xie Yuanjing at last.

He took a sip of his newly cooled tea, and his brow faintly tightened, barely perceptible.

"And—the household knows you've gotten engaged, but not to whom. Your grandmother's intentions are plain enough to you. That one has been hoping for an opening for a long time—I imagine she's looking to use it to have you take that girl in as well—"

"Looking for an opening?"

Xie Yuanjing cut his mother off directly. "She might as well save herself the trouble and die. It would be faster."

"Don't upset your grandmother—if you actually make a move, and your grandmother takes ill over it, the whole wedding with the Lu family might fall through."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. The hall chilled in an instant, a heaviness pressing through the air.

Lady Xie was about to urge him to endure it through this period when she heard the person before her say with deliberate calm: "Let her try. Let her see how much reach the marquis' household has left—to come between me and my wedding."

Lady Xie's heart lurched. She wasn't quite certain whether her son's "her" meant the Old Madam—or the female cousin residing in the household.

"I only meant for you to keep an eye on things. Was there any need to—"

"My Lady, the Third Madam has come with the young miss."

The maidservant's voice cut in from outside. "They say they've come to drink tea with you, and to take a look at the new coral you've received."

Hearing the words "young miss," Lady Xie instinctively looked at her son.

They must have gotten word that he was here, and couldn't restrain themselves any longer—using any excuse to come and show themselves to the first branch.

She had no desire to upset the Old Madam, but her son's wishes mattered more. And that young miss was no simple creature, either—Lady Xie didn't particularly like her.

"Not today—I'm feeling a little tired. Another time, I'll invite Second Sister-in-law and Third Sister-in-law for a proper visit."

The words made no mention of the young miss. The maidservant nodded and was about to withdraw.

But then, the man who hadn't looked up called the maidservant back.

"The first branch's courtyard is not open to outsiders without cause. If Third Aunt wishes to come for tea, she comes alone."

The words left no face unsaved. But Lady Xie understood he couldn't be blamed—there had been incidents before, caused by someone with unusually thick skin.

After lingering a little longer—drinking some of the freshly cooled tea—Xie Yuanjing rose and left.

Outside the courtyard, a few servants were passing by. Catching sight of him, they immediately lowered their eyes and stepped aside, not daring to move without permission.

Walking behind him was his trusted man, Gong Fei.

Having just overheard Lady Xie's words of reproach, he found it hard to hold back something he wanted to say.

"Master, why not tell Lady Xie plainly that this marriage is nothing more than—"

"No need."

Xie Yuanjing saw nothing problematic in any of it himself.

A cooperative arrangement—each getting what they needed.

After the wedding, he would give Lu Huaixi every dignity befitting the household's head mistress. He would look after her as one of his own. After the dissolution in one year, he would not turn cold or disavow her.

But none of that needed to be known by his mother.

If she were to learn that this marriage was a pretense from start to finish, her instinct would be to treat the girl with a careful, distancing politeness. And then Lu Huaixi's days in the household would not be easy.

"This matter is not to be mentioned again. When she comes, she is likewise the master of this house."

chapters.title: She Is Really Getting Married
chapters.content:
Days moved quickly. Half a month later, the Lu household suddenly became busy.

There was no grand ceremony—but it was clearly visible that the first branch was preparing for something joyful.

Lu Tangshu endured it for a few days before she simply couldn't anymore, and found a pretext to come over.

"Second Sister, let's take the midday meal together today."

She timed her visit carefully—only to find Lu Huaixi about to leave the courtyard. "Second Sister, are you heading out?"

"Mm. I made plans with Sister Xianya—going to pick up a few things."

"Shopping? Then could Second Sister take me along?"

Lu Tangshu was nervous inside, but nothing showed on her face. She only smiled and drew close. "I've barely been outside the estate in ages—Second Sister would be doing me a favor, and besides, it stops all those idle rumors from spreading."

Lu Huaixi also curved her eyes into a smile—but it was a different kind of smile.

"What idle rumors? I haven't heard any."

"Oh—just some nonsense going around. People are even saying Second Sister is about to be married—that the Lu family is celebrating quietly."

Lu Tangshu probed carefully, her eyes fixed on the person before her, unblinking.

She didn't believe Lu Huaixi could possibly be getting married—after all, she had still been looking through portrait scrolls not long ago—but the first branch had clearly been bringing in festive items. Without a straight answer, she couldn't rest easy.

And not only was there movement in the Lu household. A few days earlier, she had heard that the Chengen Marquis' household was also preparing for a wedding.

She had yet to find out whom Xie Yuanjing was marrying. And now that she was seeing the decorations being put up here, she had no choice but to press for information about the first branch first.

"See what Second Sister makes people laugh about—"

"Actually, they weren't wrong."

Lu Huaixi broke in quietly, her tone soft—carrying an air of slight embarrassment, and yet a quiet hopefulness too.

Lu Tangshu went blank. For a moment she couldn't control her expression.

"Impossible. Who would marry you at a time like this?"

"Why wouldn't they?"

Lu Huaixi's eyes went wide—clear and uncomplicated, settling on the other girl's face—as if startled by her raised voice. "We've been engaged for a long time—since a year ago."

"What?"

Lu Tangshu fought to keep her expression in check. "How could you possibly be engaged to someone? You're supposed to be entering the palace—how can you get married now?"

"What do you mean, entering the palace? I don't understand what Third Sister is saying."

Lu Huaixi played confused—blinked at her—as though startled by the sharpness of her voice and pressing down the urge to look hurt.

"I have a betrothal contract to prove it. Why would I lie to you? And as for what you just said—why would I be entering the palace?"

"You—"

Seeing her expression completely serious and nothing like pretense, Lu Tangshu felt her heart plummet.

In her eyes, Lu Huaixi was a pretty but hollow fool. Rather than let her be deceived by someone into a bad marriage, she was better off in the palace—useful to everyone and a vehicle to lift her own standing.

Not to mention that a woman should provide for her family, and she would be well positioned to help the Lu family. Even if her days weren't easy, that was all the more reason to go.

But Lu Huaixi was claiming a betrothal—and about to be married?

Impossible. Lu Tangshu didn't believe it.

If her mother hadn't done her research, she would never have put Lu Huaixi on that list.

Lu Huaixi must have found something out. That was the only explanation.

The thought sent a bolt of urgency through Lu Tangshu. She didn't even try to hide it anymore.

"No one in the capital has announced an engagement—Second Sister, why are you making things up? And not long ago you were still going through portrait scrolls. Who could you possibly be marrying?"

"When have I ever been going through portraits? Or comparing them? Third Sister—where did you hear all this?"

"Stop pretending, Lu Huaixi—you found out about the palace, didn't you? You grabbed the first person you could find to cover it up?"

Lu Tangshu's grip on her sleeve tightened. The words came to her mouth, urgent, and then she reined herself back with effort—swallowing the wild look that had almost broken through.

"Second Sister, don't be angry. I'm saying this for your sake too. I know you may not want to enter the palace—but if you've gone and married someone at random just to dodge the selection, and the palace finds out, there'll be no one left to protect you. And it would bring trouble to the Lu family as well."

Lu Tangshu kept her voice reasonable:

"Even if you don't care about yourself, think about the family. And Second Sister, you're beautiful—you'll surely rise in the palace. Compared to marrying just anyone and being looked down on all your life, isn't it better to enter the palace and have something to show for it?"

Lu Huaixi had been silent throughout—eyes downcast.

Lu Tangshu grew more anxious at the sight of it.

But she also didn't really believe that in so short a time, Lu Huaixi could have found anyone—most likely some low-ranked scholar with no background, deceiving people into thinking she'd climbed high.

"Why would you say I'm supposed to enter the palace?"

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long time before she finally spoke.

The person before her was caught off guard by the question for a moment. "Naturally, because I heard it."

"What one hears doesn't hold."

"How can it not hold? Rumors don't come from nothing—since—"

"Whether it holds or not, I'm not going."

Lu Huaixi cut her off, and let the look of easy simplicity fall away. She met Lu Tangshu's eyes.

"I'm getting married. Until something is proved, Third Sister had best not bring it up again—lest my husband's family take offense."

"What husband's family—some penniless scholar with no backing, I suppose?"

Lu Tangshu held her gaze just as hard.

Lu Huaixi must have learned about all of it, and was keeping it from everyone until just before the wedding on purpose.

Yet Lu Huaixi—too uninformed about books, too little learned for her own good—was still doing something this selfish at her age, thinking only of herself.

Listed on the Flower and Bird Envoy register, and she dares to get married? She wants to drag the entire Lu family down with her!

"Second Sister, think this through carefully."

Lu Tangshu barely held down the fire, pulling a thin smile back onto her face. "Whoever this person is—once they hear about all of this, they'll likely not dare go through with it. If that ends up being humiliating—"

"He won't."

Lu Huaixi gave her a smile.

Today she had, for once, added a touch of cosmetics—and when she smiled at someone like that, a vivid brightness overtook her usual softness. A hint of feminine charm slipped through—the kind that momentarily stunned the eyes.

Not long after, Zhou Xianya's voice drifted in from outside, calling her name.

Lu Huaixi turned to the person in front of her with an expression of perfect innocence. "Are you still not leaving, Third Sister?"

Lu Tangshu's grip tightened in her sleeve. She watched her walk away so freely, clearly heading toward the man who had spoken up for her, and a knot of something complex and unwilling pressed against her chest.

"Lu Huaixi—are you really so selfish?"

"I don't know what you're talking about."

"Fine. Then I'll be watching. Watching to see whether this husband of yours really has the guts to come and marry you."

She turned sharply and went to find her mother.

"Young Miss..."

"Leave her."

She had been waiting a long time for the second branch to show their hand—and now they had. Lu Huaixi watched her go, without a word.

That same day, Lady Luo of the second branch went to the Old Madam.

Under the banner of concern for the Lu family, she wept and wailed until the Old Madam was convinced that Lu Huaixi would be the ruin of everything.

Lady Liu had long suspected the second branch of being behind it all—having it confirmed now only pressed a weight onto her chest. But she had no intention of tearing things open at this moment. She let Lady Luo carry on at the Old Madam's side, let them hold each other and weep.

Until the two of them began taking turns at Lu Huaixi—calling her useless and cold-blooded, one phrase after another—that Lady Liu finally snapped, and hurled a teacup at Lady Luo.

The Lu Old Master arrived shortly after, and only then did the whole thing begin to quiet.

But the Old Madam still wasn't satisfied with the marriage.

"Everyone else would leap at the chance to enter the palace—but not her. Only ever thinking of herself, not a single thought for the Lu family! And something as large as getting married, done so secretively—what kind of person did Lu Huaixi run off and marry? Does the Lu family still have any dignity?"

Lu Huaixi was out of the house and knew nothing of any of it.

When she returned, she spotted Xie Yuanjing outside the gates.

They hadn't seen each other in quite a few days. After all the time apart, with something new between them, there was an awkwardness in drawing close that she hadn't had to think about before.

The awkwardness, of course, was mostly Lu Huaixi's.

Xie Yuanjing was perfectly at ease—eyes cast downward, looking at the small girl who only came up to his chest.

"I heard about what happened today."

He said it plainly: "I'll have her placed on the list to take your spot."

"No need."

Lu Huaixi sniffed once. Met his gaze for a moment, then turned her head away.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze lingered on the upturned tip of her nose.

He didn't quite agree with Lu Huaixi being too soft on people—but this was still the Lu family's own affair.

"Still holding back?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi shook her head—no hesitation—and after a quiet moment, said softly: "I'll send the name myself. She said I only care about myself. So let her enter the palace and plan for the Lu family's future instead."

Xie Yuanjing raised a brow. This was not the first time this girl had surprised him—and though it was only a flicker, the feeling made him laugh.

Both families, now certain the marriage was secure, had each let it slip that there had been a prior engagement. But the specifics—who to—had not been tracked down by anyone.

Now the wedding was near, and the two of them shouldn't, strictly speaking, be meeting. But Lu Huaixi thought—this man didn't care about the marriage to begin with. He probably didn't care about these formalities either.

After Xie Yuanjing left, Lu Huaixi went back to her own courtyard.

She had spent the whole day running about. Right now she barely had the energy to speak.

She had just been thinking of lying down for a short nap when Yaoshu came in carrying a letter.

"Miss, someone sent gifts to the door."

"Who?"

"It's Miss Wenlian."

Yaoshu had not been with Lu Huaixi when she went out that day, but she had later sensed—vaguely—that her young miss and the Wenlian girl had parted ways.

She hadn't dared ask more, but today the woman had sent someone with gifts and a letter, and there was no way to avoid it.

Lu Huaixi said nothing. After a moment, she took the letter and read it.

The handwriting was neat and fine. The letter was not long—it said she had been having a difficult time in the Wu household lately, and had been ill, which was why she only heard now that Lu Huaixi was about to be wed.

It also said she had been consumed with regret since that day—had not understood why her heart had clouded over and made her act as she had, and that she had felt terrible.

And it said she was wrong—but she didn't want this friendship to end. She asked Lu Huaixi to give her one more chance to meet, just once.

Lu Huaixi read through it quickly. Then she rose and walked to the lamp nearby.

The room had been lit early; the flames burned bright as daylight.

"Have someone return the gifts. Tell her the well-wishes are received—but there's no need to stay in contact."

Lu Huaixi burned the letter. Said nothing more. Did not believe a word of it.

Once the news spread, the days moved even faster. In the blink of an eye, it was time—the day Lu Huaixi was to be married out of the Lu family.

In the lead-up to the wedding, the first branch had revealed no further details, so Lady Luo had not dared make any bold moves.

That morning, before dawn had even broken, the room was already full of movement.

Lu Huaixi sat before the bronze mirror. Her dark eyes held drowsiness and uncertainty—and also, arriving late, a dawning, unguarded bashfulness.

She was really getting married. Looking at the dazzling bridal garments before her, her heart gave one heavy thud after another.

chapters.title: Waiting to Watch Her Embarrass Herself at the Wedding
chapters.content:
Ever since Lu Tangshu had spoken her mind that day, the second branch had been bracing for the first branch to come down on them with questions and trouble.

But no one paid them the slightest attention. After that one scene at the Old Madam's side in the beginning, the household had been perfectly calm ever since.

Lady Luo had been stewing in silence—and it was only today, on the day of Lu Huaixi's wedding, that she finally accepted the truth: that man was really going through with it. He had no intention of calling it off.

Compared to Lady Luo, who was still swallowing her disappointment with forced composure, Lu Tangshu grew harder to contain with each passing day.

Especially after having nurtured that particular thought, after having made her plans around it—Lu Huaixi's sudden marriage felt like a cut across the path of her future, and she found herself deepening into resentment.

But she wasn't foolish enough to make a scene on a day like this.

"There will be plenty of people out there today. Mind yourself—if you hear anyone mocking Lu Huaixi, don't you dare pretend not to notice. When necessary, speak up for her."

"I understand, Mother."

She couldn't wait to see Lu Huaixi humiliated—but for now, what she needed most was a good reputation for herself.

"Don't be in such a hurry. Getting her into the palace may have fallen through, but she's married off just the same. All that talk about a prior engagement is nothing but a cover story—whoever the man is, he must have been some stopgap she grabbed at random. He can't possibly be anyone with real standing."

"Going forward she'll always be a step below you. When that day comes, you'll be the only legitimate daughter left in the Lu household. Once your reputation for defending your sisters gets out there, you'll have no shortage of suitors."

Lu Tangshu nodded.

Thinking of how young Lu Huaixi was, being forced to marry—and to some unremarkable scholar at that—a little of her bitter resentment eased.

There would be plenty of people to laugh at her in time. She would simply sit back and enjoy the show.

Still, a worry surfaced. "Mother—with Lu Huaixi suddenly getting married like this, could the matter of the list cause us any trouble?"

"Once this juncture passes, your father will find a way to have Lu Huaixi's name removed, but there will certainly be some fallout."

Lady Luo spoke in a low voice, expression unpleasant.

"Worst case, we put up more silver. I'll go say a few words to your grandmother later and get the first branch to chip in. And now that Lu Huaixi is married off, her share of the household allowance ought naturally to be passed to you."

Hearing that, Lu Tangshu finally relaxed.

The first branch had always been generous—especially toward Lu Huaixi. It was no wonder the girl had been raised so pampered and self-centered, unwilling to suffer even the smallest hardship.

"Never mind all that for now—go keep Lu Huaixi company first. Your other sisters are all there too. Don't let them steal the lead from you."

"Don't worry, Mother. I intend to be the first one to get a good look at my dear Second Sister's husband-to-be, and offer her my very warmest congratulations right to her face."

She was practically itching to watch Lu Huaixi embarrass herself at the wedding—to hear people gossip about this pampered darling of a girl, dragged down from her high perch.

"Do as you like—just don't let anyone see through you, and give people nothing to use against us."

—

The bridal dress was elaborate. By the time Lu Huaixi had everything on, fine beads of sweat had gathered at her temples.

The attending matron beside her was smiling so broadly she couldn't close her mouth. Though she had only been brought in to look after the bride for a few days, she had already grown genuinely fond of the girl before her.

"This wedding gown truly suits the young miss."

The matron praised lavishly, sighing with admiration.

Without true regard, no one would pour so much silver into a garment made in such a short time—and to make something this beautiful, no less.

Lu Huaixi couldn't help glancing down at her skirt.

A flush rose to her cheeks, lingering even after she heard someone come in from outside. Only then did she come back to herself, picking up the cold tea beside her for a sip.

"Second Sister."

"Second Sister, you look beautiful! What a shame our eldest sister has to wait a little longer to see you."

Her younger sisters came over laughing, with the quiet Lu Tangshu at the front.

Lu Huaixi glanced briefly across her face and pretended not to notice the barely concealed delight in her eyes.

"Has Elder Sister arrived?"

"She came early—but First Aunt called her over to help."

Lu Ningyou, the eldest daughter, was Lu Huaixi's elder sister, three years her senior. She had married last year and was now expecting a child toward the end of the year.

Having always been considerate of her sister's condition, Lu Huaixi had said little about her engagement to her.

"Why is she being put to work?"

"It's not real work—the whole family is looking out for her. It's just that several wives have arrived, and First Aunt couldn't get away, so she asked Elder Sister to go receive them."

Lu Huaixi heard this and smiled.

She had almost forgotten—of all the sisters, it was her eldest who had always been the best with gentle words.

A maidservant nearby, seeing Lu Huaixi in conversation, waited a moment before stepping forward to touch up her lip rouge.

The other girls all stepped back to give her room.

Only Lu Tangshu, thinking of something she couldn't name, smiled and moved closer.

"I haven't had the chance to congratulate Second Sister yet."

She stopped at Lu Huaixi's other side. The moment the maidservant finished the rouge and turned away to fetch something else, Lu Tangshu leaned in slightly, drawing close to her ear, meeting the vivid, flower-bright reflection in the bronze mirror.

A flash of envy crossed her eyes—but it was quickly pressed back down.

"Second Sister, even after you're married, remember to come back to the family often. No matter what happens, the Lu household will always stand behind you. I will too—please don't ever feel ashamed, and don't ever think that we at home would look down on you."

She paused briefly, then continued.

"And honestly, I do have a small bone to pick with Second Brother-in-law. The wedding day is already here and I, as your younger sister, still haven't laid eyes on him. Even if he is below expectations, that's no way to carry himself—really, only Second Sister with your patience would put up with it. But that said, Second Sister, please don't think so little of yourself. If the chance arises, I'll absolutely give Second Brother-in-law a proper talking-to."

"You're quite right."

Lu Huaixi followed her words with a nod, her red lips curving into a lovely arc, a smile blooming. "You'll see him in a moment. You're my younger sister—if you have any grievances, make sure to tell him in person. Warn him. Stand up for me."

Lu Tangshu froze for a moment, unable to tell whether the person in front of her had said it deliberately or simply hadn't understood the sarcasm. She found herself at a loss for words.

But Lu Huaixi didn't wait for her. She only held her gaze for a moment through the bronze mirror, then rose to her feet, smiling.

The auspicious hour was approaching. The bridal veil was lowered, shutting out the light.

All the Lu sisters had finally gathered in one place, and Lu Yuanzhao stood outside the room, waiting to carry his sister out on his back.

The sounds outside grew livelier—gongs and drums swelling from a distance, drawing near.

"He's here! The bridegroom has come to receive the bride!"

Someone shouted from outside, and in that moment, Lu Huaixi finally felt a nervousness she had never felt before.

chapters.title: They Were Talking About Xie Yuanjing
chapters.content:
Outside the Lu family gates, a distinguished and strikingly handsome young man rode on horseback, reins in hand, leading a dazzling wedding procession slowly forward.

The crimson ceremonial robes set off his complexion beautifully—pale and clear as jade. Sunlight fell across his refined features, softening the usual cool distance in his bearing and drawing out a faint, anticipatory warmth.

The bystanders on either side of the road had been wondering who could command such a grand procession—until they caught a clear view of the man at the front and suddenly put the two families together.

The eldest young lord of the Chengen Marquis' household was taking a wife—and he was marrying none other than the quietly reserved second daughter of the Lu family.

The jeering, festive shouts of the crowd dropped at once, and even those who had been about to clamor for lucky coins hesitated.

Only a few of the younger children pushed forward to try to get a look, but their families quickly pulled them back.

"Don't cause trouble—be careful you don't offend the gentry!"

"It's a joyous day for them! Who's going to lose their temper now?"

Watching the unruly little ones refuse to be reined in, the adults around them grew anxious and called out, "What do you know? The marquis' eldest son's wedding isn't some grand affair—the Lu family is keeping things quiet too. If the man truly wanted to make a show, would they have been hiding it all this time?"

There was some truth to that. For an ordinary household, the wedding would have been announced weeks in advance with posted notices and red banners, afraid the whole world might not know.

Yet these two families—the finest in the land—had said nothing, nothing, right up until the wedding day itself.

But no sooner had those words been said than a wave of startled gasps rose from the crowd at the front.

Everyone craned to look—and then they saw it: stretching back as far as the eye could see, the procession of guards and attendants, one after another; chest after chest of gifts and dowry; and matrons and maidservants on both sides distributing festive coins and wedding cakes without pause.

They had only glimpsed the beginning and already assumed it was some great and powerful household. Now, looking the length of it, they realized the spectacle was even larger than they had imagined.

"Now this is what you'd call hiding something," someone marveled. "This looks more like making sure the whole world knows exactly who he's marrying."

The one who had just spoken up to quiet the children didn't dare say another word—only pressed forward with the rest, wanting a glimpse of the gentry in their glory.

Lu Huaixi knew nothing of what was happening outside. She sat still and proper, staring at the hem of her own skirt, unable to see forward.

During the bride-receiving rite, she wouldn't see Xie Yuanjing—at most she'd hear his voice, be stopped by him to recite a poem, and exchange pleasantries with the elders.

The thought of someone like Xie Yuanjing dutifully going through a bride-receiving ceremony suddenly dissolved most of her earlier nerves.

She couldn't help laughing to herself—and then her thoughts were drowned out by the exclamations drifting in from outside.

"Second Sister—how come you never said Second Brother-in-law was coming with such a procession..."

A few of her sisters had slipped away to the front to find out what was happening, stolen a few glimpses, and come hurrying back—too astonished to get their words out properly.

"Second Sister, you—he—"

Lu Tangshu was somewhat displeased by a few of the concubine-born sisters' lack of composure. She grabbed the fourth sister, who was close to her in age, and hissed in a low voice.

"What are you making such a fuss about? Look at you—people will think Mother treated you badly, that you've never seen anything respectable in your life!"

"No—it's not that, Third Sister, I'm not making a fuss."

The fourth sister was a concubine-born daughter of the second branch, and her behavior had always been governed by Lu Tangshu's moods. Seeing her displeasure, she kept her excitement in check.

"It's the front—Second Brother-in-law has arrived, Third Sister. Go and see for yourself. It's quite an occasion out there. Grandfather and Grandmother are both smiling so wide—"

"Impossible!"

Lu Tangshu's expression shifted. Realizing her voice had come out too loud, she quickly reined herself in.

Grandfather might smile and receive the man graciously for the sake of the Lu family's reputation—but Grandmother had always been partial to her. She would never be too warm toward Lu Huaixi's convenient husband.

"You stay here. I'm going to the front to see for myself!"

Eager to watch Lu Huaixi make a spectacle of herself, Lu Tangshu stopped asking questions and pushed past the concubine-born sister in front of her.

No matter what she thought of him, she should at least go and get a proper look at the man.

The front was even livelier than Lu Tangshu had expected—a large crowd had gathered and people were holding the procession up, insisting the bridegroom compose a proper verse before they'd let him pass.

Lu Tangshu gave a quiet scoff, thinking that men of learning really only had this one trick to show off—and then she heard the wife of a distant Lu family branch speaking in wistful admiration beside her.

"Whatever anyone says, it's still the marquis' household. Never mind that the eldest son has power and influence—his looks alone are unmatched. What other family's daughter could easily land someone like that?"

Lu Tangshu's frown deepened. The movement of turning her head was faintly stiff.

"Exactly—if the marquis' household were really in decline, would the first branch have been willing to marry off a proper legitimate daughter there?"

"That's not necessarily true. I heard the engagement was set over a year ago, with a contract to prove it. Now that so many eyes are watching, the Lu family can't possibly back out. It's not like she had a choice."

The moment Lu Tangshu confirmed they were talking about Xie Yuanjing, she felt as though her breathing had gone uneven.

She pressed down the dizziness rising from her fury, and tightened her fist slowly inside her sleeve.

An engagement from a year ago? With a written contract?

Lu Tangshu worked furiously to recall the events of the past weeks.

In her mind, the marquis' household's preparations for a wedding and the first branch's additions of festive items came together, piece by piece.

From the failure to find out who Xie Yuanjing was courting, to Lu Huaixi's guileless smile in front of her—a number of inexplicable things suddenly seemed to find their explanation.

The whole mansion was festooned with blazing red silk, and Lu Tangshu stared fixedly at the scene ahead, as if she could see Lu Huaixi's deliberate mockery woven into that sea of crimson.

As her thoughts churned, the crowd blocking the way at the front finally stepped aside.

The man who people spoke of as inscrutable and untouchable was now walking through the gates of the Lu household—an easy half-smile at his lips, stepping closer.

Xie Yuanjing had always been sharp.

Almost immediately, he detected one particular gaze amid all the cheerful commotion—watchful, resentful.

It seemed barely restrained, carrying the pressure of an emotion desperate to erupt but held forcibly in check.

His dark eyes narrowed slightly, then his lids lifted with a casual lift of his gaze, sweeping across the space not far away.

In that instant his eyes went cold—sharp and ice-edged as an arrow, dangerous and cutting, as though it could pierce through a person's chest in the very next moment.

Lu Tangshu jolted awake, jerking her gaze away in a panic. A thin layer of cold sweat had broken out on her back.

She instinctively stepped backward—and in her haste, caught her foot on an uneven stone and tumbled to the ground.

The people at the front were absorbed in the shock and delight of learning the bridegroom was the marquis' eldest son. Only those standing nearby turned at her commotion.

Lu Tangshu swallowed her humiliation and scrambled to her feet. When she looked over again with trembling eyes, she found that the man had already withdrawn his gaze and moved past her position.

As if that brief glance had been nothing more than coincidence. As if his eyes had carried no warning, no pressure.

But Lu Tangshu knew. Xie Yuanjing had been displeased. He didn't like her—in fact—

Lu Tangshu clenched her fist and followed behind the crowd, teeth set.

Goaded by her bitterness, only one thought occupied her mind: to make Xie Yuanjing understand that Lu Huaixi was meant for the palace. The marquis' household must not have known—which was why they had been misled by her.

But before Lu Tangshu could take a single step in that direction, she was shoved aside by the crowd and nearly lost her footing again. She had no way of getting any closer.

—

In the inner courtyard, the matron led Lu Huaixi to her feet.

The excitement outside belonged to others. All Lu Huaixi had was hunger and sleepiness—and a curiosity about how Xie Yuanjing would look in wedding robes being put through all the ceremonial fuss.

Around her, the murmur of her sisters' chatter came and went, and occasionally she could hear her eldest sister offering warm, private counsel on how to manage the inner household after she arrived.

But at a certain moment, those voices fell suddenly quiet.

"What's he doing back here? He can't be here to see you—so soon. How impatient."

Lu Huaixi startled at her eldest sister's words. After a beat, she worked out that "he" must be referring to Xie Yuanjing.

She had no idea how to explain it—she and Xie Yuanjing weren't nearly familiar enough to need to see each other every day. She thought about it for a moment, and then simply said nothing.

Whatever puzzlement was in those words, however, when Xie Yuanjing drew near her eldest sister still made room for him.

chapters.title: No One Will Ever Say You Are Not Cherished
chapters.content:
The person approaching brought with them the distinctive scent that belonged to him.

Lu Huaixi couldn't see him, but by instinct she lowered her eyes, catching just a corner of ceremonial red beneath the bridal veil.

The matron had said the two of them couldn't meet before the bridal chamber—but since this wasn't a real wedding, Xie Yuanjing was clearly unconcerned with such rules, following none of them at all.

Lu Huaixi didn't find it troubling either. With his presence confirmed within her sight, she inexplicably felt much calmer.

And Xie Yuanjing, as though knowing what she was thinking, stopped and offered a quiet explanation.

"The veil hasn't been lifted. That doesn't break any rules."

"Is that allowed?"

"It is. Today, what you and I say goes."

He paused, then added: "Just now I saw your third sister. She has a scheme, but it's a stupid one."

Lu Huaixi paused, thinking of the barely-concealed spite in Lu Tangshu's eyes a moment ago. She pursed her lips in quiet amusement. "You came all the way back here just to tell me that?"

"Not only that. I was worried you might feel unsettled on your wedding day. Wanted to check in."

From the start, the wedding hadn't been meant to be a grand affair—partly to avoid drawing attention from those who might want to interfere with the marquis' household's new arrangement, and partly because Xie Yuanjing himself had simply had no particular feelings about it.

So when he and Lu Huaixi had agreed to keep things simple, he had thought nothing more of it.

But later, his mother's words had given him pause.

How one conducted a wedding reflected how much one valued one's future wife. Too casual—that wouldn't do.

"There are twenty-four of my personal guards stationed outside, with two more companies of trusted men following behind. The palanquin is the auspicious cloud-and-peacock pattern you like. The betrothal gifts have been expanded to thirty-six chests, and they are following behind."

"Today, lucky coins and wedding cakes will be distributed throughout both the east and west parts of the city. In both our names, I have also donated to two academies and one girls' school in the western district. Even a year from now, no one will dare say you were not valued by the Chengen Marquis' household."

The words came without warning, catching Lu Huaixi completely off guard.

Whether it was the tone—so composed, as if conducting business—or the attentiveness his words revealed, she didn't know how to respond.

This kind of regard was more than she had anticipated.

For a moment, the heart she had just steadied began to pound again—this time with something close to gratitude.

"You didn't have to do any of this. After all, we already agreed..."

"I'm telling you so that you don't feel uncomfortable after you arrive at the household. None of this counts against our arrangement. You don't owe me anything for it, so you needn't worry about it."

Right. Xie Yuanjing understood her.

Lu Huaixi let out a quiet breath of relief.

But the atmosphere had grown a touch strange regardless, so she pulled the conversation back to what he had first mentioned.

"Just now you said you saw my third sister—did she speak to you?"

"Why would she speak to me?"

"Because earlier today she told me she was very dissatisfied with her future Second Brother-in-law and wanted to give him a piece of her mind. She also said she would stand up for me, and that I shouldn't think less of myself just because I was married."

Lu Huaixi tilted her head slightly, smiling as the bridal veil swayed. "Did she give you that talking-to?"

She wasn't actually trying to complain—she had no need to complain. But perhaps because Xie Yuanjing's earlier words had brought them a little closer, she had found herself unable to resist telling him.

Only after the words "Second Brother-in-law" left her mouth did she feel that there was something oddly intimate about the phrase, not quite in keeping with what their relationship actually was.

The atmosphere shifted—from strange to awkward.

Especially since Xie Yuanjing had gone silent and said nothing in response.

Unable to see his expression, she could only guess. Lu Huaixi's heart began to beat unsteadily, and she was just preparing to say something to pass it off as a joke, when the person in front of her gave a quiet laugh.

Low-toned, languid—without a face to go with it, the sound was inexplicably more captivating.

"No."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his voice. "What right does she have to warn me? She nearly sent my wife out of the family and ruined my wedding. Every one of those offenses is her looking for her own end."

"?"

"First let me get through the next stretch of business."

"What are you going to do?"

"Her newly appointed Second Brother-in-law will make sure she understands her own worth. When the time comes, remember to go and comfort her—and tell her not to 'think less of herself.'"

Lu Huaixi was thoroughly overwhelmed by his words and couldn't think straight.

When she finally registered that this man was standing up for her, she couldn't hold back a laugh.

Xie Yuanjing joking with a perfectly straight face—he was really something.

The sounds outside grew loud again. Seeing the matron come in, Xie Yuanjing didn't linger.

Shortly after, gongs and firecrackers sounded in another round. Lu Huaixi was carried out on her brother's back, one step at a time, toward the wedding palanquin.

The shoulders carrying her were wide and steady, his steps measured. As they walked toward the gate, all the young man's usual playfulness was gone, and his expression held nothing but gravity.

Lu Huaixi hadn't planned to cry—after all, she wasn't truly getting married.

But as they passed that stone-paved road she had walked for more than a decade, and she heard her brother—not knowing any of it—speak low and gentle words of comfort, a sharp sting hit the tip of her nose without warning. Tears welled in her eyes.

"If anyone in the marquis' household gives you grief, or if Xie Yuanjing treats you poorly, your brother will come and bring you home."

Lu Huaixi cried after all.

After that, the palanquin was lifted. The procession moved through the city with music and fanfare, arriving at the marquis' household.

Red silk was pulled for the bowing ceremony before heaven and earth.

Xie Yuanjing even guided her by the hand, taking over where the matron would have, leading her to the inner chambers—as though he had genuinely stepped into the role her brother had just relinquished.

Only when the chamber door closed and the matron took up her place beside Yaoshu on one side did that aching, swollen feeling in her chest finally begin to subside.

When she next spoke, her nose was still a little stopped up.

—

Xie Yuanjing returned before it grew too late. A faint trace of wine clung to him—light enough that it wasn't unpleasant.

When the matron presented the jade ruyi before him, Lu Huaixi's hands inside her wide sleeves tightened with nerves.

She had just stolen a bite of jujube a moment ago, and now, as she bit down on her lip, the faint sweetness still lingered at the corner of her mouth.

The jade ruyi was soon before her eyes, rising from below—inching upward—until it touched the edge of the bridal veil.

The touch was so light it was barely there, yet it struck something in Lu Huaixi's chest and left her at a complete loss.

Xie Yuanjing's hand stilled there.

As if a thought had come to him, he said softly, "Don't be afraid. I had the small kitchen cook you some noodles."

She didn't know why those two things had been said together, but Lu Huaixi did relax a little.

She gave a nod, realizing after the fact that she was genuinely, extremely hungry.

"Is there more?"

"Also delicate steamed dumplings and clear-broth lamb. Don't eat too much this late."

"Then I'd also like one serving of something sweet—something with cake."

"No. I'll have it made tomorrow."

"Just tonight—I'll eat only a little. Please?"

"No. It's too late. Be sensible."

One side of the room held Yaoshu and the matron who had come from the Lu family to attend Lu Huaixi; the other side held the marquis' household's own staff.

Hearing this exchange, the Lu family's people found nothing amiss—it was no different from how their master and mistress had always indulged the young miss.

But the marquis' household's own maidservants and matrons were inwardly stunned—and gave the figure at the front one furtive, disbelieving glance after another.

They would sooner believe the man before them was a guard in disguise than accept that their eldest young master was speaking in this coaxing tone.

Xie Yuanjing paid no attention to anyone else's expression.

With the words settled, the jade ruyi lifted again, and the veil was raised.

The expression on Lu Huaixi's face fell into Xie Yuanjing's view just as she was pressing her lips together in displeasure at being refused.

She seemed to be about to throw a small tantrum—then seemed to remember she was at someone else's mercy, and so turned her vexation back on herself.

Xie Yuanjing couldn't help but smile.

The candlelight caught the curve of his mouth—faint, barely there, yet enough to startle the already bewildered onlookers.

But Lu Huaixi didn't notice.

Her suddenly expanded field of vision made her forget what had just happened. The warm glow of red candles fell into her eyes. She blinked to adjust—and then, in the shifting light, looked up at the person in front of her.

Brilliant ceremonial robes. A man of rare and striking beauty.

Lu Huaixi thought about it. She didn't think she had ever seen anyone more beautiful than Xie Yuanjing.

Still in something of a daze, she was brought back by the sound of the matron presenting two cups of wine at her side.

The wedding cup of union. They had to be drunk.

Lu Huaixi had barely ever touched alcohol—only the light, fruity sweet wine that couldn't make anyone drunk.

She reached for her cup with a sudden eager anticipation—only to hear the person ahead speak.

"She doesn't drink wine."

"Young Master, this—this isn't proper..."

"We don't follow other people's rules here. Go exchange it for tea."

chapters.title: A Small Sense of Peace
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi watched with longing eyes—but in the end, she didn't have the nerve to defy Xie Yuanjing's word.

Perhaps it was the roof over her head, or perhaps she was mindful of owing someone a favor later on—either way, she watched her wine cup be replaced with a tea cup and said nothing.

Still, when she went to drink, she couldn't help stealing a glance at the wine cup in Xie Yuanjing's hand.

Lu Huaixi tilted her head back.

The man across from her was standing very close—their linked arms, through the layers of fabric, transmitted a warmth that was impossible to ignore.

She watched him raise his cup and bring it slowly to his lips, and for a moment forgot that she was also supposed to drink at the same time. Her gaze traveled along the sharp, perfect line of his jaw and came to rest at one corner of his thin lips.

She was even more curious to try the wine now. Lu Huaixi blinked.

Xie Yuanjing had intended to down his in one go and be done with it. His movement was swift—he had barely lifted the cup to his mouth when he noticed the person beside him hadn't moved.

The arm pressed against his was slender and slight, with little real strength to it—it couldn't possibly have been enough to stop him. Yet Xie Yuanjing paused all the same.

He lowered his eyes to look. He assumed she needed to say something.

"What is it?"

Lu Huaixi met Xie Yuanjing's questioning gaze and startled slightly, realizing she had perhaps been a little rude just now.

But stepping back would have been odd too. She came back to herself, shook the cup lightly in her hand, and took the lead—tilting her head back and draining it in one clean swallow.

Xie Yuanjing followed shortly after.

The man's originally flat, unsmiling lips were touched now with a faint gloss. Because they were standing so close, Lu Huaixi thought she could even catch a thin trace of new wine in the air.

It was, oddly, a little pleasant.

"Go wash up first."

Xie Yuanjing set down his cup. "Come back and eat afterward."

Lu Huaixi had no wish to wash up and then eat, only to have to wash up again. She looked at the person in front of her, reluctant to move.

Noticing she seemed to be in a mild daze, the man who had been about to step back found the whole thing oddly amusing. He avoided her pinned hair and reached up to give her head a gentle pat.

"You can't sit comfortably in that gown."

The warmth of the touch broke through Lu Huaixi's haze at once. She didn't dare look at him and only bowed her head in awkward sheepishness.

The wedding dress was indeed very heavy, and the skirt was enormous.

"Understood."

The flushed girl muttered under her breath, thinking only that this man's hand was even larger than her brother's.
