But it was warm. The faint calluses that had just passed over her head—they made one feel quite settled.

As she walked out, Lu Huaixi took a quick look around the room. It was spacious, and the furnishings were few—but what was there all looked refined.

Nothing like her own room, which was packed with things. One glance here told you its occupant was no young child.

After Lu Huaixi left, Gong Fei entered.

"Master."

He lowered his head, not daring to look around the room. "Today our men kept He Jianxing pressed in the crowd and forced him to watch the entire bride-receiving procession."

"Mm. Was he happy watching?"

Xie Yuanjing gave a light acknowledgment.

Without Lu Huaixi nearby, he had set aside the manner of someone tending a small child. Now his voice carried a note of contemptuous amusement, with an undercurrent of cold.

Gong Fei thought of the reports that had come in and pressed down a laugh.

"He Jianxing didn't believe it at first—he was mouthing off in there. Then when he heard it was you coming to receive the bride, with such a procession, his face turned green with rage. But there was no way out. He had to stand there and watch—watch the young mistress board the palanquin."

"Good. When there's a spare moment, let him see a few more things."

Xie Yuanjing hadn't originally given the man much thought.

It wasn't unusual for Lu Huaixi to have admirers. But this particular man had made the mistake of being far too presumptuous.

And Xie Yuanjing happened to have some idle time at the moment. The girl was newly his to look after. Naturally he would make sure this person understood the difference.

"Understood, this subordinate will see to it."

Gong Fei lowered his head. "There is also the matter of the young mistress—the Lu family's second branch has not dared act on the list matter these past days, most likely for fear of drawing attention. However, the young mistress had word passed out a few days ago."

"Using the same method they used?"

Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed slightly. He put one hand behind his back and lifted his gaze to the window.

The Lu family's second branch had dared to spread the rumor precisely because Lu Huaixi's name was genuinely on the list—which was why they had felt bold enough to block her path. But Lu Huaixi spreading rumors in return wouldn't actually threaten the second branch.

A different approach was needed.

"In reply to Master—the young mistress did not spread the news about the second branch's daughter entering the palace. She spread the news that someone had bribed their way onto the list."

"Bribed their way on?"

"Yes. Now the person who handled the matter is under scrutiny—they can't casually remove anyone from the list. If it comes out that a married woman is still on it, they would be found derelict in their duties as well."

So a substitution was urgent.

But the Lu family was no minor household. Lu Huaixi's spot couldn't simply be filled by some nobody.

Counting the days, the only candidate who would be close enough in timing was the second branch's legitimate daughter, who was soon to come of age.

But there was real risk in this. Once the scrutinized parties recovered their footing, it wouldn't take long for them to trace the trail back to Lu Huaixi.

"Bring in a fresh group of people with no connection to the young mistress to take over, and find a few other pieces of news to put out at the same time."

"Understood."

Better to muddy the water entirely—so that no one could trace anything back to anyone.

After Gong Fei withdrew, Xie Yuanjing stood a while longer by the window. He hadn't intended to dwell on anything in particular—yet his mind, without prompting, drifted back to the image of a small girl staring hungrily at his wine cup.

He hadn't missed it.

Xie Yuanjing couldn't help smiling again—the corner of his mouth tilting up slightly, the curve gone almost before it formed.

He suddenly thought that the coming year, with this new arrival in the household, might not be the same stagnant, dull expanse it had always been.

A breeze passed through the courtyard outside, lifting and scattering the leaves.

Xie Yuanjing collected himself. He had no plans to go back out to the front of the house. He would head to the bath early.

But just as he reached the doorway, he saw the head matron Zhao come in from outside, a handkerchief folded in her hands.

"This old servant greets the eldest young master."

She bowed respectfully. "Young Master, the young mistress only brought one maidservant and one matron with her. Lady Xie's thought is to send someone from her own staff tomorrow—someone the young mistress might take to—to serve her."

"The matter of maidservants I will arrange myself."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze fell briefly on what Matron Zhao was carrying, and he said coolly, "Take those things away. She is still young. Tell my mother not to rush."

Matron Zhao was momentarily at a loss, caught between two impossible positions. "Yes, this old servant understands. Only—if others were to find out that you and the young mistress have not yet..."

The words consummated the marriage never left her mouth. Xie Yuanjing had already waved a hand.

"Stop gossiping. Others won't find out. Everyone withdraw—no one needs to remain in the room."

Matron Zhao snapped her mouth shut without another word and immediately backed out.

Lu Huaixi had no idea that Xie Yuanjing had already deflected the matron's arrangements on her behalf. She had changed into new clothes, washed the cosmetics from her face, and was sitting fresh and easy at the table.

Her skin, still damp from washing, was even finer and more translucent than usual—candlelight falling on her made it seem as though she were faintly glowing.

Yaoshu was at her back, tying her towel-dried hair, when someone knocked at the outer door and announced herself as one of the household's maidservants, sent by the Old Madam to deliver a gift.

A gift sent to the bridal chamber—Lu Huaixi wasn't quite sure what to make of it.

Not wanting to make her feel awkward, no one else had been kept in the room for the moment. She now had no one but Yaoshu to look at.

"Can I accept it?"

Yaoshu blinked. "I should think so—she is, after all, the Old Madam of this household."

Lu Huaixi considered briefly, then stopped worrying about it. "You're right. If it weren't allowed, the maidservant wouldn't have been let into the courtyard."

Soon the visitors entered, bearing a scroll painting in both hands and a large wooden box, with another maidservant behind them carrying a pair of black boots embroidered with gold trim.

"Servants greet the eldest young mistress."

Both bowed respectfully, placing their items before Lu Huaixi on the table.

The boots were set on the floor. Lu Huaixi glanced at them.

The craftsmanship was fine—the gold trim delicate but understated. These were a man's items.

They must have been intended for Xie Yuanjing—but judging by the style alone, they didn't seem like something worth sending by special courier on a wedding night.

Does Xie Yuanjing really need shoes that badly? Lu Huaixi frowned slightly, perplexed.

chapters.title: How Do We Sleep Tonight
chapters.content:
The maidservant had kept her head down the entire time.

Only once the items were set down did the one at the front speak.

"Young mistress, this is a painting in the Old Master Yuan's own hand—the Old Madam received it recently and especially wanted to present it to you today, to bring some happiness on this auspicious occasion. And this is a set of jewelry she picked out for you herself, to wear whenever you please."

Lu Huaixi accepted the gifts without hesitation, openly and graciously.

But after a moment, when the maidservant made no mention of the boots—only curtsied respectfully and withdrew—Lu Huaixi's gaze kept drifting back to them.

Once the room was empty again, Yaoshu unrolled the painting on her young mistress's behalf and was about to hand it over when she noticed Lu Huaixi's eyes hadn't moved from the boots on the floor.

"What is it, miss—young mistress?"

Lu Huaixi shook her head, then looked away.

She was about to take the painting when she suddenly recalled what the maidservant had said.

Old Master Yuan?

She wasn't one for calligraphy and painting—but she had heard of many of the great names in the field.

This Old Master Yuan she had also heard of. Unlike other masters who excelled in landscapes or figures, this one had changed his style entirely at some point and dedicated himself exclusively to paintings of "a hundred children"—and legend had it that every person who obtained one of his works had their heart's desire fulfilled. After Old Master Yuan passed away, his paintings vanished from the world. They became impossible to find and increasingly priceless.

Lu Huaixi looked up.

The moment she caught sight of the grapes and split pomegranates on the scroll, she yanked her gaze away—her ears inexplicably warm.

Better not to look. It had little to do with her anyway.

When Xie Yuanjing came in, the freshly cooked noodles had just arrived, along with translucent delicate dumplings and perfectly tender lamb.

Lu Huaixi had been about to tell him about the gifts, but before she could speak, he had already called her over to the table, and the food quickly drew her full attention.

Lu Huaixi had genuinely been starving. Aside from a few stolen bites of fruit during the day, she had barely eaten a thing—and she had just bathed, which had used up a little more energy besides.

Xie Yuanjing didn't eat much—he joined her for a few bites out of courtesy, then set down his chopsticks.

The small girl beside him, however, ate with complete focus: a bite of noodles, a bite of side dish, a slice of lamb.

Her table manners were lovely. Even with something as brothy and splashy as noodles, she managed not to get much of it on her lips.

Only every now and then, when some thought seemed to pass through her mind, she would accidentally let the noodles burn her tongue—but even then she didn't frown. Just a faint, fleeting curl of her tongue, and it was over.

By the time she finished, Xie Yuanjing realized—he had been watching her eat for quite some time.

After rinsing her mouth again, Lu Huaixi rose to her feet.

Thinking of the painting, she felt a flush that still hadn't quite faded—and an embarrassment she couldn't quite name—even though she knew nothing was going to happen.

"Something on your mind?"

Xie Yuanjing could see she was hiding something. He stopped her, cutting through her distraction. "Tell me."

She was in a strange new household, and an unknown year lay ahead—it was only natural that Lu Huaixi felt some measure of unease.

She didn't show it on the surface, but internally she was bound to feel somewhat adrift.

Yet Xie Yuanjing's quiet "tell me" was like the steady approach of a small boat on a rocking surface—catching her, drawing her toward safety.

"Nothing."

Lu Huaixi shook her head. But her bright, clear eyes looked straight at him, full of trust.

"Just—earlier, the Old Madam sent someone to deliver gifts. I accepted them. Is that all right?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't answer immediately. He held her earnest, open gaze—a gaze that, somehow, had taken on the faintest tint of reliance—and was briefly, inexplicably struck.

The Lu family's inner workings were, in truth, anything but peaceful. The first and second branches were at odds, tangled in the same kind of mutual pulling and maneuvering as any other prominent household—a dynamic perhaps even less settled than the third branch that had been posted away from the capital.

Yet despite all of that, Lu Huaixi had been raised with a nature that was remarkably, genuinely pure—nothing to do with how clever or foolish she was.

She extended goodwill first. Unlike others who approached with caution, probing for what they could gain. She would extend it, and if it was accepted, she would give trust—openly, without concealment, letting others see her reliance and warmth.

And if the goodwill wasn't returned, it was fine too. She seemed born with the ability to heal herself—for her own sake, and for others'.

Of course, there was also the clean, decisive willingness to cut things off entirely when needed.

"Can I not accept it?"

Seeing that Xie Yuanjing hadn't responded, Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together and asked again.

She had already, without thinking, placed Xie Yuanjing on her side.

Even here in the Xie household, even though she was speaking of Xie Yuanjing's own grandmother—she had drawn Xie Yuanjing to her corner without a second thought.

"You can accept it. It's fine."

After a long moment, Xie Yuanjing finally spoke. His voice came out a little low. He lifted his teacup and took a measured sip.

"I thought you weren't saying anything because it broke some rule."

"Not breaking a rule wouldn't have stopped you either."

"How do you know I'm not afraid?"

Lu Huaixi muttered under her breath, then turned and found herself another place to sit—right next to where the maidservant had left the new boots.

Xie Yuanjing still didn't answer. He just gave a quiet laugh, his gaze dropping to the empty bowl on the table.

Lu Huaixi followed his eyes and felt her cheeks heat.

She could tell perfectly well: Xie Yuanjing was laughing at her. Laughing because she had been frightened, yet still managed such a good appetite.

Too thin-skinned for her own good, Lu Huaixi turned her head away. After a pause to recover, she steered the conversation back.

"The Old Madam sent a painting and a set of jewelry. And these boots as well."

She pointed to the items on the floor, and asked with some puzzlement, "Are you very short on shoes?"

The smile that had been faint on Xie Yuanjing's face faded as the topic changed. His eyes dropped, expression cooling.

"No."

He swept a glance over the boots, and when the servant came to tidy up, said coldly, "Take those. Throw them away."

Lu Huaixi was a little taken aback.

The shoes were somewhat plain, but not so offensive as to deserve being thrown out.

Before she could puzzle it out, Xie Yuanjing had already risen.

"If there's anything you need added to the room, tell Gong Fei to arrange it. If any of the furnishings feel too heavy or stuffy, you can change them. Don't feel constrained."

Watching him head toward the inner room, she stopped wondering about the shoes and only looked around once more. "It's not stuffy. It's beautiful."

The maidservants quickly withdrew, and the room was left with just the two of them again.

But more than admiring Xie Yuanjing's quarters, Lu Huaixi had something more pressing on her mind.

"Tonight... how do we sleep?"

"Up to you. How would you like to?"

"?"

Xie Yuanjing's steps paused. Right beside him was a newly moved-in daybed.

He didn't say so out loud—he only turned toward the outer room. "On the bed, or on the floor. Either works for me."

The room fell abruptly quiet.

Lu Huaixi lowered her head, not quite knowing how to respond.

At the flower-viewing gathering the day Lady Xie had hosted, she and Xie Yuanjing had talked for quite a while at the water pavilion. Before she left, he had called her back, saying he also had terms that required her agreement.

She had naturally said yes—and among those terms was one that said the two of them would not sleep separately for the first three months after the wedding.

No giving anyone reason to suspect. No letting anything look out of place.

This couldn't reasonably be refused. Lu Huaixi understood that clearly.

But now that the day had actually arrived, she found herself suddenly flustered, and had no idea how to arrange things.

This was someone else's room. She couldn't very well ask him to sleep on the floor for three months—but if she took the floor herself, she was certain she'd wake up unable to move.

"Come here."

She was still deliberating when a quiet laugh fell—low and warm, pleasant to hear.

chapters.title: The First Time Sharing a Room
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing had watched her stand there, head down, looking pitifully obedient, for long enough. He called her over with a smile.

Lu Huaixi stepped inside properly, and saw the brand new daybed.

"Do you like room dividers?"

She was still startled by how perfectly timed its arrival had been. She shook her head at the question. "I don't."

"...Then we won't use one. This is how it'll be from now on—you sleep on the bed, I'll take the daybed."

"For three months?"

"What else?"

Lu Huaixi considered this. "Otherwise, we could take turns."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her again and laughed quietly. "No need for you to take a turn. There's no reason you should sleep worse here than at the Lu household."

Those words sent another jolt through Lu Huaixi's chest, and the last of her awkwardness dissolved under his low, unhurried, and unexpectedly gentle tone.

"You go settle in. I'll look through some papers in the outer room."

"No need to use the study?"

"How could I go to the study tonight?"

Xie Yuanjing lowered his eyes. "No need. The outer room is enough."

There were hardly any real papers to attend to on a wedding night. He simply didn't want her to feel uncomfortable—he wanted her to fall asleep first.

After a few more exchanges, Lu Huaixi had guessed at his intention. She watched his retreating figure, pressed her lips together softly, and felt genuinely relieved by what he had done.

—

The red candles in the outer room were a touch bright. Xie Yuanjing turned the pages of the ledger in his hand without taking much of it in.

Only when the small rustling sounds from the inner room had gone still—when the turning of sheets had stopped—did he set down what he was holding and press his fingers briefly to his brow.

The whole room seemed to have taken on a faint, sweet fragrance.

He had always lived alone. Incense was rarely burned in here. After adding a full bookshelf to the room, the air carried mainly the scent of ink and old paper.

But now a new fragrance had made its presence enormously felt, saturating every corner of the room.

It had nothing of its owner's usual restraint—it staked its claim boldly, refusing to disperse from around the tip of his nose.

Unable to concentrate, Xie Yuanjing gave up trying to force himself.

He put things away and stood, extinguished the red candles in the outer room, and lightened his steps.

Before the last lights in the inner room went out, he looked across the distance at Lu Huaixi for a brief moment.

The thin blanket was pulled up to the tip of her nose. Above it, long lashes lay shut—thick, softly curled.

She was sleeping soundly—more soundly than he'd expected. He wasn't sure whether to call that a big heart or simply enviable.

He extinguished the last few lamps, and finally lay down, pulling a thin blanket over himself.

Darkness filled his vision. It took him a moment to adjust.

Perhaps because it was the first time sharing a room with someone, Xie Yuanjing closed and opened his eyes—not a trace of sleepiness in them.

Moonlight fell in from outside, and lying where he was, if he turned his head just slightly, he could see the bed.

He didn't look.

Just as he was preparing to force his eyes closed again, a soft, small sound reached him, accompanied by the faint shifting of blankets.

"Sleepy."

Xie Yuanjing went still. After a brief silence, he kept his voice quiet. "...You're still awake?"

The person on the bed didn't seem to be responding to him at all.

"So sleepy."

Lu Huaixi murmured, half-mumbling, turning over and making a small smacking sound with her lips. "Sweetcakes tomorrow. Big Brother is buying."

That was what she hadn't been able to eat at dinner.

Realizing she was talking in her sleep, Xie Yuanjing paused for a moment.

Then he got up with a helpless sigh, casually draping an outer robe over his shoulders, and walked to the bedside in the cool moonlight.

The blanket had indeed been pushed aside at one corner, exposing the snow-white inner garment at Lu Huaixi's neck and shoulder. He was silent for a moment—then reached over and tucked it carefully back around her.

He returned to the daybed, pressed his fingers to his brow, and forced his eyes shut—drifting off at last in the soft sound of her breathing.

—

In the rear quarters of the marquis' household, the Old Madam, still awake well past the hour for sleep, let out a sigh—weariness on her face.

A young woman sat before her, head slightly lowered, in a plain, pale green dress—simple and unadorned. She said nothing, only let fall the occasional tear, looking quite pitiful.

"Nianwei, regardless of whether Yuanjing acted willingly or not, that place is no longer yours for the taking. But if you are wise, and play a longer game—entering the inner household is still possible."

"I know Grandaunt cares for me."

Mu Nianwei took a slow breath and held back her tears.

"Now that my cousin has married, I wouldn't dare hope for anything more. I only wish the woman he married will look after him well, manage the household properly, and give Grandaunt a great-grandchild soon."

"That you can think this way is good. Of everyone, I naturally still value you most—only..."

The Old Madam shook her head.

She had already arranged a good many opportunities for the girl before her, and had come near to a complete and permanent falling-out with her own grandson.

Today, she hadn't originally planned to send a gift to the new bride so suddenly—but seeing Nianwei's longing to give Yuanjing a pair of shoes she had made herself, she had found a pretext and carried out that small wish for her.

She could see clearly what the girl before her was hoping for.

Sending a handmade pair of shoes on a wedding night—to make him think of her; to give the new bride something to wonder about.

It wasn't a particularly high-minded ploy, but that didn't mean it was entirely without use.

"This kind of thing—only once."

The Old Madam's somewhat clouded eyes narrowed slightly. "You have always been sensible. If you truly mean to contend, wait at least until Yuanjing has moved past this stage."

"I understand. My cousin..."

Mu Nianwei lowered her eyes and touched a handkerchief to her eye corners.

"Even if it was not by choice, my cousin has already married her. I only fault myself for having no standing that could help him. Tonight I sent the shoes partly to remind myself of him—and partly to learn whether the young mistress is easy to get along with. Whether she would give my cousin trouble with her temperament."

"Are you certain Yuanjing has no feeling for the new bride?"

"Grandaunt, I heard the old master's own words to my cousin—he told him to keep the larger picture in mind."

She paused, then said in a hoarse voice, "From what I heard, that Lu family noble daughter sounds rather willful and pampered."

The Old Madam fell into silence at that.

She had originally thought that having Nianwei marry in could help create a softer influence on her grandson—someone to make him more manageable. She hadn't expected him to drive Nianwei out so bluntly, without the slightest consideration.

Though she and this eldest grandson were not particularly close, she had no wish to push things to a genuine breaking point.

And besides, the younger ones truly needed his help to rise.

"Since she is willful, you be even more even-tempered."

The Old Madam closed her eyes briefly, then opened them. "Yuanjing's inner household will not remain with just one person. There will always be a need for someone who knows how to be pleasing and considerate."

"I understand, Grandaunt. As long as I can care for you and my cousin, I'll do whatever is needed. Even if I can never be his—truly his—Nianwei won't speak a single word of complaint."

Outside the room, the second branch's wife Qi Miaoyi had just arrived with soup medicine and caught the last two lines.

She couldn't help a small curl of her lip—a look of dry amusement at this so-called cousin.

"The bride is already in the house, and she's still dreaming."

The matron beside her was startled and quickly cautioned her. "We're in the Old Madam's courtyard—really, Second Madam, this isn't something to say out loud."

"What's there to fear? It's this late—no one can hear."

Qi Miaoyi simply stopped outside the room.

"What is our Old Madam thinking, really? Taking in some distant relation is one thing, but trying to tie her own grandson to the girl? Never mind anything else—isn't the Lu girl good enough? What exactly is she trying to gain?"

Today had been the first branch's great occasion, and she had been in good spirits, looking forward to meeting the new bride tomorrow.

If they got along, she thought, it could lead to more contact going forward.

But then, just as she'd been about to retire for the night, she'd been summoned over here.

It was usually the third branch's wife who attended to these things—the Old Madam had always favored the youngest and often used such occasions to add benefits to the third branch. But tonight the hour was too late for the Old Madam to bother summoning the third branch wife—and the first branch refused to come—so she'd been called instead.

Qi Miaoyi had a whole belly full of frustration with nowhere to put it. Hearing this kind of absurdity, she naturally couldn't hold her tongue about standing up for the first branch.

chapters.title: I Am Behind You
chapters.content:
The next morning, when Lu Huaixi woke, the sun outside was already bright.

She opened her eyes to an unfamiliar place and lay in a daze for a long while before slowly sitting up.

At the sound of movement, Yaoshu came in from outside the door, followed by a maidservant carrying warm water.

"I am Jingshuang. Greetings, eldest young mistress."

Lu Huaixi was still drowsy, barely taking it in, and gave only a vague sound of acknowledgment.

She didn't fully wake until she took the warm cloth offered to her.

"We still have to pour tea for the elders today, don't we?"

Lu Huaixi suddenly rallied, looked outside, and frowned. "Have I slept past the time? Why didn't anyone wake me?"

"Don't be anxious, Young Mistress."

Yaoshu picked up the thread and soothed her. "Before the eldest young master left for the study, he gave instructions—he said there was no need to be so early, and that he would come and escort you over himself."

"Still, I shouldn't have slept so late. It's the first day—going late isn't a good impression, however things stand."

Regardless of what the marriage was, there was no excuse for keeping the elders waiting.

Yaoshu didn't dare let things drag further, and together with Jingshuang helped her change her clothes and arrange her hair.

Afterward, Lu Huaixi stepped outside, intending to ask when Xie Yuanjing would be arriving—only to look up and find two matrons waiting for her outside.

One was Matron Ying, who had come from the Lu household to attend her—warm and familiar. The other she didn't recognize, clearly one of the marquis' household's own, with an air of sternness.

"The eldest young mistress has slept rather late today. At this point, when you arrive, you must remember to ask the elders' pardon."

Matron Ying's brow furrowed at the tone, clearly displeased.

But Lu Huaixi felt no reproach whatsoever. Her eyes held nothing but candid self-accountability.

"I will apologize. I did oversleep today."

The speaking matron had been braced for resistance and was briefly caught off guard. She found she had nothing to pounce on.

She was a matron from the Old Madam's courtyard. The night before, the Old Madam had heard that the new bride was spoiled and had a difficult temperament, and had sent her first thing in the morning to take a look—and to deliver a little warning.

She had barely arrived before she heard that someone inside had overslept.

"Though the eldest young mistress is young, that is no excuse to neglect the rules. Going forward, please mind the hour for morning greetings. Being married is not the same as being at home."

"Of course. Though I would note that there was no reminder from your end, leaving me and my household to unknowingly commit a breach of courtesy—which might also be considered a lapse on your part."

Lu Huaixi finished her apology without a trace of the shame and embarrassment the matron had anticipated.

Instead, she met that stern gaze squarely, brow slightly creased, and asked with full sincerity: "Are you a matron assigned to the eldest young master's court?"

The matron paused again, expression shifting.

"I serve the Old Madam, but even if I were not from the eldest young master's court, the Old Madam's authority gives me standing to instruct the eldest young mistress on proper conduct."

The crease between Lu Huaixi's brows had not smoothed.

Those usually clear and bright eyes were not as carefree as usual today—they held a layer of thought.

She was still weighing whether to give the Old Madam some face on this, the first day, when she heard footsteps approaching from ahead.

Looking up, she saw Xie Yuanjing returning from the study.

"You slept late last night—why not sleep a little longer?"

The matron had been on the verge of probing why there had been no sign of the eldest young master in the room—but hearing this, she swallowed the question back down.

Even so, her heart was beating a little faster. She didn't want to truly provoke this one's displeasure.

"I need to pour tea for the elders. I'm already late."

Lu Huaixi answered him without thinking anything was amiss in what he'd said.

Xie Yuanjing gave a brief acknowledgment and, very naturally, reached out and pressed her hand briefly. Before Lu Huaixi could react, the hand had already released.

"Your hand is cold. From now on, you needn't get up so early."

Then Xie Yuanjing suddenly looked up at the people following behind.

His tone was the same—but when his words fell, the air around them went inexplicably cold, filling with a quiet pressure.

"Have I not said before? No unauthorized entry to my courtyard."

"We beg the eldest young master's forgiveness!"

The figures behind scrambled in a rush, lowering their heads to confess. "It was our negligence—we failed to stop them!"

"Once last night, once this morning."

Xie Yuanjing swept a glance over them. "This is the third day of the wedding—blood is not to be drawn within three days. After those three days, present yourselves for punishment."

The matron nearby, hearing this, trembled from head to toe.

She suddenly understood: no matter how willful the new bride, her behavior only had consequences within the inner household. But this man—if displeased—was not the sort to observe decorum or spare anyone's feelings.

In her panic, the matron also lowered her head and began to ask forgiveness.

"Twenty strikes to the face."

Xie Yuanjing had no intention of letting it go. "So she doesn't forget—and doesn't think she can come to my courtyard to instruct my wife on proper behavior."

The punishment was declared. There was no room for argument.

Lu Huaixi said nothing, and simply walked out alongside Xie Yuanjing.

From behind them came the crisp sound of the punishment being carried out—clearly without any attempt to soften the blows.

But more than what was happening behind her, her thoughts had lingered on the moment Xie Yuanjing had said "my wife" in that cold, measured tone.

"Rather more capable than I'd imagined. I thought you might just swallow the reproach."

"What?"

Lu Huaixi's train of thought was interrupted. She turned her head to look at him, puzzled. "What capability? Where?"

"Just now—calling her derelict. Was that not intended as a reprimand?"

"No."

Thinking back on it, Lu Huaixi shook her head, looking at him with surprise. "If she were a matron assigned to your court, then she was derelict. I was simply pointing it out so she would know."

A beat. Then she asked with genuine curiosity: "Could she be punished for it?"

Xie Yuanjing was briefly caught off guard.

For a moment he had nothing to say. Watching her blink, her expression perfectly guileless, he raised his hand—for some reason—and gave her head another light pat.

"She could. Anyone who is disrespectful to you—punish them however you see fit."

"Even those from the Old Madam's court?"

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing liked watching her eyes. He liked watching himself reflected in them too.

As if, with her looking at him, he could for that one moment exist within something clear and untroubled.

"My court doesn't normally allow outside people to come and go. Last night they used the commotion of the wedding to slip in. It won't happen again."

"You seem to be quite an authority in this household."

"I am."

Xie Yuanjing smiled briefly. "I am behind you—so you can be a little bolder."

The small cloud that had come with waking up in an unfamiliar place, and the small irritation of being unreasonably lectured—half of it had vanished the instant Xie Yuanjing touched her hand. The other half dissolved in his reassuring words.

Lu Huaixi tilted her head, smiling. "Then for this one year, I intend to be an idle, somewhat imperious head of the inner household."

"Fine."

There was still some distance to the front hall.

Lu Huaixi was in good spirits, following along—stone-paved path beneath their feet, then a covered walkway, and then past a small flower bed.

Half-height trellises were wound with vines, from which small nameless blossoms had opened in clusters.

Compared to the prized varieties in the flower bed, Lu Huaixi found the small ones that could sway in the breeze far more appealing.

Xie Yuanjing noticed and looked alongside her.

"Those flowers in there—my mother had them arranged. On our way back I'll come with you to pick some."

"It's all right."

Lu Huaixi shook her head.

She had just been about to say it wasn't the inner flowers she was looking at, when she felt the wind pick up.

A strong gust—and one small purple blossom from the vines was caught up and sent tumbling.

The petals fluttered like a butterfly without a plan—and came to rest, at last, in Lu Huaixi's open palm.

"Why are you so happy?"

Hearing a quiet laugh, Xie Yuanjing turned his head to look.

Lu Huaixi always loved to share her joy. Her eyes curved like crescent moons, stars glinting in the brightness.

"Look."

She extended her open hand, showing him the flower resting there.

"Happy because my luck is good."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze rested on the flower in her palm for a long moment. Then, unhurried, he smiled too.

"Yes."

After a moment he looked back at Lu Huaixi's eyes, and said once more:

"My luck is also very good."

chapters.title: What Is Mine Is Yours
chapters.content:
In the main hall, all the branches of the Xie family had already taken their seats.

Although Lu Huaixi had been given trouble by the Old Madam's matron that morning, now, sitting across from this grandmother, she couldn't detect a trace of displeasure in her.

The maidservant soon brought the tea.

Directly across from Lu Huaixi sat Lady Xie, who watched her lift the teacup with a warm, gracious smile.

Beside Lady Xie sat the Marquis of Chengen—his face carrying some fatigue, yet still radiating the gravity of a man long accustomed to high station.

After her engagement, Lu Huaixi had heard a few things about the marquis' household—she knew that the Marquis had been drawn into a case about a year ago, had come close to imprisonment, and had nearly lost his life in proving his innocence.

The case had eventually been resolved, but something of the Emperor's displeasure had taken root.

She had also heard, by chance, that the case had originally had nothing to do with the Marquis—that it was he who had insisted on inserting himself into it, bringing the trouble upon himself.

She didn't know the reasons behind it, nor could she confirm what was true and what wasn't. But she could feel that when Xie Yuanjing faced his father, the flat line of his lips spoke only of cold indifference.

"Father, please have some tea. Mother, please have some tea."

Lu Huaixi lowered her head and offered the cups alongside Xie Yuanjing.

Lady Xie was evidently very pleased, appearing entirely satisfied with the match.

Lu Huaixi saw this and smiled warmly in return, her reply appropriate and fitting—giving as good as she received.

But when it came to the Marquis, she composed herself a little and only maintained the proper level of courtesy—head bowed, listening attentively while he spoke.

The Marquis, perhaps still recovering, didn't linger long after his gifts had been given. When he rose, he pressed a fist to his lips and coughed at length, then looked at the younger generation before him and offered a few more words of counsel before departing.

No one in the hall found anything out of place, and Lu Huaixi could see that the Marquis's health was genuinely still on the mend.

She thought little more of it—but Xie Yuanjing, in the brief lull of the conversation ahead, leaned slightly and murmured near her.

"He is still resting and convalescing. He holds no displeasure toward anyone."

Xie Yuanjing's head turned just slightly, his thin lips very close to her ear.

Lu Huaixi blinked, and after a moment understood that "he" meant the Marquis.

"I know."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing asked, "Were you afraid of him just now?"

She had no idea why he would ask that. She shook her head. "I wasn't afraid. My father sometimes looks more severe than the Marquis."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing—but his gaze fell squarely on her, clearly having noticed the difference in how she had treated the two.

Sensing that he was waiting, Lu Huaixi drew a quiet breath and lowered her eyes.

"I noticed you seemed unhappy."

They were father and son, after all. She caught herself and immediately revised: "Not unhappy—I noticed you seemed a little serious."

She thought about it, then looked up at him again, earnest. "We're on the same side. I'll naturally follow your lead. If I ever follow wrong, tell me."

Xie Yuanjing hadn't expected that to be the reason. He still said nothing—but the gaze he turned on Lu Huaixi held a brief, quiet depth.

Something odd seemed to flicker in the air between them, and when their eyes met, it felt—inexplicably—less easy than usual.

But before Lu Huaixi had a chance to think about what felt off, laughter sounded from beside them.

"All right, I know you just got married yesterday—but there are still people waiting for you to pour tea up front! Save the sweetness for your own room!"

At that, Lu Huaixi looked over and felt the tips of her ears heat.

The speaker was the Second Branch's wife of the Xie family—she had met her at the flower-viewing gathering, a woman who smiled warmly and spoke frankly.

Seeing her tease them, Lu Huaixi had no time to dwell on Xie Yuanjing's expression from a moment ago. She pressed her lips together and moved to the front, waiting for the maidservant to hand over the tea.

Xie Yuanjing had just pulled himself from his previous thoughts. He glanced at her obedient, well-behaved demeanor and found it rather amusing.

"Why so far away—come here."

He drew her by the wrist, and when he let go, the two of them were standing close enough that any movement at all would brush against her sleeve.

"My second aunt and mother are close friends. No ill intent."

"Oh, good."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes, quietly filing the second branch into her "possible to befriend" list.

"Is there anyone else? What about the others?"

A maidservant brought fresh tea, and Xie Yuanjing accepted it alongside her. "Others too. We'll talk more when we get back."

"All right."

The people sitting at the head of the table were the Xie household's Old Master and Old Madam.

Compared to the Marquis from earlier, Lu Huaixi felt that the Old Master carried an even weightier presence of someone long accustomed to high station.

She glanced at him once, then called out "Grandfather" and "Grandmother" along with Xie Yuanjing.

Just as she was about to offer the tea, a small stir came from nearby, and then someone entered and stopped beside the Old Madam.

Maidservants moved in and out of the hall occasionally—that was nothing unusual—and Lu Huaixi hadn't paid it much mind at first. But this newcomer's dress and hair were nothing like a servant's, and while her garments were simple, the fabric was fine quality.

And yet, if she was a daughter of the household, she had taken her place behind the Old Madam—leaning in to say something, in a familiar, easy way, with no intention of being seated.

Lu Huaixi quickly withdrew her gaze.

Xie Yuanjing had spared the newcomer not a single glance.

After finishing with this pair of elders, he led Lu Huaixi in a full round of introductions until she had drunk so many cups of tea she was nearly full. Only then was every branch of the Xie family accounted for.

But Lu Huaixi had not grown impatient.

She had kept her eyes curved with a smile throughout. With each gift received, that smile grew a fraction warmer, and those watching couldn't help but start to tease.

"Sister-in-law, the way you're smiling—you look like a little money-lover. Has Big Brother been withholding your allowance?"

"What are you saying? Don't be rude to your sister-in-law."

The speaker was Xie family's fourth daughter, Xie Zhenyin—a daughter of the second branch, about the same age as Lu Huaixi.

The words were barely out before the second branch's wife reached over and tapped her affectionately.

But she was utterly undaunted and only laughed more.

"I'm saying Big Brother and Sister-in-law are well matched!"

Fourth daughter Xie Zhenyin said her piece, then winked at Lu Huaixi. "Sister-in-law definitely didn't marry the wrong person marrying Big Brother."

"Why is that?"

Seeing her speak so brightly—and being in the more approachable second branch—Lu Huaixi let herself relax a little.

Though she was briefly thrown by hearing herself called "Sister-in-law," she recovered quickly and smiled back, head tilted. "Because I'm a money-lover?"

"Exactly—Big Brother has plenty of money, and he's perfect for a money-lover."

Xie Zhenyin continued, "Big Brother doesn't spend much normally. He's either working or disciplining people. Sometimes I used to worry—what's to be done with all that money?"

"Is that so—"

Lu Huaixi glanced back at Xie Yuanjing with mock solemnity. Seeing he didn't seem particularly bothered, she let herself go a little further.

"Then I'll come and spend it from now on."

After saying it, she still felt a touch uncertain and couldn't help asking Xie Yuanjing directly.

"Is that all right?"

When Lu Huaixi smiled, the outer corners of her eyes dropped slightly—her bright dark pupils like glass beads laced with morning dew, clear and lovely.

Now she tilted her head just slightly, bold and yet carrying the faintest note of regret, as if she half-wished she hadn't let her mouth run away with her.

Yet nothing showed too plainly on her face—she just watched him with those earnest, wistful eyes. Like a child who knows she's made a small mistake but still hopes to be praised for it—impossible to find fault with.

Xie Yuanjing was in rare good form around her.

He watched her, and when she was on the verge of deflating, gave a slow, easy nod with a quiet smile.

"It's fine."

He said, unhurried: "What is mine is yours."

Beside them, Xie Zhenyin blinked—then, after a beat, allowed herself to believe what she had just heard.

Rarely having seen her Big Brother this agreeable, she was the first to push forward. "Then I'm joining in—Sister-in-law, don't forget about me!"

The hall grew livelier by the moment. The assembled wives took no pleasure in dampening things and chatted among themselves at the front, making no effort to interrupt the younger generation—even the Old Madam didn't speak up to scold them, only sat with her tea.

It was Xie Yuanjing who found things getting rather noisy. He stepped forward to take Lu Huaixi away.

"All right. She can. The rest of you cannot."

"..."

Though they knew it was in jest, the younger girls didn't quite dare make a fuss at Xie Yuanjing.

Even Xie Zhenyin could only pull a face at Lu Huaixi and hold back from pushing further.

Lu Huaixi found the whole thing delightful and was just about to toss a word back to Xie Zhenyin when she felt an odd gaze fall on her.

She looked up sharply—and caught, right at that moment, the unfurrowed brow of the girl who had been standing behind the Old Madam.

She looked like she was feeling some displeasure—some unhappiness.

That was rather curious.

Lu Huaixi withdrew her gaze quickly, and something suddenly clicked into place in her mind.

Could this be the one her brother had mentioned—the moon right next to his window that no one had managed to catch?

chapters.title: Be a Little More Imperious
chapters.content:
Once the tea-pouring was done, Xie Yuanjing quickly led her away from the main hall.

Lu Huaixi was belatedly realizing she probably shouldn't have said all of that—but before she could think it through, the person beside her had already pulled her thoughts elsewhere.

"In the future, if they invite you over there again, just decline. Tell them I said no."

He had said this a good while ago and still hadn't heard a response. He looked back, and saw the small girl staring off into space—expression troubled, the look of someone who genuinely couldn't figure something out.

He watched for a moment. Seeing that crease between her brows still hadn't relaxed, and her half-lidded eyes weren't watching the path, he slowed his pace.

There were a few stone steps at the end of the covered walkway. Xie Yuanjing simply watched as she lifted her foot and missed the step entirely—her eyes going wide as she lurched forward. He was quiet for a moment—and at the last possible second, reached out and caught her.

Once Lu Huaixi had her footing back and the fear had set in, he let go and came to stand at her side.

"Learned your lesson?"

They were very close. Xie Yuanjing could still feel the warmth radiating through her waist.

Lu Huaixi's attention wasn't on the hand he had just released. She only lightly patted her own chest, and when she turned her head to look at him, there was still unspent fright in her eyes.

Below the steps was a stone-paved path. The stones had been polished somewhat, but they were still hard and unforgiving.

If she had truly fallen, her face would have been damaged—and her head likely wouldn't have fared much better.

"You were watching me that whole time?"

Lu Huaixi spoke to him, tilting her head back.

"Yes. Waiting to watch you fall."

"But you caught me in the end."

The muttered words carried a trace of mild complaint—and yet, remembering he had caught her, it wasn't a real grievance. "You could have said something sooner."

Xie Yuanjing found this amusing.

"Not watching the path, nearly falling, and somehow it becomes someone else's fault?"

Lu Huaixi's lips pressed together lightly. "I didn't."

Passing servants caught a glimpse of the eldest young master and the young mistress standing together—one looking up to speak, one looking down to listen, patient and unhurried—and were quietly taken aback.

But however startled, none of them dared take a long, obvious look.

By the time Lu Huaixi noticed people bowing and passing again, she felt a little self-conscious. She composed herself.

"Let's go."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing made a sound of agreement but didn't move. "What were you thinking about just now?"

"...Nothing."

"Can't say?"

Of course she couldn't say.

Lu Huaixi turned her head away and said vaguely, "Let's go—I'm hungry. You had lunch already. I haven't."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her, and the corner of his mouth curved again.

Then he raised his hand and gave her head a light knock. He didn't press further.

"Watch the path from now on."

"I know, I know."

—

Back at the Lu household, not even a full day after Lu Huaixi's departure, the first branch felt considerably quieter.

The eldest daughter, Lu Ningyou, worried her mother wasn't adjusting well and had come over from her husband's family to keep her company, her voice warm and unhurried.

She knew perfectly well that her sister had not had any prior engagement—Lady Liu hadn't tried to hide it from her. But she had spared her the other details, afraid of burdening her.

"Mother, Huaixi getting married is a happy occasion. Don't work yourself into a state like this. You know what that girl is like—she manages to find joy wherever she ends up. Do you really think she'll be mistreated?"

That was easy to say—but Lu Huaixi was still so young, and her relationship with that Xie eldest was only newly begun. Lu Ningyou was hardly worry-free.

"Yesterday the Xie eldest son's procession was there for everyone to see. You can't say Huaixi isn't valued. And Mother—you don't know this, but even my in-laws, who never pay attention to gossip, were talking about the Xie eldest son, saying he was clearly someone who had put genuine care into it."

Lady Liu's lips moved, but she said nothing.

She could hardly tell her eldest daughter: your sister's is a pretend marriage, and a year from now they'll formally dissolve it.

"Mother, please stop fretting. Meeting someone, getting married—that's how it goes for most women. And Huaixi's got a husband of fine family and good looks, from the marquis' household no less. Besides, I could see yesterday—Huaixi trusted him, the two of them were fine."

"They were... all right?"

"Yes, Mother."

Lu Ningyou smiled. "Yesterday my brother-in-law made a point of going to speak to Huaixi personally—had her laughing a good few times. People say he's hard to read and difficult to get along with—I didn't get that impression at all. At least not in front of Huaixi."

"That I didn't see."

Lady Liu sighed—though his words had also eased some of her worry.

She wasn't unaware that fretting was useless, and the marriage was done. Her task now was to be her daughter's support.

But a mother couldn't help it. Her daughter had been pushed into a rushed marriage to avoid the palace, with a dissolution looming afterward—no matter how she turned it over, she couldn't swallow the injustice.

"I hope they do well together. But you know your sister—she looks gentle and easy on the surface, which fools people well enough. In reality she's quite a handful. And the Xie eldest with his cold temperament..."

"Don't worry, Mother. From what I could see, my brother-in-law treats Huaixi very well. Cold temperament? Those two will warm up to each other for quite a few years."

"..."

Lady Liu felt more unsettled than before.

The dissolution was inevitable. She had never imagined that someone like Xie Yuanjing would change his mind, or that the two families would remain as in-laws.

But Huaixi was in the haze of youth. She didn't know—with time spent alongside Xie Yuanjing, whether she might come to feel something.

"Never mind that. Their business is something outsiders can't interfere in. I just worry—the marquis' household isn't entirely peaceful inside."

"Every inner household has its murky corners. Even our own Lu family—"

Something seemed to occur to her, and Lu Ningyou's expression cooled.

"I never imagined the second branch, mother and daughter both, could harbor such vicious plans. Has Grandfather's side sent any word?"

That question dimmed Lady Liu's face.

The Old Master did love Lu Huaixi dearly and had resolved to protect her—but the second branch were Lu family too.

Learning that the first branch wouldn't back down, the Old Master had turned around and tried to mediate.

At the end of the day, he couldn't bring himself to send either granddaughter off.

Lady Liu understood his dilemma. But she could not relent—and she could not simply let her daughter's suffering pass without consequence.

Her Huaixi should have had a few more peaceful years at home—slowly looking, slowly choosing, waiting for the right feeling to come naturally.

All of that had been ruined by the second branch.

Not only had she been driven to marry far too young—she would also end up with the name of a dissolved marriage to carry. No matter how she thought about it, Lady Liu couldn't swallow the bitterness.

"Whether or not your grandfather sends word, the second branch is not getting away with this unscathed."

"Of course. If there's anything I can help with, Mother, please tell me."

Lu Ningyou's expression hardened, and she thought of a matron who had come yesterday to tell her that Lu Tangshu had actually attempted to stop Xie Yuanjing. She gave a cold laugh.

What extraordinary presumption.

On that alone—regardless of whether the Xie eldest was right for Huaixi—Lu Tangshu would not be getting off easily.

"That's enough. I just wanted to say it to you. Mind your own health. I worry about Huaixi, and I worry about you too."

"Don't worry, Mother. My in-laws and husband treat me well."

"I can see that. If they weren't easy to deal with, they wouldn't keep letting you go off on your own so often. Sit a while and then go back—don't be out too long."

"No rush. My husband is coming to collect me when his duties are finished."

At that, Lu Ningyou smiled, expression softening.

"I just can't come back for Huaixi's return visit—what a pity. It would have been nice to talk to her properly."

"Stay home and keep still."

Lady Liu looked at her elder daughter's belly and shook her head. "She listens to you. You're her elder sister—you'll have to set her a good example."

"Goes without saying."

Lu Ningyou blinked, thinking of the small box of books she had privately slipped to her sister, and laughed again.

Mother had said privately that Huaixi was young, and that the Xie eldest wouldn't do anything to her.

But some things—even if it was a little early—better to teach than not.

chapters.title: Well, You Are Very Kind
chapters.content:
Lady Xie's words ended there—but the expression she'd worn was enough to leave the meddlesome Third Madam feeling put out.

Mu Nianwei had barely steadied herself when she looked up and saw the Old Madam, ahead of her, sink into thought—seemingly prompted by the first branch's words.

Her heart sank.

Her background was an undeniable shortcoming she couldn't change. But she couldn't actually allow the Old Madam to come around to favoring that Lu family woman.

Immediately she went over and took her by the arm, lowering her voice.

"Grandaunt, please don't upset yourself. It was Nianwei who shouldn't have come to deliver the medicine patch at such a time. Just now Nianwei should have excused herself earlier—but she heard Sister-in-law say she wanted to spend her husband's money, and was so startled that she forgot herself and stayed."

Hearing that, the Old Madam's expression shifted at once.

Now that she thought of it, she was also a little displeased.

What young wife of a good family would say so openly, right after the wedding, that she intended to spend her husband's money? Clearly a girl raised without discipline.

"No need for you to apologize for it."

"I know Grandaunt cares for me. But since Third Aunt brought me up, I couldn't very well not explain. And just now, Nianwei was here first—I should have withdrawn."

She continued, "Let me escort Grandaunt back to the room first. Today you waited so long for Sister-in-law, and you've been sitting with a sore back without any medicine—please don't keep sitting, or it'll be worse. Let me go with you for a walk through the courtyard later."

The Old Madam gave a heavy sound of acknowledgment and left. On her way out, she looked at her eldest daughter-in-law with an unfavorable expression.

When they stepped outside the courtyard, the Old Madam's footsteps suddenly stopped, and she turned to give instructions to a nearby person.

"Go and summon Yuanjing's wife to my courtyard."

"Let me go, Grandaunt."

Mu Nianwei took over, concealing what she felt. "I should properly greet Sister-in-law as well—so we don't remain strangers in our own family."

The Old Madam considered briefly, then nodded.

"I need to rest for a while. Tell her to come after she's had her morning meal."

—

Lu Huaixi wound her way around the first branch's grounds, walking and pausing, and finally neared Xie Yuanjing's courtyard.

Yaoshu had been beside her talking the whole way. The two of them only stopped when they spotted a figure waiting ahead.

"Nianwei greets Sister-in-law."

The moment Lu Huaixi drew close, the girl bowed gracefully.

She wore her hair in a young woman's style, with simple, clean cosmetics. The single emerald plum blossom hairpin was striking, and as she dipped into the bow, her pale garments fell in natural folds, the hem sweeping to cover her shoes.

It was the girl who had been standing behind the Old Madam in the main hall earlier.

Lu Huaixi looked at her and asked with genuine curiosity, "Sister-in-law?"

Mu Nianwei kept her head lowered, and at those words gave a faint smile. "Yes. The Old Madam of this household is my grandaunt. She brought me to the marquis' household to raise by her side when I was ten. Since then I grew up alongside my cousin."

Grew up with Xie Yuanjing.

Lu Huaixi nodded, and once again matched this person to the one her brother had mentioned.

But having made the connection, she suddenly felt that the situation was a little tricky.

She wore the head wife's title—but she had no intention of severing Xie Yuanjing's connections.

Especially since she had no idea what weight this person carried in Xie Yuanjing's heart. What if it were a case of deep feeling that couldn't be made formal? If so, the next year was likely to be eventful.

"Are you here looking for your cousin?"

Lu Huaixi looked at her. "He's gone out. Would you like to come back later?"

The words were said so naturally they left Mu Nianwei momentarily at a loss.

She had imagined countless versions of this encounter—but not once had she pictured being told to come back later, as though it simply didn't register.

"Sister-in-law—you truly don't mind me seeing my cousin?"

"Why would I mind? Come to see him whenever you like—you're family here, no need for a calling card. Just—not today. I won't invite you in now, since he's not here."

Mu Nianwei found herself at a loss again.

She looked at the woman before her, searching for some performance of generosity masking hidden bitterness.

There was none. Only a lovely, youthful face—and a pair of open, unhurried eyes.

Some things can't be compared. The moment a comparison is made, the one who comes up shorter has built their own cage.

"Sister-in-law misunderstands. I didn't come today for my cousin."

Mu Nianwei steadied herself and met Lu Huaixi's gaze with a lowered-eye smile.

"My cousin would not want to see me. I came because Grandaunt wishes to invite Sister-in-law to visit."

"Now?"

"Yes."

She made no mention of the Old Madam needing to rest first, and simply stepped to one side. "Please, Sister-in-law—do not keep Grandaunt waiting again."

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed slightly. She found this visitor's manner a little disagreeable.

Nothing too overtly rude had been said—but something about the air around her made Lu Huaixi uncomfortable.

Though it was possible she was just hungry.

Her appetite wasn't enormous, but she needed to eat at every meal. Missing a meal made her irritable.

"A little later."

Lu Huaixi's thoughts turned briefly—she recalled the matron the Old Madam had sent to lecture her that morning, and Xie Yuanjing's response.

"I can't get away just yet. My husband said to go back to the court and meet the household staff."

"But Grandaunt—"

"I'll go over a little later and apologize to Grandmother myself. After all, it's the first branch's business—I imagine Grandmother won't take offense."

Lu Huaixi's voice was soft and gentle, her lovely face looking entirely guileless and innocent.

But her answer to Mu Nianwei carried an unmistakable finality—leaving no room to press further.

After a moment, Mu Nianwei smiled again.

"Sister-in-law is right. My cousin's instructions come first."

Then she added, "Since I'm here, I should also explain something—about those boots that were sent over last night."

So the boots were from her.

Lu Huaixi felt a brief flicker of surprise—but quickly understood.

"My cousin is rather particular about shoes. I once promised to make him a pair—but I never found the right opportunity. There was a misunderstanding afterward, and the matter was put aside... If Sister-in-law happened to see those boots yesterday, please don't take it to heart."

"I won't."

Lu Huaixi's lips curved, easy and unhurried.

The boots had already been thrown out. There was nothing left to take to heart.

And besides, the boots, as far as she could tell, weren't the sort of style someone who was "particular about shoes" would actually wear.

"I'm glad Sister-in-law isn't bothered. A few days ago I was with the Old Madam listening to some rumors from outside, and I kept trying to tell her that Sister-in-law would surely not be that kind of spoiled person—that once you arrived, you'd put the marquis' household and my cousin first in everything."

"Well, you are very kind."

"..."

After that, whatever Mu Nianwei said, the response she received was the same unhurried, unbothered warmth.

Like a fist thrown into cotton—the force of it bounced back against herself.

Mu Nianwei gradually lost patience. She had no more desire to linger.

Lu Huaixi had more or less read her intentions, but had no plans to expose them.

After Mu Nianwei left, the only one whose expression changed was Yaoshu.

She watched that retreating figure with wary eyes.

"Young Miss—Young Mistress, that cousin came specifically to look you over, and she was saying things designed to land, one way or another. She's clearly up to no good. Please don't let your guard down—you can never be too careful."

"She came specifically to look me over? More like she came to see Xie Yuanjing."

"...Which is exactly why you need to be on guard, Young Mistress."

Yaoshu fell into step behind her. "And I don't know what the Old Madam wants calling you over now. That matron this morning was obviously not an easy one. You need to be careful when you go later..."

"Don't worry. I'll take my time getting there."

Lu Huaixi withdrew her gaze and walked into the courtyard.

She wasn't so possessive as to truly sever someone's match. But she certainly wasn't going to go out of her way to be obliging either, especially when she found this person disagreeable to be around.

Whether to be civil to someone—that depended on Xie Yuanjing's thoughts.

After all, in the entire marquis' household, only he and she were on the same boat.

"Hungry."

Lu Huaixi gave a quiet sigh.

Married into a new family, and she couldn't even get a proper breakfast. She was really about to make a fuss.

chapters.title: Don't Talk About My Wife Behind Her Back
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing arrived early.

The plan had originally been a gathering at Shen Zhoushu's villa on the outskirts, but it was a bit far and the day had turned warm, so they had relocated to the Juexian Pavilion in the city.

When Xie Yuanjing was shown into the private room, Shen Zhoushu and Qin Yiyun had already arrived.

One was telling the other about possible hardships and heartfelt ambitions for the years ahead across great distances. The other was listening with half-lidded, faintly sleepy eyes.

At the sight of the newcomer, both turned to look.

"Brother Yuanjing is here. Inviting Brother Yuanjing out on the second day of your wedding—we hope the young mistress won't hold it against us."

The speaker was Qin Yiyun—upright in character, with a slight stiffness to him.

His reassignment had arrived somewhat late, and he had been held up by something else in the days prior—it was only right before his departure that he'd been able to breathe.

He and Xie Yuanjing had not originally had much in common, but Qin Yiyun had a way of getting fixated on things. He felt that Xie Yuanjing had learning and insight, and so had refused to let him go—until in the end, Xie Yuanjing had begrudgingly developed something like a collegial fondness for him.

The one beside him was Shen Zhoushu—the man from the carriage that day, one of the few Xie Yuanjing could genuinely call a friend.

He hadn't originally planned to come to this gathering, but hearing that Xie Yuanjing had agreed, he decided to join the fun.

Seeing the man arrive now, the drowsiness around Shen Zhoushu's brow lifted.

"The great Xie eldest marries and things change—even evening wine banquets get moved to daytime."

Thinking of yesterday, he couldn't resist a jab. "I thought our great Xie eldest didn't care about the business of taking a wife—yet yesterday he somehow managed to put on quite a procession. I imagine even the palace has heard about it by now..."

Xie Yuanjing was entirely unbothered by the mockery.

He stepped into the room. The expression on his otherwise unreadable face had a brief, unexpected smile.

Then he found a seat, picked up the fresh cup of wine set before him, and raised it toward Qin Yiyun.

After drinking, he set the cup down and casually wiped his fingertips with the cloth beside him, the whole bearing exuding an effortless, somewhat imperious ease.

"If one is to take a wife, of course one takes it seriously."

He lowered his gaze—tone quiet and unaffected.

Qin Yiyun had been briefly called away by an attendant. With the private room briefly empty, Shen Zhoushu dropped any pretense.

"You're telling me this is the same person who said it was mutually convenient and just going through the motions?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't reply, as if too lazy to engage.

Shen Zhoushu had been irritable since waking too early, and seeing this only made it worse.

"Who said he hated fanfare—said he wasn't going to make a big occasion of it?"

"Who said that?"

Xie Yuanjing returned, and reached for the teacup beside him, pouring himself a cup.

Shen Zhoushu was briefly stopped in his tracks, just gearing up for more, when Qin Yiyun pushed the door open and came back in, others following.

With the room filling up, Shen Zhoushu reined himself in and said no more.

"To be able to share one last gathering with good friends before departing the capital—this is a great fortune for Qin."

Qin Yiyun raised his cup after sitting. "This parting may mean years of distance and unknown hardships ahead. I have been helped and supported by each of you in my time here—allow me to offer this first cup to you all."

This wine carried a tinge of sorrow. Those who heard it felt it, and couldn't help a moment's sentiment.

But not Xie Yuanjing. And not Shen Zhoushu.

One had always been coldly indifferent to sentimentality. The other had drunk through half the night and was barely keeping his eyes open.

But no one would pick on these two, so the conversation carried on, and the room gradually livened.

There are few in this world who can fully avoid talk of others, and after several rounds of wine—once the young lords had said their piece about ambition and the wider world—they inevitably turned to gossip.

The man seated next to Qin Yiyun gave a wine-hiccup first, then spoke.

"How come the Shao family's young one isn't here today? I recall Shao's younger brother and Brother Qin are quite close. Did you arrange something for the evening?"

"That couldn't be managed."

Qin Yiyun smiled and waved it off—the wine flowing fast was hitting him fast. "Young Master Shao has had some inconvenience about going out lately. It wasn't right to press the invitation."

"Inconvenient to go out?"

The man asked again. "Could it be that there really was a falling-out with his family?"

With someone else's private business on the table, Qin Yiyun didn't pick it up—but someone else across the table did.

"It really did happen. Who could have guessed Shao's little brother had it in him to fight so hard for love—I hear he's even prepared to throw away his future for that woman."

Xie Yuanjing still said nothing—still uninterested.

Shen Zhoushu had more of the seven human emotions than him, and when something interesting came up, he'd occasionally add a word or two. But this particular subject he couldn't contribute to—and couldn't understand.

"Wasn't he engaged to someone? How's that going nowhere now?"

"There's nowhere, because he never agreed in the first place. Says he absolutely must marry whoever he likes—only the one he likes happens to be a singer, which is a bit low in standing to take in even as a concubine."

Shen Zhoushu gave a quiet snort and shook his head along with the others.

He might have seemed a bit careless, but he and Xie Yuanjing were fundamentally the same type.

Power and standing, securely in hand—that was the only thing that was truly reassuring.

And besides, such things were hardly impossible to arrange—wait for the marriage to be settled and the footing to be firm, then bring the girl back to the inner household. They could still be together day after day.

"Stubbornness now, regret later."

Shen Zhoushu finished and turned to Xie Yuanjing. "What do you think?"

"Think about what?"

"Throwing away your future for a woman, throwing caution to the wind for love—can you understand it?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet answer, then called out for his attendant Gong Zhuo, and added: "But I don't need to understand it. I don't have that kind of conflict."

"...Right—you've married your noble wife and all that."

Shen Zhoushu gave a somewhat ill-tempered laugh, then dropped his voice.

"A fine wife married not out of feeling, where neither gets close to the other. Heaven falls down and our great Xie eldest will never have a day of fighting-mad devotion for anyone."

"You already know—why ask?"

"Just want to know—don't you genuinely envy people's moonlit courtyard nights, a beauty beside them with a glass of wine?"

The reply was a faint, dismissive laugh—as though the question hadn't been worth taking seriously.

"No need. Don't envy it."

Then Xie Yuanjing extended his right hand and rapped his knuckles lightly on the table in front of Shen Zhoushu.

"In public—don't talk about my wife."

As the words landed, Gong Zhuo arrived and stepped to his side.

"Master."

Xie Yuanjing withdrew his gaze. "Go to the kitchen and ask for a serving of sweet pastries. Add a few other light snacks and cakes and have them wrapped up. If I haven't come downstairs within the hour, have them sent back to the household first."

Gong Zhuo paused briefly—then understood it must be for the young mistress.

He gave a quick nod and withdrew to one side.

Xie Yuanjing had no taste for sweets, and had never been this thoughtful—Shen Zhoushu opened his mouth to say something, remembered the warning just given, and swallowed it back.

Fine.

He said nothing. What was there to say? Looking after a child—bringing home a little snack, that wasn't anything.

chapters.title: Soft Blade, Met With Soft Blade
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had finished meeting the household staff and listening to Gong Fei's long account of what Xie Yuanjing held—by the end of which she decided she couldn't drag it out any further, and set off for the Old Madam's courtyard.

She had eaten something earlier, but not much. By the time she had walked some distance, she was feeling peckish again.

"Young Mistress, that courtyard is just ahead."

This time, Lu Huaixi had brought Jingshuang with her.

When she had been half-asleep getting up that morning, she hadn't paid close attention. But later, when Jingshuang came to serve her, she noticed: Jingshuang never crowded out Yaoshu's closeness, and never spoke out of turn—she simply stood quietly behind her, watchful for anything that needed a hand, stepping in with neat efficiency. It was deeply comfortable to be around.

Lu Huaixi had found herself looking at Jingshuang a second time.

A slightly spirited face—hair swept up high, cheeks a little lean, but with bright eyes and a high-bridged nose. When she was silent, the set of her mouth was just slightly taut, lending her a touch of severity. But when she spoke to Lu Huaixi, her voice softened, and if she smiled—the sternness gave way, and something warm and reassuring took its place.

"Young Mistress, please don't worry. If the Old Madam tries to make trouble for you, just turn and leave—no need to give it a second thought."

Lu Huaixi nodded, then turned to look at her.

"If someone tries to block me, you can take care of them, can't you?"

"I can. With me here, Young Mistress has nothing to fear."

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but laugh.

Perhaps she was the only person in the world who had just married and was already thinking about coming to blows with her husband's family elders.

As she was musing, a matron appeared ahead—and looked faintly surprised to see her.

"This old servant greets the eldest young mistress."

The newcomer was nothing like the one from that morning—she bowed properly, with respect. "The Old Madam has not yet woken from her rest. Young Mistress has come quite early—it may be a little longer."

"Early?"

A look of puzzlement crossed Lu Huaixi's eyes.

More than an hour had passed since Mu Nianwei left—and the Old Madam had apparently already been waiting to see her when Nianwei came. She had taken her time before coming, and now she was early?

"Yes—Young Mistress may not know, but our Old Madam does genuinely sleep when she says she's resting."

The matron said gently while stepping aside. "The courtyard is sunny—please come inside and have some tea first. The Old Madam should be awake shortly. This old servant will go check."

Lu Huaixi understood perfectly.

She followed the woman inside, her smile faint and thin.

How quickly they'd come for her.

Once the matron had withdrawn, Lu Huaixi sat in her place. The tea beside her was a little hot—she didn't touch it, letting her thoughts drift with the steam.

"The Old Madam already wanted to see you—and then had that cousin come to summon you—and then made you sit here and wait? This is deliberate, isn't it?"

Yaoshu, without others around, was barely keeping her temper.

Lu Huaixi showed no emotion whatsoever—just gave a soft, unhurried acknowledgment.

"Isn't it just that. Bullying me."

Fortunately she had delayed earlier. If she had come when first summoned, she would have been caught—no way to wait and no way to leave.

Wait, and it was the Old Madam putting the new bride in her place. It reflected on the whole first branch, not just Lu Huaixi.

Don't wait, and she was guilty of disrespect—anyone who brought it up would have nothing to say.

But whether this was the Old Madam's idea or Mu Nianwei's, Lu Huaixi hadn't yet worked out.

"Miss, you've been wronged."

"'Wronged'? Don't call me 'Miss'—you're meant to call me 'Young Mistress.'"

When Lu Huaixi looked up at Yaoshu, her eyes had come back to life.

The reassurance was plain and open—voice still carrying a tone of ease—like someone who didn't take being maneuvered against the slightest bit seriously.

Jingshuang nearby glanced over at her quietly, saw no trace of any forced composure—only a fair, clear face, not a flicker of negativity—and felt something at the corner of her own mouth shift.

Then she said softly: "Young Mistress, you could leave."

"I won't."

Lu Huaixi waved a hand, entirely at ease.

"If I leave now, how does that look? I'd be handing them something to use against me. I'm not making a loss like that."

Then she gave a small sound of pique—like a child digging in their heels, refusing to be bested. "I'm going to complain to Xie Yuanjing about this when I see him."

It was a funny thing to say—but Lu Huaixi had no real intention of making trouble.

If she had truly been Xie Yuanjing's wife, she might have had genuine grievances to air—toward the Old Madam, or toward that cousin.

But she wasn't. Plainly put, she was just a temporary guest in the household. She had no heart for petty squabbles.

If there was any real displeasure, it was that no sooner had the year begun than someone was already looking to make her life difficult and disturb her peace.

"Oh well—so I've been played a little. It's nothing."

Lu Huaixi picked up her tea, smiling as she muttered.

She wasn't actually bothered—those words were meant deliberately for Yaoshu to hear. She didn't want Yaoshu worrying for her, and from there her mother worrying needlessly.

As she was speaking, sounds came from the inner room—a soft stir, accompanied by a few coughs.

Lu Huaixi looked over—and then a figure entered from outside and moved straight toward the inner room, the movement a little hasty.

As if she hadn't noticed Lu Huaixi sitting there. Or as if she was deliberately making a show of her importance in this place.

"Grandaunt, you've woken up."

The voice sounded from within, full of worry.

"How is your back? Today you waited for Sister-in-law so long, and you didn't have the medicine patch on—please don't keep sitting once we're done here. Tonight I'll walk with you through the courtyard for a while."

Hearing it was Mu Nianwei—and hearing the words land squarely on her again—Lu Huaixi felt no more urgency. She leisurely reached for the teacup.

Only when the bead curtain stirred did she rise and look at the newcomer, dipping into a slight bow. "Granddaughter-in-law greets Grandmother."

The Old Madam had just woken—her throat dry. At the sound, she gave only a brief sound of acknowledgment and accepted the warm water handed to her, drinking a sip.

She settled, and only once she was seated again did her expression carry a more alert quality.

"Have you been here long?"

"In reply to Grandmother—only just arrived."

Lu Huaixi smiled, as if a little apologetic.

"I was more than an hour late arriving—I truly didn't know how to make it up to you. It was just that I couldn't get away from the other side. I hope Grandmother won't be cross."

"Not late at all. Just right."

The Old Madam's expression was somewhat severe, but her tone was adequate. "Had you come earlier I'd have been resting anyway. I tire easily at my age."

"As long as you're not upset."

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Just now, the Young Miss Nianwei asked me to come right away—and didn't mention that Grandmother was going to rest first. I was worried for a moment—fortunately Grandmother doesn't blame me."

Mu Nianwei heard this and looked over at once.

She had indeed set a trap deliberately—hoping to make Lu Huaixi lose face, to make it look as though the Old Madam had no patience for the new bride and was already putting her in her place.

She had also prepared herself for the possibility that if it came to light, she could push the blame back onto Lu Huaixi—say she'd misunderstood, or that Lu Huaixi had done it on purpose.

But Lu Huaixi had refused her outright. Smilingly.

And before Mu Nianwei had time to think of anything to add in front of the Old Madam, Lu Huaixi had simply gone ahead and said it herself.

Soft on the outside, blade on the inside—delivered with a smile.

The Old Madam heard it and was silent for a moment—then looked up at the figure before her with a faintly probing quality in her eyes.

Lu Huaixi seemed to notice nothing, meeting her gaze openly with a wide, clear smile.

After a moment, the Old Madam stepped back first.

"It was probably Nianwei who didn't explain clearly. Nothing serious—I just had her invite you over for a sit-down. Where is Yuanjing?"

"In reply to Grandmother—he's gone out. A colleague of his."

The two women's expressions both shifted—one going still, the other moving from irritation to barely-concealed satisfaction.

Lu Huaixi pretended not to notice either—and kept her smile fixed on the Old Madam.
