chapters.title: My Wife's Account—I'll Settle It With You Slowly
chapters.content:
The last trace of expression left Xie Yuanjing's face. His bearing was cold and imperious, a flicker of danger glinting in his brow—yet his voice remained perfectly measured, each word delivered without haste, his manner as unruffled as someone discussing the weather.

"And—the matter of the attempt to send her to the palace. I will settle that account with you slowly."

Lu Tangshu went white.

Perhaps she had not expected Xie Yuanjing to name it outright, or had not expected him to stand up for Lu Huaixi this firmly.

For a moment she couldn't produce a single word. Only then did the fear and dread rush in all at once.

There was no one beside her, and even if there had been, no one would have dared come to her aid.

In her panic, Lu Tangshu looked toward Lu Huaixi, pleading—every trace of the resentment she had been harbouring moments ago gone, only naked desperation in her eyes.

"Second Sister, there's been a misunderstanding—please help me. Let me explain..."

Lu Huaixi didn't respond.

She had felt a flash of surprise when Xie Yuanjing openly raised the matter of the palace. But she steadied herself almost immediately.

They were on the same side. If she showed any reaction now, the second branch would read a hundred things into it.

And she had no intention of going soft on Lu Tangshu.

The one who broke the standstill was Old Master Lu, not far away.

After issuing a few instructions, he looked back and saw that Xie Yuanjing was still speaking with his granddaughter. He raised his hand and beckoned.

"Yuanjing, come have tea."

Old Master Lu appeared to have grown genuinely fond of Xie Yuanjing.

What had begun as cautious probing had since shifted into evident regard—warmth visibly more natural than before.

Xie Yuanjing gave a response and then, without any particular effort at concealment, let out a quiet laugh.

It looked like a man sharing a private jest—but the words that followed gave no one face at all.

"Old Master, the quality of education for the young ladies in this household leaves quite a lot to be desired."

Lady Luo was still deep in conversation with Lady Liu and hadn't noticed.

Old Master Lu's gaze rested on Lu Tangshu for a moment, then shifted away without expression—his face changing slightly, though he remained as steady and immovable as ever.

"The girls are young and thoughtless. Put a few of them together and they'll say things they shouldn't. If any offence has been given, I hope Yuanjing will overlook it for Huaixi's sake."

With that, the Old Master looked back toward the side and let his tone carry a note of edge. "Tangshu—go back to your own courtyard!"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing more, but the set of his expression didn't improve.

The Old Master's words had signalled something.

Huaixi was his blood granddaughter. So was the second branch. On a day like this, discretion called for things to be smoothed over.

"Today is a return visit day. In the ordinary way of things, this sort of thing should be set aside and laughed off. But when it concerns my wife, some things can be let go—and some cannot."

Xie Yuanjing had put his displeasure plainly on the table, without dismantling the Old Master's intent—but he had also made his own position clear.

"Whatever grievance my wife has suffered in the past—simply moving past it is not an option."

Lu Yandao, standing to one side, had not opened his mouth until now. But he pressed his brow, then smoothed it, and the look he turned on Xie Yuanjing deepened with meaning.

This wasn't about Lu Tangshu's provocation just now. This was a statement—that the second branch of the Lu family scheming to send Lu Huaixi to the palace would not simply be forgotten.

Xie Yuanjing didn't concern himself with anyone else's reaction.

Having spoken, he looked back at Lu Huaixi, who had been quiet for some time, and let the sharpness ease. The corner of his mouth curved slightly, as though he had entirely forgotten he had just been issuing a warning.

"All right. Go and play."

He squeezed her fingertips once more. "Your mother has been waiting a while."

—

In the back courtyard, Lu Huaixi's room was exactly as it had always been.

Three days really wasn't long enough. Short enough that when Lu Huaixi walked in, she was momentarily confused—as if she wasn't entirely sure whether she'd actually left.

Lady Liu sat down at the front of the room.

She hadn't caught everything that had just happened, but the words Xie Yuanjing had spoken she had heard clearly enough.

Having him take this kind of stand eased the weight that had been sitting in Lady Liu's chest over these three days.

"Just now he came out and said what he said plainly—it means he intends to take the matter in hand and stand up for you. Your father had been worried he might only concern himself with the marriage itself. Now that he's shown his hand, your father and he will likely have considerably more dealings ahead."

Lu Huaixi came back to herself from Xie Yuanjing's defense of her a moment ago, took a beat, then nodded.

It was genuine sincerity—the kind that concerned both families.

She gave a sound of acknowledgment but didn't much feel like saying more.

"Let's not talk about that for now, Mother. Is the second branch asking something of you?"

She steadied her thoughts, set aside what she'd been turning over, and remembered the second Madam's manner toward her today, and the Old Master's reaction. Her brow furrowed slightly.

"Is it about the palace list?"

"Yes, it is."

Lady Liu didn't hide it. She knew her daughter cared about this matter—and she knew that for all the appearance of composure, this girl was not someone who simply bore a grievance in silence.

"The name can't be removed from the list. But Lu Tangshu refuses to go to the palace. Lady Luo doesn't dare make a scene with me directly, so she went to your grandfather first and then through him."

"So Grandfather is also reluctant to send her."

Lady Liu didn't answer immediately, but Lu Huaixi had already guessed the outcome.

It was precisely because the Old Master had relented that Lady Luo had then turned and come to Lady Liu.

As long as the first branch was willing to look the other way rather than press the matter, the second branch still had room to find a solution.

"Yes. Your grandfather was angry—but he wants to protect the Lu family's daughters from entering the palace."

Lady Liu's expression grew cool. "But he wants to protect his granddaughter. I want to protect my daughter. Each of us will make our own move."

"Mother—"

"Though there's also a clever one."

Lady Liu seemed to recall something and added: "Fourth Sister came to find me yesterday."

"Fourth Sister?"

Lu Huaixi was surprised.

"Fourth Sister is lively but timid—she always looks to Lu Tangshu before she does anything. How could she suddenly come to you? Does the second branch know?"

Fourth Miss Lu Sui-dong was the second branch's concubine-born daughter, almost the same age as Lu Tangshu.

Her mother had once been greatly favoured—Lu Huaixi remembered as a child often seeing her second uncle with Lu Sui-dong's mother close at his side.

But then her mother had caused a scene, and Lu Sui-dong had been left out in the cold. To get by, she had been forced to pull in her own nature and endlessly please the principal wife.

Later, when Lu Tangshu couldn't find anyone to play with, she had become something between a companion and a servant—following her around, keeping her company, learning to wait on her.

"Most likely they don't know."

Lady Liu said: "Lady Luo's private methods are severe. Fourth Sister wants to live a peaceful life, so she's had to learn to watch moods. But I only just found out—she has a great deal of nerve."

chapters.title: Just Waiting to Come Home in One Year
chapters.content:
On the day Lu Huaixi had married out, Fourth Miss Lu Sui-dong had been absolutely delighted.

When all the girls gathered together, every one of them had been curious about this unknown second brother-in-law they had yet to see.

Lu Huaixi heard from her eldest sister that on that day, Lu Sui-dong had been so exuberantly happy that she caught the sharp end of Lu Tangshu's tongue—and didn't dare say another word after that.

Now her mother was saying Fourth Sister had nerve—Lu Huaixi found it genuinely difficult to picture the girl sitting quietly and speaking with her mother.

Lady Liu didn't keep her wondering long.

"Once the Flower and Bird Envoy's list became known, almost all the girls in the household had their suspicions. Especially since Lu Tangshu had made such a scene, crying and smashing things—and yesterday Fourth Sister came without any preamble. She went straight to the point: she wants to take her elder sister's place and enter the palace."

"...Was she forced to come by the Second Madam?"

"At first I assumed the same. She and Lu Tangshu may be legitimate and concubine-born, but they're still both of the Lu family. If it came to entering the palace, there are ways to arrange it—but the more I listened, the clearer it became that she wants to go of her own will. And she's hiding it from Lady Luo."

Thinking of those words, Lady Liu let out a soft exhale.

"She had a good childhood once—then she was suppressed and never got back up. It's a hard way to live. I understand what she means. Her marriage will be entirely in Lady Luo's hands—but she doesn't want that. She wants to find her own way out."

"But..."

"She told me plainly—even if this doesn't work out, she'll find another way. She refuses to be handed off to some man's inner household as a concubine, and she refuses to be Lady Luo's good deed. This palace—she is going in."

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long moment.

This fourth sister of hers had always been in close contact with her. Or rather—in the Lu household, apart from Lu Tangshu whose heart had gone crooked, her other sisters had all been reasonably close to her.

But however warm Fourth Sister was toward her, she was still the second branch's concubine-born daughter. Every move she made required watching Lady Luo's face first.

To come behind the second branch's back and petition Lady Liu directly—she must have decided to burn the boat.

"Doesn't she know that going into the palace—life and death would truly be..."

"How could she not know? But she says she doesn't care. Marrying anyone else is also life and death uncertain. And she's not wrong—for any other girl, Lady Luo might play the good person. But for her... it would be difficult."

Hearing that, Lu Huaixi's lips moved.

Lady Luo would likely not find her a particularly good match. The jealousy and hatred Lady Luo had once harboured for that concubine was something even Lu Huaixi had heard about.

Fourth Sister probably knew it too. Which was why, faced with the choice between becoming a concubine herself or suffering through someone's bitter inner household, she had chosen to take a chance.

"Did you agree, Mother?"

"No."

Lady Liu still kept her voice cool. "But her coming to me in secret, without Lady Luo knowing—that reasoning is not without consideration."

"What does that mean? She wants more than just the standing she'd get from entering the palace?"

"Yes. She doesn't want Lu Tangshu to fare well."

Lady Liu said: "She wants my help in getting her into the palace. In return, she would help me deal with Lady Luo and her daughter. Her meaning is that if Lu Tangshu were to enter the palace and be favoured, she would certainly seek revenge—but Fourth Sister would not."

Managing the inner household was not something Lady Liu had ever had any interest in outsourcing to another. And she certainly had no need to bargain with anyone.

If she wanted to stand up for her daughter, she had methods enough—clean ones, without underhanded schemes.

Lu Tangshu had wanted to destroy her daughter's future and climb over her to rise. So she would return the favour.

Send her to the palace to be her "honoured lady"—give her exactly what she wanted. It was a perfectly fine outcome.

But there was also another path.

"Huaixi—what do you think?"

Lady Liu came back to herself and looked at her daughter.

"I want to hear your thoughts first."

"Is it because you think sending her to the palace has risks?" Lu Huaixi replied.

"You don't need to worry about what comes after. The household will handle those considerations."

Lady Liu had thought it through: if Lu Tangshu went to the palace, the Lu family would inevitably be bound to her to some degree. Even if they kept their distance and didn't interfere, she would have her moment of prominence for a while. Looking at it—that was always going to feel like swallowing something uncomfortable.

And given the direction Lu Tangshu's thinking had gone, if her life were hard she might do something even more reckless. The first branch wasn't afraid—they would just be sending her step by step toward her own end. But none of it was pleasant.

Whatever the outcome, she needed to hear her daughter's thoughts first.

Her daughter might want the scheme returned to the sender in full—and if so, that was exactly what she would do.

"Mother, I'm not letting this go."

Lu Huaixi looked up with unhurried candour—her clear, limpid dark eyes catching the light and looking bright and guileless.

But the words she spoke carried a calm that had nothing of the naivety written on her face.

"Have Third Sister betrothed and married."

Lu Huaixi smiled, eyes curving.

"She doesn't want to go to the palace? Then let her marry. And quickly—pick fast, marry fast. If something well-matched isn't available, then something below her standing. I've already married ahead of her as the elder sister, so her marrying now isn't improper."

Lu Tangshu wanted to raise her own standing, wanted a splendid marriage, wanted everyone to envy her. Then let every one of those wishes be turned on its head.

When Lu Huaixi said these things, she didn't feel the slightest bit cruel.

And she wasn't afraid of anyone objecting—she said it at her own unhurried pace, as casually as if she were describing what good things she'd eaten that day.

Lady Liu looked at her, and her expression softened involuntarily—a thread of guilt surfacing in her eyes.

Not catching the second branch's intentions in time had forced her easygoing, carefree girl into an early marriage.

Now her daughter looked composed enough—but Lady Liu knew her child.

If she truly felt nothing, she wouldn't be this composed about proposing to have Lu Tangshu betrothed and married off.

She still minded. She still felt the injustice.

"Then let her be married off."

Lady Liu took Lu Huaixi's hand. "She wanted to step on you to raise her standing. Let her fall until she has no standing left."

Not long after, a maidservant came from outside to refill the tea—adding some of the cakes that Lu Huaixi had always liked.

Lady Liu saw what had been brought and thought again of what she had overheard when her daughter stepped down from the carriage.

"I didn't get to say this to you earlier—when you go out with someone, Yaoshu is right there with you. How could you put Xie Yuanjing to work tidying the food box for you?"

Having finished the serious talk, Lady Liu's tone gentled, and thinking of something, she shook her head slightly.

"I know you've had to carry a lot. Coming home, perhaps you let your guard down. But however agreeable his temperament, the two of you are not truly husband and wife. These things—don't let yourself get too used to expecting them."

"I didn't suffer any hardship."

Lu Huaixi thought about saying his temperament wasn't actually all that agreeable—then reconsidered, and found that actually, it kind of was.

Xie Yuanjing had never shown her a cold face, let alone lost his temper.

When he was with her he was patient and warm—and always found ways to show, openly, that she had someone backing her in the marquis' household. He made sure everyone could see it.

Whatever he had said about "as it should be," he had handled everything with care and exactness. There was nothing to fault.

At that thought, Lu Huaixi swallowed what she'd been about to say.

"Don't worry, Mother. I remember that he and I aren't truly husband and wife. Today I really did just sleep in—I'll call for Yaoshu next time. I won't trouble him."

"Of course I'm not blaming you—I'm only worried that over time you'll get used to it, and start expecting it outside too. He is the marquis' household's First Young Lord after all. Even if he and our Lu family's first branch are on the same ship right now, he's still someone with his own temperament. And besides, everything he does has a purpose—"

Lady Liu looked at her and paused, then spoke more deliberately.

"That said—don't hear what I'm saying and turn cold toward him either. The way he looks after you is, one could argue, what's due to you. And what's due to you, your father will compensate him in equal—or even greater—measure. So if you suffer any grievance in the marquis' household, you don't need to be afraid."

There were things Lady Liu had hesitated to say.

Her daughter was very clever, and she already understood perfectly well what Xie Yuanjing's warmth was for.

But she still had to be careful. Because this eldest young lord of the Xie family, if he wanted someone to grow attached, was far too capable of it.

"I know, Mother."

Lu Huaixi looked down and idly brushed the small embroidered flowers on her skirt.

"Does Mother still not trust me? I'm very smart, you know. Right now I'm just waiting—waiting to come home happily in one year."

chapters.title: Forced to Bow Her Head
chapters.content:
Up in the front hall, Lu Tangshu had been confined to her own room and told she wasn't to go anywhere.

On any ordinary day, she would have cried and made a scene, perhaps smashing a few things for good measure, and bullied the maidservants into stepping aside.

But right now she had only fear.

Since hearing Xie Yuanjing's warning, the colour hadn't returned to her face. She had been led back to her own courtyard, sat down, drunk a cup of tea—and still her heart pounded wildly.

She didn't dare think about what Xie Yuanjing might do to her.

And yet she was consumed by helpless resentment, unable to understand why a man like Xie Yuanjing would involve himself in inner household matters for the sake of Lu Huaixi.

"Third Miss—these are the books the Old Master has asked you to copy today."

The maidservant Qiao-ling called softly from nearby, carefully setting down what she'd brought.

Lu Tangshu looked up. The fear and fury in her eyes were naked and unguarded.

"What's happening outside? And Lu Huaixi—where is she?"

"In answer to Miss—the banquet outside hasn't broken up yet. Second Miss is still there."

"And Grandmother? Has Grandmother asked about me?"

Qiao-ling lowered her head, and after a pause said quietly, "The Old Madam seems to have tired—she couldn't spare a moment just now."

Lu Tangshu's face grew more pinched. She held herself in check, pressed her lips hard together.

"Miss, please don't upset yourself. Madam said to make sure you don't act impulsively at a time like this."

Qiao-ling chose her words carefully. "Second Miss has just married—it's natural for her husband to be attentive right now. Those words were probably just said for the first branch's benefit. Once said and done, that's the end of it."

Lu Tangshu still said nothing. She only gripped the handkerchief in her hands tighter and tighter.

She had always disliked Lu Huaixi—disliked that guileless, everything-rolls-off-me face. As if nothing was ever worth caring about.

And heaven itself seemed to take special care of her. Whatever she wanted—even things sold out at a roadside stall—would somehow end up in her hands.

And the first branch's path kept getting better and better—Lu Huaixi's father's position had at one point outranked her father's.

Her mother wasn't satisfied. And neither was she.

Even being equally legitimate daughters of the same household, the Old Master had always been visibly more invested in the first branch.

She hadn't asked for much—only for Lu Huaixi to give something back. And yet Lu Huaixi had gone off behind the second branch's back, betrothed herself quietly and married, and played her for a fool.

"She got so much from this family—the palace was always supposed to be hers!"

Lu Tangshu could no longer hold it back. Her eyes were filled with grievance.

"Acting so high and mighty—no idea how she got Xie Yuanjing to come to her defense. Probably used that face of hers. I used to think the marquis' eldest young lord was above such things—turns out he's just another man ruled by a pretty face."

"Third Miss, please—"

"Shut up!"

Lu Tangshu had just managed to bite back the urge to snap when footsteps approached outside.

She looked up and found one of her mother's matrons standing there.

"Third Miss—the banquet is almost over at the front. Madam said she's keeping watch up there and asked you to use this opportunity to go and find Second Miss. Say something conciliatory. Second Miss has a soft heart—a few words of placating should do. With things like this, neither the first branch nor the Xie household would truly get involved."

"I should go and say conciliatory things to her?"

Lu Tangshu's voice rose. "She's what—"

"Third Miss—the first branch has made it clear they intend to split from the second branch. If you don't lower your head now, do you really want to wait until they make a full scene and send you to the palace?"

The matron reasoned with her. "The newly wed heat hasn't passed yet. Endure it a little longer. Once the business about the palace is settled, Second Miss will have no one propping her up—you'll have your chance to vent then."

"Can Xie Yuanjing really just threaten someone like this on her behalf? Isn't he afraid it'll get around and people will say he's bullying a defenceless young woman? And Lu Huaixi—she married into a fallen marquis' household, what does she have to be so proud about!"

Even so, Lu Tangshu stood up.

She was genuinely frightened—frightened of truly being sent into that imperial abyss. Even more frightened of the first branch and Xie Yuanjing retaliating.

The matron saw the girl's resistance plainly, but couldn't help adding one more nudge.

"However fallen the marquis' household, the title is still there. Third Miss had best keep those words inside these four walls. Right now you're about to go and ask forgiveness of Second Miss—you really cannot be this indiscreet... Madam was already hoping for today when Second Miss returned home. Getting Second Miss to speak for you now is the best way forward."

Lu Tangshu's expression soured further.

To have to depend on Lu Huaixi for this was enough to make her feel half-sick.

She pressed her lips until they had nearly drawn blood, endured it for a long while, and finally—unable to do otherwise—clenched her teeth and accepted that she was going to have to bow her head and beg.

Lu Huaixi was in the courtyard aiding her digestion.

She was in a less ebullient mood than when she had first arrived—partly because she was about to leave again, and partly because she had sorted out her thoughts about Xie Yuanjing and found herself, for the moment, with nothing in particular to care about.

She was letting her mind wander when a figure appeared at the edge of her vision.

"Second Sister, I was wrong."

Lu Tangshu came from one side, blocking Lu Huaixi's path. Whether she didn't dare look up or simply couldn't, she kept her head low, her voice barely audible.

"I know I'm always thinking of you—I don't know what came over me today. I just started saying things I shouldn't. Can Second Sister not be angry with me?"

The sudden appearance startled Lu Huaixi.

She stepped back a pace, and trying to avoid accidentally treading on Yaoshu behind her, twisted her ankle slightly.

"And the thing Second Brother-in-law said—I really don't know about that, I truly don't. Second Sister, you know what I'm like—at most I lose my temper over small things. I wouldn't have the kind of grand plans he was implying..."

Lu Tangshu kept talking, and her voice began to carry a hint of catching in the throat.

Her hands at her sides were lightly gripping her clothes, as though she had called up every ounce of courage.

"Besides, we're sisters. Second Sister, you always said—no matter how good other people are, they can't compare to one's own sisters... Second Sister, I truly know I was wrong. Please don't hold it against me. Forgive me just this once?"

Lu Huaixi frowned, coming back to herself, and looked down to check her ankle.

The twist hadn't been severe—Yaoshu had caught her—but it still ached a little.

The person in front of her was still saying her piece, putting on the same pleasant-faced contrition as her mother Lady Luo—the first such apology and show of goodwill in all these years.

But when Lu Huaixi looked up, she could see the corners of her mouth pressed flat to a thin line through sheer restraint, and the jaw held rigid with the effort of biting down on something.

She still hadn't accepted it.

Lu Huaixi felt no particular surprise—and nothing like disappointment.

Whatever had passed between her and Lu Tangshu could never be reconciled, and forgiveness was never on the table.

"Second Sister, just believe me this once. I really did..."

"Which time do you want me to believe you?"

Lu Huaixi cut her off. She thought for a moment, then gave a small smile in her direction.

But before she could say anything more, someone spoke behind her.

"What happened to your foot?"

chapters.title: Applying Medicine
chapters.content:
A figure in dark robes appeared suddenly on the quiet path.

As Xie Yuanjing drew near, the wind he brought carried a faint trace of wine.

"What happened?"

Lu Huaixi hadn't expected him to be this perceptive—to catch something was wrong from this distance.

Thinking of how many times he had told her to watch where she was going—and here she was, having hurt herself again—she felt a sting of embarrassment.

But even more than embarrassment, she was afraid of being told off. She pushed off Yaoshu to edge back a step—and had barely moved when she was stopped.

"You twisted your foot?"

"...Mm."

"And you're still trying to move around?"

"It's not serious. I just turned it a little."

He came to stand before her, brow furrowing slightly, eyes dropping to the hem of her skirt.

Nothing to see—only the flowing drape of her clothes and shoes that were still clean after a full walk around the grounds.

Lu Huaixi was about to say she could manage if she just pushed through it, when the ground seemed to vanish beneath her feet, her eyes tilted, and Xie Yuanjing had scooped her up.

She had never been carried like this before. The shock rushed up the same moment her body left the ground, and her hands flew out instinctively.

"Point the way to your room."

As Xie Yuanjing moved, Lu Huaixi's hands—with nowhere else to go—came down on his shoulder.

But the sensation through the thin robe was impossible to ignore—the hardness of it—and her palm went warm.

She slid her hand down quickly, carefully taking hold of his lapel instead.

The man carrying her hadn't noticed her movement. Once she was securely settled, his gaze moved to Lu Tangshu—who was standing frozen and speechless nearby.

"One more entry in the ledger, Third Miss Lu."

With that he withdrew his gaze, face still set, and carried her away.

Lu Tangshu came back to herself to find that what she remembered most was the cold edge in Xie Yuanjing's eyes.

She grew more and more frightened, and tried to rush after them and explain, beg for mercy—but she had only gone a few steps before Old Master Lu spotted her and stopped her cold.

"Still daring to run out and cause trouble?"

"And you're still trying to move around?"

In Lu Huaixi's room, Xie Yuanjing's voice fell. Her forehead received a light tap—the motion somewhere between suppressed temper and helpless resignation.

"I've said it how many times now—watch where you're going. Is it going to take actually getting hurt before you'll remember?"

On the low wooden table beside the daybed sat a few boxes of medicinal ointment. Yaoshu was standing to one side, holding a small basin of warm water that had just been brought in, a cloth soaking inside.

"It's not bad at all. I'm perfectly fine now."

Lu Huaixi moved her ankle experimentally. It had been a little sore at first, but now she could barely feel anything. "If you don't believe me, I'll walk for you."

She started to put her foot down—and before she had it fully placed, Xie Yuanjing had already risen. He came to stand directly in front of her, looking down in silence.

When Xie Yuanjing said nothing, he always carried a certain cool severity. Looking down from above like this, that casual, unhurried coolness always seemed to carry an edge of pressure.

With him staring at her like this, Lu Huaixi's movement froze mid-way.

Especially seeing the seriousness in his dark eyes—she felt inexplicably as though she'd done something wrong, and the face she'd been lifting suddenly didn't dare meet his gaze. She looked instead at the firm set of his lips, and then at the sharp line of his jaw.

"It really is fine now. There's no need to look especially—"

"Take them off."

Before she could finish, the man standing over her spoke.

His voice was cool and flat—nothing like his usual measured tone.

"Your shoes and socks."

Xie Yuanjing said. "Right now."

His tone carried an undeniable force that couldn't be ignored. Even knowing he was concerned about her injured ankle, it still made Lu Huaixi bow her head with a flash of annoyance.

This time it wasn't even her fault for not watching her step. And besides—taking off shoes and socks, like this—that wasn't really appropriate.

Seeing her hold her position without moving, head down, expression hidden, stiffening into a standoff, Xie Yuanjing was quiet for a long moment alongside her.

Yaoshu beside them was so anxious her heart jumped.

She was just steeling herself to say she'd apply the medicine on the First Young Mistress's behalf—when she heard the person standing there sigh.

The tension in the air softened at once.

"Throwing a temper tantrum, are we?"

Xie Yuanjing shook his head, his voice easing. "What did I say?"

Lu Huaixi was the kind of person who always knew when to back down with people she was close to. Hearing him step back first, she stopped holding out.

"But it wasn't my fault just now."

She looked at him. "Lu Tangshu jumped out at me without warning and startled me."

"Mm. Not your fault."

Xie Yuanjing gestured for Yaoshu to put things down, then crouched in front of her. "Next time you go out, bring Jing Shuang too—she knows martial arts. Between her and Yaoshu, they'll be enough."

As his voice finished, his hands came to her ankle.

The person sitting on the daybed had been about to say something, but his touch startled her backward.

"Don't move."

That hand settled lightly on her foot. "A foot injury can be minor or serious. No pain doesn't mean it's fine—it still needs medicine."

Xie Yuanjing softened the pressure of his authority, eyes sweeping over the medicine beside him. "Unless you'd rather spend half a month laid up in this room, unable to walk or go outside? Do you want that?"

"...I don't."

"Then be still."

Xie Yuanjing's hands were exactly as Lu Huaixi had imagined—long and finely shaped.

There were calluses at his fingertips and the webbing of his thumb. When he removed her shoes and socks and accidentally caught her skin, it grazed her lightly.

That instant, both of them seemed to go still at the same time—though Lu Huaixi didn't see it. She pressed her lips together, turned her head slightly to the side, not daring to look.

Then the movement continued.

Xie Yuanjing looked at the faint redness at her ankle, extended two inches from the place he'd just examined, worked some medicinal ointment open with the warmth of his palm, and applied it.

The sensation under his hand was unlike anything he had touched before.

His attention splintered briefly. He also found himself, for the first time, regretting the impulse that had led to him doing this himself—wishing he had let the maidservant handle it.

But then he dismissed the thought.

Children say one thing and mean another. He didn't trust her to have said it right. He had to look himself.

Neither of them spoke. Xie Yuanjing kept his eyes down, and looked at the site of the injury. Where his hand had barely applied any pressure at all, the skin had already gone pink.

When he stood, the room had already been taken over by the smell of the ointment.

"Don't rush back. Rest a little longer."

Lu Huaixi didn't answer. After a long moment, she said a very small, slightly awkward thank you.

Xie Yuanjing's steps toward the outer room paused—and something in him went inexplicably soft at that muffled, somewhat reluctant tone.

While waiting for hot water to wash his hands, Gong Fei was standing outside.

"My lord."

Xie Yuanjing glanced toward the inner room, saw Lu Huaixi had put her shoes and socks back on and was curled up on the daybed whispering with Yaoshu, and nodded, indicating the man could come in.

Gong Fei had been at Xie Yuanjing's side longer even than Gong Zhuo.

When he first saw Lu Huaixi move into the master's room, he had been genuinely worried—afraid his master would resist too strongly, and afraid that this Lu family noblewoman wouldn't be able to bear the coldness of the place.

But several days had passed now.

Their First Young Mistress was eating well and sleeping well.

And their master showed no sign whatsoever of being unhappy. If anything, there seemed to be a faint, indescribable liveliness about him—an interest he hadn't had before, finding himself attentive to food and comfort matters every day.

Quite surprising.

"My lord, Young Master Shen has sent a card."

Gong Fei stepped closer, head down, suppressing his thoughts. "Today he likely meant to invite you, but remembered it was the First Young Mistress's return visit day, so he left only his card and went. He said he'd invite you and the First Young Mistress out for a boat trip on the lake sometime."

Xie Yuanjing didn't reach for the card.

The ointment was stubborn—he kept his hands in the water for a good while, and even after drying there was still a faint herbal smell. He had to wash them again.

"A boat trip? He's in that kind of mood?"

He said it without much interest. "Tell him later."

"Yes."

Gong Fei had naturally caught the smell that still lingered even now, somewhat diluted by the air.

He had already been startled when he saw his master carry the First Young Mistress in. Now realising the master might have applied medicine to her himself, his mind went completely blank.

Almost instinctively, he looked up.

The man before him was calm-faced, eyes down, washing his hands carefully—none of the usual displeasure after being touched by someone, none of the resistance to closeness with others.

"Anything else?"

Xie Yuanjing finished washing, picked up a cloth to dry the water from his hands, and glanced over at Gong Fei.

Gong Fei immediately lowered his head and stepped back.

"Then this servant will go reply to Young Master Shen."

"A moment."

Xie Yuanjing thought, then added: "I'll ask first."

Ask who—about what.

Gong Fei stood to one side and held back from looking.

chapters.title: Making Things Up
chapters.content:
After Gong Fei withdrew, Xie Yuanjing stood in place for a moment.

By now the room was no longer as taut as it had been—occasional soft laughter drifted through, as if Lu Huaixi had hit on something amusing and was laughing with a hand pressed to her lips.

Her unhappiness came fast and went fast, and she made no effort to hide either.

Xie Yuanjing found himself looking toward the sound, peering through the swaying bead curtain at the person inside.

In his view, Lu Huaixi's face was vivid and bright. Her lovely eyes were curved from laughing, her usually pressed lips opening and closing, occasionally pausing mid-word in surprise before her eyes went wide and she looked at Yaoshu.

You might call it unpolished—but what came to mind more was something simple, something honest. Or perhaps the image of flawless, beautiful glass—utterly transparent.

Xie Yuanjing found himself thinking of He Jianxing—someone he didn't ordinarily let occupy a thought.

He wondered whether, back when the He and Lu families were still friendly, the simple, unguarded Lu Huaixi had given that man the same complete trust she had given others.

Xie Yuanjing's brow contracted briefly—the calm in him disturbed, just for a moment.

Then the laughter came again from inside, pulling his thoughts back immediately.

He watched a little longer, then looked down at his just-washed palm.

Applying medicine to someone's ankle—it was something he had never imagined doing for anyone. But having done it, he found there was actually nothing he couldn't accept about it.

"Do you want to go on a lake trip?"

Xie Yuanjing spoke up. As intended, he drew Lu Huaixi's gaze.

"In a few days—how do you feel about a boat trip on the lake?"

"With who?"

"With me."

Xie Yuanjing thought, then added: "And a close friend."

"Yes! I'll go!"

Lu Huaixi barely hesitated. But then she asked: "You're getting together with your friend—am I allowed?"

"Of course you are."

"Then I'm going. And I want to listen to music on the lake!"

Lu Huaixi said it and broke into a smile—as if she had already forgotten that moments ago the two of them had been in a standoff, showing no trace of any lingering awkwardness.

Xie Yuanjing was briefly caught off guard by that smile, and only after a beat remembered to respond.

"If you want music, shall we bring your people?"

Seeing the surprise in her expression, he continued. "If you're afraid of being bored on the boat for a long stretch, you could invite someone to keep you company as well. The boat is large. One gathering on each side—no need for you to run into each other."

"Really? Would that be appropriate?"

"It would."

Well—perhaps it wouldn't, quite.

Honestly speaking, when he and Shen Zhoushu met privately, there had never been outsiders. Strangers whom he had never met before—whether Lu Huaixi's friends or the singers and dancers she kept at Shun'an Lane—would all be entirely without trust where he was concerned.

But Xie Yuanjing inexplicably wanted to coax her into smiling. The way she had been pressed into bowing her head just now, unhappy—he really didn't want to see that again.

—

Perhaps because of the lake trip to look forward to, Lu Huaixi was in better spirits returning to the marquis' household than she'd been on the way there.

She even waved away Xie Yuanjing's offer to see her back to her courtyard before heading off to deal with business—and made her own unhurried way through the grounds with Yaoshu's support, taking in the marquis' household's scenery along the way.

"First Young Mistress, your foot is still injured."

Yaoshu's brow creased with worry. "Why don't we go back to the room to rest first? The scenery will still be here tomorrow."

Lu Huaixi waved it off, not the least bit concerned.

Truthfully it didn't hurt anymore—she didn't know whether to credit Xie Yuanjing for the way he had massaged it, or the ointment for being that effective.

"Don't worry. When I can't walk any further, I'll stop."

"But you... this servant has finally worked it out. The Madam back home can't get you to listen—it's only the First Young Lord's words you'll actually follow a little."

"Hardly—"

"But at least the First Young Lord is genuinely devoted to you. I'm convinced of that now."

"Convinced of what?" Lu Huaixi turned curiously.

"Convinced that the First Young Lord has been waiting for you since long before you came of age."

Yaoshu said quietly. "This servant heard it too—people are saying the First Young Lord has been fond of you for a very long time."

"..."

If she had heard this half a day earlier, Lu Huaixi's heart might have skipped a few beats—even knowing it was false.

But she had since sorted things through clearly, and now she was beyond the confines of the identity of Xie Yuanjing's wife. Her heart was still as water.

Thinking that she, at her young age, had already seen clearly through matters of the heart, she couldn't help smiling at herself.

"Stop listening to gossip."

"This is hardly gossip—you don't know—"

"First Young Mistress."

A voice came from behind, cutting off Yaoshu's words.

Lu Huaixi turned to look—and saw a maidservant from the Old Madam's courtyard, bowing to her with a smile.

"This servant greets the First Young Mistress."

The girl's manner was respectful, and she had stopped at the courtyard entrance—not daring to come a step further inside without being invited.

Lu Huaixi wasn't surprised. She simply nodded back, lips curved in an easy smile, thoroughly composed.

Ever since the day she had mentioned Old Master Zeng and Little Doctor Zeng, the Old Madam had been extraordinarily warm toward her for several days running.

Not only had she been excused from morning greetings—the Old Madam had also been sending little gifts on and off, and occasionally invited her over for meals.

But Lu Huaixi didn't enjoy eating with people she wasn't familiar with, and each time had used Xie Yuanjing as her excuse to slip away.

"The Old Madam has been waiting for the First Young Mistress since early. A few other Ladies are also there—she says she hopes you'll come join them."

Yaoshu was about to say that the First Young Mistress had turned her ankle and probably couldn't come—and had barely opened her mouth when her hand was lightly tapped.

Lu Huaixi hadn't let her speak.

"At this hour—won't we be disturbing Grandmother's evening meal?"

"In answer to the First Young Mistress—the Grand Madam is also there, and the Old Madam eats very little at dinner. Not wanting to dampen everyone's spirits, she didn't have the Ladies stay for dinner either. Right now they're playing Leaf tiles, and waiting for you to join them."

Playing along and appearing agreeable was something Lu Huaixi had always found effortless.

When she wanted to, she could make anyone she chose perfectly happy.

Today she hadn't come intending to coax anyone. But with Ladies from several branches of the Xie household all present, she couldn't very well not go.

"Oh, they're playing Leaf tiles."

Lu Huaixi smiled. "Good—I don't know how to play. I'll go and learn."

"First Young Mistress, your foot..."

"A small thing."

Lu Huaixi gave Yaoshu a wink.

She had already turned down the Old Madam several times. If she refused again, that one would look for fault regardless—and besides, keeping the household's inner affairs settled was also part of what she was meant to do. She would go and take a look, treat it as a little diversion.

"I need to go and do my bit for your master's reputation. Didn't someone say he's been fond of me for a long time? I can't let all that fondness go to waste."

"First Young Mistress, you... you're so good to the First Young Lord!"

"Of course I am. I've been fond of him for a very long time too—you didn't know?"

Yaoshu was genuinely moved, moved enough that Lu Huaixi felt she might have taken the fiction a little too far.

And a little way back, Gong Zhuo—who had been about to come over and ask after the First Young Mistress after seeing her waylaid—stopped where he was.

He appeared to have overheard something he shouldn't have. Gong Zhuo stood there, entirely at a loss for what to do.

chapters.title: Harmonious
chapters.content:
In the Old Madam's courtyard, Lu Huaixi had only just walked in when laughter from inside the room reached her.

It was genuinely a scene of warmth and contentment—nothing to suggest the first branch and third branch Ladies had exchanged sharp words just days ago.

Lu Huaixi's foot still bothered her a little, and she had made the whole walk over as slowly as she could, half-worried Xie Yuanjing would say something about it.

She had barely finished paying her respects to the Old Madam at the head of the room when a woman's voice drifted over, light and floating.

"First Cousin's wife has finally come—Grand-Aunt has had her on her mind all evening and hasn't been able to enjoy the game at all."

The voice carried a faint smile but a tone that wasn't exactly trying to say anything friendly.

Lu Huaixi waited until the words had finished before she looked over and returned a small smile.

Mu Weiming couldn't read her expression. But unable to stop herself, she pushed on.

"The maidservant was away quite a while without any word—Weiming was starting to think First Cousin's wife was dragging her feet and didn't want to come. I was just thinking of going to find you myself. Fortunately I can see you now."

"I should have waited for you to come, then."

Lu Huaixi adopted her tone and curved her eyes, affecting helplessness.

"I turned my ankle today, and you-know-who was like a tutor scolding me half the afternoon for it. If you'd come for me, he might have shown more lenience—don't you think, Cousin?"

Laughter came from nearby. Lu Huaixi didn't look back to see who.

She hadn't meant to needle her—only to hand the problem back to its rightful owner.

Mu Weiming was here for Xie Yuanjing. If anyone had to deal with that, it was his responsibility—and since that man had told her he had no one he cared for and had never entertained such thoughts, Mu Weiming was not someone she needed to keep any consideration for.

She was just about to smile again in Mu Weiming's direction when another voice came from toward the Leaf tiles table.

"You foolish girl—if you turned your ankle, why didn't you stay in your room and rest? Do you think your Grandmother would blame you for not coming?"

It was Lady Xie.

Her gaze hadn't rested on Mu Weiming for a moment—it went straight to Lu Huaixi.

"Yuanjing was right to tell you off. A foot injury is no small thing—if it settles into something chronic, you'll suffer for it later."

"Mother—I've already come all this way, don't team up with my husband and scold me too."

Lu Huaixi had a gift for this kind of coaxing.

She only had to let her voice trail slightly at the end and look up with that warm, lazy gaze, lashes drooping just so—and no one who saw it could bring themselves to say anything too harsh.

Especially once she said "husband"—everyone else in the room looked at each other with knowing expressions.

"Don't be too hard on her, Elder Sister-in-law—watching you two together, it would break anyone's heart. If Yuanjing heard you, he'd never forgive you for it."

Second Madam Qi Miaoyi picked up the thread, playing a card from her hand.

"Elder Sister-in-law, don't take out your card losses on your own daughter-in-law."

"A few coins of silver isn't going to bother me."

Lady Xie answered with a laugh, then looked toward the maidservant. "Help First Young Mistress over here to sit—right beside me."

From start to finish, no one in the room had picked up Mu Weiming's remark or given it any further attention.

The moment the tension had been introduced, it sank without a ripple.

"Did you have medicine put on the ankle?"

"I did, Mother. Please don't worry."

Lu Huaixi sat obediently to one side. At the head of the room sat the Old Madam, with Mu Weiming attending close by.

Third Madam Zhao—whether on the Old Madam's instructions or her own account—was notably pleasant today.

The smile was there, though if you looked closely there was a thread of reluctance woven through it. But all these Ladies had long since mastered the art of presentation—if they wished to appear agreeable, agreeable was exactly what you'd see.

Lu Huaixi kept up her end of things too, eyes trained on Lady Xie's tiles, maintaining the very picture of gentle and unruffled composure.

"My luck has been truly terrible today—look at these."

Lady Xie made a show of holding up her tiles for Lu Huaixi to see, as though complaining. "At least I'm only losing to your Grandmother. If I were losing to your Second Aunt, I'd be too annoyed to eat dinner tonight."

"Elder Sister, you've only been winning ever since daughter-in-law arrived—stop covering it up and trying to save face."

Second Madam Qi burst in with a laugh. "Don't shield yourself behind your daughter-in-law from the moment she walks in."

The Old Madam was amused too and joined in: "Since Huaixi is here, I'll be a little more generous and win a little less—Elder Sister-in-law, put some effort in. Don't lose face in front of your daughter-in-law."

The whole room was easy and cheerful.

Although Lu Huaixi had no objection to this kind of surface-level pleasantness, the Ladies of the Xie household were genuinely skilled—enough that she quietly thought: impressive.

If Xie Yuanjing hadn't told her that the third branch and the Old Madam were in the same camp, she would never have seen where the lines were drawn. There was friction everywhere in this household, and yet none of it was visible.

"Huaixi, would you like to have a try?"

Lady Xie laughed and looked over. "Have you played before?"

"Mother, I don't know how to play this."

Lu Huaixi shook her head with a smile. "At home I was always the one collecting winnings—I'd just sit like this, wait for whoever had a bad run, say a few nice things, give someone's tiles a feel, and sit back and wait for the split."

"How does that work?"

Lady Xie blinked, then laughed until her eyes were slits. "All right, come try your hand over here."

Nobody in the room believed her—but they all laughed along and watched Lu Huaixi go over and help Lady Xie draw tiles.

As it happened, Lady Xie, who had genuinely been thinking of calling it an early night, suddenly started showing signs of a genuine turnaround—coming up with just the right tile, time and time again.

Lu Huaixi didn't really know much about it. But she kept up the pretence.

Each time she brought a tile over she would hold it up in front of the person beside her, asking with great gravity in a low voice: "Mother, will this one do?"

After a few more rounds, Second Madam Qi couldn't hold back any longer. "Don't ask anymore, dear—your mother's mouth is already stretching from ear to ear!"

Lu Huaixi laughed over at Qi at once. "Grandmother and the two Second Aunts are the ones who agreed to let me help Mother draw tiles. When it's all settled, Second Aunts can't be genuinely cross."

She gave a confiding lean toward Lady Xie. "Grandmother's luck is too good to beat—but against the two Second Aunts, Mother doesn't need to hold back. I won't let you."

"Ooh, you think you can take money from us?"

Qi smiled. "Let your mother win back what she's lost first—then we'll talk."

Third Madam Zhao gave a nod. "Since Yuanjing's wife arrived, your Elder Sister's luck has certainly improved—but winning it all back will be a stretch. Best not to hope."

"She can win it. Both Second Aunts just wait and see."

Lady Xie laughed and shook her head at Lu Huaixi's breezy confidence.

She was young, after all—still carrying something childlike about her.

Though Lady Xie had raised a few concerns about this marriage from the start, now that the girl was here and she had spent time with her, her good qualities far outweighed the troubling ones.

"Since it's Huaixi's word, then—today at this table, let's set sisterly feeling aside."

The room went on in warmth and noise, so lively that even the maidservants nearby couldn't help relaxing.

The matron standing behind the Old Madam couldn't help looking at Lu Huaixi, taking a quiet mental note.

On ordinary occasions, these polite gatherings always passed in the same round of smiles and laughter—keeping the Old Lord informed that the inner household was peaceful, and setting aside a few problems in the process. They gathered, and they left.

But today she genuinely heard something different.

Including from the Old Madam herself, who had been genuinely difficult to please.

Not a change of heart—but at least at this moment, the Old Madam was actually being won over by this First Young Mistress. That much was real.

Thinking this through, the matron instinctively looked over at the courtesy cousin on the other side.

The courtesy cousin was smiling too—same as always. But the unconscious tightness at the corner of her mouth gave away that none of this was coming willingly.

Perhaps she was also feeling the sting of something she hadn't expected—that the Old Madam who had always been uniquely warm with her alone had, now that this First Young Mistress was here, completely forgotten to invite her to sit down.

chapters.title: Lucky
chapters.content:
The Leaf tiles game wrapped up by evening.

The Old Madam finally showed signs of weariness.

As the gathering broke up, Lady Xie immediately split her winnings in half and gave them directly to Lu Huaixi. Lu Huaixi was momentarily taken aback, but quickly smiled and had Yaoshu accept without ceremony.

"I'm not going to pretend with you, Mother—I'll be back for more next time."

Lady Xie smiled at the frankness of the person before her.

She had genuinely enjoyed herself for once in the Old Madam's courtyard—no need to be on guard, no calculations required. It had been rather relaxed.

"As long as that prim husband of yours doesn't say you're wasting time playing Leaf tiles, I'll take you every time."

"He says things like that?"

Lu Huaixi looked surprised, then pressed her hand over her mouth to laugh. "Then I'll share the winnings with him when we get back. Once he's taken money, he can't complain—he'd be taking advantage while saying nothing."

Lady Xie had just been laughing—she was about to add a few more words complaining about her son's dullness—when a voice came from outside.

"Who's taking advantage for free?"

Everyone turned.

They spotted Xie Yuanjing in a fine robe, stepping into the courtyard.

Before anyone had time to be surprised, he went and paid his respects to the Old Madam, then walked toward Lu Huaixi and gave the top of her head a light knock.

"One moment of inattention and you're over at Grandmother's playing Leaf tiles?"

"I can't play?"

Lu Huaixi blinked at him. "I wasn't playing—I was helping Mother win money."

"Won a lot?"

"I couldn't get anything from Grandmother because she was too good—but both Second Aunts gave generously."

That drew another laugh from the Old Madam up front, who reached out and called Lu Huaixi to her side, taking her hand and chatting.

This was the first time Xie Yuanjing had ever seen the Xie household's inner quarters so effortlessly uncomplicated.

He blinked—a flash of surprise crossing the calm of his eyes—and then settled back into composure, standing to one side and waiting for Lu Huaixi.

The person who had been called over was talking and laughing freely, looking as though she had lived here for years—picking up every thread of conversation naturally.

Occasionally she would even make a small, agreeable sound—entirely naturally, like a young person warmly teasing an elder.

Xie Yuanjing withdrew what he had said the first time he laid eyes on Lu Huaixi.

Children were not hard to manage. Children were formidable.

In the quiet, someone drew closer to his side—a thin, soft voice reaching him.

"Cousin."

A faint fragrance floated past his nose. Not unpleasant, but instinctively he felt his brow contract.

His gaze didn't move toward the speaker. He simply walked forward, stepping past her, and came to a stop beside Lu Huaixi.

"Don't keep Grandmother up—your foot still needs medicine. We can talk next time."

Lu Huaixi had been waiting for this line for quite some time now. Her face had grown a little stiff from holding her smile.

She turned back to look at Xie Yuanjing, and caught—not far away—a gaze that hadn't been withdrawn in time. The look in it was not friendly.

But Lu Huaixi didn't look away. She met that gaze directly, raised a smile, and calmly took in every trace of Mu Weiming's resentment and the panic of being caught.

"You have quite a lot of trouble, don't you."

"What?"

Xie Yuanjing asked, then noticed where her attention had just been resting. He paused. "She has nothing to do with me."

Lu Huaixi didn't answer—didn't make a sound, neither agreeing nor denying.

Xie Yuanjing thought again and reached up to take hold of her wrist. "If she bothers you, I'll have her removed."

Lu Huaixi's eyes widened slightly.

"You're going to harm me?"

She lowered her voice quickly so others wouldn't catch her expression. Her mouth still curved into a smile.

"Not harm—I'm afraid you can't be bothered dealing with her."

"You want to remove her now—after all this time of not doing it? What's the logic?"

Lu Huaixi couldn't follow the reasoning. She furrowed her brow slightly, then heard the Old Madam call her again and immediately smoothed her expression, glancing back with a warm smile.

"Don't cause me problems, Eldest Young Lord. I can manage this much trouble."

"Really no need for me to remove her?"

"My plan is to spend a peaceful year and go home a woman of good character. Don't ruin my gentle, biddable reputation—"

"Ow, easy!"

Lu Huaixi didn't finish before she looked down, staring at the fingertips being squeezed by Xie Yuanjing.

"What is this, private revenge? Petty."

"Young but thinking far ahead."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her. "A little child, already thinking about remarrying."

"You're the little child."

On the other side, Second Madam Qi, on her way out, paused in front of Lady Xie.

She glanced back at Lu Huaixi, currently talking with Xie Yuanjing, and pressed her handkerchief to her lips to hold back a smile.

"Elder Sister-in-law, your daughter-in-law—she's the lucky sort."

Lady Xie's run of good cards after Lu Huaixi appeared had been uncanny—almost like something out of the ordinary.

And later, when Third Madam Zhao had jokingly told Lu Huaixi not to help anymore, she had sat back cheerfully and not pushed it.

Just talked and talked—and the right tiles seemed to come anyway.

"I said the very first time I saw her—a girl from the Lu family, that face and that look of hers, she was plainly the lucky kind. A little young, perhaps—but there's time. A girl her age marrying into a household is common enough, and with you beside her, she'll grow closer to you for it."

Second Madam Qi continued. "Elder Sister-in-law, don't look only at what's on the page. Just look at our difficult Old Madam—she can't say a harsh word to her now. And as for Yuanjing..."

Lady Xie followed her gaze to her son—who was standing there, head inclined, listening to Lu Huaixi speak.

"When has Yuanjing ever come to the Old Madam's courtyard of his own accord—and without that frozen expression? Come to think of it, this is the first time since that courtesy cousin arrived, isn't it?"

chapters.title: Making Trouble
chapters.content:
After that occasion when Xie Yuanjing brought Lu Huaixi back from the Old Madam's courtyard, he made a point of notifying all the branches in the household.

Until Lu Huaixi's foot healed completely, his wife was not going anywhere.

Lady Xie heard the message and blinked, then shook her head with a helpless, laughing expression.

Lu Huaixi herself accepted Xie Yuanjing's fussing rather quickly. She happened to have some leisure and was working her way through the account books for her various properties.

She had people managing them for her, but every two months she would still read through them herself.

"First Young Mistress—the lake trip has been set for the third day of next month. Is there anything you'd like me to prepare?"

Jing Shuang came in from outside, carrying the latest ledger Xie Yuanjing had sent over.

"Third of next month... I should go to Shun'an Lane in a few days."

Lu Huaixi made her plans. "I also need to send a card to Sister Xianyu—she's wanted to go out on the lake too. When we're on the boat, while Xie Yuanjing is with his friend, I'll be on the other end with Sister Xianyu listening to music and watching the dancing."

Having sorted out her own arrangements, without waiting for a reply she looked at what was in Jing Shuang's hands. "What's this?"

Jing Shuang immediately came back to herself and passed it over.

"The First Young Lord had this sent over. He said the First Young Mistress seems to have forgotten something, and seeing this will remind her."

"I forgot something?"

Lu Huaixi took it and looked—calligraphy copybooks.

"..."

"The First Young Lord also said that since you're resting, this gives you something to do with your hands. And he said it was to remind you to produce what you promised him."

"...His memory is remarkable."

Lu Huaixi wrinkled her nose. "He isn't even in the household?"

"In answer to the First Young Mistress—these were left behind before the First Young Lord went out. Gong Fei was afraid you might not be up yet this morning, so he waited until just now to bring them. He also brought the brushes and ink."

Jing Shuang continued. "The First Young Lord said you can write in the outer room first—if sitting there gets uncomfortable, he'll have a new writing table and chair brought to the study."

Lu Huaixi was already surprised and about to decline when Yaoshu came in from outside, her expression carrying a thread of urgency.

She looked up.

"What is it?"

"First Young Mistress, there's trouble at Shun'an Lane. It seems to have been going on for several days."

Because of the wedding, Lu Huaixi hadn't been by Shun'an Lane since that last visit.

The only two people there who knew her real identity had sent a couple of gifts in the meantime through their private channel, but nothing else had come through.

Shun'an Lane had always been peaceful—Qing Ling kept tight watch over things, and because the girls there performed for their living and nothing else, there had only been one incident in all the time she'd been running it. Today was the first time since she'd taken over the place that she'd heard of trouble this serious.

And if word had reached her ears, it meant Qing Ling hadn't been able to keep it contained.

"Have the carriage readied. I'm going."

Lu Huaixi rose, thought again, and went back inside to change.

"Jing Shuang and Yaoshu will come with me... and is Gong Fei outside?"

"In answer to the First Young Mistress—he should be standing watch outside the courtyard."

"Then go and let him know—I'm going to Shun'an Lane shortly."

Jing Shuang acknowledged this, then asked: "How many men should she have Gong Fei bring?"

"No need for him to bring people—just let him know."

Lu Huaixi hadn't forgotten what she had agreed to with Xie Yuanjing—but she had also never intended to use Xie Yuanjing's people.

She had her own. And besides, this was her private affair. It was her place to handle it.

Hearing this, Jing Shuang paused slightly, then looked at the First Young Mistress already unpinning her hair, and didn't dare delay. She hurried out.

—

At Shun'an Lane, Qing Ling stood cold-eyed, looking at the couple who had planted themselves at the entrance.

The woman held a cleaver, mouth running with curses. The man behind her was unshaven, standing back without speaking.

Alongside her were a few rough-looking men holding clubs—not moving to approach.

They just stood around outside. Enough to make pedestrians and neighbouring shopkeepers want nothing to do with any of it.

"Sister Qing Ling, she's been like this for days—blocking the entrance, not letting us open for business. The hired men won't really do anything so the officials don't care—if this goes on another couple of days, we might really not be able to run this place anymore."

"I know. But she's standing where our authority doesn't reach. If our people restrain her from here, she'd have grounds to make even more trouble."

"So we just wait it out? We can't!"

The girl beside her said: "Those two aren't human beings. The man had his own ideas and got nothing for it—and now the woman comes to make our lives hell, won't let anyone go about their business, and screams disgusting things..."

"I know how angry everyone is."

Qing Ling said evenly. "But she's being clever about it this time—she's staying outside our territory, keeping those hired men from actually crossing the line. We've moved against her once and chased her off once—but then she threw herself on the ground and screamed that someone was going to kill her, and that scared off half our customers."

"Where's Xixi Juan?" Qing Ling asked.

"Hiding inside crying. She keeps thinking it's her fault—she was even planning to confront the man and tell him, if nothing else worked, she'd leave Shun'an Lane so we wouldn't have the trouble. I sent someone to stop her. She's not allowed out of her room."

"Good. None of this is her doing. It's this couple who are out to extort people."

It was still daylight—not many people outside yet.

But the woman's wailing was drawing eyes.

When Lu Huaixi came in through the back door, Qi Rui had just run out of patience and was hauling out a wooden chair, about to go and throw it at someone.

She rushed forward and called out—then had the page boy go to the front and stall things.

"Sister Qi Rui—you throw that and she'll be left half-dead. Do you want to end up in jail?"

"Little Mistress?"

Qi Rui turned, saw Lu Huaixi come from the back. "How did you end up here? Don't get involved—and don't let anyone figure out who you are."

"If you throw it I'll be the one fishing you out. Then everyone will figure out who I am."

Qi Rui knew this perfectly well—she'd just been at the end of her rope.

"So we just leave it?"

Qi Rui fumed. "I'd be justified in smashing their heads in—this is absolutely what they deserve!"

"I know everyone's furious."

Lu Huaixi found a seat in the hall with a clear view of the commotion outside—the woman waving her cleaver and carrying on.

"What exactly happened?"

Qi Rui said nothing, as if unsure where to start.

Qing Ling saw Lu Huaixi and was briefly surprised, then quickly settled.

"Same thing as last time."

She looked at Lu Huaixi. "Unpleasant business. I hadn't wanted you to hear about it."

chapters.title: Shouting
chapters.content:
Shun'an Lane occasionally had trouble.

But it was always drunk men using liquor for bravery—one look at the hired guards and their boldness evaporated.

A shrew blocking business this persistently was something none of them had ever seen.

"The one from that time—said her husband had been bewitched?"

Lu Huaixi thought back and her brow furrowed slightly.

Qing Ling heard her say it so directly and paused a beat before picking up the thread.

"Yes. That one."

"Why is she back? I thought she caused a scene once, got frightened off, and left."

"We got rid of her that day and she was quiet for a few days—but then the man came back twice. The first time I didn't catch it, and he came in and drank some wine. The second time I was there and turned him away, and gave instructions that we wouldn't receive him anymore."

Qing Ling refilled Lu Huaixi's tea as she talked.

"That was fine for a while. And then two days ago this woman showed up again, screaming that our dancer had sweet-talked her husband out of a huge sum of money—and that we put on a front of performing with nothing else going on, but really did every dirty trick in the book to make money. And she said..."

Qing Ling didn't go into the specifics of what followed—but from the fragments of shouting still carrying from outside, it wasn't hard to guess the rest was ugly.

"And quite a few people joined in watching. There was even that man himself, who came and stood outside ruining Xixi Juan's reputation for everyone to hear."

"So what do they actually want?"

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed again, and she felt a wave of revulsion—but kept her head. She homed in on what mattered quickly. "They can't just be here to make noise and destroy our business."

"Correct. At first the woman wouldn't say—just stood there causing a scene. It was only yesterday that she finally spoke: she wants every coin her husband ever spent here returned to her, and she wants Xixi Juan to come out and kneel and confess her wrongs—then go home with her husband to wait on him."

Hearing that, Qi Rui beside her couldn't hold back.

"The nerve of her—she wants us to hand back five thousand taels for whatever her husband spent here, she publicly destroys Xixi Juan's reputation, and she wants her to go with that man? She has no idea what she is."

"She really doesn't lack nerve."

The easy warmth in Lu Huaixi's expression had cooled. The usual soft droop of her eyes was now touched with a cold edge.

The smile was gone from her lips—her beautiful face stripped of all its girlish softness, carrying only a rare, clean sharpness.

"Little Mistress, don't get involved—this is dirty business. You've only just married. Don't let your husband's family hear about this."

"I'm not afraid."

Thinking of the marquis' household, Lu Huaixi didn't feel entirely confident—but compared to the girls' livelihoods here, her small lack of confidence became barely visible.

"If I don't deal with this, you'd have already thrown that chair—and then a little silver wouldn't be enough to cover it."

"I was just angry."

"I know everyone is angry."

Lu Huaixi drank her tea and steadied the flare of anger she'd felt.

Then she called Jing Shuang over, gave a few quiet instructions, and looked toward the front.

"They want their money back, do they? Have them come in a little closer so I can actually hear them. Not outside."

"Little Mistress?"

Qing Ling turned, brow furrowed. "If she comes in she'll push further. And they've been smart about it—they're afraid we'll do something inside. They won't really come in."

"Of course I don't mean bring them all in and bar the door—that would just give people something to talk about. It'd look like Shun'an Lane really has something to hide."

Lu Huaixi wasn't in a rush. She sat a while longer, listening carefully to what was coming in from outside.

About half an incense-stick's worth of time later, she rose and walked forward a little—stopping somewhere both sides could see clearly—and sat down again.

The woman outside saw a young, well-dressed girl come out and sit within reach without any sign of alarm, and paused mid-scream.

"Who are you? I want to see your manager. And that little hussy—others don't need to stick their noses in! Get out of the way!"

She came back to herself quickly, raised the cleaver, and unleashed another torrent—spitting as she went.

"Don't think hiding inside makes it go away! You swindled my husband out of thousands of taels, all kinds of filth going on behind closed doors! Today you either return every coin or send that little slut out here—let her kneel in front of me and then come home with my husband! Otherwise this place is never opening again!"

After the woman finished, the man who had been quiet behind her looked over too, and what came into his eyes made her stomach turn.

He stepped forward, a smirk in his voice.

"Haven't seen you before—are you new?"

He came closer—wrinkled, loose-hanging robes around a wiry frame, a shadow of grey under each eye, as though drink had hollowed him out.

"Not much older than Xixi Juan, are you?"

Lu Huaixi didn't acknowledge him. She looked at the woman only. "Thousands of taels? What does your household do for a living, to have that much to spend on wine and entertainment?"

She let her gaze pass over the two of them once and didn't try to hide the contempt in it.

The couple flared up immediately. Lu Huaixi continued. "The girls of Shun'an Lane are performers who earn their keep with skill, not otherwise. Bewitched you? Bewitched him?"

The blunt words cut off the bystanders who had been joining in with the shouting, leaving them momentarily unable to respond.

Qing Ling saw the opening and stepped forward.

"Shun'an Lane has never needed your few coins. We state our terms openly when we do business. For someone like you, we decided long ago we weren't interested in your custom."

The man, face burning, charged forward a few steps.

"This is your business? Performer and nothing else? Save that for fools! Nothing that pays this well is that clean! Days that little slut spent begging me to stay—and now she's got the money she's hiding? Today I'm stating my terms plainly: pay back what you owe me, send her to me, or I'll tear this place apart!"

"You keep saying that—I'll smash your skull in!"

Qi Rui flew in from the back, chair in hand again. "You make your living this way and still think you're something? As if anything you're saying is real!"

"I'm disgusting? Who's been doing disgusting things? Who's been leaving disgusting marks everywhere? Look—look here, these—"

The man was yelling and yanking at his collar, pulling the fabric aside to show several marks on his neck.

Lu Huaixi had never encountered anything like this, but thanks to her sister's very thorough long-distance education, she immediately knew what she was looking at.

The next instant, both Yaoshu and Qing Ling had stepped in front of her so she couldn't see.

"You're all with this place—you'll cover for each other! Fine—in front of all these people, if you've got the backbone, call a matron over to check her—let everyone hear whether she's really clean—then come back and argue with me. Do you dare?"

The man kept shouting, his words getting coarser.

Outside, some in the crowd started taking it up.

"He's right—call a matron to check, that's all it takes. If she's so innocent what are you afraid of?"

chapters.title: Confronting Him
chapters.content:
Calling a matron to inspect a woman's purity—whatever the result—was never a good thing.

For Xixi Juan it would be a violation, a mark on her that could never be undone.

The man seemed to have anticipated they wouldn't agree to it, and his words grew more and more brazen.

"As luck would have it, I know a skilled matron. If you've got the backbone, I'll have her called over right now, and you can tell the crowd exactly what the result is—speak up if I'm lying. She slept with me—"

His words cut off as water came pouring down from the upper floor.

It didn't land fully on him, but it left him thoroughly dishevelled.

He shouted curses up at the upper floor, and Lu Huaixi waited a moment longer—then finally saw Jing Shuang return.

"First Young Mistress—the couple's home did have strangers visit recently. The people brought in also turned up a sum of silver from their house—more than they could have earned themselves. The timing is tight, and the neighbours' accounts were vague, so it's hard to confirm yet whether someone put them up to this."

Jing Shuang finished without pausing. "But this man does have a woman on the side. She's been brought in—being held in the back."

"What does she say?"

"At first she wouldn't acknowledge the relationship. We tried silver and she didn't budge. Then I frightened her a little—she was afraid to die and wouldn't hide it anymore."

"Press her on it."

Lu Huaixi tilted her chin toward the front and said: "Those marks on his neck—if his woman on the side left them, bring her out."

From the beginning Lu Huaixi hadn't thought this was the couple's own scheme.

If they were this clever—knowing to stay outside where she couldn't touch them—they wouldn't have stormed straight into the building the first time, and they wouldn't have come empty-handed.

Coming back after so long, specifically to make Shun'an Lane unable to do business—that spoke of someone behind them.

As for the mistress—the moment the woman had come the first time, screaming about her husband being bewitched, Lu Huaixi had already suspected she existed.

"Come on then, show everyone! Call your matron!"

The man had wiped the water from his face and was at it again. "I told you already—either send me the money or send me the girl! Otherwise this matter isn't over!"

"What a mouth on you—you've got nothing on my girls, and you still think you're someone?"

Qing Ling had also stepped forward a few paces.

"Shun'an Lane has never had what you're accusing us of. Open for business, state our terms plainly—for people like you, we made it clear from the start we want nothing to do with you."

The man, stung by the disdain, surged forward.

"This is your business and you're still putting on airs? Performer and nothing else? Say that to someone stupid—no one makes this kind of money that clean! Today I'm putting it plainly: hand over what you owe, send her to me, or I'll smash this place—"

"You keep saying—I'll smash your head in!"

Qi Rui burst in from the back, wooden chair in hand again. "Making your living this way, still think you're worth something? As if a word you say is true!"

"I'm disgusting? Who's been doing disgusting things here? Look at me—look at these—"

The man was yelling and pulling at his collar, exposing the marks on his neck.

Lu Huaixi might not have known what she was looking at before—but thanks to her eldest sister's very thorough long-distance education, she understood immediately.

The next moment, both Yaoshu and Qing Ling stepped in front of her to block her view.

"You're all in it together—you'll all cover for each other! Fine—in front of everyone here, if you've got the nerve, call a matron over and let her look, then come back here and argue with me—do you dare or don't you?"

The man kept shouting, words dropping lower and lower.

Outside, some in the crowd took up the call.

"He's right—call a matron, it's one simple thing. If she's innocent what is there to be afraid of?"

Lu Huaixi, though she hadn't seen what she wasn't supposed to, had heard perfectly clearly what those marks meant.

And the next moment, without waiting for anyone, she spoke.

"Bring out that woman you have in the back."

A murmur ran through those who heard it—outside and in.

The man in front paused his shouting, staring at her.

"What woman? What are you trying to pull?"

"No tricks."

Lu Huaixi looked at him steadily. "You have a woman on the side. She's been brought in."

She watched the flicker of alarm cross his face before it was swallowed by bluster.

"Nonsense—"

"I'll ask you one more time."

Lu Huaixi's voice didn't rise. She looked at him with the same unhurried steadiness. "Those marks on your neck—who left them? Was it Xixi Juan of this establishment, or someone else?"

"Shut your mouth—you're a little girl making up stories, trying to get me to say something different? I'm warning you—let me go, or you'll have worse coming—"

Lu Huaixi wasn't in any hurry. She simply gave a slight nod, then looked over at the woman beside the man.

"You've all come inside now and you won't be leaving. You came in here and smashed what you smashed—right now I'll give you one chance. Speak honestly, and when the officials come, I'll put all of this on her."

She indicated the woman.

The man stared at Lu Huaixi, said nothing—but the shouting had clearly stopped. He was calculating something.

Before he finished his thinking, Jing Shuang had already dragged the trembling woman forward.

chapters.title: Resistance
chapters.content:
"The losses here would cost you your lives and still not cover it. Are you sure you don't want someone to help you?"

"I..."

The man seemed to finally feel fear. He opened his mouth as though making one last struggle.

"Fine, then we'll wait for the constables—"

"I'll talk! As long as you don't let the constables arrest me, I'll tell you everything!"
