Lu Huaixi glanced around, then had someone open the front doors wider so that the people outside could see everything clearly.

The woman came forward and caught sight of the person being held at the front. She panicked immediately, wailing as she called out to the man, then was forced to her knees before him as he looked on in shock.

"Save me, Brother Qin, save me..."

With the real lover revealed, and the man unwilling to pay for the damages, it took only a few exchanges before everything was pushed onto the wife's jealousy.

But beyond that, nothing more came of it. The man never once mentioned being put up to it by someone else, and no matter how many times Lu Huaixi probed, she could not extract a single useful lead.

What surprised her more, however, was the wife's attitude toward her husband's lover.

It seemed she had known of the woman's existence all along. The scene she'd caused had only erupted because her husband had shifted the blame onto her.

By the end, Lu Huaixi had grown weary of the spectacle. She sat in a chair waiting for the constables, watching the two in front of her trade insults.

"First Young Mistress, the situation isn't going to stir up much trouble now, and there are more and more people gathering outside. Would you like to retire to the back and rest?"

"Not yet."

Lu Huaixi shook her head.

Her thoughts had not yet untangled themselves from the matter. Beyond having caught the troublemaking couple, there seemed to be something else waiting for her to work out.

She was just about to say something more to Yaoshu when a rush of urgent footsteps came from the back. The curtain was flung aside, and someone came running out like the wind.

"Xiyuan!"

A voice called out from behind. Lu Huaixi heard the commotion and turned.

"I'm willing to let the matron examine me and prove my innocence!"

Xiyuan had slipped out without anyone noticing. One look made it plain she had been crying for a very long time — her eyes swollen shut, their original shape lost entirely.

But she was not crying now. Jaw set, she cast a furious glance at the couple being detained up front, then looked back at Qingling beside her.

"Qingling jiejie, I'm willing to let the matron examine me. I am clean. I have never had any improper dealings with anyone. I am standing right here, today, and I will wait for someone to come and give me justice."

"Xiyuan, don't be rash!"

Qingling stepped forward and gripped her arm, trying to steer her back.

"Dongxi — since Xiyuan's already had that woman's real lover brought out, and the woman has admitted those marks were her doing, this matter will no longer be pinned on you. You don't need to—"

"It won't matter. I know Xiyuan jiejie helped me, but from the moment that woman first came to cause trouble, I was already no longer 'clean.' I don't plan to marry in the future, and I don't care much for my reputation — but I don't want to drag Shun'an Fang's name into baseless speculation."

Xiyuan sniffled and forced a smile.

"I just want to clear my name once, and then go on living in Shun'an Fang with my head held high. I don't want to dance someday and have people whispering behind my back. And I don't want Shun'an Fang to carry this kind of slander for no reason."

Xiyuan's voice was loud. With the front doors thrown wide open, the people outside could see every detail of the scene within.

Yet the crowd, which should have been buzzing with chatter, fell into a strange quiet in the wake of Xiyuan's fierce, ringing words.

Lu Huaixi said nothing either.

After a long moment, she felt Qingling and Qirui looking toward her — and it seemed she had finally worked out what she hadn't been able to grasp before.

In the next instant, she turned to look at Xiyuan.

"Have you thought this through?"

Seeing Xiyuan nod with great force, Lu Huaixi did not try to dissuade her.

She smiled at her — part comfort, part encouragement.

"Then send for someone."

"Xiyuan—"

"Yaoshu, go in my name and invite the matrons from the yamen."

Lu Huaixi spoke each word with deliberate care. "Go openly. Hold your head high."

The voice that had been on the verge of protest fell silent. Qingling looked at the young woman before her without a word.

The second young miss of the Lu family she had known had always loved to smile. Her eyes were forever curved in that gentle arc; her voice soft and sweet when she spoke. Even when she was cross with someone, it came through with a girl's tenderness and soft heart.

And so even knowing she was a daughter of a noble house — and the true proprietress of Shun'an Fang — what Qingling felt for her was mostly a fond, protective warmth.

But now, watching her speak with a steadiness unlike her usual self — as though she had shed her girlish nature in an instant, calm and collected — Qingling felt, inexplicably, a rare and settled peace come over her.

She said nothing more. Instead, she quietly reached out and took Xiyuan's hand in hers.

—

Xie Yuanjing had been due to leave the city today on official business, but an order had come down from the palace assigning him a case.

The case itself was not complicated, but it involved a former Remonstrance Official who had been thrown in prison half a month ago, so he had gone to see to it in person.

When he finished and turned to leave, Gong Zhuo fell into step behind him, as though there was something to report.

"My lord, half an hour ago, the First Young Mistress's people went to the yamen. They first filed a report, then requested a matron under the Lu family's name to accompany them to Shun'an Fang."

Xie Yuanjing swung into the saddle and gathered the reins. At those words, he stilled. "What happened?"

Hearing Shun'an Fang, Xie Yuanjing took a moment to place the name.

Then he asked, "She went to Shun'an Fang today? How long has she been there?"

"Yes, my lord. The First Young Mistress informed Gong Fei before leaving the residence. She has been there approximately two hours. Just now, a guard overheard someone mention the First Young Mistress and took note — but the details are still unclear to this subordinate."

Knowing what his master would ask next, Gong Zhuo quickly added:

"The First Young Mistress did not take any of the residence's men with her. Apart from Jingshuang and Yaoshu, the rest are her own people — which is why word reached us more slowly."

Xie Yuanjing did not answer immediately.

He sat on horseback, his expression still carrying the cold austerity that lingered from his time in the prison.

Lu Huaixi had not brought his people. She had not sent word to him. When trouble arose, she had gone straight to the yamen herself — with no intention whatsoever of asking for his help.

Xie Yuanjing adjusted the reins. After a long pause, he lowered his gaze and said, "Lead the way."

—

Two matrons arrived from the yamen, accompanied by constables sent to take the troublemakers into custody.

When the matrons caught sight of Lu Huaixi, they offered her a respectful bow — a gesture that bewildered the onlookers who didn't know the full story.

Shortly after, Xiyuan was led away by the matrons — jaw clenched, no longer on the verge of tears.

"Everything inside was destroyed by these people."

Yaoshu and Qingling stepped forward, pointing at the couple and the hired thugs. "They also injured people. Those injured are in the back being tended to right now. Everyone here, inside and out, is a witness."

"This has nothing to do with me! Constable, sir, it was my jealous wife who came here to cause trouble — I was forced into it..." The man, now that a full squad of constables had arrived, had completely lost his nerve. "Ask the girl — she knows everything. None of this is my fault, it's all my—"

"Silence!"

The nearest constable raised a hand and rattled the hilt of his blade.

Lu Huaixi did not move back. She raised her eyes and looked.

"Him. Her. And them."

Her fingertip moved from one person to the next.

"These people destroyed my property, smashed my possessions, and injured my people. I am here today to file an official complaint. I will accept no mediation. I will accept no verbal apologies. I want them to pay for the damages — and I want them behind bars."

A brief silence fell over the hall.

Then someone murmured quietly, "Your... your property?"

chapters.title: I Came to Back You Up — But It Seems My Wife Doesn't Need Me
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had first taken ownership of this place for herself.

She had no shortage of silver, no great ambitions to make a fortune. She had only wanted a quiet place — somewhere for herself, and for those singing girls and dancers who had nowhere to go and no wish to sell themselves, to have a foothold in the world.

The more she came, the fonder she grew of it.

But she had been young when she took it on, and her thinking had been mostly playful. She had given almost no thought to what lay behind Shun'an Fang, or to its future.

By the time she thought to, she had already been warned: do not show your face openly; do not let people know. Better to stay safe in the shadows.

But now, standing here, thinking of Xiyuan just moments ago — eyes swollen from crying yet utterly resolute, willing to see herself disgraced in order to prove her innocence — Lu Huaixi suddenly felt that something had changed.

If she could not protect them, what was the point of keeping them here?

The onlookers were slowly making sense of what Lu Huaixi had just said.

Besides the girls of Shun'an Fang, there were also pedestrians from the surrounding lanes and the proprietors of nearby establishments — drawn in by the commotion, all craning their necks to peer inside.

"The proprietress of Shun'an Fang is a young girl?"

Someone else asked, and the murmuring spread.

"She doesn't look like she's from an ordinary family. Even if Shun'an Fang doesn't deal in that kind of trade, it's still a place for music and drink. For a girl to have a place like this in her hands, she must be..."

"She probably has some connections. Did you see those two matrons the yamen sent? A person powerful enough to make them bow their heads in greeting..."

"I just heard the head constable address her as Second Miss Lu. She's surnamed Lu..."

The voices came in fragments. Lu Huaixi paid them no mind.

She stood there and watched the constables bind them one by one.

"Who — who exactly are you?"

The man's eyes were wild with panic. His face, drained of color from fear, gave him a hollow, untethered look.

The woman beside him had been gagged. The arrogance with which she had glared at Lu Huaixi earlier was gone — only dread remained.

"You said — you said as long as I explained clearly, you — you wouldn't pursue it—"

"I am the proprietress of Shun'an Fang."

Lu Huaixi cut off his noise. In her eyes was the anger and grief of someone who had watched Xiyuan be wronged — but more than that, a cold sharpness that said these people would answer for what they had done.

"You wanted to see someone in charge. So here I am."

Lu Huaixi swept her gaze over them, then looked toward the door.

The Lu family would be easy enough to identify. The widely gossiped-about Second Miss Lu would be even harder to conceal, especially after the grand wedding not long past.

But that was precisely what Lu Huaixi wanted — for them to figure it out.

She wanted them to understand: Shun'an Fang was not a place anyone could simply walk in and trample on.

Once it became known that the proprietress behind Shun'an Fang was the newly wed Second Miss Lu of the Lu family, the murmuring swelled again.

Some spoke of the Lu family. Some of Cheng'en Marquis's residence. Some of Lu Huaixi herself.

Lu Huaixi did not move away. She stood there before everyone and acknowledged her identity openly.

"Shun'an Fang is mine — Lu Huaixi's."

Her voice was unhurried, soft yet carrying a quiet resilience that drifted outward on the breeze.

"I, Lu Huaixi, am not short on silver. I have no need for any pretense to hide behind. Shun'an Fang does not need underhanded dealings to survive. Let me say it plainly, here and now — whether before today or from this day forward, every girl who enters Shun'an Fang will always sell her art, and never her body."

The noise that had been rippling outside fell quiet. Lu Huaixi's voice was not particularly loud, but it brought those murmurs to a stop of their own accord.

"From today, Shun'an Fang continues its business as usual. Those who wish to listen to music and watch performances are welcome at any time. But if anyone comes here with the intention of causing trouble, first ask yourself whether you have what it takes to back it up. If you believe you do — come find Lu Huaixi directly."

Qingling and Qirui stood at her side and could not find words for a long moment.

It was only when one of the girls gently tugged at Qingling's sleeve that she came back to herself and looked over.

"Xiyuan — Xiyuan is our proprietress?"

Qingling nodded.

"And a noble daughter of the Lu family?"

Qingling nodded again.

But looking at the confusion on their faces, she glanced once toward the front, then turned back to them with a smile.

"Don't overthink it. Whoever the proprietress is, nothing changes. Things will go on the same as before — no need to feel awkward about anything."

She paused, then lowered her voice. "Look at those long faces. Don't go frightening the young proprietress when she comes back — making her think she did something wrong by stepping forward."

"We would never — that's not what we meant at all!"

The girls were startled, yes — but they knew who was on their side.

Before long, someone had drawn up a list of the damaged items and brought it over.

Qingling read through it carefully, then added the valuations at the end.

Then the matrons came out from the back.

The two of them remained just as respectful as before. The one in front spoke with a calm authority, though her tone softened slightly of its own accord when she caught sight of Lu Huaixi.

The result was exactly as expected: clean and untarnished. But even so, anger rose in Lu Huaixi all the same.

The detained troublemakers appeared to want to plead for mercy, but Lu Huaixi turned her face away.

Whether they had been put up to it or not, they would pay the price.

As the constables departed, the one leading them made a point of stopping in front of Lu Huaixi and dipping his head in a bow.

"Second Miss Lu, is there anything further you wish to instruct?"

"I thank you for your trouble."

Lu Huaixi nodded. Her voice carried more steel than before. "When dealing with people like this, I hope the constable will not be lenient."

Then she added, "And one more thing — these people came in with too much purpose and too clear a plan. When you investigate, I would ask that you dig deeper."

"We understand. Second Miss Lu, please set your mind at ease."

After watching the constables leave, the crowd outside showed no sign of dispersing.

Perhaps it was curiosity about this noble young woman from the Lu family — but as long as Lu Huaixi remained standing there, the onlookers seemed to have no intention of leaving.

"Who'd dare go after Shun'an Fang now? Even the constables were perfectly respectful!"

Someone in the crowd called out — clearly talking to whoever stood beside them, but with a voice far too loud to be private.

"Those people probably figured Shun'an Fang had no backing and thought they could shake it down for some silver. Just like that tavern up the road — someone came in a few days ago claiming they'd gotten sick from the food, and bullied the owner into paying a hundred taels!"

"Exactly! And this young lady just got married, hasn't she? With the Lu family behind her and the Marquis's residence too — who's going to come and make trouble at Shun'an Fang now?"

"Cheng'en Marquis's residence?"

Someone picked up the thread, hesitant. "The Marquis's residence probably won't get involved in something like this, will they? And she's a new bride besides. Who knows how they'll feel, learning she has a place like this..."

"That's true enough. If that backing falls away, Shun'an Fang..."

Lu Huaixi's movement paused mid-turn.

As though only just thinking of Xie Yuanjing, a flicker of something complicated passed through her eyes.

But it was gone just as quickly. She smoothed her expression, raised her head toward the direction of the voice, and let the corner of her mouth curve up slightly.

"Even without any other backing, I, Lu Huaixi, am more than capable of protecting Shun'an Fang."

—

When Xie Yuanjing arrived, he saw Lu Huaixi standing on the slightly raised stone steps, expression cool yet with a faint smile at the corner of her lips, looking sidelong toward one part of the crowd.

The eaves above stretched outward, cutting off some of the bright midday light — but she stood there luminous and unguarded, more dazzling than the sunlight itself.

Xie Yuanjing held the reins and watched from across the crowd, and heard her say —

"Even without any other backing, I, Lu Huaixi, am more than capable of protecting Shun'an Fang."

The irritation that had been building because she had shut him out so completely had not yet faded — but in that moment, Xie Yuanjing felt his resolve soften.

She really was perfectly capable of handling it herself.

But as for being her backing — that was something he found he rather wanted to be.

A man on horseback always drew attention.

Lu Huaixi noticed him soon enough.

She froze for a moment, forgetting to school her expression, and simply stared.

The onlookers followed her gaze. They saw the newcomers — and in particular the figure at the front — and instinctively parted to let them through.

"Is he here to arrest someone or to help someone?"

Someone murmured, "He looks a little frightening, doesn't he."

Xie Yuanjing didn't move, still astride his horse, back straight, brow cool and proud.

After a moment, his lips moved.

"To back someone up."

The person who had spoken nearly frightened themselves senseless at being answered.

But Xie Yuanjing seemed unaware of it. He simply looked across the distance at Lu Huaixi standing at the front, and said it once more.

"To back up my wife."

He smiled slightly. "Though my wife is formidable enough that it seems she doesn't need me."

chapters.title: I Really Will Punish You
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing's words did not quite reach Lu Huaixi's ears clearly.

There was a crowd between them — a considerable distance.

She had not expected Xie Yuanjing to appear at this moment, and even less expected that he would arrive just in time to hear what she had said.

By the time she came back to herself, she had already been holding his gaze for quite a while.

"That's the First Young Master..." Yaoshu murmured beside her, as though startled.

"Mm. I see him."

"The First Young Master wouldn't be here to... could he have just been passing by?"

Lu Huaixi drew a slow breath and turned the events of the afternoon over in her mind.

Thinking it through honestly, she didn't feel she had done anything wrong. The only thing that might not sit quite right was that she hadn't discussed it with Xie Yuanjing beforehand.

But even if she had — the outcome would have been the same.

She would still have stepped forward. She would still have claimed Shun'an Fang openly.

While she was still thinking, the man up ahead swung down from his horse.

Perhaps he had said something, or perhaps it was simply the force of his presence — but after he dismounted, the onlookers began to drift away of their own accord, and the long street gradually returned to the width it had been before.

Xie Yuanjing walked toward her.

Lu Huaixi was just trying to decide what to say when he stopped at the foot of the stone steps, the easy warmth he usually wore nowhere to be found, brow faintly creased.

"You waited until it looked like this to report it?"

His gaze went straight past her into the hall.

Lu Huaixi followed his eyes back inside. She saw the mess on the floor that had not yet been swept up, and pressed her lips together, unable to tell from his tone whether this was mild concern or genuine displeasure.

Was he commenting on the severity of the damage, or was he upset?

"It was left on purpose for the constables to see. No one's had a chance to clean up yet."

"Where were you when they were smashing things?"

"I was—"

Lu Huaixi lifted a hand to point — but something stopped her. When she thought back to the moment the confrontation had started, a twinge of guilt surfaced unexpectedly, and she drew her hand back before it had fully extended.

"In the hall."

"Which part of the hall."

Xie Yuanjing's question was direct, his tone carrying a quiet pressure. "Tell me, or I'll have someone come and ask."

"...Over there."

When Xie Yuanjing moved to call for someone, Lu Huaixi relented and pointed — to where she had been sitting, not far from the pile of broken fragments.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. His dark eyes were unreadable.

But there was no mistaking the cold edge in them. He stood there looking into the room without moving, and succeeded in frightening off several of the girls.

"Nothing really happened. I had people protecting me, and those thugs didn't dare actually throw things at anyone... I just needed some reason to have them detained..."

"You have such exquisite manners when it comes to detaining people?"

The corner of Xie Yuanjing's mouth curved — a cold, humorless arc, as though he was laughing out of anger rather than amusement.

"I won't say anything about you not wanting my help — you had your reasons. But you are the legitimate daughter of the Lu family's main branch. To detain a few hired thugs, you had to be civil with them, let them go back and forth before you could act?"

Lu Huaixi stilled.

"You mean I should have just had them dragged off directly?"

She wasn't quite sure how to respond. After a pause, she said quietly, "I've never done anything like this before. It was the first time. I didn't know how."

The softness that crept into Lu Huaixi's voice — the hesitation, the careful restraint in it, the way the last syllable lingered just slightly — fell against Xie Yuanjing's ear like the brush of a feather.

Whatever he'd been about to say stopped short. The vague, hard-to-name anger that had been simmering also scattered, mostly.

If he was honest, the moment he'd seen her standing there holding her own, his chest had already softened.

It was only when he saw the wreckage of the room that it hardened again.

"And you want there to be a second time?"

"I don't."

Lu Huaixi answered immediately. But having said it, she couldn't think of what else to add.

She could tell his anger had come down a little. But she didn't understand why he'd been angry to begin with.

After a moment of quiet, she thought it over and took two steps closer, lowering her voice.

"Are you... upset?"

Upset because she had openly claimed Shun'an Fang without his knowledge, stirring up gossip that had, in passing, dragged the Cheng'en Marquis's residence into it.

"People outside probably won't bring the Marquis's residence into it, and this kind of thing — it's just something people watch for a moment and then forget. No one will really remember—"

"You think what I'm upset about is Shun'an Fang?"

"Well — what else?"

Lu Huaixi looked up and met his eyes, which had grown a shade darker.

She hadn't noticed how close she'd drifted to him when she leaned in. Now she could see it — Xie Yuanjing was near, closer than she'd realized. Especially when he was looking down at her like this; she had the strange sense that his breath could reach her face.

Lu Huaixi instinctively wanted to step back. But the moment she moved, the man shifted toward her.

"Stay still."

The step froze. Her whole body went stiff.

Then, not long after, she felt warmth settle at the side of her neck — fingertips, rough-edged, tracing gently over the skin there. Along with the tingling that spread from his touch came a faint, precise sting.

"Next time something like this happens and you don't tell me, Lu Huaixi — I really will punish you."

Called by her full name, Lu Huaixi found herself completely without words.

But she recovered quickly and furrowed her brow, tilting her head slightly away. "That hurts a little."

"You were cut."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her. "Did you hear what I just said?"

Without waiting for her answer, he continued, "I was genuinely angry. From the moment I heard you had gone to the yamen, all the way here, I've been holding it in."

Passersby drifted past outside. Some caught sight of the two of them standing this close and instinctively looked over to stare.

Whatever composure Lu Huaixi had shown in front of the crowd a moment ago was entirely gone. She felt as though she had been folded into Xie Yuanjing's breath, her whole body rigid and unsteady, the only sensation she could properly register being the touch at the side of her neck that refused to be ignored.

Like a caress. Like a reprimand.

"Why — why are you angry? Can we go inside and sit down first, please?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't move. His fingertips remained where they were, beside the thin mark.

With just a little more pressure, a faint flush would bloom in the skin beneath his touch.

"Today it was only a few easily cowed thugs. But if it had been someone sent with a purpose — someone willing to kill for money, a desperate man with nothing to lose — do you think the handful of people you brought could have protected you long enough for the constables to arrive?"

"It wasn't that serious... I do know my limits. If I couldn't handle it, I wouldn't have pushed my luck."

She hesitated, then asked quietly, "Is that why you're angry?"

Xie Yuanjing neither confirmed nor denied it. He only dropped his voice and asked, "So you'll keep going out alone."

He said, "You'll keep shutting me out and handling everything yourself. Is that how it's going to be?"

chapters.title: Are You Still Angry
chapters.content:
Though Xie Yuanjing's voice was not raised, it carried a gravity that had not been there before.

Lu Huaixi opened her mouth. The words wouldn't come. The look she turned on him grew inexplicably tinged with grievance.

"I didn't."

After a long moment, she managed two words through her teeth.

She didn't like his cold sternness — it reminded her of a tutor about to deliver a scolding, except with more weight behind it than any tutor she'd known.

Xie Yuanjing hadn't meant to frighten her. He'd come prepared to speak with her calmly.

But when he arrived and saw the wreckage in the room, and the thin red line a shard of flying porcelain had left on the side of her neck, he had changed his mind.

Or perhaps — he had simply found, in that moment, that he could not quite hold his temper.

He wanted her to understand: shutting him out was the worst thing she had done today.

"This fine little cut was made by a single shard of flying porcelain. It will fade in a day or two, leaving no trace. But if what flew at you today had been a blade — have you thought about what that would mean?"

"...I hadn't. But I do know."

Lu Huaixi looked down, jaw set. She took a moment longer before she spoke, the words coming out stiffly. "I was sure they were ordinary thugs, and I didn't mean to shut you out. I was only—"

"You were only thinking that the Lu name was enough. That you didn't need anyone else."

Xie Yuanjing cut her off. "Then let me tell you plainly — it isn't."

"You—"

"Going forward, I won't stop you from leaving the residence. But my people must be with you. And the things that happen to you — I cannot be the last to know."

He had no patience for her to formulate an excuse, and no wish to watch her frown and push back. Xie Yuanjing simply said it outright.

With the words still in the air, his fingertips pressed again against the mark on her neck — firmer this time than before.

He didn't release the pressure until he heard her catch her breath in pain, then finally let go and looked at her.

"Good. Remember how that feels. And remember what I said — if you won't listen, Lu Huaixi, I really will punish you."

Xiyuan came out to prostrate herself in apology while the two of them were still standing outside the front door.

The two matrons from the yamen had not laid a hand on her — only looked her over briefly and asked a few questions, without a trace of impatience or contempt.

When Xiyuan learned that Lu Huaixi was the proprietress of Shun'an Fang, the understanding struck her belatedly: it was her proprietress who had been protecting her all along. Though she had agreed to Xiyuan's demand, she had never actually let the matrons touch her, knowing it would cause her pain.

The more she understood, the heavier the guilt became.

Xiyuan wiped her tears and shuffled forward. She had a great deal she wanted to say — to ask for punishment, to express her gratitude. But she had barely gotten two words out before she noticed something was not quite right between the two people standing there.

"Pro... proprietress..."

The words she had prepared were many — but after only two syllables, the man standing before her proprietress startled her into silence.

A young nobleman in fine robes, his bearing upright, his features striking.

Handsome enough to take one's breath away, yet his entire presence carried an air that made one instinctively wary.

Xiyuan's feet stopped where they were. Forward didn't feel right. Back didn't feel right either.

It was only when Lu Huaixi noticed her discomfort and gave a light cough or two that she found a thread to follow.

"Why are you out here?"

Lu Huaixi's voice was steady and calm, carrying a gentle reassurance. Xiyuan felt something settle inside her when she heard it.

Though only Lu Huaixi knew how hard she was working to appear composed right now.

She didn't want them to see her rattled. She didn't want them thinking their proprietress was being scolded.

"Nothing more to worry about out here. Those troublemakers won't dare show their faces so easily again. Rest and recover — we can talk once you're better."

"Thank you, proprietress. I — I..."

Xiyuan stumbled several times, and her surreptitious glances at Xie Yuanjing did not escape Lu Huaixi — giving her an unexpected sense of kinship.

They were both frightened of him. It wasn't just her.

"Don't think on those things anymore. From here on, stay close to Qingling jiejie. Shun'an Fang will still be Shun'an Fang — nothing will change."

Perhaps because Xie Yuanjing's presence was truly too overwhelming, Xiyuan left without managing to say a single one of the things she had planned. She lingered awkwardly for a while, then retreated to the back under Lu Huaixi's gentle reassurances.

After she had gone, Lu Huaixi let out a quiet sigh — though the interruption had actually helped her collect herself considerably.

"Would you like to come in for tea?"

She asked it casually.

Lu Huaixi didn't think this man, having just finished lecturing her, would be in any mood to accept. Yet when the words left her mouth, Xie Yuanjing nodded.

She stared at him again. "Don't you have official business today?"

"Was that question meant to show me the door?"

He turned it back on her immediately, drawing out a flicker of guilt she couldn't quite hide.

"Of course not."

Lu Huaixi rubbed the side of her nose. Seeing that he had no intention of changing his mind, she stepped aside and steeled herself. "I was afraid you'd be bored. Not much to enjoy in there."

"I'll admit the appeal is limited."

Xie Yuanjing continued without missing a beat. "But Lu Huaixi — in name, I am still your husband. I went out of my way to come and back you up. Even if you didn't need it, this scene still has to play out properly."

"In name..."

A complicated look passed through Lu Huaixi's eyes. Then understanding settled in.

He meant they needed to be seen getting along well.

"Right, I see."

"See what?"

Xie Yuanjing exhaled quietly and followed her inside.

"Don't listen to only half of what someone says."

Lu Huaixi led him up to the private room on the upper floor. She was at the top of the stairs before it struck her — there had been more to that sentence.

Going out of his way. To back her up.

—

After the troublemakers were escorted away, someone had quietly followed the constables.

Once they were at a distance, the man being detained managed to shake the gag from his mouth and spat viciously at the woman beside him.

He was just drawing breath to curse when the nearest constable's boot connected with his ribs.

"Keep still! Still looking for trouble?"

"Constable, sir, I've been wrongly accused!"

The man, unwilling to let the opportunity pass, shouted at the figures ahead. "It was all that shrew stirring things up! Once she got a few words of gossip in her ear, there was no stopping her! I was driven half mad and dragged into going along — I never wanted to cause any trouble, sir, I swear it!"

The constable beside him was about to tell him to be quiet when the man in charge suddenly seemed to remember something and gestured for him to wait.

"A few words of gossip, and you expect that to explain away the damage and the injuries?"

"I wouldn't dare deceive you, sir! It really was this woman — she heard someone say that if you wanted something sorted, you had to make a scene, and then she ran out here to humiliate herself. You don't believe me, sir, question her yourself!"

Seeing that the constable showed no sign of relenting, the man turned to curse at the woman for a few more exchanges, then launched back into his pleas.

"I really am being wronged, sir! And the woman who said that — she's a formidable sort herself. Before this, my wife used to work for her, helped her out with quite a bit. This really isn't anything to do with me — it was this jealous woman acting on her own, finding thugs to make trouble!"

"Where is this woman from?"

"From the embroidery house on the west side of the city, the front street. But she already closed up and left for home — went just a few days ago. That gossiping woman, if I ever run into her again, I'll—"

"Enough."

The man had been on the verge of saying more when he seemed to catch himself. "Sir, I didn't hurt anyone — I want to be clear about that! Just now I was worked up by what that girl said and smashed a few things, but I didn't hurt anyone!"

The constable beside him gave him a look, then shoved the gag back in his mouth.

Not far behind, the figure who had been following listened carefully, then made note of the embroidery house on the west side.

But the figure didn't leave. And didn't entirely believe the story.

"Keep watching. Keep digging."

The quiet instruction was given.

The man's account had too deliberately redirected everything toward the wife's jealousy. If it held, the sentencing would come out light.

But the silver found in their home, and the readiness with which they had moved — all of it pointed to premeditation.

If that was the case, then whoever had sent them had not been targeting Shun'an Fang alone.

chapters.title: Let Me Make It Up to You
chapters.content:
Inside Shun'an Fang's private room, Lu Huaixi had barely finished settling Xie Yuanjing into a seat before Qingling came in with a note.

"Proprietress."

She didn't dare look at the First Young Master of the Xie family beside her, and kept her head lowered, treading with unusual care.

"This is from the proprietor of the tavern at the street entrance. He says it's his first time meeting the proprietress of Shun'an Fang, and since they're neighbors on the same street, he hopes you'll do him the honor of sharing a cup of tea. His proprietor has also sent gifts, and says he'd like to discuss a potential business arrangement — though I didn't let them bring the gifts in."

Lu Huaixi took the note and glanced at it, but didn't open it.

"That tavern at the entrance? Didn't they used to try and undercut our business all the time? They even poached our people once."

"That's right. I expect they never imagined our proprietress was you."

Qingling agreed. "Just now, the man they sent over was so nervous he wouldn't even look properly in our direction, afraid of catching someone's eye. That's nothing like how they used to behave. Before all this, they never had such a pleasant manner."

Lu Huaixi gave a quiet scoff and tossed the note aside.

"Their faces change fast enough. Before, their people were saying that Shun'an Fang was all women and couldn't be managed properly — and now they're running over to invite that same woman to tea. Hmph. Who wants to have tea with them? And what makes them think they even have tea worth drinking?"

Qingling was almost undone by Lu Huaixi's petulant tone.

But with someone else in the room, she held it in.

"Then I'll go and turn them down. In any case, Shun'an Fang and that tavern have always been at odds, and I hear they've brought in a group of girls from the south and are keeping them in the back. Sounds like they're looking to run a different kind of trade out of the place."

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed.

Clearly they intended to deal in exactly the kind of business Shun'an Fang refused to touch.

But she couldn't be bothered to dwell on that. She was already turning over the calculation in her mind — whether it was more worthwhile to cut ties entirely or to maintain the thinnest appearance of civility.

"Wait."

Lu Huaixi called Qingling back quickly. "The entrance is the best position on this street. We never made a complete break with them before, and there's even less reason to now. Left to their own devices, they wouldn't dare try anything with us anymore. Go tell them—"

"She won't be going."

From beside her, Xie Yuanjing spoke for the first time, his voice low and level, and the breath Qingling had only just let out caught hard in her throat again.

"Go back and turn them down. Tell them it's from me — and tell them to think carefully about who they're sending a note to."

He paused, then glanced briefly at Qingling and called Gong Zhuo over with a word.

"Go with her. Tell them the First Young Mistress is here on a casual visit, nothing more. If they want to discuss business — they can come to me."

Anyone who heard it would understand at once: no one was going to walk through the door to Xie Yuanjing to discuss a business arrangement. It wasn't an invitation. It was a warning — delivered in person by the man himself.

Qingling looked toward Lu Huaixi, and seeing that she looked startled, as though she hadn't expected this, but showed no sign of disagreeing — Qingling thought for a moment, pressed her lips together in a quiet smile, and stepped out.

"I didn't think you'd involve yourself in something so small."

Once the room had emptied, Lu Huaixi spoke under her breath — and acknowledged the favor in the same breath.

A business dispute among neighbors on the same street — turning them down herself would always invite comment. Accepting would be no better. But Xie Yuanjing had stepped in, and in doing so had both extricated her and held her position.

"I didn't think the proprietress of Shun'an Fang would want me involved in something so small."

Xie Yuanjing echoed her words back to her, with a faint note of reproach woven in — which, inexplicably, made Lu Huaixi laugh.

"What is that. Why are you repeating what I say."

Before the words had fully settled, there was a knock at the door.

It opened to admit Qirui, carrying tea and a plate of rabbit-shaped soft cakes, shaped with particular care.

Something Lu Huaixi liked.

"These are from Xiyuan."

Seeing Lu Huaixi staring at them, Qirui smiled. "She said she was sorry, but she didn't dare come and trouble the proprietress again. So she made some of the things you usually like."

Lu Huaixi didn't make a show of it. She took the plate the same way she always did — with a cheerful, unguarded smile — and tried one.

"These are wonderful. Just the right amount of sweet."

She spooned up another piece and said, "When Xiyuan has a free moment, ask her to think up more things like this. I'll want them again next time I come."

"Of course. I'll go tell her now."

Qirui said nothing further, offered a bow to Lu Huaixi and Xie Yuanjing, and slipped out with the empty tray.

But everyone who heard understood — it was a quiet reassurance meant for Xiyuan. A way of telling her she was still here, still settled, still wanted.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze had barely left Lu Huaixi's face. He waited until she finished the last piece before he finally spoke.

"If you didn't want people to know about your connection to Shun'an Fang, why not keep it hidden?"

He lowered his voice. "If you had wanted to conceal it, it would have been easy enough."

Lu Huaixi dabbed at the corner of her mouth with a handkerchief and took a sip of tea.

Without his displeasure and with the favor he'd just done her still warm between them, his voice in the quiet had a texture to it that was almost comfortable — and she found herself, without quite deciding to, settling into the ease of it.

"It's not that I necessarily had to keep it hidden."

She curved her eyes at him. "Xiyuan, just now — she's a little younger than me. And she's not the only one. There are quite a few girls in Shun'an Fang around that age. The youngest is seven."

"Because she wants to be a dancer?"

"Not entirely, I think — but many of them are girls who simply couldn't find enough to eat. I hadn't thought much about it before today. But today it became clear to me — a proprietress who works only from behind the scenes, with no one to stand behind her, means the girls here will always be at someone's mercy."

Lu Huaixi said it quietly, without drama.

"I may not be anyone particularly formidable, but I do have a name that counts for something. If I want to protect them, I can at least protect them in some small way."

Xie Yuanjing didn't respond.

The private room held only the soft rise and fall of the qin, like wisps of smoke curling upward — gentle threads drifting toward the rafters, catching on nothing, then dissolving.

"Not formidable? What do you mean, not formidable?"

At last he spoke. He reached out and touched her face lightly — just a brush of fingertips. "You're already more than formidable enough. I was angry earlier — but I cannot deny that you had presence out there."

"Really?"

Lu Huaixi blinked, and from that small touch caught, inexplicably, a sense of warmth.

She attributed it to familiarity — the same feeling she had with her mother — and without overthinking it, let her cheek lean a fraction into his hand the way she sometimes did, by way of response.

"Was I convincing? Did I manage to intimidate people?"

"You were. When I arrived, I could see people careful not to get on the wrong side of Second Miss Lu."

Xie Yuanjing spoke, and then smiled again to himself.

Lu Huaixi's cheek had already pulled back. But his hand, oddly, was reluctant to follow.

"I don't believe you for a second."

She made a quiet sound of skepticism, then said, "Are you still angry?"

One piece of music ended. The qin fell silent. The room settled back into stillness.

Xie Yuanjing met her eyes — bright and clear, carrying something that looked unmistakably like trust — and felt something shift, just for a moment.

His fingertips felt warm. Some feeling that refused to be named was seeping through him, strand by strand — making him hesitate, making him want to step back.

But words moved faster than thought.

"If I am — what then?"

"Then I'll make it up to you."

Lu Huaixi answered simply.

Then, thinking of all the times she'd gotten herself in trouble with her mother and gone back with her best apologetic face to talk her way back into her good graces, she couldn't help but let her eyes curve up with a smile.

"I won't dance for you — I'm not that good. But I can play you something on the qin. As thanks for frightening off the tavern keeper for me. Would you like that?"

Xie Yuanjing forgot to respond. He only held onto that phrase — make it up to you.

He sat quietly for a moment, and somewhere in the hollow place inside him it felt as though something was being filled — a fine, spreading warmth that made him reluctant to let his mind wander elsewhere.

chapters.title: Going Back Home to Make Trouble
chapters.content:
After returning to the marquis estate from Shun'an Fang that day, Lu Huaixi had braced herself for a reprimand from the estate's Old Madam or the First Madam.

But nearly three days had passed, and not a single person in the estate had come to ask about it.

The Lu family hadn't either. Only her eldest brother, Lu Yuanzhao, had sent her a letter saying she had gotten impressive — though whether he was genuinely praising her or thinking about giving her a good smack was hard to tell.

A few more days passed.

When Lu Huaixi finally had a quiet moment to think about new dance routines, Jingshuang came in from outside.

"First Young Madam, there's news from Qingling."

"What is it?"

"The messenger says that although those people have been detained, only one charge of theft and one of assault and public disturbance could be established. Nothing else was found."

Jingshuang continued, "Though those two charges are no small thing either — enough to keep them from ever getting back on their feet."

Lu Huaixi had been reclining against the soft chaise with one cheek propped in her hand, turning things over in her mind. She sat up at this, her expression turning serious.

"Nothing else? What about the silver?"

"They're saying the silver came from the woman helping a manager at her former workplace sell off some things. When that place started failing and was about to close, she skimmed some off the top and stole a few things besides."

Jingshuang didn't look convinced by this either, and spoke with a furrowed brow.

"The couple did, in fact, act on someone's advice — that manager's, apparently. He told the woman to go in and make a scene, not let anyone take advantage of them. After that, the manager closed up shop and went back to his hometown, and no one can find him now."

"What did this manager do? Has anyone looked into this business of him going back to his hometown?"

"They have. He ran an embroidery shop for several years, on the front street in the west end of the city."

Jingshuang paused when she finished, then lifted her head slightly and added:

"The manager had no contact with anyone suspicious. The only thing of note is that Third Miss Lu visited that embroidery shop once, some time ago. Though she apparently found it beneath her standards and didn't go back."

Lu Huaixi's brow creased at this. "When? Is it certain it was her?"

"Just two days after your return visit to the Lu family. The west end of the city doesn't see many wealthy visitors, and that embroidery street in particular does sluggish business — the people on that street remember clearly who has come by and who looked well-off.

"When your maidservant heard it mentioned, she thought it sounded like Third Miss Lu, so she had someone make further inquiries at the Lu estate — and it was confirmed that on that day, Third Miss Lu did leave the estate and go to the west end of the city."

Jingshuang said earnestly, "Though all the neighbors say Third Miss Lu only went the once, and didn't stay in the shop long — just took one look and left with a rather disdainful expression."

"Why do they remember it so clearly?"

"They were all standing out front, hoping to draw wealthy customers into their own shops."

Lu Huaixi said nothing more after hearing this.

It was Jingshuang who, after waiting a long while and still feeling uneasy, spoke again. "The embroidery shop closing up so suddenly is admittedly strange. Your maidservant has already arranged to pass word of the couple's situation to Third Miss Lu's side — if it really is——"

"It's probably her."

Lu Huaixi said it lightly, and didn't seem particularly angry.

"Everything she uses has to be refined and costly. There's no way she'd have any interest in wandering around a place she looks down on — the west end of the city especially, she never goes there. Though it is rather foolish of her to be traced back to that embroidery shop so easily."

"Third Miss Lu must have been trying to keep it secret. She simply stands out too much."

Jingshuang watched Lu Huaixi as she spoke. "The people investigating had to spend two days on it. They said that on the day Third Miss Lu left the estate, she changed locations several times and even changed her clothes — as though she was going to meet someone."

"By all appearances, this matter can't be separated from her. But there's something I genuinely can't work out: what does Third Miss Lu gain from going to all this trouble to scheme against you?"

"She gains from me not doing well."

Lu Huaixi's tone was indifferent. As she rose, she picked up a piece of pastry from the side table and put it in her mouth.

When she had finished, she continued, "She probably thought Shun'an Fang truly was running dirty business, and wanted to humiliate me in public — have people point their fingers, and then have my husband's family turn against me."

There were still a few things she hadn't quite sorted out.

Such as how Lu Tangshu had even learned about Shun'an Fang. And if she had been clever enough to hatch such a roundabout scheme, why hadn't she been clever enough to not go to the west end of the city herself?

"Have someone prepare the carriage."

"First Young Madam is going out?"

"Yes. Back to the Lu estate."

Lu Huaixi walked toward the bronze mirror. "Life has been too dull lately. I'm going back to make a little trouble. Oh, and — find a way to make sure those two in prison don't have too comfortable a time of it."

Xie Yuanjing had said she was too well-mannered — that even with her standing behind her, she still insisted on following proper procedure. Fine then. She would stop concerning herself with procedure entirely.

Even if nothing else could be pinned on them, they were going to suffer in there.

In the carriage, Yaoshu, who had by now heard the news, was feeling indignant on her behalf.

"I never thought she could be this vicious. You're already married and out of the house, and she's still scheming against you — she must just not be able to stand......"

The words trailed off there. Perhaps thinking better of it, Yaoshu swallowed the rest of the phrase — can't stand to see you do well.

But she didn't stay quiet for long. After a moment, she leaned over again and said quietly:

"First Young Madam, don't let this weigh on you. No matter what happens with Shun'an Fang, the Young Master keeps you in mind and looks out for you. Let that one stew in her own bitterness."

"How do you know about that?"

"I caught a little bit."

Yaoshu smiled. "The day the Young Master was outside Shun'an Fang, he said out loud in front of everyone that he had come to back you up. It's been the talk of the street for days now."

This was news to Lu Huaixi.

That day outside Shun'an Fang, she and Xie Yuanjing had been too far apart — she hadn't caught what he said to the crowd. She had thought that coming in person was already enough to show where he stood, but she hadn't imagined he would say it plainly to strangers.

Lu Huaixi was about to ask Yaoshu more when the carriage suddenly slowed.

"Are we there already?"

Yaoshu leaned forward and lifted a corner of the curtain. "Couldn't be this quick yet."

"We're getting close, but the road ahead is blocked. We'll have to cut through this side alley — there's a carriage stopped right up ahead, sitting there taking up space, right in the middle of everything."

The driver said a few words, and Yaoshu followed his line of sight to look.

Lu Huaixi did the same.

"That carriage...... looks a little familiar."

After a moment, Lu Huaixi thought back to that time before the wedding, when she had been lured out under false pretenses and found He Jianxing in a drunken state — and it seemed like it had been this same sort of carriage.

"Isn't that the young master of the He family?"

Yaoshu had seen him once before. She narrowed her eyes to look more carefully. "What is the He family's carriage doing stopped here? They don't live around here anymore."

Just before she dropped the curtain, Yaoshu looked one more time — and then, as if something had occurred to her, lowered her voice to murmur:

"Word is this He young master's engagement has fallen apart. The girl's family has kicked up a fuss and called off the match. And here he is, not trying to save his own engagement, just sitting around with nothing better to do."

Lu Huaixi raised an eyebrow. She didn't pick up a lot of gossip, but that didn't mean she didn't listen.

Especially now, when she had a rather strong distaste for He Jianxing.

"You know about that too?"

"Your maidservant has to keep watch. Last time this He young master already had a betrothal, and yet his portrait somehow ended up in your hands — of course your maidservant had to keep her ears open after that. Can't have someone taking advantage of the situation with bad intentions."

Yaoshu said it earnestly, with a furrowed brow.

"Word is this Young Master He isn't someone who keeps himself in line. He was already about to take a wife, and was still keeping another woman's things on him — and not the drinking and carousing kind, either. Your maidservant suspects they were things like handkerchiefs and jade pendants.

"When this came to light, he apparently felt humiliated, shoved the girl, and then turned around and accused her of being jealous and having too much of a temper."

Lu Huaixi had gotten the general picture.

Along with disgust, there was a flicker of genuine disbelief.

A man who needed his wife's family to prop him up, and he still had the audacity to carry on like this — truly believing he was something remarkable. What a laughingstock.

"Your maidservant even made special inquiries about the young lady's family. Truly a respectable scholarly household — good that she's calling off the engagement. If she hadn't, your maidservant would have been tempted to go and talk some sense into her."

Lu Huaixi burst out laughing.

"You looked into that too? Were you actually thinking of going and getting involved in someone else's engagement?"

"You really do mind everyone's business."

At the same hour, Xie Yuanjing was in the deep red of his official robes, cold and impassive.

Shen Zhouxu stood beside him, and after listening to him call Gong Zhuo over to give instructions, couldn't help muttering:

"You're keeping track of how many young girls are in Lu Huaixi's shop? Why don't you just open a proper school for girls and make her the teacher?"

"Be quiet."

Xie Yuanjing didn't even look up.

chapters.title: You Mind Too Much of Other People's Business
chapters.content:
Shen Zhouxu was about to say something back when a young man came walking over from the side.

Seeing the two of them, he stopped, gave Shen Zhouxu a nod, and then looked toward Xie Yuanjing.

"I was still on my way back to the capital when you got married — didn't make it in time. But from what I hear, your wife is quite young. Getting along with someone like that must be a bit of a trial, I'd imagine."

The man was dressed in fine brocade, every inch of him radiating wealth.

He spoke with a smile, outwardly pleasant, yet with an undercurrent of arrogance that made him difficult to warm to.

"Get together tonight? I've just taken in a new batch — right around the right age. Come pick a couple to bring back and keep yourself entertained."

Xie Yuanjing's brow drew together, almost imperceptibly, and then the man continued: "Oh, and someone asked me to bring you something — said it's to congratulate the great Young Master Xie on his wedding. The poor thing — I couldn't bring myself to refuse on your behalf."

"Don't know who it's from. Not accepting it."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at the man, his tone perfectly flat.

The man didn't seem particularly bothered, only smiled again. "Really not taking it? I thought the person was, at the very least, something of a...... confidante of yours?"

Xie Yuanjing's lips curved, just slightly, and a short quiet laugh escaped him.

"Officer Zheng has been away from the capital for some years — misunderstandings are inevitable. But that phrase — best not to say it loosely going forward. My wife has a candid nature; if she heard it, she'd believe it."

The words away from the capital for some years made the man's expression shift briefly — though he recovered quickly.

"So you've taken this marriage seriously after all. I'd assumed it was a matter of going through the motions, giving the Lu family some face...... it seems certain things are better left unsaid from now on."

After the man left, Shen Zhouxu's eyes lingered on his retreating figure.

He was just about to say something when the man beside him turned and made to leave.

"Where are you going? Want to have a drink tonight?"

"To the Lu estate."

Xie Yuanjing recalled the news he had just received, and said without particular urgency, "She's going back there today to make trouble. I'll go and pick her up."

"...... What kind of trouble needs you to make the trip yourself? And she's not exactly going to come off the worse end of things in the Lu estate, is she? Did Zheng Xiaoqi just get under your skin?"

"You mind too much of other people's business."

The phrase thrown right back at him made Shen Zhouxu sputter.

—

Inside the Lu estate, Lu Huaixi went directly to Lu Tangshu's Lanqing Courtyard. She didn't even wait to be announced — she simply pushed the door open and walked in.

The person inside hadn't had time to school her expression. Lu Huaixi caught a flash of irritation on her face at a glance.

And then, upon seeing who it was — surprise.

"You——"

She seemed to be about to demand why Lu Huaixi had barged in unannounced, but Lu Huaixi didn't give her the chance.

"Wanted to see me make a fool of myself, did you?"

She walked over and sat down naturally beside Lu Tangshu, unhurried, even helping herself to a cup of tea. "Next time you want to pull something like this, be cleaner about it. Either leave no trace at all, or come at me directly."

"What — what are you talking about? You're making no sense."

Lu Tangshu was rattled. She bit her lip and glared at the person in front of her.

She was still seething inside, half-tempted to fly at her right then and there. But she didn't dare.

She still needed the first branch to show her some leniency. And besides, she had the nagging sense that this supposedly worthless second sister of hers was somehow harder to get past than she used to be.

Seeing her hesitate, Lu Huaixi let her gaze rest on her face for a moment, then smiled at her — the picture of easy-going affability.

"Those people who caused trouble at Shun'an Fang are already in prison. I won't let them out anytime soon. The way I see it, they'll need to come out of there missing an arm or a leg before my anger cools. As for you — don't sleep too soundly."

"What — what Shun'an Fang, what prison — I don't know what you're talking about."

Lu Tangshu went a shade paler, but held herself together well enough, only tightening her grip around her teacup.

"Second Sister barging into my courtyard like this and throwing all this mud at me — isn't that a bit much? Even if something has truly happened, Second Sister should at least come with evidence."

"I don't have evidence."

Lu Huaixi said it plainly. "And I'm too lazy to go looking for any. This is just the two of us dropping all pretense — no need for that sort of thing."

"You——"

"Instead of spending your time thinking about how to make the marquis estate turn against me, you'd do better thinking about your own marriage prospects. The marquis estate isn't going to do anything to me. My father and mother won't blame me either. It's you who should be worried — if you can't find a husband, and then end up in the palace without knowing how to conduct yourself, you'll end up with nothing in the end."

At the mention of marriage, a flash of vexation crossed Lu Tangshu's face.

Lu Huaixi caught it clearly, then looked away as if she hadn't noticed, and picked up the teacup beside her.

Having been struck where it hurt, and with the other person now making it clear she was done being civil, Lu Tangshu had no more patience for keeping her temper in check. She fixed Lu Huaixi with a hard stare, her eyes full of fury and resentment.

"Going into the palace was your doing all along! Isn't it enough that you've ruined me — now you want to blame it on me too? Do you really think that just because you've married into the marquis estate, you have someone to fall back on? Xie Yuanjing just finds you a novelty. Once he comes back to his senses and remembers you have nothing to offer, neither he nor the estate will give you a second glance!"

"And yet here you are, spending your energy worrying about whether he'll give me a second glance."

Lu Huaixi let out a short laugh. "Whoever has reaped what they sowed knows it themselves. I didn't come here today to discuss anything else with you. I came to tell you——"

She glanced at Jingshuang, who stepped forward immediately, seized Lu Tangshu's arms with one hand, and with the other gripped her by the jaw, pinning her so she couldn't move.

The maidservant who tried to run out and alert someone was shoved firmly back in by Yaoshu.

In short order, the pain of having her arm twisted behind her back brought tears spilling from Lu Tangshu's eyes.

Lu Huaixi paid no attention. She raised her hand and tipped the contents of the teacup directly into Lu Tangshu's face.

"Because of your own selfish designs, you nearly destroyed the lives of the girls in my Shun'an Fang. I will not let that go. And another thing — I don't care where you got your information, but if you want to use something like this to ruin my reputation, you had best think harder first. Never mind one Shun'an Fang — even if I had truly opened a brothel, a trick as feeble as this could never bring me down."

The tea slid down Lu Tangshu's face.

Her eyes, which had been open at first, closed instinctively. Her eyes reddened — whether from the water stinging them, or because she had actually begun to cry.

"You don't need to feel aggrieved about any of this. The gates of the Chengen Marquis Estate are right there. If you think Xie Yuanjing would have been better off marrying you instead of me — go tell him so yourself. If you can get him to annul the marriage and take you instead, I won't say a single word against it. I'll even help dress you for the wedding and see you off in style."

Lu Huaixi had genuinely lost her temper. Looking at her, she couldn't help lifting the now-empty teacup and smashing it on the floor.

"All these schemes you run day after day — and in the end you can't even keep them from getting traced back to you. Lu Tangshu. You are truly, deeply stupid."

chapters.title: The Punishment You Have Coming Is Different From Everyone Else's
chapters.content:
By the time Xie Yuanjing arrived at the Lu estate, Lu Huaixi had already gotten her grievances out and made her way to her mother's courtyard.

For a married daughter to suddenly come running home — Madam Liu was so doting that she could only feel delighted.

Even when she heard about the commotion that had just come from the second branch, she didn't find anything amiss.

"Mother, find a few people to keep an eye on Lu Tangshu. I have a feeling she's been corresponding privately with someone."

"Someone you know?"

"Yes."

"I've been keeping an eye on the second branch overall — I forgot to watch her separately."

Madam Liu thought of it and felt only irritated. "All that pleasantness to your face while stabbing you in the back — with a mind like that, imagine what she'd get up to inside the palace, where you'd never be rid of her."

Vicious people should be left to be ground down by other vicious people. A moment's softness would only harm yourself.

"Don't trouble yourself with it. I have my hands in her affairs already. At most it's another two months, and there's still the fourth one waiting to make her life miserable — that one won't let Lu Tangshu get off easy."

"I know. I just find her irritating to look at. She can't even scheme properly — she's both foolish and infuriating."

"Complaining that her methods are too crude, are you?"

At this, Madam Liu couldn't help laughing. Then, as if something had occurred to her, she took her daughter's hand and said, "Since Shun'an Fang is yours, the next time we host a banquet, we'll invite performers from there. What do you think?"

"Fine by me."

Lu Huaixi nodded and curved her lips into a smile. "Though you'll have to pay the proper rate, Mother. It goes in the ledger."

"Keeping such strict accounts — you're not planning to come out of pocket even once?"

"Of course not. I'm already married out of the family. That can wait until I'm back visiting. And when I am back, I'll cover one or two evenings for you — but we'd have to be discreet about it. Our head manager is very strict."

"Strict is good. Otherwise with someone like you in charge, you'd be giving money away."

"How could that be? Mother, you really have no faith in me at all."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft indignant sound, but her face never lost its smile — clearly unaffected by any of the events of the day.

Madam Liu looked at her and finally let out a breath of relief.

She had said that for two reasons: first, to show her attitude toward Shun'an Fang and put her daughter's mind at ease; and second, because for estate banquets, this arrangement was genuinely the most convenient.

But as they exchanged a few laughing words, her gaze drifted to Lu Huaixi's face and stayed there.

Her daughter was at exactly the age when the heart first begins to stir. Spending so much time with someone like Xie Yuanjing — it would be hard not to develop some soft, hazy feelings.

Madam Liu sometimes worried. She was afraid her daughter might fall for someone unsuitable, and then find it hard to let go when the year was up and they parted ways.

But looking at her now, she seemed — all right. For the time being.

"You — honestly, all you ever think about is how to get money out of your mother."

Madam Liu said it teasingly, and tapped her daughter's forehead with one finger.

Lu Huaixi didn't look the least bit embarrassed. She hooked her arm through Madam Liu's and gave it a little swing.

She was just about to say that she wanted to stay and eat dinner at the estate tonight, when the voice of a maidservant drifted in from outside.

"Your maidservant pays her respects to the Young Master."

The words Lu Huaixi hadn't yet spoken died on her lips. She turned her head toward the wooden door, eyes rounding with curiosity.

She hadn't been paying attention when it was said on the day of her return visit after the wedding — but hearing the words Young Master spoken aloud today felt, for some strange reason, quite novel.

Madam Liu was also a little surprised. She glanced at her daughter. "You asked him to come?"

"No." Lu Huaixi shook her head immediately. "I came to deal with Lu Tangshu. Why would I ask him along?"

"Could he have come to keep you in line? Your father isn't here, so it can't be on your father's account."

"Him coming to keep me in line wouldn't be unusual."

Lu Huaixi muttered under her breath, "He looks like he doesn't say much and keeps to himself, but actually he manages me quite a lot."

Madam Liu paused. The look she turned on her daughter suddenly held a hint of something more careful.

But she didn't dwell on it for long. Seeing the maidservant enter, she gathered herself and rose.

"Madam, the Young Master has come to take Second Miss home. Not wanting to disturb Madam and Miss from their private conversation, he is currently waiting in the courtyard."

"Waiting outside? In this heat? Go and invite him in at once. Bring tea."

"Wait."

Lu Huaixi called the retreating maidservant back. "Bring some ice as well."

"Ice for what?" Madam Liu asked.

"To put in the tea."

—

"Please have some tea, Officer Zheng."

Zheng Xiaoqi, who had received nothing but a cold reception from Xie Yuanjing, was now seated in a teahouse where he had arranged to meet a colleague.

He had only recently been transferred back to the capital. Compared to his more brash days, he had smoothed out considerably — otherwise, a modest teahouse like this and a colleague of no particular standing would never have merited his time.

"You've had a long day, Officer Zheng."

"Not at all, Officer Zhou."

Zheng Xiaoqi answered offhandedly.

"I saw Officer Zheng speaking with Lord Xie today, and knowing the two of you are acquainted, I had actually thought to invite Lord Xie to join us."

The man beside him was somewhere around thirty, his manner of speaking carrying a mild flattery that was nonetheless easy to sit with.

"Is that so — and why didn't you? Because Yuanjing wouldn't come?"

"Not exactly. I just remembered that Lord Xie has rarely gone out to socialize since his wedding — I didn't think it was my place to ask."

The man smiled. "After all, Lord Xie was just married. Naturally he'd want to keep his household happy."

"That does sound rather unlike him."

Zheng Xiaoqi seemed to find his interest suddenly piqued, and sat up slightly. "I heard Lord Xie's new wife is quite young, and that the wedding wasn't originally planned to be a large affair — no one knew anything about it?"

"She's not especially young — the second daughter of the Lu family. By all accounts a very fine young lady in both appearance and temperament. There's the occasional bit of talk here and there, but nothing serious. As for the wedding not being planned as a large affair — that's not quite right either."

The man said, "The day he came to ask for her hand, quite a stir was made of it. Word even reached the palace. His Majesty, who normally keeps a cool expression around Lord Xie, actually smiled a few times when it came up."

Zheng Xiaoqi nodded with a smile, looking perfectly pleasant on the surface — though a flash of quiet disdain moved quickly through his eyes.

Whether that imperial smile was because of the Lu family, or because of Xie Yuanjing himself, remained to be seen.

"A young lady from the Lu family — of course she'd be exceptional."

Zheng Xiaoqi poured himself another cup of tea. "I also heard the young lady runs a little entertainment venue of some kind — quite an interesting character, by the sound of it."

"It's not much more than a young girl's little amusement. Though a few of the dancers there are quite remarkable — I wouldn't have expected them to be under this Second Miss Lu's care."

"Is that so. Then I'll have to go and take a look sometime — show my support."

Zheng Xiaoqi smiled. "Yuanjing used to enjoy listening to a particular girl sing, even stood up for her once. I wonder if there's anyone at Shun'an Fang who suits him even better."

The man across from him did not pick up that thread. He didn't so much as show the slightest curiosity about the girl who had been mentioned.

He wasn't foolish enough to. Flattering one person by slighting another was a trade not worth making.

Zheng Xiaoqi didn't seem to care whether or not he was being listened to, and went on drinking his tea.

—

In the carriage, Lu Huaixi sat beside Xie Yuanjing, gazing at the curtain ahead, her mind drifting slightly.

Before long she grew drowsy, and stifled a yawn.

"You came all that way to make trouble — so why the long face?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at Lu Huaixi, who hadn't said a word, and watched the full range of her emotions display themselves plainly across her face. He let out a quiet laugh.

"If the trouble wasn't satisfying enough, we can turn around right now."

That finally made Lu Huaixi look at him.

"And what would we do if we went back?"

"Have her tied up and beaten."

Xie Yuanjing said it casually. "There are instruments in the dungeon. A few days in there, and she'd be much more well-behaved."

The man before her spoke as though it were nothing, yet Lu Huaixi had the inexplicable sense that he would actually do it.

She looked at him — studying the handsome face, beautiful and cold all at once.

"You're genuinely frightening."

"Have I frightened you?"

Lu Huaixi thought about it, then shook her head. "No."

"Good. Because I won't frighten you."

At those words, Lu Huaixi fixed her eyes on his carefully. "Then if I get into trouble, or cause some disaster — you won't frighten me either?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her, then curved his lips toward her slightly. "You have your own punishment coming. It's different from everyone else's."

chapters.title: Do You Trust Me?
chapters.content:
The carriage moved along the main street. Perhaps because the road ahead had more people than usual, it slowed, and every now and then the faint sounds from outside drifted in.

When Lu Huaixi grew bored in a carriage, she would usually lift the curtain to look outside.

But right now, she couldn't spare a single thought for it.

"What punishment?"

She couldn't help leaning toward Xie Yuanjing, her dark eyes full of undisguised curiosity. "Like how my father punishes my elder brother?"

"If you want to know, cause some trouble next time and find out."

"......"

Lu Huaixi sat back before long. "I don't want to know."

The person in front of him was genuinely entertaining. Xie Yuanjing reached out instinctively, wanting to pinch her cheek again.

But the moment the pad of his finger touched her face, something in him flickered.

The warmth of it made his heartbeat slow for just an instant. Delayed, he realized he shouldn't be giving in to these unguarded gestures of closeness.

He stopped where he was, his movement growing slightly stiff, as if his mind had wandered.

Lu Huaixi, watching him, assumed he was going to soothe her the same way as before. With easy familiarity, she leaned her cheek into his hand on her own, just barely, and then sat back upright.

"My mother says I don't need to bother with Lu Tangshu's affairs."

"Mm."

"She says it's only another two months or so. She says Lu Tangshu wants everything and will end up with nothing."

"Mm."

"But I'm still going to get involved. I'm not going to just——"

Xie Yuanjing made another sound of acknowledgment. Lu Huaixi frowned and looked at him.

"Never mind, I'm not talking to you. You're just going through the motions."

When Xie Yuanjing withdrew his hand, the carriage had turned off that street, and the pace picked up again.

Lu Huaixi used the gentle sway of the turn as cover to shift herself outward, putting some distance between them.

The blatant sulking of it pulled him back from wherever his thoughts had gone.

Xie Yuanjing rubbed his fingertips together quietly, then looked at the side of her face where she had turned away.

Without much delay — almost at once — he pulled her back toward him.

"Sit properly."

He said it quietly. "I wasn't going through the motions. I was thinking."

Seeing that Lu Huaixi's curiosity had turned her face back toward him, Xie Yuanjing gave a small inward smile, though his expression was now considerably more serious.

"Have you already guessed that what happened with Shun'an Fang involves someone else besides your third sister?"

"Yes."

"Then why are you unhappy, even though you have a lead?"

Xie Yuanjing asked, "When you got into the carriage just now — you were already thinking about this, weren't you?"

"Yes. How do you always know everything."

Lu Huaixi settled back beside him. "If there really is someone else behind this — it has to be someone I know...... no, someone I'm close to."

An ordinary person would have no way of knowing about Shun'an Fang. Whoever knew, or could even have guessed, must have had some degree of closeness with her at some point.

Back to the matter at hand, Lu Huaixi's eyelids drooped, the energy going out of her. "Whoever it is — it's someone familiar who has turned against me. What is there to be happy about?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at her and said nothing.

He rarely saw dejection or low spirits on Lu Huaixi's face.

She always seemed to have energy to spare — even when she was unhappy, it was written all over her face, a clear invitation for someone to come and coax her. Very easy to comfort.

But now — she was genuinely disappointed.

Xie Yuanjing decided this time was not the moment for comfort. He felt that Lu Huaixi needed to learn to keep faith in people — in anyone.

"You——"

His lips parted, the words ready — but when he caught the look of dimmed brightness in her eyes, something shifted without his meaning it to, and a different sentence came out instead.

"I'll have people look into this. You don't need to worry about it anymore."

Seeing her look up at him, he continued, "I hear business at Shun'an Fang has been good lately. Instead of sitting here brooding and making yourself miserable, put your mind to making money — and making other people miserable."

He paused, and looked at her. "Do you trust me?"

After a moment, Lu Huaixi nodded.

"I do."

—

Once they returned to the estate, the carriage didn't linger — it turned and headed back out again.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing about where he was going. Lu Huaixi only watched the carriage roll away into the distance, and didn't ask.

Some things were better not thought about too long. The longer you dwelt on them, the more likely they were to drift in the wrong direction.

Two more days passed before Zhou Xianya came to find her.

Lu Huaixi had just finished making plans for the lake excursion when she heard Zhou Xianya's invitation to go out. She turned at once and called Yaoshu to come help her change.

"Xianya jiejie isn't coming in?"

"She isn't, First Young Madam."

Yaoshu held up a light-colored dress. "Miss Zhou says she came without notice, and that this isn't the Lu estate — she said it would be presumptuous to come in unannounced."

Lu Huaixi said nothing for a moment at that.

Come to think of it, she supposed that was true. At the Lu estate, Zhou Xianya could drop by to see her at any time. But here at the marquis estate, even she herself was only a temporary guest.

"First Young Madam, don't be downcast. Miss Zhou says Miao Zhen Pavilion has just received a lot of new things from outside, and she slipped out herself without even taking the family carriage."

While they were talking, Gong Zhuo stopped Jingshuang outside and said a few words. Jingshuang then came in carrying a small booklet.

"First Young Madam, this is a record the Young Master had drawn up of the younger girls at Shun'an Fang. The Young Master says to have a look — if any of them would like to attend a girls' school, arrangements have already been made on that end. They can be sent over starting tomorrow."

Lu Huaixi was taken aback.

She took the booklet and looked through it. The girls listed were all around ten years of age or younger. A few had marks beside their names — presumably indicating they wished to go to school.

"The Young Master says Shun'an Fang doesn't only need singers and dancers. Girls who have no interest in performing can learn other things and still be Shun'an Fang's people — and even if they don't stay on there in the long run, it would still be to the First Young Madam's benefit."

Lu Huaixi fell quiet. She thought back suddenly to what she had said to Xie Yuanjing that day.

"The youngest is only seven. Some of them don't really have their hearts in it — they're just looking for a way to make a living. Trying to carve out some path for themselves."

He had taken those words to heart.
