And what he was doing was genuinely an act of kindness — more thoughtful than what she herself had managed. Yet she knew this person didn't do things out of sudden goodwill. He was doing this because of what Jingshuang had said at the end: to her benefit.

To her benefit.

Lu Huaixi turned it over in her mind again.

Her reputation, Shun'an Fang's reputation — both would shift, in some way, because of this.

"I understand."

After a long moment, Lu Huaixi finally nodded.

There was no reason to refuse. She would accept his kindness, and she would remember it.

"I'll take them myself tomorrow."

—

It was only when Lu Huaixi stepped out of the estate and saw Zhou Xianya that the tangle of thoughts finally scattered, and a smile found its way back to her face.

The two of them hadn't managed a private outing since the wedding, and finally getting together today made Lu Huaixi so happy she almost felt like crying.

"Don't stand there tearing up at the estate gate. They'll have you hauled off."

"Hauled off for what?"

"For upsetting the First Young Madam of the marquis estate."

Zhou Xianya laughed — the composed, gentle manner she wore for outsiders gone, replaced by the easy closeness of an old friend.

"So then," she said, giving Lu Huaixi's cheek a gentle pinch. "Is your husband treating you well?"

chapters.title: A Familiar Face You Don't Like
chapters.content:
There were many forms of address after the wedding that still caught Lu Huaixi off guard.

Like the words Young Master spoken by the maidservants on her last visit to the Lu estate. And now, the word husband in Zhou Xianya's mouth.

When she herself said it in jest, it never felt like much. But hearing it from someone close to her — that was a different matter. Lu Huaixi had, as ever, a rather telling reaction: her face went warm.

She was not a coy person by nature, and she hadn't taken any real liberties with Xie Yuanjing, so she simply composed herself and nodded.

"He's a good person. Treats me quite well."

Zhou Xianya seemed relieved, though she was clearly still a little astonished — their whole circuit of Miao Zhen Pavilion wasn't enough to put an end to her exclamations about Xie Yuanjing.

Only when they settled into a newly opened restaurant did Lu Huaixi's ears get any peace.

"Isn't the lake excursion coming up in a few days?"

Lu Huaixi took her arm as they walked. "You'll get to see him then. Though he can look rather severe sometimes — but it's just how he looks. Don't take it too much to heart, Xianya jiejie."

"Just how he looks?"

Zhou Xianya's eyes went wide. "Do you know what people say about your husband out there? Though of course rumors aren't always reliable, and I trust you over anything else."

"Being severe doesn't mean he bites people." Lu Huaixi laughed.

"You'd think, but you can't always be sure...... this place looks busy, I wonder if there are still rooms upstairs — let me find someone to ask——"

"There are, there are — right this way, two young misses."

The words had barely left her mouth when the proprietor came forward with a smile.

"Perfect timing, young misses — there's one last room upstairs. Brand new, clean and bright."

He led the way. "You two look like fine and distinguished ladies — as it happens, the kitchen is testing new dishes today. I'll have the server bring you a special portion of our house specialty, plus some tea and pastries on the side. Come back again if it suits your taste."

Lu Huaixi blinked. It was her first time encountering a proprietor this enthusiastic.

But when they reached the upper floor and saw the room nearest the staircase, it became clear why.

Private enough, in its way — but it was the room closest to the outside. You could hear anyone coming or going on the stairs, and if the door was left open, you might even catch someone's eye as they passed.

Zhou Xianya hesitated. She looked at Lu Huaixi. "Should we...... go somewhere else?"

This was a new place, and Zhou Xianya hadn't been able to go out much lately. She had been looking forward to it when they arrived.

Lu Huaixi could see she was only thinking of her — worried she wouldn't be able to eat in peace. She shook her head and curved her eyes into a smile.

"The proprietor's going to bring us extra food. That's practically free money — we're not going anywhere else."

That one smile, and the whole room smiled along with her.

The door was soon shut, cutting off the noise from outside.

"This place really is doing well — the food must be decent."

Zhou Xianya settled into her seat. "I've been hungry for a while now."

The restaurant was busy, but the dishes came out at a reasonable pace. In addition to the local flavors of the capital, there was a decent selection from other regions as well.

Lu Huaixi had a sweet tooth, and later ordered a braised pork dish from the south, which leaned on the sweeter side.

When the red-glazed stewed meat arrived, the server also brought out an extra serving of post-meal tea and pastries.

With people coming in and out to deliver dishes, the door was left open a crack.

Lu Huaixi was busy staring at the braised pork, which looked as good as it smelled, when an elbow nudged her gently.

"What is it, Xianya jiejie?"

She looked up and found the person beside her had her gaze fixed on something outside. She followed it.

"That's...... Lu Tangshu?"

Not far off, at the top of the staircase, Lu Tangshu emerged with an irritated expression — she seemed to have been called over by someone, for she paused there briefly.

But she turned away quickly and left without lingering.

"Your sister is out meeting someone, looking that put-out about it."

"I don't know."

Lu Huaixi looked away and carefully lifted a piece of meat into her own dish.

She set her chopsticks down before eating, though, since they were still talking.

"She can't have been having a good time of it lately."

"Is that so? I heard the second branch has been arranging matches for her — I'd have thought she was doing well enough. Though I'm only telling you this."

Zhou Xianya lowered her voice. "It was the same with your wedding — one day there was nothing, and the next it was settled and done with. Now this third sister of yours seems to be in the same situation, sneaking around to meet potential matches in secret. What's with your family and all this secrecy?"

Lu Huaixi was momentarily at a loss, and then she smiled at the person in front of her.

"Since it's all being done in secret, Xianya jiejie, how do you know she's looking for a match?"

"Because they came sniffing around my brother."

Zhou Xianya didn't bother softening it. "Between you and me, if it were you — I wouldn't say a single word against it, I'd help things along myself. But your third sister——"

She said it directly. "I don't like her. And neither does my brother."

"Well, your brother didn't exactly like me either."

Lu Huaixi laughed. "When I was going through the matchmaking process, I never saw your brother's portrait. Clearly he didn't want to be considered."

"Impossible. My brother would never not want to be considered."

Zhou Xianya was unconvinced. "Don't try to pull something over on me — did you forget I know you two were already matched before, so there was no need for portraits?"

Lu Huaixi choked on her words, only then realizing she had let something slip.

She didn't want to keep things from Zhou Xianya, but this sort of thing — best not to drag anyone else into the water.

Though it was true she had never seen Zhou Xianya's brother's portrait. Maybe it hadn't been put in, or maybe someone had taken it out.

"I was just talking. So your family isn't willing to consider it?"

"Not willing. My mother said if it were you...... anyway, never mind you, let's talk about your third sister."

Lu Huaixi listened a while longer.

She wasn't particularly surprised. She knew her mother had been working on the question of Lu Tangshu's marriage — and she had no intention of letting her have an easy time of it. A few well-placed pieces of information were enough to make the second branch panic, and their desperation made them more careless than she had ever been when she was being matched. And the more desperate they were, the more likely they were to make mistakes.

While Zhou Xianya was still talking, someone passed outside the door again.

Both of them instinctively glanced at the movement beyond.

"That's......"

Lu Huaixi recognized the figure and her brow drew together, a flash of distaste moving through her eyes.

He Jianxing again. All dressed up, fancying himself charming and debonair — one look was already one look too many.

"Why is it always someone unpleasant everywhere I turn — first your third sister, now this He family......"

Zhou Xianya's words were still coming.

Lu Huaixi reached for her teacup — and froze the moment her fingers found the warmth of the cup.

A thought surfaced in her mind, unbidden and unwelcome.

These two. Could they actually be here together?

If so — the carriage stopped in the side alley near the Lu estate a few days ago — could that have had something to do with Lu Tangshu too?

"Jingshuang."

Lu Huaixi looked up at once. "Go and see."

Lu Tangshu looked down on He Jianxing — that was certain. And He Jianxing would never be able to tolerate Lu Tangshu's temper. If these two were somehow entangled, the days ahead would be nothing but chaos for them.

But their chaos, for her, would be a rather satisfying kind of relief.

Thinking of it that way, it actually didn't seem so bad.

Lu Huaixi tucked her expression away and turned back to chatting with Zhou Xianya.

The two of them finished their meal, lingered over tea for a while, and when they finally came downstairs, the noise of the restaurant had quieted considerably — barely half the crowd of when they had arrived.

As they prepared to head back, Zhou Xianya took her arm with a reluctant expression.

"I can't exactly come to the marquis estate, so next time you come to mine. You haven't been in ages — we can't only see each other a handful of times in a whole year."

She sighed.

"Not long ago you used to bring Wu Wenlan along to keep me company every now and then. Now...... speaking of which, I ran into Wu Wenlan a couple of days ago. She was asking after you — whether you were doing well, whether you'd been treated poorly."

Zhou Xianya frowned. "I told her of course you were doing well, and of course you weren't being mistreated. Though I'd guess she's trying to make amends and just using me as an excuse to bring it up. She has no idea how to go about it."

chapters.title: Are You Dealing With Her, or Dealing With Me?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi stilled for just a moment at the name, but quickly let the feeling pass.

"I'm not reconciling with anyone. If two people can't walk the same path, they part ways."

"I know your nature. You never owed her anything — she was the one who wronged your trust."

Zhou Xianya gave her a gentle hug, confirmed the time of the lake outing once more, and returned to her own carriage.

Beyond that first brief moment, Wu Wenlan's name left no lasting impression. By the time Lu Huaixi stepped through the gates of the marquis estate, she had already forgotten the conversation.

Yaoshu came to find her just as Lu Huaixi had finished a visit to the First Madam's courtyard.

She wanted to bathe early tonight so she'd have the energy tomorrow to bring the girls from Shun'an Fang to the school.

Come to think of it, she hadn't seen a teacher in a long time. Tomorrow's teacher wouldn't be there for her, and yet she still had an inexplicable, jittery feeling — as though her palms might get smacked.

She was still thinking about this when Yaoshu came in, carrying two small boxes.

"Young Madam."

She said, "Little Doctor Zeng had these two boxes of her newly made beauty pills sent over for you. The messenger also said that Old Master Zeng wants to know why you've stopped coming to see him — and whether you've been off somewhere enjoying yourself and forgotten all about him."

"I'm not going anywhere near there. The heat is unbearable — that old man just wants me to come harvest herbs for him."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft snort, then took the boxes from Yaoshu's hands. "Newly made again, and I'm supposed to be the first to try them? Being useless would be one thing, but let's hope they don't upset my stomach."

Yaoshu couldn't help laughing at that.

"You're not the first to try them, Young Madam. These have already been on sale at Little Doctor Zeng's medicine shop for several days now — people can hardly get their hands on them. A box or two comes out every few days at most. It seems Little Doctor Zeng makes them more for her own amusement."

"Then I'll hold onto them for now. At my age, I don't really need to be taking things like these......"

She stopped mid-sentence and suddenly looked up. "Wait — these aren't meant for me to give to my mother and the First Madam, are they?"

Yaoshu pressed her lips together to keep from laughing and said nothing.

She didn't dare say that the two madams were getting on in years — but she rather suspected that was the idea.

"Fine, fine. I'll play the gracious gift-giver and go deliver them."

Just as she said it, two figures approached in the distance. Lu Huaixi looked up and immediately recognized the maidservant from the Old Madam's courtyard — and beside her, Mu Nianwei, smiling at her with careful, proper composure.

Several days had passed since they last met, and the young cousin-in-law had settled considerably.

Lu Huaixi took a quiet, measured look, then shifted her gaze to the maidservant.

Little Doctor Zeng's people had only just left, and here was the Old Madam already sending someone. No need to think too hard about why.

But she'd been stalling long enough. It was time to throw them something.

"Cousin-in-law."

Mu Nianwei dipped into a curtsy. The maidservant beside her also lowered her head in greeting. "Your maidservant pays respects to the First Young Madam."

"Cousin, you've come — would you like to come in and sit?"

Lu Huaixi said it easily, but a flash of embarrassment and displeasure crossed Mu Nianwei's face.

She quickly lowered her head again and said softly:

"I wouldn't dare impose on cousin-in-law. Great-Aunt said she hadn't seen cousin-in-law today and had been thinking of her, so she sent someone to check in. Nianwei has been thinking of cousin-in-law as well — and knowing that cousin-in-law's husband is so often away and no one is there to keep her company, Nianwei thought to come and have a chat."

"Grandmother is so good to me. And so is cousin."

Lu Huaixi smiled warmly, her eyes curving with the expression, her face the picture of genuine fondness — as if she truly were close to the Old Madam.

"I'd actually been worried at first that Grandmother and cousin didn't care for me. And yet it turns out it's Grandmother and cousin who think of me most in this household — especially cousin, who wants to see me every single day. Even more than your cousin-brother does."

Mu Nianwei's smile twitched. She couldn't tell whether she was being complimented or mocked.

She was about to say something more when a manservant passed nearby, carrying a load of ice.

The weather was warm, but not so oppressive that this amount of ice needed to be moved around every day.

Mu Nianwei looked at it, and her brow drew together. "Cousin-in-law, this is...... a little indulgent, isn't it?"

She said it with a trace of dissatisfaction. "Cousin-in-law may not have managed the household yet and might not know how these things are budgeted. The ice here was set aside from the beginning, but it's not something to be used so freely. It's nearly sundown now — for cousin-in-law to be using this much—"

"You make a fair point, cousin."

Lu Huaixi blinked, and called out to the manservant who had already entered the courtyard.

"Go ahead and take it back. Cousin says it's not right to be wasteful, and we shouldn't break the rules of the household."

The group of them froze. But since the First Young Madam was also their mistress, no one spoke up to question it. After a brief exchange of glances, they followed the order and withdrew.

A glimmer of satisfaction crossed Mu Nianwei's face, the irritation at being kept out of the courtyard dissolving in an instant.

She was about to add a few more words — but the Lu Huaixi before her had already dropped her smile, her expression cool and unhurried.

"I just remembered I have account books I need to start looking over. Since cousin doesn't wish to come inside, I won't keep you."

With that, Lu Huaixi glanced at the maidservant beside Mu Nianwei. "As it happens, I've set aside a box of Doctor Zeng's pills for Grandmother — just the thing to help her health. Please let Grandmother know, and I'll have someone send it over shortly."

"Yes, your maidservant will go and inform the Old Madam at once."

The First Young Madam's displeasure was plain enough — but since she had genuinely received something from the little miracle doctor, the maidservant didn't dare linger. She noted that she would also need to report the earlier exchange to the Old Madam.

Mu Nianwei too assumed she had finally managed to get under Lu Huaixi's skin.

Her chin lifted slightly, and she didn't stop to consider the value of the pills Lu Huaixi had mentioned.

"Cousin-in-law isn't upset about just now, is she?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing.

"Cousin-in-law looks a little displeased. And sending the pills by messenger instead of letting my maidservant take them now — could it be that cousin-in-law has misunderstood Nianwei——"

"Why would I be upset? That ice wasn't mine to begin with."

Lu Huaixi gave a light smile and glanced at her, her tone easy and offhand.

"That ice was your cousin-brother's. Not mine. But I'm glad you reminded me the household has its rules — now I have every reason to have it taken away without question. Otherwise, sleeping tonight with all that ice nearby — it would have been far too cold."

Hearing that it was Xie Yuanjing's doing, Mu Nianwei's expression froze. Her face twisted, her mouth opening and closing without producing a sound.

Lu Huaixi acted as though she hadn't noticed, and turned to leave.

"All right — I'm going in now. Next time you come, cousin, just walk right into the courtyard. No need to stand on ceremony the way you do with your cousin-brother."

—

By the time Xie Yuanjing returned to the estate, Yaoshu had just come back from delivering the gift and was still feeling a pang of regret on her young madam's behalf.

"Young Madam, did you really set that box of pills aside specially for the Old Madam? When Old Master Zeng finds out, he'll use it as an excuse to make you come plant herbs for him again as payment."

"As if I have the energy for that."

Lu Huaixi said it idly. "I just grabbed a random box of the old tonic pills — as long as they don't upset her stomach, that's enough. If I don't throw them something soon, that courtyard's maidservants are going to wear a path through my floor."

"That's true...... and that young cousin-in-law — she's really quite unpleasant to deal with."

"Don't worry. The maidservant will tell the Old Madam that I'm displeased. The Old Madam just received something from me — even if it's only for appearances, she'll step in and say something on my behalf this time."

While she was still speaking, someone came in from outside.

Xie Yuanjing had not yet changed out of his official robes, still dressed in deep crimson, looking cold and composed.

"Go ahead and play her — but taking my ice in the process?"

He walked straight toward her, an exasperated curve at the corner of his mouth. "Are you dealing with her, or dealing with me?"

chapters.title: Do You Want Me to Let Go?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi was seated in the chair. When Xie Yuanjing stopped before her, his presence seemed to fold around her entirely.

She tilted her head back to look up at him, and blinked at that rather close distance between them.

"I didn't do anything. She was the one who said the household has its rules, and that I didn't know how to manage the budget."

Lu Huaixi made no effort to hide it, neatly passing off the whole thing. "I'm just a new bride who came in from outside. Of course I have to follow the household's rules — otherwise Grandmother and Mother-in-law would be displeased with me."

"Is that so?"

Xie Yuanjing looked down at her. "From where I stand, you seem to have them both quite happy."

He gave a quiet laugh. "I thought I had a well-behaved little rabbit on my hands. Turns out she's been calculating things quite thoroughly all along."

"I have not. I'm nothing like you."

Lu Huaixi turned her head away after saying it. Xie Yuanjing gave her a look, then went inside to change his clothes.

"You've been waiting a long time for an opportunity like that, haven't you? If you're cold at night, just tell me directly next time."

"It wasn't like that. It was just convenient."

She watched his retreating figure and said:

"I'm fine under the blankets — I don't get that cold. But your mother said it's too early to be using ice, and my mother always said not to let yourself get chilled in the night. No one was looking out for you before, but I'm here now. I can't exactly watch you be so careless about it."

Xie Yuanjing's hands stilled. He turned his head and looked at her again. "Oh? You're going to manage me now?"

"Yes, a little."

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Is that not allowed?"

Silence from inside for quite some time. Then, after a long pause, came a quiet laugh. "It is."

Xie Yuanjing changed quickly. When he came back out, Lu Huaixi was still sitting where she had been, turning over the little trinkets she and Zhou Xianya had bought that day.

Watching her absorbed, head bent, Xie Yuanjing didn't say anything at first.

The quiet of the room gave him a feeling of steadiness he had never quite had before. He looked at the figure in the lamplight, his gaze resting on the soft downward sweep of her lashes — then drifting, without meaning to, a few inches further.

He had been watching for quite a while. Only when Lu Huaixi was on the verge of looking up did he finally speak.

"You had that much fun today — why didn't you have your friend stay for dinner?"

"We already ate out."

Lu Huaixi knew he meant Zhou Xianya, and answered simply. "And this isn't the Lu estate. It wouldn't have been right."

"What wouldn't be right about it?"

"It's just not quite appropriate." Lu Huaixi set down what she was holding. "It's not her own home — inviting someone here would make her uncomfortable."

The moment those words landed, Jingshuang, who had just come in to refill the tea, felt her heart give a small lurch.

She didn't dare raise her head, but borrowed the edge of her vision to steal a glance at the two of them.

Her young madam looked perfectly composed, her tone relaxed and easy. But the Young Master standing beside her — his expression was something else entirely.

She didn't look again. She lowered her head and retreated quickly.

The silence stretched for a long while before Xie Yuanjing spoke again.

"Come here."

He stood at the beaded curtain without moving. Lu Huaixi had no idea what he was about, but she set her things down and rose, puzzled.

"What is it?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't answer. Instead, when she drew near, he reached out and took her hand, leading her to the inner room and settling her onto the edge of the bed.

Then he leaned in slightly, one hand resting against her shoulder, bowing his head so that his face came to rest just beside her ear.

A very intimate gesture — one that made Lu Huaixi forget, quite suddenly, how to speak.

"The main bedroom is the bed you sleep in. Half the things in this room are things you've put there. Every manservant and maidservant in this courtyard follows your instructions before they follow mine. When you gave the word about that ice just now, not one of them came to ask me a single thing."

Xie Yuanjing spoke slowly, his low voice carrying the weight of some held-back feeling.

Lu Huaixi felt the warmth of his breath settle against her earlobe, then drift down the length of her neck — until her palms began to heat.

She instinctively tried to lean back, to put a little space between them. But the moment she moved, he noticed, and the hand on her shoulder pressed down with more intention.

"Before, no one could come into my quarters. Every decision, no matter who in the household came to ask about it, had to wait on me. Now, with a word from you, things get done. Even when the Old Madam and the others want to see me, they come to you first to ask when I might be free."

Xie Yuanjing shifted slightly, paused for a breath, then looked down and used his other hand to gently hold her chin in place.

"And yet, with all of that, you still say this isn't your own home? You can still call it uncomfortable?"

The light from behind was mostly blocked by him now.

Beneath his fingers, her chin went warm and numb.

Lu Huaixi blinked, slightly at a loss — and then met his eyes, dark and unreadable.

She didn't speak. She seemed to be thinking.

Xie Yuanjing didn't pull back to create distance, and he didn't press her.

They were very close. Close enough that if he shifted even slightly, he would brush against her nose.

"If what you said just now — about being on my side — was only something you said carelessly, then tell me now, and I'll let go."

After a long pause, Xie Yuanjing's lips finally moved.

His expression didn't change much on the surface. But that nameless feeling that had been surfacing in him, bit by bit, seemed in this moment to have grown a little clearer.

When he heard Lu Huaixi draw such a firm line between herself and the marquis estate, the emotion he had always found easy to press down suddenly gained the upper hand and pushed back against him.

"Do you want me to let go?"

He asked it again.

After a moment, the tight press of Lu Huaixi's lips eased. The gaze she had been holding on him shifted slightly — as if it had drifted to somewhere behind him.

"I didn't say it carelessly."

Her voice was soft. "I really am on your side."

"Then what you said just now — still saying it?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her hand resting on the bed beside her, fingers curled inward from discomfort, and let out a quiet breath.

Then, gradually, the coldness in his voice softened. His tone eased into something closer to gentle coaxing. "This place is yours too, Lu Huaixi. Have you got that clearly, this time?"

Outside, the sky had already grown considerably darker.

When Xie Yuanjing came out of the room, there was still a trace of warmth in his eyes that hadn't faded.

Gong Zhuo had just been thinking that the Young Master's temperament had been growing noticeably easier these days — when, in the very next moment, that cool and level voice came.

"Go to the Old Madam's courtyard. Tell her: if Mu Nianwei cannot learn her place and continues to involve herself in what goes on in this part of the estate, the First Young Madam may be too good-natured to take it to heart — but I am not. One more time, and I will have her removed from the estate entirely."

—

Word traveled quickly.

By the time Mu Nianwei heard, she had just sat through a long scolding from the Old Madam and had not yet fully recovered — and now, on top of that, she received Xie Yuanjing's warning, delivered without the slightest mercy. She felt something hot and bitter surging up in her chest, again and again.

This was far from the first time he had stood up for Lu Huaixi.

A worthless noble young lady who had appeared out of nowhere, who knew nothing — and yet time and again she made Xie Yuanjing make exceptions for her. Mu Nianwei had held feelings for Xie Yuanjing for so long, and yet she had never once managed to earn so much as a glance.

No matter how she turned it over, she could not understand. And she could not accept it.

"Great-Aunt——"

"You close your mouth! How many times have I told you to wait, to be patient — and now look at the situation you've created. Are you satisfied?"

The Old Madam gripped the box of pills Lu Huaixi had just sent over, growing angrier the longer she thought about it.

"With a head like yours, even if I managed to get you into his inner rooms, all you'd ever be is someone he eventually tires of and discards!"

Mu Nianwei's heart sank. She didn't dare make a sound.

Again, here in the Old Madam's courtyard, she felt the sensation she had been feeling since Lu Huaixi arrived — that spreading, creeping sense of things slipping out of her control.

"Great-Aunt, Nianwei was wrong."

Before long, Mu Nianwei sank to her knees. "Nianwei would never dare act like this again. Whatever Great-Aunt tells me to do, I will do. However long Great-Aunt tells me to wait, I will wait."

She knocked her head against the floor, not daring to give the person before her even a moment's irritation.

She knew clearly: as long as she was still in the estate, she still had a chance. So she could not truly let the Old Madam stop looking after her affairs.

Mu Nianwei didn't hesitate. Each bow was pressed down with full force.

And yet the resentment inside her did not leave.

When she closed her eyes, what surfaced again was something she had once overheard.

That Xie Yuanjing had been forced to take this marriage for the sake of the bigger picture — Lu Huaixi surely didn't know that yet. She must believe that Xie Yuanjing truly cared for her.

She could wait. When the truth eventually came to light, she refused to believe Lu Huaixi wouldn't be affected.

chapters.title: I'll Watch You Practice
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi heard about the matter later from Yaoshu.

But what surprised her more than learning that Xie Yuanjing had sent someone to warn Mu Nianwei was Yaoshu's sheer talent for gathering information.

"With you around, I'll never need to hire a spy."

Lu Huaixi couldn't help laughing. "Back when we were at home, I never saw you pick things up this quickly."

"Young Madam, please don't tease me."

Yaoshu lowered her head, a little embarrassed.

"Your maidservant has regrets about that, actually. Back at the Lu estate, things felt easy — and even though Third Miss had her little schemes, your maidservant always felt that no one would truly hurt Young Madam. So I wasn't as sharp as I should have been."

She paused, then added, "But not anymore. Young Madam was dealt such a heavy blow by the second branch — your maidservant has remembered it all. And it's a blessing that Young Madam married the Young Master, two people who truly care for each other — heaven's mercy, not letting the wicked have their way."

Lu Huaixi had been about to say something light, but when she heard the phrase two people who truly care for each other, she stopped, briefly at a loss.

Letting the silence drag on would only feel strange, but explaining didn't seem right either — she didn't want anyone thinking she had something to hide.

For a moment the carriage fell quiet, and stayed that way until they collected the girls from Shun'an Fang, and the chatter filled the space again.

Today, Lu Huaixi was bringing them to the school.

She had apparently always had a deep, irrational fear of teachers — so when they arrived and went inside, she was barely doing better than the girls themselves.

"Pro — Proprietress, can we really stay here and study?"

Beside her, a very slight young girl — apparently seeing a place this quiet and dignified for the first time — couldn't help edging closer to Lu Huaixi.

The moment she spoke, Lu Huaixi's own nervousness settled considerably.

It was like being frightened of ghosts — and then realizing the person next to you is even more frightened. Somehow that always makes one braver.

"Don't worry. As long as you want to study, and are willing to study properly, you can stay."

Lu Huaixi gave her a reassuring smile. "So once you're inside, you need to listen carefully to the teachers — memorize your texts, practice your characters, not one thing left out."

"But we don't have any money. We can't pay the tuition......"

"That's not for you to worry about."

The girls crowded around Lu Huaixi. When they heard this, several of them bowed their heads and pressed their hands to their eyes.

Lu Huaixi was just about to say something comforting when a firm, resonant voice came from behind her.

Strangely familiar — enough that she instinctively drew a breath, and forgot entirely what she had been about to say.

She turned around stiffly.

"Master — Master Xu."

What a coincidence.

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together and gave a rigid bow of greeting, and somehow her palms began to ache.

If she had known that the man overseeing this school was the very teacher who had taught her for so many years, nothing in the world would have gotten her through that door today.

"What is the teacher doing here?"

"Came to see the student who gave me the most grief, all those years ago."

The man smiled as he spoke, his white beard swaying with the expression.

"And she really has grown up. Married, a young woman now."

"I......"

For some reason, Lu Huaixi suddenly found herself without words.

The old teacher had been strict with her — and yet in private, he had looked after her with real care. On the occasions when he had truly lost his temper and rapped her palms, he would afterward send his wife to apply medicine.

And later, when she wanted to study dance and her father was reluctant to agree, it was Master Xu who had finally confirmed his support and sent his wife to speak on her behalf.

Lu Huaixi was genuinely afraid of him — and genuinely respected him.

"There are many students here waiting, Teacher."

She said it quietly. "Young girls who are coming to enroll."

The old teacher had no real intention of embarrassing her. He drew a hand across his beard and laughed heartily several times, then led the group forward.

Lu Huaixi followed quietly at his side, and after a moment spoke again.

"Are you well, Teacher? Two years ago I heard from my elder brother that you were thinking of returning home. When I later sent a card and tried to visit, I couldn't reach you — your student assumed you had already left the capital."

"I did go back for a time."

The old teacher nodded. "But there is a great deal of rain in my hometown, and my wife's old leg condition acts up because of it. So at the start of this year we came back to the capital."

He looked ahead, and then, as if remembering something, added, "Though we returned, we live in a small house outside the city. If Xie Young Master hadn't kept asking me to come here, I probably wouldn't have come into the city at all."

Lu Huaixi blinked. "He asked you to come?"

"He did. Not long before your wedding, he came to see me a few times. He said that if I had managed to teach you for so many years, my patience must be considerable, and I couldn't be too harsh on the students."

"......"

Seeing she hadn't spoken, the old teacher glanced back, his face warm with the fondness one has for younger generations.

"This Young Master Xie has a careful heart. This school owes a great deal to him. At first I assumed he was doing it for his own name — but he took the trouble to come and seek me out personally, and arranged for the girls in your household to enroll. It seems he was thinking of you."

Lu Huaixi didn't know what to say, and murmured only a soft sound in response.

The old teacher didn't linger on it, and turned his gaze forward again, continuing in an easy, unhurried voice.

"You were never very fond of studying back then, and your calligraphy was certainly not your strong suit. But you were never genuinely lacking, either — your mind was sharp as anyone's, whatever your brushwork might say. From now on, if anyone speaks ill of you, send them to me."

"Teacher......"

"I'm not complimenting your handwriting, mind you."

The old teacher laughed as he cut her off. "You are my student. As long as I am here, there is no reason for anyone to speak poorly of you."

Lu Huaixi had no idea why she felt like crying so easily today.

Again she found herself without words — partly because of the old teacher, and partly because of Xie Yuanjing.

Her emotions were still swelling when one of the girls who had been led into the schoolroom came running back out and tugged lightly at the hem of her sleeve.

"What are you doing out here?"

Lu Huaixi came back to herself, pressed her feelings down, and looked over.

"Is Xixi jiejie leaving?"

"Don't call me proprietress — just call me what you've always called me."

"Oh. Then is Xixi jiejie leaving?"

Lu Huaixi glanced at the sky. "Soon. Once you're all settled, I'll head back."

The small girl didn't let go. She held on gently, for a long while, then softly said, "Xixi jiejie, I'm a little scared."

She looked up at Lu Huaixi with wide, pitiful eyes. "There's a teacher inside who wants us to practice writing. I don't know how."

"Not knowing how is fine — if you already knew everything, why would you come here to learn?"

Lu Huaixi laughed and gave the girl a light pat on the head. "Don't be afraid. It's only writing."

The girl listened, pressed her lips together, and after a moment, answered with great conviction.

"Xixi jiejie is so capable, her writing must be really beautiful too. I want to be just like Xixi jiejie someday!"

Whatever complicated feelings had been lingering in Lu Huaixi were, in an instant, gone.

She gave a short, quiet cough, and touched her nose.

—

After returning to the estate, it took Lu Huaixi quite a while to shake off the lingering awkwardness of the situation. But somehow — she wasn't sure how — Xie Yuanjing got wind of it. The moment dusk fell, he appeared before her.

"Come."

"Where?" Lu Huaixi asked.

"The study."

Xie Yuanjing's lips curved in a faint, unhurried way. His whole bearing was lax and easy, his tone casual, touched with just the smallest trace of delight. "To practice your calligraphy. I'll watch you practice."

chapters.title: An Old Acquaintance on the Lake
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi thought Xie Yuanjing took the whole thing a bit too seriously. He also had a habit of not quite keeping his word.

He was the one who had told her, early on, that he found her calligraphy interesting. But he was also the one who had announced that day that he was going to supervise her practice.

And from that day forward, he had made good on it — calling her to the study with quiet regularity.

He would see to his official matters; she would sit at the small desk they had set up beside him and practice her characters. Ugly was acceptable. Not writing was not. Half-hearted efforts were not.

Lu Huaixi endured it for several days, privately deciding that the next time he asked her to go practice, she was going to pick a fight with him.

But before she got the chance, the day of the lake outing arrived.

"Don't worry — if I have anything to say, I'll wait until after we're back from the lake."

Lu Huaixi gave Yaoshu a reassuring pat. After several rounds of being talked out of doing something impulsive, she set off for the carriage with a bright and cheerful expression.

The boat had been arranged by Shen Zhouxu, but the singers and dancers on board were all from Shun'an Fang.

When Lu Huaixi stepped out of the carriage, she spotted Zhou Xianya coming from the other direction and went over to meet her.

The wind off the river was strong, sending the hem of her skirt swaying.

"This boat is enormous — you could host my family's banquets on this thing."

Zhou Xianya looked at it in surprise. Lu Huaixi glanced over as well. "I had no idea either. I thought it would just be a regular boat."

The two of them took it in with wide eyes.

Every summer when the weather warmed, gatherings on the water were commonplace — and one didn't even need to wait for summer. Spring banquets already saw no shortage of young men and women setting out on the lake to enjoy music and the scenery.

Lu Huaixi and Zhou Xianya had both been on the lake many times. But a vessel this grand and beautiful — this was a first for both of them.

"Must be a new boat brought in from somewhere else," Zhou Xianya said, looking at her. "Is it going to be a large party today?"

"From what I heard, just a few of his close friends. We'll go on board, say hello, and then head to our own end of the boat to do as we please. I snuck some wine in — brewed it myself before the new year."

"You brew wine?"

Zhou Xianya was even more surprised, and couldn't help laughing. "Is it actually drinkable? If it didn't turn out right, drinking it could send you straight to a physician."

Lu Huaixi shot her a look, then tilted her chin up slightly and gave a light huff. "Fine then, you're not getting any."

"No, I want some."

"Too bad."

The two of them were still bickering when a voice came from behind them — a man's voice, warm in tone, easy and refined.

"Miss Lu."

A pause, then a quiet laugh. "Force of habit — it should be First Young Madam of the Xie household now."

The voice was familiar. Lu Huaixi was just about to turn around when Zhou Xianya called out beside her:

"Older brother? What are you doing here?"

"You and your fine taste for leisure — I can't claim the same."

The man handed his horse's reins to the manservant behind him and walked over. "I'm here on business. Passed by and saw the family's carriage, so I stopped to check."

"You'd better be. If you came out on the lake without telling me, I'd go home and make your life very difficult."

"And did you invite me when you arranged this outing?"

The teasing remark left Zhou Xianya momentarily speechless, a glimmer of surprise in her eyes.

She had never once heard her brother make a remark like that. It was rather alarming.

"Well. Now that I know it's you two, I should be on my way."

He clearly had no intention of staying — but as he finished speaking, he turned his head slightly.

Lu Huaixi had been listening to the siblings go back and forth. When she saw him look over, she smiled at him.

"Older Brother Zhou."

"Mm."

The man gave a quiet response. Then, after a brief pause, he spoke again. "It hasn't been that long since we've seen each other. And yet somehow you've grown up all at once."

Zhou Young Master was known for being warm and steady. Even in private conversation, his voice was soft and measured — like a gentle spring wind, pleasant to be near.

But those words — grown up — had a different quality to them.

Lu Huaixi blinked, not quite sure what to make of it. She thought she heard, somewhere in the phrasing, a faint and indefinable sigh — different in feeling from when Master Xu had said something similar.

But she didn't dwell on it. She smiled at him.

"I'm not that much younger than Xianya jiejie."

"That's true."

He nodded along with her words. His feet, which had been about to move, stilled for no obvious reason. Only when Zhou Xianya called out to him again did he seem to come back to himself, and spoke, unhurried.

"I heard that you and Xie Young Master — you were already matched long ago?"

"...... Yes."

"That explains it."

"Hmm?"

Lu Huaixi lifted her voice with a note of curiosity, wanting to know what it explained.

But before she could ask, someone interrupted the moment.

The voice had been absent for a long time — and yet it was still familiar.

"Huaixi......"

There was a small sound of surprise in it, then warmth. After calling Lu Huaixi's name, she called out to Zhou Xianya as well.

Everyone turned to look.

Wu Wenlan stood in a simple dress of soft green-blue — the understated, unadorned style she always favored — among a small group of young women.

"Huaixi, you're here for the lake outing too?"

Wu Wenlan walked a few steps forward, then seemed to think of something and stopped partway, her expression caught between hesitation and timidity.

"Huaixi, are you — are you still angry with me?"

Lu Huaixi didn't speak. The smile on her face faded.

She was not a person who held onto grievances — but looking back on her friendship with Wu Wenlan from the outside, she could see how foolish she had been.

"It's not anger. I don't go getting angry at just anyone."

She said it and withdrew her gaze, making no move to look over again. "Xianya jiejie, should we—"

"Huaixi, I really didn't mean to that day. I know I upset you, and I've been regretting it ever since. The cards and letters I sent — you never replied. I wanted to send you something, but I didn't know what you'd like. I truly didn't know what to do......"

"I did reply."

Lu Huaixi looked up. Her face turned slightly, her profile clear and cool in the sunlight.

"I replied very plainly. What's done is done."

"But I......"

Wu Wenlan seemed genuinely distressed, her eyes reddening quickly.

She stopped short of finishing, glanced at Zhou Xianya, then at the man standing beside Lu Huaixi, and pressed her lips together before asking:

"Is it because Brother Zhou is here that you can't speak freely, Huaixi? At first I thought he was your husband — I didn't expect—"

"What does it matter who's standing here? Is there anything left for you and me to say?"

Lu Huaixi cut her off.

Seeing Zhou Xianya's brow furrow in preparation to say something pointed, she stepped forward and took her arm, and didn't look over again.

"Let's go, Xianya jiejie. They're probably all on board by now."

"You're so cold-hearted."

Behind them, a voice suddenly rose — one of the girls who had come with Wu Wenlan. "Wenlan has been trying to make peace in everything she's said, she was practically on the verge of tears, and you treat her like this just because you have a higher standing? Is that how it works?"

Lu Huaixi kept walking. Zhou Xianya, however, could not let it pass, and turned around.

"Crying means you're right, does it? Then you go ahead and cry too — might as well say we're trampling all over you while we're at it."

"You—"

"What about me? If you know you're not welcome, step aside. You came looking for trouble yourselves, and now you're complaining that no one gave you a warm reception. Don't you have anything better to do?"

Zhou Xianya didn't actually know the full story of what had happened between Lu Huaixi and Wu Wenlan.

She had a rough sense of it — but she hadn't pressed for details. She was Lu Huaixi's friend. Toward other people she was pleasant only because of Lu Huaixi, and she trusted her.

Having said her piece, Zhou Xianya gave a cool little laugh.

"After enjoying years of someone's kindness and good graces, then turning around and selling her out — and for what? If you'd at least managed to climb somewhere worthwhile, that would be one thing. But look at the situation now — still just as unimpressive. Still not worth being taken seriously."

chapters.title: Closeness
chapters.content:
Zhou Xianya's words were blunt. Wu Wenlan's expression faltered, and the redness that had only been gathering at the edges of her eyes now spilled over into actual tears.

The girl who had stepped in to defend her was even more furious, and stepped forward to stand at Wu Wenlan's side.

"What's so great about either of you? Throwing your status around to bully people — aren't you afraid of what comes back to you?"

The girl took Wu Wenlan's arm and raised her chin. "All this talk of years of kindness and good graces — as if Wenlan has been taking advantage of you all this time! Ridiculous — if you're so generous and capable, why are you here picking over old grievances?"

Zhou Xianya's temper flared to the top in an instant. But just as she was about to step forward, Lu Huaixi blocked her.

"What are you stopping me for?"

She shifted her arm, trying to get past. When she couldn't, she looked to her brother.

"Older brother!"

The girl who had been speaking gave a short, disdainful sound at that.

Wu Wenlan looked up quickly, then hurried to catch the girl's arm. "Don't — it's my fault, don't get into trouble on my account."

"What is there to be afraid of? High-born families aren't untouchable forever. You call yourself the second daughter of the Lu family — you were perfectly happy bullying her before, and now that you've been found out, here you are putting on a pitiful face and waiting for someone to save you. Honestly——"

The girl turned to look at Lu Huaixi. "Wenlan's been worrying about whether you'd have a harder time of it after getting married, and yet here you are out on boats having fun — clearly you have no respect for rules. You've been spoiled to the bone. I don't know what your husband's family must think——"

"What happens between them is not for an outsider to say."

Zhou Young Master spoke suddenly, his brow drawn together as he stepped forward.

But before he could put himself between them, Lu Huaixi tilted her head slightly and spoke up.

"Which family are you from?"

She looked at the young woman before her — who had the air of someone even more imperious than a princess. "State your family first. If you have the standing, then we can talk about rules."

Lu Huaixi had not genuinely wanted to waste her time here.

She had wanted to get on the boat and enjoy the outing — music and a breeze and sweet pastries.

But this person had launched into a righteous, heated tirade, and now Lu Huaixi found herself rather curious. And she began to pay closer attention to Wu Wenlan as well.

"What, nothing to say? Afraid I'll find out who you are?"

Seeing the girl go silent, Lu Huaixi smiled and pressed the question.

She had almost never used her position to bear down on anyone — just as Xie Yuanjing had said, even when she had someone arrested, she did it by the book, through proper channels.

But today, for some reason, she decided that being reasonable about everything wasn't always the right approach.

"Say it, then. Otherwise, when I go and find out myself, things won't go particularly well for your entire household."

"You — what are you trying to do?" the girl snapped through clenched teeth.

"You won't even state your family name, and you come here to throw your weight around in front of me?"

Lu Huaixi looked at her steadily, her tone unhurried.

"Tell me — what exactly do you have that you think I should be concerned about? Enough to bother dealing with, enough to put on a pitiful show over? Is it your family's connections? Your money? Your learning? Or perhaps your face?"

She must have struck something true — both of their expressions collapsed at once, the humiliation and fury impossible to conceal.

But then the girl's chin went up again, and she couldn't stop herself from snapping back:

"You say you don't care, so what do you call this? You threatened me into naming my family, didn't you? Isn't that revenge? That's exactly what it is!"

"So I'm just supposed to stand here and let you speak, and then smile and wave as you walk away? Do you even know who you are?"

Lu Huaixi gave a cool, dismissive sound.

She was just about to call someone over to deal with them when footsteps came from behind.

A familiar presence. The moment she sensed it, Lu Huaixi went quiet — and the heat of her temper dropped considerably.

"Why are you standing out here in the wind?"

The voice was low, the tone cool — and yet somehow it carried an inexplicable thread of warmth.

He reached out and brushed the back of his hand against Lu Huaixi's cheek, and as he drew it back, let his arm settle around her waist, drawing her in close beside him.

"I'm only a little late because something came up, and you've already let someone bother you?"

Xie Yuanjing spoke with the ease of intimacy, and his gestures matched it.

He hadn't even glanced at anyone else. Aside from the briefest pause on Zhou Xianya's brother as he arrived, his attention had been entirely on Lu Huaixi.

"If your hands get any colder, you're not getting on that boat today."

"Absolutely not."

Lu Huaixi turned to look at him at last, forgetting entirely about the distance between them, eyes wide. "I'm going."

Xie Yuanjing laughed softly at her indignant tone and gave a quiet sound of assent.

Whether for the benefit of onlookers or simply without thinking, Xie Yuanjing suddenly tightened his arm — as if to soothe her — and drew her briefly into a light embrace.

But just as quickly, the embrace released. When Lu Huaixi's nose was nearly at his chest, his arm relaxed.

"Stop paying attention to just anyone who comes along."

Xie Yuanjing's tone was measured and easy. He was looking at her as he spoke, yet the words were plainly a warning to everyone else.

"So many people have to send a card and wait for your reply before they can see you, wait until you have a free moment. A few unremarkable strangers wanting to stop you and say a word — just have them removed. They're not worth spending a thought on."

Still a little dazed from that brief embrace, Lu Huaixi had yet to fully collect herself.

Xie Yuanjing didn't seem to need a response. He simply lifted his gaze past her once he had finished speaking, finally giving the others a portion of his attention.

"So it was them?"

For Wu Wenlan, the fear she had been suppressing was briefly overtaken by something else entirely.

She watched Lu Huaixi held in close like that — as though she were infinitely valued and treasured — and felt something press down heavily on her chest.

This was an image she would never have. If she didn't fight for herself, a man like that would always be beyond her reach.

And yet she truly did resent Lu Huaixi.

They had been such close friends — and Lu Huaixi had never once mentioned that she had a fiancé like this.

In the haze of those thoughts, a cold and piercing gaze swept over her — carrying weight enough to shock her fear back to the surface.

Then someone grabbed her arm. It was the girl beside her, who had stepped in for her and was now just as frightened.

"Wenlan......" she called softly.

She had been about to ask whether Wu Wenlan wanted to plead with the Lu family's noble daughter — but then a different thought crept in. "He's a marquis estate young master. He — he probably won't bother with something this small, will he?"

Wu Wenlan had no answer to give her.

She wanted to know as well. How far would a man like him go for Lu Huaixi?

Probably just to comfort her, and then take her away.

But what Wu Wenlan wanted to see was Lu Huaixi fall out of favor. She wanted her to push too far, make him angry — ideally bringing all the old business with it, so that Lu Huaixi would be abandoned in the inner quarters, no longer the pampered girl she had always been.

The thought of it stirred something in her beneath all that suppression — a flicker of anticipation.

She held her hands tightly together inside her sleeves, bracing herself for the words she had been waiting to hear.

Before long, the man at the front finally spoke. But his voice, cold as ice, landed on the ears of those nearby and drained them of all warmth.

"Since they don't know their manners and can't hold their tongues, educate them."

His gaze swept over, then withdrew — as if a second look would be more than they deserved. "No need to take them anywhere. Teach them right here."

Xie Yuanjing had spoken, and that made it the word of the marquis estate's Young Master.

He stood where he was, unmoved. He didn't concern himself with how loud the sounds of punishment became on the other side of the crowd, nor with how much fear and curiosity filled the onlookers' eyes.

"Shall we get on the boat?"

He looked back at Lu Huaixi. When she nodded, he finally turned — and spoke the first words he had addressed to Zhou Xianya's brother all afternoon.

"Young Master Zhou — join us on the lake?"

The man, who had been silent for a long while, no longer wore the open, easy expression of when they had first met.

He smiled, glanced at Lu Huaixi, then looked away. "I still have matters to attend to. Another time — I'll extend the invitation myself."

Xie Yuanjing also smiled — neither accepting nor declining — and simply drew his hand back from around Lu Huaixi's waist, letting it fall instead to her wrist.

chapters.title: What He Feels for Her
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi hadn't noticed the strange undercurrent between the two men. Her mind had been on the look in Wu Wenlan's eyes just now.

It had made her uncomfortable — not frightened, not disgusted, just the sudden realization that she had perhaps never truly known this person at all.

After saying goodbye to Zhou Young Master, Lu Huaixi paused and glanced back.

Xie Yuanjing's people were not in the habit of going easy on anyone. If they had been given the order to act, they would not leave any room for mercy.

And that was simply his nature — he had told them to do it right there, in front of everyone, which meant he had intended for everyone to see.

"Are people going to say something about you?"

Lu Huaixi tilted her head and asked, not even noticing that her hand was still being held in his. "They're unpleasant, I know, but I could have had someone deal with it. You speaking up like that will draw more attention."

"That was the point."

Xie Yuanjing led her on board, his gaze on her footing, his tone easy. "Otherwise there will always be people who forget — that among those behind you, there is me."

There were already people waiting on the boat. Seeing them come aboard, they rose to greet them.

Lu Huaixi hadn't met Shen Zhouxu before, but she had heard his name. The other two men were also clearly of no ordinary standing.

She was just about to ask quietly when a voice rang out from up ahead, cheerful and a little too loud.

"Well, well — you two are rather——"

The man standing at the front wore a pale moonlit robe with cloud patterns, a folding fan in hand that he didn't bother using, just held and swung idly.

His voice carried easily, and the teasing in his eyes made it plain he was the one most familiar with Xie Yuanjing.

Lu Huaixi startled at his sudden remark and instinctively took a step back, half-hiding herself — and didn't notice that he had been looking at the hand Xie Yuanjing was holding.

"Don't mind him."

Xie Yuanjing tilted his head but made no move to pull her out from behind him. "He's always like this."

Zhou Xianya was still at Lu Huaixi's side, and though none of them had met before, their fathers all served at court — the names were familiar enough.

"Young Madam and Miss Zhou, please don't take offense — I was only joking around."

Shen Zhouxu composed himself, the smile still at his mouth, but his tone settling back to normal.

Though the composure lasted only a moment. When the boat began to move, he gave another quiet laugh. "First time seeing Yuanjing's softer side. Takes a bit of getting used to."

At that, Lu Huaixi looked over at Shen Zhouxu. "Was it really soft? Just now?"

His manner when he gave the order had been ice-cold — nothing remotely warm about it. Coming aboard had been slightly better, but there was still a heaviness to him that hadn't quite lifted.

"It was, don't doubt it."

Shen Zhouxu was direct about it. "That commotion outside just now — that was him, wasn't it?"

He looked at Lu Huaixi with a grin. "We placed a wager, a few of us, on whether he'd involve himself in something like that."

Xie Yuanjing stepping in over a quarrel between young women, then arriving at the riverbank early just to receive his wife before boarding — none of them had thought he'd do it.

The bet had barely seemed worth making. Shen Zhouxu had already been about to send someone on Lu Huaixi's behalf.

But then he'd hesitated, wondering whether Xie Yuanjing might actually go himself — on the grounds that he was invested in looking after the girl.

So two against one, he'd made the bet at the last moment.

The outcome had surprised him. Not only had he won, but he had seen something rather extraordinary.

Because looking after a young girl didn't require you to stand quite that close.

"You three——"

Lu Huaixi looked a little taken aback, then couldn't help glancing between them. "There are only three of you — and you still made a proper wager? Three people, going to the trouble of placing bets?"

Shen Zhouxu had not expected his story to be met with this — a note of disbelief, and mild exasperation at their gambling habits.

He was about to set her straight on the matter, when he turned and saw Xie Yuanjing suddenly curve his lips and laugh — and then cut him off.

"They do have a bit of a gambling habit. Which is why I don't often go out with them."

Xie Yuanjing ignored the looks from the others, then paused and added, "You really won't stay with me?"

From the start Lu Huaixi had told him she didn't want to be in the same group on board. Though an outing like this — friends on a lake enjoying music — was the sort of occasion where it didn't much matter whether men and women mixed, Zhou Xianya was not familiar with these men, and neither was she.

And this gathering had been arranged by Shen Zhouxu anyway. His sister would be joining on the girls' side, and together with the performers from Shun'an Fang, they would have their own lively time of it.

With that, Lu Huaixi shook her head.

"You all talk about things I don't understand and it gives me a headache. I want to spend time with Xianya jiejie. I heard there's fishing on the boat too — once the music is done I want to try. Oh, and — has Miss Shen arrived yet?"

Xie Yuanjing waited a moment before quietly answering.

And finally let go of her hand.

"Later in the trip the boat will pass a small island. Shen Zhouxu's sister will board there. She left the Shen household a long time ago and doesn't stand on ceremony — if you want to talk, talk; if not, there's no obligation."

The warmth in Lu Huaixi's hand faded, and all at once her palm felt empty.

It was only then that she realized — Xie Yuanjing had been holding her hand this whole time without letting go.

The image of Shen Zhouxu's expression when they boarded came back to her, and suddenly she understood exactly why he had smiled the way he had.

"Fishing is fine, but the boat can't stop too long — you're unlikely to catch anything. And the wind is strong out there, you can't stay outside the whole time."

"I know."

"Good. Then go. If you need anything, call for Gong Fei — or come find me."

Xie Yuanjing appeared not to notice her embarrassment, and said it all with a perfectly composed expression.

Lu Huaixi couldn't very well stand there going over it any further. She gave a vague reply and called for Zhou Xianya, and the two of them headed to the other end of the boat.

Behind her, Xie Yuanjing hadn't moved from where he stood.

Shen Zhouxu was enjoying the spectacle too much to move either.

A long while passed. Only when the figures had disappeared from sight did Xie Yuanjing finally look away. He dropped his gaze, eyes sweeping briefly over his own sleeve.

"Something's different about you," Shen Zhouxu said, watching him.

"Less different than you."

Xie Yuanjing didn't even look up. Seeming to know this person would find a way to keep him talking, he made no particular move to go inside.

"Say what you want to say."

"You were waiting for me to ask?"

Shen Zhouxu raised an eyebrow and clicked his tongue a couple of times. "Is that it? Waiting for me to ask?"

"I'd rather you ask now than go and bother her about it later."

"If you hadn't kept fobbing me off with that looking after a child line, would I need to make such a fuss about it?"

Shen Zhouxu took a few steps toward him, looked out at the rippling water, then looked back.

"Is it that you actually feel something for her, or is it because of the Lu family? I've been hearing that Lu Patriarch has been speaking well of you in front of His Majesty lately — not even bothering to conceal the support he's extending. You suddenly showing more interest in the man's daughter — I genuinely can't work out what you're about."

Shen Zhouxu's words carried over the sound of moving water, easy and unhurried.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing at first. He let the river wind lift the corner of his robe and said nothing, eyes lowered in silence.

He seemed to be thinking about a great many things — and then, almost at once, seemed to reach a decision.

Before long he raised his eyes and looked out into the distance, his handsome features carrying the quiet arrogance that was always there.

"Is it that obvious."

"What?"

Shen Zhouxu blinked. The casual teasing of moments ago gave way to a genuine shock, as if he had glimpsed something he hadn't expected — like being caught off guard by the very joke he'd been making.

"What do you mean obvious, you——"

"It's what you think it is."

Shen Zhouxu was completely speechless. After quite a long pause, he came back to himself — and burst out laughing.

"Well then, you're done for, aren't you, Young Master Xie."

chapters.title: This Boat Has No Shortage of Passengers
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi and Zhou Xianya made their way toward the interior of the boat.

The wind off the water was strong, and within just a few steps, the warmth lingering in her palm had been carried away entirely.

Zhou Xianya walked beside her, looking composed on the surface — but she had been holding back quite a few words.

Seeing that no one was following them now, she couldn't help leaning a little closer.

"I got a fright just now."

"What happened?"

"I hadn't expected Xie Young Master's close friend to be Shen Zhouxu. I'd assumed they were just slightly more than nodding acquaintances."

She said it quietly. "And those other two — most people wouldn't even have that much connection with them. And yet in private they're all that familiar with each other."

At that, Lu Huaixi glanced over at her. "Xianya jiejie knows them?"

"Not personally — just heard of them. It's always the same circle, going around and around. And one of the others has ties to the imperial family as well. All people of real standing."

She looked at Lu Huaixi and continued:

"I'm not making a mountain of it — I was just surprised and wanted to say something. Think about it yourself. Has your husband ever, in anything you've heard, had a particularly close friend — a young man he was known to be genuinely close with?"

"Now that you put it that way — no."

"Exactly. And that's why people say no one dares get close to him."

Zhou Xianya took her arm, and as she said it, something settled into her expression — a certain deliberateness.

"There is no shortage of cold and distant people in the capital, and the capable ones are all ruthless to some degree. But even among them, most have two or three real friends. Only Xie Young Master — aside from a few colleagues he might occasionally mention — has given no sign of genuinely getting along with anyone. Which is why seeing what I just saw came as such a shock."

"He's really not that unapproachable......"

"That's your perspective."

Zhou Xianya looked at her with considerable seriousness.

"The ease between those men just now — one look and you could tell they'd known each other for years. And they're all people of real consequence. The fact that they've kept it this quiet means there are things going on between them that aren't meant to be seen — plans and arrangements not for outside eyes."

Lu Huaixi had already understood the point of her conversation. Before she could respond, Zhou Xianya's already quiet voice dropped a little further.

"I know this isn't the best moment to say any of this — after all, he was willing to bring you here today, and willing to let you bring me, and even left the performers entirely in your hands. That's all him telling you he trusts you. But Huaixi — he is clearly far more calculating beneath the surface than anyone on the outside sees."

Zhou Xianya paused before going on. "And it isn't only him. Everyone on this boat is."

Even from the moment Zhou Xianya had begun speaking, Lu Huaixi had already half-guessed where it was going. Now that it was laid out plainly, she wasn't particularly surprised.

Xie Yuanjing naturally had his own designs. His position in the world wouldn't permit him to be without them — otherwise, when people spoke of him in laughing tones as a crafty old fox, his name would never have come up.

But Lu Huaixi didn't find herself especially troubled by it.

In Zhou Xianya's eyes, she was Xie Yuanjing's wife for life, and Zhou Xianya worried for her — worried she wasn't thinking things through, that she was too breezy and inattentive.

But that wasn't quite right. She had already known, long before today, that Xie Yuanjing had depths he didn't show. She had known he might have used her, and she hadn't looked away from it.

And compared to Zhou Xianya's caution, what this lake outing meant to Lu Huaixi was something rather different —

He was letting her see his real friends. And letting them see her. Once that happened, they would truly be on the same side. Truly on the same boat.

"I'm not gossiping for the sake of it. And honestly, the two of you do seem well-suited to each other, from what I can see. I'm just afraid you'll be too easygoing about it — not thinking ahead, not attending to things — because when two people are bound together, they do need to support each other. Feelings and all that...... when it comes down to it, they matter less in the long run than family connections. Do you take my meaning?"

"Xianya jiejie has never said this kind of thing to me before."

Lu Huaixi glanced at her, something quietly surprised moving through her chest.

"I thought Xianya jiejie cared more about...... two hearts that feel the same."

"I would rather marry someone I love — but wanting it doesn't make it happen. In the end it comes down to what heaven arranges. And I say this to you, but I'm also saying it to myself."

Zhou Xianya took her hand and looked out at the distance.

"Honestly, marrying someone you only somewhat like isn't necessarily the worst thing. In the end you'll be managing the inner household regardless — watching him take concubines, one after another. And if you marry someone with a complicated standing, you'll have to think even about the concubines' family backgrounds — whether they'd be useful to him, whether you should be the one to facilitate those arrangements."

Lu Huaixi hadn't given much thought to any of this. Or rather, she had rarely let herself.

But listening now, she found her mind turning to Xie Yuanjing with startling ease.

He had chosen to work with the Lu family for reasons of his own. In the same way, he would, in time, form other ties and alliances with other people for reasons of suitability. His boat would never be short of new passengers.

"It's probably too early to be saying all this to you — it's just that I thought of myself all of a sudden and couldn't hold it in."

Zhou Xianya came back to herself and saw the thoughtful look on the person beside her. A pang of regret moved through her.

"Just take it as something to half-listen to. You're different from me — you married someone whose heart is already with you. Whatever happens after, the connection between you two will always be something particular."

"I...... we're not quite what you think, Xianya jiejie."

"You don't need to be embarrassed in front of me. But now that I think about it — I was curious before, how the two of you would manage. You don't like anything too dull or confined, and you're not one to stay in one place for long. And Xie Yuanjing is known by everyone to be cold. When you said he was good to you, I wasn't entirely sure I believed it."

Lu Huaixi blinked.

Hearing the note of reassurance tucked into Zhou Xianya's words, she swallowed the explanation she'd been about to offer, let out a small laugh instead, and let the moment move on.

"And now that you've seen it for yourself?"

"Now I believe it. The way he stood up for you just now — that kind of protectiveness made even me hold my breath."

In the time it took to say a few sentences, the two of them were laughing again on their own account.

These were the kinds of things that lived at the heart of a girl's inner life — only now they were wound up with marriage, and so the girlish feelings carried a little more weight, a little less of that original purity.

But these were the things that could never be avoided. Born into wealth and rank, one always had to shoulder some portion of what came with it.

"After that commotion, Wu Wenlan probably won't have an easy time of it. I wonder whether she'll end up directing her resentment at you......"

"Hasn't she already?"

Lu Huaixi picked up the thread, and the lightness faded slightly from her expression.

Without Lu Huaixi and Zhou Xianya as noble friends, the Wu family would not treat Wu Wenlan gently.

Especially now that things had been made openly hostile.

But that was no longer her concern. She had no intention of feeling sorry for someone who had betrayed her.

"And that girl who stepped in for her — she probably resents us too."

"That's what makes me angry."

Zhou Xianya's brow drew together. "Anyone who didn't know better would think she was some princess. As if making a scene like that means people will praise her for loyalty and righteousness. What a nuisance."

Lu Huaixi listened without speaking.

Though nothing showed on her face, there was, for no reason she could name, a faint heaviness settling inside her.

Perhaps it was the thought of whoever might one day board Xie Yuanjing's boat. Perhaps it was a vague, formless confusion about whether she ever wanted to get married at all.

Either way, in the pauses where she might have spoken, she only moved her lips — and found, in the end, she had very little to say.

chapters.title: I Wanted to See You
chapters.content:
The business with Wu Wenlan had genuinely gotten to Zhou Xianya. In the end it was Lu Huaixi who came back to herself first and gently talked her around.

Then Lu Huaixi seemed to remember something and called Yaoshu over.

"Has anyone been keeping an eye on Wu Wenlan's side?"

"First Young Madam, please don't worry — we've had someone watching."

"Watching for what?" Zhou Xianya, who had caught this, asked.

Lu Huaixi glanced at her and answered plainly, "Honestly, I'm not sure yet. Just watching for now. But let's not talk about it — she's not worth our time."

At the bow of the boat was a slightly raised wooden rail, better positioned to see across the water.

Rather than going inside, Lu Huaixi stopped there and looked out at the distance where the water had no visible end.

It was so peaceful. If not for the wind being so strong, she could have gladly spent a night right here.

"Proprietress."

She was still thinking this when a voice came from behind.

Both of them turned. Qingling was walking toward them with a manservant carrying a small brazier behind her.

Lu Huaixi's mood immediately lifted. She put aside whatever had been weighing on her and pulled Zhou Xianya along to meet them.

"It's rather warm out, First Young Madam, so this is just a start — try it out, and if the coals are tricky to manage, the kitchen has prepared ingredients for grilling as well, so you'll have that option too."

The brazier wasn't particularly large, but once the coals were properly going, even with the wind, it would put out real heat.

But grilling something over fire was all about the experience. Talking anyone out of it would be too much of a dampener.

Lu Huaixi also knew perfectly well she wouldn't get much of anything to turn out right — but she felt inexplicably excited about trying. Especially after Gong Zhuo had mentioned a few days ago that Xie Yuanjing's grilled meat was excellent, which only made her want to try for herself.

Besides, she planned to have him try whatever she made. He had said himself he'd eat whatever it turned out like.

"Where's your wine?"

Zhou Xianya watched her squinting through the smoke with complete seriousness as she cut at the meat, and asked with some concern.

"Actually, let's just drink the wine. This whole setup is looking rather difficult — at this rate you'll just smoke yourself black and upset your stomach."

"The wine is right there."

Lu Huaixi didn't look up. "I'm making this for Xie Yuanjing. He can eat it."

"...... Are you certain he can eat it?"

—

"Are you certain you want to eat this?"

When the blackened meat was delivered to Xie Yuanjing, everyone at the table stared.

Shen Zhouxu took the plate and looked it over carefully, just to confirm that what was inside was overcooked meat and not charcoal from the brazier.

Xie Yuanjing, to his credit, was composed — only a flash of startled disbelief crossed his face, followed by a small upward curve of his lips.

He was just about to reach for the plate when the manservant beside him quickly spoke up:

"Young Master, First Young Madam says this is only for you to look at. She said you mustn't eat it."

Xie Yuanjing looked up and said nothing. He had said he would try her first attempt at cooking — even if what was delivered was a dish of coal.

"First Young Madam says that seeing it counts as tasting it. She says this time she just wanted you to see the level of her cooking and have a rough idea of what you're working with. Once you've taught her and she's practiced, then she'll let you eat."

Beside him, Shen Zhouxu let out a breath of relief. "Thank goodness your First Young Madam has more sense than your Young Master."

The way Xie Yuanjing had looked a moment ago — the next move would clearly have been to pick up a piece and put it in his mouth.

After the manservant withdrew, that particular episode passed quickly.

Quite a bit of wine had been drunk at the table, but at some point while the others were deep in conversation, Xie Yuanjing rose quietly and stepped out of the room.

Some things, before they're confirmed, can still be treated as if they don't exist. But once settled — the feelings that have been let out grow like vines, fast and relentless, no longer easy to ignore.

Like that plate of grilled meat just now, delivered to be seen but not eaten. One look, and he couldn't help wanting to know what Lu Huaixi had looked like while she was making it — whether she'd gotten annoyed partway through and lost patience.

The wind outside hadn't let up. To his right, the wide expanse of the river, carrying a cool damp wind that pressed against him.

He had only walked partway when he saw a figure approaching in the distance.

He stopped.

After a moment, the figure spotted him too, and came running toward him — eyes curved, smiling.

"Why are you out here?"

"Why did you come this way?"

Both of them spoke at the same moment.

There was something held back in Xie Yuanjing's voice. Watching Lu Huaixi come toward him without a moment's hesitation, he felt something shift in his chest.

"Was it getting a little dull on your end?" he said.

"No."

Lu Huaixi stopped in front of him and looked up at him. "It's been wonderful over there. I'm going to try fishing in a bit."

"Then why did you come over? Looking for me?"

"Yes. Gong Fei said you'd been drinking without eating anything, so I came to check."

"And now that you've checked?"

"Now I make you eat something."

Lu Huaixi smiled, her bright eyes catching the broken light off the water — a match for any ripple or shimmer on the river.

Xie Yuanjing felt himself go soft. His raised hand paused near her face, then came to rest at her earlobe.

Held back — and also not quite. That was the way he touched her, as if he were fighting himself every step of the way.

"That sure I'll listen to you?"

"Not entirely sure."

Lu Huaixi hesitated for just a moment, then looked at him again. "Will you?"

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing answered quietly. Then confirmed it once more. "I will."
