Lu Huaixi hadn't been thinking too much when she came over.

Those thoughts from earlier had been pressed down, but they had left traces — and now, threading back up, they were tugging at something she'd briefly felt once before and then pushed aside.

She had expected to feel self-conscious when she saw Xie Yuanjing, expected things to be less easy than usual between them. But running into him like this in the middle of the boat — her first reaction, without thinking, had been something close to delight.

And all those faint, restless feelings — the quiet heaviness, the things she hadn't quite been able to name — dissolved completely.

They got along well. The thought surfaced in her, quietly. They really did.

And if they were on the same boat, they ought to be honest about it.

"You still haven't said — why did you come out?"

Lu Huaixi looked up at him and asked.

Something warm landed on her ear — a brief, faint tingle of heat, then gone.

Something in her chest seemed to brush against something soft. Her lips moved slightly. She didn't dare make a sound.

Xie Yuanjing looked down at her, his eyes still dark and clear, even though the edges of his gaze had been touched by the wine.

"I wanted to see you."

He said it quietly, pressing the words down — and the low, soft tone scattered at once in the wind, drifting in every direction. "Wanted to, badly enough to get a headache. So I came."

There was nowhere to put a response like that.

Lu Huaixi's eyes went wide at his words. The composure she had been so ready to offer a moment ago began to waver.

She stood very still, genuinely unable to tell whether he was drunk or not.

Only the light wind remained, exploring the space between them — and the quiet, lapping sound of water.

A long while passed. Just as Lu Huaixi was nearly at the limit of holding it in, the man in front of her finally spoke again.

"Where's the meat you grilled?"

"Hmm?"

"The meat you sent over just now — was it all thrown away?"

He changed the subject so quickly it took her a moment to catch up. "No — there's still some left. It's sitting on the table."

"Why wasn't it thrown away?"

"They said they wanted to keep looking at it, because......"

She trailed off. She was debating whether or not to admit that she had been laughed at.

But Xie Yuanjing finished her sentence before she could.

"Because no one could have done a worse job grilling, so they wanted to hold onto it for comparison?"

Whatever lingering glow from a moment ago vanished entirely. Lu Huaixi went from bewildered to indignant in less than a second.

chapters.title: Sick
chapters.content:
"You're laughing at me!"

Lu Huaixi looked at him, genuinely annoyed. She had intended to give him a withering look — but her eyes went, without her permission, to the faint upward curve of his lips, and her indignation lost half its force.

What was there to smile about!

"I'm not talking to you anymore. I'm going fishing."

Lu Huaixi turned to leave.

Cooking took skill, but fishing — fishing was luck. She still had a chance.

Someone caught her arm before she got far, followed by a quiet "Wait" — and Xie Yuanjing had already moved in front of her, blocking her path.

The faint smile was still there, but his voice had dropped a little.

"Stay a little longer."

"For what?"

Lu Huaixi tilted her head back to look at him, her dark eyes making no secret of their displeasure.

He stopped her without saying anything more, just looked at her — until the last of her irritation had finally run out, and only then did he speak quietly.

"Don't be upset. When autumn comes, I'll take you to the mountain retreat."

Lu Huaixi turned her face away and said nothing.

"There's forest there for hunting, and you can make a proper fire for grilling. I'll teach you then."

He paused, then added, "I wasn't laughing at you. And I won't laugh at you for any reason, going forward."

"Then stop making me practice calligraphy."

"That one's non-negotiable."

"......"

Xie Yuanjing stood on the outer side, closer to the water. If he raised his arm only slightly, it would be enough to draw her in close.

But he held himself back and didn't move.

Even with the wine running through him — making it harder than usual to stay calm — all he had done was brush his fingers against her ear, and then catch her arm when she turned to leave.

And Lu Huaixi was no longer as unhappy as she had been a moment ago.

Once the mood had passed, it was only teasing — the kind that comes from being at ease with someone.

And now she'd somehow also acquired a trip to the mountains. Perhaps even hunting. Her tolerance for the calligraphy sessions had, rather involuntarily, grown a shade more generous.

"You can't take back what you said about the mountain retreat."

"I won't."

Xie Yuanjing said, "Not angry anymore?"

"I can endure."

Lu Huaixi gave a generous wave of her hand, and a smile found its way to her lips before she noticed. "I'm going now — they're waiting for me."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing didn't move aside. Instead he looked down at her hand, "Before you go — there's something I want to know."

"Go ahead."

Lu Huaixi was in a good mood now, and didn't notice the look on his face after he lowered his eyes.

From somewhere not far behind, the sound of footsteps approached — the guards accompanying those gentlemen, it seemed. Lu Huaixi glanced back, looked for a moment, then turned back around and stepped a little closer to Xie Yuanjing.

"What is it? Ask me quietly."

The sudden closeness made something in Xie Yuanjing's composure waver. The depths of his eyes were half-covered by lowered lids.

A moment later, he lost the argument with himself. He reached out and drew her into his arms.

The feeling that had been floating without purchase for days settled, at last, into something real. And whatever unnamed wrongness that had been troubling him — that rare, persistent discomfort — came undone in the closeness between them, as if it had found its answer.

Lu Huaixi hadn't even had time to make a sound of alarm before his low, quiet voice came down near her ear.

"They're watching."

"Who — watching what?"

"Watching how a husband and wife get on."

Xie Yuanjing breathed close to her ear. "I won't do anything to you. Just — hold you for a moment."

"Aren't they your close friends? In front of close friends, do you still need to......"

"Even close friends have things that haven't been said yet." He said. "I'm sorry — I didn't mean to startle you. I didn't expect them to come out."

The frantic beating of Lu Huaixi's heart steadied under the self-reproach in his voice.

Remembering why the two of them were together in the first place, she found she could no longer quite hold onto the shock and confusion of that first instant of being held.

"You don't need to apologize. You told me from the beginning that people can't be allowed to notice anything is off."

"Then don't be angry with me."

"I'm not angry."

In the middle of Lu Huaixi's gentle, accommodating words, Xie Yuanjing's arm tightened around her. His other hand rested lightly at the back of her neck, drawing her in just a little further.

"Just a moment more."

"......Mm."

He felt no guilt. No sense of deception.

Compared to something too formless and distant to reach, the change that had happened inside him toward Lu Huaixi was far more worth thinking about.

And besides — it was only an embrace. He was being quite restrained.

"What were you going to ask me just now?"

Perhaps because the silence had gone on too long, Lu Huaixi couldn't quite help it — she tilted her head back to look at him, waiting.

Xie Yuanjing was quiet for a beat before answering. "How long have you known Zhou family's eldest son?"

—

Lu Huaixi didn't spend long turning over the question. She didn't find it particularly strange that Xie Yuanjing would take an interest in the Zhou family.

The Zhous were not inferior to the Lus. Zhou Eldest Son, Zhou Jieyü, was the kind of young man others frequently spoke well of.

If his portrait had been among those sent over during the matchmaking, her family might truly have considered him.

Though that was only speculation — the absence of his portrait meant that side had not been willing to be considered at all.

So Lu Huaixi told Xie Yuanjing plainly about the relationship between the Lu and Zhou families. Everything except the portrait.

She even thought of what Zhou Xianya had said earlier — that a wife was not only meant to manage the inner household, but to be attentive to what would benefit her husband.

Managing the inner household was something she had no particular desire to do at the moment. But she was considerate enough to add a few more words — about Zhou Jieyü's temperament and his preferences.

Not long after she returned to the other end of the boat, it pulled alongside a small island. Shen Zhouxu's sister came aboard soon after.

She was a young woman who appeared somewhat cool at first glance — but turned out, the moment she spoke, to have a very gentle manner.

Lu Huaixi found herself thoroughly enjoying her stories about the world outside. She carried none of the constraints that came with being a noble daughter, and there was an easy freedom about her.

Only she didn't get to listen for long. Whether from hours in the wind or from standing too long over the brazier earlier, Lu Huaixi wasn't sure — but before too long, a headache set in.

By the time Xie Yuanjing came to find her, she had already been asleep inside for quite a while.

She had no memory of how she got off the boat. And the moment between her and Xie Yuanjing — that brief embrace — stayed on the boat too, as neither of them brought it up again.

"First Young Madam, are you still feeling dizzy today?"

Jingshuang came in from outside carrying the medicine, and within moments the room was thick with the smell of it.

Lu Huaixi's brow creased, and she quickly popped a dried plum into her mouth.

"I'm not drinking that."

"This is the last bowl for today, Young Madam — just endure a little longer?"

"Still not drinking it. I'm already better."

Lu Huaixi turned her face away and said under her breath:

"I felt fine the moment I woke up and had that pill. And yet a physician still had to be called — and then Mother's physician, and then the Old Madam insisted on calling her own, so I had three physicians come to look at me in one day. Xie Yuanjing didn't say a word — just stood there watching me swallow all those useless bitter medicines."

After all this time following Lu Huaixi around, Jingshuang had come to know her mistress's nature fairly well.

No matter how much the complaint sounded like displeasure, as long as no one had actually done something wrong, she could be coaxed back around. Simple enough, really — genuinely no guile about her, just like a child, the sort of person who made you want to look after her.

"The Young Master is worried about you, Young Madam."

Jingshuang said gently:

"He knows the pills came from Little Doctor Zeng, but without having a physician come to look, he couldn't quite rest easy. You may not know this, but that day — you were carried back by the Young Master himself. You slept without making a sound the whole way, and by evening your whole body was burning with fever. The physicians' medicine wouldn't even go down."

"He was worried, and yet he hasn't come to see me in days?"

Lu Huaixi said it almost without thinking.

Jingshuang froze. The words went out of her.

That day, the Young Master had carried her back, and the look on his face had frightened everyone who saw it.

But the day after the First Young Madam woke, once the physicians had confirmed there was nothing seriously wrong, the Young Master had not come to check on her again. Each night when he returned to the estate, it was after the First Young Madam had already fallen asleep.

The thought made Jingshuang's heart give an uneasy lurch. She looked up instinctively at the person before her, afraid she was angry.

chapters.title: Old Acquaintances, All of Them
chapters.content:
When Lu Huaixi first said it, there hadn't been much behind it — she had only said it in passing.

But after the words were out, she couldn't help frowning. Something very faint and formless settled in her chest.

All that talk of caring and worry — and yet he hadn't even been coming back to the estate. From the day she woke up and took the medicine to today, Xie Yuanjing had been absent for four days without a word of explanation.

Lu Huaixi wasn't even sure whether it was because of her being there that he had stopped coming home.

"I'm really not drinking this. It's sour and bitter both at once, and drinking it only makes my head ache more. Just take it away and pour it out."

Lu Huaixi glanced once more at the dark medicine in the bowl, then rose and walked toward the inner room.

It wasn't anger exactly — the word didn't quite fit what she and Xie Yuanjing were to each other. But she didn't feel like talking, and she didn't feel like bringing it up.

"First Young Madam, would you like to change?"

Jingshuang, who had followed her in with the things she'd set down, looked at her.

Lu Huaixi nodded. "I'm going to Shun'an Fang."

"But your health has only just recovered......"

"I'm just going to sit."

Lu Huaixi chose a dress in soft blue-green — fresh-looking and bright. "I've been completely fine for days. Don't worry. If you don't trust me, at least trust Little Doctor Zeng."

"Your maidservant only worries about you catching a wind again."

Jingshuang knew there was no point arguing. She pressed her lips together, turned it over for a moment, then spoke again. "Should your maidservant go and let Gong Zhuo know?"

"Yes, go ahead."

She had said she wouldn't bring it up, but that was a separate matter from the promise she had made. Lu Huaixi would not do things out of spite.

Shun'an Fang was usually quieter in the daytime — but ever since the incident, people had taken to dropping by even on ordinary afternoons to enjoy the music.

Lu Huaixi had taken her time getting there, and it was mid-afternoon by the time she arrived. Entering through the back courtyard, she could already hear the sound of strings and woodwinds drifting from the front hall.

Neither Qingling nor Qirui was in the back. Lu Huaixi didn't need anyone to attend her — she led her two maidservants straight through the rear courtyard and up to the private room she kept for herself on the upper floor.

"You drank your medicine this morning, Young Madam — no tea today, please."

Yaoshu hadn't caught the earlier conversation between Lu Huaixi and Jingshuang, and poured out a cup of warm water without looking up.

"Your maidservant just heard some of the girls talking — the kitchen has been experimenting with plum tea and sweet chilled rice cakes. You're still not supposed to have cold things, so perhaps try the plum tea instead?"

Lu Huaixi was waiting for Qingling to finish up and come find her to go through the account books. At the suggestion, she nodded. "The plum tea should be a little cool at least — don't serve it warm. That ruins it."

"That won't do——"

"Then room temperature."

Knowing this wasn't up for discussion, Yaoshu dropped the subject.

Room temperature was still better than cold.

Yaoshu pushed the door open to go out, and as she turned to pull it shut, she spotted Qingling coming up the wooden stairs at a quick pace from the floor below.

"Don't rush — you'll hurt yourself."

"I won't, I've run up these stairs a hundred times, I could do it with my eyes closed."

Qingling gave her a quick smile. "There's someone downstairs asking to see the proprietress. Not the first time either — the person doesn't look ordinary, and I didn't want to make any decisions without asking."

"Where are they?"

Yaoshu leaned out to look. "In one of the curtained rooms?"

"That's right. Very distinguished-looking, with quite a few people alongside them. I'm going in to tell the proprietress now."

Lu Huaixi hadn't expected to walk in and immediately find herself with a visitor.

And from what Qingling was describing, this was clearly no ordinary person.

"Do they know I'm here?"

"Probably not. They came once before too — heard the proprietress was out that time, listened to a song or two, and left."

Qingling lowered her voice. "The person doesn't look like they're here for trouble. They said something about everyone being old acquaintances, and that they'd be visiting the estate in a few days — but what they said is a little hard to read."

"What did they say exactly?"

"There's a young woman with them — looks about seventeen or eighteen. I heard them tell her that the singers here don't come close to her voice, not good enough, not even worth comparing. And then they said that as long as she was willing, the person she wanted to see could definitely be arranged."

Lu Huaixi said nothing. That was an odd thing to say — though it was also possible the young woman was genuinely exceptional.

After all, a dancer could make a name for herself in the capital on technique and grace alone, but the art of singing — beyond skill, it had to be able to reach the listener's heart.

Still, she noted it.

But she didn't think the person was here to cause trouble.

Shun'an Fang had come out into the open now. Only a fool would come looking for problems right under her nose.

"Does the proprietress want to go and meet them? I'm not sure what to make of it this time — the person kept smiling the whole time, but there was something in their eyes that didn't feel easy. Made me a little unsettled the longer I looked."

"I'll go."

Lu Huaixi rose.

"This place probably isn't somewhere that person frequents. For them to come twice and ask for me by name — they must genuinely want a meeting."

Under other circumstances she might not have cared.

But the person had mentioned the Chengen Marquis Estate — which meant they might have come on account of Xie Yuanjing, and might know the Lu family as well.

Even if not, just for what they'd said about the girls' singing not being good enough — she ought to go and see exactly how impressive this person thought they were.

Downstairs, a song was just drawing to a close.

As Lu Huaixi made her way down, she caught the last few notes, and found nothing lacking in the girls' voices.

The beaded curtain was lifted before she reached it — as if the person inside had known she was coming.

"Second Miss Lu?"

The person asked, dressed in deep blue brocade, with the same air of easy elegance as Shen Zhouxu — though without Shen Zhouxu's open warmth.

He paused, then smiled. "I'm getting ahead of myself — I should say, Madam Xie."

At his words, the people behind him all lowered their heads and stepped back. Lu Huaixi didn't look directly at them, but she could sense that the only young woman among them had looked up at those words.

Just the one glance, though. Very quickly, she lowered her head again.

"My name is Zheng Xiaoqi. Yuanjing and I have been close for many years. I only recently returned to the capital. By rights, I can call you sister-in-law."

The man rose and gestured for Lu Huaixi to sit.

"It's a shame I couldn't make it to his wedding. I had been planning to visit the estate in a few days — but when I heard that sister-in-law had a place like this for listening to music and watching performances, I thought I'd come here first to take a look, and to meet you properly."

Lu Huaixi smiled, her expression easy and giving nothing away, and took the seat beside him without hesitation.

She wasn't sure how deep his friendship with Xie Yuanjing actually ran, but close friends of many years — she doubted that was quite right.

And though she didn't pay much attention to the affairs of the great families, the Zheng family was not one she was completely unfamiliar with. Not a name you wanted to make an enemy of, but not one that required any fawning either.

"Shun'an Fang is a place to sit and enjoy some quiet in one's leisure time, but the girls here who sing and dance are not inferior to any other establishment."

Lu Huaixi was warm without being overly close, still keeping that faint, measured distance. Remembering what had been said about the singing, she kept her tone unhurried.

"If it suits your taste, Officer Zheng, please stay as long as you like. If there is anything that falls short in our hospitality, please do say so."

"Sister-in-law needn't be so formal. This place really is pleasant — otherwise I wouldn't have come once and found reason to come back."

Zheng Xiaoqi lifted his teacup, gave an easy smile, then looked up again.

"Come to think of it, everyone in this room is an old acquaintance of Yuanjing's. Myself — and this person too. So sister-in-law, there's no need to stand on ceremony with me."

With that, Zheng Xiaoqi glanced at the young woman who had said nothing at his side, and smiled again:

"Back then, Yuanjing nearly...... but never mind that. It's all past now. And it's a funny thing — since sister-in-law has so many performers here, perhaps in future there can be more contact between them and Linian."

"Oh? And this young lady would be......"

Lu Huaixi had already caught the deliberate pause in Zheng Xiaoqi's words.

Not only her — the two maidservants at her side and Qingling had caught it too.

Several pairs of eyes shifted to her instinctively.

But the curve of Lu Huaixi's lips didn't waver. Her gaze followed his, and landed precisely on the young woman who was slowly lifting her head.

Dark brows, a hint of something melancholy in the eyes. But undeniably — a striking face.

chapters.title: I Won't Be His Master
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had never thought it improper for someone to harbour feelings for Xie Yuanjing.

Even she herself, when the matter of marriage arose, would turn it over in her mind once or twice — wondering whether a person was suitable, wondering whether someone better might exist.

After marrying Xie Yuanjing, she understood clearly that this was nothing more than a transaction, and so she had never intended to pry into his past or his future plans.

And so when Mu Nianwei stirred up trouble in front of her time and again, she had simply watched it as one watches a diversion.

If the other party went too far, she would strike back. Otherwise, let each keep to their own peace, and bother no one.

But today's scene — played out right before her, and involving a young woman who appeared to hold no particular status, merely an old acquaintance — left her, for no clear reason, more unsettled than anything before.

Yet the unease was not directed at this girl who had yet to utter a single word. It was directed at something Xie Yuanjing had once said.

He had said he had no one he liked, and did not consider love and affection something he needed.

In other words, as long as the arrangement was suitable, anyone would do.

But the more cold and rational a person was, the more likely it was that a woman like this one — with no status to lean on, no support she could offer him — had once meant something real to Xie Yuanjing.

Lu Huaixi turned the thought over once in her mind, then settled back into calm with remarkable speed.

She smiled again, her brows and eyes curved in their usual way — gentle and bright.

The girl seemed to freeze for a moment at that smile, standing there in a daze before she finally came back to herself and dropped into a curtsy.

"To answer the Young Mistress's question — Liniang was a singing girl on the riverbanks of Rongcheng, in earlier years."

Singing girls made their living by song, and not infrequently met with difficult men.

The fortunate ones sang for a few years, saved enough, and quietly moved on to a better life elsewhere. The less fortunate — well, that was harder to speak of.

Lu Huaixi showed no surprise at the answer. When the girl finished speaking, she simply gave a small nod. "Then the songs this young lady sings must be quite beautiful."

Rongcheng was rather far from the capital.

To have gone from being a singing girl there to now being acquainted with two young masters — one from the Marquis's household and one from the Zheng family — she could not have managed without some genuine ability.

Perhaps finding nothing amiss on Lu Huaixi's face, Zheng Xiaoqi, who had been silent for some time, looked over again.

"Why not mention the part where Yuanjing took you away and arranged a place for you elsewhere?"

He spoke as though merely making casual conversation. "The Young Mistress is not an outsider. If you two get along, she may even take you to see Yuanjing again. When he cut ties with you back then, it was out of necessity — for your sake, when all is said and done."

The tea in the cup was nearly gone.

Lu Huaixi watched Qingling's hands tremble slightly as she refilled it, and knew at once that the girl was regretting having delivered that message and brought her here.

She reached over and gave Qingling's hand a light pat on the back. When Qingling looked up, holding back her feelings, Lu Huaixi smiled at her warmly.

Unlike the perfunctory smiles from before, this one was sincere — she wanted Qingling not to be angry on someone else's behalf.

"Look at me, I promised not to bring up the past, and here I couldn't help myself."

Zheng Xiaoqi feigned self-reproach.

"Sister-in-law, don't take it to heart. I hadn't originally planned to bring Liniang along, but I heard that Yuanjing — a man who never meddles in others' affairs — had recently stepped in on behalf of Shun'an Fang. I thought perhaps he was remembering old times, so I brought her along to have a look."

"Hearing you speak of it, it seems you and he are quite close."

Lu Huaixi withdrew her gaze and met Zheng Xiaoqi's eyes.

He paused for a moment, caught in the faint smile she had not quite put away, and said nothing for a beat before finally nodding.

"He and I were acquainted before either of us had even entered the academy. It's only that I've been away from the capital these past two years and couldn't remain at his side."

"Is that so."

Lu Huaixi sounded as though she had just understood something, but then furrowed her brow slightly, a look of puzzlement crossing her face. "I don't believe I've ever heard him mention you, Master Zheng. When I first heard your name just now, I thought you were trying to deceive me."

"He—"

"I know all his colleagues. He mentions them from time to time, and introduced me to them one by one. But you, Master Zheng—"

Lu Huaixi curved her lips, and as she spoke, two slightly pointed teeth showed the faintest peek. "You, Master Zheng, I am hearing of for the very first time. Had I not heard it today, I would never have imagined you two were close."

Zheng Xiaoqi's expression did not change, but his eyes were no longer as composed as before.

He smiled along with her and said, "The friendship between Yuanjing and me has never been measured by such superficialities."

Then he glanced back at Liniang and continued, "There are things Yuanjing finds difficult to say himself. But since I know of them, I naturally intend to speak up on his behalf. Sister-in-law, please don't misunderstand, and don't be angry with him."

"Master Zheng needn't be modest. Speak up all you like — I'm not sure I'm in any position to do anything about it either way."

"How refreshingly direct, Sister-in-law."

Zheng Xiaoqi set down his teacup.

"Since the time Yuanjing took Liniang away, she has not sung again. Later, when he ended things with her, she was foolish enough to stay and wait for him in that place. I felt sorry for her and brought her back to the capital, but she didn't want to trouble anyone. So I thought I would help her find somewhere she could make a living."

Lu Huaixi said nothing. She sat there and listened at an unhurried pace, her face betraying nothing beyond what it usually showed.

Unable to read her thoughts, Zheng Xiaoqi's eyes darkened for a moment — but his words did not stop.

"Liniang had quite a reputation as a singer in Rongcheng, and her voice is a rare gift. Since Sister-in-law holds Shun'an Fang in her hands, why not be generous and keep her on here? In the future, Yuanjing will naturally be grateful to Sister-in-law for it."

Behind them came the sound of a cup shifting — Liniang had bumped it in her startlement.

Lu Huaixi's fingertip tapped lightly against the wooden armrest of her chair. She did not look over, and she did not respond.

"Sister-in-law, do not be displeased with me over my words. I'm not one for roundabout talk, but the meaning is what it is."

Zheng Xiaoqi pressed on. "I am genuinely thinking of Yuanjing's wellbeing. Besides, Shun'an Fang is already a place for listening to music and watching dance. With Liniang here, she will surely lighten Sister-in-law's burdens."

The person across from him remained lukewarm and unreadable, and Zheng Xiaoqi's composure had by now frayed noticeably from how it had been at the start.

He had wanted to see this second daughter of the Lu family lose her temper and make a scene — and then carry that scene back to Xie Yuanjing.

If things grew unpleasant enough, the Marquis's household would suffer, and so would the Lu family.

That way, Xie Yuanjing would lose his backing, and would no longer be able to outmanoeuvre him at every turn as he always had.

Yet after all this time, he had not managed to draw a single unfavourable expression from this young woman's face.

Instead, her easy, offhand responses had made him feel, for a strange moment, a flicker of envy toward Xie Yuanjing.

"Sister-in-law—"

"No."

Lu Huaixi finally gave her answer. She picked up the teacup beside her, took a sip, and set it back down.

"Shun'an Fang is my own establishment. I won't be adding people on a whim. However, if this young lady is willing, she may remain here for now."

Jingshuang and Yaoxu behind her startled, and moved instinctively to step forward.

But before they could speak, they heard her say, "Jingshuang, take this young lady to our First Young Master. I may not be adding anyone here, but he can find another way — it need not go through me."

"Young Mistress—"

"Sister-in-law, is that quite right?"

Zheng Xiaoqi was caught off guard by how cleanly and swiftly she had washed her hands of it, and stood there momentarily taken aback.

But Lu Huaixi paid no attention. She rose to her feet and smiled at him once more.

"His old acquaintances, his old affairs — I won't be the one making decisions. He can come do that himself."

chapters.title: Please Let Me Stay
chapters.content:
When Lu Huaixi left, the expressions on the handmaids' faces were not particularly pleasant.

There was anger at the people in that private room, and indignation on behalf of their own young mistress.

Lu Huaixi, however, remained calm throughout, her expression composed and unhurried.

The only difference was that the smile at the corners of her mouth lacked the brightness it had carried when she arrived — it held a slight edge of feeling.

Zheng Xiaoqi had not anticipated her being so decisive. He had wanted to exchange more words with her, but she had not even left him a parting glance.

No matter how slow one might be, she could see plainly that Zheng Xiaoqi meant no good.

"Young Mistress..."

Jingshuang had not stayed behind. She had given instructions to the others to wait there, and followed Lu Huaixi instead.

She trailed a step behind, wanting to say something — her lips moved, but the words would not come.

She had been under Gong Zhuo's charge before, but aside from her daily duties, she did not know much of the First Young Master's affairs. Even if she wanted to offer some comfort, she could not say with certainty that the young woman had nothing to do with him.

And yet, in her heart, she did not believe they had.

The words died at "Young Mistress," and Jingshuang hesitated, unsure how to begin. Yaoxu picked up instead.

"That person actually had the nerve to think up such a scheme — and calls himself close with the First Young Master? I'd say he's rotten to the core!"

Yaoxu glanced back as the curtain fell, and caught just a glimpse of the young woman standing inside, her eyes distant and unfocused.

She frowned. "A singing girl from Rongcheng chasing all the way to the capital — don't tell me it was just to catch up with an old acquaintance. Even if she didn't know before, now that she's heard that the First Young Master is already married, she still followed along to Shun'an Fang. What is that if not deliberate provocation toward the Young Mistress?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing. She was not as furious as Yaoxu — she did not even have what one might call intense emotion.

But she was genuinely unsettled.

That unsettledness was like anticipating a long-awaited outing, preparing everything with high spirits and stepping out the gate — only to be met with rain.

She could blame no one. She had no standing to blame anyone. All she could do was press down that smouldering flicker of irritation, accept the sudden rain, and let the flame of that outing go out.

Even after the rain stopped, she could no longer find the mood she'd had at the start.

"I simply cannot let this go. Just now she stood there and said nothing — what does that mean? Tacit agreement?"

Yaoxu grew more indignant the more she spoke. "Looking at her like that, she really did want to stay in Shun'an Fang. What gives her the right? She thinks very highly of herself!"

"That's enough."

Seeing that Yaoxu was on the verge of losing herself entirely, Lu Huaixi stopped her. "Why blame her for it?"

"Young Mistress—"

"If she had any choice, why would she be following behind someone surnamed Zheng?"

Lu Huaixi's gaze settled somewhere in the distance, her voice unhurried.

From time to time, a familiar face passed by, and she still turned to offer them a gentle smile — the kind that suited her well.

"I haven't given this much thought. You needn't dwell on it either. But Qingling, in the future — if that Zheng person comes again, remember to have someone keep a close eye on things."

"Understood, I'll remember."

"Though he probably won't come again. He's accomplished what he set out to do. There's no reason for him to return."

She said nothing further. As she passed through the main hall, she paused near the back and turned to look at the stage — at the young woman who had just begun to sing.

This was the first time she had heard this girl's voice. It was lovely.

"Mistress, shall I—"

"Young Mistress Xie."

Qingling had been about to ask whether she would be staying for a meal, when a voice came from behind — low and soft, carrying a trace of timidity.

The voice held uncertainty, but also a kind of resolve, as though the speaker had thrown caution to the wind.

Lu Huaixi did not respond immediately. She listened until the singer on stage finished the line, then turned her head to look.

"Is there something more, miss?"

"Liniang knows this is presumptuous."

The young woman bit her lip, her hands at her sides clutching the corner of her skirt, as though summoning enormous courage. "Liniang wishes to ask Young Mistress Xie's grace — to let Liniang stay."

Her voice was swallowed almost at once by the sound of the qin strings, as though she had said nothing at all.

But Lu Huaixi had heard her.

The others nearby exchanged glances of surprise, then instinctively furrowed their brows, dissatisfied with this Liniang.

To approach their young mistress and speak in such a tone — what nerve.

Qingling moved forward a step, about to speak. Lu Huaixi raised a hand and gently pressed it against her forearm.

"Mistress—"

"Don't."

Lu Huaixi said this, then looked back toward the one who had come. Her dark eyes were clear and still, the corners of her lips carrying a faint curve from having just spoken — not a trace of anger in her expression.

Liniang had been standing with her head half-bowed, but when she heard Lu Huaixi's voice, she could not help looking up.

"Young Mistress Xie, Liniang knows this is far too impolite and rash. But Liniang came to speak to you of her own accord, not because of anyone else... I heard that Shun'an Fang is a place that sells art, not the person. I... I wanted to try."

Perhaps from nerves, her voice trembled slightly — but she did not stop.

"I can play the qin and sing. I know a little dance as well. I have no intention of making things difficult for Young Mistress Xie. I only want a place to stay. If I am allowed to remain, I swear I will not let the past cause any trouble between you and the First Young Master. I will stay out of sight and keep to myself. Please, Young Mistress — give me a chance."

The words "the past" in Liniang's plea carried more weight than all the verbose nonsense Zheng Xiaoqi had poured out in that room.

Lu Huaixi studied the young woman a little more carefully this time and met her eyes.

Liniang quickly looked away, her gaze dropping in timidity.

"It is true that this is a place that sells art, not the person. But I am not short of people at the moment."

The song on stage had just ended, which made Lu Huaixi's voice all the clearer — steady and composed.

"My decision not to keep you is not entirely because of the 'past' between you and Xie Yuanjing. To speak plainly, I know nothing at all about that past you speak of, so it has never factored into my considerations. What I feel is a simple displeasure, and an unwillingness to let anyone use any reason whatsoever to draw Shun'an Fang into their affairs."

Liniang seemed startled. Her lips parted slightly, as though this was the first time she had heard someone speak so casually and yet so honestly.

"I don't know if you can follow my meaning — to put it directly: Shun'an Fang has nothing to do with the person Xie Yuanjing. This is my place. And so whether it is Master Zheng or yourself — you are welcome to come spend money listening to music. But if you intend to come here and drag in anything connected to Xie Yuanjing, to let my Shun'an Fang become the subject of other people's gossip, then that I will not allow."

"But — but is not the Young Mistress's establishment also the First Young Master's—"

"No."

Lu Huaixi cut her off. "My place is my place. This building is one I took over from the very beginning, piece by piece, with my own money. The people inside are young women selected one by one — and properly trained — by my head manager."

When those words fell, not only Liniang, but everyone else who had overheard wore a flash of surprise on their faces.

None of them had expected her to draw the line between herself and Xie Yuanjing so clearly. And none had expected a young noblewoman of no more than fifteen or sixteen — raised in comfort and privilege — to speak with such lucid self-possession.

"The young women I take in are often those without backing or status, and they have had a hard time of it. But this is not a charity. I run a business. I cannot simply nod and let someone stay just because she says she is wretched. Liniang — I hope you don't mind my calling you that — rather than coming to me, you would do better to find Xie Yuanjing yourself, and soon."

By the time Lu Huaixi finished speaking, Zheng Xiaoqi had already lifted the curtain and stepped out from the room.

She did not know how much he had heard. She glanced at him once, then looked away.

"The two of you can work it out yourselves. Whatever you decide in the end, there is no need to come and inform me."

"Young Mistress Xie—"

chapters.title: She Won't Interfere
chapters.content:
Seeing the person turn to leave after having said her piece, Liniang instinctively called out to stop her.

In truth, she did not know what she could possibly say once she had stopped her. She did not even have the courage to beg a second time.

And yet she was genuinely curious — curious about what kind of young woman could make a man like him settle his heart.

Today she had seen for herself: beyond a beauty one could not easily forget, there was a bearing and a self-assurance that suffused every inch of her — like glass that had caught the light, so striking that those who looked on felt a pang of inadequacy by comparison.

That was how Liniang felt.

She was greedy for one more look. And yet, when she truly looked, she feared what she might see of herself in those bright, clear eyes.

"Young Mistress Xie, I am sorry."

Liniang spoke softly. "I did not mean to make you unhappy. I did not want you to be angry over any of this. I only thought... I only thought that..."

That she might truly be allowed to stay.

That if she stayed, she might be a little closer to him. Even if she could do nothing. Even if she could not win a single glance from him. She would be willing.

"I am sorry."

She said it again.

There was still fear in her — fear that this high-born noblewoman would punish her, have her seized and sold off.

She was timid and felt small. Yet somewhere beneath it all, she still nursed a faint, stubborn hope that she might have some small thread of connection to him again — or that, if nothing else, someone might take pity on her and he would reach out once more.

"I beg Young Mistress to forgive me."

Liniang lowered her head further, at a loss for what more to say, and simply repeated herself. "I beg Young Mistress to forgive me."

Lu Huaixi's gaze lingered for a moment on the slight trembling of the girl's hands. After a long pause, she finally said something.

"You need not beg my forgiveness. I bear you no ill will."

Liniang looked up in startlement at those words. Lu Huaixi continued, "You have done me no harm. I have no intention of doing anything to you — nor would I think you wrong simply because of who you love or what past you may have shared with someone."

"Young Mistress..."

"But that is only so long as our paths do not cross. If you were to set your sights on me or on what is mine, then I cannot make any promises."

"I won't, I won't..."

Liniang spoke in a rush.

In all the days since Zheng Xiaoqi had found her and spoken of that man, she had not once been nervous enough to cry. But now, at the words "I would not think you wrong for who you love or what past you shared with someone," the tears she had been holding back suddenly threatened to spill.

She did not dare cry. She only blinked, forced the sting back, and then gripped her sleeves more tightly, filled with a different kind of nerves.

"There are other establishments besides my Shun'an Fang that sell art without selling the person. And apart from singing, there are other ways to make a living. Since you have come all this way for him, go and find him directly. But—"

Lu Huaixi paused, and in the end, she could not help adding one more line. "Before you go chasing after something so uncertain, you had best make sure you can get through each day first."

What the uncertain thing was — perhaps each person had their own answer.

It might be love. It might be the wish to be seen and valued by someone.

Lu Huaixi said no more after that. Out of the corner of her eye, she saw Zheng Xiaoqi emerge, and having no interest in pleasantries with him, she gave him only a casual smile before turning away.

From behind came Jingshuang's voice, asking Liniang whether she was leaving now.

Liniang seemed to choke back something, but Lu Huaixi had no inclination to turn around and look.

Many people called her kind-hearted, the sort most easily moved. But she did not see herself that way.

Today, for instance.

She could see that Liniang had misgivings, and she could tell that the girl had come here largely because Zheng Xiaoqi had coaxed and baited her into it. Even so, she would not allow the girl to stay simply because she seemed pitiable.

In Lu Huaixi's mind, this person was not worth more than Shun'an Fang.

No matter how wretched Liniang's history might truly be, no matter how much hardship she might have truly suffered, no matter whether Xie Yuanjing might feel something or wish to provide for her — she would not keep someone who could at any moment be a threat to Shun'an Fang.

Yet she was not entirely without feeling. In the end, she did remind Jingshuang to let Xie Yuanjing know that the person had been brought by Zheng Xiaoqi — she had not come on her own.

Whatever the two of them decided after that, she would not involve herself. It had nothing to do with her.

"Young Mistress, shall this servant take the person over now?" Jingshuang said in a low voice.

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Go ahead."

"Yes... then, do you have any words you'd like this servant to pass along to the First Young Master?"

"No."

Truly nothing. And even if there were, she had no interest in saying it.

Lu Huaixi chose a seat in the hall and settled herself down. After all that commotion, she wanted nothing more than to sit quietly and listen to the new music.

As for Xie Yuanjing, whom she had not laid eyes on for several days — she had no intention of sparing him any thought right now.

"Are all the young ladies performing today singing for the first time?"

Lu Huaixi looked toward Qingling, making it clear she had no wish to speak of anything else. Jingshuang did not press her further, and slipped away with a low bow.

Yaoxu watched until Jingshuang had escorted the others out of Shun'an Fang before withdrawing her gaze. She, too, turned to look at the stage, as though nothing at all had happened.

"Yes, it's their first time. A bit later there's also a new dance — something the Mistress and Qirui came up with a while back."

"That's ready as well?"

Lu Huaixi sounded genuinely surprised. It was true she had helped choreograph it, but with everything that had happened — entering the palace, the wedding — she had only offered a few ideas at the start, and never touched it again afterward.

"It is, though Qirui isn't certain whether it came out the way the Mistress originally imagined."

"What I had in mind was just a passing thought while watching the flowers bloom — nothing concrete at all. It was all down to you. I'll watch properly later. I'm sure it's beautiful."

The person before them smiled with curved eyes, her dark gaze bright. Two faintly pointed teeth peeked out, and she looked nothing like she had a moment ago.

Qingling watched her carefully, and quietly let out a breath of relief. She smiled back.

"Will the Mistress practise today?"

"Not today. I want to hear their new music. And Qingling, please don't call me 'Mistress' anymore — it makes me sound terribly old."

Qingling laughed softly, and was about to reply when someone came in through the outer door.

Out of the corner of her eye, Qirui moved to meet them. The two exchanged a few quiet words, and then both pairs of eyes turned toward where Lu Huaixi was sitting.

After what had just happened with that insufferable Zheng Xiaoqi, Qingling had become thoroughly guarded. Taking advantage of the moment while Lu Huaixi was watching the stage, she turned and walked toward Qirui.

Who is it? she mouthed silently. For the Mistress?

Qirui met her eyes and gave a small gesture.

Qingling's expression grew more cautious. She looked toward the person stepping into the main hall.

It was a young gentleman of refined and scholarly bearing — handsome and gracious, his manner one of quiet ease. When he caught her looking, a smile rose to his lips, warm and arresting as willows in spring moonlight.

chapters.title: As Long as You're Well
chapters.content:
Shun'an Fang received guests of all walks. On any given day there would be elegant, refined young gentlemen, or young masters whose every gesture radiated ease and wealth.

The Zheng Xiaoqi who had arrived earlier, with all his visible entourage, was clearly the free-spending sort at a glance.

But the one who had come now was different.

This person's noble bearing was tempered by a deliberate restraint of presence. He had fewer attendants than Zheng Xiaoqi, but it was plain he was no ordinary man — set apart from the common folk who walked on the ground.

Qingling's instinct told her he meant no harm. But after what had just happened, she did not trust her own instincts.

She also understood: the moment someone occupied the heights these fine lords did, they could never be entirely harmless.

"Has the gentleman come to listen to music?"

Qingling approached and stopped before him.

She had been about to say more, when she saw him nod. "I've come to have a look."

He then glanced toward Qirui beside her, clearly having already exchanged a few words with her earlier.

"Then speak with her, please."

His voice was unhurried, like the sound of water running over stones — gentle and warm. "I am Miss Zhou's elder brother. I happen to be passing by today. If she has a free moment, I'd be glad to share a cup of tea with her. If she's occupied, that is perfectly fine too. Whatever is convenient."

A few words, and it became clear that this person was nothing like Zheng Xiaoqi.

Both carried the same air of fine breeding, but this gentleman had about him a distinct warmth — and he was strikingly handsome, at that.

Qingling gave Qirui a small nod, murmured for him to wait a moment, and turned back.

When Lu Huaixi heard that someone else wished to see her, she looked a little dazed.

"Who did you say?"

"Miss Zhou's elder brother," said Qingling.

Lu Huaixi came back to herself.

Miss Zhou's elder brother — Zhou Jieyu?

She turned and looked toward the main entrance. The moment she did, she met the eyes of the visitor, who was already watching her with a smile.

—

When Jingshuang arrived with the person in tow, Xie Yuanjing had just left for the prison in connection with official business.

After waiting nearly an hour without sight of him — with officials coming and going the entire time — Jingshuang did not dare linger, and led the young woman away.

Liniang had followed silently behind her all this while. When she saw Jingshuang turning to leave, a flash of panic crossed her eyes.

"Jingshuang, we... we haven't seen him yet..."

Her reluctance and her feelings were written too plainly on her face. Seeing that she had seemed to accept things a moment ago and was now staring after him with such longing again, Jingshuang made no effort to soften her tone.

"Since our Young Mistress gave the word, she will see to it that you meet the First Young Master."

She glanced at her. "You need not feel that anyone here will deceive you or do you harm. If they truly had no intention of letting you meet him, you would not have been allowed out of Shun'an Fang to begin with."

"I... I didn't mean it that way..."

Liniang lowered her head. "I only thought — we've already waited so long. If we leave now, I worry it will all have been for nothing."

"It is only wasted time if you don't see him today. As long as you do see him — no matter how long you waited or where — it will not have been for nothing."

Jingshuang said nothing more after that, turning her thoughts instead to the path toward the Marquis's residence.

"Go and send word to the Young Mistress," she told the handmaid beside her. "The First Young Master is occupied. We may need to wait at the main gate before we can get sight of him."

—

By the time Lu Huaixi came to meet him, she and Zhou Jieyu had already finished an entire pot of tea.

Between them sat a wide table. Spread with the teapot, cups, and a few dishes of tea pastries, there was still space to spare.

But despite that distance, despite the music playing above them, Lu Huaixi could hear Zhou Jieyu's casual words with perfect clarity.

It was a steady, settled voice, carrying with it the attentiveness of an elder brother.

"I haven't had an opportunity to ask until now — after the wedding, have you been settling in well at the Marquis's household?"

From another person, the question might have felt abrupt. But Lu Huaixi only paused for a moment before thinking of her own friendship with Zhou Xianya, and gave him a small nod.

"Very well. Besides, I can make a good life wherever I am."

"That does sound like you."

Zhou Jieyu lowered his eyes to his teacup. "As long as you're well, that's what matters."

Whether it was the teacup partially obscuring his face, she could not be sure, but when Lu Huaixi looked over, she had the sense that the smile at his lips was not quite as full as before.

She did not intend to look into it. Her gaze drifted back to the stage, and she left the remark unanswered.

"And will Xie the First Young Master come to collect you today?"

Zhou Jieyu spoke again not long after. Lu Huaixi paused, then smiled easily. "He won't. He's been rather busy of late."

"So he has."

Zhou Jieyu nodded. "He would be. These past few days I've had occasion to meet with Senior Official Xun at court, and I heard that he recently took on a new student — someone with some connection to Xie the First Young Master."

Lu Huaixi did not know this Senior Official Xun, but she found herself looking over instinctively, genuinely puzzled as to why Zhou Jieyu was telling her all this.

"You need not look at me like that. I don't usually talk about people behind their backs. But if I regard you as a little sister, then some things are simply worth mentioning in passing."

"Does Brother Zhou mean that this student and Xie Yuanjing are on bad terms?"

"Your mind works faster than Xianya's. But it would be more accurate to say that Xie the First Young Master is deeply displeased with him. The two came to blows before — he nearly beat the man to death, after what happened to the Cheng'en Marquis."

Zhou Jieyu kept his gaze on the performers above. He did not turn to look at Lu Huaixi.

Perhaps it was a casual posture. Perhaps he was giving her room to take things in at her own pace.

"Very few people know about Xie the First Young Master striking him. He doesn't make a habit of leaving loose ends, and personally raising his hand like that — it has only happened that once."

He continued, "Even so, it wouldn't hurt to offer a quiet word of caution when the time is right. That student has always had a reputation in others' eyes for being gentle and proper. Now that he has a senior official's recommendation and is gaining favour, he will only be seen as someone of admirable temperament going forward."

Zhou Jieyu did not say a great deal, but in a few words he gave Lu Huaixi the essential shape of the situation.

She could not help glancing at him again.

Her friendship with Zhou Xianya was close, but she had not seen this elder brother often, and so she was not entirely certain: when he brought up the Lu family — seemingly in passing, after sharing those details — did it mean he already knew something? Or was he genuinely saying it for her sake?

But if it was purely for her sake, then their relationship had not quite reached that point.

Before she could think it through further, Zhou Jieyu set down his teacup and tilted his head toward her, smiling.

"First time talking about someone behind their back. I must confess it feels a little strange."

Lu Huaixi curved her lips in return, utterly composed. "First time hearing Brother Zhou speak like this. It startled me a little too."

"You'd be used to it if it were Xianya?"

Zhou Jieyu laughed softly.

"The two of you get along like true sisters. Since you count as family, I might as well include myself as the elder brother along with that. And rather than wait for Xianya to piece things together from scraps she catches here and there, it's better for me to say what I know early."

Those few words set Lu Huaixi at ease considerably, and the uncertainty she'd felt a moment ago dissolved without a trace.

She tilted her head as well and looked at him honestly, her eyes curving with a warm smile. "Then I must thank you, Brother Zhou."

"Don't mention it. Just—" He paused, then added one final line. "Just be well."

Then, after a beat: "Little sister of the Lu family."

Lu Huaixi was about to say something more, when the handmaid sent by Jingshuang appeared and leaned close to speak softly in her ear.

She let the thought pass, lowered her gaze, and listened to what the girl had to say.

"Wait wherever is convenient — inside the residence or outside, either will do."

After the handmaid withdrew, Zhou Jieyu's eyes lingered on Lu Huaixi's face a moment longer, as though he had been about to ask her something — but in the end, he said nothing.

chapters.title: Overheard
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing had been occupied with a great deal of official business these past few days. By the time he finished, evening had already fallen. Even so, it was the earliest he had returned to the residence in all of those days.

He asked after Lu Huaixi, and was told she had also come back. With that, he put his mind at ease and went straight to the study.

Since the night Lu Huaixi had fallen ill and he had stayed by her side until morning — having heard certain words she murmured in her sleep — he had not slept soundly in days.

He had not been avoiding her deliberately. But once he was certain she had recovered, he felt he needed to take stock of himself, and work out what to do about the emotions that had appeared where they had no business appearing, and that he could not seem to control.

He was in the middle of that thought when someone knocked at the study door, which he had just shut.

A few raps, then silence. Then came Shen Zhoushu's voice.

Xie Yuanjing pressed his fingers to his brow and told him to come in.

The outer attendants withdrew after he entered, and the room fell quiet again.

Shen Zhoushu handed him what he had asked for, then found himself a seat, making himself at home as though it were his own study.

"Your father hasn't gone to see that mother and son these past few days, it's true. But the woman's son has recently entered Senior Official Xun's circle. To be favoured to that degree — it's likely your father who put in the recommendation."

"Let him."

Xie Yuanjing leafed through the ledger, not raising his eyes.

Shen Zhoushu looked at him and leaned back with a slow shake of his head.

"That person can't stir up too much trouble on his own, but he's sly enough. Don't underestimate him. And the Marquis's position is what it is — even with the Emperor that furious, he still chose not to strip your father of his title. That tells you it's a position worth contesting."

"Then let him come and contest it. If he can take something from the household I have built and maintained, that is my own failing. I would gladly yield the title to him."

"You really are... forget it."

Shen Zhoushu gave up that line of argument, dealt with a few practical matters, then looked up and saw that the other man's spirits were low. Remembering something he had heard, his expression shifted abruptly, and he leaned in with curiosity.

"I heard from Gong Fei that you haven't been sleeping well lately. I hadn't paid attention, but now that I look at you..." He clicked his tongue. "Even that perfunctory smile you use for dealing with people has vanished entirely."

"I've had rather more on my hands of late."

"Don't try to fool me. Did your affairs keep you away from the residence for several days? If I recall correctly, the Lu second daughter took ill the day we disembarked — and you'd just admitted to having your eye on her. Did you turn around and leave her on her own in the residence?"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. Not until he had finished reading through the ledger did he look up slightly.

"She has fully recovered. And I return to the residence every night — you're sitting in my study at this very moment."

It was true that Lu Huaixi had not seen him in days. But he had, in fact, been sleeping under the same roof as her every night.

Each evening before bed, he would sit beside her for a while.

"Then how is it that people are saying the First Young Mistress at home has fallen out of favour—"

"I'll let Gong Fei know that the reason he receives punishment today is you."

Xie Yuanjing cut him off. He didn't know whether it was because someone had mentioned the poor sleep, but he suddenly felt genuinely tired.

Yet he knew that even if he lay down this instant, he would not be able to sleep.

"Anything else?"

"Why are you punishing Gong Fei? It wasn't him who said it."

Shen Zhoushu decided not to push his luck any further, for fear of actually dragging Gong Fei into it. But he had no intention of letting the person in front of him off so easily either.

It was Xie Yuanjing himself who had once sworn with great conviction that no beautiful face could ever move his heart. He could at least have the decency to eat his own words.

With that thought in mind, Shen Zhoushu listened for a moment more, then drew out his words deliberately.

"Fine. I'll say no more."

He stretched lazily. "I know the Lu second daughter is not the wife Xie the First Young Master married for sentiment. I know what you want is two people living in mutual courtesy, neither drawing close to the other. The way things are right now suits you perfectly. I won't try to persuade you."

Shen Zhoushu paused, then said, "I just don't know whether the Lu second daughter might find it hard."

Lu Huaixi had not visited Xie Yuanjing's study in several days.

After recovering from her illness and finding no sign of him, she had stopped coming to practise her calligraphy there.

That she was here at this hour was partly because she had run into Xie's First Madam on her way back, who had asked her to bring a bowl of soup — and partly because of a few things Zhou Jieyu had happened to mention.

Whatever became of their relationship in the future, she felt Xie Yuanjing should know.

But now she stood outside the study, listening as Shen Zhoushu's voice carried clearly through the door, saying aloud things that both of them already knew in their hearts — and Lu Huaixi found she no longer had the will to push open that door.

Hard? Not exactly.

But having it laid out so plainly was, after all, uncomfortable to hear.

It was as though everyone had already decided that Xie Yuanjing would always be the one holding the reins — while she was the one who might lose herself, lose her composure.

She turned around. Someone had come up behind her at some point. Even though she had done her best to conceal her expression, the unease of having overheard something still lingered at the corners of her eyes.

"Young Mistress, this servant has brought the person inside."

It was Jingshuang, back with the group she had taken to find Xie Yuanjing.

It was also because Lu Huaixi had given permission earlier that Jingshuang had waited as long as she had before finally bringing the person into the residence — only to arrive at this particular moment.

Lu Huaixi showed no discomfort at having been overheard. She even gave Jingshuang a small nod.

"Since you're here, one of you can deliver this soup."

"Yes, Young Mistress."

That voice was very calm. So calm that Liniang, standing behind in timid silence, could not help looking up.

Seeing this Young Mistress in a different setting, she felt her heart thump all the harder.

Especially knowing that this Young Mistress had heard what was said inside and still showed no sign of distress — her very manner of leaving was composed and unruffled. Liniang was struck by a rush of feeling, half admiration and half envy, though she could not have said quite what she was envying.

The sounds outside had filtered through to the study regardless.

Xie Yuanjing instinctively frowned, but what Shen Zhoushu had just said kept him from turning his attention elsewhere.

Those were words he had agreed to once. But hearing them now, for some reason, they sat uneasily with him.

"Is there anything you'd like to say in response, Xie the First Young Master?"

Shen Zhoushu didn't bother holding back and was about to press further, when Gong Fei's lowered voice came from outside.

"My lord, Jingshuang has come."

Since Jingshuang always accompanied Lu Huaixi, hearing she had come, Xie Yuanjing did not spare Shen Zhoushu another thought.

"Enter."

He said it with a furrowed brow. "Something happened on that end?"

The door swung open quickly. A flicker of hesitation passed over Gong Fei's face. "In reply to my lord, the Young Mistress... is well. But there is someone who wishes to see you. They say they are... an old acquaintance of yours."

Before Xie Yuanjing could grow displeased, Gong Fei stepped to the side and glanced out, then entered the study, head lowered as he spoke.

"Zheng Xiaoqi brought someone to Shun'an Fang and asked the Young Mistress to arrange a place for them. When the Young Mistress heard it was an old acquaintance of yours, she had Jingshuang bring the person directly to you. She said these matters are not hers to manage, and that everything... should be arranged by you."

"An old acquaintance? A young woman?"

Shen Zhoushu spoke before Xie Yuanjing could, the question coming almost before Gong Fei had finished. "You have someone you were fond of, Xie the First Young Master?"

"Enough."

Xie Yuanjing did not even look back. "Who is it?"

"In reply to my lord — she is a singing girl by the name of Liniang. She says you once helped her and arranged lodgings for her, in Rongcheng."

Shen Zhoushu's surprise deepened, but it was no longer his turn to speak. He could feel it — a quietly dangerous pressure settling over Xie Yuanjing's bearing, pressing low.

The study fell silent in an instant.

As Gong Fei made his report, Jingshuang led the others closer and waited just outside the doorway.

At her side stood a young woman, positioned exactly where Xie Yuanjing's gaze would land the moment he looked up.

The young woman had been watching him with longing eyes. But the moment his gaze reached her, excitement and panic flashed across her face at once.

Then she shifted her foot forward slightly, as though wanting to step closer and speak to him. But something seemed to give her pause — and that foot, in the end, stayed where it was. Her hands at her sides clenched tightly around her sleeves.

chapters.title: The Young Mistress Had Just Come
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing had no interest in doing good deeds. He looked once, then withdrew his gaze.

"Give her a sum of money."

His expression was blank. "She can continue following Zheng Xiaoqi, or she can take the money and leave. That is up to her. But there will be no next time — her good fortune will only carry her this far."

Gong Fei received the order. But in the very next moment, a voice came through, trembling slightly, as though its owner had summoned every last ounce of courage.

"First Young Master Xie."

Liniang stepped forward, but was quickly stopped.

She did not dare force her way through. She stood there and spoke her plea. "Liniang does not want the money. Being able to see the First Young Master again is Liniang's fortune. Liniang is bold enough to ask — please, let Liniang stay."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing, but something cold and dangerous had crept into the set of his brows.

"Liniang does not dare hope for anything more. She only wishes to remain at the First Young Master's side and serve him. Liniang can do whatever any maidservant does. Liniang will never be disrespectful to the First Young Mistress."

The air in the study had turned low and suffocating.

Shen Zhoushu had only been stirring up amusement, but at these words, he fell into a rare moment of genuine bewilderment and stared at the person before him.

"What is this — she followed you all the way here? So she really is your old acquaintance? Then that Lu second daughter over at Shun'an Fang must have had quite a lot said to her, things that should and shouldn't have been said alike."

At the mention of the Young Mistress, Gong Fei's expression grew increasingly strained. So did Jingshuang's, from outside.

Liniang's words did not stop for long. Soon that trembling voice returned, carrying within it a stubborn, throw-caution-to-the-wind resolve.

"Liniang does not dare conceal anything from the First Young Master. Just now Liniang inadvertently overheard your conversation with this gentleman. But please be at ease, First Young Master — even though you did not marry your wife out of love, Liniang knows that the First Young Mistress is a good person. Liniang also knows she does not have the Young Mistress's standing and cannot offer the First Young Master any support... but Liniang can do anything for the First Young Master. Just now the First Young Mistress also said that however you choose to handle Liniang, she will not interfere. So please — please be merciful one more time..."

What Shen Zhoushu had said was a deliberate jab, meant to watch Xie Yuanjing get caught out. He had not expected those words to fall into someone else's ears — and be repeated aloud.

His heart sank. He immediately looked up, wishing he could reach through the doorway and throttle the woman outside for her careless mouth.

But before he could say anything, the silent Xie Yuanjing suddenly spoke.

"Not married out of love — your words?"

Xie Yuanjing's voice was cold, carrying a clear warning.

The person outside seemed to freeze for a moment and fell silent.

"If I hear another half-word spoken to my wife's disadvantage, your life ends in the capital — a fitting end for someone whose adopted parents never got to see this city."

The chill laced through those words was unmistakable to anyone who heard them.

Whatever courage Liniang had gathered seemed to shatter in that instant, impossible to collect again.

Her legs went weak, and she nearly failed to keep her footing.

"First Young Master, please calm your anger — Liniang had no intention of harming the First Young Mistress. Liniang only..."

"What you only did is not my concern. That is your affair. If you come seeking me again with the words 'old acquaintance,' you will bear the consequences yourself."

Xie Yuanjing had no patience to hear more and cut her off, his expression edging toward irritation.

He should not have chosen this moment of all moments to try and sort through his thoughts. He had heard what he'd heard of Lu Huaixi's words in her sleep — what was done was done. What cause did he have to be vexed with her?

She had sent Jingshuang to bring the person to him — the meaning was clear enough. She was washing her hands of it and staying out.

Xie Yuanjing rose. He noticed that gaze still fixed on him, and did not turn his head even slightly.

"My wife is kind-hearted, and so today, I will not take your life."

Paying no mind to the stunned silence behind him, Xie Yuanjing continued coldly:

"But since you are so full of ideas, there is no need to take the money either. From here on, whether you live or die is your own affair. If you cannot manage it, go down and make your peace with your adopted parents yourself."

Liniang finally understood that she had drawn this man's displeasure.

She was frantic and at a loss. She could not comprehend why, having already lowered herself so completely, she had still provoked his anger.

"First Young Master — please don't send me away! You made a promise to my father that you would protect my life. I don't dare hope for anything else. I only want to stay and serve... I can do many things. I can bring you soup, lighten the Young Mistress's burdens. I—"

As her words fell, Xie Yuanjing finally noticed that the maidservant beside Jingshuang was carrying something in her hands.

His brow furrowed. As though recalling something, he paid no attention to the tearful regret coming from behind him, and his expression darkened another shade.

"Who sent the soup?"

Gong Fei sighed inwardly. He remembered the Young Mistress saying not to mention her name, and hesitated, uncertain whether to speak now.

Jingshuang was faster. Almost the instant Gong Fei lowered his head, she replied.

"In answer to the First Young Master — the Young Mistress came just now."

She spoke without pause, her voice carrying a suppressed edge of feeling. "It was the Young Mistress who brought the soup for you. But it seems the timing was not quite right — she heard you and Master Shen speaking inside, and so she did not stay to wait."

The implication was plain: their Young Mistress had overheard what had been said.

It was the first time Jingshuang had spoken to this man in such a manner, her words carrying a trace of emotion.

But if it came to it again, she knew she would do the same.

Xie Yuanjing's brow pulled together at this. He had not expected Lu Huaixi to have come. His chest tightened, and his expression went cold in an instant.

"Why was I not informed?"

"In reply to my lord — the Young Mistress did not allow it."

Gong Fei replied with his head lowered.

Xie Yuanjing swept him a glance, asked nothing further, and walked out.

As he stepped out of the study, a small, tearful voice sounded beside him, calling his name once more. Xie Yuanjing seemed to think of something and stopped.

Liniang thought he had changed his mind. She could not help looking up at him — but his profile was cold and unyielding, and he did not turn his head by even a fraction.

"When did Zheng Xiaoqi go to Shun'an Fang?"

"Two or three hours ago."

"How many times has he gone?"

Gong Fei was uncertain. Jingshuang answered for him. "In answer to the First Young Master — twice. The first time he also asked to see the Young Mistress, but that day she had not gone to Shun'an Fang."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was cold when he spoke, his tone even, betraying nothing of his feelings.

But Gong Fei knew — this was anger.

Surely enough, within moments, the order came.

"Have him bound."

His voice was low and steady. "Two years ago he used that broken leg of his to stir up trouble. Today, I will give him what he is looking for. He wants something severed — let him have it."

Gong Fei's expression stilled for a moment, but he quickly lowered his head and accepted the order.

Xie Yuanjing spoke without any effort to lower his voice, as though he had no care for who might hear.

Liniang's face drained of colour. Her body trembled, her expression a mixture of shock and terror.

The Xie Yuanjing she knew had been a good man — one who would step in to help ordinary people. She could not understand how a man like that could have become so cold-blooded, speaking of crippling someone's leg as easily as breathing.

Her lips moved. The fear that crashed over her was sharp and overwhelming, burying every other feeling she had come with.

"First Young Master Xie..."

"You may go and tell Zheng Xiaoqi now, if you wish."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her once, then turned away. "Tell him — he will be losing a leg at my hands."

chapters.title: Why Didn't You Come and Ask Me
chapters.content:
Liniang nearly crumpled to the ground. She wanted to ask one more thing, but the person before her gave her no further opportunity.

Shen Zhoushu finally came back to his senses amid the commotion. Seeing Xie Yuanjing about to leave, he rushed after him at once. "Where are you going?"

He dropped his voice. "Don't make this too big. Actually crippling his leg will bring a great deal of trouble."

Xie Yuanjing glanced back at him and said nothing.

Shen Zhoushu's feet instinctively stopped. He reached up and rubbed his nose, and did not dare follow.

If he hadn't run his mouth earlier, this whole thing would not have become so complicated. Now that Xie Yuanjing's attention was elsewhere, there was no telling what would happen once he came back to his senses — whether he might simply tear him apart on the spot.

"Master Shen, you really are..." Gong Fei stepped forward, unable to hold it in. "Please don't talk about our Young Mistress again next time."

Shen Zhoushu had no nerve left to be glib. He waved a hand. "I won't, I won't. Tomorrow I'll go and apologise to your Young Mistress in person."

As the words left his mouth, he remembered what had just happened. His eyes swept briefly over Liniang, who was being led away, then returned to Gong Fei.

"As for Zheng Xiaoqi — three months bedridden is enough. If his leg is actually ruined, this will certainly be traced back to your First Young Master."

Shen Zhoushu spoke with uncharacteristic seriousness. "He's acting out of anger right now and is bound to overstep. Go ahead and have the man bound as ordered — let him vent, let him act. But use some other pretext. Don't leave any evidence to be used against you. If you're worried he won't have gotten it out of his system, let your Young Mistress go and talk him down. And—"

He looked toward the figure ahead, moving slowly, as though she had lost her bearings. His brow furrowed. "She overheard things. That means she can't be left unwatched. Keep someone on her for the time being."

"Understood," Gong Fei replied with a nod.

He had no intention of letting Liniang go and warn anyone regardless. Even setting aside that matter, he would have had her watched — to prevent her from being used again by someone else to stir up more trouble.

—

By the time Lu Huaixi returned to her courtyard, Yaoxu was inside adding fresh ice to the room.

The moment she stepped in, the coolness swept over her and quenched the heat she had carried back with her the entire way.

Perhaps not expecting her to return so soon, Yaoxu started slightly before coming to greet her. "Young Mistress, why are you back so quickly? This servant was still arranging the ice, thinking you'd be a while yet."

Lu Huaixi accepted the warm water she offered and took several slow sips.

Of course she was quick. She hadn't even stepped through the door.

"You rest first. Once you've finished the tea I'll go have the meal brought."

"Don't bother. I don't feel like eating tonight."

With her thirst quenched, Lu Huaixi felt somewhat more herself.

The stifled unease she had felt outside Xie Yuanjing's study began to dissolve, and it was as though she had come alive again.

As for that vague and nameless feeling — pressing it back down was not the first time.

Either way, life went on wherever one was. She counted on her fingers — not much of the year remained.

"That won't do."

Yaoxu frowned. "If it's the heat bothering you, rest a little longer."

"Resting more won't make me hungry."

Lu Huaixi set down the cup. The coolness in the room made her feel pleasantly lazy.

She rose and walked to the soft daybed inside, settling herself against the end nearest the ice.

"I'll tell you if I get hungry."

"You're putting me off again, Young Mistress. You said the same thing at lunch, and then hardly touched anything. You ought to eat something tonight."

Yaoxu pressed on. "There are a few things you like today. At least take a look. If you truly can't manage it, have a bowl of soup — the kitchen has had it simmering for a long time and put plenty of good things in it."

Lu Huaixi was about to refuse again when a sound came from outside.

Perhaps because she had not heard it in several days, there was something faintly unfamiliar about it — something that made her mind slip, just for a moment.

"Go have the meal brought. Now."

Xie Yuanjing stepped into the room. His gaze paused on Lu Huaixi's face for an instant. "And add a bowl of cherry cream."

"Yes, First Young Master."

Yaoxu bowed her head in acknowledgment. "Will the First Young Master be staying for dinner?"

"Yes."

Seeing that though the Young Mistress had furrowed her brow, she had not refused the First Young Master's words, Yaoxu let out a small breath of relief and hurried out of the room.

She was afraid that if she lingered even a moment, one of the two inside might change their mind about eating.

Soon the room held only the two of them.
