Xie Yuanjing said nothing. Lu Huaixi simply pulled the corners of her lips into a perfunctory smile in his direction, then settled back into the daybed and reached for the ledger she had left unfinished.

She had no intention of asking where he had been these past days, nor any desire to enquire about how he had handled Liniang.

But counting the time, he should have already seen her.

Just perhaps had not yet had the chance to catch up on old times.

Lu Huaixi drew her gaze away. She did not give any thought to whether the silence might feel stifling, and simply turned back to the ledger she had not yet finished.

"Why did you not eat properly at lunch?"

The quiet was finally broken by Xie Yuanjing. He moved closer, and as his shadow fell over her, his scent — belonging only to him — wrapped itself around her.

Lu Huaixi's thoughts drifted for a moment. She remembered the day on the pleasure boat, when he had held her, and how her clothes had taken on that same familiar smell afterward.

But scent was a thing impossible to hold.

In the days Xie Yuanjing had been absent, a single passing breeze was enough to sweep away every last trace.

"I wasn't hungry."

Lu Huaixi kept one fingertip pressed to the open page, eyes not lifting, and turned to the next page when she reached the bottom.

"Hungry or not, it doesn't matter."

Xie Yuanjing continued, "Next time you skip a meal, I'll have the kitchen staff replaced — one by one, until you eat."

The hand turning the page stilled for a moment. Lu Huaixi felt herself go quietly blank at the care folded into his words.

Xie Yuanjing was a composed and measured man. His likes and dislikes were never written on his face.

His consideration for her — it was rooted in the connection to the Lu family. That much she knew.

She had never thought this arrangement was poorly suited. But the thought that this man could, on occasion, sincerely look out for someone without any thought to gain — it reminded her how little she had ever truly seen through him. Not even a little.

She had let go of other thoughts by now. Yet when she recalled it, something small and unruly still tightened in her chest, and she almost had to laugh at herself for it.

Lu Huaixi set down what she was holding. Unable to make sense of her own wandering mind, she simply let herself look at him openly.

"Don't go frightening people."

She looked at him, and feeling that holding eye contact in silence was a little strange, she added another line. "Why did you come to eat here tonight?"

"Where else would I go?"

"I don't know."

Lu Huaixi thought about it, then shook her head. "You have many places you could go. I simply didn't expect you to come here for dinner tonight."

Xie Yuanjing did not reply. He only looked at her eyes.

When he had learned that she had come to the study, his chest had dropped. A rare tightness had seized him — worry that she had heard those careless words, worry that she had seen someone who had nothing to do with her.

And now, looking at her, Xie Yuanjing realised that what unsettled him even more than the worry was her indifference.

"Do you think I ought to be having dinner with that person instead?"

Xie Yuanjing's lips moved. His voice came down quieter, and he put the thing plainly. "Why didn't you come and ask me?"

"Ask what?"

"When you saw that person was here — why didn't you simply ask me directly? When you heard Shen Zhoushu's remarks — why didn't you push open that door?"

Lu Huaixi found herself a little confused by what he was saying.

She blinked, looking up at him, her eyes filled with genuine, helpless bewilderment.

"Don't do that again."

Xie Yuanjing moved two steps closer, until he was almost upon her.

When he looked down and saw those clear, luminous eyes, he felt as though he had stepped into the brightest hour of a summer's day — warmth flooding through him all at once.

"We are on the same side. Whenever someone I don't know comes looking for me, you should ask me directly. When you hear something troubling, you should tell me. You should come to me with fire in your eyes and tell me — that I cannot treat you poorly."

Xie Yuanjing pressed down the surge rising within him and coaxed her.

In truth, there was much he wanted to say — explanations, reassurances.

But the moment he truly saw her, all of that was pushed to the very end.

He was like a fox with a mind sharp as seven apertures, calculating — how best to make this young woman take his words to heart and remember them.

And so he tempted her, following the current of her own feelings, drawing out the posture in which she would most naturally trust him.

"We ought to be the ones who trust each other most. Lu Huaixi — how could you ask nothing at all and simply send that person to me like that?"

"I—"

In the instant guilt surfaced in her eyes, Xie Yuanjing leaned in.

Close enough that his reflection appeared in her suddenly widening eyes. Close enough that the tips of their noses nearly touched.

"Let me explain."

chapters.title: What Happened That Year
chapters.content:
After Xie Yuanjing's words fell, the sound of a heartbeat grew very loud.

Lu Huaixi did not know why she had so little control over herself. She swallowed, and instinctively leaned back.

But behind her was solid wood — cool against her back — pressing into her and blocking her retreat.

With nowhere left to go, Xie Yuanjing straightened.

"I do know that young woman."

His voice was calm and unhurried, and it pulled Lu Huaixi's scattered thoughts back into place.

She collected herself along with his words. She watched him refill her cup with water, then, as though it were a perfectly natural thing to do, reach out and ruffle her ear lightly before sitting down beside her.

For a moment she could only hold onto the word "know" from his sentence, and forgot entirely to stop him from touching her.

"Her adopted father was a hunter. Several years ago, when I led troops to suppress a bandit group, I stayed at his home during a reconnaissance."

Xie Yuanjing began, his voice carrying little variation in tone.

"At the time, the bandit leader had colluded with rebel forces, and used someone I trusted to set up an ambush. My trusted men and I were trapped in the mountains. Our provisions were destroyed, and it was the dead of winter with heavy snow. We could not have held out more than three days. The nearby villages had long since been abandoned. It was her adopted father who risked his life to guide the relief forces in."

He kept it simple, as though unwilling to dwell on how dangerous it had truly been, and gave only the broad outline.

Lu Huaixi's hand closed slightly at her side. She pressed her lips together and listened as he continued.

"But the hunter and his wife were stubborn. Poor as they were, they refused to accept any reward for what they had done, and would not take my assistance either. I arranged for someone to quietly look after them. Later, he met with an accident suddenly, and his dying wishes came down to two things."

Xie Yuanjing paused after this. Whether it was a quiet sigh or something harder to name, his tone did not reveal it.

Lu Huaixi looked at him, and followed the thread of his words. "One of them was to ask you to look after Liniang. And you agreed, arranged things for her, but eventually parted ways?"

As though finally receiving what he had been waiting for — her question — Xie Yuanjing was in no hurry to answer. He only looked up and met her gaze.

He searched her expression, trying to find in her puzzled look the thing he wanted to see.

After a long moment, he reached out and lightly flicked her on the forehead.

"Parted ways is not how that phrase is used. If you don't want to practise calligraphy, fine — but do you not read books either?"

Lu Huaixi raised her hand and touched the spot where he had flicked her, then pursed her lips slightly.

It did not hurt. But it felt strange. Even now that she knew Liniang truly was Xie Yuanjing's old acquaintance — and that there existed between them a debt of trust and the weight of someone's dying wish — she was no longer as unsettled as she had been when she first heard about it earlier in the day.

"Then what should I say?"

"It was nothing more than honouring a request and offering a hand. She was fortunate, in a way — she had adoptive parents who gave her everything they had."

"And what happened after that?"

Lu Huaixi furrowed her brow slightly.

Xie Yuanjing was no saint, but he never went back on a promise he had made.

If he had agreed to offer a hand, he would not have withdrawn halfway.

"How did she come to say she could never see you?"

"What would she need to see me for? I had people move her somewhere safe and gave her silver and a house to live in. She did not treasure the life she had been protected into. Naturally I was not going to keep meddling."

Xie Yuanjing seemed to think of something. His gaze drifted to the candlelight flickering in the corner, and something cold entered his expression.

"Her adoptive father was hurt because of his efforts to protect her. Her adoptive mother knelt and begged her not to sing anymore, for her own safety. But she would not listen. She believed herself to be the lone clear-headed soul in a world of fools, convinced that justice would eventually come to her because she deserved it."

Xie Yuanjing picked up his teacup.

"If she had only been willing to hold out a few days and wait for her adopted father to send word, those men would not have been driven to such extremes. That year, her adoptive parents had also planned to make a trip to the capital — to see a city they had never seen."

Lu Huaixi opened her mouth, but found no words.

She was somewhat taken aback. She turned the image of the young woman she had seen today over in her mind, and felt it did not quite match the person Xie Yuanjing was describing.

Perhaps it could, in some small measure. But only just.

After a long silence, she let out a soft breath.

"I wouldn't have guessed it from looking at her."

She had been listening so intently that she had propped her chin in one hand without realising it, turning the past over in her mind again. When she had finally made sense of it, she sat up straight again.

"But she stopped singing in the end, didn't she? Could it be she came around, and that is why she came to me saying she wanted a place that sells art without selling the person?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at her once, and said nothing.

Lu Huaixi did not quite follow, and after a moment it came to her. "Is it because of you?"

Her eyes went wide. "Because you stopped having people look out for her, she finally understood — that you disapproved of her singing?"

"I never managed anything of the sort. Whether she sings or not has nothing to do with me. I said already — I only helped save her life and offered a hand."

"Alright, alright — you never managed anything."

Lu Huaixi waved a hand at him, then shifted slightly closer to where he sat. "Then it was simply her own affair."

"Yes. I have had no dealings with her. When I stayed a while longer in Rongcheng at the time, it was partly because of the hunter's matter, and partly because I was investigating a case. When I returned to Rongcheng later and she stopped me, I did not linger."

"Then why does Zheng Xiaoqi know her?"

"He was there during the bandit suppression as well."

"He..."

Lu Huaixi instinctively recalled the hint of betrayal she had heard earlier in Xie Yuanjing's words.

Her thoughts moved quickly, turned it over, and she spoke again. "I could see today that he meant no good."

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing replied. "You saw that he meant no good, and yet between him and me, you chose to believe what he told you. Should I compliment you on that?"

"...When did any of this have anything to do with believing or not believing? I never thought you had done anything to be ashamed of. Didn't I send someone to find you directly?"

Her voice carried a trace of hesitation — as though she were genuinely beginning to reflect.

Xie Yuanjing let the pause stretch deliberately, until it had settled deeply in her, before finally speaking. "I told you once that I had never liked anyone before. Did you truly believe me?"

The words came naturally, and Lu Huaixi — already being led along by him, one sentence at a time, into a growing sense of not being trusted — did not notice the word "before" in that sentence.

"I did."

She nodded, a little slowly, with a vague sense that something was off.

Xie Yuanjing calculated his timing with precision. In her moment of uncertainty, he reached out and took her hand, and produced, from somewhere she had not noticed, a bracelet of gleaming, translucent jade — which he slid onto her wrist.

And that was not enough. He kept hold of her hand, his thumb resting against her fingertips, pretending he was simply still talking and had forgotten to let go.

"If you truly believe it, then you ought to act as someone who truly believes it. You are my wife now. Going forward, it is you who should be making decisions on my behalf — no one else has the right. Whoever comes, it will not do."

He paused, then looked at her. "Do you understand?"

The room had grown cooler with the fresh ice that had been added.

The heat Lu Huaixi had picked up outside had long since faded.

But now, where Xie Yuanjing held her wrist, warmth seeped in, thread by thread — like something lightly grazing her skin, leaving a tingling, faintly dizzying sensation.

She lowered her gaze and looked down, uncertain whether she was looking at his hand or at the jade bracelet he had placed on her.

"This bracelet is beautiful."

She said quietly, "Is it for me?"

chapters.title: The Balance Between Them Is Broken
chapters.content:
When she thought about it carefully, Xie Yuanjing had given her many things. The betrothal gifts alone had filled her entire courtyard.

And she had always accepted them without any awkwardness.

But this time felt somehow different from before.

Lu Huaixi could not say why. She only sat with her eyes cast downward.

She had little confidence in her own changes. Thoughts grown too complicated had a way of leading one astray in both judgment and action.

"Yes. Chosen and given to you."

Xie Yuanjing did not stay silent for long. He replied softly.

"Do you like it?"

The jade was flawless and clear, with the faintest shimmer beneath the surface. Even someone who knew nothing of such things could see at a glance that it was a rare piece.

"I like it, but—"

"If you like it, then wear it."

Xie Yuanjing cut off whatever came after that "but."

He did not want to hear what came after that word. He wanted this bracelet to stay on Lu Huaixi's wrist — carrying his hidden intentions, drawing her, little by little, toward himself.

But he could also see her hesitation.

Xie Yuanjing gave nothing away. After having just spoken about trust, he asked her in a perfectly even tone.

"Or was the 'I like it' you said just now simply to appease me, and you don't actually feel that way at all?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi shook her head quickly, withdrawing the gaze she had let fall on her own wrist, and looked up.

There was genuine hesitation in her — but not because she didn't like it. It was because she did not want to accept it.

The reason, aside from this strange mood that had settled over her, was what she had overheard outside Xie Yuanjing's study.

The two of them were meant to appear as a harmonious couple in public. In private, there was no need for them to be too close.

They both knew this. It was understood between them without being said.

And so his closeness now, and the thing on her wrist — neither was truly necessary.

"I only meant to say — you don't need to give me things like this."

Lu Huaixi did not pause for long.

She looked at him, took a slow breath, and said, "I took in what you said just now, and the bracelet is beautiful, and I was not trying to appease you. But you don't have to be this way with me."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing, and waited for her to continue.

With that opening made, the rest came more easily.

"I have promised you that I will behave as expected in front of others. So in private, do as you please. You don't need to... take so much care of me."

The words "we can live with courtesy and keep our distance, neither drawing close to the other" never made it out of her mouth.

To bring it up would be too awkward. Regardless of any explanation, it suited neither of them well in this moment.

"Even if you gave me nothing, I would still be a good First Young Mistress."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze did not leave her face.

When Lu Huaixi said all this, her expression was earnest, her eyes very bright.

She seemed to have no displeasure at all — not even any lingering unhappiness over what had happened at the study.

And yet Xie Yuanjing perceived it: beneath that bright and guileless surface was a quietness and a clarity. She had never considered what might happen between the two of them. Not in the slightest.

"Why aren't you saying anything?"

Lu Huaixi asked again. The dark of her pupils held the wavering of candlelight.

For some reason, Xie Yuanjing suddenly thought of that day at the pavilion by the water, when she had been feeding the fish — those same bright, gleaming eyes, certain she would catch that flash of gold twice.

She had, in the end.

And so he trusted her luck. He trusted her ability.

At this turn in the conversation, Xie Yuanjing should have accepted what she offered and agreed to maintain a careful distance between them in private — so as not to invite unnecessary complications.

But what he wanted now was no longer just the role of a First Young Mistress.

"Giving you things is what I want to do in private."

Xie Yuanjing finally spoke, and did not let her evade. "The reason I said nothing was because I was thinking — why did you not ask me about what you heard outside the study?"

Lu Huaixi went still.

She did not know how this could be brought up without becoming impossible to resolve.

Anyone with half a mind would know that what had been said in there had at some point carried Xie Yuanjing's own agreement. So there was no point in seeking an explanation, and no call to make a scene — it would only leave things suspended in an uncomfortable middle ground. Better to simply move past it.

"There's no need to ask, is there? It wasn't as if I overheard any great secret."

Lu Huaixi gave a light, easy smile.

Not wanting to sit here so close to him and discuss all of this, she rose. "I'll go and check on dinner."

"Hear me out."

Xie Yuanjing stopped her. The hem of his robe brushed against her skirt — an intimacy that was difficult to ignore.

"I will not deny it. The first time Shen Zhoushu brought it up, I did agree."

Hearing him admit it outright, something in Lu Huaixi's chest tightened — a faint, sour sensation.

Even now that she had drawn herself back from those feelings, she could not help but think: in the days when she had, without quite knowing it, begun to feel something — he had been establishing with a friend how little she meant to him.

It was, after all, a little deflating.

"Yes. I could tell. But it doesn't matter."

Lu Huaixi pressed down the feeling, turned slightly to the side, and put a little space between them.

She curved her lips into a smile. Her expression was somewhat subdued, yet carried a perfectly fitting warmth. "There's no need to explain specially. As I said before — in private, we can be however you like."

"Doesn't matter?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at her, his gaze deepening. "If it truly doesn't matter, then why did you not bring the soup in?"

Lu Huaixi went still again, and could not find an answer.

Xie Yuanjing did not wait for one, and continued. "You say you don't mind. I can ask nothing more of that. But the words 'we can be however you like' — can I take you at those?"

"...Yes."

"Then what about this?"

The moment the words landed, Lu Huaixi felt a tug at her waist.

She could not keep her footing. Her body, which she had just moved away, lurched straight back into Xie Yuanjing.

She was caught in a full embrace — but just as quickly, released.

"People can change sometimes."

Xie Yuanjing said to the stunned face before him: "I have changed. At the beginning, I did think that way. But not anymore."

Lu Huaixi stayed silent. Xie Yuanjing did not rush her — he waited for her to come back to herself.

After a long while, when the faint sounds of the serving maidservants could be heard from outside, Lu Huaixi finally looked over again.

"If you've changed, then... you've changed. Let's eat first. I think I'm a little hungry."

The deflection was too obvious. Xie Yuanjing did not reply, and did not move.

Lu Huaixi did not say anything else either.

She thought that perhaps she was reading too much into things.

But she had no wish to puzzle out the meaning behind Xie Yuanjing's words, and she did not believe that this man was someone who could change when it came to matters of the heart.

Right now, the balance between them was just right. If Xie Yuanjing felt an impulse to upset it, he had the ability to step back and forth at will. She did not. And so she could not allow it.

Compared to being adrift inside a Marquis's household she had not yet learned, living in fear of the day Xie Yuanjing might suddenly grow cold and withdraw — she wanted something solid. Something like the freedom waiting at the end of one year.

That was also why she had been able to clear her head so quickly that time.

She knew herself. And that was exactly why she had been so swift to root out and sever that small feeling before it had even fully surfaced.

Neither of them spoke. They were at a stalemate when, outside, Yaoxu came carrying a wooden box and stopped in the outer room without entering.

"First Young Master. Young Mistress."

She set it down, then spoke softly toward the inner room.

"Young Mistress, just now Master Zhou had someone send over a tea set, along with some tea from outside. He said if you enjoy it, he will have a batch sent over to Shun'an Fang."

At this, Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed. "Zhou Jieyu went to Shun'an Fang?"

"Yes, he came by for tea today."

Relieved that he had not returned to the subject from before, Lu Huaixi exhaled quietly.

Xie Yuanjing caught the shift, and asked further. "Do you want to keep the things?"

Lu Huaixi gave it no particular thought and nodded.

"Yes, keep them. He mentioned the tea to me — said it has a somewhat different taste and asked me to try it. The tea set is also something he came across some time ago, and he wants me to keep it at Shun'an Fang for my own use."

The openness on Lu Huaixi's face dissolved whatever slow and careful plan Xie Yuanjing had been forming.

He pressed down a nameless, smouldering irritation and met her eyes — forthright, with a barely-concealed nervousness beneath.

She was hiding behind this news, composing herself deliberately, not wanting to hear his explanation about what had been said in the study.

And so he did not know what to say, or whether there was anything left to say.

He only knew there was something he very much wanted to do right now. He did not hesitate over whether he should or shouldn't do it. He simply took Lu Huaixi's hand, drew her toward him, and leaned in.

Different from the closeness of before.

In this moment, Xie Yuanjing held nothing back — something possessive and undisguised was in his gaze as it met hers, then traced down past the tip of her nose, and settled on her lips, which had parted ever so slightly in surprise.

They would be very soft, he thought, with feeling he could not quite name.

But if he kissed her, she would likely be angry. She would pull away, retreat, and avoid him after — which would make this kiss rather poor value.

Xie Yuanjing should have stopped to weigh these things. He did not.

He simply angled his head slightly as he drew close, and pressed his lips to hers — those lips that had instinctively, at the last moment, closed.

chapters.title: I'll Wait for You to Think It Through
chapters.content:
The kiss was very light.

Their breaths tangled together — one anxious and uncertain, the other carrying a quiet insistence.

Lu Huaixi had forgotten to struggle. She stood there frozen in place, and then was folded into Xie Yuanjing's arms.

Very soft indeed.

In the instant his lips brushed the corner of hers, Xie Yuanjing exhaled something wordless, deep within himself.

He wanted more — wanted her to part her lips again the way they had just been, wanted to take things further. But he still had a few remnants of reason left.

The kiss did not linger. Before Lu Huaixi could fully process what was happening, he drew back slightly, and made no further move.

The room grew very quiet. Quiet enough that it was impossible to tell whose heartbeat it was, tangled somewhere amid the soft, erratic crackling of the candleflame.

The sweltering heat of summer rushed in, and the ice that had been carefully arranged suddenly lost all effect.

Lu Huaixi felt as though she might be dizzy from the warmth. Especially when she looked at Xie Yuanjing, still so close, his gaze still lowered to her lips — she did not dare move a single inch.

Xie Yuanjing did not speak either. He only stood in silence, letting the closeness settle around her.

The person before him was dazed and at a loss. The composure and steadiness from before had dissolved entirely. She looked like a startled fawn, caught in her own bewilderment, wondering whether to resist.

The thin thread of clarity Xie Yuanjing had managed to hold began to fray again. He stopped three inches from her, then drew close once more — and pressed a kiss to the tip of her nose.

Unlike the touch of lips on lips, this kiss landed on the tip of her nose with a tenderness carried to the very edge of itself.

That strangely gentle and unexpectedly familiar sensation was what finally brought Lu Huaixi back to herself.

She shoved him away abruptly. As she stepped back, her breathing came a little uneven, and the flush that had risen to her cheeks had spread all the way to the tips of her ears.

The one responsible showed not the slightest remorse. He watched her, his gaze deep and still — and when she made to flee, he caught her wrist again.

"Where do you think you're going?"

Xie Yuanjing's voice had gone slightly rough. Something in it sent a tremor through Lu Huaixi's chest.

Unease rose in her, quick and unbidden, and not entirely under her control.

She struggled several times without breaking free. Her teeth pressed into her lower lip. She raised her eyes and glared at him.

At the sight of her like this, Xie Yuanjing let out a quiet breath.

"You can ignore me. But you have to eat first."

He lowered his gaze, his voice carrying a low, subdued weight. "What I just did was out of line. But since we have spoken of trust — I don't want to conceal things from you."

He said quietly, "Shen Zhoushu was laughing at me earlier. It doesn't happen often, so when he saw something was off with me, he stopped watching his words."

Lu Huaixi parted her lips to speak, but recalled what had just happened and fell silent again, closing her mouth.

"If what is too heavy to hear, I won't say it. The reason I haven't come to see you these past days — it was not because I wanted to leave you cold."

Xie Yuanjing spoke carefully, his tone earnest. "What I did to you just now — I had not been waiting for this moment to do it. There were certain things I had not yet worked through in my mind, and I was afraid that if I stayed near you, I would not be able to hold them back."

Lu Huaixi's eyes went a little wider. Her indignation was written through with shock and disbelief.

Xie Yuanjing offered no further explanation. He only looked at her, and waited for her to scold him and vent her anger.

In truth, that impulse was only a very small part of the reason. The greater part was that he was still annoyed with her — annoyed over what she had said on the boat that day about all her exchanges with Zhou Jieyu.

Even when she had been drifting in and out of sleep and he had asked her about it, she had nodded along in that half-conscious state and said that if Zhou Jieyu had sent a portrait, she likely would have chosen him.

It was a good thing, in the end, that the portrait had never reached her.

Something dark stirred in the depths of Xie Yuanjing's gaze — but he pressed it back down quickly, and lowered his voice toward the person before him. "What I did today, I did. And I mean what I've said — I do have feelings for you that I had not expected before."

Before Lu Huaixi could shake off his hold again, Xie Yuanjing gave her wrist a light squeeze, then let go, yielding to her.

"I will not argue in my own defence. I'll wait for you to think it through."

When she passed the wooden box holding the tea set, Lu Huaixi did not remember to glance at it. She walked quickly, wanting nothing more than to put distance between herself and Xie Yuanjing.

The restless irritation that had been coiling in Xie Yuanjing quieted considerably at her complete disregard for that box.

His gaze dropped toward it. His lips did not move — only a brief, cool sound of dissatisfaction escaped him.

—

After nightfall, Xie Yuanjing of his own accord went to the study.

Before he left, he told Jingshuang to have half the ice taken away, and reminded her that there was no need to leave a lamp burning for him.

Lu Huaixi had been looking for somewhere to retreat. Hearing that he was leaving, she instinctively let out a breath.

She glanced toward the door just as Xie Yuanjing turned to look back. Those dark eyes read nothing — they held her gaze for one quiet, still moment, then he turned and walked out of the room.

Lu Huaixi's feelings were somewhat tangled.

She watched as Yaoxu had people clear away the ice, and then watched her shut the door, cutting off the last trace of Xie Yuanjing's silhouette — and in the end, she said nothing, and curled back up on the daybed.

He preferred the cool, but had cut the ice in half at night to accommodate her.

Sometimes she would wake in a half-dreaming state past midnight and see him wrapped in his outer robe, slipping out — or returning to the room after dipping his hands in cold water.

But he had never once expressed any displeasure. He would even turn back to remind her, on the occasions she was self-indulgent about the cold, that she was not to push her luck.

And she, toward him — had rarely thought to notice such things in return.

Lu Huaixi furrowed her brow without meaning to, and settled lazily against the side of the daybed.

Her thoughts were not quite under her control. One moment she was replaying everything that had left her so unsteady this evening. The next she was drifting back to when she and Xie Yuanjing had first been acquainted.

In the beginning, Xie Yuanjing had kept a very distinct distance.

Even when he smiled, his tone carried a polite reserve — not cold exactly, yet never at the same level as the person he was addressing.

He was born with a presence that set him above others. How much of it any given person felt depended entirely on how much he had chosen to soften it.

Later, after she entered the Marquis's household, Xie Yuanjing's manner toward her warmed by one degree.

He remembered what she said carefully, and kept his promise to look out for her — giving her considerably more freedom within the Marquis's household than she had expected.

Yet however comfortable it was, this was still the Marquis's household. It was still a place where she had to keep her wits about her.

The degree of trust she could place in Xie Yuanjing now — all of it rested on the fact that their arrangement only needed to last one year. Within that year, neither he nor she would change.

Her thoughts made a full circle and came to rest.

Lu Huaixi lowered her gaze to her own wrist.

The jade bracelet gleamed even more brightly in the light. She pressed her lips together, and could not help glancing toward the door once more.

He had not asked for a lamp to be left — that probably meant he would not be coming back to sleep tonight.

But where would he sleep then?

The study did not seem to have any proper bed or resting place. The side rooms in the courtyard had not been prepared in advance either.

If he was not staying — could it be he was leaving the residence entirely?

"Young Mistress, are you thinking about the First Young Master?"

Yaoxu came back in, her voice bright with barely-concealed delight, cutting through Lu Huaixi's thoughts. "This servant has noticed you glancing outside several times."

Lu Huaixi was so startled she nearly sat bolt upright.

She blinked, then looked at her with a somewhat serious expression. "I was not. Don't go guessing things."

"This servant would not dare guess. I only thought, since you and the First Young Master have just made up, you might be a little reluctant to part."

Yaoxu pressed her lips together, holding back a smile. She turned to refill the cup beside her, and did not see the look of bewilderment on Lu Huaixi's face just then.

"Made up from what?"

"From everything that happened today. This servant heard from Jingshuang — the First Young Master showed no mercy earlier, and when he heard that you had come by, he didn't even spare Master Shen a glance and came straight after you."

Lu Huaixi opened her mouth slightly, and forgot to speak.

Yaoxu did not stop. "This servant also heard something rather alarming."

She set down what she was holding, leaned in quietly, and said in a low voice, "When the First Young Master learned that the Zheng gentleman had gone to Shun'an Fang, he gave the order to have a leg broken."

Lu Huaixi was briefly surprised — but when it came to Xie Yuanjing going after Zheng Xiaoqi, the surprise did not linger into particular curiosity.

There must be old scores between them. Today's matter alone was surely not the full reason.

She drew her thoughts back and let her gaze sweep across the room.

After a moment, it occurred to her that she had forgotten something.

"Whatever Master Zhou sent over — where is it?"

"The First Young Master took it with him."

Yaoxu said. "He said the tea is not suitable for you to drink at night, and that he would be the one to judge whether it is good or not. Oh, and—"

Before Lu Huaixi could react, Yaoxu turned to her again. "Gong Fei just came to pass on a message. He said Master Shen would like to come tomorrow and apologise to you in person — if you are free, he will come early."

"Shen Zhoushu?"

Lu Huaixi paused, mildly dazed. "And if I'm not free?"

"He said if you are not free, he will wait in the courtyard. He will come regardless — otherwise he won't sleep soundly."

chapters.title: Helping Someone Court a Girl
chapters.content:
Shen Zhoushu went straight back to the Shen residence and did not leave his own courtyard for the rest of the evening.

The easy, flirtatious look that usually graced his brows had given way to something like worry. He did not even have the heart to fidget with the folding fan he habitually kept in his hands.

When his manservant came to help him change, he showed none of his usual fussiness over what he would wear the next day, and did not even glance at the colour of what the boy had brought.

After a long while, just as the manservant was about to venture a question, Shen Zhoushu sat down and spoke first.

"If someone wanted to help another person court a girl — where would you start?"

The manservant, who had been quietly worried that something dreadful had happened to his young master, exhaled in complete relief at those words.

"Young Master, please don't test this servant with such things. When it comes to charming young ladies, who in this whole household could match you?"

"When have I ever courted anyone? And it's not the same thing."

Shen Zhoushu picked up the fresh tea that had been brought and took a sip, then had the manservant stand behind the ice block and fan him for a while.

"Then what sort of thing is it, Young Master?"

The manservant was baffled, and after a pause finally figured it out.

"Young Master means the proper kind of liking? That's simple enough — arrange a few chance encounters out and about, so the young lady remembers who you are. After that, send things now and then that suit her tastes, subtly, without making it obvious. Better still if you can manage a rescue-the-maiden moment. Then wait for the right occasion and send someone to propose."

Shen Zhoushu found the words "proper kind" a little grating.

But he had no energy to dwell on that, and only furrowed his brow more deeply.

"None of what you said is of any use here."

Xie Yuanjing had already married the woman and brought her home quite some time ago. Aside from the rescue-the-maiden part, everything else listed had long since been done.

No — the rescue had happened too. Competing with the palace to bring her out — what was that if not a rescue?

"Then what would you like to hear, Young Master? Courting a girl is all these same things — make yourself visible, cater to her preferences to make her happy, settle problems on her behalf so she finds you dependable. If all else fails, make some grand gesture to stir her heart, and winning her over won't be far off."

After listening to the full rundown, Shen Zhoushu waved a hand, head aching slightly.

For an ordinary man and woman just getting acquainted, something like that might work. But what hadn't the Lu second daughter seen? What problem couldn't she handle on her own?

"They're already married. No need to win anyone over."

"Already married?"

The manservant looked surprised. "Young Master, if they're already married, why are you troubling yourself? A husband and wife will naturally find their own way of being together. Surely you're not worried a wedded woman might have a change of heart?"

"It's not that I want to be involved."

But hadn't he gone and made a mess of things?

Shen Zhoushu turned it over in his mind a few times. He thought of his friend, who had so rarely ever let his heart be moved — and how he, of all people, had chosen this of all moments to go and say that. The worry sat heavy in him.

He was afraid he had genuinely done damage. He was also afraid Xie Yuanjing might actually come back and tear him apart.

"If you ask this servant, Young Master, you needn't fret. No matter what things were like before the wedding, now that she's married, who could be closer to a woman than her own husband? If you truly feel you must help, find a way to make her feel a little jealous. Otherwise it's back to those same methods."

Shen Zhoushu tapped his fingertip lightly against the tabletop, turning the manservant's words over.

Making her jealous — that wouldn't be necessary.

Today's business had been more stirring than any jealousy.

As for the other methods—

Lu Huaixi was young and had none of their calculating ways. When she decided someone was good, she would give her whole heart to it sincerely.

"Has there been a lantern fair at Huique Slope recently?"

"Yes, Young Master, it has been going on for several days now. Tomorrow night is the last."

The manservant said this, thought for a moment, and added:

"But that place is already outside the city proper. If you're thinking of inviting someone there, you would want to prepare early. And while the area is no longer abandoned, it is still nothing like the city."

"Yes, that is precisely why — because it's nothing like the city."

Huique Slope had once been quite lively.

On one side, the scenery was lovely — peaceful and unhurried. On the other, a bustling stretch of shops and stalls drew many high-ranking officials and wealthy merchants to build residences there.

But in the previous dynasty, a series of cases had unfolded in that area, and several officials were arrested in succession. The place grew cold after that.

Whether official or merchant, everyone minded their luck in choosing where to plant their roots.

Over time, Huique Slope fell into neglect, and no one saw fit to attend to it.

It was only in recent years that some travelling merchants had settled there, bringing with them goods rarely seen in the capital, and the area had begun to liven up again on occasion.

"After tomorrow there will be no more lanterns?"

"In reply to Young Master — it is only a handful of stalls. This lantern fair was put together because some new goods are coming in soon — just a bit of advance excitement."

"If there aren't enough stalls, add some. We go the day after tomorrow."

"Ah?"

The manservant stared blankly. Then he heard the person in front of him continue, "Send some people over in advance and have them follow my instructions."

Shen Zhoushu finished speaking and watched his manservant stand there looking utterly dazed.

"What are you standing around for?"

"Yes, yes, this servant will go at once."

The manservant scrambled to attention, very nearly receiving a kick in the process. "Then, Young Master — which young lady are you inviting? Should this servant send word in advance?"

"Someone else's young lady."

But this message could not be sent by him, and the invitation could not come from him either.

"Go outside for a moment."

Shen Zhoushu gave a few more instructions, then leaned back in his chair.

With all of that arranged, the gloom from earlier had lifted entirely from his face. His brow arched upward, and he began to hum a tune with no small amount of satisfaction.

Just wait. Once this played out, Xie Yuanjing would have no choice but to come and thank him.

—

First thing the following morning, Lu Huaixi received a card from Shen Zhoushu's younger sister, inviting her to come watch the lanterns.

She stared at the card in a daze, the last traces of sleep not yet fully cleared.

"Why would Miss Shen invite you to Huique Slope? It isn't exactly a lively spot — outside the main streets it gets rather desolate. The most you'd find there are some travelling merchants, and if you're lucky, something unusual."

Yaoxu frowned as she looked at the card.

Lu Huaixi, however, showed no particular reaction.

She set the card down, then rose and reached for her washcloth.

Shen Zhoushu's younger sister, Shen Ruojin, was different from most young noblewomen. She had left the Shen household when she was very young, and lived quite apart from the family.

The last time they had spent any time together was on the boat a few days ago, and it had been pleasant. An impromptu trip to Huique Slope to watch lanterns — from Shen Ruojin, this did not seem strange at all.

In truth, she was a little curious herself. And so she was willing to go.

"Young Mistress, why not suggest somewhere else to Miss Shen instead? This servant always felt there was something a little unsettling about Huique Slope."

"I've never been to Huique Slope." Lu Huaixi blinked.

"Then there's no need to go."

Yaoxu lowered her voice. "This servant has heard that Huique Slope is... not entirely clean. That is why, all these years, it has never truly come back to life."

chapters.title: She Was Like a Bully Who Had Taken Someone Else's Spot
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi opened her eyes a little wider.

Not entirely clean — did that mean what she thought it meant?

"Isn't it alright though? There's even a lantern fair to see."

"Only every so often. The abandoned residences there are large and fine — if the place were truly clean, someone would have claimed them long ago. I've heard that even the authorities won't touch several of the properties. Aside from travelling merchants, almost no one stays there long-term. The homeless sometimes go to sleep there, but it's too far from the markets in the city, so lying down there doesn't put food in anyone's belly."

"Is that so."

The more Lu Huaixi heard, the more intrigued she felt. What little drowsiness had remained in her eyes brightened into genuine interest.

"Indeed. Young Mistress, and with your... smaller-than-average courage... going there at night, you might not sleep soundly afterward."

Lu Huaixi did not respond immediately. After a moment she spoke. "But I want to go. Besides, Miss Shen is inviting me privately for the first time. I don't want to refuse her."

Then she gave a small huff. "When have I ever been lacking in courage?"

"I didn't truly say you were lacking in courage, it's just—"

Yaoxu tried to explain, but in the end, could not.

Their Young Mistress had been timid even back when she was still an unmarried girl. She was not afraid of most things — just that sort of vague, unnameable kind, and every time she so much as heard mention of it, she would lie awake all night.

"Alright, alright. I'm not afraid of any of that anymore. When we go, I'll bring all of you along, and I'll buy lanterns for everyone."

Lu Huaixi settled the matter quickly and decisively.

Most of the irritation from not sleeping well over Xie Yuanjing's doings had also dissipated since last night.

She sat down after washing up, watching the maidservants bring out one dish after another for the morning meal. She picked out the bowl of savoury congee she liked and drew it toward herself.

Everyone in the room knew Lu Huaixi's habits at mealtimes.

Jingshuang had something to report and had been waiting at the side for quite some time before she finally approached.

"Young Mistress, Lu Tangshu has sent you a letter."

Because of what the Lu second branch had done, no one around Lu Huaixi called her "Third Miss of the Lu family" anymore. When they used her name at all, it was with barely-concealed contempt.

"She actually writes letters? How unusual."

Lu Huaixi accepted it and gave it a cursory glance.

"Will you be going, Young Mistress?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi's fingers loosened, and she let the letter fall to the table.

"If she wants something from me, she can either ask me to return to the Lu residence, or send a card here to the Marquis's household. Summoning me out somewhere like this — and promising to tell me some secret — does she think I'm as simple-minded as she is?"

"Then this servant will have someone send a refusal."

"No need. Have someone reply that I'll go."

Lu Huaixi called Jingshuang back. "Have someone look into He Jianhang's schedule around that time, then send someone to my mother. If things are as I suspect, we'll settle her affairs on that day while we're at it."

Ever since Lu Tangshu had begun desperately casting about for a match, Lu Huaixi had kept the pressure on.

But lately she had deliberately eased up and stopped paying attention, letting Lu Tangshu believe that the main branch had run out of ways to handle her — and giving her time to grow bold again.

She had also confirmed that Lu Tangshu and He Jianhang had met privately more than once, not only that time at the restaurant.

Though the two of them did not seem to have anything between them.

Every time, Lu Tangshu had worn her usual imperious, impatient look. He Jianhang, though shadowed and noticeably more sullen than before, still deferred to Lu Tangshu — though with an undisguised reluctance.

They looked every bit like enemies. But that was precisely what made it enjoyable to watch, as far as Lu Huaixi was concerned.

"Oh, and Young Mistress—"

Jingshuang seemed to remember something and spoke again, cutting through her thoughts.

"You recently had someone keep watch on Wu Wenlian. This servant received word that she was beaten when she returned home that day — and so was the other one. What happened at that time has spread outside. Yesterday the Wu family were apparently saying they would haul Wu Wenlian in to apologise to you in person."

Lu Huaixi felt an immediate aversion at the mention of the Wu family.

It used to be on account of Wu Wenlian. Now it was on account of the whole family's greed and ignorance.

Lu Huaixi's clear eyes sharpened into something uncharacteristically stern. "If the Wu family comes, have them turned away. I don't want them in my sight. If they try to cause any trouble, send people to make a scene right back at them."

"Understood, this servant knows what to do."

Jingshuang bowed her head in assent, then heard the person before her ask, "Besides being beaten, has Wu Wenlian had anything else happen to her recently? Has she been going out?"

"She has gone out, Young Mistress — twice, both times to the western part of the city."

The western district again.

But Wu Wenlian going to the western district made sense. She often went there.

Still, Lu Huaixi found herself paying closer attention without quite knowing why. "Do we know where in the western district?"

"We do."

The matter of Wu Wenlian did not take long. Lu Huaixi added a few more instructions for Jingshuang, then let out a drowsy yawn.

When she blinked her eyes back open, they were slightly wet, giving her gaze an even clearer quality, and making the whole of her look entirely innocent.

"Shall we put you down for a little more sleep, Young Mistress?"

Yaoxu's heart softened at the sight. She stepped forward and began massaging Lu Huaixi's shoulders. "This servant can see you didn't rest well."

"A little, yes. But I won't sleep more — isn't Master Shen still coming to 'apologise'?"

At the mention of this, Lu Huaixi could not help pursing her lips. It brought to mind Xie Yuanjing, who had come back in the middle of the night.

He said he had been returning to the room every night these past several days — only arriving and rising after she had fallen deeply asleep.

Last night, perhaps still avoiding her, he had crept back in the dark, and was already up and gone before dawn, earlier than even a morning at court would require.

The thought of it irritated her.

He was the one who had done something wrong. He dropped a few pretty words and then disappeared — and yet she, the one who had been wronged, ended up looking like the bully who had taken someone else's spot, as though she were the one forcing him out of his own room.

—

By the time the news reached Lu Tangshu that Lu Huaixi had agreed to come, she was standing in the summer heat, regarding the man in front of her with undisguised contempt.

In this kind of weather, standing outside for even a short while was enough to work up a sweat.

"I've arranged for the person to come out. If you still can't manage to get a handle on things after this, then you're truly useless — and don't come bothering me again!"

The man facing her had also been pushed past patience by the heat.

Especially when he caught the look of disgust in Lu Tangshu's eyes. The already-slack expression on his face darkened further.

"Don't use that tone with me. You said you could set those two against each other — how did that work out?"

He Jianhang let out a cold laugh. "All that did was give Xie Yuanjing reason to step in. Can you even get a moment of their attention anymore? Can you set foot in that Marquis's household even once?"

"You—"

"And you dare look down on me? That little fixation you have on your brother-in-law — did you think I hadn't noticed?"

He Jianhang spat to the side. The stubble on his face and the dullness left by drink gave him a dishevelled appearance, which, combined with the narrow, half-lidded set of his eyes, made him look all the more seedy and sinister.

The blood drained from Lu Tangshu's face. Fury surged up in her — all the cold indifference she had been receiving from her grandfather lately, wrapped up and unleashed in a single sharp slap.

"A discarded pawn that the He family has thrown away — and you dare question me? What do you think you are!"

She raised her hand and struck him hard. Every ounce of resentment from the recent coolness she had faced from her grandfather poured into that blow.

"Don't forget — you still have to come begging me just to get a single look at her! Without me, what are you? A useless wreck of a man who can do nothing — and you think you can act against someone connected to Xie Yuanjing? You think you can touch that idiot?"

The slap landed, and the red that flooded He Jianhang's eyes in that instant was murderous.

Lu Tangshu had little real force behind her hand, but she had deliberately curled her fingers so her nails raked across his face.

It barely stung. But the humiliation it carried was immense.

"You vicious creature — you're asking for death!"

"You dare! Try touching me — just try!"

chapters.title: Shen Zhoushu's Apology
chapters.content:
Over Lu Tangshu's sharp cry, He Jianhang's swinging hand clenched into a tight fist mid-swing. The vacant look in his eyes was immediately replaced by something savage and unrestrained.

He very much wanted to strangle the creature in front of him. But the last thread of his reason told him — not yet.

"Go ahead and hit me. Why have you stopped?"

Lu Tangshu read his restraint plainly. She pressed down the flash of alarm that had struck her a moment ago, and her eyes filled with scorn.

"Useless. Do you dare lay a hand on me? Never mind that right now you're nothing but a cornered rat with no way out — even before, you were never worth a second look from me. I'm only being generous, letting you have that dimwit Lu Huaixi."

He Jianhang held himself back and said nothing, but the corners of his mouth pulled into a twisted, rage-edged smile.

After his engagement was broken off, the He family had cast him aside entirely and shifted their attention to another son in the household to support his elder brother instead.

Whatever regard had once been shown to him had transformed entirely into his father's fury and contempt.

He had nothing now. From a He family son with a promising future, he had become someone the whole household spoke of with pity and disdain.

He would not accept it.

They had both fallen low — so why could the Cheng'en Marquis's household keep standing? Why did Xie Yuanjing get to marry a beauty and receive the backing of the Lu family?

While he was stuck in this cramped, dingy alley that he would never have deigned to notice before, listening to this vile woman's insults.

If Lu Huaixi had married him. If the Lu main branch had become his ally. He would never have sunk to this. He could have measured himself against his own elder brother.

"Don't think about pulling tricks. And don't think you can turn on me."

Lu Tangshu had finally exhausted her rage. She looked at the man before her with deep revulsion. "If you expose what I've done, you won't get away either. I'll make sure you're the first to go down."

He Jianhang crushed the urge to kill her, and after a long pause, replied in a cold, flat voice. "Of course not. But if you dare give me anything less than your full cooperation, I will not let it pass."

He paused, exhaled slowly, then continued. "Have everything and everyone ready. That day — I will see her."

"And tell your people to keep their eyes open. If I so much as get a scratch, I'll make you pay for it."

Lu Tangshu gave a warning and then a dismissive snort.

"As long as you remember, once you've had your fill, to ruin her and Xie Yuanjing's relationship — destroy her reputation completely — I will have my father pull you up. He will do it."

Her voice carried an edge of wild, barely-contained fervour. "Then you can take your elder brother's place, bring Lu Huaixi back as a concubine, and have both your beauty and your future — while still marrying some well-positioned woman who can give you proper support. Won't that be a fine life indeed."

The red in He Jianhang's eyes deepened.

These words sent a rush of excitement through the resentment and humiliation he had been barely holding together, making the look on his face all the more unsettling.

He said nothing, but a series of cold laughs echoed silently in his chest.

What Lu Tangshu wanted was for Lu Huaixi to be so thoroughly destroyed she could never hold her head up again.

She was willing to stake the entire reputation of a Lu family noblewoman on it, just to see Lu Huaixi despised by Xie Yuanjing and mocked by all — reduced to the shame of the Lu family. Her ruthlessness was not to be underestimated.

Someone like this had to be guarded against.

She assumed he shared her reasoning — that for the sake of his resentment, for the sake of gaining the Lu family's support, he would join her in ruining the woman.

But Lu Tangshu had miscalculated.

He would certainly have the woman — but his purpose was never to wait for this vile creature's father to give him a leg up.

The only person in the Lu family with real power to lift someone was the patriarch himself, Lu Yandao. Lu Tangshu was nothing but a fool borrowing the Lu family's name.

But threatening and coercing Lu Huaixi was still necessary. A married woman who had been ruined — if she wanted no one to know, if she wanted to preserve her reputation — would have no choice but to beg him to stay silent.

And the moment Lu Huaixi came to him begging, he could take back everything.

—

Shen Zhoushu's apology was not a grand production.

He sent a chest of gifts to Lu Huaixi, and since it was not appropriate to enter the Marquis's residence so openly, he waited until evening and went together with Xie Yuanjing to his courtyard.

Lu Huaixi was inside selecting what to wear to Huique Slope the following day.

The area was mostly home to travelling merchants — people there to sell goods and make money. If she wore her usual clothes, she would stand out rather obviously.

After considering it back and forth, she settled on a set at the very bottom of the pile — a plain ivory-white man's robe made of ordinary cloth.

She was still mulling it over when several loud noises suddenly carried in from outside, along with what sounded like someone calling out "Young Mistress Xie," startling her.

But the sound stopped just as quickly, as though someone had cut it off.

Lu Huaixi set down what she was holding and looked toward the door.

"What's that noise?"

Jingshuang pushed open the door, her expression carrying a trace of helplessness. "Young Mistress, it's Master Shen."

"Shen Zhoushu? Why is he here again?"

"He came with the First Young Master. He said calling during the day and staying long would be improper, so he made a special trip in the evening — so he could offer his apology in person, with the First Young Master present."

"Was that noise just now him apologising?"

Lu Huaixi blinked. "He shouted like that — I thought there was an intruder."

Yaoxu stifled a laugh, then crouched down and took out the robe Lu Huaixi had been looking at.

"He said it was too late to come close to the entrance without being rude, so he stopped in the courtyard. From what this servant can tell, he's had a bit to drink. The First Young Master looks thoroughly fed up and is having people drag him away."

Jingshuang glanced back once. "Though Master Shen is still refusing to leave. He keeps saying he has already made all the arrangements, and that the Young Mistress is sure to have a wonderful time tomorrow."

"Wonderful. I'm sure I will."

Lu Huaixi gave a perfunctory nod, then grew a little curious and ran over to the window to look outside.

It was evening in name, but the red clouds had already faded from the horizon.

Lanterns lit up the corridor, which made the courtyard beyond them look even darker by contrast.

Lu Huaixi had been hoping to glimpse exactly how thoroughly fed up Xie Yuanjing looked, but no matter how long she squinted, all she could make out were the tall silhouettes of several figures.

She recognised Xie Yuanjing's shape immediately, but his face was entirely lost to the darkness.

She was about to close the window when a gaze came to rest on her.

She could not see anything in the darkened courtyard — but Lu Huaixi, standing in the light, fell easily into Xie Yuanjing's line of sight.

He looked over without any attempt to conceal it, his eyes coming to rest on her face. Knowing she could not make out his expression, he smiled at her anyway.

Lu Huaixi's hand paused mid-motion.

She could feel someone watching her, and of everyone out there, only Xie Yuanjing was facing this window.

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together. The thought that he could see her perfectly while she could not tell who was who among the figures out there rubbed her the wrong way.

She instinctively scowled in that direction — a flash of the accumulated irritation over his avoidance these past days — then snapped the window shut.

Who eventually sent Shen Zhoushu home, Lu Huaixi never found out. All she knew was that when Xie Yuanjing came in, the faint trace of alcohol on him was unmistakable.

She was sitting in the chair reading, though the page had barely turned in the better part of an hour.

Jingshuang and Yaoxu soon withdrew, leaving only the two of them.

Feeling that Xie Yuanjing was still watching her after he came in, Lu Huaixi found it increasingly impossible to settle.

She tried to make herself look at the words on the page, but his upright figure kept sliding into the edge of her vision, and his presence seemed to wind itself around her, inch by inch.

Lu Huaixi grew more irritated the longer she tried to read, and finally set the book aside altogether and looked over.

But asking him "why are you staring at me" felt a little too bold to actually say. She held her breath, and after a long pause, managed to push out one line instead. "Did you drink?"

Xie Yuanjing stood not far from her. He thought about it, then shook his head.

"No."

"...You're lying."

Lu Huaixi stared at him with widened eyes, hardly able to believe he would say something so blatantly untrue to her face.

She naturally had no intention of admitting that her own question had been equally pointless.

She only felt that the way Xie Yuanjing was watching her, with that gentle and unhurried gaze, as though he could see straight through every bit of her flustered uncertainty — was genuinely insufferable.

chapters.title: Do You Want to Smell?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi's single word — "you're lying" — drew a quiet laugh from Xie Yuanjing.

That low, slightly rough sound was like a stone dropped into still water, sending outward rings of perfectly even, achingly beautiful ripples.

Lu Huaixi held his gaze for only a few beats before she turned her head away, undone by that lazy, unhurried tone.

"I'm not lying. I would never lie to you."

Xie Yuanjing moved a little closer, then continued, "The smell isn't mine."

Lu Huaixi felt herself enveloped by this person all over again with no resistance at all. In her unease, it occurred to her that staying seated might put her at a disadvantage — and she stood up abruptly.

The two of them, who had been a short distance apart a moment ago, now had their faces in far clearer view of each other's, simply because she had risen.

In an instant Lu Huaixi thought of the two kisses from the night before. Before she had time to react to that thought, she was drawn toward him.

Xie Yuanjing gathered her into a brief, light embrace.

"Do you want to smell?"

He tilted his face toward hers, his voice carrying an unhurried ease, pitched low.

Not quite flirtatious, yet nothing like his usual proper manner.

"Is there still any smell of alcohol?"

The words, warm with his breath, fell directly into Lu Huaixi's ear.

She had never heard Xie Yuanjing speak quite like this. She felt as though something had crept into her ear and begun to make it itch.

The tingling sensation spread slowly outward, tracing its way through her limbs, then gathered at her chest — a soft, rhythmic tapping, folding in with her heartbeat.

The stubborn desire not to give in was swept entirely from her mind. Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes without dignity, lips pressed together, unable to say a word.

She could not blame herself for lacking resolve. She had, after all, been drawn to Xie Yuanjing in the first place.

Even though she had since drawn those feelings back in, and even though she was now timid and at a loss — she could not deny that this person had something rather bewitching about him.

"The alcohol is Shen Zhoushu's. He knocked over a cup when he got up, and a few drops landed on my robe. I was in a hurry to get back, and he insisted on coming along to apologise to you."

Lu Huaixi still said nothing.

Xie Yuanjing's voice was unhurried, and because of how close he was, it reached her a little lower and softer than it usually did.

"I didn't have time to change. I was afraid he might startle you, and afraid you might think I was avoiding you again, so I came straight back. But I truly haven't drunk anything tonight — smell again, if you'd like."

The latter part of what he said was more measured, less like what he had said before. But Lu Huaixi seemed still caught somewhere in the tone of his earlier words, and it was a long time before the corners of her lips finally moved.

"Understood."

"Understood — so you believe me now?"

The words had barely left his mouth when the person who was already standing very close tilted his head slightly.

Lu Huaixi felt that warmth again, heavier this time, and so close that the whole of her began to go faintly numb.

Something inside her felt like it had tied itself into a knot. She did not dislike Xie Yuanjing's nearness, and yet she did not want him near.

"Could you... move back a little?"

"Why?"

Lu Huaixi's lips moved but nothing came out.

Xie Yuanjing did not move either.

When he set his mind on something, he gave it his full patience. When to press forward and when to ease off — he had always thought it through.

Right now, he could not actually see the expression on Lu Huaixi's face. But he could sense her uncertainty.

Yet within that uncertainty and resistance, there was no aversion. He had tested it. It was just enough to take the next step.

"Are you afraid of me?"

Xie Yuanjing suddenly spoke with complete seriousness. "Last night I failed to restrain myself. But until you have thought things through, I will not do that again."

Lu Huaixi was pulled back from her thoughts by these words. After a small pause, she asked with some uncertainty.

"Really?"

"Yes. Really."

Xie Yuanjing kept his expression perfectly composed. "But given that I do have feelings for you, my mind cannot be entirely clean about it. When I can't hold back, I will ask you first. But I will not do anything more than that. I'll only kiss you."

Lu Huaixi was struck dumb.

But she forgot entirely to take him to task for saying something so brazen with such composure. She only found that within those words "when I can't hold back," her mind had suddenly jumped to the little booklet her eldest sister had once sent her.

And then felt embarrassed at herself for wandering there of all places.

Lu Huaixi pushed that entirely inexplicable thought aside and drew in a breath through her nose, trying to settle herself.

But then she paused — and leaned slightly forward.

She sniffed several times, and then abruptly stepped back.

"There is a smell of fragrant cream on you."

Lu Huaixi stated this with certainty. "It's the kind women use. I've used it."

The subject changed so abruptly that Xie Yuanjing was, for a rare moment, caught off guard. Then something in his eyes flickered — recognition, and brief hesitation.

But seeing her expression utterly sure and impossible to bluff, he did not stay silent.

"How is your nose this sharp."

Xie Yuanjing sounded helpless.

He was about to draw her back, but she had already taken two quick steps backward.

Like a child who simply had to hear him say yes.

The warmth of the moment dissolved, and the feeling of emptiness where she had been in his arms came faster than he had expected.

Xie Yuanjing exhaled quietly. Then he reached into his robe and produced a small jar of fragrant cream, which he set on the table beside them.

It was a very small jar — round, barely half the size of Lu Huaixi's palm.

"I asked the maidservants who came from the Lu residence. They said this is the scent you like."

Xie Yuanjing said, "I went and found some. But I only had the one jar on me."

Lu Huaixi stared at it. She picked up the small jar, opened it, and held it up to her nose.

It was from the shop she always went to.

The shop's proprietress was an exceptionally beautiful woman, perhaps ten years her senior, whose manner of speaking was gentle as flowing water — though when it came to business, she was brisk and decisive.

Lu Huaixi was particularly fond of her, and so she would drop in from time to time.

Almost half the things in the shop were made by the proprietress herself, with distinctive, pleasant scents unlike anything sold elsewhere.

But like the medicine pills from young Dr. Zeng's practice, they only made so much each month. Whatever was available was available, and when it ran out, it ran out — no matter who came asking.

"How did you..."

Lu Huaixi could not help but curve her eyes into a smile, looking again and again in a sort of disbelief.

It was her favourite scent — and the hardest one to obtain.

Even as well-acquainted as she was with the proprietress, she could only get one extra jar per month more than the average customer. No more than that.

And she was generous with it in her use. A jar this small never lasted long enough.

Even so, fond as she was of it, this was very much a matter between women. It had never occurred to her that Xie Yuanjing would have taken note.

Before she could ask anything further, Xie Yuanjing said, "I had not originally intended for you to know about this one. But with a nose like yours, even from that far away, with the smell of alcohol over it — you still caught it."

"You said — you went yourself?"

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing nodded. "This afternoon."

He could have sent someone, of course. But when he thought that this was something Lu Huaixi loved, and that she would put it on her skin — he found he did not want anyone else's hands on it.

As for keeping one jar on himself — that had been an impulse he could not quite account for.

He had no interest in fragrances. It had simply occurred to him, all at once, that carrying it this way was rather like having Lu Huaixi leave something of herself behind on him.

"Why did you not want me to know?"

Lu Huaixi looked at him curiously.

But Xie Yuanjing did not answer. He only looked at her quietly for a moment, then turned the subject elsewhere. "I've left the rest with your maidservants. Don't read too late. Sleep early."

Seeing Xie Yuanjing turn to leave so suddenly — just like these past few days, clean and abrupt, without a backward glance — Lu Huaixi went blank for a moment.

And then, for reasons she could not entirely name, the happiness she had felt at seeing the fragrant cream was pressed flat all at once.

She furrowed her brow, and called after him with a flash of irritation.

"Xie Yuanjing!"

chapters.title: She Knew How to Choose
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi was angry, but she remembered to set down what she was holding first.

"Why are you leaving again? You said you weren't avoiding me — if this isn't avoiding me, what is?"

Her voice came out flat and blunt, her brow faintly drawn together. "If you don't want to be in the same room as me, then have Gong Zhuo prepare a separate room. Stop dragging it out every night."

She hated that Xie Yuanjing came back so late every night just to avoid her.

He had said he would wait for her to take her time thinking things through — and yet he was getting barely any sleep at all. This was not waiting. This was pressuring her into a decision.

Lu Huaixi could have simply said outright: no need to think it over, I choose freedom at the end of one year. But everything had happened so fast.

She could not read what Xie Yuanjing was truly thinking, and she was not, in truth, as decisive as she liked to believe she was.

As for what it was she was hesitating over — privately, Lu Huaixi suspected it had to do with not wanting to upset the arrangement between the two families.

She hoped Xie Yuanjing would calm down on his own. And knowing his character, she trusted he would — quickly — and after that would extract himself just as swiftly and act as though none of this had ever happened.

Having said her piece, Lu Huaixi looked down, let the tangle of feelings from a moment ago ease slightly, and softened her tone.

"Never mind. Do as you like. It's not as though it's me losing sleep over it. And if your mother asks one day, I won't be covering for you."

Xie Yuanjing stopped walking. Watching Lu Huaixi go from her earlier displeasure to standing there now with her eyes downcast and her mood unreadable, he hesitated for a brief moment.

But then his brow gave the faintest lift. He curved his lips, and smiled.

"I'm going to bathe and change."

He said quietly, "You don't like the smell of alcohol. I only wanted to get rid of it first."

"Change clothes until I fall asleep?"

Lu Huaixi did not believe him. She had no desire at all to be cast as the bully — as though she were the one forcing Xie Yuanjing out of his own room.

She also felt uneasy at the thought of Xie Yuanjing truly moving to another room and leaving her here alone.

There seemed to be no right answer no matter what she did.

"Forget it. I'm not asking anymore."

Lu Huaixi said, without much patience, and made to go back inside — but caught the sound of Xie Yuanjing's quiet exhale as she turned.

"Do you think you stay awake very late?"

He said, with a touch of helplessness. "I told you to sleep early because you didn't rest well last night. Aside from yesterday, every other night — haven't you been asleep the moment you lie down?"

Lu Huaixi opened her mouth, surprise mingling with a flicker of sheepishness. She closed it again and took a small breath through her nose.

"And furthermore—" Xie Yuanjing looked down at her, a smile at the corner of his mouth, though his eyes held something harder to name. "Separate rooms — put that thought away. I won't be sleeping elsewhere. And you would do well not to think about it either."

He was choosing not to push her. That, in itself, was no small generosity on his part.

—

That very same generous Xie Yuanjing was detained by official matters well past midnight. Lu Huaixi did not see him again until she woke the next morning.

The restlessness that had flared up last night was gone. Whether from sleep, or from having lost some internal wager in her dreams, she found herself with a clear sense of what she ought to choose — and she felt oddly calm about it.

Even so, when she caught sight of the small jar of fragrant cream, she felt a faint ripple pass through her.

Xie Yuanjing had gone himself.

A tall, composed man stepping into that small shop filled with fragrance, drawing startled glances from the young women inside, picking up that little jar.

Perhaps asking whether there was more available, or which scents women preferred.

Lu Huaixi found she could not quite picture what expression Xie Yuanjing would have worn in that shop.

No matter how she tried to imagine it, he seemed entirely out of place there.

Yet though her face showed nothing in particular, the motion with which she opened the jar was more careful than usual. And when she used it, she was less careless than before.

After lunch came the hottest part of the day.

Lu Huaixi rested indoors to escape the heat, waiting for the time to come and meet Shen Ruojin.

She was looking forward to the outing to Huique Slope. If she had not unexpectedly married, she would still be at the age for exactly this sort of carefree wandering.

She was just about to change into the plain men's robe, when Jingshuang came in — so quickly she had not even wiped the perspiration from her forehead.

"Young Mistress, the Lu eldest young master just passed by the Marquis's residence and sent some things for you. He happened to find the Lord in the main hall, and the two of them spoke for a while. The Lord is now asking you to come."

"In weather this hot, why did my elder brother come? Is he still there?"

Lu Huaixi spoke and rose in the same motion, not giving the blazing sun outside a second thought as she headed for the door.

The door had only opened a crack when the heat beyond struck her like a wall.

"What on earth couldn't wait, that he had to send it now? Does he have no sense?"

"Young Mistress, don't rush — the people who came said the eldest young master travelled by carriage, and he arrived looking perfectly fresh and comfortable. There is ice in the main hall, and the Lord has made sure of it throughout."

Jingshuang kept pace with her. "This servant is not certain whether the eldest young master is still there — from what was reported, he seemed to have other things to attend to."

"He probably didn't stay long then."

Lu Huaixi knew her elder brother well. He could barely sit still in his own home — let alone in the Marquis's household, which he had barely any familiarity with.

What she did not understand was why the Marquis had asked to see her. She had only exchanged words with him once, on the day she had served tea.

If it were simply on account of her elder brother's visit, it seemed unlike the Marquis's nature — not one for casual conversation when he was supposed to be resting and avoiding guests — to bother calling her in.

But whatever the reason, Lu Huaixi's steps did not slow.

It was truly too hot outside. She would rather get it over with quickly and stay somewhere with ice.

When she arrived, only the Marquis was in the main hall. The coolness settled over her the moment she stepped in, though with the main doors open, it was still not as comfortable as her own room.

"Father."

Lu Huaixi approached and curtsied.

She had glanced over on her way in. The Marquis's complexion did not look as well as the last time she had seen him — the space between his brows seemed pressed down by something unseen, lending him a heavier, more shadowed look.

Having paid her respects, Lu Huaixi said nothing further.

The person before her did not make her wait long. In the time it took to drink one mouthful of tea, the Marquis spoke.

"I just spoke with your elder brother for a while. I hear your father has been working particularly hard of late and hasn't had a proper rest. I imagine some of that is owing to matters connected to Yuanjing as well."

"I have not enquired into the affairs at home. My father has always had a great deal of official business. But if it also involves my husband, that is only as it should be — we are all one family."

Lu Huaixi said these outwardly warm words with a perfectly composed expression, her downcast eyes very calm.

The Marquis was quiet for a moment. "You are a sensible girl."

He set down his teacup. His tone carried a certain authority, and it was plain he had not come here to offer pleasantries.

"Since you came into the Marquis's household, I have never sat down properly to speak with either you or Yuanjing. Certain rules of the household, and certain proprieties expected of a new daughter-in-law, I have turned a blind eye to — never truly enforced. But that is not entirely for the sake of the Lu family. It is also because of Yuanjing's nature."

Lu Huaixi listened without speaking.

She was not afraid of handling this.

By now she had learned the Marquis's household almost through and through. With the divine physician's treatment still in her hands, even the most difficult person in the household — the Old Marchioness — treated her with unfailing courtesy, their manner toward each other outwardly as warm as grandmother and granddaughter.

Facing the Marquis, all she needed to do was sit quietly, offer the occasional reply, and find her way to the purpose of today's conversation.
