Seeing Lu Huaixi sitting with her head slightly lowered, listening obediently, the Marquis did not pause for long and continued:

"I know my own son. Everything he does has a purpose. He never takes a needless step — especially these past years. Even something like marriage, he had it mapped out long before it happened: who could be married, who would suit him best. He calculated it all clearly. But I am glad that in the end, the one he sought out was you."

The Marquis said, "The Lu family has given him a great deal of support. I, as his father, can do very little to help him now — and so naturally I must think more carefully about what comes after."

At the word "after," Lu Huaixi's lips pulled into a faint curve despite the faint displeasure rising inside her.

She could not quite manage a full smile. But the Marquis was, in truth, rather amusing.

Beyond that, Lu Huaixi found herself wondering, with a flicker of idle curiosity: when Xie Yuanjing eventually dissolved this marriage and took a new wife — and the next noblewoman to enter this household heard these same words — what sort of reaction she might have.

chapters.title: What If I Changed My Mind
chapters.content:
The wind blowing through the main hall grew hotter by degrees, and those sitting inside had begun to perspire.

Lu Huaixi did not look up, which meant the faint, contemptuous curl of her lips went unseen.

"It is only right that Yuanjing treats you well for now. But once his footing is more firmly established, the support from your father will carry less and less weight. When that time comes, the inner courtyard will begin to fill with other women. He would not truly cast you aside, but there will be a degree of neglect.

"So now is the time to learn well how to manage the inner household and share his burdens. Otherwise, even if I and your mother side with you going forward, we cannot override whom Yuanjing chooses to favour. You would be the one at a disadvantage."

The Marquis paused, his sharp gaze settling on Lu Huaixi, who had been sitting quietly without a word.

He did not give her much time to think. Very quickly, he continued.

"You must be clear-eyed about this. Yuanjing has always been this way — deep in thought and strategy, but cold in nature. He has only ever listened to his grandfather, and his grandfather's sole concern is the Marquis's household. So is his. Right now you are useful to him, and so naturally he treats you more warmly than others.

"But a man should not be entangled by sentiment. Your mother has always praised your temperament. I imagine that when, in time, another noblewoman enters the household as his secondary wife, you will be magnanimous about it."

Lu Huaixi finally understood why she had been summoned.

She pressed down the irritation and stifled frustration rising within her, and saw through it plainly: the Marquis was sowing discord.

He did not want Xie Yuanjing to have support.

And so he used words that a woman could never easily raise with her husband — words that settled in the heart as a suppressed, unvoiced unease, growing into a knot that could not be questioned outright, then slowly widening into a rift over time.

If it had been any other woman, a few words like these might have chilled half her heart on the spot.

But it happened to be her — Lu Huaixi — that the Marquis was dealing with.

Even so, she could not deny that those words had caused a ripple.

What the Marquis said was not wrong. If Xie Yuanjing had not had this sudden change of feeling, he was exactly as described — every action he took had its purpose and calculation.

His consideration for her was not because of who she was as a person.

The difference, however, was that she had known this from the very beginning. She had agreed to enter his scheme, to stand alongside him — each using the other, and being used in turn.

When she left the main hall, the sky outside had clouded over somewhat, though it was still very hot.

Lu Huaixi walked more slowly than she had coming. Her mind was elsewhere, and she did not notice the figure waiting for her beneath the corridor ahead.

Not until she nearly walked straight into him did she finally come back to herself.

"Why aren't you watching where you're going?"

Xie Yuanjing's voice reached her. He must have come in a hurry — a bead of perspiration ran down the line of his jaw and fell.

Lu Huaixi had been thinking of him, and now here he was, standing in front of her without warning. She blinked — and all she could see was his sharp profile, damp with heat, and the warm, familiar scent of him rolling toward her.

She had been thinking of him just now. Her breath caught, and her heart stopped, unbidden, for a single beat.

"Why are you back?"

"I was passing by. I brought you iced dessert from Feiyu Tower."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her. "What did he say?"

The moment he arrived at the residence he had learned that Lu Huaixi had been summoned. He had intended to go fetch her directly, but by the time he reached the main hall, he was told she had already gone back to her courtyard.

He had walked in, and yet the person who had left before him was slower to return than he was.

"What was said — tell me."

In truth, Lu Huaixi had no intention of reporting anything. There was nothing worth saying, and in some matters, she might understand the situation even better than the Marquis did.

But this person had appeared so suddenly that he had thrown all her thoughts into disarray. She no longer had the energy to come up with anything to conceal.

"It wasn't much. The Marquis ran into my elder brother when he came to deliver things, and so he called me over and said a few things. Gave me some advice."

Lu Huaixi smiled at Xie Yuanjing, then recalled his mention of the iced dessert, and felt a soft warmth push back some of the weight that had settled in her.

"Though your father is really something..."

"Really what?"

Seeing her hesitate, seeming to have reverted to her usual untroubled manner, Xie Yuanjing did not relax. If anything, something in him sank.

He took hold of her hand, his thumb pressing down slightly. "Really not a decent person?"

"...I didn't say that."

Lu Huaixi grew a little tense. The place where he held her hand had begun to warm again.

"He said he was thinking ahead on your behalf, so he earnestly advised me to learn to manage the inner household — so that later, when the Lu family is no longer of use to you, when you have other alliances, when there are secondary wives, I can at least keep something for myself."

The corridor was empty. Even the maidservants who had been following had slipped back to a distance.

Lu Huaixi deliberately ignored the sensation of his hand. She did not understand why she was reacting more strongly to Xie Yuanjing's closeness each time it happened.

She lowered her head and continued: "He also said you have a purpose behind everything you do — thorough and calculating but cold in nature, that you never do anything without reason, so you didn't marry me with genuine feeling and never would."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft laugh at that, her tone shifting into something lighter.

"I'm not accusing anyone, but the way he spoke was clearly meant to stir trouble — to make me quarrel with you. He probably didn't account for the fact that we have an agreement in place..."

"What if I changed my mind?"

Xie Yuanjing interrupted her. His brow had pulled together at some point, and his dark eyes had gone so deep there was nothing readable in them.

But the hand holding hers had not loosened at all, and when he spoke, his voice was not as composed as before.

"I don't want to honour the one-year agreement anymore. I've changed my mind about it, Lu Huaixi."

Feeling her hand go rigid against his palm, Xie Yuanjing held back what he wanted to say and added, "I said you could take your time thinking. There is still time. You don't need to give me an answer now."

Lu Huaixi stopped walking.

She thought her expression must have betrayed something — otherwise he would not have caught on so quickly to the fact that she had still been counting on the dissolution of the marriage.

"Actually, you don't need to wait."

Lu Huaixi thought for a moment, a heaviness pressing in her chest that she could not quite account for.

Even so, she did not linger on it. She parted her lips and continued.

"I don't want to stay in the Marquis's household. No matter how long I think about it, that will be my answer."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing.

Lu Huaixi suddenly found she could not look at him. She lowered her head, blinked, and felt the unfamiliar sting behind her eyes with some discomfort.

But she would not take the words back.

In her view, Xie Yuanjing had had a passing impulse. Even if he had genuinely felt something, it would not occupy much space in a heart like his.

That was simply his nature. Otherwise, Shen Zhoushu would not have made those jokes — and Xie Yuanjing himself had once agreed with them. He knew his own character.

Given all of that, it was neither possible nor wise for her to give away her heart over a few words from him.

"Is it that you don't like me, or that you don't like the Marquis's household?"

After a long silence, Xie Yuanjing finally spoke again.

She could not read the feeling behind his question. But her heart gave an involuntary, inexplicable tremor.

Didn't like him, or didn't like the Marquis's household.

She certainly did not like the Marquis's household. And she was fairly certain she had already stopped liking Xie Yuanjing.

And yet Lu Huaixi's lips moved — and she could not make herself answer him.

"It seems the iced dessert won't keep."

After a long wait, Xie Yuanjing stopped waiting for her reply.

He gave a sudden quiet laugh, took her hand, and led her forward. "Go and enjoy yourself at Huique Slope. It's a bit desolate out there — make sure you don't get separated from anyone."

Lu Huaixi did not try to pull her hand back. She followed him in silence, and for the first time, she felt a kind of sadness settle in her that she could not put into words.

She wanted to turn and look at him, but she never quite did — holding still against herself, not knowing what it was she wanted.

"I have an engagement tonight. It will run late."

Xie Yuanjing said quietly: "Don't be upset. I won't bring it up again. Liking or not liking — in the end, it's not that important."

Lu Huaixi finally looked over.

That did sound like something Xie Yuanjing would say.

She watched his cool, composed profile.

Liking or not liking — for him, it truly was not that important.

chapters.title: Don't Touch the People in My Courtyard
chapters.content:
The road to Huique Slope was easy to travel — wide and nearly empty, so much so that even a carriage could move at something close to a gallop.

Lu Huaixi sat inside, the excitement from before having faded. She was pensive the whole way, carrying a heaviness she could not name.

It was not until she met up with Shen Ruojin that her expression eased a little.

"It might be quite late going back tonight. Will Xie Daren come to collect you?"

Shen Ruojin was also dressed in men's robes, a shade darker than Lu Huaixi's. Seated together, the two of them made for rather a dashing pair.

"My brother said he'll come if he's free. He's never had a proper look around Huique Slope — he thought he might come and see if there's anything worth finding."

Lu Huaixi's thoughts were still drifting. Whether it was because Xie Yuanjing's expression had been so cold when he left, she felt a persistent restlessness she could not quite settle.

And so when Shen Ruojin mentioned him, the faint smile at Lu Huaixi's lips stiffened almost imperceptibly. She dropped her gaze, shielding something in her eyes.

"He has an engagement tonight. The road back from here is straightforward enough — I don't need anyone to come for me."

A flash of surprise crossed Shen Ruojin's face. She was about to ask more, but her sharp eye caught the shift in the other girl's mood.

She did not pursue it. She simply nodded along.

"The road really is wide and clear. Once we get there we can also try some things you won't find in the capital — just roadside stalls, though, temporary ones. They'll only be there a few days."

Seeing Lu Huaixi's slightly puzzled look, Shen Ruojin smiled.

"If it weren't for the lantern fair and the Ghost Market coming up, who would bother with Huique Slope at this time of year? Those small stalls are all put up by travelling merchants' people on a whim — if there are customers, they sell things; if not, they eat and drink among themselves."

"There's a Ghost Market?"

"Yes. The Ghost Market is when Huique Slope is at its most lively all year. The things inside are goods you'd never find in proper shops — some with a history of blood, some without, some strange, some precious. The lantern fair is just the opening act — a way of drawing people in."

"So your brother coming to have a look — that's about whether the Ghost Market has anything worth having?"

"Oh, the Ghost Market isn't open yet. Half a month away, at least. It only opens once a year."

Shen Ruojin shook her head. "There'll be word beforehand, though — word of what remarkable things will be there."

The Ghost Market pulled Lu Huaixi's thoughts away, and most of the gloom from before lifted without her noticing.

Shen Ruojin let out a small breath of relief, and seeing that she had finally brightened, smiled back at her with curved eyes.

"Do you want to go?"

Shen Ruojin asked, reading her interest.

Lu Huaixi thought about it, then answered with some measure of reason. "Can I? I'm curious, but I dislike trouble even more."

"Probably best not to, then. Most of the people who go are trouble themselves. You smell of money — going in would be like a lamb walking into a den of wolves."

"Fair enough. Then I won't go."

"You really do take advice well."

Shen Ruojin laughed.

She particularly liked that quality in Lu Huaixi — that easy, unaffected manner, and those eyes that listened to people with such sincerity, bright as sparkling water when she smiled.

It was why, when her brother's letter came asking her to invite Lu Huaixi out to see the lanterns, she had agreed without hesitation.

"Huique Slope is actually quite large."

Shen Ruojin lifted the carriage curtain. "We're already in it — this entire stretch is part of it. This side is all sealed-up residences, backed against the mountain. We have to pass through this section before we get to the streets."

Lu Huaixi looked out.

The carriage was just passing a residence.

The grey walls looked as though they had weathered countless storms — saturated with the weight of years. The double doors, which should have been a proud vermillion, had darkened to a dull, ashen shade. The cold that seeped from them spread across the entire road.

Even at a glance, this was clearly no ordinary house. But it had long since become lifeless — every trace of its former grandeur entirely gone.

Lu Huaixi looked for a moment, her gaze resting on those dust-covered doors.

Solid and heavy as they were, she felt somehow that she could see straight through to the desolation within.

A chill rose along her back before she could stop it. Lu Huaixi did not dare look again, and quickly drew her eyes away.

As the carriage moved further along, it slowed. The residences they passed began to have black doors instead — some smaller ones bare of any colour at all, the kind belonging to ordinary people.

But the stillness and desolation persisted. Apart from the rhythm of hooves and the roll of wheels, there was no sound at all. No sense of life.

The road grew less wide further ahead, and the residences gave way to shabby little houses.

The carriage turned several times before Lu Huaixi finally glimpsed storefronts and the silhouettes of people.

But even then, it was sparse and scattered. Despite the lanterns strung up on both sides and the few stalls dotting the entrance to the road, it could not by any measure be called lively.

"I've actually been wanting to ask," Lu Huaixi said, looking ahead and letting the tension from those empty residences ease a little. "Why did you invite me here to see lanterns, Ruojin?"

Shen Ruojin was caught off guard.

She glanced at the scene ahead — far quieter than the last few days — and found herself also wanting to drag her unreliable brother here and demand an explanation.

But before she could work out what to say, Lu Huaixi had already answered her own question, and talked herself into contentment.

"Though I suppose nowhere else would be this thrilling. The fewer people and the more desolate the place, the more interesting it is to look at lanterns at night. That's the point, isn't it, Ruojin?"

"...Yes."

Shen Ruojin felt a faint chill run up her spine at the words, despite the blazing heat. The warmth she had arrived with had entirely abandoned her.

Lu Huaixi was the same. She was the first to hop out of the carriage, then turned back. "And I have to say — Huique Slope is much cooler than the city."

—

Xie Yuanjing returned to the residence at dusk and made his way to the Marquis's courtyard.

He could not remember the last time he had sat down and spoken properly with this man he called father.

From the moment that mother and son had been found, and the Marquis of Cheng'en — with no regard for his own reputation — had stepped forward to help them, arranging their lodgings and ensuring they were taken care of on all sides, Xie Yuanjing had known that their family could no longer sit together.

His mother had kept the greater picture in mind, had thought of him, and had not made a scene.

But the day he saw the son walking behind that woman — a son of the same age as himself — Xie Yuanjing had never spoken properly with this father of his again.

Their last remaining thread of father and son had snapped when the Marquis forcibly intervened in a court case.

To protect that woman's son, he had disregarded his own household entirely, and nearly pushed the Xie family to the brink of ruin.

Yet Xie Yuanjing had not expected that even that was not enough — that his father had now begun to set his sights on him, afraid that his growing power would destroy that person's path forward.

When the Marquis saw him enter the room, he looked genuinely surprised, as though he had never expected him to come.

But then he frowned, and spoke with a note of displeasure.

"That girl is sharper than I thought. She went to find you so quickly."

"What would she have to report?"

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet, scornful sound. He made no move to sit, standing there looking at the man before him. "Right now it is I who need the Lu family's support, I who must keep her content. What would she need to report?"

"You—"

The Marquis's expression darkened at those words, and he was about to say something reproving, when Xie Yuanjing continued:

"The person outside — that is your son, isn't he? Sending him into Senior Official Xun's circle now — is that to lay the groundwork, so he can enter the Marquis's household in time?"

Xie Yuanjing's tone carried a trace of dry amusement, free of anger.

He even laughed slightly as he said it, as though speaking of something that had nothing to do with him.

"I heard he is older than me. So when does Father plan to have me — the First Young Master — step aside and make way for him?"

"What nonsense are you spouting!"

The Marquis was struck at the core of what he had been thinking, and fury rose in him.

But just as he brought his palm down on the table, the face of the person before him went cold in an instant.

"You may work to cut off my path on his behalf. We can each rely on our own abilities. But the people in my courtyard — I would advise Father not to touch them."

Xie Yuanjing said it word by word, unhurriedly. "To make it even plainer: the Lu family and she — I want both."

The colour drained from the Marquis's face with rage.

He stared fixedly at this son who had long since refused to be arranged or directed by him.

Right until Xie Yuanjing was nearly at the door, the Marquis gave a sudden cold laugh.

"You want her. Does she want you?"

chapters.title: Sudden Chaos
chapters.content:
The lantern fair at Huique Slope was more beautiful than Lu Huaixi had imagined.

It bore no resemblance to the lanterns in the city, hung neatly and predictably on either side of the street. Nor did it resemble the ordinary lanterns she was used to — charming enough, but never surprising.

Most of these she had never seen before. They came in all shapes and forms.

Some were wound together, arranged into mysterious patterns that suggested ancient totems. Some blazed with vivid colour, painted with celestial figures — strange and extravagant.

Lu Huaixi became absorbed in looking, following the crowd forward, stopping now and then to examine what the roadside vendors were selling and picking out small novelties she had never come across.

After dusk, the area grew more populated, unlike what she had seen on arrival. The street gradually became lively.

"There are more people up ahead, and a raised platform — probably the most interesting part of the fair."

Lu Huaixi looked toward the widening road before them. It opened into a circular clearing with paths leading off in several directions, and the street they had come from was just one of them.

Looking further out, a ring of mountains enclosed the clearing from the far side.

Whenever a gust came through, it carried with it a string of sharp, slightly unsettling sounds.

And the lanterns swayed, their light tracing the ridgeline of the mountains in the distance — layering the whole scene in an atmosphere that was difficult to name.

"This place really is strange."

Yaoxu looked around, then turned back toward the liveliest spot. "I think they're doing lantern riddles over there. I heard some of the people passing say the prizes tonight are very good."

"No wonder there are so many people. More than the past few days combined."

Shen Ruojin sounded mildly surprised as well.

In the space of those few exchanges, Lu Huaixi and the others had been gradually pressed forward by the growing crowd.

Ordinarily, anywhere this crowded would be stifling with summer heat — but somehow this place had very little of it.

Lu Huaixi was watching the liveliest spot when she became aware of the crowd around her thickening. People pressed in on all sides.

She was about to turn back and look for Yaoxu when a commotion broke out near the platform ahead.

Someone was throwing things outward — red cloth bundles, one after another, scattered in all directions. Whether they contained silver or treasures was hard to tell, but they flew without pause into the crowd.

The crowd erupted. What had already been a tight press grew chaotic.

In the midst of the noise, Lu Huaixi heard someone calling her name.

Only then did she realise she had been swept away from the group and into a different part of the crowd.

Before she could turn to look, she felt someone grab her hand and pull her sideways.

She caught a glimpse of pale blue — the same colour as Shen Ruojin's robe.

The tight knot in Lu Huaixi's chest loosened. She was about to call out when the grip on her arm suddenly released — whoever it was had taken hold of the wrong person.

She turned to find her way back. But behind the noise of the crowd, a new sound broke through — the clatter of hooves, coming from some distance away and drawing rapidly closer, echoing off the encircling mountains.

And alongside it: the ring of blades being drawn, and then — screaming, erupting in the crowd.

Someone had forced their way in. Lu Huaixi's heart dropped.

A group of people were clearly searching for something. They drove toward the platform with swift and brutal strikes.

At the same time, others in the crowd who had been indistinguishable from ordinary people suddenly changed — and began seizing others.

In moments, people were falling where they stood, with no chance to react.

The sudden violence sent panic tearing through the crowd. The instinct for survival took over. People fled in every direction — and more and more were knocked to the ground in the rush.

Lu Huaixi forced herself into cold calm as quickly as she could. She did not dare fight against the current of fleeing people.

She did not know whether Shen Ruojin and Yaoxu were safe. But she knew she had to make sure she did not become a liability.

In the space of a single thought, she had already been pushed to the mouth of one of the roads leading off the clearing.

Behind her, the screaming rose and fell without pause. She even heard the dull, agonised sound of steel entering flesh.

"Help... help me..."

Someone wailed, the cries surfacing and then being swallowed by the chaos.

Lu Huaixi's heart hammered. She would not let herself look back — there was no time to look back.

Each of the road mouths was filling with fleeing people, and the darkness beyond each of them was unfamiliar and complete.

Lu Huaixi's hands and feet had gone cold, but her forehead was damp with sweat.

The armed group seemed to be spreading out and taking over the clearing. Someone was closing in behind her, exuding a violence and a hunger for blood — and the sounds of fierce fighting followed.

She did not dare stop. She clenched her jaw, and on instinct ran into one of the roads.

Ahead of her, someone had fallen — a girl of around six or seven, her face scored with scratches, her shabby clothes muddied from being trodden on.

One person looked back briefly. Seeing that the panicking crowd would trample the child, they hesitated — but in the end forced themselves not to stop, grabbed the person beside them, and kept running.

The girl's small, thin body had no strength to resist. She could only curl up and endure the feet coming down on her.

Lu Huaixi bit hard at her lip. After one split second of hesitation, she reached out and hauled the child up with great effort.

"If you want to live, run with me. Don't talk."

One sentence, and she closed her mouth.

She could not spend any more strength than necessary.

What she had to do was find a safe place to shelter through this sudden chaos.

Her people would find her. The Marquis's household's people, the Shen family's people — they would come. She would be all right.

Lu Huaixi did not slow her steps, pressing onward, following instinct through one winding alley after another.

The wind rushed past her ears, mixing with the fierce pounding of her own heartbeat.

She did not know how long she ran. Only when she was almost unable to draw breath did she finally allow herself to stop.

The noise and chaos had fallen away behind her at some point. The place where she now stood was dim and desolate.

Lu Huaixi felt as though every drop of strength had been wrung out of her. She could barely make out anything around her — she only knew her palms were slick with perspiration.

On one side was a grimy stone wall. She gripped the child's hand with one hand and braced herself against the wall with the other, just to keep standing.

Behind her, the sounds seemed to have gone. But she did not dare let her guard down.

She steadied herself with one hand on the wall and moved slowly forward. But she had taken only a few steps before her legs nearly gave way.

She was not the only one. The child she had been holding on to had run until her lips had gone colourless, all the blood drained from her face — she looked as though she might go unconscious in the next instant.

"What... what do we do, older sister..."

The girl's words came out with great effort. She gasped for breath, her whole body trembling, her eyes wide and a little glassy.

"I... I can't run anymore..."

The wind had dried the tears on her face long since. What remained was the pain of exhaustion, and beneath it, fear and confusion.

But then she loosened her grip on her own accord.

"Older sister, run. You don't have to... to look after me anymore."

Beside them was a door — grey and crumbling, blending into the stone wall around it as though it too had long since given itself up to the weather.

Lu Huaixi said nothing. She had little strength left for words.

She looked back once. The dim road behind was empty, without a single light.

The armed men might have gone to chase other people, but that was no guarantee they would not come this way.

Yet ahead, the only way to keep going was into the mountain.

These mountains had been without visitors for years. Even if she and the child had the strength to make it to the base — which they did not — going in would mean never coming out.

"We stop here. We wait."

Lu Huaixi took the child's hand again, and without much hesitation, pushed open the door.

chapters.title: He Would Have to Become a Widower First
chapters.content:
The door had been shut for so long that when it swung open, it gave a long, grinding shriek.

Against the backdrop of waist-high weeds and indistinct mounds of earth within, it was enough to make one's skin crawl and the back run cold.

When the men had first come charging in, Lu Huaixi's reaction had been mostly panic, followed quickly by a cold-headed clarity: she needed to find somewhere to hide.

But now she was genuinely afraid. It was the kind of fear for which there was no solution.

Especially when, the moment she stepped inside, something — wind or something else — pushed the door shut behind them with a dull, heavy thud, as though an iron chain were being dragged across the ground.

The child beside her shuddered violently.

Lu Huaixi had not yet turned to look, but her eyes — now adjusted to the dark — caught something flicker across the space ahead.

"S-sister..."

The girl's voice trembled badly. Both hands clutched at Lu Huaixi in a tight reverse grip. "Sister, we can't stay here... we can't..."

"Why?"

Lu Huaixi's own voice was a little uneven. She pressed it flat, but did not push forward.

"Those... those things..."

The girl looked toward the mounds of earth. She had been about to retreat behind Lu Huaixi, but something made her stop herself and stand beside her instead.

"My mother said... if you see these in a house... never go near them. You'll... you'll take on something bad..."

"What's in there?"

"Bones."

The girl whispered in fear. "If there are some here, there will be more inside. A lot of houses here are like this. They... they choose their places..."

Even though Lu Huaixi had already begun to guess what was in those mounds, her whole body went rigid on hearing it said aloud.

Her instinct was to leave immediately, but the image of those men's brutality rose again in her mind.

Whether they were bandits, rebels, or those who had come hunting for some treasure from the martial world — she had not the faintest idea. The only thing she was certain of was that those men had not intended to leave anyone alive.

She herself could still run for a while. But the girl beside her could barely take another step.

Before she could think further, a rustling sound came from somewhere deeper in the courtyard, followed by wave after wave of cold air drifting through.

That cool air should have been refreshing in the summer heat. Instead it felt as though it was threading itself under her skin — like tiny things slowly gnawing their way through, leaving her whole body prickling.

She felt the urge to cry. Then she turned to find the child beside her already crying first, and Lu Huaixi bit through her own tongue to force the fear back down.

"There's nothing to be afraid of."

Lu Huaixi held herself upright with sheer stubbornness. "The living ones outside are far more dangerous."

—

Shen Zhoushu received the news just as he was riding into Huique Slope.

His plan had been simple enough: let Lu Huaixi see the lanterns, hear a few unsettling tales, take her through the teahouse for a turn, and then — at the height of her fright — let Xie Yuanjing appear to collect her.

Fear in a dark place was perfect for apologies and confessions — far more effective at winning someone's heart than ten dramatic rescues in the city in broad daylight.

What he had not expected was that there would be an actual uprising.

"Say that again?"

"Young Master — Young Mistress Xie and our Miss have — have both been separated from the group—"

Shen Zhoushu's expression went flat and hard. The hand gripping the reins showed white at the knuckles. "That many people watching, and you couldn't keep a few young ladies safe?"

"Young Master, please calm yourself! Those armed men are all from the jianghu — likely come for some specific item. They had planted people inside Huique Slope well in advance."

The man lowered his head. "But none of the injured that have been found are Young Mistress Xie or our Miss. It is likely that they—"

Before he could finish, the sound of hooves came from not far off — not many, probably four or five riders.

Shen Zhoushu frowned and looked up — and met the taut, expressionless face of Xie Yuanjing approaching from ahead.

Behind him was Gong Fei, equally grim-faced, brow furrowed. When he caught sight of Shen Zhoushu, his eyes carried a complicated look that resisted easy description.

In that single instant, Shen Zhoushu knew: his offences had now compounded on top of each other, and if anything happened to Lu Huaixi, he might find himself paying with half his life.

—

The Lu Huaixi who was so fervently being thought of had, in fact, already pulled the child through the door of the residence.

She had not dared go into the inner rooms, and instead found a corner backed against the wall.

She looked outwardly calm, but her hands at this moment were cold as deep-winter ice.

The only reason she kept a firm hold of the child was so she herself would not pass out.

"Don't be afraid. They won't rush into a ruin like this."

Lu Huaixi kept her voice low, holding herself together and showing not even a trace of the fear she felt. "Someone will come looking for us very soon. When they do, I'll have them send you home."

"I... I'm not afraid. Don't be afraid, sister."

The girl pressed herself close against Lu Huaixi's side.

Not long after they sat down, a faint fragrance reached the girl's nose — gradually replacing the damp, abandoned smell that had hung over the courtyard.

She had never smelled anything so lovely, and could not help leaning closer.

"Sister, you're such a kind person."

She said softly, "Just now when you pulled me up and ran with me — I thought I was seeing a deity come down from the heavens."

The mention of just now brought to mind the man who had been running ahead of them. Lu Huaixi hesitated, then asked anyway.

"That person — who was he to you?"

"My father. He heard that some wealthy people had sponsored a special lantern display today, and he brought my brother along to have a look. I'd never seen anything like it, so I begged my brother to bring me."

The girl's matter-of-fact tone made Lu Huaixi forget the circumstances they were in for a moment.

She looked at her with some surprise, and before she could say anything, the girl spoke again. "My father tried to give me away to someone once before. It didn't work out."

What she left unsaid was plain: she had known long ago that no one would mind what happened to her.

Lu Huaixi's lips moved, but she decided not to offer comfort.

Some people did not need it — like stubborn wild grass that had already learned to grow along its own lines.

She used her free hand to gently pat the top of the girl's head, and smiled at her.

The girl smiled back, then winced as the expression tugged at the cuts on her face.

"I was actually a little happy, though. Just now my father looked like he might have wanted to come back for me. I thought he wouldn't even turn his head."

Lu Huaixi did not know what to say to that. The sadness of it settled over her, and for a moment, even the fear was pressed further down by it.

But before she could dwell on it, a quick rustling sound swept through the weed-choked courtyard, pulling both of them back to the present.

The waist-high weeds bent to one side, held there for a moment, then swayed back.

There was no wind in the courtyard now. And yet the grass moved in wide, sweeping waves, again and again.

"Sister... there's something..."

Every feeling Lu Huaixi had been holding dissolved in that instant.

Against her will, her mind filled with the stories she had heard as a child. The hand gripping the girl tightened without her realising.

But when two frightened people are together, one of them has to force themselves to be the brave one.

That was what Lu Huaixi did.

"It's all right. Don't be afraid."

She said don't be afraid. She was, in truth, absolutely terrified.

"Someone will come for us. Very soon—"

And before she could finish the sentence, sounds came from outside.

In the stillness of that desolate place, even through several walls, those sounds carried clearly — growing closer, little by little.

Lu Huaixi's hand was gripped tight. The child's terrified trembling came through clear and sharp.

She should have been afraid too. But instead, for some reason she could not explain, she thought of Xie Yuanjing.

If she got scared to death here, Xie Yuanjing would have no way to dissolve the marriage and remarry. He would have to become a widower first, and then take a new wife through the proper channels.

When she thought about it that way, the number of women the Xie family's First Young Master could marry had shrunk considerably.

chapters.title: Do You Want to Follow Me
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had never once thought Xie Yuanjing would come.

Back at the residence, his reaction had been perfectly clear — composed and unhurried. He had it entirely in hand.

After she had stated her choice plainly, he had shown neither surprise nor displeasure. In his usual calm tone, he had said he had an engagement that evening.

She did not know who he was meeting, but she was certain that at this hour, he should have been seated somewhere, cup in hand, exchanging pleasantries.

Even so, when she heard Gong Fei's voice — in that single instant — her pounding heart lurched to a stop.

But the strange feeling dissolved just as quickly. Lu Huaixi took the child's hand and stood up. The moment the tension broke, her legs nearly gave way, and she almost could not keep herself upright.

"Young Mistress!"

When Gong Fei found her, Lu Huaixi instinctively looked behind him.

She did not see Xie Yuanjing, and felt no particular strangeness about that. The glance she had cast was nothing more than instinct — after holding herself together through all that fear for so long, she wanted to find someone familiar to move toward.

Torchlight flooded the abandoned courtyard and made visible what the darkness had been hiding. The full scene fell into Lu Huaixi's eyes.

"Where is Yaoxu? And Ruojin?"

Her voice came out sounding steady — but only Lu Huaixi herself knew that if she said one more word, the faint tremor beneath it would be impossible to suppress.

Gong Fei did not hear it. He lowered his head and clasped his hands. "Young Mistress, please be at ease. Yaoxu and Miss Shen have both been found. My lord—"

He had not finished the sentence when new footsteps came from outside, approaching steadily at first, then growing more urgent as they drew near.

Lu Huaixi did not wait for Gong Fei to continue. Her heart began to rise with each approaching sound, beating faster and faster.

She did not know what she was waiting for.

But it was as though she was waiting for Xie Yuanjing.

She could not explain the reason. She simply wanted to see him in this cold and eerie place — to hear him speak — because without that, even with all these people around her, she was still a little afraid.

"Let's go."

Lu Huaixi pressed down the beat of her heart, and did not let herself wait.

Then her mind drifted, incongruously: Gong Fei had come, so Xie Yuanjing would not have to be a widower. Her thoughts were in chaos.

"Go to Yaoxu first. And this child—"

"Lu Huaixi."

Someone called her name. The voice was low and familiar, parting the layers of wild grass in the courtyard and falling into her ears.

Lu Huaixi was caught completely off guard. The rest of what she had been saying simply stopped.

The composure she had been holding onto quietly cracked, piece by piece. She blinked — and then, inexplicably, the faintest edge of a grievance welled up in her. Even the tips of her long lashes were tinged with a faint dampness.

"Come here."

But even as he said "come here," the person who had spoken did not stop moving.

He stepped out of the darkness, into the light that had fallen across the courtyard, and moved toward Lu Huaixi — who had not moved at all.

The child beside her was guided away by Gong Fei. Lu Huaixi did not even notice when she had let go of the child's hand.

She only kept her eyes on Xie Yuanjing as he came closer — stepping through this cold and unsettling place, past the corridor where the shadow had appeared earlier. All the clarity and caution she had been holding onto abandoned her entirely, and she lurched forward and threw herself toward him.

Xie Yuanjing raised his arms and caught her.

He patted her back, slowly and gently, one steady beat after another.

"It's all right. I'm here."

Xie Yuanjing held her tightly with one arm, lowered his head, and in the place she could not see, let out a long, long breath. The darkness that had settled deep in his eyes finally began to clear.

"Don't be afraid. We'll go back to the residence first. You can cry when we're back."

He asked nothing. Lu Huaixi had no wish to relive what had just happened either.

But the gentler he was, the more aggrieved she felt — and the more she wanted to be unreasonable.

"I am going to cry. And I'm going to cry right here."

Lu Huaixi said it flatly, her voice thick.

She did not understand why she lost control of herself like this whenever she saw Xie Yuanjing. The moment she heard him trying to comfort her, everything she had barely managed to hold together simply collapsed.

She could not even recall how she had been a moment ago — the absolute refusal to go down quietly, the determination to take someone with her if it came to that.

"I was so scared. Just now there were terrifying things — they were running, and crying, and making horrible sounds! There was a little girl beside me, and she was scared too, and she cried, and then I had to hold it in. I held it in for so long!"

Lu Huaixi did not quite know what she was saying anymore. The words came out halting and fragmented.

Like someone so aggrieved they could not stop making accusations — except that the things being accused could not be caught or held.

Xie Yuanjing's heart softened past the point of anything he could describe. He glanced to the side, and seeing that Gong Fei had already taken the child away — no one left to see her cry her face into a ruin — he could not help pulling her tighter.

"Then cry. Cry and then we'll go back."

His voice was gentle in a way that was almost unlike him. With half the torches withdrawn, the soft light of the moon had gradually revealed itself, spilling across his dark robes.

"Once you've cried, you won't be afraid anymore."

Lu Huaixi sniffed. She blinked — and the tears began to fall again.

But this time, she stopped herself from being completely careless.

Perhaps having come back to herself enough to feel embarrassed, Lu Huaixi pulled back and used her sleeve to wipe her face. Then she tilted her chin up and turned her head away.

"I wasn't afraid. I only got scared when I saw you."

"Yes. It is entirely my fault."

Xie Yuanjing felt a pang of tenderness — and underneath it, a quiet urge to laugh.

But he knew this person's temper well enough by now.

In front of others, she had the poise of a noble daughter — bright and assured, or occasionally wilful, but always measured. In private, she was all child — if she said she was unhappy, her face said it too, without any concealment, as though she fully expected someone to come and coax her.

Xie Yuanjing pressed down gently on the back of her neck, as one might soothe a startled creature, and then released her.

"Shall we go now?"

Lu Huaixi nodded.

Xie Yuanjing turned and she followed a step behind — and seeing that he was not looking, she slipped a little closer, tucking herself just beside the edge of his robe, finding the exact angle where she could not see the courtyard anymore.

Xie Yuanjing pretended he had not noticed. He let her stay close because of her fear, and privately hoped she might cling to him a little more.

But he knew very well: once this was over, Lu Huaixi's heart would harden again.

Xie Yuanjing slowed his pace. In the corner of his eye, her hand hovered uncertainly — touching the edge of his sleeve lightly, as though she wanted to take hold of it but did not dare.

He curved his lips slightly, and used the moonlight as cover to glance at her.

"Did you hear anything just now?"

"What?"

Lu Huaixi's head snapped up, fear and reliance both vivid in her eyes as she looked at him. "You heard something?"

"I'm not sure. I thought I heard a sound. Perhaps I was wrong."

Having said this, Xie Yuanjing simply reached over and took her huddled hand in his. "I'll take you out."

Lu Huaixi had never been this obedient. She nodded without hesitation, and even opened her hand of her own accord to hold his back.

Xie Yuanjing did not immediately move. He looked down for a moment, ran his thumb across the back of her hand, and then closed his fingers around hers.

In the shifting light and shadow, Xie Yuanjing's thoughts drifted to the last thing his father had said — that cold, parting laugh:

"You want her. Does she want you?"

A breeze passed through the courtyard, finding its way between the two of them with perfect timing, trailing with it a touch of cool.

Xie Yuanjing's lips moved. He spoke, as though in passing.

"Do you want to follow me, Lu Huaixi?"

chapters.title: How About I Vent Your Anger For You
chapters.content:
Outside the dilapidated old house, Gong Fei stood waiting with his men.

The little girl lingered nearby, not daring to look, frightened and timid.

When the people inside came out, her eyes instantly lit up — she wanted to run over but didn't dare, and so she stood there without moving.

"My lord. Young Madam."

Gong Fei stepped forward and bowed his head toward Xie Yuanjing.

"The criminals have been apprehended, and the injured civilians have all been taken away to have their wounds dressed. Young Master Shen is over there conducting the interrogations. He says to tell you not to get involved in this matter — when the time comes for the investigation, he will say that this lantern festival was something he arranged on a whim for someone else."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing, but his expression cooled by a few degrees.

Lu Huaixi had only caught fragments of the exchange and was a little confused.

"What does that mean — wasn't this lantern festival put on by Huiquebo?"

"To answer Young Madam, it is both yes and no."

Seeing that the person before him showed no sign of stopping him, Gong Fei continued, "The lantern festival here at Huiquebo had originally ended yesterday. Lord Shen wanted you to come admire the lanterns as an act of apology, so he spent money to add another night."

"Then why didn't Sister Ruojin say anything?"

"Miss Shen likely didn't know about it either. After all, Lord Shen did it in order to..."

"In order to what?"

Gong Fei glanced at Xie Yuanjing again. Noticing this, Lu Huaixi narrowed her eyes.

"Why do you keep looking at him? Does he know the lantern festival was fake too?"

"Young Madam misunderstands — my lord only found out not long ago himself."

Gong Fei quickly said, "Lord Shen arranged the lantern festival to give my lord the opportunity to protect Young Madam. But who could have known — before his men even had a chance to do anything, those bandits got there first."

"......"

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a moment. Something crossed her mind, and her expression became complicated and conflicted.

Xie Yuanjing gently brushed the back of her hand again, and when she looked up, he smiled at her.

"What are you thinking about?"

After a brief silence, Lu Huaixi furrowed her brow slightly and asked Gong Fei, with an air of exasperation, "Are you saying that even if those bandits hadn't shown up, he was originally planning to frighten me anyway — is that right?"

Gong Fei sorted through his thoughts, then nodded.

Simply put — yes, that was exactly right.

Lu Huaixi let out a cold laugh and pulled her hand away.

She had no intention of taking out her anger on the wrong person, but the irritation written across her face practically screamed don't come near me — and the clinging tenderness she'd shown just moments ago had vanished without a trace.

Xie Yuanjing felt a dull ache forming at his temples. He drew her back to his side. "What's wrong?"

He said softly, "Are you angry?"

"I wouldn't dare."

Lu Huaixi turned her head away, growing more agitated the more she thought about it.

"Is he apologizing to me or to you? He calls this an apology — having someone come and scare me?"

"He—"

"Didn't you say you had plans tonight? So you weren't going to come in the first place — it was only after you found out he'd set a trap that you suddenly showed up, isn't that right?"

Without waiting for him to respond, Lu Huaixi hardened her voice and continued, "I don't need you to come pick me up. And for the rest of our days — it's either him or me. Where he is, I am not. Where I am, he is not."

Xie Yuanjing's brow twitched violently several times. On one hand, he wanted nothing more than to haul Shen Zhouzhu out and beat him senseless — and on the other, he couldn't help but be amused by what Lu Huaixi had just said.

He had an almost uncontrollable urge to pull her into his arms, but there were too many people around. Without even having to think about it, he could already guess how furious she would be if he actually did it.

"I didn't have plans. Whether or not this had happened, I would have come to get you."

"Liar. Weren't those your own words?"

"They were. You turned me down so cleanly, it made me angry — so I gave myself a way out."

"You—"

Lu Huaixi stopped short.

In an instant, she remembered what had happened earlier in the day.

And then, right after that, the image surfaced in her mind — Xie Yuanjing's voice inside the house just now, low and gentle, close to her ear.

Lu Huaixi said nothing more, but the tips of her ears had started to turn red, little by little.

Seeing her like this, genuinely afraid he wouldn't be able to stop himself from doing something, Xie Yuanjing changed the subject.

"Those bandits just now — did you get a good look at any of them?"

"No. I didn't even know where I'd been pushed to in the crowd — I certainly wasn't looking at them."

He steered her into responding, and with something weighing on her mind, she didn't continue scolding Shen Zhouzhu for the moment.

"Who exactly are those people? Huiquebo is such a remote and desolate area — how did it end up drawing so many ferocious bandits? Surely they didn't come all this way just to kill people out of spite?"

"Sister, I know what they came to do."

The little girl nearby suddenly spoke up timidly, looking over at the people ahead.

"You know?"

Lu Huaixi's train of thought was interrupted. She walked over to the girl, her expression softening considerably. "Does your family live somewhere near Huiquebo?"

"Yes — my family lives in the village just over that way."

The little girl nodded.

She had been listening to them say many things she didn't understand, and it was only that last sentence that she had actually followed.

And seeing that the sister she adored had let her gathered black hair come loose, as beautiful as the immortals she'd glimpsed in paintings, much of the timidity she felt in the presence of noble people had faded away.

"A couple of years ago there were people who came to steal things at Huiquebo too, but it was nothing as frightening as today. I heard the villagers say it's because someone is selling treasures."

"Selling treasures?"

"Yes — treasures from Ghost Street."

Hearing Ghost Street mentioned again, Lu Huaixi felt more curious than she had before.

But she also knew where to draw the line. She had just been through a terrible fright, and she had no intention of going through another.

"Are the things at Ghost Street really that wonderful? Does it open every year?"

"I've never seen any real treasures myself. But a lot of the things from Ghost Street — our family has them too. The villagers don't like going to Ghost Street to look. Sometimes they dig up things they don't want, and outside merchants come from far away fighting to buy them up."

Lu Huaixi was somewhat surprised.

"Don't they go dig for themselves?"

"They can't."

The little girl said earnestly, "Our village is on the other side of the mountain. The mountain roads are hard to travel — those who go in can't get out."

"Have you ever told anyone else about this?"

"No. I'm only telling Sister. It's a secret of our village — if word gets out, others will come to take the money."

Lu Huaixi let out a breath of relief and ruffled her hair.

"When you get home, don't tell your family that you told someone."

"Alright. But Sister saved me — I want to give her a gift."

The little girl took hold of her hand. "I've secretly kept a box of things. Please come pick one, Sister."

Lu Huaixi was not particularly drawn to treasures. She disliked complications, and from what had just happened, Ghost Street was clearly a very troublesome place — anything connected to it was something she wanted nothing to do with.

But the little girl was gazing at her with such bright, earnest eyes that she found it impossible to refuse.

She thought it over and took her hand. "But I have to go home too. How about you choose one and have someone bring it to me? I'm already going to have someone see you home — would you be willing?"

The little girl was, truthfully, a little reluctant. But she seemed well accustomed to not burdening others, and she nodded without hesitation.

"I won't delay Sister from going home. What I have aren't really treasures — they're just things my family didn't want that I picked up myself. They're not worthy of Sister, but I still want to give one."

"They will be worthy. I'll love whatever you choose."

Lu Huaixi saw how truly well-behaved she was and couldn't help but sigh inwardly.

She could take this little girl away. She could give her money, let her go to school. But her help would only be of use if the person herself was also willing.

Just now, she had sensed it — even after being abandoned, everything this little girl's heart held was her family.

She raised her head. Xie Yuanjing was watching her.

"Have Gong Fei and your maidservant take her home — one to apply pressure, one to offer comfort. Her family will understand what's expected of them."

As though he knew exactly what she was thinking, Xie Yuanjing spoke to her. She was surprised for a brief moment, then nodded after a pause.

When it came to this kind of reading of people's hearts — he was indeed better at it than she was.

"Now that everyone else has been looked after, what about you?"

Xie Yuanjing watched as she raised her hand to rub her eyes. Her slender fingertips rested at the corner of her eye, and for a fleeting moment, a look of dazed exhaustion passed through her gaze. Something dark stirred in the depths of his eyes.

"Can you come home with me now?"

Seeing that Lu Huaixi was pressing her lips together without answering, he smiled with characteristic patience. "Or — how about I go find Shen Zhouzhu and vent your anger for you."

chapters.title: Can I Kiss You?
chapters.content:
Though Lu Huaixi was furious at Shen Zhouzhu for coming up with such a rotten idea, she was well aware that what had just happened was no small matter.

She wasn't about to go looking for trouble right now and delay what actually needed to be done.

"Let's put it on account for now. I want to go back to the manor."

Lu Huaixi shook her head, her voice listless.

She followed Xie Yuanjing back the way they had come, and halfway there she spotted the carriage that had pulled up to wait.

Once the taut string inside her finally loosened, exhaustion was all that was left. After seeing the little girl off, she was dazed and soft-limbed, her whole body drained — yet her hand still had a firm grip on Xie Yuanjing's sleeve.

She wouldn't let him hold her hand, but she had to hold onto something to feel at ease.

Xie Yuanjing knew she had been truly frightened. He was too consumed with tender concern to think about coaxing her into closeness.

The moment they were inside the carriage, Lu Huaixi leaned against the side wall and closed her eyes. Even when the wheels jolted a few times, she didn't open them.

But her sleep was not peaceful. Beneath her eyelids, her eyes moved faintly from time to time, and her long lashes trembled with them — as though she were trying to wake but couldn't quite break free. Only the hand pressed against Xie Yuanjing never loosened its hold.

The road in the dark was uneven, the surface cracked and split in places.

After a long silence, Xie Yuanjing finally reached out and drew her into his arms when the carriage jolted once more.

Even that much movement didn't wake her.

She only furrowed her brow in vague discomfort, her freed hand flailing restlessly until it found the front of Xie Yuanjing's robe and seized it tight — and then she stilled.

"Run... don't speak..."

Lu Huaixi's voice in her sleep was very small, threaded with a faint tremor. "Don't be afraid, don't be afraid..."

The words should have been comfort meant for someone else, yet tears were gathering slowly at the corners of her eyes.

She was terrified herself, and yet she had stood in front of others. Xie Yuanjing's chest tightened at the thought, and a shadow moved through the depths of his gaze from what had happened earlier.

"It's over. Everything is over now."

He murmured soft reassurances, his thumb pressing gently against her brow and stroking upward.

Perhaps the motion helped somehow — the tight crease between Lu Huaixi's brows eased a little, her breathing steadied, though her hand remained clenched and did not let go.

She sank deeper and deeper into sleep.

Xie Yuanjing kept his gaze lowered, watching her. He saw her lips go from pressed tight to slightly parted, and then she turned her head and nestled against his chest, searching out that spot — and even a man who had had no intentions of letting his mind wander just then found it difficult not to feel a stir.

He exhaled quietly. The arm resting at her back tightened its hold, and the more he held her, the more acutely he felt how impossibly slender her waist was.

"Clingy when you're like this, but when you're awake all you can remember is counting the days until you leave. Who taught you to be so cruel?"

Xie Yuanjing couldn't stop himself from pinching her ear. The memory of her earlier in the day, saying without a moment's hesitation that she was still waiting for her divorce, made his grip go slightly heavier.

The person in his arms let out a murmured sound.

The whole carriage was filled with the scent of her fragrance, and she, without her waking awareness to hold her back, was unconsciously pressing herself against him — warm as it was, she still insisted on being close.

Xie Yuanjing felt as though every ounce of his self-control had already been spent on Lu Huaixi, and it still wasn't quite enough.

When he caught sight of the flush creeping up her ear, his gaze settled there and did not move. He lowered his head and pressed his lips to it.

Lu Huaixi stirred, feeling a vague ticklishness.

Just then, the wheel rolled over a stone. The carriage lurched again, and the jolt nudged her eyes partway open.

But her eyes were still unfocused, and out of instinct she murmured softly, "It'll be alright, don't be afraid."

It was dark, with no lantern inside — only the light filtering in from the torches outside gave the interior any glow at all. Lu Huaixi strained to see for a long moment before her gaze finally found Xie Yuanjing's eyes.

But she was still dazed, her focus drifting and unable to settle anywhere. She struggled to close her eyes again.

Her mouth still wouldn't quiet. Half-asleep and deeply exhausted, Lu Huaixi reached out the other hand on instinct and gave a soft, light pat at the air in front of her.

"Don't be afraid. I'm here with you..."

The touch was so gentle it was like a cat's paw brushing across fabric — seemingly grazing his robe, but in truth, it traced a line across the very bottom of Xie Yuanjing's heart.

Xie Yuanjing didn't concern himself with whether she was mistaking him for the little girl from earlier, or for someone else from her dreams who needed protecting. He lowered his head, letting out a little of the feeling he carried for her.

"Having you here with me isn't enough. It's too dark outside."

His low voice was softer than usual, as though drawing someone into a response.

After he spoke, not a trace of hesitation or shame crossed his face. His gaze stayed on Lu Huaixi.

What kind of man was he?

To call him shameless would be an overstatement — but to call him upright and honorable would be nowhere near the truth.

He was the kind of man who, once he had a purpose, would not let go. He wanted to draw Lu Huaixi closer to him, and naturally, he was not going to do nothing at all.

"There's no lantern. You're the only one I can see."

The person in his arms stirred at the sound of his voice, didn't open her eyes — only let out a soft sound from somewhere in her throat.

Xie Yuanjing lowered his gaze and spoke to her again.

"This road is so long. Lu Huaixi — I'm a little afraid too."

As though these words pulled her partway out of her dream, Lu Huaixi struggled for a moment and opened her eyes a thin crack.

She looked at him — whether she could actually make him out was uncertain. Her voice came out husky. "Then I'll... keep you company and talk."

The person he thought of day and night revealed a softness she never showed when she was awake. The dependence that radiated from her was no longer tangled up in the calculations of their two families' relationship.

She was drawing close to him on instinct — and in the absence of all those complications, something existed in her that even she herself was not aware of.

To receive this kind of response had already surpassed anything Xie Yuanjing had anticipated.

Something seemed to lodge in his throat. His eyes gave away his feelings before his voice could.

After a long moment, he bent his fingers and gently brushed her face.

"Keeping me company isn't enough either. I'm still afraid."

"Then what should we do?"

Xie Yuanjing met her unfocused eyes, as though he had given it genuine thought, and then said softly, "I want to kiss you. Is that alright?"

Lu Huaixi had no capacity left to think about what wanting to kiss meant, or why he suddenly wanted to, or anything of the sort. She could barely keep her eyes open, and all she knew was that she needed to stay close to this person — only then could she feel safe.

Seeing her go silent again and nearly slip back under, Xie Yuanjing leaned in a little closer.

Their noses touched. He tilted his head slightly — and then his lips found hers.

She was too drowsy, still half-submerged in sleep, sitting there in a daze as though she hadn't fully woken from her dream. Xie Yuanjing felt not a single flicker of guilt about taking advantage of her. After pressing his lips to hers for a moment, he lightly bit her lower lip.

The person before him flinched at the small sting and let out an incredibly faint sound — which only made Xie Yuanjing, who had never made much effort to conceal his intentions, grow bolder still.

He was no longer content with the mere touch of lips. He wanted to taste more of her.

Xie Yuanjing pressed deeper, coaxing, tracing the shape of her, utterly commanding — allowing her no room to turn away.

At last the carriage rolled away from the rough, jolting ground onto a smooth stretch of road, and the lanterns hung high all along the way outside brought light into the dim interior.

Lu Huaixi held his robe in her fist, her eyes half-closed, without a trace of clarity.

"Sleep when the kiss is done."

Xie Yuanjing spoke with his lips still close against hers, lifting one hand to cover her eyes. "Once the kiss is done, there'll be nothing to fear in your dreams."

He had never taken advantage of someone in this way before — and yet now he did it with ease.

He wished he could see his own hypocrisy through to the very end and kiss her fiercely all over again.

But the person before him was genuinely fragile just then, and even after suffering such a liberty, she still hadn't fully come back to herself.

Whatever conscience Xie Yuanjing had left made his heart ache. He pulled her close and held her, and did not continue.

"There are still many days ahead. You're hard-hearted — I'll wear you down, slowly, with time."

He looked down at her curling lashes, his fingertips grazing lightly past the corner of her lips. He smiled, soft and quiet.

chapters.title: Pushing His Luck
chapters.content:
The carriage arrived back at the Marquis's manor, and only then was Lu Huaixi fully roused from sleep.

Xie Yuanjing's robe had been crumpled somewhat by her grip. She moved her lips, and in the haze of half-wakefulness something flickered through her mind.

A moment later she startled, and looked up at Xie Yuanjing.

Seeing nothing but calm on his face, without a trace of emotion, she hesitated, parted her lips — then closed them again without asking.

But Xie Yuanjing had already set his mind to this, and with his quick, fox-like intelligence, how could he possibly let her forget entirely.

He led her off the carriage and, as he did, took hold of her hand.

"What is it?"

He tilted his head to look at her. "Didn't sleep well? Did you dream of something?"

His tone was just as it always was, as though he were asking out of genuine care.

And yet in the face of that calm, Lu Huaixi was suddenly struck with unease.

She glanced at him. Seeing that his dark eyes still betrayed no emotion, she instinctively turned her head away, afraid of giving away her agitation.

"I did sleep a bit poorly."

Lu Huaixi replied in a small voice. "How is your arm? You should have woken me sooner."

When Lu Huaixi had been roused, she had been leaning against Xie Yuanjing, one hand still clutching his sleeve so tightly her fingertips had gone pale.

And so when she'd just remembered that she might have kissed him in his arms — after her panic, she told herself it must have been a dream.

But even if it had only been a dream, it was more than enough to make her unable to lift her head.

Just hours ago she had turned someone down so decisively and with such conviction — and now, just hours later, one single fright and all she could remember was to press herself close to him.

The more Lu Huaixi thought about it, the more mortified she felt — yet beneath the shame was something inexplicably settled and reassured, a tangle of emotions she couldn't begin to name.

Xie Yuanjing noticed her evasiveness. He gave no sign of it, and went along with what she'd said. "My arm went a little numb. It'll pass."

Lu Huaixi found herself even more at a loss for words.

Xie Yuanjing pushed his luck and deliberately brought it up again.

"Just now — what did you dream about?"

He walked with her along the covered corridor, knowing she wouldn't answer. His gaze drifted to the path ahead, his voice low and unhurried, carrying a faint note of something dissolute. "I had a dream too. I dreamed I kissed you."

The person beside him stumbled to a halt. Xie Yuanjing stopped with her and looked at her wide eyes.

"It wasn't like last time. This time you were very well-behaved — you let me."

"You..."

"I was holding you when I kissed you, but your waist is too slender, Lu Huaixi. Eat your meals properly from now on, or else I'll make that dream—"

"Stop talking!"

"Just one more sentence."

Xie Yuanjing leaned down toward her, completely unbothered by the shade of red her face had turned. Like a shameless libertine, he pressed his lips directly to the tip of her nose — then lowered his voice a little further.

"The next time you don't eat properly, I'll hold you in my arms, on the bed I sleep in, and kiss you just like I did in that dream."

Xie Yuanjing did not get to walk back to the courtyard with her that night.

Lu Huaixi flung his hand away, stared at him with an expression of disbelief she had never worn before, and then fled back to her courtyard on her own.

Xie Yuanjing finally had the sense to know when to stop, and followed at a retreating distance behind her.

—

After handling the situation at Huiquebo, Shen Zhouzhu rushed to find Xie Yuanjing without stopping for breath.

He couldn't fully wash his hands of this matter, and he would have to go to the palace first thing in the morning to prostrate himself in apology — but before he went, he needed to speak with Xie Yuanjing. Even knowing that this time he might well receive a beating from Eldest Young Master Xie.

The night air was cooler than it had been in the daytime. When Shen Zhouzhu arrived, there was no one in the study.

Gong Zhuo lit a lamp for him, and the look he gave Shen Zhouzhu was just as complicated as Gong Fei's had been.

Shen Zhouzhu clapped him on the shoulder and sighed. "Just say what's on your mind. Your master is brutal — who knows when the next time I'll see him will be."

"I wouldn't dare."

Gong Zhuo tugged at the corner of his mouth. Thinking back on the way his lord and the Young Madam had been with each other just now — different from anything he'd seen before — he thought that perhaps this time would not end quite so brutally.

But in the end he said nothing. After all, regardless of how things had unfolded, their Young Madam had been frightened tonight.

Xie Yuanjing arrived very late. Shen Zhouzhu had nearly nodded off before footsteps finally sounded outside.

A moment later the door was pushed open. He grabbed the cold tea on the table beside him and drank two big gulps.

He was just about to go over and speak, when the next instant he was seized by the front of his robe, and then a fist came down and sent him flying.

Shen Zhouzhu tasted something copper and sweet. He had barely lifted his hand to wipe the corner of his mouth when a ferocious palm strike came flying at him.

He took the full force of it in silence, and the table and chairs that caught his back were knocked out of place with a tremendous crash.

But how could he dare to fight back.

The fact that Xie Yuanjing had let him into the study meant that once this beating was over, the matter would be closed — he wouldn't truly cut ties with him.

But asking him to calm down easily wasn't possible either. Xie Yuanjing struck without hesitation, a severity in his eyes rarely seen.

By the end, Shen Zhouzhu's face was a patchwork of bruises and swelling before Xie Yuanjing finally stayed his hand. He stood in the middle of the study, looking down at the man sprawled on the floor gasping for breath.

"It's a good thing she wasn't hurt."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was not entirely steady either. The hand hanging at his side clenched tight for a moment, then released.

Shen Zhouzhu didn't dare make a sound or say a word.

He and Xie Yuanjing had known each other for many years — from using each other to having each other's backs, then to a place where scheming and helping were both done without much thought as to who owed whom. He knew the man before him better than almost anyone.

If it was not someone Xie Yuanjing cared about, he could watch a person die right before his eyes and not offer a single shred of mercy.

But once he took someone to heart, let anyone so much as graze them and they were courting death — let alone what had happened today, which had been so dangerous. The fact that he hadn't driven a sword through Shen Zhouzhu on the spot was already a mercy borrowed from Lu Huaixi.

"Not dead? Then get yourself up."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at him, then turned back to the table. "After this matter — until she's no longer angry at you, we don't meet."

"Come on! I'll make it up to her properly this time — I genuinely wanted to help you keep her, nothing else!"

"I don't need your help."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was cold. "If she falls ill tonight because of that fright, I will settle that debt with you separately."

It still carried pressure, but Shen Zhouzhu felt relief wash over him anyway.

If he could say that much, it meant his anger had already subsided by half. As for the other half — he would have to wear it down himself, slowly.

Shen Zhouzhu hauled himself upright, and through the ache radiating from his body, he raised a hand and tentatively touched his own face.

The next instant, his brow crumpled in pain.

"Fine, hit hard, I can take it — but why do you always go for the face?"

He raised his voice in protest. "I still have to go to the palace tomorrow. Do you want me to stand before all those court ministers looking like this — nose swollen, face black and blue?"

"If I hadn't remembered that you needed to go to the palace, they would have carried you out."

Xie Yuanjing tamped down his remaining anger and didn't bother looking at him.

He'd been measured about it. Today's incident couldn't be laid entirely at Shen Zhouzhu's feet, though his handling of things had indeed been reckless.

Besides — the injuries left behind were heavy, and highly conspicuous. Seeing them would do something to soften Lu Huaixi's anger. And even those in the palace, seeing him in such a state, wouldn't be too furious.

Thinking of Lu Huaixi, Xie Yuanjing found himself regretting having come to the study at all.

He should have stayed nearby. Even if she drove him away, he should have watched until she fell asleep before coming.

"I was reckless this time — I didn't think it through. I forgot that a place even the authorities don't want to touch is naturally not somewhere you can move on lightly. And then we really did run into a group with no regard for their own lives, and ended up dragging the two of you into it."

"You've got it wrong."

Xie Yuanjing swept a glance at him, his voice still carrying a faint chill.

"It was your sudden appearance at Huiquebo that left people unsure of your intentions. Had it not been for that, those people wouldn't necessarily have made their move at this particular time."

Shen Zhouzhu was silent for a moment, but as the logic settled in, he realized he had genuinely failed to connect the threads.

He had thought he was simply adding one more night of lanterns and leaving a few extra people to keep watch.

But in the eyes of someone paying close attention, this person who had appeared out of nowhere was a provocation — a deliberate mystery, a sign that something of value was being hidden.

Just as they were speaking, Gong Fei returned from seeing the girl home, stopping outside the door.

"My lord — the item that little girl chose has been delivered to the Young Madam. It appears to be something of some origin. The Young Madam seems quite taken with it."

"Something actually worth something?"

Shen Zhouzhu's interest was stirred.

Xie Yuanjing glanced at him, his voice flat and cold. "Even if it is — it belongs to her."

chapters.title: A Real Treasure?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi's dark hair was still slightly damp.

She sat before the bronze mirror and watched as Jing Shuang carefully dried it for her, growing drowsy.

But the moment she closed her eyes, her thoughts ran out of her control. She kept her eyes cast downward, unwilling to let too much show on her face.

Before long, the door was pushed gently open. Yao Xu lowered her head and carried in a basin of clean water to replace the damp cloths.

At this hour, there was usually idle conversation in the room, but tonight it was strangely quiet.

Lu Huaixi's thoughts had drifted to the small object just sent over and placed on the table, and she hadn't noticed anything amiss.

It was the treasure the little girl had chosen for her.

It looked like a scroll, yet it was no larger than a palm, and even rolled up as it was, the uneven edges were visible — as though something had been torn away from it at some point.

Inside was something Lu Huaixi couldn't quite make sense of. But at the edge of the scroll, she could see a painted figure — a woman in magnificent robes, with streaming ribbons caught in the wind, her form swaying with grace, as radiant as an immortal descended from the heavens.

She supposed that was probably why the little girl had chosen it for her.

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but smile.

This thing might count for nothing in someone else's eyes — but she was willing to receive the sentiment behind it, and so as far as she was concerned, it was a wonderful thing.

It wasn't long before Jing Shuang's hands stilled.

In the summer heat, long hair dried quickly.

Lu Huaixi was about to rise, intending to pick up the scroll and examine it a little more, when she looked up and found that the two women who had been standing behind her had dropped to their knees before her in unison.

"We failed in our duty today. We await your punishment, Young Madam."

Lu Huaixi was, in truth, taken aback for a moment — but no ripple crossed her face. She appeared quite composed.

The two of them pressed their foreheads to the ground again. When their brows met the floor, the sound was clear and solid, without a moment's hesitation.

A word of rise hovered at the tip of Lu Huaixi's tongue. She looked at them, and the lips she'd parted slightly closed again without a sound.

"I knew that Huiquebo was a place that called for more than ordinary vigilance, and yet I still allowed myself to be distracted and lost sight of the Young Madam. I have failed in my duty — I nearly caused something irreparable. I am guilty!"

Yao Xu pressed her forehead to the floor, her back arching in a curve, her voice trembling and thick with self-reproach.

When she finished, she knocked her head against the ground again, hard with remorse for her lapse of attention at Huiquebo. "I await your punishment, Young Madam!"

"I await your punishment as well, Young Madam!"

Jing Shuang spoke in turn.

Her composure was steady. When she bent forward to the floor, the curve of her back was lower than Yao Xu's, and each time she lifted and lowered her head, she returned to exactly the same position.

Lu Huaixi watched them in silence. After a long while, her fingertips finally moved, coming to rest against the surface of the table.

"You have been with me the longest. You know that I have never liked to punish people."

Lu Huaixi looked at Yao Xu and pressed down the instinct toward softness.

On the way back earlier, she hadn't thought about punishment. Once her heart had settled, she'd thought about it even less — and even after learning that Shen Zhouzhu had originally planned to frighten her, she had only been angry for a brief moment.

But now, with both of them kneeling before her, she suddenly understood — some things could not be let go too lightly.

There were eyes everywhere. The eyes of others, and the eyes these two women turned on themselves.

"This incident came on suddenly, and the fault cannot fall entirely on the two of you — but a mistake cannot go unaddressed.
