Starting today, three months of deducted wages as a light punishment and a strong reminder. For the next two days, other maids will take your place — you two are relieved of close attendance."

More than the loss of wages, being replaced in attendance was the truer punishment.

Yao Xu's eyes immediately reddened. She panicked so much that tears nearly fell.

"I accept my guilt! I am willing to accept any punishment! Please give me another chance, Young Madam — do not send me away. I want to serve by your side!"

From the moment she had come to serve Lu Huaixi, she had never once been away. No matter how angry Lu Huaixi had been, she had never let anyone replace her.

Yao Xu had never once imagined that there might come a day in her life when she could no longer follow Lu Huaixi. She would sooner take a caning than lose the right to serve at her side.

Jing Shuang pressed her lips tight, the color draining from her face.

Her failure today had already been treated as a serious offense in Gong Fei's reckoning — and yet the Young Madam before her now offered her words that hardly constituted a punishment at all. That, somehow, made it harder to bear.

"Young Madam, I too accept my punishment willingly. Please do not replace me!"

Lu Huaixi said nothing, and gave no sign of changing her mind.

Yao Xu had been with her too long — attentive and thoughtful, the most trusted person at her side. But precisely because it had been so long, she had in many things grown too comfortable. Too easy.

She had no real intention of letting her go. But she intended to use this to deliver a quiet reminder.

And as for Jing Shuang — had she not intervened, whatever punishment she faced from Gong Fei's side would certainly have been far harsher. Now that she had become her maidservant, she would naturally be treated the same as Yao Xu.

Sounds drifted in from outside — the voices of maids offering their greetings broke through the silence in the room.

A moment later the door was pushed open and Xie Yuanjing stepped in.

His gaze moved first to Lu Huaixi at the bronze mirror, then fell to the two figures kneeling on the floor. A faint edge of severity passed through his eyes.

Lu Huaixi glanced at him as well, but didn't speak first.

"Is the punishment done?"

Xie Yuanjing settled into a seat not far from her. The darkness in his eyes hadn't dispersed, and though he didn't look at the two women on the floor again, the pressure emanating from him was unmistakable.

"You heard everything. Why ask."

Lu Huaixi gave no reaction to the displeasure she could read in his brow, and gestured for Yao Xu and Jing Shuang to rise. "You may go. Think carefully over the next two days."

Seeing her this way, Xie Yuanjing made no further objection. He simply picked up the item on the table and began looking at it.

"Handing down punishment deliberately for me to hear?"

He smiled lightly, with a look of quiet significance. "You knew I was coming."

Lu Huaixi rose from the stool in front of the bronze mirror, not making any attempt to hide it. "More or less — but if you truly intended to punish them, you would have said something when we arrived."

He hadn't. That meant he was waiting to see what she would do.

"In my house, the words 'light punishment and strong reminder' don't exist."

Xie Yuanjing paused and then said, "But your maids are not my place to speak about. If I truly punish them, you'll have no one you trust to attend you."

His words were cold, leaving little room for leniency — and yet after speaking, he lowered his gaze back to the object in his hand. "But this is the only time. If it proves useless again and again, then they'll be replaced."

By now, Lu Huaixi had a rough read on his temperament. She wasn't right every time, but she could generally get the shape of it.

Take this moment, for example. She had in fact sensed his arrival when he came, and she had in fact said the words of punishment deliberately for him to hear. But she knew Xie Yuanjing wouldn't be angry.

His intention too had been to issue a warning — and he had left the matter to her.

Lu Huaixi sat down in the spot beside him, gave a quiet sound of acknowledgment, and found herself reluctant to look at him — yet kept catching herself wanting to guess what expression he wore right now.

Her own mood was beyond her, and in the middle of puzzling over it, the person beside her spoke first.

"This object is likely something useful. Keep it safe, and bring it back for your father to look at."

Lu Huaixi's attention snapped back immediately, and she looked toward the scroll.

"A real treasure?"

"Hard to say."

Xie Yuanjing said, "These two marked locations — I've seen them somewhere else."

He passed the item back to her and met her eyes. "If it is what I'm thinking, this thing could be sent into the palace. But don't let anyone know — don't mention it to a soul."

Lu Huaixi picked it up and held it to the light.

There was something that looked like a route marked on it, but the markers left behind made no sense to her — like totems, or perhaps a cipher.

"Don't you want it?"

She studied it with keen interest, but in the end couldn't make anything out. "I still think the painting on the side is the prettier part."

"That is a tomb guardian."

"A tomb guardian? I thought it was an immortal in flight." Lu Huaixi looked up in surprise. "How do you know?"

Xie Yuanjing was amused by her. The warmth in his eyes deepened almost without his notice. "I guessed — which is why we need your father to have a look."

"Then if it really is something valuable, what happens?"

"What do you mean, what happens?"

"Does it count as my father's, or as yours?"

Xie Yuanjing hadn't expected her to still be thinking of him. He schooled his expression somewhat, his fingertips tapping idly, and the look he gave her carried a hint of meaning. "You won't even speak to me, and you're still thinking about whether something might count as mine?"

Xie Yuanjing had barely said it before the reminder brought everything back to Lu Huaixi — all his audacious words from before.

The smile faded from her face. She took the object with her and went into the inner room.

chapters.title: She Actually Wanted to Wait For Him to Come Back Before Sleeping
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had a guilty conscience.

She felt that the dream she'd had in the carriage had been far too bold and reckless — and so faced with Xie Yuanjing's unguarded mouth, what she felt more than anything was embarrassment curdling into anger.

But she couldn't afford to show weakness.

She had barely stepped inside, however, before the shameless man followed her in.

The beaded curtain swayed as strand after strand brushed against each other, the soft and delicate sound falling with precise effect into a listener's heart, evoking something suggestive and intimate without quite meaning to.

Xie Yuanjing didn't tease her further. He stopped not far from where she stood.

"Once Ghost Street opens — do you want to go?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi shook her head quickly. When it came to serious matters, she had never been one to let her emotions color her judgment. "I don't chase that kind of dangerous excitement. And even if I actually laid eyes on a treasure, I wouldn't necessarily be able to take it."

With that, she held up the scroll. "This is already wonderful. Whether it turns out to be a treasure or not — I like it very much."

"Then keep it for yourself."

Xie Yuanjing watched her narrow her eyes, any trace of her earlier anger forgotten the moment the scroll came up. He was quiet for a moment.

"There's no need for the Lù family to take risks for this. Huiquebo has me — there's no reason to gamble with something you care about to gain anything. Rather than giving this away for some advantage, I'd rather see you happy. Lu Huaixi — don't go around thinking the only thing to do is avoid me."

Words like these, once spoken, would naturally strike listeners as startling and laughable.

Shen Zhouzhu would probably jab a finger at him after too many drinks and shout — oh, so you've come to this, Xie Yuanjing.

He knew it himself. If the scroll truly was what he suspected — one piece of a larger whole — sending it into the palace would almost certainly earn the emperor's attention. From there, he could use it to consolidate more power, and gradually draw it back into his own hands.

Before, regardless of whether the thing was genuine or not, he would have taken it the moment he had it and sorted out the truth later.

But now—

Compared to all those vague and shifting ambitions, it seemed he would rather watch the bright light that came into Lu Huaixi's eyes when she saw something she loved.

He had simply fallen in love with her.

"Don't keep saying things like that."

Lu Huaixi blinked. After the initial surprise came something like flustered confusion, and she turned away from his words. "I just like the woman in the painting. She looks as though she's dancing. Very beautiful."

"I know. So you keep it. I don't want it — and your father loves you. He won't want it either."

"But..."

Lu Huaixi found herself genuinely at a loss for words in that moment. In her eyes, Xie Yuanjing had always been clear-headed and composed.

His purposes had always been plain. His actions had never been colored by anything besides those purposes.

And yet right now, without even confirming what the item actually was, he had let go of what sounded like a rather significant fragment of a scroll.

Lu Huaixi couldn't quite be certain — she didn't know whether he was tricking her again.

But somehow, she found herself leaning more toward believing that Xie Yuanjing was giving this up because of her.

"You really don't want it? What if it turns out to be useful?"

"Useful things can still go unused. More than this object — I'd rather you remember something good about me."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her. Seeing her tilt her head up with that earnest expression, he couldn't help but think of the carriage — her drowsy, unguarded, pliant self.

The eldest branch of the Lù family had raised her well. She had the poise of a highborn young lady for the outside world — composed, graceful, sometimes gentle and sometimes cool — yet somewhere inside her, there had always remained a space of pure, unclouded goodness.

Even when she deliberately steeled herself, her soft-hearted nature was always hidden just beneath.

And yet her kindness had its limits. She never lost herself to it, never let herself be led astray, and her judgment was of the finest sort.

Xie Yuanjing felt genuinely grateful that he had walked into the Lù family with less-than-pure intentions, all those years ago.

"Alright — do you realize your eyes are practically closing right now? Either keep talking with me about what happened in the carriage during that dream, or go to sleep."

Seeing that the person before him still hadn't recovered the vitality she'd had before leaving the manor, her complexion still without its usual bloom, Xie Yuanjing reached out and touched her face lightly, then pressed his hand to her forehead.

Confirming nothing was wrong, he withdrew his hand and stood.

"You don't need to worry about tomorrow's affairs either. I know you've been letting Lù Tangshu bring trouble on herself — you've done exactly the right amount. I'll handle what's left."

He gave a few more instructions, saw the drowsiness rise in her again, and quietly talked down the urge to move closer. He didn't linger.

"Get some sleep. I'm heading out — get changed."

The corners of Lu Huaixi's lips pressed together. She watched him step out of the inner room, then cross past the daybed, and he was almost at the outer door — her hand on the thin coverlet curled inward and gripped it, without thinking.

The empty room was already a little frightening. The dilapidated old house she'd all but put out of her mind drifted back in front of her eyes.

And then the strange swaying of the weeds. The dark shapes she hadn't been able to make out at all.

After letting her thoughts run to their end, Lu Huaixi called out to him, reckless with resignation.

"Where are you going?"

Xie Yuanjing stopped and turned. The expression on his face was hard to read in the light.

The lamplight traced the outline of his tall, upright figure. Both hands hung at his sides, and the sash beneath his broad shoulders marked out a trim, narrow waist.

Lu Huaixi had been held by him. She knew how that waist felt — lean and firm, and even the lightest touch revealed the solid strength beneath.

"Where are you going?"

Lu Huaixi fought down the sudden heat rushing to her face and asked again.

"To bathe and change."

Xie Yuanjing answered her, something in his tone carrying a meaning she couldn't quite place. "I'll come back once you've lain down."

Come back once she'd lain down — meaning he would wait until she'd changed before returning.

Lu Huaixi said nothing more. Though she couldn't make out his face clearly, she instinctively glanced away to avoid his eyes.

Soon there was no trace of Xie Yuanjing left in the room.

Lu Huaixi lay in bed turning from side to side. The drowsiness that had been pressing down on her moments ago had vanished without a trace.

She was restless and vaguely unsettled, and then she realized with a sudden jolt of awareness — she actually wanted to wait for Xie Yuanjing to come back before she fell asleep.

chapters.title: Dog Eat Dog
chapters.content:
Lù Tangshu's appointment fell on the day right after Huiquebo.

Lu Huaixi had no intention of going, and therefore no intention of leaving the manor.

She woke somewhat late that morning. By the time she rose, Xie Yuanjing was already long gone from the room — but a small peach-wood sword left beside her pillow reminded her that she had, in fact, waited for him to return last night before falling asleep.

She still remembered it clearly. It was the height of summer, and when he came in, the cool dampness of his bath had not yet left him.

When he placed the object beside her pillow, he leaned slightly over her, carrying the clean, fresh scent of someone just out of the bath.

Lu Huaixi had feigned sleep and said nothing — but then, without warning, that shameless man had lowered his head and kissed her. When he finally pulled back, he even laughed quietly, his low voice sending a hum through her ears.

She held her breath and refused to make a sound. Xie Yuanjing didn't call her out on it.

It was only when Lu Huaixi was about to break under the strain of pretending that he finally touched her brow, rose to his feet, and turned away.

The moment his back was to her, Lu Huaixi stole a glance with one half-open eye.

With the lamps extinguished, the room was dim — but she could still make out, in that darkness, the lines of Xie Yuanjing's form beneath his inner robe, the power in his silhouette unmistakable.

In an instant, she was reminded of the warmth of his arm pressing against her body when he had kissed her just now — and the solid firmness she had felt.

Xie Yuanjing lay down not long after, and only then did Lu Huaixi finally dare to breathe a long, quiet breath.

She curled her fingers slowly into the thin coverlet. In hindsight, she realized that just moments ago, she had felt nothing but startled panic — not a single trace of resistance.

That wasn't exactly a good thing. After coming fully back to herself, Lu Huaixi furrowed her brow slightly and let her gaze drift toward the low bed where Xie Yuanjing had slept.

A soft knock came at the outer door, followed by a maid's voice announcing hot water.

Lu Huaixi snapped back to the present, remembering that different maids had been sent in to attend to her these past two days.

She answered and let them in.

—

Lù Tangshu didn't grow impatient and leave the house until late afternoon.

She had spent most of the day looking through portrait after portrait of eligible men, and the only one she found even remotely satisfying was Zhou Jieyu, the eldest young master of the Zhou family.

She hadn't put much thought into the Zhou family specifically — it was simply that Zhou Jieyu himself was the one she found tolerable. She had even stopped wanting to look further. The elder branch had listened to their grandfather and backed off from pressing her, but her mother still wouldn't permit her to stop.

Her mother was still afraid that the elder branch might suddenly dream up some new scheme to harm her.

Until the matter of the list was resolved once and for all, she needed to secure an escape route first.

"Go tell Mother — if nothing better than the Zhou family turns up after this, she needn't keep sending anyone. I'm tired of looking at them."

Lù Tangshu said this in a cold, flat tone, then turned to the maidservant beside her. "Do you even know how to use that fan? Can't you see the breeze isn't even reaching my head?"

She shot the girl a withering look, then stepped out into the courtyard with the summer heat beating down.

The maid didn't dare dawdle and hurried after her.

"In heat like this — if that useless wretch can't even handle one woman, I'll make sure he can't stay in the He family either, sooner or later!"

Lù Tangshu was thoroughly baked and seething with irritation, still muttering curses even after she'd climbed into the carriage.

Before long, the wheels began to roll, swaying as they went.

The place she had chosen was a teahouse on the western side of the city that had only opened at the beginning of the year.

Because of its somewhat out-of-the-way location, the rent was cheap. The proprietor had used what it would cost for half a courtyard in the east of the city to buy this entire building outright in the west. The front served tea and meals; the back offered lodgings. It had a decent reputation in the western district.

The western quarter was not as wealthy as the east — it had more poor people, and more villagers coming in from the surrounding countryside.

Under ordinary circumstances, it didn't matter how grand a teahouse was — if it was in the west of the city, Lù Tangshu wouldn't have been caught dead there.

But today was different. She had specifically chosen this place because she wanted to see Lu Huaixi's reputation destroyed in a district she looked down upon, wanted her to be seen by exactly the kind of people she looked down upon, and talked about.

Beyond that, the western quarter was a more natural setting for bandits and ruffians to appear.

The eastern side had too many informants, and security was too tight. It wasn't safe for her and He Jianhang's people to move there. Otherwise, she would have much preferred to stage her performance in the crowded east — a scene of a noble girl sacrificing herself to save her sister, a touching display of deep sisterly devotion.

The carriage rode on for a long time. There was little wind, and the interior was stuffy and stifling.

Just as Lù Tangshu was about to boil over, the rocking carriage finally slowed and came to a stop.

She shoved the maid's fanning hand aside, yanked open the curtain, and leapt down.

The teahouse was occupied by a scattering of customers — ordinary folk who clearly had little money to spare.

A flash of contempt crossed Lù Tangshu's eyes. She had just raised her handkerchief to cover her nose when she happened to notice the woman stepping out of a narrow, battered carriage parked nearby.

Wu Wenlian.

Lù Tangshu's gaze lingered on the teahouse for a moment, then shifted to look at the small shop beside it.

She let out a brief, scornful laugh, her thoughts turning to everything she knew about Wu Wenlian's scheming. She walked straight toward her.

"Miss Wu."

She called out to her, the look in her eyes openly mocking. "You really do have a cold heart, Miss Wu — for all that you were supposed to be close as sisters. My Second Sister may be useless in many ways, but she was always generous with you. And yet here you are, so eager to move against her."

"Third Miss Lù."

A flicker of unease crossed Wu Wenlian's face when she saw her, but she quickly steadied herself, dipped into a curtsy, and lowered her head.

"I'm afraid I don't quite follow Third Miss Lù's meaning. I'd arranged to come to the western quarter today to go shopping with a close friend, but she had something come up at the last minute and left early. I'm just having a look around on my own — I didn't expect to run into Third Miss Lù."

"What are you putting on that act for? I'm not the naive fool that Lù Huaixi is."

Lù Tangshu cut her off. The unconcealed contempt in her voice made Wu Wenlian's expression tighten with growing humiliation.

"Do you really think I couldn't read between the lines of those little hints you let slip to me before? If the person you wanted rid of hadn't happened to be the same person I wanted gone, I'd have had you dealt with a long time ago — with your paltry schemes. Did you even stop to think what you are, daring to use me like that?"

The hands hidden in Wu Wenlian's sleeves clenched tight. The color drained from her lips.

People nearby had begun to look over. Kneeling there with her head bowed before Lù Tangshu, she felt as though she looked exactly like one of her servants.

"I'm afraid I don't understand what Third Miss Lù means, nor do I know when I displeased her enough to deserve such treatment. My conduct has always been proper — though my station is somewhat lower, I have never—"

"Proper conduct? Don't make me sick."

Lù Tangshu had no patience for the performance. She held her hand out behind her, and the maid placed a purse into it immediately.

"I've heard you come to the western quarter quite often. What, are you really that poor?"

She sneered. "There are quite a few banquets coming up — flower-viewing parties, poetry gatherings — the only chance you'll have to redeem yourself in your stepmother's eyes. But you've stirred up such a mess lately, I'd wager you can't even afford a decent piece of jewelry to wear. And that outfit you have on right now... even my maids wouldn't bother with it."

With that, Lù Tangshu weighed the purse in her hand, then dropped it onto the ground. Her foot even nudged it idly with the toe of her shoe.

"There's enough inside to outfit yourself several times over in the finest things. If you want it — get on your knees and pick it up. Then beg me nicely, and say what I want to hear."

This kind of humiliation was no different from a stinging slap across the face.

And yet Wu Wenlian couldn't deny that Lù Tangshu had struck a sore nerve.

With Lu Huaixi's cold shoulder, she had fallen out of favor at home. If she couldn't find a way to distinguish herself, she would remain forever crushed underfoot in the Wu household, with no hope of ever rising again.

"What? Too proud?"

Lù Tangshu gave a mocking smile. "Fine, don't kneel then. I have plenty of people to give silver to — I'm not standing here waiting for you. I still have to go inside and have tea with that old friend of yours."

The moment the words left her mouth, just as Lù Tangshu turned to go, Wu Wenlian seemed to throw caution to the wind. She bit down hard and dropped to her knees.

The hand she reached out trembled slightly. Once her fingers closed around the purse, she gripped it with bone-white knuckles.

Lù Tangshu couldn't see her face, only hear her voice, pressed tight against the threat of a choked sob.

"Wenlian is grateful for Third Miss Lù's generosity."

"It's loose change. Feeding a dog costs more than this. Consider it a tip for a servant."

Seeing that she had actually knelt, Lù Tangshu looked at her the way one might look at something filthy — with unconcealed revulsion — yet she was still smiling, arrogant and dismissive.

"Since you've taken my silver, do you now understand clearly what I said to you a moment ago?"

chapters.title: This Is What He Looks Like When He's Truly Angry
chapters.content:
Wu Wenlian held herself together, biting the tip of her tongue to force down the humiliation.

She stopped pretending and answered in a very small voice. "I understand clearly, Third Miss Lù."

"Good. You don't need to put on a show in front of me about wanting Lù Huaixi brought low. I know."

Lù Tangshu finished speaking and gave her another look. "Right then. Since you're already here, stand over to the side and watch. You've been waiting for this long enough — if you don't see it with your own eyes, you won't feel satisfied."

Wu Wenlian waited until she had gone before standing.

A carriage at the side had blocked some of the view, shielding her from the worst of her shame — but she had still catalogued every moment of it.

Her knees ached dully. Wu Wenlian clutched the purse in a death grip and made her way back to the battered carriage reserved for the Wu household's servants.

Alone at last, her complexion was somewhat better than it had been outside.

She bowed her head and tipped the silver out of the purse to count. There were gold melon seeds as well — truly enough for several outfits worthy of being seen in public.

When she finished counting, Wu Wenlian suddenly laughed. Her eyes turned cold and dark, nothing like the pitiful creature she had appeared to be outside.

Lù Tangshu really deserved to die. But someone that deserving of death was also, genuinely, a fool.

How convenient — once this sisterly bloodbath was over, once Lù Huaixi's air of untouchable superiority was shattered, the next one to be talked about would be Lù Tangshu herself.

Arrogant, domineering, and carrying the taint of conspiring against her own sister. Neither of them would escape it.

She was still savoring her resentment when the carriage suddenly lurched into motion.

Wu Wenlian started. She had barely lifted the curtain to look out before someone shoved it back with a palm strike that knocked the breath from her.

—

"Ouch—"

Lu Huaixi was jabbed by the needle. A small bead of blood welled at her fingertip.

She frowned, half wanting to cry out in pain but feeling it wasn't quite worth it.

The maid attending her hesitated a moment, then stepped forward and offered a gentle suggestion.

"Young Madam, the sun is much gentler now — it isn't nearly as harsh as midday. Perhaps you might rest a little and take a stroll in the courtyard?"

Lu Huaixi looked at what she was holding. She had spent half a shichen without managing to embroider so much as a single bamboo leaf. She finally gave in and set it aside.

She rose and stepped out of the room, and the first thing she saw was Yao Xu and Jing Shuang waiting in the covered walkway, not daring to come too close.

They had been told not to attend her inside, yet neither of them was willing to go far. They just stayed there, side by side, heads bowed and ears tuned to every sound from within the room, occasionally leaning in to whisper instructions to the maids who were going back and forth.

Lu Huaixi had not been unaware.

As the sky gradually deepened toward evening, she walked in the courtyard and let them fall in behind her.

Before long, someone stopped at the entrance to the courtyard with what appeared to be news to report. Lu Huaixi watched as Jing Shuang went over and then brought the person forward.

"Young Madam — Wu Wenlian has been taken away by the Young Master's people."

The man bowed and said, "Outside a teahouse in the western quarter. Before she was taken, Lù Tangshu also made her kneel there and beg for mercy."

Lu Huaixi had been absently touching a flower that had just come into bloom — brilliant and pretty, but the summer heat meant it would not last more than two days before it fell.

At his words, her fingertips stilled on the petal. When she raised her hand again, she accidentally took the whole flower with it.

She blinked, standing there with it in her hand, not knowing where to put it.

"Lù Tangshu made her kneel in public?"

"Yes — and the spot wasn't well shielded. Just a worn-down carriage to one side. A fair number of people saw it."

Lu Huaixi had already given up saying how foolish it was.

This was the first time she had ever seen someone make such a spectacle of themselves before committing a crime.

"Leave her to it. What about He Jianhang?"

"Young Madam, the He family's people don't have much time left to strut about. The Young Master has gone to the western quarter himself and told us to return to the manor ahead of him."

—

Lù Tangshu and He Jianhang had waited a long time for this day. Both of them had their eyes fixed on Lù Huaixi.

One wanted to see her reputation destroyed, to have the world mock and despise her. The other wanted her person — not just to have her stay with him, but to have the elder branch of the Lù family give him their support as well.

The invitation had been sent personally by Lù Tangshu. She didn't dare rashly abandon Lu Huaixi and give people anything to talk about, so He Jianhang had hired a group of ruthless hired thugs with no care for their own lives.

The plan was simple: in the chaos, stage a scene where she was knocked unconscious while trying to save her sister — and then use the opportunity to have someone abduct Lù Huaixi.

Once she was found, Lu Huaixi's reputation would be ruined beyond repair. And Lù Tangshu, wounded and full of self-reproach, would have nothing to answer for.

Lù Tangshu sat in the private room of the teahouse, suppressing her impatience as she waited for Lù Huaixi.

By the time the sky had darkened another shade, there was finally movement outside.

She sprang to her feet, nearly wanting to throw the cup of tea in her hands straight at the door.

"Second Sister is certainly precious — the nerve of her making someone wait this long just for tea. This woman who married into a—"

The words died on her lips. A woman stepped through the door — ordinary looking, holding a teapot, but with a face that carried an unmistakable cold severity.

Lù Tangshu's expression immediately fell.

In the next instant, a deep unease rose in her chest. She was about to call for help when the woman jabbed a needle into her neck and then struck her with a swift, clean blow.

When Lù Tangshu came to again, she was in a room that smelled faintly of incense.

Her hands and feet were bound so she couldn't move. Even her mouth had been stuffed, and she couldn't make a sound.

At first she was frantic, struggling without stop, trying to work free of the ropes — but before long she became aware of a spreading heat through her body, an aching, tingling, crawling sensation moving outward from somewhere deep within.

It was as though small creatures were gnawing at her from the inside. The sensation was unbearable.

Then someone entered the room.

When Lù Tangshu saw Xie Yuanjing appear in front of her and take a seat, she felt both panicked and relieved at once.

Whether it was instinct or that the burning sensation was simply too much to bear, she began moving toward him.

It was agonizingly slow. She was frantic — and yet she managed, little by little, to drag herself closer.

Xie Yuanjing did not move aside. Since entering, he had not once looked at her.

Just as she was about to touch the hem of his robe, someone at the side raised a sword and forced her back.

A moment later, someone stepped forward and pulled the gag from Lù Tangshu's mouth.

"Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, save me—"

"How does the medicine taste?"

Xie Yuanjing finally looked up, his expression ice cold. "Such refined tastes — even keeping this on your maid's person."

"No — it's not — brother-in-law, I don't know about any of this—"

The moment Lù Tangshu had laid eyes on Xie Yuanjing, she had known that her scheme had likely been exposed.

But her mind was already beginning to unravel. She could think of nothing except her desperate, all-consuming urge to move toward him.

"Help me, brother-in-law... Xie Yuanjing, I'm not worse than Lù Huaixi. She can't compare to me. She can't—"

"You dare compare yourself to her?"

A cold laugh fell. Xie Yuanjing said it lightly, his eyes darkening.

He sat back in his wooden chair, said it, then tilted his head slightly. A moment later someone dragged a figure in from outside.

It was He Jianhang, still unconscious, his brows drawn tight in discomfort, face flushed, breathing labored — clearly he had been dosed some time ago.

Outside the door, someone else lingered beside Gong Zhuo — dressed in the clothes of a young manservant, but noticeably slighter than the others.

"Young Madam — perhaps... you should not go inside?"

Gong Zhuo was visibly uncomfortable with the situation.

He was worried that the person before him might be frightened by what lay inside, sending the carefully gained closeness of recent days tumbling back to square one. He had been conflicted for some time.

"The He fellow was nothing but the architect of his own destruction. Our lord does strike hard as a rule, but he would never raise a hand against someone like that without cause."

"I know. I won't go in."

Lu Huaixi stood where she was. She had just caught Xie Yuanjing's words as he spoke in her defense.

But the voice that carried them — cold and cutting, a tone she had never once heard from him — was nothing like anything she had known. Like a demon from the depths of hell. Even when it smiled, it felt like a summons to the grave.

This was Xie Yuanjing in true fury.

This was the face he wore when he stripped away the aloof mask he showed the world — the face of someone genuinely and deeply ruthless.

chapters.title: Did You Put On the Fragrance?
chapters.content:
When the news of Lu Huaixi's impending betrothal had first spread, she had heard no shortage of rumors about Xie Yuanjing.

Some had been gathered by her elder brother; others had come through Yao Xu from people outside.

The rumors were all much the same — this eldest young master was not a particularly virtuous man. Deep and calculating by nature, cold and distant toward people, not someone easy to get along with.

At the time, Lu Huaixi had met him a few times.

Her heart had been in her throat for the first two encounters. After that, whenever she saw him again, she never found him as frightening as his reputation suggested.

Even knowing that Xie Yuanjing was not a soft-hearted person and that he certainly had his own calculations, she still found him gentle, thoughtful, and easy to talk to.

But just now she had heard him speak in a voice she had never heard before — giving the order, in that tone, to have the unconscious He Jianhang dragged inside. And it struck her with sudden, sharp clarity that she actually knew very little about Xie Yuanjing.

What was more, because of his pleasant, unguarded surface, she had grown careless about danger even in a place where she ought to have been on guard.

Lu Huaixi stood outside without moving. She had no intention of going in.

Her lips pressed together gently, then softened and parted. She lowered her eyes and listened to the sounds inside with a composed expression.

The room went quiet for a beat when He Jianhang was dragged in — but it wasn't long before sound returned, shrill and unhinged.

"No — don't be fooled by Lù Huaixi! Don't let her deceive you! She and He Jianhang — they—"

Lù Tangshu's voice had a rawness to it she never had on normal days, and yet the force of her shouting made it cut through clearly anyway.

She glanced at the figure on the floor, not yet fully conscious, and shook her head with wild desperation. A strange flush crept up her face.

"She and He Jianhang were involved long before your engagement was settled! She has been using you all along! And even after the wedding, she and He Jianhang were still meeting in secret — unclean dealings — she has been deceiving you the whole time!"

Lù Tangshu's breathing grew labored, and her eyes were starting to lose their focus.

But she still stared at the man across from her with a hunger that consumed her entirely — full of resentment and malice, and a thin thread of hope.

"Today was He Jianhang who told me to come. They wanted to use my name to meet in secret — I was forced into all of this! But I'm willing to let you know the truth... Lù Huaixi has no real feelings for you at all. All she wanted was this marriage. I'm different, Xie Yuanjing — I'm different—"

Even knowing every word of it was false, just hearing those two names spoken in the same breath made Xie Yuanjing's temper flare.

The hand toying idly with the medicine vial went still. His fingertips moved unhurriedly over the gourd-shaped stopper. His expression didn't change, but the darkness in his eyes deepened with every passing second.

"Real feelings? Whatever she wants I can give her. Who do you think you are, to have any say about her feelings?"

He spoke at an unhurried pace, the corner of his mouth curving in a cold, sharp arc. "That Lù surname of yours has kept your life intact — consider it your good fortune. But you and He Jianhang — do you think trash like you deserves to be mentioned in the same breath as someone who belongs to me?"

"No — that's not how it is—"

Lù Tangshu was already losing her grip on clarity, but his words still drew a surge of violent rage from somewhere deep inside.

Her eyes went fierce, but they couldn't hold steady in one place. She looked like a soul unmoored — deranged and scattered.

"You've been bewitched by her — she's clouded your mind! You've been deceived by her! She only wanted to avoid being sent to the palace — she was just—"

"It wasn't her who wanted to avoid the palace. It was I who didn't want her in the palace. This marriage — I tricked her into it."

Xie Yuanjing said it coldly, then tossed the medicine vial in his hand to the guard at his side.

The guard caught it, uncorked it, and forced Lù Tangshu's jaw open.

"You prepared the medicine yourself — have a little more of it. Though if I'm honest — you really are different. Your character is so base that killing you would dirty my hands. I didn't want her eyes contaminated by the sight of either of you, so I came here personally."

When he finished speaking, someone carried in a basin of water and poured it over the figure on the floor.

He Jianhang wrenched his eyes open in pain, his gaze red-rimmed and glazed with the raw, animalistic instinct of a creature stripped of reason.

Lù Tangshu was gagging and coughing from being force-fed, sprawled on the floor gasping for air.

A slow wave of terror began to spread through her. The pain in her jaw brought her a few degrees more clarity than she'd had before.

She tried to struggle, but found she had not a shred of strength left.

"Let go of me — let go — Xie Yuanjing, save me — I am a daughter of the Lù family, the Third Miss of the Lù family! Who dares—"

"The Lù family having a daughter like you — that's just the misfortune written into their fate."

Xie Yuanjing paid her no more attention and rose to his feet. He walked to the incense burner, casually picking up the powder on the side and tipping it in.

"Have you ever seen a person skinned alive?"

He said it without inflection. "Both of you should count yourselves fortunate that this filth never touched her. Because if it had, the next lantern festival would have had blood-soaked human-skin lanterns — made from the two of you, with your names written across them."

The scent in the room began to sharpen.

They could no longer be counted on to hear much of anything clearly. But the cold emanating from Xie Yuanjing still reached them where they lay on the floor, and made them tremble with fear.

Before long, Xie Yuanjing finished arranging the incense.

With the casual ease of a man in his own study, he set down what he was holding and accepted a handkerchief from someone to wipe his hands.

"Keep track of the time."

He walked out of the room. Not long after, the only people left inside were Lù Tangshu and He Jianhang.

As the door swung shut, the sounds from within grew loud and violent. Xie Yuanjing stood just outside, as though he heard none of it. His face was expressionless.

"Spread word about those hired thugs and draw the authorities in to have them all arrested."

When he left that place, Xie Yuanjing noticed Gong Zhuo standing not far from the building's entrance, with a carriage stopped nearby.

He didn't know who was inside the carriage — but with Gong Zhuo keeping watch outside, it had to be someone he couldn't afford to avoid.

His brow furrowed slightly as he walked over.

As he drew near, the curtain was pushed back. Lu Huaixi was sitting inside.

She was in the clothes of a young manservant. Her lowered head lifted at the sound of his approach, a small face half-hidden in the shadows, her expression not quite readable.

Xie Yuanjing's expression shifted slightly. Before he could say a word, she turned her head to the side and pretended to be annoyed.

"You took forever! You've never taken this long going to meet Shen Zhouzhu!"

Xie Yuanjing could see perfectly well that she was covering something up.

In an instant, what had happened inside that room flashed through his mind. He wasn't certain how much she had seen — and he didn't know whether, if she had seen it, it would have left her afraid of him, or made her want to put more distance between them.

But then he softened his expression, bent down, and stepped into the carriage.

"What brought you here?"

He reached out and drew her toward him. "Were you worried about me?"

Lu Huaixi fell against him and quickly tilted her chin up, turning to the side with an air of exaggerated disdain. "You stink — the incense you've picked up smells absolutely foul."

The hand resting at her waist did not release her.

Xie Yuanjing pressed his nose against the side of her neck and confirmed what he had suspected: she had gone inside, if only briefly.

She had seen what happened in that room — and had likely also come across He Jianhang being dragged in — which was why she had picked up such a faint, faint trace of that scent.

But she didn't bring it up, and so Xie Yuanjing naturally didn't expose her.

The little one had deliberately put her claws up — which meant she had no intention of asking about it. And he had not yet won his way into her heart. He was not about to take this moment to spread all his darker aspects out before her.

She could know. She could weigh it on her own terms.

He would not stand in her way. He would only draw her closer.

"How could incense smell foul? Give it another try."

Xie Yuanjing had no shame whatsoever. He turned his head, his thin lips grazing her earlobe.

Lu Huaixi's bravado instantly collapsed. She sat rigid, and went silent.

"If you don't like it, I'll just pick up more of your scent instead."

He laughed softly — languid and roguish. "Did you put on the fragrance?"

chapters.title: Don't Go Around Saying Things You Shouldn't
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi forgot why she had come in the first place. In a daze, she followed him back to the manor without asking a single question.

Xie Yuanjing walked her to her room, and before he left, he pinched her cheek.

"Tomorrow the matter will blow up. If you want to go back to the Lù estate, I'll take you in a few days."

With something practical to focus on, Lu Huaixi put aside the lingering fluster from moments ago.

The corners of her lips tightened, drawing faintly downward. She thought back to what she had overheard from Lù Tangshu outside that room, and whatever last scraps of pity she had held on to for her grandfather's sake scattered completely.

The second branch had brought this upon themselves. If she felt any discomfort about it, that was simply the price of standing between them and their wickedness.

"I do want to go. Otherwise this scheme of Lù Tangshu's has no proper ending."

Her voice was slightly subdued, her gaze drifting somewhere in the distance. She looked both aggrieved and exhausted.

"I'd planned to go tomorrow — but I can't find a convincing reason, and I don't know whether Second Aunt will go to my mother and cause a scene."

"Even if she does, it won't help her. Your mother isn't someone she can push around."

Xie Yuanjing watched the brief shadow that crossed her eyes, quickly suppressed, and reached up to gently smooth the corner of her eye.

Perhaps she was thinking too hard to notice. Lu Huaixi had no particular reaction.

She even, on instinct, pressed into his touch the way a small creature seeking comfort might, drowsy and slow.

"Still — it'll bring unrest to the household. The Lù family will suffer for it. But even so, if I had to do it over, I still wouldn't have let her run her schemes unchecked."

"A little unrest now is better than the Lù estate being dragged down by her later. The moment she could move against you without hesitation, she had already decided the elder branch was in her way. This confrontation was always going to come — sooner or later."

"I know."

Lu Huaixi's voice was not despondent, but it lacked the energy she had shown earlier.

She looked out into the distance for a moment, then turned and went into the inner room, picking up a cup of water and taking a small sip.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing more. He glanced at her once, and then the step that had been about to take him away turned instead. He followed her inside and sat down beside her.

The scent of that incense drifted in with him and began to spread.

Lu Huaixi didn't like that smell. It always made her feel unsettled after too much of it — especially because it kept bringing back the memory of just now in the carriage, of this man cornering her and saying those insufferable things.

"Don't come in here. It stinks."

Her train of thought broken, she pushed aside the lingering mood from before.

Lu Huaixi decided she wanted to bathe, and called for a maid.

But Xie Yuanjing insisted on teasing her. He walked over and bent down, and once her eyes had gone wide, stopped just beside her ear.

"That isn't actually ordinary incense."

He lowered his voice and let the warmth of his breath fall against her ear. "That particular combination, mixed with the drug they were given — it inflames desire, heightens sensation. So you should hold your breath. You mustn't breathe in too much."

Lu Huaixi immediately raised both hands and clamped them over her nose. Her eyes brimmed with accusation.

But then she caught the edge of Xie Yuanjing's smug, unscrupulous smile, and her suspicion quietly resurfaced.

"You're lying to me."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing stood, and admitted it almost immediately. "Foolish girl. If it were true, a whiff would've been enough — you wouldn't have stopped at a mere embrace in that carriage just now."

"You—"

Having been teased several times over, Lu Huaixi had completely forgotten her earlier state of mind.

She stood and was about to push him out of the way and head inside when a maid came through the outer door.

"Young Madam — someone has come from the Lù estate."

Lu Huaixi paused mid-step and looked up.

"The person is a nanny from the Second Madam's side of the household. She says that the Third Miss had an appointment today to have tea with you in the western quarter — but the Third Miss still hasn't come home, and they can't locate her. So they've sent someone here to ask."

"An appointment to have tea with me?"

Lu Huaixi blinked. Then she smiled, just slightly.

"My Third Sister has never once set foot in the western quarter. And I never accepted any such invitation. If you're looking for someone, look — but don't go around saying things you have no business saying."

"Yes, this servant will go and relay that right away."

The maid withdrew quickly and was not heard from again.

Half an hour later, at the Lù estate, Second Madam Luo Yuehui smashed the teacup in her hands. Both furious and frantic.

"She's sitting perfectly fine in the Marquis's manor and still has the audacity to say she never accepted any appointment? She must have done something — it had to be her! That Lù Huaixi — how dare she do this to my Shū'er! Someone come with me — I'm going to the Marquis's manor and I'm taking her!"

"Second Madam — Second Madam, please calm yourself!"

The nanny saw her charging for the door and rushed forward to stop her.

"If you go over there now, won't that be the same as telling everyone that the Third Miss has gone missing? If that gets out, the Third Miss's reputation will be ruined for good! And that is the Marquis's manor — you can't just walk in there and expect to see anyone!"

Luo Yuehui's feet slowed.

Her face was livid. She stood there seething, eyes wide, every line of her expression tight with fury.

"That little wretch calculated that I wouldn't dare make a scene! And I'd wager it was all Liù Piaoran's idea — she wants to ruin my Shū'er's name! Those two, mother and daughter — they'd actually stoop to this! Not one decent bone between them!"

Luo Yuehui grabbed whatever was within reach and hurled it to the ground.

"Get more people out there looking! Even if you have to tear apart every last inch of that wretched western quarter — find my daughter! My poor Shū'er, what on earth must she be suffering!"

"Second Madam, please don't panic — perhaps the Third Miss has gone to someone else's house. It's still not too late — maybe she'll be back at the estate before long—"

"She would not have made another appointment today."

Luo Yuehui's voice was low and heavy, and she was grinding the handkerchief in her hands into a ball.

She didn't know exactly what her daughter had been planning, but she knew that if her daughter had invited Lù Huaixi, she must have had everything in order.

Yet Lù Huaixi was sitting perfectly well in the Marquis's manor — and her own daughter had vanished. That vile creature had to have done something.

"Where is the Master? Still with that fox woman and not come back yet?"

Luo Yuehui's expression turned hard and vicious. She stepped out of the room. "Go fetch him back! If anything happens to my Shū'er, he can watch his dignity crumble and the elder branch grind him into the dust for the rest of his days!"

"Second Madam — Second Madam, where are you going?"

"Where else would I go? To find my 'dear' sister-in-law and get my daughter back, naturally!"

She had assumed the silence from the elder branch these past few days meant they had come to their senses and didn't dare go against the Old Master and Old Madam — but who could have known they were carrying out something this vicious behind closed doors, even going so far as to harm her Shū'er!

"Does Lù Huaixi think she can get away with this? She agreed to her own sister's invitation, and now that sister is missing without a trace — who's going to hear that and not call her wicked?!"

Luo Yuehui stormed toward the elder branch's courtyard in a righteous fury.

But she never got to see Liù Piaoran. She was stopped outside the gate entirely.

"Our First Madam says that any matter requires evidence."

The elder branch's nanny came out unhurriedly from inside, offered a curtsy, then stood just within the courtyard wall and spoke at her own leisurely pace.

"Our Lord and First Madam are resting right now. If the Second Madam wishes to make a scene, she may either go to the Old Master or report it to the authorities — whichever she pleases. But please don't come here to our First Madam — she has to go to the palace tomorrow and hasn't the time to spare."

"They're quite content to play the villains, are they?!"

Luo Yuehui let out a cold laugh, throwing all pretense aside. "Lù Huaixi accepted my daughter's invitation — and now with a single word of being busy she expects to just brush it off? She harmed someone and now she's too guilty to show her face?"

"Accepted an invitation? Second Madam, you cannot simply drag people into things on a whim."

The nanny laughed sharply.

"As for this invitation the Second Madam speaks of — is our young lady's written reply in your possession? Aside from your own words and your second branch's claims, who can prove any of this actually happened? Our young lady is now the wife of the Marquis of Chengen. To have your lips part and immediately pull our young lady into this — that is not appropriate."

Luo Yuehui's face fell. She had been backed into a corner and had nothing left to say.

chapters.title: She Had Her Plans From the Start
chapters.content:
Of course Lu Huaixi would not receive anyone Luo Yuehui sent. From the moment she had deliberately let the appointment stand, she had already had her plans in place.

Nor did she believe the second branch had anything in the way of evidence. She had sent no written reply. The person who had gone back to deliver her answer was someone from her own household. A single casual remark — who could say with certainty whether it had been an acceptance or something else entirely?

And then there was the location — the western quarter.

Even if there had truly been an appointment, neither of them would have passed up Shùnan Lane, which was right at hand, to go all the way to somewhere Lù Tangshu had never deigned to set foot. It made no sense.

Lu Huaixi settled into bed and turned it over once, let the cool drift from the ice blocks wash over her, and closed her eyes.

She had expected not to be able to sleep — but when she next opened her eyes, it was already the following morning.

"Young Madam."

A maid came in at the sound of movement and set down the hot water.

When she saw her finally come fully awake and get out of bed, she stepped forward and poured her a cup of warm tea. "Young Madam — the Third Miss has been found."

Lu Huaixi nodded and took the cup, drinking in small sips to ease her throat.

"However, the situation has caused quite a stir. There's considerable unrest at the Lù estate. The First Madam says you should keep your distance for the next few days and not go back."

"Who found her?"

"It was the Third Miss's own maidservant. When she was found, the Third Miss and He Jianhang were in a room together in a state of dishevelment. After they came to, the two of them got into a fight — the Third Miss smashed something over He Jianhang's head and drew blood."

Lu Huaixi set down her cup and wandered at a languid pace toward the wooden rack where the wash basin was.

"With that kind of commotion, there must have been even more people who saw it."

"Far more than just a few — it's already making the rounds."

The maid relayed what she had just been told by Jing Shuang in careful detail:

"It started with just the people nearby watching the scene unfold, so word didn't spread that quickly at first. But it so happened that the authorities were there at the time making arrests — a group of ruthless hired men with no regard for their own lives. A large number of officers had been sent. When the officers saw the two of them fighting, they stepped in to intervene — and the moment they did, the Third Miss and the He family heir were both standing right there, and people recognized them on the spot."

At the mention of the authorities making arrests, Lu Huaixi's thoughts drifted for a moment.

She had never pressed Xie Yuanjing for the full details of his side of things. He had told her not to worry about it, and she hadn't tried to pry.

That those hired thugs had appeared at such a convenient moment — she found it hard to believe it had nothing to do with Lù Tangshu's business.

"Keep it at knowing — don't send anyone to dig around for more. But keep an eye on the He family. If He Jianhang drags his feet about coming to propose, give things a push."

Lu Huaixi's mind came back to the present. She dipped her hand into the basin and stirred the water. "For the next two days, if anyone sends a calling card, tell them I'm resting and not receiving visitors."

"Yes, this servant understands."

The Lù family had suffered because of Lù Tangshu's actions. For Lu Huaixi, a daughter already married out, to be too upset to leave the manor was only fitting.

—

After being sent home, Lù Tangshu had not quieted down for two days. She smashed everything in her room to pieces.

She had beaten every maid who came near her. She trembled with rage, was too furious to speak without bringing up blood, her eyes holding nothing but venom and wrath.

But there was nothing she could say. Xie Yuanjing's threat — even in her dazed state, she had heard every word of it, and it would not leave her.

On the afternoon of the second day, Qiáolíng came in carrying medicine with barely concealed dread.

With nothing left in the room to smash, Lù Tangshu picked up the wooden tray the moment she saw her and hurled it at her.

Qiáolíng waited for the storm to pass, then spoke through the pain, choosing her words with great care. "Miss — the He family has sent someone. They say — they say they've come to propose a marriage."

At the mention of the He family, Lù Tangshu's entire body began to shake. She clenched both hands into fists, her eyes blazing red.

"A bastard like him dares ask to marry me?!"

She screamed it out, and with nothing useful to throw, she grabbed that bowl of medicine and sent it crashing to the floor.

The smell of medicine in the room immediately grew even heavier. Qiáolíng stood with her head down, not daring to move.

"What does he think he is? He's not fit to carry my shoes, and he has the nerve to come proposing! Useless waste of a man! Vile creature! He couldn't even control one woman — all of this is his fault! Worthless, disgusting — how dare he touch me! How dare he, how dare he!"

The words had barely left her mouth when Luo Yuehui walked in from outside, both angry and fraught.

She couldn't help a flash of tenderness when she saw her daughter's state. But she still took hold of her and pulled her close.

"Your father wants you to go and meet with the He family. Mother knows you can't stand He Jianhang — but don't make a scene for now. This is still the height of all the attention. Even if you want to find a way out, that will have to wait a while."

Luo Yuehui said this, and a flicker of bitter reluctance passed through her eyes. "It's all the fault of those two — mother and daughter from the elder branch! They're vicious enough — they'll get what's coming to them eventually!"

Malicious people always find ways to push the blame to others. They never remember how much wickedness they have committed themselves.

Lù Tangshu was furious and humiliated, seething with resentment but too afraid to act rashly. She could only cry and make a scene, clinging to Luo Yuehui and refusing to go.

"Mother, please help me — please. I won't marry that worthless bastard! He has nothing in the He family — he's completely useless — if your daughter marries him, that's the end of everything, Mother!"

"Mother doesn't want you to marry him either — but now..."

Now that the scandal had spread all through the capital, it would have been manageable if it could be pinned on Lù Huaixi. But that vile creature had laid her plans from the start and kept herself completely clean.

"I tell you you've got no sense and you don't want to hear it! Setting something like this in motion without telling me first is one thing — but then you had to go and make that scene outside the teahouse! Now on top of what happened between you and He Jianhang, people are saying you're overbearing and tyrannical, and that you drove someone to contemplate ending their own life!"

Luo Yuehui grew angrier as she spoke, and she raised her hand and struck her daughter.

"And you're still sitting here looking down on the He family? If that He Jianhang gets stubborn and refuses to marry you, what kind of face are you going to show to the world for the rest of your life?"

"Why would he dare refuse? He's a nobody who can't even stand up while his elder brother's pressing him down — and he has the nerve to look down on him being connected to the Lù family? He ought to kneel down and be grateful! He couldn't even handle one woman — that's all on him for being useless! That disgusting creature — how dare he touch me! How dare he—"

The words were barely out of her mouth before someone in the doorway let out a cold laugh.

Everyone in the room looked up in unison, and there was Second Master Lù, a few steps away, his expression dark and foreboding — and behind him, He Jianhang, his face just as ominous and vicious.

In the next instant, Second Master Lù strode into the room, raised his hand, and brought it down in a hard slap across Lù Tangshu's face.

"You insolent little wretch! Do you think you still get to pick and choose?!"

He Jianhang stood behind him, his gaze fixed on her, full of violence and cold malice.

—

Lu Huaixi had heard bits and pieces of the news from the Lù estate. She gave no reaction, showed very little expression, and lay contentedly at the waterside pavilion inside the manor, feeding the fish.

That flash of brilliant gold darted and shimmered through the water.

It had seemingly come to recognize her — every time she came, the fish would leap out of the water to meet her.

Even the Old Madam, who happened to see it once, was utterly astonished. She took Lu Huaixi by the hands and turned her this way and that, looking her over — it was the first time she had ever looked at her with the expression of someone regarding a true treasure.

Lu Huaixi played along, adding a touch of gentle innocence to her manner. It was enough to make Mù Nianwēi's eyes go red with envy.

"Young Madam — are you warm?"

Yao Xu came over and set a bowl of shaved ice with sweet toppings before her.

She and Jing Shuang had been on the outside looking in for a few days. Now that they were finally back at her side, they couldn't help but hover, and found every small piece of news worth coming to tell her.

"New bamboo mats were sent to the room today — Young Madam will see them when she goes back. It's just that the Young Master's low bed is a bit small, so a new one will have to be made."

Lu Huaixi's hand stilled where she'd been scattering fish feed.

Time had slipped by so quickly. She hadn't had a chance to think about it much.

It was only now, calling to mind how tall Xie Yuanjing was and how long he had been sleeping on that low bed without even a new mat to sleep on, that something she couldn't quite name settled uncomfortably in her chest.

"How long will it take to have it made?"

"Not long, Young Madam — please don't worry."

Yao Xu smiled. "The Young Master said this ice treat is the only one you should have for the next few days — too much of it and you won't eat your meals. The Young Master also said to tell you to wait a little — he'll take you back to the Lù estate in a day or two."

The corner of Lu Huaixi's lips moved. But in the end she said nothing.

She leaned back against the wooden railing and watched the fish in the water.

The last time Xie Yuanjing had brought it up, he had said that whether she liked him or not didn't really matter — and she had assumed he meant he'd made up his mind to let go. But right now, Lu Huaixi found she genuinely wasn't sure what he meant.

"Set aside a bowl for him too."

Lu Huaixi turned her head away, not letting anyone see her expression, and muttered stubbornly, "No — half a bowl."

chapters.title: Coming To Offer Her Congratulations
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi spent a few quiet, unhurried days at the manor.

She waited until the events of that morning had fully spread through the capital. She waited until He Jianhang had been strong-armed into a reluctant visit to the Lù estate to propose. She waited until Lù Tangshu had been driven to a fit so severe she fainted and needed a physician called, triggering yet another great storm of commotion — and only then did she have a carriage prepared and return to the Lù estate.

She did not wait for Xie Yuanjing.

He had been very busy these past few days.

The people in the manor, when they saw him, felt mostly fear or the need to ingratiate themselves. There was almost no one who actually thought to ask after his health.

But Lu Huaixi found she cared. She didn't want him making an extra trip on her account.

The Lù estate, where red silk had been hung in celebration, was draped in a kind of muted stillness. Even the servants moving through the courtyards kept their heads lowered, none of the liveliness of ordinary days.

It was only once she entered the elder branch's quarters that the heavy atmosphere lifted.

Lu Huaixi didn't let any of it weigh on her. She walked along the covered walkway and stepped into her mother's room.

"You've come back at this hour?"

Madame Liù pulled her inside to sit down and took the fan from the maid's hand to fan her herself.

"The wedding has been settled now, but the second branch is making a terrible fuss. Once they see you, you won't have a moment's peace."

"I'm not worried — I brought a lot of people today."

Lu Huaixi smiled at Madame Liù. "With my Third Sister about to have such a great occasion, I naturally had to come back and see for myself. Anything less would be hard to explain."

Lù Tangshu was getting married — and to He Jianhang, of all people, someone she could barely stand the sight of. How could Lu Huaixi stay away without making even a quiet appearance?

No matter how much the second branch screamed and raged, she was coming. Personally, to offer her congratulations.

"You can be forceful with the second branch if you need to, but show a little restraint when you're in front of your grandfather. He's been upset about the second branch's business these past few days. He hasn't said anything, but he likely has some sense that you were involved."

"Then I'll arrange to have the young physician from the Zeng line come visit him tomorrow."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes, thought a moment, then said quietly:

"Even if I was involved — they came after me first. If I hadn't protected myself, her little scheme would have ended her troubles with a marriage, while I'd have been drowned in a sack. My life on the line."

"Of course none of this is your fault. Your grandfather knows that too — he just has the weight of years on him. Looking at the Lù family as it is today, he feels his strength failing him."

Madame Liù took her daughter's hand and said with deep tenderness:

"Even if Lù Tangshu ends up losing her reputation and being married off regardless, it's still a consequence of her own making. And yet even so, the wrongs she did you can never be made right. If it hadn't been for you and the Marquis's household agreeing to terms from the very beginning, with her stirring up trouble over and over again, you'd have been in trouble at your husband's family long before now."

The more Madame Liù spoke, the angrier she became. "Thinking about it this way — I almost feel like marrying her off is letting her off too lightly!"

"Mother, how did you end up getting upset yourself?"

Lu Huaixi startled slightly, and then quickly rose and moved to sit beside her mother.

"Marrying He Jianhang is no blessing. The two of them can't stand each other — they'll have plenty to quarrel about going forward."

"That's true, Madam."

The nanny nearby added her voice in consolation:

"Evil is its own punishment. Please don't let people like that upset you."

Then the nanny turned her gaze to Lu Huaixi.

"The Second Young Miss may not have heard — when that He family son was forced to come and propose two days ago, the Third Miss quarreled with everyone and reportedly even got slapped by the He family's heir. It drove the Second Madam to order her people to retaliate on the spot."

This was news to Lu Huaixi. She listened with a flicker of curiosity.

"Did she hit back?"

"She didn't. But that He fellow had her in his grip — using the ruin of her reputation to threaten her — and a single word of I won't marry you was enough to make the Second Madam swallow her rage. Afterward, that He family's heir even suggested she come as a concubine. In the end, out of deference to the Old Master, he didn't truly have the nerve to go that far."

The nanny said this last part in a lower voice, a flash of contempt in her eyes.

"That He family's son is no good thing either. One look at the face and you can tell. The two of them ended up injuring each other before it was over — both injuries on their faces, at that."

Yao Xu had just returned from bringing tea together with Madame Liù's maid.

Hearing the nanny's words, she set everything down and added her own line.

"That man is rotten through. And to think he dared covet our young lady. And the Third Miss is no better — after people saw what happened between the two of them, she and he both tried to point the blame at our young lady. When they saw that no one was willing to believe it, they turned on each other like cornered animals, and that was that."

Yao Xu had prepared the tea with a few petals steeped in for Lu Huaixi.

She carefully handed the cup over, then stepped back to the side.

Lu Huaixi lifted the lid and stirred the petals gently, took a small sip, then seemed to recall something and spoke.

"I didn't expect the young lady who'd broken off her engagement to come forward and speak. To say plainly that she'd seen a handkerchief with the character Tāng embroidered on it."

"She was probably too angry to stay quiet. After all, she came from a family of scholars — and after the engagement was broken off, she was talked about for a long time."

Madame Liù said, "It's a good thing that engagement was broken early. He Jianhang was never worthy of a girl like that."

Lu Huaixi agreed.

Regardless of how that handkerchief had come to be in He Jianhang's possession, and regardless of who had seen it, that young lady's testimony had confirmed that the two of them had been involved before any of this.

Lu Huaixi knew their earlier meetings had almost certainly been for the purpose of scheming against her. But since heaven had offered its assistance, she was naturally going to receive it with both hands.

As they were speaking, the very people they had been discussing arrived — and sure enough, came straight here, creating a commotion outside and demanding to be let in.

Lu Huaixi leisurely took another sip of warm tea.

She set down the cup, rose, and smiled softly at Madame Liù.

"Don't worry, Mother. I want to see her too. I have a few words I'd like to say."

Lù Tangshu's ruin of her own fortune had not entirely satisfied Lu Huaixi.

She had endured her schemes without cause, time and again.

It had begun with the entry-to-the-palace list. It had begun with the interference in her marriage. She had been passive and on the receiving end all along.

If she was being truly honest, she hadn't really won much. It was only luck — running into Xie Yuanjing, who had his own purposes.

But she had her grievances too. Her discontent too.

In the courtyard, Lù Tangshu was being restrained, held out under the sun.

Her eyes still burned with defiance.

But beneath it was pain and resentment, and a desperation wrapped in helpless longing — a tangle of emotions far too complicated to name.

Lu Huaixi walked over and stopped in the cool of the shade.

One face was tranquil. The other was furious.

After a moment, Lu Huaixi smiled at her.

"The wedding is almost upon you. Congratulations, Third Sister."

"How dare you say that to me?!"

Days of screaming had left Lù Tangshu's voice rough and hoarse.

"You had the nerve to send Xie Yuanjing to ruin me! Do you think no one will find out what you did just because you won't admit to accepting my invitation?!"

Lu Huaixi did not respond to any of that. She simply took two more steps forward, bent down, and lowered her voice near her ear.

Lù Tangshu was held in place and couldn't move. She strained to stare at her, and couldn't see her — caught between fear and rage.

"What are you doing — you—"

"I was right outside that room."

Lu Huaixi smiled, using a voice completely devoid of any cruelty — the light, guileless tone of someone saying something perfectly innocent — and drove it straight into Lù Tangshu's heart.

"I heard everything you said. I also saw He Jianhang being dragged in. He'd been given the drug, hadn't he? Was it very painful? I heard you — you were crying, I think."

chapters.title: Not Planning to Seek a Divorce
chapters.content:
The color of humiliation spread slowly across Lù Tangshu's face.

The marks on her body had not yet faded.

The memory of waking to someone else's screaming, only to find herself lying beside that useless wretch He Jianhang — it made her chest heave.

And then the thought of how she could no longer hold her head up anywhere in the capital, how all her hopes for rank and wealth and standing had been dragged down — how even the concubines in her own household might outrank her in the end — made her so furious she brought up blood and could barely stay on her feet.

All of this was Lù Huaixi's fault. And yet she couldn't touch her.

"You've always been pretending! You're just as vicious as I am — aren't you afraid of getting your own punishment someday!"

"I could never match your cruelty."

Lu Huaixi gave a quiet laugh, her voice as light and unencumbered as a drifting feather — casual, and devastatingly pointed.

"You and He Jianhang are perfectly suited — equally foolish, equally repulsive. You really are, the two of you, a match made by heaven."

Lu Huaixi's words pushed Lù Tangshu to the edge of madness.

She was supposed to be a gem of the highest order — a daughter born to marry into one of the great and powerful houses of the realm.

But because of Lù Huaixi, she was going to be married into the He family, which had never gotten on with the Lùs, and married to a man with nothing to show for himself.

"What gives you the right to look at me like that?! You think you're better than me? If you didn't have someone to rely on—"

"Aren't you also a Lù?"

Lu Huaixi cut her off.

"We have the same grandfather and grandmother. I carry the Lù name. So do you."

Lu Huaixi was rarely one to mock.

But this once, she drew back a little, eyes lowered as she looked at her, her beautiful face wearing an expression of pure contempt.

"Or is it the 'support' you're referring to — Xie Yuanjing?"

At the mention of Xie Yuanjing, Lù Tangshu still flinched involuntarily.

That man's voice, saying those words about skinning people alive in that cold, flat tone — it had become her worst nightmare these past few days.

"What about him?"

Lù Tangshu forced herself to hold on to the last of her dignity.

After what had happened, she was genuinely too afraid to do anything to Lù Huaixi.

But she couldn't accept it. She would not accept it, even dying.

What right did Lù Huaixi have to a better life than hers? What right did she have to be held in such regard by such a man?

Even if she could do nothing now, she could not let Lù Huaixi live easily!

"You're just lucky you married into the Marquis's household! But do you think a man as arrogant and ruthless as Xie Yuanjing can really treat you well forever — can really stand up for you forever? Stop dreaming, Lù Huaixi!"

Lù Tangshu screamed:

"He's just weighing the scales and putting on a performance for your father! A man like him, no one can hold onto him — before long he'll have someone else, and he'll start caring about someone else, and being despised and cast aside is only a matter of time for you!"

"Perhaps."

Lu Huaixi gave a faint sound of acknowledgment. Her tone was utterly undisturbed — impossible to tell whether she had taken any of it to heart.

"But have you forgotten? Xie Yuanjing's marriage to me — you and your mother made that happen. From beginning to end, the one who pushed me into the Marquis's household was you."

She smiled faintly, then — though the beautiful eyes, always so bright and lively, had gone clear and cool as glass.

She had caught sight of someone entering through the courtyard gate.

Deep violet official robes in this summer heat carried a particular coolness — but her words did not stop for it.

"You and your mother weren't wrong. I married to avoid being sent to the palace. I've known Xie Yuanjing for only a few months — where would a betrothal from a year ago even come from."

"You—"

"And I've said it before — the Marquis's household is right there. If you can make Xie Yuanjing marry you, I'll step aside with grace and give you the position. But I've been waiting all this time, and you still can't get through the door. The truth is, if you had simply treated me with any decency, you wouldn't have been kept outside at all."

Lu Huaixi said it slowly, one word at a time:

"You called me Second Sister with real feeling once, and I haven't forgotten it. But from now on, I will treat the Lù Tangshu I once knew as having died somewhere else long ago. All of the bitter fruit you're eating now — you planted every seed of it yourself. And in the days to come, I will be watching as you and He Jianhang, as husband and wife, settle what you owe, slowly."

By the time she finished speaking, the newcomer had already reached Lu Huaixi.

He didn't speak, didn't look to the side. He simply reached out and took hold of her wrist, drawing her slightly toward him.

"Warm?"

His eyes lowered to the person before him, and he smiled very faintly. But the gaze at the corner of those lowered eyes held a chill.

"Why didn't you wait for me? Came back to the Lù estate on your own?"

Lu Huaixi looked back at him in turn.

His face, as always, was strikingly handsome.

Without a smile, it was beautiful and cold — not the kind of face you approached without thinking twice.

Lu Huaixi held his gaze for a moment, and without quite knowing when it had started, she realized she was no longer afraid of him. She could even, without thinking, let her feelings show.

But it was always just like this.

Just when some hazy feeling would begin to take shape in her, the person before her would say something to remind her — there were unresolved things between them.

"I wanted to come back early to congratulate my Third Sister."

"Mm. Are the congratulations finished?"

Lu Huaixi didn't answer. She only looked back toward Lù Tangshu, who had suddenly gone still and pale and silent.

"Third Sister — does she think I've finished?"

She tilted her head a little, the curve of her lips unrelenting, and yet it was nothing like her usual gentle, easy manner.

"If Third Sister doesn't accept it, I can congratulate her again."

Lù Tangshu found she suddenly had nothing to say.

She parted her lips, staring at this second sister she appeared to have underestimated — wanting to cry, wanting to rage.

Only the rage had changed in character. She couldn't name it. She couldn't even tell anymore where to direct the hatred.

"...I accept."

After a long moment, the words came out of Lù Tangshu with great difficulty.

She was full of resentment and unwillingness — but she was afraid of Xie Yuanjing, and she did not want to hear anything more about what had happened that day.

She had also, she realized with an unsettling jolt, grown a little afraid of the Lù Huaixi standing before her. There was something unfamiliar about her that she couldn't place — and it made Lù Tangshu unwilling to cause any more trouble.

"Well then — I won't keep Third Sister any longer. Go back and prepare. I hear the wedding is next month — just like mine was, in such a rush."

Lu Huaixi turned and didn't look back.

Xie Yuanjing walked back alongside her.

For a while neither spoke. But just as they were about to step up onto the stone stairs, Xie Yuanjing slowed his pace.

"Step aside with grace. Give her the position."

He said it quietly, his tone even. "When did you say that?"

When Lu Huaixi wanted to say something cutting, she rarely left herself room to retreat.

Perhaps she didn't want to admit it herself — but Lù Tangshu's words had struck a nerve.

She certainly didn't believe Xie Yuanjing would ever turn cold on her.
