As long as the elder branch of the Lù family still stood, as long as she remained the first wife of the Xie household, no matter who else entered the inner chambers, Xie Yuanjing would always give her enough respect.

But respect was not the same as freedom. And respect was not all she wanted.

Or, to put it another way — Xie Yuanjing's softness toward her and his warmth were compelling, but the unease he brought was heavier still.

"I've been saying it for a long time."

Lu Huaixi acknowledged it without hesitation.

She gave him a smile — but the smile was clearly perfunctory.

She was not happy.

Xie Yuanjing regarded her quietly for a moment. Then, in silence, he guided her up the stone stairs.

Then he turned his gaze back to the path ahead, and the hand holding hers went cold, degree by degree.

"Lù Huaixi — do I matter so little to you? Not even a trace of care?"

Something pricked at Lu Huaixi's chest.

The hazy, ambiguous feelings she had been carrying these past few days made her ache in a way she couldn't name. She looked at him, lips parting — and closing again, several times.

"Watch where you're walking."

"What about you?"

After a long silence, Lu Huaixi finally found her voice. "What is it that you actually want from—"

"I thought it was obvious."

Xie Yuanjing finished the sentence for her.

He was perhaps genuinely angered — because this time, he didn't press gently or test the ground as usual. His voice was cool and hard, without a trace of softness.

"I am not planning to seek a divorce."

chapters.title: She Doesn't Necessarily Not Like You
chapters.content:
They didn't stay outside for long.

Madame Liù came out and, catching sight of Xie Yuanjing standing beside her daughter, was mildly surprised — but she quickly had tea brought out regardless.

Lu Huaixi couldn't find a good way to respond to any of it, and Xie Yuanjing didn't seem to have any interest in hearing her speak at this moment either.

From the moment they went inside, Xie Yuanjing behaved exactly as he always did — occasionally responding to something Madame Liù said, occasionally sitting quietly to the side and listening, waiting for the mother and daughter to finish before taking her home.

But Lu Huaixi could feel that he was suppressing something.

Xie Yuanjing's warmth ended on the carriage ride home.

He still remembered to lift the curtain for her, to help her up into the carriage — but once they were away from everyone else, he didn't open his mouth once the entire way.

Lu Huaixi found this unsettling, and she began carefully turning over how perhaps she should have a real talk with him.

She hadn't wanted to stay at the Marquis's household. And she held doubts about his words. But she hadn't been as indifferent as all that — and she wasn't as unbothered as he seemed to think.

With that in mind, she turned toward him.

"Just now — you—"

The line of Xie Yuanjing's profile was striking. They were not far apart, and Lu Huaixi could clearly make out the high line of his nose and his thin lips, which carried no particular curve.

He turned his head at the movement, his dark eyes deep and unreadable, his expression still.

Their eyes met, and just like that, Lu Huaixi forgot what she had been going to say.

But she didn't look away.

In the end it was Xie Yuanjing's lips that moved first — as though he were about to sigh, or as though he were about to break the silence himself.

But in the next instant, the carriage lurched violently.

Something slammed into it from the side. The carriage tilted sharply, swinging toward a stone wall along the road's edge.

Lu Huaixi had no time to react. She felt herself suddenly pulled toward someone, a force surrounding her entirely, shielding her from the impact of the collision.

Almost immediately, Gong Zhuo's voice sounded from outside, along with the scraping ring of blades being drawn.

Whatever had struck them ground along the side of the carriage and moved ahead. Wood scraped and dragged. The horse let out panicked, sharp sounds, straining to move away — but the carriage was caught on something and would not budge.

Xie Yuanjing's arm was wedged between her and the side of the carriage.

Lu Huaixi hadn't even gotten out a single are you hurt before a long arrow flew in and embedded itself hard into the outer frame.

At first there were one or two. Then the arrows came in a relentless stream. The people outside seemed to be struggling to hold them off, and once in a while a shaft tore through the curtain and into the carriage interior.

Xie Yuanjing had positioned her in a corner and put himself between her and the arrows — standing in the most exposed, most dangerous spot.

"Don't worry about me — where I'm standing won't be hit. Move back a little, and let me see your arm!"

Lu Huaixi tried to pull him to the side. He didn't move.

"Stay still."

His voice was low and cold. He reached back and took hold of her hand, as though in reassurance. "My arm is fine."

It couldn't be fine.

Lu Huaixi's eyes fell on the arm that had taken the impact shielding her just now.

But he showed very little on his face, his attention fixed entirely on the arrows that could come flying through the curtain at any moment. There was no way for her to check how badly it was hurt.

"Stay steady. These people won't dare do anything too serious. It'll stop soon."

Perhaps sensing her tension, Xie Yuanjing spoke again in a lowered voice.

He couldn't turn around — but Lu Huaixi could still picture clearly, from the sound of him, what his face must look like right now.

And then, in a sudden flash, she remembered that this man was still angry.

But even angry, the instinct that had him throwing himself in front of her had not hesitated for a single breath.

Lu Huaixi's clarity retreated, step by step.

She looked down at the corner she had been tucked into and, after a moment, pressed her lips together quietly and moved closer to his back.

Xie Yuanjing thought she was frightened. Without stopping to wait for her to speak or refuse, he turned and drew her into his arms, leaning back against the side of the carriage.

"These aren't people after the Lù family. They're not from last time either. There's nothing to fear — it'll be safe soon."

The sounds outside did indeed begin to die down not long after he spoke. The arrows came less fiercely — only the occasional probing shot.

Before long, Gong Zhuo's voice sounded from outside. Some of the attackers had been captured. But they were all dead soldiers, and had already taken their own lives.

The daylight was not yet gone, but the sky had already lost its brightness. Lu Huaixi straightened, and as he made to rise, she instinctively caught hold of his sleeve.

"Why dead soldiers? These people wanted to harm you?"

"Yes. They were coming for me."

Xie Yuanjing raised his hand, intending to touch her face in some small gesture of comfort.

But then he seemed to think of something. The motion stopped in midair, and his raised hand came back down.

"But they wouldn't dare actually kill me. The reason they sent dead soldiers is because anyone caught moving against someone within the city would inevitably be traced. Whoever sent them didn't want to be found."

He paused briefly, then finally smiled at Lu Huaixi.

"Gong Zhuo will see you back to the manor. Don't be afraid — small-time troublemakers aren't worth worrying about."

Lu Huaixi saw his hand rise and fall.

Something in her chest grew heavier, harder to name.

She lowered her eyes and looked at her own hand, still holding his sleeve.

She did not believe for one moment the calm in his voice.

If this truly were nothing, those arrows would not have come so ferociously. Even if it was a show of force, whoever was behind it had certainly harbored the wish for him to come to harm.

But Lu Huaixi knew she could not stop him from going.

"I'm not afraid."

She let go of his sleeve and looked up at him. "The manor isn't far from here. You don't need to worry about me. I can get back safely on my own."

In this moment, she felt as though there were many things she wanted to say to Xie Yuanjing.

There was what she had wanted to respond with earlier at the Lù estate. There were her doubts, about a promise he had never actually given. And there was her confusion about this.

But when she tried to form the words, none of them felt like the thing she most wanted to say.

What she most wanted to say was that Xie Yuanjing needed to come back safely.

But of course Xie Yuanjing wasn't going to take Gong Zhuo with him.

He looked at her hand as it withdrew, his fingertips shifting slightly — but he didn't go after it.

Just as he was about to speak again, a guard's voice came from outside.

"My lord — there is a matter at the palace."

Xie Yuanjing's reaction was unhurried.

He gave a quiet sound of acknowledgment, then called Gong Zhuo over. "See the Young Madam back to the manor."

"Xie Yuanjing—"

"I'm going into the palace. I don't need to bring many people."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his gaze, thought for a moment, and then said: "If my caring for you is truly something that makes you unhappy — wait for me to come back and tell me. I can consider, going forward, giving you more distance."

Lu Huaixi's eyes flew up. Another sharp pang in her chest.

—

Near the palace gate, Xie Yuanjing spotted Shen Zhouzhu waiting for him.

Shen Zhouzhu stepped up into the carriage from the side. Without Lu Huaixi there, Xie Yuanjing carried not a trace of warmth.

"I told you that man was no easy adversary. He'd barely gotten under Lord Xùn's wing before he had the man eating out of his hand. I've just heard that the Marquis of Chengen has entered the palace as well — likely over the matter of the injury."

Shen Zhouzhu saw the man arrive and couldn't help opening his mouth.

Then he looked up, caught sight of that cold face, and swallowed the rest of what he'd been going to say.

"This doesn't have to be as bad as it sounds. Even if the matter has reached the Emperor, His Majesty will still side with you. He's not going to take someone's word for it that you did it just because they say you did."

"Whether he does or doesn't doesn't matter to me. He wants to invite death — I'm not going to stop him."

Xie Yuanjing cut him off without patience. "Anything else? If not, I'm going in."

"So it's not that man giving you trouble?"

Shen Zhouzhu looked him over again, then narrowed his eyes. "Then why that look on your face, like everyone on earth has offended you — don't tell me it's still Lù Huaixi?"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. His thin lips were cool and flat.

"Truly?"

Shen Zhouzhu thought back to the events of a few days ago, then considered it in earnest.

"You know, I actually think — Lù Huaixi doesn't necessarily not like you."

He'd heard at least a little about how much she had depended on this man that day.

If she were truly completely indifferent, he wouldn't believe it.

"Maybe there's some other reason she's unwilling to give you an answer. Ask her directly. Or test the ground a little."

Shen Zhouzhu's beating still ached a little, but he bore it and kept going:

"Maybe you frightened her somehow, and she hasn't had time to think it through. You need to give her time. Let her know that you're genuinely devoted to her."

He paused a moment, then tilted his chin up and gave his folding fan an unhurried flick.

"And most importantly — you need to tell her that even if there are ever other people in your inner chambers, she will always be the one who matters most to you. No one will ever be placed above her."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. But at last he raised his eyes and looked at him.

chapters.title: She Wanted to See Xie Yuanjing
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi had barely returned to the Marquis's manor when Jing Shuang told her that the First Madam had gotten into an argument with the Marquis, after which the Marquis had gone to the palace.

She hadn't even made it back to her own courtyard. At those words, without thinking, she went straight to the First Madam's quarters.

The elder branch's part of the manor was always quiet. The servants inside were all people that Xie Yuanjing himself had placed there. When they saw her arrive, the nanny, who was carrying medicine, didn't conceal anything.

"The First Madam has a bit of a headache today and couldn't get up. Young Madam, please go in and sit."

The room carried a faint smell of medicine. Even with the windows open, the smell hadn't fully aired out.

Lu Huaixi didn't look too closely, and she didn't ask directly — but it was obvious enough that this wasn't the first day the First Madam had been taking medicine.

"How is Mother feeling now?"

"Young Madam, the Madam is much better. She didn't sleep well last night. The physician said it's nothing serious — a few days of rest will see her right."

The nanny took the medicine in, and the person inside, hearing movement, finished it and sat up.

"Huaixi's come."

The First Madam had dressed properly, her hair still neatly pinned, as composed as always — but her complexion was indeed not as rosy as usual.

Lu Huaixi quickly moved to meet her, brow faintly creased.

"Mother, if you weren't feeling well, why didn't you tell me? I have medicine from the old physician — I can have a doctor look at whether it's suitable to take."

"There's no need for anything from the old physician. This is an old ailment. It aches for a day or two and then it's better."

The First Madam said this, then coughed a few times, and released Lu Huaixi's hands. "Come sit and talk with me — but stay a little distance away. I don't want you catching anything."

"I'll be fine, Mother."

Lu Huaixi sat beside the First Madam.

Normally she would have said something to make her smile and lighten the mood — but after everything that had just happened, and knowing that Xie Yuanjing had been summoned to the palace, she couldn't stop her mind from circling back to it. The unease simply wouldn't settle.

And that was without mentioning that she had also heard the Marquis had gone to the palace.

She was not entirely sure what to make of the Marquis's relationship with his own son.

She was still mulling it over when the First Madam spoke first.

"Yuanjing has gone into the palace?"

"Mother already knows?"

The First Madam made a sound of acknowledgment, and her expression sobered.

"Lord Xùn has accused Yuanjing before the Emperor — saying he raised a hand against one of his students, suppressed and framed the man for personal gain."

"How could that possibly be him?"

Lu Huaixi's brow knit tighter, and her eyes flared with a frustration she hadn't noticed herself. "And he wouldn't just hurt someone for no reason. He has been occupied recently—"

She stopped.

Xie Yuanjing had indeed been very busy recently. She didn't know exactly what he had been doing.

But to say he had deliberately sought out this person to harm, and put himself in harm's way to do it — Lu Huaixi didn't believe it.

"And Father going to the palace — is it for this matter?"

"Yes."

At the mention of the Marquis of Chengen, a rare coldness entered the First Madam's face.

Lu Huaixi's heart sank a little.

That expression, on this face, meant the Marquis was not going to help Xie Yuanjing.

And indeed — the First Madam raised a hand and came down hard on the table, then clenched her handkerchief tight. "He's gone to seek justice on behalf of the one who was injured."

"......"

Whoever was the injured party — it was certainly not Xie Yuanjing, who had been summoned to the palace at a moment's notice.

Lu Huaixi was at a loss for words.

She suddenly recalled what Zhou Jieyu had told her that day at Shùnan Lane.

He had said there was only one time Xie Yuanjing had ever struck someone of his own accord — and it had been after the Marquis intervened in a certain case.

After a moment, Lu Huaixi asked: "The injured party — is it the same one as before?"

With no context to the question, the First Madam nonetheless understood her.

She didn't hide it from her, and turned to look at her.

"It is. Yuanjing moved against him once. This time, that person was the target of an ambush — and it was laid at Yuanjing's feet."

The First Madam said coldly:

"That person took up a post not long ago. He was originally accompanying a party sent to arrest someone outside the capital, but the target was never caught — and those dispatched ended up walking into an ambush. With the arrests in the western quarter just a few days ago, word spread that it had been Yuanjing's people who gave the tip, and the blame was steered straight toward Yuanjing."

"He couldn't have had anything to do with it!"

Lu Huaixi gripped the armrest without thinking.

"What happened in the western quarter has nothing to do with him — I can vouch for that. And just now, on the way back here, our carriage was run off the road by attackers. It was Xie Yuanjing who was ambushed — he couldn't possibly have had his mind on what some Lord Xùn or Lord Mǎ was doing!"

Lu Huaixi's words came out fast. She had brought up the attack on the road as well, and the First Madam didn't catch that she had called her son by his given name.

But the moment she finished speaking, she realized the incident on the road might not be something that could be used in her defense.

If the charges had already been brought, then those attackers earlier would simply be seen, in everyone else's eyes, as a move Xie Yuanjing had staged deliberately to clear his own name.

The First Madam had come to the same thought.

Her expression remained troubled, her brow still drawn together, weighed down by a low, heavy tension.

But she didn't stay silent for long. She turned the conversation and began offering Lu Huaixi reassurance.

"You don't need to worry too much. Yuanjing has navigated things far harder than this. A trick this simple can't really hurt him."

The First Madam pressed her fingertips against her brow for a moment, then smiled at Lu Huaixi.

"I'm not telling you all this to make you anxious. I was afraid that, the first time you encountered something like this, you'd panic. You can rest easy — His Majesty won't truly do anything to Yuanjing. Even for the sake of the late Empress, this matter won't be allowed to spiral out of hand."

"But with Father going to the palace — won't that make things..."

"It will."

The First Madam didn't hesitate, and her eyes turned sharp for a moment.

"He wants to seek justice for people unworthy of his attention and go against his own son — let him. This way, His Majesty will see clearly, and in the future when he causes trouble, it won't drag Yuanjing into it."

There was nothing Lu Huaixi could say to that.

She felt as though she could see the shape of it all — the turns and knots hidden beneath the surface — but she didn't dare follow the thought to its end. Being brought in by your own father to answer for a crime — the suffering of that was something she could barely imagine.

And then she thought of when Xie Yuanjing had acted himself, and how he would have had to be pushed past the limits of his patience — past caring about appearances — to do it.

Because back then, the Marquis must have already blamed him. For raising his hand against someone he shouldn't have. For being too ruthless.

And Xie Yuanjing — had he just held all of it in, alone, and said nothing to anyone?

Just like earlier at the Lù estate.

He had swallowed his anger for so long, alone, and yet he still remembered to shield her when danger came. Still tried to stay composed and reassure her. Still said he was willing to take a step back.

Something pressed heavily in Lu Huaixi's chest.

She had never, until this moment, wanted so badly to see Xie Yuanjing — to be with him, to talk to him.

"In the next few days, people will certainly be trying to fish for information. Those people won't be able to see me — so they'll find ways to reach you."

The First Madam brought her back to the present with a gentle steadiness. "You mustn't lose your footing. Carry on exactly as usual — see who you want to see, and turn away whoever you don't."

"I understand, Mother."

Lu Huaixi's lips pressed together. Then she steadied herself. "I'll be waiting for him to come back."

chapters.title: Defiant and Arrogant
chapters.content:
In the palace.

Xie Yuanjing saw his own father standing beside the deeply displeased Lord Xùn, regarding him with the same accusatory look as everyone else in the room.

He spared it one glance, then withdrew his gaze. He turned to offer a bow to the Emperor and stood to wait.

The Marquis of Chengen, seeing that his own son had looked at him and shown not even the faintest reaction, felt a flare of anger by instinct.

Yet the person before him had no intention of looking at him at all. There was nothing concealed about it — he was openly showing the room his cold indifference.

"Lord Xùn has brought a complaint before Us, saying that you laid hands on a student under his tutelage and suppressed and framed him for personal gain."

The man on the high seat did not follow the Marquis of Chengen's lead.

He looked at the figure standing below, his voice cool and measured, his bearing severe.

"People have been apprehended, and evidence has been gathered. The student in question is still bedridden, and has indicated he has no wish to press charges against you. Do you confess to this offense?"

"This minister does not confess."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his head. The straight line of his back bent only slightly — and yet it gave no one the impression of bowing before anyone.

He even let out a faint, scornful sound and lifted his voice, bold and unhesitating.

"This minister only acts in service to Your Majesty. He has had no dealings with Lord Xùn, and a student who has just entered the court — what would there be worth this minister's effort to suppress and frame?"

The man on the high seat showed no sign of anger at those words. It was the Marquis of Chengen to the side whose face flushed with displeasure.

"Insolent — dare you show such disrespect before His Majesty! Bìnxìn is sincere in character and straightforward in conduct — and after suffering such a serious injury, he still counseled Lord Xùn not to misplace blame on you. And you?!"

"Bìnxìn?"

Xie Yuanjing turned his head, his gaze flat. "I don't know anyone by that name. If Father has come today to lay a charge at my feet on behalf of this so-called Bìnxìn, then let's first establish clearly — in what capacity, and with what evidence."

"Is this how you speak to your own father?"

The Marquis of Chengen stepped forward, only to find that the young man before him was half a head taller than himself.

The commanding presence of an established marquis had somehow, at some point, been pushed down by this son who would not be managed.

He felt both flustered and furious. His instinct was to force the young man to his knees.

"Bìnxìn has always gotten on well with everyone — it is only you who holds a grievance against him on every front! Don't think that because His Majesty values you, you can do as you please! To lay hands on a court official without sanction — and not for the first time — to conduct yourself with such lawlessness — should you not kneel before His Majesty immediately and plead for leniency?"

At all these words, Xie Yuanjing didn't so much as twitch an eyelid.

This matter was, in truth, something that could not really be made into anything serious. Investigated, it would take little effort to unravel.

Just now, the Emperor had offered only the lightest mention — hadn't even had the evidence laid out yet — which made it clear this was nothing more than a perfunctory gesture to appease an old minister.

But once the Marquis of Chengen inserted himself, and began dragging up the old case, the man on the high seat would inevitably grow annoyed.

Xie Yuanjing had read him perfectly. His father simply wanted to win a certain justice for Hé Bìnxìn — to use him as a stepping stone, to lift Hé Bìnxìn higher in the capital, and give him a stronger foothold going forward.

Xie Yuanjing let the Marquis of Chengen berate him without reaction.

He kept his eyes half-lowered.

The arm being pushed and jostled sent a dim ache through him — subtle, but enough to conjure, in a flash, the image of Lu Huaixi in the carriage just now, the worry in her eyes.

"Your Majesty — this old minister also finds the young Lord Xie too unruly. He acts without restraint, and with Your Majesty's trust to embolden him, he knows no law."

Lord Xùn also stepped forward, bowing his head:

"This old minister's student has never wronged a single person. Though he is of a similar age to Lord Xie, he has always held him in admiration. And yet Lord Xie looks down on all people, and not only that — he struck my student this seriously out of nothing but selfish interest! Your Majesty, you must see justice done for this old minister's student!"

The man on the high seat made no response. A weight of pressure settled over the hall.

The Emperor's silence bore down on everything. The Marquis of Chengen and Lord Xùn, who had still been pressing their case a moment ago, fell quiet.

After a while, the man above spoke — but not in answer. The Emperor looked at the figure standing in the center of the hall, his gaze falling to the arm at his side.

"Injured?"

"Your Majesty — I was set upon by attackers on the way here."

Xie Yuanjing's tone was unhurried.

The Marquis of Chengen did not push him to kneel again. He hesitated briefly, but soon set his face once more.

"What attacker would be so bold — and so conveniently timed?"

To hear those words from his own father made Xie Yuanjing, despite himself, almost laugh.

The Marquis of Chengen turned to the Emperor and bowed his head:

"Your Majesty, though Yuanjing is this minister's eldest son, guilt must be punished. The evidence is before us, and Yuanjing has a private grievance with Bìnxìn — this minister cannot and will not shield him in any way!"

The evidence pointed at Xie Yuanjing. On the surface, he did appear to be the one who had moved against this person. And there was the private grievance between them — even his own father didn't believe in his own son.

Lord Xùn pressed steadily from the side, closing in from every angle.

The Emperor on the high seat narrowed his eyes, feeling a headache of his own beginning. His old ministers were not easy to manage. He had assumed Xie Yuanjing, having followed him long enough, would know that now was not the moment for a direct confrontation.

But as soon as the Emperor opened his mouth to speak, Xie Yuanjing broke from his usual manner with unusual and unbending coldness.

He did not confess. But neither did he offer any defense, nor did he make any effort to clear his name or produce any witnesses. He simply spoke — and it was nothing short of outright defiance.

"Why should I prove my own innocence?"

Xie Yuanjing was openly reckless, his eyes carrying a red that spoke of someone with no intention of backing down.

"Lord Xùn barely registers on my list of concerns — let alone some unknown student. And as for what Father just said — whether I am his eldest son or not, that is a question worth examining."

When those words fell, the entire hall seemed to grow heavier with shadow.

—

In the Marquis's manor, Lu Huaixi walked back toward her courtyard. Her expression was unreadable — not visibly upset, not visibly at ease.

But those close to her knew: if everything were truly fine, the corner of her mouth would have carried just the faintest upward curve.

Yao Xu and Jing Shuang exchanged a glance and stayed quietly in step behind her.

It was only when nightfall came and every lamp in the courtyard had been lit that Lu Huaixi finally stirred.

She called Yao Xu over, about to ask her to take people back to the Lù estate — but before she could get the words out, Gong Fei came hurrying in.

"Young Madam, the Young Master left instructions before entering the palace. If he has not returned by nightfall, you are to rest well and not trouble yourself — and not involve the Lù family."

Lu Huaixi looked up, brow faintly creased.

"Why can't the Lù family be involved? He said there would be no trouble."

"There will be no trouble — Young Madam, please don't worry. The Young Master simply doesn't want your father drawn into this. After all, the Marquis has also entered the palace, and this may well involve certain older matters."

Gong Fei lowered his head:

"What's more, the Lù estate has been in enough of a difficult position lately. The elder branch has been somewhat caught in the aftermath already. He doesn't want your father to draw attention at a time like this, to give people things to say. This kind of matter — the Young Master can manage."

The hands hidden in Lu Huaixi's sleeves curled slowly inward.

She wanted instinctively to hold tight to something. But she felt his absence, and everything her hand closed around was hollow and empty. So she let go.

After a long while, she lowered her eyes.

"In the beginning — why did the Marquis intervene in that case? When Xie Yuanjing moved against that person — was it because that person also had a hand in the matter?"

Gong Fei paused, a faint hesitation crossing his face.

But he didn't make her wait long. He thought it over, and then spoke.

"Young Madam, the man's name is Hé Bìnxìn. His mother is a woman the Marquis once saved when he led his first campaign. The case at the time involved an imperial prince and certain elements of a former reign — His Majesty was furious, and almost no court official dared go near it."

Gong Fei's voice was measured and even as he continued:

"But Hé Bìnxìn happened to help someone — a person who had been drawn into the case — without realizing it. Hé Bìnxìn believed the person to be kind-hearted and didn't report him, even going so far as to protect him multiple times. When the matter grew larger, Hé Bìnxìn's mother was frightened of her son being implicated, and went to the Marquis to plead for his help."

"So the Marquis of Chengen was willing to risk the entire Marquis's household to come forward and protect Hé Bìnxìn?"

"Yes."

Even seeing Gong Fei nod in confirmation, Lu Huaixi still felt as though she must have heard wrong.

She could not begin to understand how anyone could grow so dim with age — and someone who had fought in campaigns and won honors with his life at that.

"Then why did Xie Yuanjing actually lay hands on him?"

He was not the kind of person who acted out of temporary anger.

Lu Huaixi did not for one moment believe Xie Yuanjing would strike someone over something like this, of all things — or that he would leave that kind of evidence against himself.

"The Young Master was indeed not moved to do anything against Hé Bìnxìn, but that person is not as candid and virtuous as people say. This servant was not present at the time — but it was clear that Hé Bìnxìn had deliberately provoked the Young Master into striking him."

Lu Huaixi's lips moved, but she said nothing more.

She wanted to ask how Xie Yuanjing could have been provoked so easily — but then she thought again, and it came to her: Xie Yuanjing was still a person. Why would he never be provoked? Why would he never feel fury?

He could be disciplined and composed. That didn't mean he was immune to anger.

Lu Huaixi felt a sudden wave of indignation rise in her chest — and alongside it, tangled up with it, something that felt very much like ache. The heaviness in her heart pressed heavier still.

chapters.title: What Business Is It Of Yours How We Sleep?
chapters.content:
After Gong Fei withdrew, the room quickly fell quiet.

Lu Huaixi gazed at the flickering candlelight on the wall and, without quite realizing it, drifted over to the low bed where Xie Yuanjing slept each night.

She sat down on it.

Thinking about how these past days he had been sleeping here — going to bed later than her, rising earlier than her, not even allowed the comfort of ice — Lu Huaixi felt like a very, very terrible person.

Jing Shuang came in to help her change.

Seeing her sit in silence without a word, she finally couldn't help offering a few words of comfort.

"Young Madam, please don't worry. If something were truly wrong with the Young Master, you wouldn't need to wait for word from the palace — the Old Master would have acted immediately."

Lu Huaixi paused without responding.

She knew, of course, that the manor's stillness meant Xie Yuanjing's situation was not yet critical.

But if it wasn't critical, she couldn't understand why there had still been no news — and why even the Marquis of Chengen had not yet returned.

Yet Xie Yuanjing had told her not to send anyone prying, and not to let the Lù family get involved. She couldn't find a single place to even ask a question.

"The Young Master has not returned at this hour — he almost certainly won't be leaving the palace tonight. Young Madam, you might as well rest early. Perhaps by tomorrow morning, the Young Master will be back."

Jing Shuang combed her hair, thought for a moment, and added:

"And there is still the connection through the late Empress. No matter how displeased His Majesty might be, he would never truly do anything to the Young Master. It's you we should be thinking of — if you exhaust yourself with worry over this, the Young Master will be upset when he returns."

The corners of Lu Huaixi's lips shifted slightly.

She looked up at the bronze mirror. Whether she had taken any of it in was unclear.

But she still, after the lamp was blown out, curled obediently into bed, closed her eyes, and didn't ask anyone for more news of Xie Yuanjing.

—

The next day, Lu Huaixi woke and lay looking at the patterns on the ceiling for a long while.

Yao Xu and the others, hearing movement, came in, brought water and food, kept her company, and even brought in some account ledgers. They came and went — but still, there was no news of Xie Yuanjing.

Lu Huaixi waited through another half day. She couldn't sit still any longer. She thought it over, and decided she would go to the First Madam's quarters again.

She had barely stepped out of the courtyard when a new bamboo mat arrived from outside.

It was visibly smaller than the bed — clearly made to order. One look told you it had been made especially for something specific.

Lu Huaixi's heart was stirred again. She moved closer to have a look, and when she raised her eyes, she spotted Mù Nianwēi nearby, craning her neck to peer over.

Her mood was already thoroughly sour, and she was in no temper to hold back. She walked straight over.

Mù Nianwēi had apparently not expected to run into Lu Huaixi on a day this hot, so close to midday.

Her expression flickered with discomfort. She touched her hair with one hand, then patted the sweat from her brow with a handkerchief.

"C-Cousin-in-law."

She stretched out a smile and said with forced composure, "It's so dreadfully hot. I was just taking a little stroll — Cousin-in-law's courtyard really is the most pleasant spot."

Lu Huaixi said nothing.

Mù Nianwēi knew that excuse was a rather weak one, and she didn't continue. But now that they had run into each other, the thought pressing at the back of her mind could not be suppressed any longer.

"Cousin-in-law, a few days ago I heard that a new bamboo mat was being made for Cousin's room — but the one that just arrived looks like a different size from the bed. It seems like it could only go on the low bed. Unless—"

Mù Nianwēi kept her voice low, as though in idle conversation, her tone gentle and unhurried.

But the prying beneath it was impossible to hide.

Lu Huaixi saw her walking directly into this herself — practically handing herself over to be scolded. She looked at her and gave a mild, faint smile.

"Unless what?"

"I'm sure I've just heard things wrong. Please don't be upset, Cousin-in-law."

Mù Nianwēi said quietly, "I only heard — someone say that Cousin and Cousin-in-law don't sleep in the same place at night, and that's why there would be different mats."

She had barely finished the sentence before she seemed to startle herself, and quickly added a line to cover it.

"I told whoever said it off on the spot. Cousin treats Cousin-in-law so well — of course they wouldn't be sleeping apart."

Lu Huaixi looked at her performing this with great seriousness, that expression of barely concealed eagerness to see her and Xie Yuanjing fall out — and she suddenly felt like laughing.

She stood where she was and glanced in the direction of the people who had delivered the mat, then looked back.

"You should find someone to marry, Cousin."

Lu Huaixi met her gaze and said plainly:

"You don't understand the first thing about it, and yet here you are prying into our bedroom affairs. Even as your cousin-in-law, this is a case where speaking makes me the one at fault, and staying silent makes me the one at fault too — isn't that putting me in an impossible position?"

The words came down one after another.

Mù Nianwēi blinked, momentarily stunned. A flush began to creep up her face.

Lu Huaixi said it and still didn't feel it was quite enough.

She thought back to the way Mù Nianwēi had been craning her neck and peering over, and while it had only struck her as faintly amusing before, right now it suddenly irritated her.

What business was it of hers how she and Xie Yuanjing slept?

"My husband and I — we sleep in the bed, we sleep on the low bed, we use both. If you're that curious, I can have someone send you some books and you can sort it out yourself. As for where we actually sleep on any given night — that depends on how warm I feel, which you wouldn't understand. From now on, don't ask, and don't concern yourself with it."

Mù Nianwēi received the full force of that.

Perhaps she hadn't expected to hear anything so direct, or perhaps she hadn't expected Lu Huaixi, who looked so gentle and easy-going, to say all that without so much as a blush — whatever the reason, Mù Nianwēi genuinely couldn't collect herself.

She was still in a daze even as she walked away.

Lu Huaixi couldn't be bothered to mind her. Having vented some of her frustration there, the heaviness in her chest had eased a little. She no longer felt like going to the First Madam's quarters.

She turned and went back to her room, sitting in the breeze from the fan.

Another half day slipped by, just like that.

Yao Xu replaced the tea with a calming flower brew and brought it to her.

"Young Madam, after that talking-to you gave her, the young miss looked positively stunned — this servant heard she went back and forgot to eat lunch."

"She came to pry on her own."

In ordinary circumstances, Lu Huaixi wouldn't have been so blunt about it.

Honestly, what did she know? She and Xie Yuanjing really were sleeping separately.

But Mù Nianwēi had picked the wrong time.

"Never mind her — but do let Gong Fei know about this. If no one in the courtyard had let something slip, how would she have known what went on in our room?"

"Yes, this servant understands."

When she finished, Lu Huaixi instinctively glanced toward the inner room.

Why wasn't Xie Yuanjing back yet? Without him here, she seemed unable to settle.

chapters.title: Come Back
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi's instructions made Yao Xu's smile fade instantly, her expression growing serious.

She hadn't known until recently that her young mistress and the Young Master were sleeping apart — but this kind of thing couldn't be hidden from those who were close.

Yao Xu simply thought it was because the Young Madam was young, and the Young Master was considerate.

Besides, a low bed was a low bed — it wasn't as though they never shared the same place at night.

But if this got out to the wrong ears, it would sound like a very different matter entirely.

"This servant will go right away."

Yao Xu set down what she was holding. "It's also a good time to have the meal sent up. You've barely eaten today — please try to eat something at dinner."

"Wait a moment before sending up the meal."

Lu Huaixi called her back. "If there's still no word a little while from now, go yourself to the Lù estate."

Xie Yuanjing had told her not to involve her father, not to let the Lù family get involved — but she couldn't just sit here doing nothing.

Not getting involved was one thing. Surely going to ask her mother was still permitted?

Lu Huaixi lay there listlessly, her fingertip tracing the pattern on the rim of her teacup.

She wondered whether Xie Yuanjing had eaten.

He had said he was willing to take a step back. But step back to where — that, Lu Huaixi had no answer for.

Just thinking about what it would be like if the two of them really returned to a state of distant politeness, never again seeing the true warmth he sometimes let through — the thought made her feel stifled and miserable.

She sat in the room for a while. The heat of the afternoon began to ease in the wind outside.

The clouds at the edge of the sky wore a rim of red, and the fading light spread in a wash of color.

Lu Huaixi rose to take a turn around the courtyard, but she had barely stepped under the eaves when she heard voices somewhere ahead.

"Still no word from the palace?"

No response — only silence.

After a moment, the same voice continued:

"The Young Master told everyone not to get involved — even kept the Young Madam from going to the Lù estate to ask. It's been a full day now. If the Young Master has truly angered His Majesty, it may already be too late to intervene."

"It won't come to that. The Young Master knows what he's doing."

Another voice answered quickly, a little lower in tone than the first.

"The Marquis followed him into the palace. He will certainly bring up the time the Young Master previously struck Hé Bìnxìn. The moment that comes up, it will drag out the old case — and remind the Emperor that his own judgment of people had once been wrong, that he was betrayed by one of the princes."

The voice turned cold. "His Majesty's anger will inevitably spill onto others. The Young Master cares deeply about the Young Madam, so naturally he doesn't want the Lù family's elder master to be caught in this."

"I understand that. I know the Young Master can look after himself. But there's still been no order from him — and if this were any other matter, fine, but if he's been detained and they're using punishment—"

"Even if punishment was used, the only person it would be used on is the Young Master himself—"

The words cut off. The speaker had spotted Lu Huaixi drawing near.

Both men pulled themselves together immediately, lowering their heads in greeting.

"This subordinate pays respects to the Young Madam."

Lu Huaixi stood there. There was very little color in her face.

She was naturally fairer than most people — but even so, there was always a faint delicate flush to her paleness, bright and pretty.

Right now, her face was nothing but an excessive white, the color even drained from her lips.

Just looking at her, you could almost feel the chill in her hands without touching them.

A flash of alarm crossed both men's faces. They didn't know how to recover, and their expressions were fraught.

But Lu Huaixi didn't press them.

She stood there for a moment, and then simply asked, "If punishment has been used — can he still... come back on his own?"

She had never seen Xie Yuanjing badly hurt before. She didn't want to see it now.

Though she had always reminded herself to keep her distance, to wait for the divorce after a year — she had always loved watching Xie Yuanjing on horseback, full of presence and vigor.

He was handsome. Even doing nothing, he was simply very good to look at.

Lu Huaixi wasn't sure where her thoughts had wandered to.

One moment she was thinking of his teasing manner. The next she was desperately wanting news of him. And then, in that urgency, she caught a glimpse of her own heart.

That Xie Yuanjing would think ahead for her father's sake — did that mean something between them had indeed become a little different?

The two men in front of her didn't answer immediately. But that single moment of silence was its own truest answer.

Lu Huaixi came back to herself. She knew she couldn't go on waiting like this.

She was Xie Yuanjing's wife. In the eyes of everyone outside, they were one. There was no reason for her to do nothing.

"Jing Shuang — have the carriage prepared."

"Young Madam, you—"

"Send Yao Xu back to the Lù estate to find Mother. You come with me to find Shen Zhouzhu. And have someone take a letter to Sister Xiǎnyǎ, asking her to inquire with Eldest Brother Zhou about what happened at court today. If there's still no news by tomorrow morning, I'll seek an audience with Noble Consort Dé."

Lu Huaixi's voice was steady.

The faint tremor that had threaded through her voice moments ago when she asked if he could come back on his own — it was gone now.

She finished, then looked back at the two men.

"If he has been detained — what kind of punishment would they use?"

"Young Madam—"

The guard in front hesitated, and after a brief moment's thought, said through gritted teeth:

"The punishments are those you might expect, but the Young Master isn't necessarily truly detained. All of this is this subordinate's unfounded speculation. Young Madam, please don't take it to heart."

Lu Huaixi knew she wouldn't get anything more out of them now.

She nodded, with no intention of pressing them, then lowered her eyes and quietly turned away.

Back in the room, she changed her clothes.

It was late in the day — she couldn't go to see Shen Zhouzhu dressed as a married lady.

Lu Huaixi's color was genuinely poor by now. But when Jing Shuang came hurrying in, she still gave her a small smile.

"Is the carriage ready?"

She paused, and then felt something was wrong.

She thought of Jing Shuang's hurried steps just now, and looked at her with a trace of sudden anxiety. "Does this mean Xie Yuanjing has sent word?"

"Yes, Young Madam — the Young Master is out of the palace!"

Jing Shuang couldn't contain her relief. "Just now a message came from Gong Fei — Princess Qīnghé interceded for the Young Master. Though the Young Master refused to confess to the charges, His Majesty relented and personally ordered the matter investigated."

"Intercession... was he punished?"

Lu Huaixi had caught the implication at once.

Jing Shuang faltered a moment, but she knew this couldn't be hidden, and no longer tried to conceal it.

"Yes. Last night the Young Master endured a night of punishment. Today Princess Qīnghé pleaded before His Majesty, and Noble Consort Shū and Consort Róng each put in a word as well. His Majesty's anger eased and he gave the order to release him."

Jing Shuang said this, then quickly checked the expression on the face before her and hurried on:

"Young Madam, please don't worry — the Young Master was still able to leave the palace on his own, which means the injuries are not too severe. It's just that the road may take some time, and this servant doesn't know exactly when he left the palace, so he'll likely not arrive at the manor until later."

Hearing that he was still conscious, Lu Huaixi stopped speaking.

Her hands were very cold. After the taut, stretched thing inside her finally let go, her mind went blank — so hollow and disoriented she didn't even know what else to ask.

After a long silence, she finally spoke in a hoarse murmur. "Having someone intercede is good. I was starting to think he truly didn't want anyone to help him."

"He wouldn't, Young Madam. The Young Master must have had his own plan — he wouldn't have endured it for nothing."

Reason and composure were pushed back by the intensity of what had been building.

The steadiness Lu Huaixi had held on to all this time began, piece by piece, to dissolve once the tension released.

She listened to Jing Shuang's words, and then, without warning, a different feeling surfaced.

"Then why didn't he say anything? He obviously could have had people intercede — he obviously could have let others help — why didn't he let me do anything? Why couldn't I even know what was happening?"

Lu Huaixi found, as she was saying it, that she was close to tears — and she didn't want Jing Shuang to see.

She sniffed, turned away, and walked into the inner room.

"I need to change."

She said it in a muffled voice. "I'll do it myself. You don't need to help me."

Jing Shuang couldn't bear the sight of Lu Huaixi holding her distress in like this.

Her own heart twisted, and yet she couldn't think of a single word that would help.

Until sounds drifted in from outside. She turned her head, intending to ask someone to send in something sweet, to help settle the person within.

It seemed someone had arrived outside.

Jing Shuang went out — and the moment she raised her eyes, she went still.

The person they had just been saying would not arrive for some time had walked into the courtyard, carrying a cold stillness on him that displaced the summer heat.

Except for the slight pallor of his face, nothing seemed outwardly wrong.

"This servant greets the Young Master."

"Mm."

The newcomer's step paused. Before he mounted the stone stairs, he said in a quiet, even tone, "Go to Mother's courtyard. Tell her I'll come by later."

"Yes."

Jing Shuang answered — then thought of the Young Madam inside with her reddened eyes, hiding herself away. She summoned her courage, and said one more thing.

"Young Master."

She kept her head down and spoke softly. "The Young Madam is crying."

Xie Yuanjing went still where he stood.

Something pricked his heart. Across that cold, composed face passed a flicker of something he had never shown before — something lost and at a loss.

chapters.title: I Only Want To Spend My Days By Your Side
chapters.content:
The room was very quiet.

Lu Huaixi had sent everyone away.

Alone, she changed out of the outfit she had dressed in to go out, and put back on the clothes from before.

But the outer robe wouldn't sit right, no matter how she adjusted it.

She bent her head over it, pulling and tugging, feeling worse with every second. She finally gave up, stopped, and raised her hand to wipe her eyes.

As she wiped, the back of her hand grew damp, and her vision began to blur.

The corners of her lips were pressed together — whether because she didn't want to cry right now, or because she was being stubborn with herself, she couldn't say.

She knew she should be relieved. Yet after letting out that held breath, she found herself suddenly overwhelmed by something that felt a great deal like grievance.

But why she felt aggrieved — whether she was simply being unreasonable — she didn't know.

Lu Huaixi had no intention of letting anyone else see it.

She wiped her eyes once more, then looked down at her sash.

With slightly damp fingers, she reached for the waistband and pulled at it, teeth pressing into her lip as she tried to straighten the robe.

Just as she was about to give up entirely, the faintest sound came from the outer room.

Then, not long after, a faint fragrance drifted in from the incense burner.

Lu Huaixi assumed it was Jing Shuang coming back to add incense powder.

Without turning around, she lowered her voice. "You don't need to come and help me. I want to do it myself."

The voice she was forcing to sound composed carried the heavy weight of a stuffed nose underneath. Even though she was trying her best to sound unbothered, anyone could hear that she was not.

The sounds seemed to stop.

Lu Huaixi bent her head again.

Jing Shuang would never come in after she'd said not to.

She stood there, not wanting to deal with the robe, not wanting to move.

The evening breeze had grown stronger than it had been during the day, and it rustled against the latticed window, breaking through the silence of the room.

A single tear fell from Lu Huaixi's face and hit the floor, blooming open in a round shape, spreading out instantly.

Her nose went completely blocked. She was thinking she would let herself cry just this once, and then go outside and wait for Xie Yuanjing — and then, in the next instant, someone embraced her from behind.

One hand covered hers. The other settled at her waist. A chin came to rest against the curve of her neck.

"Why are you crying?"

Xie Yuanjing's voice fell alongside his breath.

He held her in a circle, his arms gathering force, pressing her back against his chest.

It was an intimacy unlike any before — and in this dim, hushed moment, it wound around Lu Huaixi like a tendril of climbing vine, slowly and thoroughly, until every last trace of unease inside her settled and dispersed.

Lu Huaixi forgot to breathe. She didn't dare turn around.

She only felt the warmth starting from her back, wrapped around her, and where they pressed together, a tingling, aching sensation rose — leaving her flustered, and yet entirely unwilling to pull away.

"Don't cry. Not coming back last night was my fault. Not telling you — that was my fault."

Xie Yuanjing raised one hand and touched her face, his thumb brushing the corner of her eye, then dropping to her chin, tilting her head slightly to the side.

"It won't happen again."

And so Xie Yuanjing saw it — Lu Huaixi's reddened eyes.

His chest tightened. The place in his heart that had been stung began to ache again.

"Last night I kept thinking of you. Wondering if you were worried, if you were frightened, if you were anxious. Then later I heard you had been very good, and I thought I would wait until I came back and tell you slowly then... I was wrong. If I had known you would be this heartbroken, I would have found a way—"

"I don't believe you."

Lu Huaixi didn't let him finish.

She had spent all that time not understanding why she had felt those inexplicable emotions.

It was only when Xie Yuanjing appeared, softening his voice, saying one thing after another — that she suddenly understood. It was her caring.

She cared about his safety. About what he was going through.

She cared that the person closest to him in that moment hadn't been her. And she cared that Xie Yuanjing hadn't trusted her enough to believe she could help.

But right now, Lu Huaixi didn't want to think about any of that.

She turned around, and they stood face to face — close enough that she only had to tilt her head up to touch his chin with her lips.

And then, in the fraction of a second while Xie Yuanjing was still startled, Lu Huaixi followed her instincts and held him.

The tears she had almost managed to hold back came undone all at once, like beads off a broken string — like that day at Huiquebo, yet somehow different too.

"You don't tell me anything — you just say there won't be any trouble, you just tell me to wait... other people can help you and I can't... everyone else can know what's happening to you and I can't... if you're not going to tell me anything, why did you marry me? You should have married someone you could actually talk to—"

Before Lu Huaixi could finish, she felt herself lifted.

Xie Yuanjing sat down on the bed and settled her onto his lap, then lowered his head and kissed her.

His lips were soft, faintly tinged with the salt of her tears. He caught her lower lip gently, tender and cautious.

Lu Huaixi didn't resist at all. She tilted her face up, and apart from still crying, became entirely, quietly still.

That kind of response was enough to pull Xie Yuanjing under completely.

He was no longer gentle — he became a little rough, with the flavour of someone claiming what was his, coaxing and tracing with a possessiveness that was entirely unrestrained.

He would even, when she needed to catch her breath, draw back just slightly and press against the corner of her mouth, asking her why she was so easy to hold, why her waist was so soft, why she was being so wonderfully, unexpectedly pliant.

At last Lu Huaixi cried no more. Her nose finally cleared.

But then her brow furrowed.

She shifted her arm, wanting to push aside his robe where her tears had stained it.

Before she could raise her hand, Xie Yuanjing stopped.

He touched the corner of her mouth again, reluctantly, then tilted his head and pressed his lips to her earlobe.

"I'm injured."

Xie Yuanjing's voice came close to her ear, his breath somewhat uneven. "Seeing you just now, I forgot. But I'm not quite holding together anymore."

Feeling her urgency and panic, he drew her close against him.

"Let me lie down for a while. In your bed. This time I'm telling you — please don't be angry."

In that moment, Lu Huaixi truly felt as though her heart had been seized by Xie Yuanjing and wrung apart.

She had never felt worse about herself for not having thought of something — and never more furious at him for having held on while injured.

But she didn't dare push him, and the arms she'd been holding him with drew back, not knowing where to put themselves.

"Don't hold me anymore — lie down properly. I'll go call the physician."

Lu Huaixi moved to get up, and suddenly remembered that when he had lit the incense earlier it had been to mask the smell of medicine. She blinked, and another tear fell.

"Where are you hurt? Tell me so I can call Gong Zhuo — you sleep in the bed and don't move—"

"Wait."

Xie Yuanjing took hold of her again, his thumb resting on the back of her hand, his gaze earnest and deep.

"This time — were you crying because you were worried about me? Just now, why did you let me kiss you? Why did you hold me?"

He looked at her, not letting her go, and said slowly, "I only want to spend my days by your side. There's no one else I could marry. What about you?"

chapters.title: I'll Learn Properly What It Means To Be A Married Couple
chapters.content:
Before Lu Huaixi understood anything about the feelings between a man and a woman, she had listened to her elder sister talk about marriage and wondered what kind of person she would spend her life with someday.

She had decided he must be someone capable. She liked heroes.

Then she watched how her elder brother-in-law always spoke to her elder sister in a gentle voice, and she revised her thinking — he didn't have to be everyone's hero, but he had to be like her elder brother-in-law. Someone she herself thought was good.

Even if she couldn't bring herself to like him, at the very least he had to be the right match.

Then came the push toward the palace, her refusal, and then — Xie Yuanjing.

At first she didn't like him. She was afraid of him, and didn't like the Marquis's household — it felt uncomfortable.

But Xie Yuanjing was so genuinely good to her.

Even though that goodness came wrapped in the reasoning of the Lù family connection, she still found him different from the person people described when they talked about the eldest young master of the Marquis's household.

So falling for Xie Yuanjing was not, in the end, a very difficult thing.

Only she was clear-headed, and she weighed things carefully.

She had chosen what seemed like a more stable kind of freedom, and pulled her feelings back.

But then Xie Yuanjing became even better to her. He said he didn't want a divorce. And then he kissed her.

Lu Huaixi had thought she'd made up her mind clearly — what she didn't want was something she simply wouldn't want. But now she found, all at once, that it seemed she couldn't hold to that anymore.

During the day and night he'd been without news, she had been thinking about him the whole time.

She had also been quietly regretting that she hadn't said something gentle on the carriage, hadn't taken the time before he entered the palace to talk with him properly.

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes.

The corners of her mouth had drawn tight at some point without her noticing. Her other hand was slowly clenching around her own sleeve.

She saw clearly what she felt, and she knew what ought to be said right now. But she was also uncertain — uncertain whether she should take the risk. Whether Xie Yuanjing's caring for her was worth more than her freedom.

"All right. I'm not asking anymore. Don't be unhappy."

The silence was broken by Xie Yuanjing.

He looked at the downcast eyes before him and smiled slightly.

But the light in his eyes dimmed — like this unlit room, dim and quiet.

"Last night while I was being punished, I was thinking — perhaps that thing I said before entering the palace shouldn't count after all. I've barely managed to say it, and I don't want to take a step back. But then I thought — if my closeness is truly making you miserable, making you unwilling to even talk to me — then perhaps—"

"Where would you step back to?"

Lu Huaixi interrupted him. Her voice was very small, but it sounded as though she had gathered a great deal of courage.

"What do you mean, step back? You don't tell me anything, you don't let me know anything — what we have already isn't much like being married. And you want to step back even further?"

"That's not—"

"I was crying this time because I was worried about you. And because you didn't want me — because you didn't believe I could help you. I cried for a long time. If you weren't injured right now, I'd be telling you that I hate you."

Xie Yuanjing went still, momentarily lost.

Lu Huaixi's words struck against his heart, one blow after another.

He hadn't been prepared — and yet within that impact, he caught a glimpse of the brightness he had been looking for.

"You said you've barely managed to say it, that you don't want to step back — but you said it so easily. And you've been pushing me toward you this whole time, without ever really intending to let me choose. Now you say you can step back? Then go ahead — step back and show me."

Lu Huaixi was a little angry.

When she finished, she didn't look at him — she remembered she needed to call someone, and turned around. Then she sensed him sitting up behind her.

He let out a few quiet coughs. When he spoke again, his voice was even rougher than before. Hearing it, Lu Huaixi immediately regretted saying any of that just then.

"You're right that I tricked you. I can't step back, and I don't want to let you choose. But you just said you were worried about me — that you cried for a long time because of me. Xīer, why?"

Xie Yuanjing held fast with a stubbornness that ran through his whole body.

Even as the smell of blood slowly filled the room, overcoming even the scent of medicine, he stayed upright against all of it, refusing to let go, determined to have an answer.

Lu Huaixi looked down at his hand, gripping hers.

The knuckles showed white with effort, a control unlike his usual self — and where he held her, it actually hurt a little.

Her chest trembled.

In this moment, she felt she had already finished gambling.

"You know why."

Lu Huaixi said quietly. "You've already seen it. Why do you still have to ask?"

Her voice was like gauze fine as a cicada's wing — falling into Xie Yuanjing's ear, tracing across his heart. Light as air, soft as breath.

"Don't do this again. Don't keep everything from me. Don't make your plans on your own. And don't keep leaving me outside of them. That's not what married couples do. If you trust me so little, then we shouldn't—"

The harsh thing couldn't quite be said all the way.

Lu Huaixi sniffled, and very unimpressively felt like crying again.

But Xie Yuanjing refused to let her hide. Refused to let her leave.

He leaned forward and held her, with a force like he wanted to press her into his very bones.

"Your wound—"

His answer was a low, husky laugh.

There was a thread of weakness in it — and yet beneath it, the distinctive depth of a man's voice, close against her ear, strangely and utterly compelling.

He paid no attention to the pain traveling through him. He only tightened his arms.

This was enough. He had believed, before now, that he would hear nothing at all.

"On the way back, I heard that you scolded Mù Nianwēi."

Xie Yuanjing spoke slowly, like a whispered confidence between two people close to each other, broken into pieces. "You said we sleep together as a married couple, and told her to mind her own business."

"What it means to be a married couple — I'll learn properly."

He said it again, but his voice was getting fainter.

Only — just before that voice faded entirely, he seemed to remember something. The force that had eased came back, as though he wanted to say more.

But in the next instant, a muffled sound escaped the corner of his mouth. It was clear he had pushed himself to his absolute limit.

Lu Huaixi was badly frightened. Her wide, red-rimmed eyes filled with a desperate brightness.

"Don't talk anymore, don't say anything else — let go of me first. You can say all of this later."

"I can't leave it unsaid."

Xie Yuanjing looked at the curling lashes quivering before him, and the urgency in those eyes was not pretend. It looked like exactly the caring he had been hoping for.

His chest was warm. He pressed a kiss to the corner of her lips once more.

"I didn't have anyone help me. This whole thing was deliberate on my part. Princess Qīnghé didn't intercede for my sake — she had her own reasons. And I never left you out of my plans...

"I'm not quite holding on right now. Don't cry alone. Wait for me to wake — I won't be in any danger. The wounds only look serious. After I fall asleep, anything concerning me in this household — you make the decisions..."

His voice grew smaller and smaller, until the room fell entirely silent.

The arms Xie Yuanjing had wrapped around her slid down, and his deep, dark eyes closed, little by little. All that remained was the faint sound of his breathing by her ear.

Lu Huaixi's heart dropped.

She should have been frantic — but when she truly saw Xie Yuanjing close his eyes, she went oddly calm.

With her own hands, cold as ice, she worked carefully to lay him back on the bed.

When she stood, her knees buckled and she nearly fell.

But she only raised her hand and wiped her eyes, dried the tears, and made herself completely steady.

When she opened the door, Gong Zhuo was already waiting outside with the others.

Lu Huaixi stepped aside to let them and the physician in, then asked Gong Zhuo how long he had been there.

Gong Zhuo let the physician through with the others, then bowed his head toward Lu Huaixi.

"Young Madam — this subordinate came with his people as soon as the Young Master entered the courtyard."

He didn't try to hide it. "The Young Master said he needed to speak with you first. If you hadn't opened the door and come out, no matter what sounds came from inside — even if someone called out — it meant the conversation wasn't finished, and no one was to enter."

Something acid and aching welled up in Lu Huaixi's chest. She didn't speak.

She lowered her eyes and waited for the redness around them to fade before she raised her head again.

Whether the room was too dim, or whether Xie Yuanjing looked too frail — Lu Huaixi's heart was suspended in the air again, unable to settle anywhere, heavy and suffocating.

But she knew she couldn't let any panic show right now.

She looked into the room and forced her voice to calm.

"Since this was done deliberately — then news of his injuries should be allowed to circulate."

Seeing Gong Zhuo nod, Lu Huaixi pressed down her emotions and asked, "Has the Marquis returned to the manor?"

"Young Madam — not yet."

chapters.title: A Standoff
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi didn't know what her own face looked like right now — but she imagined it was not a pleasant sight.

She was not Xie Yuanjing, and yet hearing those words, she was already beginning to feel angry.

"If he hasn't returned, send someone to find him. Whether he comes back or not is his business — but he must be told that the Young Master is gravely injured and unconscious."

Lu Huaixi's voice carried a coldness that made her sound nothing like the person she had been inside the room moments ago.

"Make sure the search is conspicuous. He is this man's father — he has no grounds to stand apart from this."

And how fitting — to let others see clearly what a distinguished Marquis of Chengen chose to do, at the very moment his own son lay injured.

Lu Huaixi held her handkerchief tight and had no intention of restraining herself.

Even if the bond between father and son was already broken beyond repair, she would not allow Xie Yuanjing to be the one who appeared in the wrong. If the Marquis of Chengen had chosen to shield others instead of his own son — then she would shield him.

Gong Zhuo heard, beneath the Young Madam's even voice, the quiet indignation and anger that hadn't quite been contained.

He gave nothing away on his face — but inwardly, he felt a small measure of surprise, and a small measure of joy on his master's behalf.

There were things the Young Master would not stoop to do, and things that were not his place to do. But the Young Madam was different. She had the standing, and the ability, to speak up in his defense.

"This subordinate will send people immediately."

Lu Huaixi went back inside. While the physician examined the injuries, she finally saw — with her own eyes — the wounds across Xie Yuanjing's body, and the sight was enough to make your heart seize.

No one would have known that the woman standing there — calm and composed and methodical in every way — was crushing the hand hidden in her sleeve with the force of her grip, because she was so afraid.

When Old Master Xie arrived, the candles in the room had already been lit.

He stepped into the inner chamber, his expression somewhat grave.

Lu Huaixi rose and addressed him as Grandfather, then moved aside and made room.

He looked at the man lying on the bed with his eyes closed, his face revealing no alarm — still carrying the dignity of age.

But there was a brief unsteadiness in his breath that betrayed the old man's worry.

Only when he had confirmed that no lasting harm had been done did Old Master Xie regain his composure.

He stood there for a while. When the room had been left to just Gong Zhuo, he looked toward Lu Huaixi.

"Sending people to find his father — was that your instruction?"

"Yes, Grandfather. That was this daughter-in-law's order."

Old Master Xie's expression gave nothing away. But those sharp eyes carried a testing, penetrating quality.

Lu Huaixi did not lose her footing. She met Old Master Xie's gaze, and said, with quiet steadiness:

"My husband has returned gravely injured. The Marquis may choose not to inquire — but he cannot be permitted not to know."

"Are you aware that if this is pushed into the open, there will be no room left for father and son to reconcile?"

"Even if it isn't pushed into the open, it will still come out — the Marquis going to the palace on someone else's behalf, making unfounded accusations against his own son."

Lu Huaixi kept her voice calm throughout, meeting Old Master Xie's gaze without a trace of fear.

"My husband does not know when he will wake. And even when he does, he will certainly not speak in his own defense. But this was clearly caused by the Marquis taking another's side — and when word of that spreads, if people say he was disrespectful to his father, cold-hearted and arrogant — who will speak for him?"

Silence fell over the room.

Old Master Xie said nothing — but he also made no effort to hold back the pressure that decades as a high-ranking official had instilled in him.

After a long while, just as Gong Zhuo was about to step forward and say something in his Young Madam's defense, Old Master Xie finally responded.

"The circumstances of your marriage, when it comes down to it, are not what they appear. The two of you were forced into each other's company, so it is no fault of yours that you don't know Yuanjing's character."

"And what is his character?"

Lu Huaixi suddenly smiled — but it was a floating, unanchored smile, nowhere near her eyes.

Old Master Xie could see clearly the dissatisfaction pressing beneath her expression, and the faint mockery in that smile.

He didn't take offense. Instead, something about the look in her eyes — her unwillingness to let it rest — made him reconsider this second daughter of the Lù family.

"His whole heart is given to the Xie family's standing and honor. A rift between father and son is damaging to the Xie family. Arguing about who is right and who is wrong with your own father is the work of someone without capability. He does not need anyone to stand up for him, and he doesn't need anyone to vent his anger. If he could not shoulder even this much, he never would have held his position as the eldest young master of this household."

He paused, then continued:

"You and he are not truly husband and wife. He naturally keeps certain things restrained in front of you. The goodwill you showed in wanting to reclaim some justice for him — the Xie family takes note of it. When the two of you part ways in the future, the Marquis's household will not allow you to suffer. We will continue to be a support to you. But this matter — do not involve yourself any further."

Lu Huaixi suddenly wanted to ask whether Old Master Xie was being this magnanimous because there was another candidate outside — someone who was, in effect, an elder grandson. Whether the Xie family still had a second option if Xie Yuanjing fell — another person ready to take up the Marquis of Chengen's position.

But she thought about it, and didn't say it.

In the end, it was only the Xie family's internal affairs. They hadn't even truly acknowledged her as a daughter-in-law — what was there for her to contest?

She was only standing up for Xie Yuanjing.

"Has the Old Master ever asked him?"

Having been reminded of this year's marriage arrangement, Lu Huaixi couldn't even be bothered with the honorific anymore.

It wasn't out of spite — she just had things she needed to say, or she wouldn't feel right.

"Has the Old Master ever truly asked him whether he doesn't care about these things? Has he asked whether he can truly feel at peace with his own father's partiality? If not — then the Old Master may not know his character quite as well as he thinks."

Before Old Master Xie could respond, Lu Huaixi smiled again.

"After the divorce — whether the Xie family is there to back me up or not doesn't matter. My father and mother would never let me suffer. Neither would my elder brother. Even my married elder sister wouldn't allow it. And I genuinely don't quite understand the Old Master's meaning — cherishing the eldest grandson, yet taking no care for the eldest grandson's actual life."

The room seemed to tip into a standoff. Gong Zhuo stood to the side with nothing but anxiety on his face.

He had been at his master's side long enough to see clearly that the Young Master had truly fallen for the Young Madam.

And yet now, with the Old Master's single declaration that this wasn't a real marriage, the person the Young Master had managed with such effort to draw a little closer was being pushed back out again.

Gong Zhuo was about to step in and try to explain something on his master's behalf — but just then, sounds came from outside the door. Something hitting the floor. The splintering of something broken.

In the next instant, someone entered from outside.

"Father, what did you just say? What do you mean by 'not a true marriage'?"

The First Madam came in, startled and furious, too agitated to hold back a cough.

She asked as she walked forward, with anxious eyes moving to the person on the bed.

When she saw her son — her son who had never once collapsed in front of her — lying there with not a shade of color on his face, her vision swam and she nearly fainted on the spot.

But she steadied herself quickly, and something seemed to occur to her — and then her expression went hard as stone.

"I don't care what relationship Huaixi and Yuanjing have. What Father told Huaixi not to do — I will do."

Her reddened eyes were fierce. She said it one word at a time: "Xie Zǐzhāng thinks he can use my son to prop up someone else? In his dreams."

chapters.title: Moved to Another Room
chapters.content:
The First Madam's arrival brought another brief silence to the room.

The true nature of the marriage could not be concealed, and Old Master Xie had no intention of concealing it any further.

But more than that, what was written across the First Madam's face was anger.

"All these years I have never mistreated the concubines in his household. If Xie Zǐzhāng had brought that woman into the Marquis's household through the front door, openly and honestly, I would not have said a single word about any of it! But he chose to keep her hidden outside, to deceive me and coax me into marrying him! And even after the wedding, he never once mentioned her — never mentioned that she existed, never mentioned that she had borne him a son!"

The steadiness and composure that usually marked the First Madam's face was entirely buried now beneath something fierce and consuming.

Her eyes were hard and dark, with a faint glimmer at the corners — but rather than softening her, it only sharpened the edge in her gaze.

"Now that the roots are established and the child is grown, he begins letting them surface, one occasion after another. And on top of that, he intends to use my son as a stepping stone to build that person up. How dare he! Does he truly think that because I've never made a scene, it means I can't bear to lose the title of Marchioness?!"

Lu Huaixi listened without speaking.

She thought that what the First Madam needed right now was not someone else's response.

She stood where she was and listened as the woman in front of her continued.

"If Yuanjing hadn't been harmed, I wouldn't have given that pair a second thought. But Xie Zǐzhāng has pushed things too far! Today — Father, whether you intend to charge me with disrespect or not — I am saying this here and now. Even if the day comes when I am no longer this Marchioness, Hé Bìnxìn will never change his name and enter this household. And the Xie family will never have a second eldest young master!"

It was said with force, and there was nothing to argue against it.

Old Master Xie's expression was not good — but he said nothing to reprimand her, which was unusually restrained.

"The Xie family will only have Yuanjing as its eldest young master. The Xie family does not take in just anyone."

He frowned. "I've already sent people to summon Zǐzhāng back. The matter from years ago is no longer your concern. That woman and her son have nothing to do with the Xie family, whatever happens. While I am here, no one will touch Yuanjing's position."

"They certainly can't touch it — if Xie Zǐzhāng hadn't kept interfering, does Hé Bìnxìn have the ability on his own to become entangled with Yuanjing? I've already lost Wénxiāo. Xie Zǐzhāng will not lay a hand on Yuanjing!"

The First Madam's laugh was cold — but aware of the person lying unconscious nearby, she swallowed the rest.

Whether Xie Zǐzhāng came back today or not, this was not going to end quietly.

Old Master Xie heard the meaning in her words perfectly, and his expression darkened further.

But perhaps thinking of the lost grandson, something of the severity went out of his face, and still he did not allow himself to grow angry.

"Very well. Whatever is to be done — all of it can wait until Yuanjing wakes. For now, the most important thing is that Yuanjing is safe."

Old Master Xie said no more, and he offered no defense of his son. Only as he was leaving did he look once more at Lu Huaixi, standing quietly to the side with an expression that revealed nothing.

The Lù family had raised her well.

Even at her most angry, this second daughter of the Lù family had not lost the bearing of a highborn young lady.
