Only that one slip — calling him Old Master Xie instead of Grandfather — still carried the faintest trace of a child's temper.

Stepping out of the room, someone came to offer counsel. Old Master Xie waved them off and walked in silence into the night.

In the room, the First Madam pressed down her emotions and asked again about the severity of Xie Yuanjing's injuries.

Lu Huaixi stood to the side. Except for the faint stir in her eyes when they moved to the bed, she showed very little else.

If someone had asked her right now what she was thinking, she probably couldn't have said.

It was something like the ease that comes with no longer having to hide anything. And yet also something that felt rather like the deflation that follows being told clearly where you stand.

"This marriage arrangement of yours — when does it end?"

With no one else left in the room, the First Madam turned to look at Lu Huaixi again.

This daughter-in-law — she had gone from uncertainty to acceptance to genuine affection.

She had just begun to feel this was a good match — only to discover that from the very beginning, it had all been false.

She could turn her face against Old Master Xie. But she could not turn her face against this girl who had married into the Marquis's household and would carry the name of a divorced woman when she left.

Especially not when this girl had just been standing up for Yuanjing moments ago.

"Lù Master has helped Yuanjing several times in recent days. I imagine your family knows the nature of your relationship with each other."

"Not all of them. My grandmother doesn't know. My elder brother and elder sister don't know either."

"Then your marriage arrangement—"

"One year."

Lu Huaixi looked up. "My arrangement with him is one year."

The First Madam's lips moved. She seemed unable to find the right words.

But Lu Huaixi could see clearly what was in her eyes — disappointment, resignation, and something that could only be described as a quiet, unnamed pity.

She wasn't certain of her read — she only knew that she felt unsettled right now as well.

The Xie family seemed to have drawn a line with her — not too close, not too far. Starting with Old Master Xie, and then the First Madam.

She remained only herself — Lu Huaixi — with no real bond connecting her to any of them. So naturally, she and Xie Yuanjing could not be expected to be close either.

"First Madam — I'm sorry."

Lu Huaixi thought it over, and offered the apology first.

She remembered the expression on the First Madam's face when she had come through the door just now.

Had the fury over the Marquis of Chengen not overtaken everything else, she imagined the First Madam would already have been demanding answers.

Fortunately, the First Madam was not in too agitated a state right now.

"This is perhaps not my place to say — but he cannot say it right now, and there's no one left but me."

"He's always done things his own way. If he hadn't already had a plan, this marriage would never have been possible to arrange. And your family — they can't have been very eager for him to take you, at the time."

The Marquis's household had been going through difficult times. The Lù family had raised such a fine daughter — there were plenty of other choices to be had.

Lu Huaixi said nothing.

The First Madam didn't wait long before continuing. "That low bed — he was the one sleeping on it?"

Hearing the title of Mother replaced with something cooler, the First Madam felt simultaneously exasperated and strangely disoriented.

She couldn't think of who to be angry at. In any case, it certainly wasn't the person in front of her.

Lu Huaixi followed the First Madam's gaze to the low bed, was quiet for a moment, then nodded.

"Yes."

The person on the bed still lay with closed eyes. The room still carried the heavy scent of medicine.

With the nature of their relationship laid bare — no particular bond, no real closeness — Lu Huaixi found she no longer knew what to say.

She didn't speak. The First Madam didn't ask anything more.

A long while later, when Jing Shuang brought in medicine, the First Madam finally spoke again.

"I'll have someone prepare a new room. You can stay there for the time being. Yuanjing is seriously injured, so naturally it would not be proper to sleep in the same space — even if people find out, no one will say anything."

The words landed in Lu Huaixi's chest like a stone — heavy and blocking.

Jing Shuang, holding what she'd brought in, also paused, and instinctively looked over at her young mistress.

The First Madam hadn't noticed. She continued in a lowered voice:

"Once he has recovered, I'll have him moved to another room. This room is better than most — you can go on living here for the rest of the time... The two of you really should have told me sooner. One year—"

One year was truly very fast. The First Madam didn't even need to do the counting.

"This marriage arrangement of his — when it comes down to it, it was reckless of him. Whatever his reasons, he should never have used your reputation to carry out his plans. As his mother, it is I who should be apologizing to you."

"That's not quite how it was."

"You don't need to speak on his behalf."

chapters.title: Perhaps It's Better She Never Truly Married In
chapters.content:
The First Madam seemed to have composed herself.

She looked at the person before her, thought back to the exchange that had just unfolded in this room, and found herself suddenly feeling — perhaps it was better that Lù Huaixi had never truly married in.

The Xie family had three branches. In which of them was the master or the young master not cold-hearted and ruthless? In which of them was the inner household not a tangle of competing complications?

Xie Zǐzhāng, to be sure, had deep feelings — for the first woman he had rescued, the first woman who had followed him. He had never forgotten her.

And yet why had he never married her? Simply because her standing was insufficient.

"Being with Yuanjing, you must have endured no small amount of hardship. When he came seeking you, he must have told you directly — and perhaps even used a little coercion and incentive along the way."

"I wasn't mistreated."

Lu Huaixi interrupted the First Madam, the hand at her side curling quietly inward.

"I agreed to this marriage. It was not recklessness on his part, and he didn't truly coerce me. I also had something I needed from him. So what we had was... a mutual arrangement."

The candle in the room let out a sudden sharp crackle as those words fell.

The light reflected on the wall flared and jumped at the gap of air pushed through the latticed window.

Lu Huaixi said that phrase — a mutual arrangement — and seemed to feel a little lighter. But in the very next moment, a quiet sadness came over her.

The beginning of what was between her and Xie Yuanjing — looking at it plainly, it really hadn't been a good one.

"The two of you..."

The First Madam was silent for a moment. Finally she shook her head.

"Marriage is not something to be taken lightly. When Yuanjing wakes I will speak with him. However it came about — the fact that he put you in the position of carrying a divorce is his fault. Whatever that means, he was wrong. But for this one year I am still your mother. And since I've been your mother for a year, I will look after your affairs going forward — whether or not the Marquis's household is technically involved."

The First Madam said it gravely and with sincerity:

"I know the standing of your Lù family — you don't need any of this. But I cannot say nothing. When you marry again in the future, I will ask around and help you look. Even after the two of you part ways, I will treat you as half a daughter."

The First Madam's expression was not good.

It also didn't look as though she had any intention of encouraging them to continue.

Lu Huaixi wanted to say something, but couldn't find how to begin, and found her throat too tight to get the words out properly.

Her gaze drifted for a moment, then fell back to Xie Yuanjing.

Unsure. A little lost.

Yet her face still showed the same composed, graceful Lù family daughter — entering and retreating with propriety, poised in all things. She would not let the turmoil inside her be seen.

"These next few days will be difficult for you. During the day, please stay nearby to keep watch. I don't know what his plans were, but I imagine that since the two of you didn't separate rooms from the start, it must have been to appear as a proper couple to the outside world. Rest assured — once this is over, I'll see to things for you and make sure you have a quieter life."

"Yes."

Lu Huaixi nodded, with a calm that gave nothing away. "First Madam, don't worry. I'll watch over him."

—

In a residential courtyard in the south of the eastern quarter, the Marquis of Chengen sat keeping watch, the weariness on his face plain.

A woman brought a bowl of medicine. Seeing him take it, she sat down beside him with reddened eyes.

"My lord — please go back to the manor. Bìnxìn's injuries are nothing serious. If people discover that you've kept watch here through the night, there's no telling what they'll say about you. Bìnxìn and I — neither of us wants you to be talked about."

"It's all right."

The Marquis of Chengen looked at the woman, his eyes full of guilt.

"If I had let you come into the household sooner, you wouldn't have had to live such a difficult life. Bìnxìn has such fine character — he should have been seen long ago."

"My lord, please don't say such things. It was my own doing — I couldn't let go of the debt of gratitude I owed my lord for saving my life, and I came to the capital against all advice. That my lord has given me a place in the city, and that I can occasionally see my lord — that alone is a blessing. I couldn't have the face to enter the household and make the First Madam uncomfortable."

The woman paused, pressing the corner of her eye with her handkerchief, then continued:

"As for Bìnxìn's situation — Bìnxìn and I had no wish for my lord to know about it. The eldest young master Xie was displeased with him — what of it? He had a little anger to vent. Bìnxìn has endured so much. Rather than suffering this small thing, he would far rather see you living well, with harmony in your household. And so would I."

At the mention of the Marquis's household and his eldest son, the Marquis's expression shifted faintly.

He had not yet sent anyone back to the manor — he didn't know how badly his son had been hurt.

But before he could call anyone to ask, the person on the bed stirred — a quiet sound, then slowly he came back to himself.

Both of them looked over.

The Marquis of Chengen set down the bowl in his hand and went to the bed.

"Zhāng — Uncle Zhāng?"

The newly awakened young man seemed stunned for a moment. He rubbed his eyes as though he couldn't quite believe it.

"Why is Uncle Zhāng here? It's so late — if people see Uncle Zhāng staying here, what will they think?"

Then he looked toward his mother, the worry on his pallid face clear.

"Mother — why didn't you stop him? My injuries are nothing. A few days of sleep and I'll be fine. Something this minor doesn't need to put Uncle Zhāng through this."

"What can I do? I can't make decisions for your Uncle Zhāng."

The woman dabbed at her eyes, as though she too was a little overwhelmed.

"My lord — please don't stay any longer. Bìnxìn and I both worry for you."

The interruption led the Marquis to look at the somewhat pale face of the young man on the bed, and he immediately forgot his intention to send someone back to the manor.

He waved the woman off and looked back at the person in the bed.

"Whether or not this was Yuanjing's doing — your Uncle Zhāng will see justice done for you."

"Uncle Zhāng..."

Hé Bìnxìn turned his head slightly, eyes a little red.

After a moment, as though he had made up his mind, he looked back again.

"Uncle Zhāng — I truly don't want to pursue this matter any further. Whether it was the eldest young master Xie or not — I don't want to investigate, and I don't want to pursue it."

He pressed his lips together, in the manner of someone accepting their fate.

"It was my own failure in the end — I didn't handle the assignment well. Pursuing it or not pursuing it means nothing at this point. I know that Uncle Zhāng cares for me. And it's precisely because of that, that I don't want Uncle Zhāng to fall out with the eldest young master Xie on my account.

"I have no other aspirations. I only entered the court because I wanted to repay Uncle Zhāng. Now that I've failed to do that, all I feel is remorse. Remorse toward Uncle Zhāng, and toward my teacher. As for everything else — it doesn't matter."

Outside, a young manservant had received a message from the manor and was trying to find a way to deliver it.

There was a moment's hesitation — but the person at the Marquis's manor was still the true eldest young master of the Xie family. No matter what, news about him could not be suppressed.

The manservant entered the courtyard. But before he came anywhere near the room, a servant intercepted him.

"Please forgive us, sir. Our young master has only just woken. The Marquis has given orders that no one is to disturb them at this hour. Besides, it's already deep in the night — there's nowhere anyone can go at this hour. We ask that you wait a little longer, sir."

"This concerns the eldest young master of the Marquis's household."

The manservant hesitated, but still didn't want to delay. "I cannot leave it unreported."

"This servant understands — but the Marquis has only just issued the order, so I truly cannot..."

The person's voice was full of difficulty.

"The eldest young master Xie is more than capable of looking after himself, and has the Marquis's household behind him — nothing can truly happen to him. The Marquis has already spent the whole day worn out with worry over our young master's injuries. If he hears news from the manor right now, and can't go back, won't that leave the Marquis in a state of prolonged anxiety?"

That reasoning wasn't entirely wrong.

The manservant looked toward the room ahead, and in the end did not persist.

"Then I'll wait a little longer. If there's any movement inside, let me know."

"Of course. This servant understands."

The figure bowed its head, voice appropriately timid — but a glimmer passed briefly through those eyes.

Their mistress and young master had worked hard to keep this man here. How could they possibly let him slip away at a time like this — letting the Marquis of Chengen return to the Marquis's manor?

"Please be at ease, sir. This servant will keep watch here through the night."

chapters.title: Who Knows Whose Family She'll End Up Being Good To
chapters.content:
In the Marquis's manor, Xie Yuanjing showed no sign of waking.

The First Madam kept watch until the latter half of the night, when her body simply couldn't hold on any longer and the nanny insisted she go back. Before she left, she stopped Lu Huaixi and told her not to stay either.

"There will certainly be many people coming to fish for news in the days ahead — even within the manor, there'll be no peace. If you keep watch at night, how are you to get through the days?"

Lu Huaixi looked at the person on the bed.

This was the first time she had ever seen him without that cold, distant reserve — lying there completely unguarded. She had no wish to go anywhere.

But of course the First Madam would not allow her to disregard herself so completely.

She firmly called her away, and personally walked her to the newly prepared room.

The new room carried a faint, clean fragrance. It was not as fine as the main room, but it was spacious and comfortable, and every detail inside had been attended to with care.

Lu Huaixi got ready for bed and lay down — exhausted and bleary — but her mind was fixed on something she couldn't let go of, and sleep simply would not come.

Jing Shuang hesitated over something, and in the end said nothing. She extinguished half the candles in the room, pulled Yao Xu out with her to keep watch outside, and they made not a single sound.

But perhaps it was the unfamiliar place.

Even in such silence, Lu Huaixi turned from side to side without the least trace of drowsiness.

By the time the candlelight had burned to its end and the room was swallowed entirely by the darkness outside, she finally sat up in the soft light of the moon.

In the latter half of the night, when Xie Yuanjing's dressings were changed, he briefly opened his eyes.

He looked beyond Gong Zhuo, his gaze not entirely clear — but instinct still remembered what it was trying to find.

The physician unwound the blood-soaked bandages, cleaned the wounds, and applied fresh medicine.

The wounds were deep, several of them enough to make your heart turn over at the sight.

But Xie Yuanjing didn't so much as flinch — only, when he heard the words that the Young Madam had returned to the new room, his throat moved silently.

The physician had told him not to speak. He ignored it, brows knitting together, unwilling to fall back asleep.

There was less than an hour left until daybreak. Xie Yuanjing couldn't truly call anyone at this hour.

He wasn't even certain whether he was fully awake. His mind felt blurred and disordered.

In a rare moment of daze, he told himself that Lu Huaixi's absence was not indifference — she had simply gone to sleep early, simply been worried for a full day and night, and was tired.

And yet one hand still curled closed on its own, the veins tensing, the movement pulling at the wound on his shoulder.

Gong Zhuo was also quietly distressed.

He didn't know how to tell his master what had happened earlier, and he wasn't sure how much of what he said his master was even able to hear right now.

"The Young Master's condition is not altogether favorable."

Taking advantage of Xie Yuanjing's half-conscious state, the physician had a fresh bowl of medicine prepared and sent in, his expression heavy.

"How can that be? You said that if he doesn't develop a fever in the night, that's a good sign?"

"He hasn't developed one yet — but the wounds weren't treated when they should have been, and were aggravated by movement on several occasions, which has caused the injuries to worsen. And looking at things as they are, this fever will come eventually."

The physician frowned. "In this summer heat especially — it is even less conducive to the Young Master's wounds healing. Whether day or night over the coming days, there should always be someone keeping watch."

He paused, glanced at the figure on the bed — brows still furrowed, rest anything but peaceful despite having closed his eyes again — and lowered his voice a little.

"The Young Master also has no personal maidservants of his own in close attendance. It would be best to find someone with a light touch and careful attention to help with his care — ideally someone with some knowledge of medicine, who understands how to look after an injured person."

Gong Zhuo felt more helpless than before.

He and the others, Gong Fei included, were people accustomed to swords. Light-handed was simply not something they could manage.

As for finding someone else...

"Besides the Young Madam, no one can get near the Young Master."

"Then perhaps the Young Madam could..."

Xie Yuanjing heard the physician's words through his haze.

Having Lu Huaixi come to care for him — he didn't want that, and he couldn't bring himself to put her through it.

After the two voices in the room went quiet, silence reclaimed the space for a time. Then, broken and intermittent, more voices — kept low.

The candle wavered. Through the blur, Xie Yuanjing thought he heard someone say it was nearly dawn.

He felt no particular worry about his own injuries. No matter how much it hurt, it wouldn't kill him.

And for the things he wanted to obtain, there was always something that had to be given in exchange.

He didn't feel there was anything wrong with having no one in close attendance. He'd been hurt and ill since he was small — no one had ever kept watch over him.

He was only thinking about where Lu Huaixi had gone to sleep — and whether she would return to the room when the sun came up.

Before long the medicine was brought in.

Outside the courtyard, a pale sliver of light had begun to show at the edge of the sky, threaded through the dark.

As the door opened, a figure came in.

Gong Zhuo moved forward to take the medicine — looked up — and stopped.

The Young Madam was standing there, holding it herself.

He was surprised for a moment. And then he couldn't help feeling glad.

Xie Yuanjing felt the calm settle over him almost the instant the words reached him.

The tumult in his clouded mind stilled. The tautness in his chest loosened. His breathing evened out.

In this moment Xie Yuanjing seemed to come back a little more clearly.

Lu Huaixi appearing before him was an uncontrolled accident.

But this accident — it mattered more to him than everything he had spent years straining and calculating to hold on to. And it was worth more too.

—

The only one who hadn't slept, aside from Lu Huaixi, was the First Madam — who had not closed her eyes all night, long past when daylight came through.

Her expression was considerably colder than it had been in front of Lu Huaixi.

Hearing that the Marquis of Chengen still had not returned to the manor, she felt no great surge of anger — only she was no longer the easy-going person she usually appeared to be.

"He's still out there keeping company with that mother and son?"

"Yes, First Madam."

The nanny kept watch beside her. Then she seemed to think of something, and her own expression followed the same downward path. The anger in her eyes was barely contained.

"The Old Master's people did not manage to bring the Marquis back. But the Marquis's manservant returned to the manor at daybreak and sought an audience with the Young Madam."

"Why seek out Huaixi? If it's to ask about Yuanjing's injuries, there's no need to go to her."

The displeasure was plain in the First Madam's brow.

The nanny stepped forward, afraid to trigger an outburst, but knowing it had to be said, and spoke with a worried expression:

"The Marquis's man came back wanting the Young Madam to send for old physician Zēng."

"To bring the old physician in — to treat the person who framed Yuanjing?"

"...Yes."

After the nanny finished speaking, the First Madam suddenly laughed.

But it was a suppressed, suffocated laugh — the kind that called to mind rolling black clouds before a violent crack of thunder, pressing a listener's heart tight.

The nanny saw her face and quickly added: "First Madam, please don't be upset — the Young Madam didn't even let the man finish speaking before she had him driven out. She didn't spare a shred of politeness."

"Xie Zǐzhāng has already lost his face. What politeness is there left to spare?"

The First Madam gripped her handkerchief.

"Since he's capable of doing something this disgusting, then going forward — none of them should expect any peace! Send word out — make his relationship with that mother and son common knowledge. He wants Hé Bìnxìn to rise? I intend to seal off every road he has. I want to see how far he can protect him!"

When she finished, the First Madam was overtaken by a succession of coughs.

She had been carrying a weight on her heart, which had left her body somewhat weakened, and her head ailment had flared up again. She hadn't been able to rest properly for some time.

And now with Yuanjing's situation, the shock and fury had made her body unable to hold steady.

The nanny hurriedly called for a maid and gave her instructions, then replaced the tea with warm water, and reached for the medicine pill that had been brought in.

"First Madam, please don't harm yourself. This matter, once it spreads, will be entirely the Marquis who is in the wrong — it will only help the Young Master. Please take your medicine first, and rest a little while. Otherwise when the Young Master wakes, he'll have to worry about you too."

The First Madam had barely received the pill when a fresh, unfamiliar scent reached her — quite different from the usual herbs.

She placed it in her mouth, swallowed it down with some water, and paused.

"Is this a new medicine the physician prescribed?"

"First Madam — the Young Madam sent this over yesterday after she went back. She had it looked over by the physician first."

The nanny saw the person before her grow a little quieter, and let out a breath of her own.

"The Young Madam's people didn't say anything. But this old servant heard from the physician that these pills are rather rare. I suspect they may have come from the old divine physician's supply."

The First Madam lowered her eyes, shielding her thoughts. After the surge of fury, something heavy and somber crept in behind it.

After a long while, she sighed.

"Wherever that girl ends up — who knows which family is going to be fortunate enough to benefit from her. The more I think about it, the more I feel it's Yuanjing who's come up short on luck."

chapters.title: Don't Touch Him
chapters.content:
Within half a day, news of Xie Yuanjing's injuries had already spread.

Calling cards arrived one after another. Lu Huaixi turned them all away.

Everything pertaining to Xie Yuanjing's courtyard — the First Madam had never involved herself in that before, and now that Xie Yuanjing was unconscious and couldn't make decisions, it was entirely Lu Huaixi's word that was followed.

Her first order was this: no one except the Old Master and the First Madam was permitted inside the room.

For those of rank who did come, she went to the main hall herself to accompany them briefly.

The First Madam didn't object. Even her own visits were never prolonged.

Beyond an occasional reminder to take care of herself, she said nothing else.

Lu Huaixi understood that the First Madam intended to wait until Xie Yuanjing woke to address the matter of the marriage arrangement. Since she didn't bring it up, Lu Huaixi simply carried on as though she didn't know.

The only thing that was raised was a single sentence from the First Madam before she left the courtyard one evening.

"You should still call me Mother."

She looked visibly exhausted, and Lu Huaixi looked at her for a moment, said nothing more, nodded, and called out, obediently, "Mother."

Since the brief, half-conscious waking in the latter part of the night, Xie Yuanjing had remained asleep through all of the following day.

Lu Huaixi finished her rounds and came back — and there was still no sign of him stirring toward consciousness.

She kept watch beside him. Several times she saw the physician frown when applying fresh medicine, and each time her heart clenched in response.

There was nothing she could do to help. She went to the kitchen herself and simmered a pot of congee, then brought the medicine that had been decocted and carried it in.

Since there was no knowing when Xie Yuanjing might wake, these things were prepared again and again.

Only this time, when Lu Huaixi returned to the room, she found that someone had entered while she was away.

"Young Madam, please don't be angry. The people inside were sent by the Marquis. They said they were here to deliver medicine for the Young Master, and that refusing to let them in would be disrespect to the Marquis."

A maid explained from the side.

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed, and something cold came into her expression.

Xie Yuanjing's room — aside from the people at his side and her own maids, no one had ever been permitted in.

The Marquis of Chengen had deliberately invoked his rank to force entry. That he had done so suggested he was certainly not here out of regret.

Lu Huaixi stepped inside. Before she could say a word, she heard the physician from within saying apologetically, "The Young Master does need someone to help tend his wounds — but you two are not suitable. You cannot go near him—"

"The two of us are here on the Marquis's orders specifically to attend closely to the Young Master. Why should we not be suitable?"

Hearing that sentence, Lu Huaixi understood the Marquis of Chengen's intent.

She set down what she was carrying and let her voice carry into the inner room, cutting through whatever was happening inside.

The physician saw her arrive and visibly relaxed.

Standing beside the physician were two young maids.

The two of them caught sight of the bowl of medicine Lu Huaixi had placed on the table, hesitated for just a beat, and then quickly came forward.

"This servant pays respects to the Young Madam."

The two of them offered her a bow, and then let their eyes drift to that bowl of medicine.

They looked as though they were eager to pick it up and take it in.

"Who gave you permission to come in?"

Lu Huaixi had taken it all in. She asked the question deliberately, keeping her voice cool.

The maids finally collected themselves and replied quickly.

"Young Madam, the two of us were sent by the Marquis to help share the Young Madam's burden and attend to the Young Master."

The maid on the left was the more bold of the two, and spoke up herself:

"The Marquis said he has official duties and cannot return to the manor in person. He asked us to bring some medicine, and the Marquis also said that there are few maids in the Young Master's courtyard, and that the Young Madam is already stretched thin, so he asked the two of us to remain in close attendance. In future, we would also be here to serve the Young Madam."

As she spoke, her eyes kept stealing glances at Lu Huaixi, trying to read her expression.

But in the end she didn't quite dare look too openly — that gaze pulled back before long, shifting elsewhere.

Lu Huaixi saw it all clearly. She also caught the flicker of eager anticipation at the back of those eyes.

This was the intent — to have Xie Yuanjing take these maids into his inner household.

She felt a sharp, dark amusement — but it wasn't only the maid's presumption that stirred it. It was also the words: the Marquis has official duties.

Lu Huaixi said nothing. With her saying nothing, the two maids didn't dare get up from their bow either.

But staying bowed like this for too long was impossible to sustain.

The maid on the left endured it as long as she could, and finally couldn't hold back.

"Young Madam — this servant noticed the physician was about to change the Young Master's dressings. Now that you've also brought the medicine — why not let this servant help administer the medicine first, and then punish us afterward? This servant only—"

"Get out."

Lu Huaixi's gaze swept across the two of them. She said it in a flat, indifferent tone that left no room for anything else.

The two maids startled, but gritted their teeth and didn't move.

"Did you not hear me tell you to leave?"

"Young Madam, please don't be angry. The Marquis said that the Young Master cannot be without someone in attendance."

The maid rose, as though throwing all caution aside. She gritted her teeth and held firm:

"The Marquis said it is unseemly that this courtyard has so few maids."

Lu Huaixi gave a cold laugh.

And then the maid opened her mouth again.

"This servant dares not defy the Young Madam. But the Marquis says that as the Young Madam, you should be magnanimous. Today it is only us, here to attend to the Young Master while he is ill — doing a servant's work, nothing more. If even we are something you cannot tolerate, then when others are added to this inner household in the coming days — what then?

"The Marquis has already begun looking at other prospects for the Young Master. He wishes the inner household to be lively, and wishes the Young Master to have more people to support him. But this servant dares hold no other thoughts. If allowed to remain, this servant would serve only the Young Master and the Young Madam."

Hearing all this, Lu Huaixi suddenly found she didn't have the energy to deal with it anymore.

These past few days had truly wrung her out.

Xie Yuanjing's anger. Then the sudden attack. Then his abrupt summons into the palace with no word after. Then him forcing her to show her hand before collapsing.

Her emotions had swung to extremes, she had been sleepless for two nights — she had been pushed nearly to her limit.

And now these two maids, using the Marquis of Chengen's medicine delivery as a pretext, had walked into this room in broad daylight.

Driving them out would make her appear unfilial and jealous. Letting them stay would mean retreating and conceding. Either way, it would do her no good.

She found herself thinking, suddenly, that this life felt rather dreary.

Caring for someone was also dreary.

And the maid hadn't been entirely wrong with one thing she'd said — right now she was on edge about just two maids, already finding it this difficult to accept. So if others were added to the inner household in the future, how would she respond? Would she actually make a scene and have it out with Xie Yuanjing?

That wouldn't do at all.

Seeing Lu Huaixi's silence, the maid assumed she had touched on something vital.

Listening to the sounds from within, remembering the instructions from the Marquis's messenger, she steeled herself, and on her own initiative picked up the bowl of medicine from the table.

"This medicine is getting cold. Let this servant find a way to feed it to the Young Master first. Young Madam, if you wish to punish this servant, do so after this servant has finished caring for the Young Master."

With that, the maid picked up the bowl, turned, and walked through the beaded curtain.

Lu Huaixi watched as her figure moved toward the bed, step by step, drawing closer.

Her thoughts rose and fell — and then settled back into place.

This kind of life truly was dreary.

But to actually let her into their inner room? To let her lay hands on Xie Yuanjing?

If she let these two stay — would she truly not care?

What the future of this marriage would bring, and whether others would enter the inner household — none of that was certain yet.

Since it was all uncertain, did she really want to let these things become a thorn between them, at the very moment she had just understood her own heart?

Jing Shuang came into the room, saw the two extra people inside, and was about to say something sharp — when she heard the Young Madam, standing there with a cool expression, speak first.

"Get out. Don't touch him."

chapters.title: Their Own Affair
chapters.content:
The coldness in Lu Huaixi's voice made everyone in the room go still for a moment.

The maid had only been told that the Young Madam was young, that she had been raised in a pampered, gentle way, that she wasn't suited for looking after people, and couldn't properly care for the Young Master.

She had forgotten to consider: a highborn young lady like this had never needed to look after anyone.

But she still clung to a layer of hope.

Behind her stood the Marquis — the Young Master's own father. She didn't believe this daughter-in-law who had married in would truly be so hard-handed.

"Young Madam — this servant was sent by the Marquis—"

"Jing Shuang."

Lu Huaixi's brow and the corner of her eyes were lowered, her clear dark pupils carrying a coldness that had appeared without her noticing.

She stood there without needing any flattery or deference from anyone else. An innate, effortless presence that did not invite trifling with.

Jing Shuang grasped the purpose of these two women in an instant.

She also guessed that the Marquis of Chengen, likely feeling that his dignity had been wounded, had deliberately sent these maids to blunt the Young Madam's edge.

Her expression went cold immediately. She stepped forward and raised her hand, bringing it down squarely across the disobedient maid's face.

The sharp sound of the slap rang out in the room and then dissipated into the surrounding air.

The maid who had been about to argue was struck sideways, and shrank involuntarily, fear seeping in.

"Return them to the Marquis. Tell the Marquis — if he wishes to place anyone in this inner household, wait until Xie Yuanjing is awake and do it properly, through the front door."

Jing Shuang acknowledged the order, pressed both women down in one smooth motion, and dragged them out through a chorus of gasps and pleas, handing them off to the people outside.

Lu Huaixi paid them no further attention. She simply picked up the bowl of medicine and walked to the bedside.

The person on the bed was still in deep sleep, not stirring at all from the commotion here.

She stopped at the side, watching the physician go out to prepare fresh dressings, and let her gaze settle on Xie Yuanjing.

This bowl of medicine would likely not get fed to him easily either.

Lu Huaixi showed little expression right now.

If someone came in to look, they would not think she had been moved by what just happened.

But only she knew — she had actually been ground down by that particular pressure into something very tired and very frustrated.

And she had no one to say it to. She couldn't even let the person most at fault for all of it know.

"Why aren't you awake yet? You said yesterday when you came back that you only needed to sleep a while."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes.

Where no one could see, her brow drooped slightly, her dark eyes creasing, her lips pressing together for a moment and then releasing.

In the quiet, her expression was restless and wronged.

There was not a trace of the cold severity she'd shown moments ago.

"I really am going to hate you. Though I think I hate the Marquis of Chengen more... After today, I am never interfering in your affairs within this manor again."

She muttered it aimlessly, like venting, and the person on the bed suddenly furrowed his brow. His closed eyes moved beneath the lids, and one hand curled, almost imperceptibly, inward.

Lu Huaixi went still. After a moment, she finally thought to call out to him.

"Xie Yuanjing?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't wake. But something in his expression grew more active with her voice.

He seemed to be struggling in a dream, both eyes still shut, as though in some pain.

Lu Huaixi had no time to think too much — she set the medicine directly on the floor, reached out, and took hold of the hand he was trying to lift.

In the next instant, the person she was holding seemed to grow a little quieter.

But his dark lashes continued to tremble, and the furrow between his brows did not ease.

After a long while, his lips parted slightly — as though he were about to speak. Lu Huaixi tilted her head close to listen.

But there was nothing. Only broken, fragmented sounds.

A little longer still, and those sounds seemed to stretch and lengthen, becoming one thing repeated — her name. Over and over.

He was calling for her. Calling Lù Huaixi.

Outside, the cicadas fell suddenly silent. Silent enough that the short, faint sound of breathing was audible.

Lu Huaixi felt something strike her chest, again and again — and then, in the low and husky sound that held only a little clarity, she heard her own heartbeat, disordered and without rhythm.

Old Master Xie's reprimand didn't matter. The First Madam's doubts about this marriage didn't matter.

Even the Marquis of Chengen's attempts to drive a wedge between them didn't matter.

The fact that Xie Yuanjing cared for her — that was something she could respond to. And that was their own affair.

"When you wake up, I'll settle this account with you properly."

Lu Huaixi muttered.

That faint response from him had made her forget about everything just now almost immediately.

She called the physician over. But she waited a long time, and the person on the bed said nothing more to her.

In the end the physician said a few words, and Lu Huaixi finally stopped hovering over him where she stood.

The bowl of medicine got only a little fed in. She set down the bowl with vague dissatisfaction, took away the damp cloth beneath his neck, and wrung a fresh one to wipe his face.

When she finished, there was a light film of perspiration on her skin.

But when she stopped, she didn't feel the discomfort of it.

From time to time a breeze drifted in from behind her.

Past the hottest part of the day, the ice in the room was doing its work more effectively.

Lu Huaixi blinked, tired, and in the end couldn't hold on — she collapsed forward and folded her arms on the edge of the bed.

Xie Yuanjing's hand had originally been resting not far from her face. In her drowsy haze, she thought she saw that hand actually lift and fall — onto her cheek.

"Don't hate me."

Lu Huaixi heard someone speaking to her.

But she was so tired. Her eyes would not open. She sank, deeply, into sleep.

—

Calling cards kept arriving at the manor.

With the exception of the elder branch, almost everyone had received some kind of invitation.

Mù Nianwēi, too, had suddenly been invited by a small circle of young ladies she occasionally gathered with.

The weather was hot, someone was passing by, and there was something they'd been meaning to deliver to her — and so they thought they might share a cup of tea.

The relationship with this person was not particularly close, but they were cordial on the surface, and declining was impossible — she would have to manage them somehow.

Mù Nianwēi went to the front to receive her.

She understood perfectly well why this visit had come so suddenly — it was to pry into the elder branch's affairs.

But that was neither here nor there, because even she, let alone the Old Madam, had little to say about what was actually going on. She hadn't been able to set foot in the elder branch's part of the manor in days.

None of this was something she would ever let an outsider know.

Her foothold in the capital, and the face she had there — a treatment not far below that of a proper young noble lady — were entirely built on what people perceived as her relationship with the Marquis's household.

"Niànwēi."

The visitor spotted her, smiled warmly, and came forward to take her arm.

Mù Nianwēi smiled back with practiced grace, and led her guest toward her own quarters.

"It's so warm out. It was good of you to come all this way, Elder Sister Wèi."

"Not at all. The height of summer is behind us — these past few days really haven't been that bad. And besides, I rarely have occasion to visit the Marquis's manor. This time I have you to thank for giving me the chance to see it for myself."

Mù Nianwēi loved hearing things like this, though nothing of that showed on her face — she only let a faint note of wryness slip through.

"Elder Sister Wèi, please don't tease me. I only get to borrow a little of Cousin's reflected glory because of Grandmother's fondness for me."

"Yes, yes, yes — you're too modest and you don't like to acknowledge these things. I won't argue with you about it."

Their voices were low, and even when they laughed, the wind carried the words away before they reached too far.

It was precisely because of this that a sudden sharp voice near the inner hanging gate came through with startling clarity.

Both of them looked up. Mù Nianwēi recognized the guard at the front immediately — he was from the elder branch's courtyard.

To be precise, he was one of Lu Huaixi's people.

Before she could process what she was seeing, the people behind him had two young maids in their grip, being hauled toward the gate.

One of the outer maids had a face that was faintly red and swollen. She was crying and pleading all the way out.

chapters.title: She Hasn't Even Sorted Out Her Own Situation — Who Else Gets a Turn?
chapters.content:
Mù Nianwēi's heart gave a startled lurch — but she quickly composed herself.

"Don't be alarmed, Elder Sister Wèi. The manor has strict rules, but every so often a maid forgets her place."

"Of course, of course. Every inner household has its share of people with their own agendas — when one turns up, you put her in her place."

The visitor smiled and agreed, but she hadn't forgotten what she'd come for, and couldn't help pressing on:

"Though those two do look rather pitiful. I wonder whose bad side they got on. I heard on my way here that your cousin was injured — and to think someone was still causing a scene in the manor at a time like this."

Mù Nianwēi could see plainly that the prying had begun. Inwardly she gave a cold laugh.

But she pulled her gaze away and let out a small sigh.

"It's probably my cousin-in-law."

She kept her voice low. "At a time like this, who in the manor has the energy to go after the maids? Only my cousin-in-law — she's young, and she has a temper."

"Your cousin-in-law... you mean the Young Madam of the house?"

The woman seemed genuinely surprised, and followed it up smoothly: "Wouldn't that disturb your cousin's recovery? Does your cousin really indulge her that much?"

She paused, as though realizing she'd gotten a little too eager. She quickly smiled and backpedaled.

"I'm being too nosy — I was just thinking out loud since we're close. But since it's come up, I won't hide it from you."

"What is it, Elder Sister Wèi?"

"It's not really a secret. It's just that early last year, the eldest young master Xie helped my family with something. So when I heard about this, my father was very worried and has been trying to come and pay his respects — but the Marquis's household isn't easy to get into, and I didn't want to put you in a difficult position."

The visitor lowered her eyes as she said this, her expression suitably troubled.

"But my family does feel this debt of gratitude. Now that I've found my way here, I still want to be shameless about it and ask — could Niànwēi perhaps take me to look in on the eldest young master Xie? Just to offer our thanks in person."

Mù Nianwēi saw through her perfectly.

Helped her family. As if.

How could Xie Yuanjing possibly go out of his way to help someone he had no connection to whatsoever?

Even she, who had admired Xie Yuanjing for so long, had never thought of him as someone who was easily moved to kindness.

With that thought, Mù Nianwēi inwardly rolled her eyes.

"I'm afraid that won't be possible, Elder Sister Wèi."

She put on a rueful expression and blamed the whole thing on Lu Huaixi.

She herself had no particular standing — but that Lù family daughter, whose temper was growing harder to predict, certainly did.

"This isn't something I can make decisions about. My cousin-in-law has a temper, and she keeps a tight rein on my cousin. Now that he's seriously injured, if I were to suddenly bring Elder Sister Wèi in, I don't know how much of her anger would come down on me."

She paused, then added:

"I shouldn't really be saying this — it is my cousin and cousin-in-law's affair — but I genuinely don't want Elder Sister Wèi to misunderstand me..."

"Is the Young Madam of this household really that possessive?"

Mù Nianwēi didn't answer this time.

Silence, sometimes, carried more weight than a direct response.

Very quickly, the visitor had no choice but to take back her words.

Not wanting to appear bitter, she pulled Mù Nianwēi close again with a smile.

"Of course I don't misunderstand you. You have your own difficulties. I'll find another opportunity to come and pay my respects another time. Though I do feel for you — having to be around such a highborn young lady every single day."

Mù Nianwēi gave what looked like a strained smile in return.

But she still said nothing, only led the guest onward, laughing inwardly.

Another opportunity. What a pretty thought.

As for Xie Yuanjing — she herself hadn't sorted out her own situation with him. Who else was going to get a foothold there?

And she hadn't said anything untrue, come to that.

Lu Huaixi was on watch around the clock — even she couldn't get in. Bringing a complete outsider along would be walking straight into her arms and asking to be scolded.

But whatever she thought, Mù Nianwēi kept all the contempt and mockery carefully tucked away, her manner warm and gentle on the surface throughout.

She led her guest inside, and deliberately, in front of her, told a maid to go to the Old Madam and ask for leave on her behalf, saying she would only be able to go and keep the Old Madam company later in the day.

This small gesture earned her several admiring looks from her visitor.

—

While Mù Nianwēi was busy collecting her flattery, Lu Huaixi — unaware of any of the resentment being directed at her from that quarter — had just woken from her nap.

She hadn't slept long. It had been barely more than a short doze.

But when she came to, she found herself lying in the bed, right next to Xie Yuanjing, with her arm draped across his waist.

She lay there unable to come back to herself for quite some time. When she finally pinched herself and felt the pain, she jerked fully awake.

She was badly startled, and her first instinct was to check Xie Yuanjing's wounds.

The movement carried, and Yao Xu came in quietly with water, setting it down before creeping inside.

There was no new blood seeping through Xie Yuanjing's inner robe. But his body felt very warm.

Lu Huaixi didn't dare move abruptly. She eased herself up little by little, then climbed out from the other side, steadied herself with Yao Xu's help, and stepped into her shoes.

"How — how did I end up in the bed?"

Her voice still carried the stuffed-nose drowsiness of someone not fully awake, but her tone was already growing urgent. "Did Xie Yuanjing wake up? He woke up, didn't he?"

Yao Xu could feel the tension in the person beside her.

She guided her toward the door, gave Lu Huaixi a small nod, and spoke in a low voice — her expression no longer as heavy as it had been before.

"This servant wasn't in the room, but Gong Fei said the Young Master did wake briefly. He didn't say so directly, but no one else would dare move you — it must have been the Young Master who saw you and put you in the bed."

Lu Huaixi went still.

She turned to look back. Knowing he had woken once, she felt an instinctive swell of emotion that nearly made her cry.

But then she thought about how he had moved her, injured as he was, and a different feeling rose — a suppressed, simmering frustration.

"What did the physician say? Has he developed a fever?"

"The physician is in the side room keeping watch. Young Madam, please don't worry."

Yao Xu handed her the freshly wrung damp cloth, then hesitated a moment and lowered her voice.

"The physician has added a new prescription. But Gong Fei says the Young Master, in his half-conscious state, gave an instruction — that the physician was not to come in until you woke."

Lu Huaixi couldn't quite put a name to what she was feeling. But her temper had entirely left her.

After a moment, she picked up the cup of water on the table, wet her throat, and said: "Invite the physician in first, and have the new medicine decocted."

The words had barely left her mouth when a maid appeared at the outer door.

"Young Madam — the Third Madam has come."

The maid kept her voice quiet. "The Third Madam heard the Young Master's injuries are severe and came specially to visit. The people outside relayed your instructions, but the Third Madam didn't want to leave, saying she is worried about the Young Master's condition."

The last traces of drowsiness evaporated from Lu Huaixi's mind.

She wasn't particularly in the mood for this.

And she had just woken — she didn't want to expend mental energy on navigating anyone right now. Even less did she want to leave Xie Yuanjing.

But hearing it was the third branch, she thought it over and nodded.

Used properly, this could be quite useful.

"I'll go and see her."

She finished, then looked back at Yao Xu. "You stay here and assist the physician. And keep waiting for word from old physician Zēng."

As she was speaking, a faint sound came from within.

Lu Huaixi turned and went back in without thinking.

Xie Yuanjing was awake — but not entirely.

The anguish of his nightmares had left his pale face. His deep, dark, long eyes were veiled in a layer of soft haze.

Perhaps because he was still somewhat dazed, the usual cold clarity between his brows was absent, and there was a fragile beauty in the illness that only added to his striking looks.

Lu Huaixi had always thought she would cry the moment she saw him wake up.

But now that she was truly seeing it, other than her hands trembling very faintly, she found a steadiness in herself she hadn't expected.

She could calmly press her hand to his brow. Could calmly take his hand. Could coherently tell him she was going to see the Third Madam, ask him to be good and take his medicine, and say she would be back.

Whether the person on the bed heard any of it, she didn't know.

He only, after their eyes met and held for a moment, closed his again.

Just as Lu Huaixi assumed he had fallen back under, the corner of Xie Yuanjing's colorless mouth curved faintly.

A low, rough sound came from his throat — a quiet response.

Then, as Lu Huaixi rose to leave, his little finger traced a slow, light stroke across her palm.

"It hurts."

That slow, hoarse voice was like a hook catching at the heart, leaving a tingling ache.

"It hurts. Wife had better come back quickly."

Wife —

Not wife in the generic sense. Not the formal term.

Something like spring blossoms fell through Lu Huaixi's heart — brilliant color drifting through every corner.

Without thinking, she pressed her lips together and said she would.

chapters.title: Refusing Visitors
chapters.content:
The Third Madam, Lady Zhào, had not had much to do with the elder branch in the past two years.

She was close to the Old Madam, and had spoken up for Mù Nianwēi on more than one occasion — which had eventually earned her Xie Yuanjing's displeasure, and added another layer of distance between their two branches.

When Lu Huaixi arrived, the Third Madam who had reportedly been held up at the door was calmly drinking tea, her face showing none of the worry that had been described.

When she spotted Lu Huaixi approaching, a calculating gleam crossed her eyes — though she apparently thought her prying and curiosity were invisible to others.

Lu Huaixi gave no indication that she saw it.

She greeted the Third Madam and accepted a cup of tea.

Lady Zhào drew in the leisurely air she'd been wearing and let a crease of concern and dissatisfaction appear between her brows.

"How is Yuanjing? If you have time to sit here drinking tea with me, you'd be better off taking me to see him. All these people turning everyone away — aren't you afraid of people saying you don't know how to behave?"

"Third Aunt, my husband is seriously injured and hasn't woken. It is not convenient for him to have visitors."

"Not convenient to have visitors — and what exactly does that mean? Am I some outsider?"

Lady Zhào's expression chilled. She set the cup down on the table with a heavy thud.

"I am Yuanjing's third aunt. His elder. He's lying there injured without a word of news, and when his aunt comes to look in on him, she needs your permission to enter the room?"

"This daughter-in-law would not dare."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes. She said she would not dare — but her tone softened not one degree.

"My husband's injuries are serious. The physician says he must be kept very carefully, that the room cannot be too warm or too cold, and that he should not be disturbed while he rests. I hope Third Aunt will understand."

"Is it me who doesn't understand, or is it you who doesn't put me, as an aunt, in your eyes? I am the Third Madam of this household — do I need to check your expression to step inside and see my own family?"

Lady Zhào wasn't necessarily set on actually seeing Xie Yuanjing.

She had come to the elder branch's quarters for two reasons: to ensure the Old Master couldn't say the third branch was cold-hearted, and to get a good look at the commotion — and, more importantly, to find out exactly how badly the eldest young master of the Xie family had been hurt.

If something truly went wrong, the elder branch did have other young masters. But none of them were legitimate heirs.

Any benefits that might fall to the third branch couldn't be allowed to slip into the hands of those concubines' sons.

And then there was the one outside the household.

The surname was Hé, not Xie — but whether there was some connection, no one could say with certainty.

That she personally didn't want to see was one thing. Being blocked by a young girl was something else entirely.

Watching Lu Huaixi hold firm, Lady Zhào felt her dignity as an elder being stepped on — and her temper surged.

"I will see him today no matter what. You're a junior, a new bride who hasn't been here long — to carry on like this, you ought to go and learn some proper manners!"

Lady Zhào rose without caring about anything else, called her maidservant over, and made a show of telling the girl to lead her in.

But she hadn't even made it out the door when Jing Shuang, who was standing guard outside, blocked her way.

Behind Jing Shuang were the two attendants who had always followed Lu Huaixi.

They were unobtrusive when not called upon — but when they stepped forward, you could see at once the cold, quiet readiness in them.

"You — you dare lay hands on me?"

"Third Aunt, I said — my husband is not available for visitors at this time. If you force your way in and worsen my husband's injuries, who will bear responsibility?"

Lu Huaixi didn't try to be pleasant about it.

She rarely showed anything cold in her manner.

Even when applying pressure, her crescent-shaped eyes usually carried an ingenuous clarity that could disarm almost anyone.

But right now those dark eyes carried no smile. They were slightly lowered.

The light reflected in those pupils was like a spring shaded with ice and snow — and even the gauzy, ethereal quality they usually held was veiled in a layer of remoteness.

Lady Zhào's anger stalled for a moment when she saw those still, untroubled eyes.

She suddenly recalled that some time ago, because of Mù Nianwēi, this eldest nephew of hers had also given an order that she was not to enter the elder branch's quarters freely.

Looking at those attendants now, she couldn't quite tell whether they were Lu Huaixi's people or Xie Yuanjing's.

She truly did not want to lose face in front of an outsider. And in front of a junior who had only just married into the household at that.

"Just going in for a look wouldn't worsen his injuries — Yuanjing isn't—"

"One never knows about these things. If Third Aunt truly intends to go against the physician, you need only say with certainty that my husband will be unharmed, and I will stop blocking you immediately."

"A physician couldn't say that — you little—"

Lu Huaixi caught the hesitation and calculation flickering across Lady Zhào's face in an instant.

Knowing she was nothing more than a paper tiger, Lu Huaixi quietly eased her tone and shifted back into something warmer.

"Third Aunt, I know you mean well. Because we are family, you are worried about my husband's injuries."

She took a beat before continuing, unhurried.

"You also know that a new bride who has only just arrived would not, for no reason, presume to make decisions about her husband's courtyard. If his injuries were not this severe, and the risk this real, I would not have given such an order on the physician's word alone."

It sounded as though Lu Huaixi was conceding ground.

But the expression on her face remained even, and there was still a faint coldness at her brow — and a pressure that was difficult to notice and yet impossible to ignore.

Lady Zhào began to feel uneasy.

Thinking of Lu Huaixi's standing as a daughter of the Lù family, and remembering how in such a short time she had won the trust of the Xie family's Old Master and the elder branch, not to mention the regard of the cold and indifferent eldest young master — Lady Zhào could no longer follow what she was actually saying.

Her mind was frantically going back over the past months, trying to recall whether, because of Mù Nianwēi, she had ever openly shown any friction with this capable Lù family daughter.

She thought not.

Once she had run through it all, Lady Zhào suddenly realized with a jolt what she had been doing.

She had been afraid. Afraid of making an enemy of Lu Huaixi.

"If Third Aunt is truly that worried about my husband and wishes to go in and see him, then please wait a little longer. It happens to be the time the physician is changing his dressings right now — he has many wounds, and they are deep. It will be at least another half hour. But should you go inside, the Old Master will be informed."

Lady Zhào slowly came back to herself.

Thinking of why she had come, and of the ways the third branch borrowed influence from the elder, she extinguished her anger and used the offered exit to climb gracefully down.

"All right, all right. Since you've explained it properly, I'm not the sort of unreasonable person who can't see that. I only came because I was worried about Yuanjing."

She gave a convincingly magnanimous sigh, her face reshaping itself into an expression of concern.

"I was just carried away earlier — don't take it to heart. But do tell your aunt truthfully — how long will it be before Yuanjing's injuries heal? His third uncle and I have been worried."

Lu Huaixi laughed inwardly. Nothing of it reached her face.

She was silent for a moment after Lady Zhào spoke.

When she looked up again, her eyes were rimmed faintly with red, and she pressed her lips together and said nothing, holding herself steady with visible effort.

Lady Zhào blinked, caught off guard.

"Don't mind me asking — I won't ask anymore."

She quickly waved it off and offered Lu Huaixi a few words of comfort.

Only when the redness had faded from Lu Huaixi's eyes did Lady Zhào find a pretext to leave.

The moment she was gone, every trace of that inexpressible pain vanished from Lu Huaixi's face. She gave one cool glance around, then walked straight back to the room.

In the room there was only Gong Fei, who had been taking Gong Zhuo's place, and several guards she recognized.

Seeing her return, they clasped their hands in salute and quietly withdrew.

She hadn't even had time to ask whether Xie Yuanjing had woken again before Jing Shuang came to her side.

"Young Madam — old physician Zēng has set out."

"He's not angry anymore?"

"It seems not. I heard he made your messenger wait quite some time before he opened the door."

"His temper comes fast and goes fast."

Hearing that the old man had let go of his sulk and was willing to make the trip, the corners of Lu Huaixi's brow finally lifted and some real color returned to her face.

"Go and tell the physician — ask him to work together with old physician Zēng when he arrives."

Lu Huaixi had sent someone up the mountain the night before.

She had been a little apprehensive at first, worried the attending physician might think she was questioning his skill by sending for another.

But it was the Marquis of Chengen's people who had inadvertently opened the door — after his servant had come with that particular request, the physician had himself brought up his past acquaintance with old physician Zēng.

Lu Huaixi had simply taken the opening and said she was trying to arrange it. If she succeeded, the two of them could consult together.

The physician was pleased, and she felt one weight lift from her shoulders.

"Once old physician Zēng arrives, let the Marquis of Chengen know."

Lu Huaixi stopped in the outer room, not hurrying inside. She kept her voice low as she gave the instruction.

Jing Shuang acknowledged it, then couldn't help asking: "If the Marquis hears — and pressures old physician Zēng to go and treat Hé Bìnxìn—"

"He can't pressure him. The old physician left the Imperial Medical Office without so much as a scratch — without any trouble at all. There's no way a Marquis of Chengen could coerce someone like that. Besides — I want him to know."

chapters.title: What My Wife Agreed To — That Won't Do
chapters.content:
To speak honestly, Lu Huaixi was still a little angry.

She could have chosen to be magnanimous and let it go. But she didn't want to. She simply couldn't swallow it.

"The Marquis of Chengen does nothing himself, and yet he thinks he can act with impunity — well, I intend to let him watch with his own eyes. Watch the man he couldn't bring here give all his care and attention to Xie Yuanjing, and meet him and that Hé Bìnxìn of his with cold indifference. And I want to make it clear to him — I am not someone who can be trifled with so easily."

She knew the old man's character far too well.

Just setting aside everything else — the fact that she had agreed to help him think through his medicinal herbs was more than enough for the old man to take her side.

Lu Huaixi let out another cold sound when she finished.

"He asks me to bring someone to tend to the man outside who helped frame Xie Yuanjing, gets refused, and so he sends maids to humiliate me — trying to install them in Xie Yuanjing's inner household. A Marquis, doing something like this. Truly impressive."

"Young Madam is right. No one should be treated this way."

Jing Shuang thought of what had happened earlier, and of the manservant the Marquis of Chengen had sent — the look on his face — and frowned reflexively.

"In the past, no matter how strained things were between the Marquis and the Young Master, the Marquis always put the Marquis's household first. He never showed this kind of total indifference toward the Young Master. But now..."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes as she listened.

Her round eyes were mostly hidden by long lashes — the emotion inside them impossible to read.

She didn't pick up where Jing Shuang had left off.

But she understood. All of this was because Xie Yuanjing had grown too capable, too independent — and the Marquis feared that with him so formidable, Hé Bìnxìn would have no way to protect himself.

"Perhaps one of these days we should ask the Old Master to bring in a master for the Marquis."

"What kind of master?"

"A master who reads the three souls and seven spirits, naturally. To have lost this much of his mind so suddenly — who knows whether he's been bewitched — oh, never mind."

Lu Huaixi stopped herself and changed the subject.

"I'm too lazy to say these things behind anyone's back."

"......"

Jing Shuang came back to herself.

One moment feeling indignant on her young mistress's behalf, the next finding she wanted to laugh.

This was, undeniably, their Young Madam.

In front of others, she could go cold in an instant — full of composure and daring. But in private, there were still moments when something childlike slipped through.

Never mind the Young Master — even those who served at her side all found themselves wanting to tether their hearts to the Young Madam.

"Young Madam doesn't need to let those things upset her. Once the Young Master is awake, he certainly won't let you suffer this kind of grievance for nothing."

Jing Shuang finished, and then looked at the tired brow and eyes before her.

She waited for a response that didn't come. Then she remembered what the Old Master and the First Madam had said the night before.

But she said nothing of it, only poured a cup of tea as though she had no idea.

Whether it was a real marriage or not — the Young Master's feelings were plain for all of them to see.

"Should I tell the First Madam about what the Third Madam put you through just now?"

"There's no need. She wasn't able to actually trouble me. No point in making a point of it."

Lu Huaixi didn't notice Jing Shuang's expression shifting through several changes.

She dismissed it with a wave of her hand, drained the cup of tea Jing Shuang had given her in one go, and rose to walk back to the inner room.

Going to see Lady Zhào just now had been deliberate.

News of Xie Yuanjing's serious injuries needed to spread — every additional person was one more mouth.

And the Third Madam was just the right sort: fond of gossip, and approaching the elder branch with a mix of prying and barely concealed schadenfreude.

A single moment of teary eyes from her had been enough. In three days' time, Lady Zhào would have carried word of Xie Yuanjing's grave injuries to every great lady's inner household in the capital.

And with a few other small moves on her part, she could arrange for Xie Yuanjing to be seen as the one being suppressed by his own father — let the Marquis of Chengen walk into a trap of his own making.

—

One thing after another, and the day flew by. By the time it was over, it was evening.

Old physician Zēng arrived before sunset.

He blew his whiskers and scolded Lu Huaixi for a while — complaining that she had ignored him for so long — but when he saw the red lines lining her eyes, he couldn't bring himself to continue, and turned to go in.

Xie Yuanjing's injuries were truly severe.

But fortunately, the attending physician was skilled. Old physician Zēng examined things for a while, gave a reassuring verdict, and applied fresh medicine.

Lu Huaixi seemed to have been waiting for exactly that verdict.

She had barely slept more than half an hour in two days. The moment she let out that held breath, she sat down right there and fell asleep.

In the end it was Yao Xu who gently roused her and led her back to the room — her eyes barely able to open.

"Just one hour. Wake me after one hour."

The moment she touched the bed, Lu Huaixi closed her eyes and consciousness left her almost at once.

But she still remembered Xie Yuanjing saying he was in pain just now. In a half-asleep murmur, she managed to remind Yao Xu.

The exhaustion written into the creases of her brow was too much to look at, the dark circles beneath her eyes too pitiful.

Yao Xu struggled with herself, then — seeing that the Young Master on the other side had still not woken — gritted her teeth and, for the first time in her life, did not obey Lu Huaixi's instruction.

She slept straight through to the middle of the night.

When Xie Yuanjing woke, the world outside had gone completely still.

The eyes that opened were no longer as hazy and confused as they had been during the day.

His gaze gradually sharpened. Aside from a slight furrow of his brow when he sat up, his expression through the rest of it showed very little strain.

If the old physician hadn't seen those wounds with his own eyes, he would have thought the man before him had simply pushed himself too hard at practice and was only now waking from a long sleep.

"This junior pays his respects to old physician Zēng."

Xie Yuanjing saw the long-bearded old gentleman not far away. He paused for only a moment — there was no great surprise in his manner.

He lowered his eyes, his voice steady, his respect simple and unaffected.

"It was a great trouble to bring old physician Zēng here. You have this junior in your debt, and this junior will see to it that old physician Zēng's fee for coming down the mountain is paid in full — there will not be the slightest cause for dissatisfaction."

"None of that. The little girl already worked something out with me. You don't need to be involved."

The old man gave a brief wave of his hand, glanced at Xie Yuanjing, and turned back to rummaging through his medicine case.

Xie Yuanjing's brow tightened at once.

He didn't know what Lu Huaixi had agreed to on his behalf — but to bring this particular person out of his mountain retreat, whatever she'd agreed to couldn't have been anything ordinary.

He absolutely was not going to let her go.

"My wife is young and doesn't have much tolerance for hardship. Whatever old physician Zēng has agreed to with her, this junior can take her place — whether it is payment or some other arrangement, this junior will see to it that old physician Zēng is more than satisfied."

"That girl really can't take much hardship. Spoilt little thing."

The old man gave a dismissive snort, then added: "But I have no use for you, either. What payment — I'm not short of silver, old as I am."

Hearing his tone, as though he didn't want to discuss it further, a faint coldness entered Xie Yuanjing's brow.

But mindful of the old man's standing and his connection to Lu Huaixi, he held himself back.

"My wife is not lacking in tolerance — but since old physician Zēng has come because of my injuries, the fee has no business being paid by someone else. If old physician Zēng will not accept payment, then let us discuss other terms. What my wife has agreed to — that will not stand."

At that, the old man finally looked up again.

As though something had caught his interest, the stern expression that had been set on his face began to shift into something more considering.

chapters.title: It Was I Who Held You
chapters.content:
The room carried a different kind of medicinal scent from usual.

There was something of the clean freshness of plants and the damp earthiness of soil — not as sharp as ordinary medicine, and not too strong on the nose.

Xie Yuanjing came more fully alert within that scent, with no intention of backing down.

"Whatever old physician Zēng names — whether or not this junior currently has it, this junior will see it done."

He had no idea what the old divine physician wanted. But he knew the man had an unpredictable temper and was not easy to read.

Whatever the case — easy or difficult — now that he was awake, he was not going to let Lu Huaixi carry out whatever she had agreed to on his behalf.

At his words, the old man gave no direct response.

He only looked Xie Yuanjing over for a moment — as though weighing something, with a trace of hesitation.

After a long pause, he looked away.

"Changing your mind now — did the two of you deliberately trick this old man into coming down the mountain?"

"This junior would not dare."

"Ha. Looks to me like you'd dare quite a lot."

The old man stroked his beard and let out a cold snort. "What I want is for that girl to do something for me. Can you do it in her place?"

"I can."

Xie Yuanjing didn't even pause. "Whatever my wife has agreed to, this junior can take her place."

"Don't say it so fast. Think it through."

The old man set down what he was holding, his eyes moving with calculation. "What I need isn't something just anyone can do for me — especially with that body of yours full of injuries."

"This junior has thought it through clearly. And since I would be doing this on old physician Zēng's behalf, if my injuries worsen in the process, you would certainly bring me back — you wouldn't simply stand aside and let things take their course."

"You're quicker than that girl."

The old man seemed to seriously consider his words, then began taking several small vials out of the medicine case and laying them out.

"I've been short of someone to trial medicine lately. Originally that girl agreed to trial two vials for me. But since you won't let her, you can come in her place. One condition, though — not a word to anyone. That includes the girl."

Xie Yuanjing looked up. His gaze moved to the table not far away.

Seeing him silent, the old man gave another huff and made as though to put things back.

"Afraid? If you don't dare, then I have no choice but to let that little girl come. She's not afraid. She and I have already agreed."

"When would we start?"

Xie Yuanjing spoke up suddenly, making the person ahead of him pause mid-motion.

"Old physician Zēng's medicine trial — when would it start?"

"Have you made up your mind? I can only guarantee these medicines won't kill anyone. I make no promises about pain."

"Yes. Since my wife has already agreed to old physician Zēng's terms — I will take her place."

"Just like that? Fine — I'll give you two days to think it over. All you'd really need to do is soak in water for a while. Though my medicine—"

"You old scoundrel — why are you tricking him?"

Before he could finish, the door flew open and Lu Huaixi stepped inside.

Her brows were drawn tight, with the daze of someone just woken — drowsiness still clinging to the corners of her eyes, a crease still fading from her fair cheek.

The candle in the corridor wavered outside. Beyond it lay a deep, undisturbed dark.

Lu Huaixi's sudden presence shattered the tranquility of the night, lighting up the cold room as though she had carried the brightness in with her.

"Who agreed to trial your medicine? And you were going to tell him not to say anything to me — you were trying to profit from both sides!"

"You — you awful girl, were you eavesdropping......"

Caught red-handed, the old man flustered for a moment, then turned away with a pointed huff and hid his embarrassment behind indignation.

"Do you have any manners? An elder is before you, and you — you are just like this, this brazen and rude?"

The bluster was clearly running out of steam.

Everyone in the room and outside it went still in astonishment.

Then Xie Yuanjing let out a soft, helpless laugh.

From where he was lying, he couldn't see Lu Huaixi — but hearing the exasperation in her voice, he could picture immediately how she looked: cheeks puffed, probably red-eyed too.

People who have fallen in love are rarely entirely rational.

Without a moment's hesitation, the man half-propped on the bed got to his feet — he only wanted to bring her in and comfort her.

"I was perfectly ready to be respectful, but you won't let me have manners! If I'd come a moment later just now, you'd have tricked him into trialing your medicine — don't think I don't know!"

"You, this awful girl — what a temper! I spent a whole day coming down that mountain, and for whom? It was only a bit of teasing—"

"Don't try to get around me. You do this every year — one person a year, don't think I'm unaware!"

Lu Huaixi narrowed her eyes, stepped forward, and took the vials from the table to look them over.

She couldn't make anything out, so she opened a stopper and brought it to her nose.

"You foolish girl, don't go sniffing randomly — you'll get it on your face and break out in a rash—"

Lu Huaixi wasn't listening. She was about to pour out some of the contents to get a proper look, when a firm pressure landed on her hand.

"Don't touch those."

Xie Yuanjing took the vial from her hand, recapped it, and set it back where it was.

The door swung closed. He withdrew his hand, and as he did, drew her a little closer to him.

Lu Huaixi let herself be pulled.

She had been so worked up she'd forgotten the reason she'd come rushing over. It was only when that steady pressure closed around her hand that she remembered.

She hadn't slept well.

The dream had been full of flashing blades, and a Xie Yuanjing soaked in blood.

Waking in fright, she hadn't even finished putting on her shoes before she ran over.

Now, seeing him not only awake but on his feet, his color nothing like the frightening pallor of her dream, she stared wide-eyed for a moment — then, without thinking, let herself follow his pull and wrapped her arms around him.

"When did you wake up? Why didn't you have someone come and get me? Did the old man give you medicine? Is it feeling better? Do you still have a fever?"

Her slender, soft hands and his waist were separated by only the thin layer of his inner robe.

The warmth of a young woman spread from the point of contact. Her particular fragrance overtook every other scent in the room in an instant.

Xie Yuanjing had not dared to imagine he would wake to this.

But his surprise lasted only a moment.
