Even with the whisker-blowing, glaring old man still seated right there, he couldn't stop himself from dropping his arm around Lu Huaixi's waist and pulling her in just a little closer.

If being injured was what it took to make her this close to him, he didn't mind staying in bed a few more times.

"Just woke."

After a long moment, Xie Yuanjing finally remembered to answer her.

His throat worked as he spoke, and when he finished he let out a soft laugh — then patiently answered her, one question at a time.

"I wanted you to sleep properly, so I didn't think to call you at this hour."

"Just woke. Haven't taken the medicine yet."

"The wound doesn't hurt anymore. The fever hasn't come back."

Lu Huaixi felt the rumble of his laugh through his chest where she was pressed against it.

Together with his voice, which had a way of making the mind go hazy, it drew her into a warmth that finally — finally — let her feel something solid beneath her feet.

She sniffled. Knowing he had genuinely come back to himself, she let herself settle into relief, and the grievance she'd been carrying came out without resistance.

But before she could even open her mouth, a pointed cough sounded nearby.

Then, perhaps by way of retaliation, the old man laughed coldly and said in an arch tone:

"True, the wound isn't hurting — it's just that the tender flesh inside is still exposed. Any movement and it will split open. But don't mind me. You two can go ahead and hold each other as long as you like. Don't worry about this old wreck. Hold it long enough and the wound will bleed through again, and then we'll just have to put the medicine on all over again."

Lu Huaixi's thoughts snapped back into place with a jolt. She released him immediately.

She thought she must have been half-asleep still. How had she just gone ahead and thrown herself at him like that?

Her ears were a little red. The urgency was back in her eyes.

But she had never been the type to act awkward in front of others. Hearing the old man's pointed displeasure, she restrained herself and asked steadily: "I couldn't help it just now — what should I do about it?"

"So now you know how to come and ask me nicely?"

The old man scored his point, turned away with residual irritation, and said: "What else is there to do — make him lie back down like a good boy. It's only because I'm a patient old man that I'm not scolding anyone. At my age."

"You're not patient at all. I haven't forgotten — you were just tricking him!"

Lu Huaixi couldn't help firing back.

The old man choked, and as he made his way out, he could be heard muttering: "Such a temper on that awful girl — and she wants me, this old man, to swallow it and say sorry."

He said it, and then seemed to think of something. He stopped at the doorway.

"I'll have the medicine decocted now. Stop clinging to him and get him lying flat — no lingering, you're making more work for me."

Outside, the courtyard was full of people.

From the moment they heard Xie Yuanjing was awake — the Old Master, the First Madam, Xie Yuanjing's own guards, even the people Lu Huaixi had brought from the Lù estate — all of them had come to wait in the courtyard.

And so, naturally, they all heard that voice in its full, vigorous projection.

Even Lu Huaixi, who was not ordinarily given to awkwardness, found in this moment that she only wanted to find a hole and disappear into it.

She bit her lip and couldn't get a single word out.

The door swung shut. Xie Yuanjing's quiet laugh fell again.

Then he stepped forward — into full view of everyone who could see — and drew her into his arms.

"You've been wronged. When the truth is — it was I who held you."

chapters.title: You Don't Know How To Tell On Someone?
chapters.content:
Though it was the middle of the night, the First Madam came quickly once word reached her.

By the time she arrived, Xie Yuanjing's wounds had been dressed again, a clean inner robe put on, and a fresh bowl of medicine taken.

He was still visibly weak — nothing like his usual self.

But to have come to his senses this quickly was already a great fortune.

The First Madam's eyes went red the moment she walked in. Even so, she didn't collapse into tears, keeping her composure throughout.

"As long as you're awake. As long as you're awake."

She stopped not far from the bed, her voice carrying a mixture of relief and lingering fear.

"Whatever you do from now on — please don't put yourself at risk again. If something had truly happened to you, what would your mother do? Those people are nothing but petty troublemakers. Are they worth this?"

Though she said nothing explicit, everyone who heard her had their own guesses.

A thing like this — Xie Yuanjing couldn't have been unprepared for it, and couldn't have had no means of fighting back.

And yet he had still endured the punishment, and still allowed himself to be drawn into the suspicions of others.

"Mother, please don't be upset. I haven't truly put myself at risk."

Xie Yuanjing leaned back against the bed, one hand resting on top of the thin coverlet, the knuckles slightly raised, fingers long and slender.

"He's been growing more and more attached to the people outside over the past two years. Something like this was always going to happen eventually. There's an advantage to it coming sooner rather than later. Mother doesn't need to worry, and needn't fret over this injury."

He was still somewhat weak. In the lamplight, the side of his face looked pale and drawn.

The First Madam knew he didn't want to speak of this right now. Her lips moved, and she let it go.

Saying more would accomplish nothing. The person before her had his own mind.

But he was still her son, and seeing him injured like this — how could she not ache for him?

The First Madam sighed.

In the corner of her vision, she caught sight of Lu Huaixi sitting nearby. Seeing the flush on her face — from the heat, or from having looked after him so long — she felt a new rise of worry.

She went over and drew her down to sit, her expression carrying a note of reproach.

"You didn't sleep when I told you to last night, and now it's the middle of the night and you're still here. Do you not care about your own body?"

The First Madam frowned.

Right now the Marquis's household was full of complications, and things outside were trained on it closely because of recent events. There was no room to let her guard down.

She had no wish to bring up the marriage arrangement at a moment like this, when both of them needed their attention elsewhere.

Besides, this girl had not argued anything. The person she needed to confront was her son — the one who always had an idea of his own.

"Don't use your youth as an excuse to run yourself ragged."

"I'm not tired, Mother. And I slept until just now tonight."

"That's still not acceptable. Starting tomorrow — no keeping watch here at night."

The First Madam's concern left Lu Huaixi vaguely dazed.

She had expected her to use Xie Yuanjing's waking as an opportunity to raise the matter of their arrangement. But right now the First Madam appeared to have no such intention.

The corners of her lips shifted — she didn't say yes, and she didn't say no.

The First Madam seemed to have already assumed her answer.

She said what she had to say, then continued: "I heard that his father sent maids over during the day — to attend personally to Yuanjing. It upset you?"

The topic shifted faster than Lu Huaixi had expected. Without thinking about it too much, she nodded.

Xie Yuanjing's brow tightened slightly at those words. His gaze moved upward, settling on Lu Huaixi's eyes, the emotion held in those depths unclear.

Lu Huaixi felt his shift, and met his eyes for a moment.

She couldn't quite read what had changed in him — didn't know whether he was saying she should not have done what she did, or something else entirely.

She looked away first, and turned her attention back to the First Madam.

"There does need to be someone attending Yuanjing. You need rest too — you can't keep watch like this day after day. But his father's people cannot remain in this inner household. The next time he sends people, you just do exactly as you did today — send them away."

Everyone understood what placing those maids in the household would have meant.

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a moment, then said yes.

"The maids in this courtyard are a little sparse, it's true. I'll pick some suitable people and send them over tomorrow. Once they've served through this period, if they suit you, you can keep them. And your own room—"

"My room doesn't need anyone added."

Xie Yuanjing said it with his eyes still on Lu Huaixi.

Only after the words were out did he wait a beat and turn his head.

"Mother doesn't need to do the choosing. Even if you did, I wouldn't take anyone."

"You—"

The First Madam was a little annoyed, but mindful of the fact that he had only just woken, she swallowed it.

"If you won't take maids, are you truly going to have Huaixi keeping watch over you day and night? After you entered the palace, she barely closed her eyes. She was criticized by your grandfather, and your father gave her a difficult time as well. Right now—"

"What did Grandfather say?"

Xie Yuanjing's brow creased. He didn't let the First Madam continue.

The First Madam paused, unsure how to answer.

In the silence, Xie Yuanjing looked at Lu Huaixi again.

Seeing her eyes fixed elsewhere, not speaking, not lifting her head — not giving any indication of what she was thinking — something uneasy stirred in him.

"Mother should go and rest."

He pressed his thoughts down and said calmly, "The courtyard has plenty of people. No maids are necessary."

"I know you have people. But Gong Zhuo and Gong Fei — can they really match a maid for attentiveness?"

"Mother."

Xie Yuanjing's tone dropped a degree. His patience had at last worn thin. "Don't pick anyone. Don't send anyone. Don't involve yourself in my courtyard's affairs. At night I'll look after her myself — it won't be like the past two days."

The First Madam felt everything she'd been about to say pushed back down her throat.

She kept feeling that something wasn't quite right — but no matter how quickly she tried to think through it, she couldn't put her finger on what.

After the First Madam left, a quiet fell over the room.

Xie Yuanjing neither asked nor said anything. He simply watched the figure not far from him for a long while, then got to his feet.

Lu Huaixi heard the movement and looked up. She saw him swing his feet to the floor and rushed over to stop him from moving carelessly.

But in drawing close, she walked straight into what he'd been waiting for — and found herself caught, with nowhere to go.

"If you've been wronged, why not say so?"

Xie Yuanjing's thumb rested against her wrist. He looked up at her, one hand curving through her waist, pressing steadily.

"You're this foolish — I've been awake this long, and you still don't know how to tell on someone?"

chapters.title: What Are We To Each Other?
chapters.content:
When Xie Yuanjing turned gentle, even his voice took on a quality that was somehow beguiling.

Lu Huaixi hadn't felt it that acutely before — but hearing that question, she suddenly felt that the past two days had been full of grievance, and full of displeasure.

She kept her eyes lowered and said nothing, letting him draw her closer and closer, one degree at a time.

"My wife drove them away for me. I'm grateful beyond words."

Xie Yuanjing settled them both into a seat.

"Every grievance you've endured on my account over these past two days — I remember it all. You can lose your temper with me. But don't let his actions make you angry at me instead. Of everyone, you and I are on the same side."

The he in question — both of them knew it meant the Marquis of Chengen.

After the words fell, Xie Yuanjing paused, then let the hand at her wrist slip lower, catching the tips of her pale, slender fingers and kneading them softly.

His tone was calm, somehow — yet with an inexplicable gravity beneath it.

"Grandfather's reprimand — do you want to tell me about it?"

Lu Huaixi still didn't speak. Only the corners of her mouth pressed together, hesitating for a moment before going loose again.

When she thought about it, it wasn't really a reprimand. Just that he didn't believe in the two of them, and didn't like her involving herself in matters between father and son.

It wasn't that she didn't want to tell on someone — it was just that, when she thought it through, there wasn't much to say.

She couldn't very well say: your grandfather doesn't intend for us to last, and it makes me unhappy.

She said nothing. Xie Yuanjing didn't push her to speak, only kept working gently at her fingers.

"It was my fault for sleeping so long and letting you exhaust yourself. Did that maid come into the room today?"

"She did."

"Then replace everything in the room she touched."

Xie Yuanjing said it slowly: "There will be no other people in this inner household. So honestly, this courtyard doesn't really need many maids at all. But you can take on two more at your side — I'll tell Gong Zhuo when the time comes, and have him choose people with some skill for your protection."

The words carried an unmistakable second meaning.

Lu Huaixi was somewhat surprised.

She glanced at him. His eyes were steady and unreadable. She hesitated several times, then looked away again.

After a while, she still asked.

"What does that mean?"

Xie Yuanjing let out a quiet laugh.

The motion pulled at his wound — but from start to finish, not a trace of discomfort showed on his face.

"What does it mean, indeed."

He repeated her words back in her own tone, and when he'd had his small amusement, turned serious again.

"It means I won't be taking anyone in. Maids or concubines — I won't take anyone. And I won't in the future either."

Xie Yuanjing stilled the hand that had been working at her fingers, and let them interlock instead. "I will not take a secondary wife. I will not have a noble concubine. And I will not keep someone outside."

Seeing the long lashes over Lu Huaixi's downcast eyes tremble faintly — a real reaction, at last — the last of the tightness in Xie Yuanjing's chest began to ease.

He wanted Lu Huaixi to give him a response. To care about him. To accompany him. Even to claim sole possession of him.

But now that it was actually happening, he was afraid that all the unpleasant and complicated things about the household would make her unwilling to deal with it, and push her away.

Like holding a rare gem — no matter how you placed it, it never felt quite safely enough done.

So after thinking it over, he decided to lay himself bare first.

But he had no intention of using that to pressure Lu Huaixi into drawing closer.

What he wanted had always been all of her — her feelings, her dependence, her trust. He wanted her to be so bound to him that they could never be separated.

So he moved carefully, a little at a time.

Knowing when to advance, when to hold one step back — he had always been able to calculate these things with precision.

Like when he had pulled back before the trip to Huiquebo.

That day he had said whether she liked him or not didn't really matter — and in return he had gotten Lu Huaixi's unease.

Even that quiet flicker of unease had been, to him, a kind of signal.

And then this injury — even in the concealing of it, there had been a deliberate design.

He thought that if she had even the smallest amount of worry over him, it would bring her one step closer.

"One wife is plenty. Any more and I'd have a headache."

With his thoughts settled, Xie Yuanjing broke the tender yet awkward tension between them in a light-handed way.

He smiled, and drew her close again.

The tautness in Lu Huaixi's heart relaxed at those words, and then her heart began to beat very fast, one after another.

The silence didn't last long. She was nervous — and she had never expected to hear such a thing, the sort of promise that if spoken aloud, most people probably wouldn't believe.

But people always find their footing when someone reaches out a branch to steady them.

"So you find me difficult."

Lu Huaixi turned her face to the side, taking the lead from his last words.

"You have the nerve to find me difficult. These past two days I was nearly frightened to death. Who's the one with the headache here?"

"You. You're the one with a headache because of me."

"You know perfectly well and you're still saying that — I haven't slept well or eaten well for two days. I was afraid to watch them dress your wounds and couldn't stand it if I didn't. Not only did I have to manage people on the outside, I also fell out with the Marquis of Chengen..."

The muttering grew heavier as it went.

Lu Huaixi said it, and found herself genuinely upset. She was getting angrier and angrier.

She raised her head and glared at him, then reached out and started pulling his inner robe open.

This move, of all things, actually startled Xie Yuanjing. He hadn't finished working out what to say to coax her, and before he knew it, she had pressed him back onto the bed.

"Look — the wound is bleeding through again!"

With the fabric half in the way, the worst of it wasn't entirely visible.

But what she could see was bad enough — even half the picture was enough to tell you things were not good.

"I'm not going to settle accounts with you right now. Lie still and let me look at the injury."

Lu Huaixi bent her head close. When she spoke, every breath fell against his chest.

The warmth spread from that patch of skin outward, rushing downward, as though lighting a line of fire as it went.

And she still didn't know it. Both hands pressing down above, grazing the uninjured places, coming to rest at his waist and abdomen.

Xie Yuanjing, who had been holding himself back for too long, felt himself respond almost instantly. He instinctively seized her hands — wanting her to come closer, and afraid of her coming closer.

In the end he exhaled, and pressed her still.

"I know what I'm doing."

He gave a helpless laugh. "Just lie down. Come and lie down with me — there's still two hours before it's light. Sleep, and you can look at it after."

"Stop trying to get around me!"

"How could I."

Xie Yuanjing gentled his voice. "I won't be like last night. Trust me — sleep now. I'll watch over you."

"I can't sleep with you. It's not appropriate."

"It is."

Xie Yuanjing didn't even look at her, just set her down toward the wall. "I'm not separating rooms."

"Even if we don't separate rooms — Mother has arranged a new room for me. And besides, I'll bump into your wounds in my sleep, and it'll delay getting your medicine applied."

She said all this, but Lu Huaixi was afraid of struggling and accidentally hurting him again, so she didn't dare actually resist.

In truth she hadn't slept well in the new room — even just now, when she'd finally dropped off from sheer exhaustion, there hadn't been a moment of real peace behind her closed eyes.

Lu Huaixi talked herself through one refusal after another, and then quite obediently rolled herself in. Her expression still held a trace of reluctance.

Xie Yuanjing found it both funny and tender — and felt, with every one of her small movements, something steadying in his chest, like a warm weight settling into place.

"The medicine in the morning can wait until after you sleep."

"But that's not right — the old man will scold me again."

"No one will say anything. Now that I'm awake, I won't let anyone say a word to you."

"But I'm afraid I'll roll onto your wound in my sleep."

"You won't."

Xie Yuanjing touched the corner of her eye. "Lie still. Don't go back to the other room. From now on, sleep here."

The moment the words were out, Lu Huaixi had already grabbed the thin coverlet and pulled it over herself.

This bed was the one she'd come to know.

And to be honest — setting aside the brief doze earlier in the day — this was the first time she and Xie Yuanjing had properly shared a bed.

But she didn't have the face to let that show. She was still deliberating over whether to wait until he fell asleep before slipping back to the other room.

Once a person relaxes, she stops paying attention to what comes out of her mouth.

Lu Huaixi squinted drowsily, and the words came out on their own: "Stop fussing over me. I'll go back to sleeping there once you're better. If anything, you're the one who needs to change rooms."

"Is that so."

Xie Yuanjing only smiled — a faint, barely-there curve. "I'm afraid that won't be happening. Stop thinking about it."

"Mother said so. Mother knows about us."

"What are we?"

Xie Yuanjing turned the question back on her, his eyes carrying a deep, unhurried significance. "Right now, you and I — what are we to each other?"

chapters.title: Inseparable
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing asked it with sudden seriousness, and he was very close. Lu Huaixi fell into those dark, feeling-laden eyes before she knew it, and her breath caught.

What are we. What are we.

It did seem as though they were the kind who could share a bed.

The thought crossed Lu Huaixi's mind with a boldness that she startled herself with — and in the next instant she was thrown into a fluster of her own making.

Xie Yuanjing laughed softly.

He didn't ask again. He simply pressed his lips to her forehead.

"It's fine if you can't say it. I can wait—"

Wait for you to give me a name.

The touch against her brow was warm and soft.

Xie Yuanjing was reluctant to draw back — and yet he knew he couldn't continue right now.

"All right. We can talk when you wake up. Close your eyes."

"......Mm."

—

Elsewhere, candle-flames were also flickering — in a house on the south side of the eastern quarter.

Hé Bìnxìn had gotten up to take his medicine and was lying in bed, his complexion not quite good.

A woman came in, looked at the attendant maid beside him, sent her back to her room, and sat down in the chair not far from the bed. When she spoke, there was a faint note of reproach.

"Why did you talk him into leaving so quickly? We'd worked so hard to keep him for one more day — such a perfect opportunity, and you didn't use it to show him more of your injuries, to win some more promises. Who knows when another chance like this will come?"

The woman was somewhat displeased.

But she kept her tone restrained, not quite willing to be too harsh with this son of hers.

"Once he's back in the manor, and he's gone to look in on that eldest young master Xie — who's going to remember you're still sitting in this house recovering? You really—"

"That's enough."

Hé Bìnxìn had heard enough.

He furrowed his brow, without a trace of the gentle courtesy he usually showed to people.

"If I didn't talk him into going back, and he stayed here indefinitely, what happens when other people start paying attention and talking?"

"What if people talk? You want people to know, don't you, so you can—"

"That's different."

Hé Bìnxìn cut her off with impatience. "What could you gain right now by getting him into the Marquis's manor? A concubine's position. And me — a concubine's son, pressed under Xie Yuanjing's thumb every day, watching their faces."

He kept his voice low:

"But if we show that we don't want to put him in a difficult position, if we speak up to protect him and distance ourselves — he'll feel guilty. He'll find ways to treat us well, find ways to pave paths for me. Once I have standing and power and come into the Marquis's manor then, it will be those two — mother and son — who look to our faces."

"I understand what you're saying, but no matter how strained things are between those two, they've lived together all these years. And from what I hear, the injuries on that side are also not light this time. What if he softens..."

"Then make sure he has no time to soften."

Hé Bìnxìn's expression darkened further.

He hadn't originally planned to let this go as far as the palace. He had simply intended to act as though he knew nothing, and use the opportunity to throw some mud at Xie Yuanjing.

Let the rift between him and the Marquis of Chengen deepen — and eventually, let it fracture.

But his teacher was too stubborn. There was no reasoning with him. He insisted on demanding an accounting.

Xie Yuanjing was the kind of person who could be made to account for anything?

He had no idea how to recover from that — so all he could do was play the part of the magnanimous one urging restraint, and in the meantime, think of something else to drive the wedge between father and son deeper.

"At first light, Mother should have someone go to the Marquis's manor."

Hé Bìnxìn considered this and said:

"The Marquis couldn't bring in the divine physician for me, and he's been feeling the embarrassment of it, feeling guilty toward me more than ever. Have Mother secretly send someone over to say I had a recurring fever in the night — that I nearly didn't make it through, and that in my delirium I only wanted to see my father once."

The woman quickly grasped what her son was suggesting.

Wanting to see him while severely ill — but restraining herself from seeing him once well again.

And to bring up the divine physician as well — a reminder to the Marquis of Chengen that a Marquis, a lord of his own household, couldn't even bring a single physician to his son's side. That meant being treated as someone not worth respecting.

"At first light I'll have someone go. And I'll have them find out while they're there what the situation really is on that side. Rest early. And don't have those distracting people in to attend you."

"I know."

Hé Bìnxìn finished and closed his eyes again.

Things all seemed to be moving within his control — yet his heart refused to settle.

He knew the only news that would ever truly give him peace was if Xie Yuanjing never woke up again.

Hé Bìnxìn lay back down and turned over. He had no intention of going back to sleep.

—

Past the height of summer, nighttime brought a genuine coolness when you let yourself feel it.

Lu Huaixi had been genuinely tired.

She truly wanted to sleep, and thought she would fall asleep the moment her eyes closed.

But now she was lying beside Xie Yuanjing, listening to his deep and even breathing, and she found herself alert again — her eyes refusing to settle shut.

She didn't dare get too close to him. Fortunately the bed was large, with plenty of space for her to roll back and forth.

On her most recent quiet shuffle sideways, the man lying still finally reacted — at last running out of patience with it.

He turned a little, extended his arm, and hooked it around Lu Huaixi's waist, drawing her toward him.

Seeing her about to struggle, he spoke first.

"Don't move. The wounds still hurt."

Most of Xie Yuanjing's injuries were across his chest. Every time he caught Lu Huaixi like this, she tended to go still for quite a while.

But this time it seemed a little harder than usual — because Xie Yuanjing's hand kept working at the soft flesh at her waist, leaving her squirming with a ticklish, flustered sensation she couldn't quite escape.

"You're the one who shouldn't be moving."

Lu Huaixi tried to shrink back — but the man who'd just claimed to want to sleep was slowly opening his eyes, looking at her from very close, very close.

Lu Huaixi went still. She didn't know what to do.

In the next instant, Xie Yuanjing's face drifted closer. Nose to nose.

"Not sleepy?"

They were so close that Lu Huaixi felt as though speaking would put her lips against something. Her heart was beating faster than it had been before. She wanted to push him back a little — but stopped herself for fear of touching the wound.

Xie Yuanjing seemed to be doing it deliberately. Noticing her suppressed endurance, he tilted his chin slightly and let it brush her lips.

"While I was unconscious, I dreamed I kissed you. You were just as soft. And you bit me, and said I wasn't doing it well enough."

"You......"

Lu Huaixi was stunned. Shocked. Lost.

The hand resting at her waist was still moving, unhurried and deliberate. She was like a fish pinned to a board — caught, with nowhere to go.

"Do you want to scold me?"

Xie Yuanjing curved his lips. Against his slightly pale face, it gave him, inexplicably, the free and dissolute air of a languid, fragile scholar.

"Scold me if you want — and then get used to this. Before, we couldn't do this — because of propriety, because the bond wasn't there, because I was afraid you'd be angry."

"And now propriety doesn't apply?"

Lu Huaixi couldn't help answering.

But sure enough, just as she'd anticipated — the moment she opened her mouth, her lips touched his.

Xie Yuanjing himself was being sorely tried.

He called it a step-by-step, tentative approach — but every time he drew close, it was he who had the harder time holding back.

And yet he lingered, unable to let go of this sweetness.

"Now we are husband and wife, one body. Now we are inseparable. Now I can't hold back—"

He stopped. Pressed his lips to hers. And swallowed the last two words.

chapters.title: Bickering
chapters.content:
The next day, after Xie Yuanjing's wounds had been freshly dressed, the old man spent a good long while blowing his whiskers and glaring.

Lu Huaixi kept her mouth shut and followed behind in silence, accepting the full weight of it without complaint.

"What do you need a physician for when you're this capable? Do whatever you like, live as long as you last — wouldn't that be nice and clean? And don't try to act well-behaved in front of me. Helping him with his medicine, watching him drink it — all pointless. Since neither of you will follow instructions, it would be simpler to just leave him lying there and let nature take its course."

Xie Yuanjing laughed at that, and couldn't help cutting in.

"Old physician, please — scold me instead. I was the one who didn't listen. I was the one who got up in the night."

"Old man, I'm scolding you!"

The old man tossed the remaining medicine into Lu Huaixi's arms. "But don't you try to get out of it either, girl."

"I wasn't trying to."

Lu Huaixi's voice was very small. She sounded rather short on conviction.

Xie Yuanjing had indeed aggravated the wound because of her the night before. And she had fallen asleep and draped her arms and legs across him.

But she hadn't known when he'd gotten up, or when he'd changed his own inner robe.

All she knew was that after Xie Yuanjing kissed her and she'd dozed off, she had peeled herself up to take a look.

The wound was still ugly — but with no new blood, she had finally let herself drop fully into sleep.

"It was I who didn't listen to her. I waited until she was asleep and got up on my own."

"Hm, and what's the point of saying so now? Expecting praise? Though you are, I'll admit, remarkably fearless. Injured like that and still carrying on — a rare breed, old man hasn't seen many of those."

The old man gave a cold snort, turned back to his prescription, and presented nothing but his back.

Xie Yuanjing, composed as ever, replied mildly: "The heat. Lying there sweating was uncomfortable."

He sat half-propped up on the bed, head tilted, still somewhat pale.

But beyond that, not a single sign of distress — as though he had recovered fully from the moment he woke last night.

Yet anyone who had seen those wounds knew that most people in his place would still be unable to so much as move.

The old man had been carrying on with his tidying, but hearing that tone — so unhurried, so unbothered about the injuries — he couldn't help glancing over.

"You'd make a fine trial subject for medicine."

He muttered, unable to stop himself. "Can take it and handle pain — where others manage one trial a day, you could probably manage three. How about—"

"Why are you still scheming to use him!"

Lu Huaixi, who had been quietly putting up with everything, looked up and glared. In an instant she had forgotten she was still in the wrong. Her voice came out loud enough to make him jump.

"You say one more thing like that, I'm done with those herbs — I won't tend them, and I won't come up the mountain to see you anymore!"

"You, you — you—"

The old man's sense of being in the wrong was immediate, and his commanding posture from a moment ago deflated all at once.

"Can't a man say anything now, can't joke around — you, girl, where does all this temper come from! Just now you were being so obedient, and now you flip around like that!"

"That's completely different!"

Lu Huaixi was on solid ground here, and she knew it.

She glanced outside at the light, set down what she was holding, and stood with her hands on her hips and her chin lifted.

"It's this hot out, and I already agreed to go gather herbs for you in a few days. And you're still trying to trick people, you're still going to go back on your word — then I'll go back on mine!"

"You can't do that! Do you know what they say about a gentleman's word?"

"I'm not a gentleman!"

Xie Yuanjing listened to their back-and-forth and laughed without comment.

After another moment, he spoke quietly. "Old physician Zēng."

When the old man looked over, he considered his words. "If old physician Zēng is looking for someone knowledgeable about medicinal plants to tend things for him, this junior has several people who could go."

"Don't need them. I have my own people."

The old man waved him off.

He knew what he meant. He turned it down before the words were done.

"Of the people who tend things for me, none grows half as much as that girl does. If not for that, with a temper like hers — I'd have no patience for talking to her."

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together and didn't expose him.

Calling her over just to talk whenever he felt like it — even when there were no herbs to tend — and still acting like this. Nothing but stubbornness.

"This isn't asking her to walk through fire. Compared to trialing medicine, she eats well, she sleeps well, and she can dig up quite a few good things on my mountain. What are you worrying about?"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing.

The sun was strong and the days were long. Lu Huaixi had been raised in comfort and gentleness, and he had no wish to send her away.

But he found no weakness in the old man he could use, and no terms he was confident he could negotiate to.

And especially now, hearing this, his mind suddenly jumped back to the first thing he had ever learned about Lu Huaixi —

She had received a pronouncement from the old abbot at Wén'ān Temple, who said she carried good fortune in her fate — exceptionally lucky, and while she wouldn't bring fortune to all the world, she was someone who would bring prosperity to whatever household and whoever she was with.

These past days, he hadn't been unaware of it.

The changes in the Xie household. Things that she had, blurrily, touched in passing — and which always seemed to come to a clean conclusion in the end. Even the company of people who tended to recover. The fish that had swum up to bite the hook when she was on the boat.

If you didn't string it together, none of it stood out. But once you connected it, Lu Huaixi's good fortune was easy to see.

Yet Xie Yuanjing did not believe this was anything to do with divination or fate.

He only thought it was a reflection of who Lu Huaixi was as a person.

She was good — and so the things that came to her could become good.

And he was not.

He was cold toward people, full of calculation, slow to trust. He would never have Lu Huaixi's clarity.

So the world would not reflect goodness back at him, and he could not take her place in doing what she had agreed to do.

That thought made Xie Yuanjing faintly restless.

"Don't go thinking she's suffering or working hard out there. The mountain is comfortable. Better than this Marquis's manor in some ways."

The old man gave him another look.

After last night, he was well aware of what this eldest young master Xie was thinking.

But this time he didn't put on airs or blow his whiskers.

Though he still wore a look of mild displeasure, there was nothing behind it — just a face that couldn't quite bring itself to manufacture a proper sulk.

"And she's this soft — do you really think she can last a full day? If she gathers ten or so plants in a day, that's already doing well!

"It's only you who's been fooled by her into thinking she suffers so much in my care. If you have the energy to worry about her, worry about your own wounds!"

Lu Huaixi wasn't planning to argue that point. She was prone to idleness during the day, and she knew it.

But her mind had caught more on the old man's last sentence.

Just then Jing Shuang brought in the medicine. She accepted it.

As she passed the old man, Lu Huaixi thought a moment, and then deliberately softened her tone.

"Old physician Zēng—" she tried, "will there really be no lasting harm from his injuries? You said just now — does that mean the injuries are still very serious?"

"Who's called old physician Zēng?"

Hearing her suddenly shift to that gentle, deferential voice, the old man nearly jumped, and the rare moment of courtesy Lu Huaixi was attempting was startled right back out of her.

"When have you ever called me old physician Zēng in that nice tone? Giving this old man a fright for nothing."

"......"

The commotion was large enough that from within the room, Xie Yuanjing burst out laughing again.

That low, contained laugh reached her, and in one instant Lu Huaixi was overcome with a vexed embarrassment — caught out, face burning, wanting to say something and unable to.

But Xie Yuanjing's voice followed quickly.

"Old physician Zēng is taking advantage of my wife now. That address — it's naturally her way of showing you respect."

The old man blinked, realized both of them were on the same side, gave a huff, and looked away without speaking.

Lu Huaixi heard Xie Yuanjing's defense and felt the lightness return to her face at once — and the awkwardness of the moment before was forgotten entirely.

She smiled and said that was exactly right, then carried the medicine inside.

But she had barely stepped through the beaded curtain when Gong Zhuo's voice came from outside.

"Young Master. Young Madam. The Marquis has come."

Lu Huaixi's eyes were still curved with a smile, and the corners of her mouth still lifted.

She had just walked past the curtain when Gong Zhuo spoke — and her gaze met Xie Yuanjing's.

At those words, she dropped her expression almost on instinct. The curve of her lips straightened, her displeasure entirely visible.

The old man noticed her change.

He stroked his beard and looked out toward the courtyard, his gaze settling on the tall figure approaching from outside.

"Truly — no manners at all! This Marquis enters this courtyard and still needs to be announced before being let in — does he still have any regard for me as a father?"

The Marquis of Chengen's opening words were a reprimand — but then he caught sight of the long-bearded old man nearby and paused, his expression shifting. He pressed down his temper and asked a question.

"Are you old physician Zēng?"

chapters.title: Standing Up For Her
chapters.content:
Xie Zǐzhāng had seen the old imperial physician in the palace years ago.

Seeing him again now, he felt the man was just as vigorous as ever — with a certain air of otherworldly ease about him as well.

A good portion of the frustration he'd been holding in dissolved. The impulse to scold his daughter-in-law for not knowing her place was put aside for the moment.

"I didn't know old physician Zēng was here at the manor. The hospitality must have been lacking. I'll have someone prepare a proper residence for old physician Zēng right away and arrange for new attendants."

Then he looked toward Lu Huaixi inside the room.

Remembering how she had turned away his people so directly the day before, he let the stern expression back onto his face.

"If Yuanjing doesn't know his place, do you have to not know yours as well? A guest of distinction arrives at the household and no one thinks to inform me. You spend your time driving people out on a jealous impulse, and now there's not even a proper maid to attend. Aren't you afraid of being laughed at?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing at first.

She carried the medicine inside, held it out to Xie Yuanjing, and signaled for him to drink it.

When the bowl was empty, she raised her hand and covered his mouth, pressed him back down, and fixed him with a look that clearly said — don't open your mouth.

"This daughter-in-law indeed falls short of magnanimity, and cannot compare to Mother's gracious patience."

Only then did Lu Huaixi rise and step out.

She didn't conceal a thing. She simply looked at the man before her with a faint, mocking smile, and said: "Mother has the capacity to put the larger picture first and swallow her own feelings. She can tolerate Father's two days outside, not inquiring about her own son's injuries. This daughter-in-law is not capable of the same."

"Impertinent! Don't speak nonsense!"

The Marquis of Chengen's expression darkened.

He hadn't anticipated her being this bold in front of an outsider — so audacious, so sharp-tongued. Fury stirred behind his eyes.

"You've been spoiled at home until you don't know how the world works. You don't even know to respect this household, and you dare to speak to your elders this way!"

"I was indeed indulged at home. But I wouldn't call it not knowing how the world works. A response of proper respect is hard to muster for someone like the Marquis, who pays no attention to his own family."

Lu Huaixi was not the least bit intimidated.

She had even said what she wanted back to Old Master Xie. Why would she hold back for a Marquis of Chengen who had already shown his cards the day before?

If he hadn't come looking for trouble, she could have endured it.

But he had come — and looked ready to take away the person she had invited, no less — and had opened with a reprimand. She was not going to hold back.

"I'm not sure which words of mine were wrong. Xie Yuanjing has been injured for two days — has the Marquis come to look in on him even once, or sent anyone to ask? Ah, but someone was sent yesterday."

Lu Huaixi paused, then bent her lips into a smile of seemingly impeccable pleasantness.

"Two maids were sent yesterday. They came to compete with me over someone who belonged here, and intended to quietly make themselves at home in this inner household. Unfortunately, I sent them back.

"The next time the Marquis wishes to send people — please wait until he's awake. Otherwise people might get the wrong idea — that the eldest young master of the Xie family is so fond of women that he can't let it rest even while gravely injured... ah, unless the Marquis wasn't actually aware that his injuries are grave?"

With every word Lu Huaixi spoke, the color drained a little more from the Marquis of Chengen's face. He felt his dignity shrinking.

Especially with the old physician he'd come to recruit standing right there — a former member of the imperial medical service.

Watching her grow more and more explicit, more and more unguarded, the Marquis of Chengen called for his people without stopping to think, intending to give her a lesson.

But when the call went out, no one entered.

After several sharp shouts, the Marquis of Chengen understood with sudden, cold clarity — his son's control over things here was even broader than he had imagined.

In his ears, a piece of news delivered that morning surfaced.

Thinking of the way that pair, mother and son outside, depended on him — so differently from how this son in here regarded him — and of the face he had lost in front of them over the matter of the physician, the Marquis of Chengen's anger surged higher.

Without thinking, he moved to grab her.

But in the next instant, a fit of violent coughing came from within.

Then a figure stepped out, drawing Lu Huaixi behind him.

Xie Yuanjing's face was considerably paler than it had been moments ago. Whether the coughing had pulled at the wound, even his lip color was lighter than when he had first woken.

The corner of his mouth was already seeping a thread of blood, and a spreading stain was showing through his inner robe.

But he still stood in front of Lu Huaixi, holding himself steady, not yielding an inch. He raised a hand and wiped the corner of his mouth, letting his fingertips take on a smear of crimson.

Lu Huaixi's heart clenched. That red was too vivid — she could barely stand to look at it a second time.

But he had been completely fine just a moment ago when she was feeding him medicine. The wound hadn't been bleeding through.

She was reaching for alarm when the hand on her forearm tightened — steady, as though in reassurance.

"What does Father intend to do?"

Xie Yuanjing's gaze settled on the Marquis of Chengen's face.

Seeing a flash of surprise there — as though the man hadn't expected the injuries to be this severe — he gave a thin, cold laugh.

Then came another wave of coughing that would not stop.

"How would His Majesty allow injuries this serious?"

The Marquis of Chengen frowned. He appeared genuinely unconvinced.

Word had spread quickly on the outside, and he had received the household's own messages — but he had never believed it.

And yet his son's injuries, right in front of him, appeared worse than anything rumor had described. It looked as though even standing for too long would be a strain.

"Father need not ask what he already knows."

Before long, Xie Yuanjing's coughing stilled. His already sharp jaw looked even more blade-like for having grown a little thinner.

"Thanks to Father's efforts, I lie here now gravely injured. Is Father satisfied with this?"

The Marquis of Chengen's brow grew tighter and tighter.

Hearing those words, he didn't know why — but the anger surged in him instinctively.

Xie Yuanjing gave him no opening. He was too tired of waiting — or perhaps simply couldn't hold on much longer.

"Father has something to say — say it now. Today Father can still enter this courtyard, only because I have just woken. After this — there's no guarantee you'll be let in."

"What does that mean? This is the Marquis's manor. I am your father!"

The Marquis of Chengen heard the implication — that he was being barred — and could not believe it. He cried out in furious disbelief:

"You intend to block me? Don't forget — you carry the Xie name from me. And the title of eldest young master of this manor — I gave you that!"

"Yes. And so from now on, this Marquis's manor — I won't be managing it."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was even. Beyond the weakness that was slightly more pronounced than usual, there was barely any fluctuation in it. Cool. Indifferent.

The Marquis of Chengen went rigid where he stood. He thought for a moment he had heard wrong.

Lu Huaixi was also stunned.

If not for Xie Yuanjing's hand still gripping her arm with a measure of force, she would have thought she had imagined the whole thing.

"Going forward, there's no need to involve me in Xie family matters. I have no interest. No interest in your title of Marquis, no interest in this household. By the same measure — don't set your sights on my people. Otherwise, I make no promises that we can continue to leave each other in peace."

When the words were done, Xie Yuanjing coughed a few more times, then looked up toward the courtyard and called for Gong Zhuo.

"I still need rest. I won't keep Father."

chapters.title: Do You Know How To Be A Married Couple?
chapters.content:
It was only when the door shut that Lu Huaixi came back from what Xie Yuanjing had just said.

Right now she had no attention to spare for the Marquis's manor or anything beyond it. The emotion she'd been holding back spilled over, and she called out to old physician Zēng with reddened eyes, her voice threaded with a panic she couldn't press down.

Xie Yuanjing's hand slid down from her forearm, folding around her palm, and then he gave her a small smile.

"Don't cry. That was to deceive him."

He glanced at old physician Zēng, and seeing the old man's brow drawn together in what looked like approaching fury, his eyes carried a faint apology.

The old man seemed to understand what he meant. He held himself back for a long moment. Finally he turned and said: "I'm going out to prepare medicine for this little wretch."

Only the two of them remained. Xie Yuanjing obediently got back on the bed.

He didn't rush to explain — only thought for a moment, then said with sincerity: "Going forward, even if I'm no longer the elder son of this Marquis's manor, I will still be able to protect you. And I won't let you suffer."

"Don't speak."

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes and began carefully unfastening his inner robe to look at the wound.

The deepest one had split open again, the raw flesh welling up — ugly and severe.

Whether he had done it deliberately, or simply had not paid it any attention — even when the pain must have been considerable, only the briefest flicker had crossed his brow. That was all.

"Just this once, I want you to know. Please don't be angry."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze rested on her face. Stubborn and unwavering.

"Whether I am or am not this household's eldest young master — I will see that you live well. I won't let you be implicated in anything because of me. And I won't let you suffer, not even a little."

"I told you not to talk!"

Lu Huaixi couldn't keep her temper.

But her voice, even when she raised it at him, never quite found its footing — it came out soft and muddled, like she was on the verge of tears.

She hadn't meant for Xie Yuanjing to get up.

Her original plan had been for him to stay lying there pretending to be asleep. She would go out, describe the injuries as severe, chase the Marquis of Chengen away with that alone — and still end up circulating whatever she needed to circulate.

But this person had had his own ideas.

She was certain he had made that decision in the brief span of time after drinking his medicine.

And that coughing — the blood — had to have been forced up with his own internal strength. It wasn't something that could have happened without cost.

"How long do you plan on staying in this bed? A month? Two? Is this what you call not letting me suffer?"

Lu Huaixi's voice was not loud. She still didn't raise her head.

The apprehension in her voice made the sound waver, just slightly.

That small fissure was caught immediately by the man before her.

"Don't be angry at me. Just now — he was about to lay hands on you. I couldn't stand aside and watch."

Xie Yuanjing softened his voice. "If I stood there and watched him come at you, what would be the point of me?"

That low, masculine voice — and yet he managed to put something plaintive into it.

Against the fragile beauty of that face in its pallor, it was the kind of thing that made anger inexplicably difficult to hold.

Lu Huaixi's heart had already ached over the weakness she'd seen in him just a moment ago.

And now, hearing him speak again in that hoarse murmur, she couldn't help thinking of the soft words he'd pressed against her ear the night before.

She had let him get to her, Lu Huaixi thought, resigned to herself.

"I wasn't afraid of him. Besides — if he'd actually done it, it would only have worked in our favor."

"I don't need that kind of advantage."

Xie Yuanjing said it quietly but firmly: "And neither do you. The only thing you need to remember is this — don't let anyone hurt you. Don't let anyone touch you."

Seeing her not respond immediately, Xie Yuanjing pressed his brow a little and asked again: "Did you hear me?"

He said: "Anyone. No one."

Lu Huaixi stilled, and looked up.

Xie Yuanjing was looking at her. His eyes were lowered, his dark lashes shading a portion of his pupils.

But the feeling roiling in those depths was still perfectly clear, entirely unguarded — his care, his possessiveness, and something bordering on the destructive, all of it displayed without a shred of concealment.

Lu Huaixi suddenly understood something of what he intended — and was somewhat startled to find that he had let obsession take root inside his loving.

She didn't know what feeling he would show if she said no. She had no intention of testing it.

She leaned toward him, and in the pause while he waited in silence for her answer, she wrapped her arms around him with care, gently, without force. Then she let out a somewhat helpless breath.

"Then you also — don't let anyone hurt you. Don't let anyone touch you. All right?"

It had all been too sudden. She hadn't been able to gather herself in time.

But thinking back on it now — wasn't every bit of it deliberate on his part?

Deliberately letting the Marquis of Chengen see the severity of his injuries. Deliberately advancing by retreating, using it to make the break.

And then deliberately throwing up his hands, stepping aside — letting the world see what the current Marquis's manor and that Hé Bìnxìn were actually made of.

Careful calculations, indeed.

Only, thinking about it this carefully, Xie Yuanjing seemed to have used similar methods with her.

Advancing by retreating — and in the process, steadily encircling her until there was no way out.

But she had decided not to concern herself with that.

She had fallen for Xie Yuanjing too. And if she was being honest — she had been the first one to be moved.

"You old fox."

Her voice was very small. She had been careful not to use any force.

At the moment Xie Yuanjing quietly agreed, she knew he was admitting it. She knew he had guessed what she meant to say.

She was still unsatisfied, and yet reluctant to do anything more about it.

She lowered her head, and bit down at the side of his neck.

Xie Yuanjing let out a muffled sound at the sudden movement, then raised his hand and curled it around her waist.

He didn't dare hold her too tightly. If the wound was made any worse, he thought he really would be lying in this bed for a month.

He didn't care for himself — but he couldn't make Lu Huaixi carry everything on her own for that long.

"If one bite isn't enough, let me offer you this side too."

Xie Yuanjing tilted his head slightly, his lips grazing her earlobe.

The warmth from the night before spread again from the point where they touched, winding downward, stoking something in him that was losing its leash.

His breathing was a little heavier than before.

He reached for the thin coverlet, the dark in his eyes deepening.

"Grow up quickly."

"What?"

Seeing Lu Huaixi look up, eyes wide with blankness, he felt a flicker of mischief. His fingertip found her ear and played with it.

"Do you know how to be a married couple?"

He smiled, watching the bewilderment on her face. Then he said, slowly: "Once I'm a little better — let's learn how to be a married couple together. All right?"

—

While Xie Yuanjing was inside coaxing her, outside, the Marquis of Chengen was being shown the door.

He could not believe the things his son had just said to him — or how calmly he had said them, as if stepping away meant nothing at all.

He stood there, stunned and furious. In the end, his anger surged and he shook his sleeve, walking away with a dark and heavy expression.

There were certain things he could choose not to give, or weigh giving to someone else — but they could not be declined. The other party was not permitted not to want them.

And yet there was also this unexplainable unease pressing at his chest, making it impossible for him to even ask in passing about the severity of the injuries.

He was the father, after all. This son — truly ungrateful!

His young manservant waited a moment before stepping forward, hesitant and quiet.

"My lord — the carriage is already prepared, and young master Bìnxìn's side is also waiting for you. Only — old physician Zēng — shall we still try to make the request?"

The Marquis of Chengen came back to himself. His gaze returned to the courtyard ahead.

The person would naturally need to be invited.

He had come today with the specific intention of bringing old physician Zēng to look at Bìnxìn's injuries.

And having already lost face once inside, now that he'd had a look at the man, there was no reason to leave without achieving at least this much.

He was just about to speak when a figure emerged from the courtyard ahead.

The old man came out carrying his things, his expression unchanged.

The two of them moved in almost the same moment.

The Marquis of Chengen stopped thinking about the people inside the room and stepped forward.

He was not worried about being refused.

In his estimation, now that the old divine physician had already come down the mountain, he couldn't possibly turn him — a Marquis — down on account of a girl.

Lù Huaixi had been posturing deliberately, trying to show off what she was capable of.

And between the two — a man who had spent years in the palace would have a clearer sense of what mattered than anyone.

chapters.title: She Has Every Right to Decide
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Cheng'en was full of assumptions.

He even imagined that if he brought the old physician to He Bingxin, the look of surprise and delight on that mother and son's faces would give him a kind of closeness and reliance that his cold-hearted son had never offered.

With that thought, he pressed down his earlier anger and stepped onto the corridor.

But he had barely called out "Elder Zeng" before the old man turned ahead and looked back at him with undisguised impatience.

Without even waiting for him to speak, the refusal came without ceremony.

"My lord, please stop there. This old man has come down the mountain solely for that young girl. I will not attend to anyone else."

The Marquis was momentarily surprised, but quickly composed himself and manufactured a smile.

"Elder Zeng, there is no need to refuse so swiftly. Lu Huaixi is but a young woman — what she can offer a divine physician is only so much. But this Marquis has spent many years in officialdom. I may not be able to help with every matter, but I can promise rather more than most."

There was something almost predatory in the Marquis's certainty.

When he chose to be, he truly did carry the weight of a Marquis's authority about him — imposing and difficult to resist.

But Elder Zeng had spent years in the palace attending to the secrets of the royal court and standing before the Son of Heaven himself. Faced with the Marquis of Cheng'en, he had not a trace of intention to yield.

"This old man knows full well that a man of your lordship's standing can accomplish things with ease. But I came down the mountain because I owe that young girl a favour — she did not come seeking me. And I long since stopped taking patients. I would ask your lordship to seek a more suitable physician elsewhere."

"Since the Elder was willing to attend to Yuanjing, what difference does one more person make?"

Having been refused, the Marquis still could not bring himself to accept it.

He forced his displeasure down and continued.

"A physician's heart is one of benevolence. I have gone to such lengths to bring you here, Elder Zeng — can you truly bring yourself to watch someone perish without raising a hand?"

Then, after a moment's thought, he added:

"If the Elder is concerned about others finding out, I give my word that I will keep this matter secret. I will ensure it brings no trouble to you."

"The capital is full of capable physicians. There is no need for your lordship to lay the charge of callous indifference at this old man's feet."

The old man was entirely unhurried. If anything, those words made him laugh.

"And speaking of benevolence — although I no longer take patients, I still have rather more of it than your lordship does."

This was plainly a remark about Xie Yuanjing, who lay gravely injured inside and had never received his father's concern.

At this moment, the old man was nothing like the ornery old trickster he became in Lu Huaixi's presence.

Having spoken, he remained unmoved. Facing the Marquis, he carried the settled, unshakeable composure of someone who had weathered much.

"Your lordship, please return. I have long since retired from court — the Emperor himself gave his blessing. I am a plain-clothed man now and am not fit to carry out a Marquis's instructions."

"Elder Zeng, are you truly this unyielding? Will you not give this Marquis even a small measure of face?"

At that, the old man stroked his beard and laughed again.

He glanced toward the distance, and after a long pause, spoke through his laughter.

"I had not intended to come this time. But aside from having a favour to ask of that young girl, I also came to mind an old debt of gratitude I owe to the former Empress. Since your lordship speaks of face — I would like to ask: the person you wish me to attend to, of which family is he? Can he be compared to the First Young Master of your household?"

The Marquis understood his meaning.

Attending to Xie Yuanjing was a courtesy extended on account of the former Empress and Lu Huaixi. The one outside had no such claim on his consideration.

Because that person was nothing.

The Marquis did not speak.

Perhaps unable to believe Lu Huaixi held such sway, and vexed that he had not managed to secure He Bingxin a more distinguished standing, he stood there in a rigid silence.

The old man made no move to hurry him.

He had been listening the whole way down the mountain, and could naturally guess who the Marquis was referring to.

But that was, after all, the Marquis's private affair, and he had no intention of prying.

"I still have medicines to prepare. The First Young Master's injuries are severe — severe enough to kill. Since the person your lordship speaks of is also gravely injured, it would be best to summon one of the better physicians in the city quickly. After all, not everyone is like the First Young Master — able to endure, and survive the two most dangerous nights through sheer will."

Having said that, the old man turned and walked away.

Without any regard for whose residence this was, or whose domain he was standing in.

The medicine boy fell into step behind him.

Not until they had moved entirely out of the Marquis's sight did the boy let out a quiet laugh at the old man's back.

"Master, you are so protective of this First Young Master Xie. If Huaixi finds out, she will be absolutely delighted."

"I am not doing this to please that troublesome girl."

The old man gave a cold huff, chin raised, beard tilting upward.

"Every time I see those two being all affectionate it irritates me. The sooner I cure that boy, the sooner I can drag the little brat back up the mountain."

He got halfway through that sentence, and the person beside him did not call him out on it — just went along and laughed twice.

Not wanting to lose face, the old man kept his expression stern as he walked ahead.

But as he went, he forgot to keep up the act.

When that girl had seen the blood at the corner of Xie Yuanjing's mouth, she had looked absolutely terrified. He wondered if she had calmed down by now.

The old man sighed, and could not help a slow shake of his head.

To speak of it plainly — the former Empress had indeed done him a kindness once. And when she spoke of her family, the person she mentioned most was this First Young Master of the Xie household.

Now the young girl had gone and married into that very household, quite by chance. Even though he had said he would no longer treat patients on a whim, he could not help feeling anxious.

Besides, setting aside all matters of human sentiment, the medicinal herbs genuinely needed to be planted at this time.

If the weather grew any colder, they would grow more slowly and the potency would suffer.

"Go ahead and deliver the powdered medicine I prepared. Keep a close eye on him before I get there — and do not let him move around."

"Yes, I'll go right away!"

—

When one is recovering from an injury, the days pass quickly.

After the incident, the Marquis of Cheng'en did not appear again.

Lu Huaixi kept Xie Yuanjing company through his recovery, and now that he had finally taken a turn for the better, she let out a breath of relief and prepared to make a trip back to the Lu residence.

"Don't stay too late. Come back for dinner."

"I know."

"If you run into anyone fishing for information about the Marquis's household, handle it however you see fit. You don't need to put yourself out."

"Yes, I will."

"About my break with the household — if your mother asks, there is no need to conceal it. I have already sent word to your father, and I have promised it will not implicate you. Also—"

"Why are you being so long-winded?"

Lu Huaixi rose from the bronze mirror, muttering with mild exasperation, and dutifully walked toward the inner room.

The two maidservants exchanged a glance, smiled, and slipped out.

"If you don't go, I won't be long-winded."

"I've been keeping you company for so many days."

Lu Huaixi looked over at him sitting propped up against the headboard, some of his usual vigour returning to his face. The hazy morning light fell across his features, tracing the clean lines of his profile.

She looked for a moment, then — unable to help herself in the face of someone this good-looking — gave up and flopped over to him.

"Don't think I don't know — you're the one waiting for me to leave."

Last night, half-asleep, she had vaguely heard Xie Yuanjing asking after the Xie patriarch and issuing a stream of instructions.

She had pretended not to hear. And he had deliberately acted gentle and cooperative, which was absolutely insufferable.

Xie Yuanjing reached out and caught her, smiled without saying a word, then lowered his head and kissed her.

What did he have going on? Only wanting to make things clear with his grandfather — that he and Lu Huaixi were going to be a real husband and wife from here on.

His affairs were matters that Lu Huaixi had every right to decide.

chapters.title: Envying Xie Yuanjing
chapters.content:
After the news spread that Xie Yuanjing had been gravely injured by a punishment, the Marquis's household received many visiting cards — and those who went to call on He Bingxin also began to multiply.

Some wanted a look at this young man of rising promise, newly favoured by Senior Official Xun.

Others wanted to take his measure — to understand how a person like him could result in a Xie family First Young Master being punished by the Emperor, and a Marquis of Cheng'en so far gone as to disregard his own son and step in to shield him.

The Marquis of Cheng'en continued to visit He Bingxin from time to time as well.

But after running into one or two recognisable faces there, and seeing the rumours outside growing more and more exaggerated, he had not shown his face for quite a long while.

He Bingxin also understood that he and his mother needed to appear magnanimous and sensible at this moment — to consider the Marquis's position.

But with no word from the Emperor's court, and no progress in Xie Yuanjing's situation, he found himself privately growing more and more anxious.

The physician had also said that his injuries were considerably better. Lying in bed day after day was becoming increasingly difficult to justify.

When another colleague came to call, he simply got up and went out to receive the visitor.

"You seem well enough now, and that's what matters. All sorts of speculation is going around outside — including one that sounds rather convincing, about the Marquis of Cheng'en breaking with you over a father-and-son dispute."

"You must think me quite ridiculous, Brother Zhou."

He Bingxin produced a smile, giving a seemingly helpless shake of his head.

The visitor, seeing this, could not help asking.

"Why are you still frowning? You have the Marquis of Cheng'en's favour, and such an excellent teacher as Senior Official Xun — there are countless people in the capital who envy you right now."

"It is all just rumour."

He Bingxin waved it off. "One hears such things and lets them pass. What I am actually concerned about is that Xie the First Young Master might take it to heart and feel displeased."

"And you're still worrying about him? He put you through all of this — if he's displeased, it's entirely his own doing."

The visitor frowned in disapproval.

"You are too good-hearted. You treat everyone so well — you'll come to grief for it eventually."

"Let's not speak of scheming or being set up. Nothing has been determined yet. There's been no word from the palace — it may well have been a coincidence."

"No determination yet? The Emperor would have ordered someone of the Xie household to be punished that severely just on coincidence? Just wait. And even if it wasn't him directly, the bandits who were caught in the western district that time are definitely connected to him."

The visitor spoke with great conviction.

"He was probably colluding with those criminals all along — using the small fry to injure you and let off some steam, then leading them straight into an arrest. And this may not even be the first time he's done it. He just happened to stumble this time because you were involved."

He Bingxin did not respond to that.

He genuinely hoped the investigation would confirm something like that. But he knew it would not.

He also was not foolish enough to believe, at this point, that a Xie Yuanjing who had been silent this whole time had no means of fighting back and had simply been at his disposal.

He thought: if the time came, he might need to go to the Marquis's household to offer an apology in person.

But fortunately, from start to finish in this affair, he had been the victim.

Whatever he had murmured during his unconscious state — even he himself did not know. And the things that had happened to conveniently align were not of his arranging.

He had only let the matter leak out, using the flow of events to his advantage.

"Speaking of which — the only difference between you and him is a matter of birth. And now he's gone and married a noblewoman from the Lu family on top of everything. He's practically untouchable. He was just born lucky."

He Bingxin heard the sourness in those words, and the corners of his mouth moved slightly.

But in the end he only lowered his head, gave a helpless laugh, and said nothing more.

"That is perhaps not the right way to put it."

He Bingxin said softly.

He appeared entirely unbothered, his expression remaining composed and mild.

But beneath his sleeve, his hand closed into a fist — and the small, involuntary gesture betrayed the resentment buried underneath.

"I hear that the second daughter of the Lu family has a lively temperament and a pleasant nature. I imagine she and Xie the First Young Master are quite well suited. Perhaps with such a fine companion at his side, he will be more willing to restrain himself at times."

"Lively and pleasant — more like spoiled and undisciplined, running around causing scenes and not knowing her place."

The visitor was dismissive, and beneath the dismissal was a hint of something that could only be called envy.

"I heard that the Lu second daughter was never fond of studying. Someone with so little substance going into his inner household — what kind of counsel could she possibly offer? If anything she sounds like a bewitching troublemaker who'll encourage him to be even more irresponsible."

"Surely not?"

"Why surely not? Do you know she went and opened a music house? Has people go in to listen to music and watch dancers — with not a scrap of decorum. If I had married a wife like that, I'd be having headaches every day, and scolding her constantly."

At this, He Bingxin let slip a thin, genuine note of contempt — though it was directed at the man speaking, not at the subject of his words.

He had actually seen the Lu family's second daughter before.

His only impression at the time had been one of dazzling brightness — extraordinarily beautiful.

And that was before considering the prestige of her family name.

A noblewoman like that — if this man were actually to marry her, He Bingxin suspected he would be on his knees, kowtowing endlessly, begging in the most abject tones imaginable for her to enter his household.

All of it was nothing but sour grapes.

Yet for all his contempt, He Bingxin's expression remained one of polite understanding.

He too was envious. He despised Xie Yuanjing. He resented Xie Yuanjing.

He wanted to take everything that man had and claim it for himself — including that unforgettable second daughter of the Lu family.

"Brother Zhou, it would be best not to say such things outside. She is, after all, a Lu family noblewoman, and the First Young Mistress of the Xie household. Whatever one may think, it is not fitting to speak carelessly of her."

"I know you can't stand loose talk. I'm only saying this to you."

The visitor sat in the courtyard a while longer, took some air, and then bid He Bingxin farewell, walking slowly out of the alley.

He was about to return to his carriage when something was thrown over his head, and he found himself unable to move.

Before he could cry out, a flurry of blows came down on him.

Each one precise, each one landing with full force. The pain blurred his vision. He did not last long before he lost consciousness.

The men beating him saw that he had gone down, and gave him a few more kicks.

Then one of them spat on the ground beside him, shook out the hand he had used with an air of distaste, and left from the side.

The group quickly resumed the appearance of ordinary city dwellers and dispersed in different directions.

The one at the front gave a small nod back toward the alley before turning away.

The figure waiting in the shadows saw it, and slipped back into the darkness.

—

Lu Huaixi had no idea that during the days she was caring for Xie Yuanjing, she had quietly come to be regarded by certain people as a mistress who could not be allowed to suffer even the slightest slight.

Nor did she know that Xie Yuanjing's people had, without a word, gone and settled a score on her behalf.

At this moment she had just stepped into the Lu residence, and the first thing she saw was her mother coming in person to receive her.

"What took you so long on the road?"

Lady Liu took hold of her and would not let go, looking her over from all angles. Only once she had confirmed her daughter had not grown thin did she release her and take her hand, leading her inside.

"I have been wanting to go to the Marquis's household to visit all this time, but your father kept stopping me. He said you would be too occupied to entertain me, and that Xie Yuanjing would be fine."

Lady Liu spoke with a trace of dissatisfaction.

"Fortunately, looking at you now, your colour is good and you don't seem to have worn yourself out. Otherwise I would have had a great deal to say to your father."

Lu Huaixi could not help but laugh, leaning over and linking her arm through her mother's.

"Please don't be hard on Father. I am not someone who suffers easily — would I really let myself be miserable?"

Lady Liu walked with her toward the courtyard.

Seeing those eyes curved with a smile, and that familiar soft-hearted tactic being deployed again, she forgot entirely to scold her for being too cavalier.

"Stay for dinner before you go. I'll have someone take you back. Since you've been away, the kitchen staff have been complaining about you every single day."

"Dinner though..."

Lu Huaixi thought of Xie Yuanjing saying to come back for the evening meal, and rubbed her nose.

"Is something happening at the Marquis's household?"

"Not exactly."

Lu Huaixi blinked, then smiled, letting her voice go a little softer.

"Xie Yuanjing is waiting for me to come back. And Elder Zeng is there too. I'm afraid if I stay too long, Xie Yuanjing will manage to irritate him."

Lady Liu felt mildly speechless, but she also knew things were complicated at the Marquis's household right now, and that it was indeed not wise to be away too long.

"Fine, then. Another time."

"You're the best, Mother."

Lu Huaixi leaned over again, taking hold of Lady Liu's arm and giving it a gentle swing.

chapters.title: Who Has the Bigger Temper
chapters.content:
This visit home had two purposes for Lu Huaixi: putting her mother at ease — and dealing with the second branch.

Since Lu Tangshu's marriage had been settled, the second branch had been growing quieter by the day.

But she did not believe for a moment that they had genuinely repented.

This quiet was nothing more than waiting for the talk outside to die down.

She arrived at Lu Tangshu's room shortly.

The maidservant at the door startled when she saw her, then immediately went in to announce her.

Lu Huaixi did not wait. She pushed the door open and walked straight in.

"Who gave you permission to come in?"

Lu Tangshu was sitting inside. When she saw her, she shot to her feet in fury.

But the ordeal of her marriage had worn some of the edge off her. Faced with Lu Huaixi's cool composure, she could no longer muster the arrogance she had once shown.

"I have no intention of arguing with you. A few words, and then I'll leave."

Lu Huaixi found herself a seat without ceremony and met Lu Tangshu's furious, resentful glare.

Lu Tangshu opened her mouth several times to snap at her, and each time swallowed it back.

She was well aware of her own situation, and had to admit — this marriage could not be undone. Once she went over there, she might yet need Lu Huaixi's help.

"What did you come for?"

Lu Tangshu gripped her handkerchief, forcing down the humiliation.

She had lost. She had not managed to outmanoeuvre Lu Huaixi, and could only watch herself be pressed down beneath her.

"If you've come to see me make a fool of myself, you've seen it. You can leave now. Right now I—"

"Your making a fool of yourself isn't worth a special trip."

Lu Huaixi cut her off. Her eyes, though lacking warmth, were still clear — but there was a layer of cold distance in them now, as though she were keeping the world at arm's length.

Lu Tangshu looked at her for an involuntary moment longer.

Seeing that she had become even more beautiful than before, Lu Tangshu felt a jealousy so acute it almost made her ill.

"Just say what you came to say. I hear things are not quiet at the Marquis's household either. You'd do better to worry about yourself, in case you end up with nothing to show for it and can't even hold on to your position as the Xie family's First Young Mistress."

Lu Huaixi heard this and showed very little reaction, as though she had truly only come to sit for a while.

Then Luo Yuehui's voice came from outside.

Lu Tangshu paused mid-sentence and frowned toward the door.

"Mother—"

"Lu Huaixi — you have brought ruin on our Tangshu and then you dare come to our branch of the family? Do you really think I won't teach you a lesson?"

"Second Aunt's words are a little off. Third Sister is not suffering a hard fate — she brought it on herself."

Lu Huaixi did not move. She sat right where she was, eyes curved pleasantly as she spoke.

Luo Yuehui flared with rage and raised her hand, but before she could act, the maidservant in front of Lu Huaixi seized her arm, locking it in place and causing enough pain that she could barely move.

"I did not come today to exchange pleasantries with Second Aunt. If Second Aunt insists on making an enemy of me, then let us lay everything out — every single matter — and let everyone see who is the truly cruel one, and who is the truly vicious one."

Luo Yuehui was somewhat unnerved by the cold edge that came through those words.
