She looked at the person before her. She was still the same young girl — still smiling — and yet there was a quality about her now that had not been there before. A sharpness, one that only showed itself toward those outside her circle.

A maidservant stepped forward to support Luo Yuehui and murmured a few words of counsel in her ear.

She seemed to come back to herself. She reined herself in again and again, and did not dare continue as she had been.

"What on earth have you come to our branch for? Tangshu's reputation has already been ruined, and she is being forced into marrying that He Jianhang. Are you still not satisfied?"

"There is no question of satisfaction. I have come for one thing."

Lu Huaixi looked up, turning her gaze to the person beside Luo Yuehui.

"If you, Lu Tangshu, want to live in peace before you are married, have Second Uncle find a way to properly clean up the matter of the bandits who were arrested in the western district."

"What are you talking about? Bandits arrested in the western district — what does that have to do with us—"

"We all know the full story. There is no need to keep pretending to be uninvolved."

Lu Huaixi cut Luo Yuehui off, her gaze unmoved, still resting on Lu Tangshu.

When officials had gone to the western district that day to make arrests, word had spread that the one who reported it had been a person of Xie Yuanjing's — which put him in a difficult position.

To explain the full circumstances would expose the entire Lu family's scandal, and implicate He Jianhang in the charge of colluding with criminals.

But to say nothing left Xie Yuanjing open to speculation of official-criminal collusion — of using the bandits and then turning them in — and so he had kept a low profile and stayed out of the public eye.

It was not a large matter, in itself. But when every smaller thing was piled on top of another, the smallest detail required the most careful handling.

And whatever mess the second branch had made — there was no reason for anyone else to bear the consequences.

"This cannot be pinned on Xie Yuanjing. No matter how much it is fanned, it will not stick to him. But you — your branch has done quite enough harm. If you truly cannot be decent people, then don't bother with pretences."

"What do you mean by that?"

"I am giving you a choice. I know exactly how He Jianhang came to bring those bandits in. You can either have Second Uncle and the He family clean this up cleanly and have her married off quietly — or I hand He Jianhang over to face justice, and she becomes a criminal's wife the moment she crosses the threshold. Your choice."

The colour drained from Lu Tangshu's face. She had taken the words in.

She no longer believed for a single moment that Lu Huaixi was naive or easily deceived.

She only felt that, when this person chose to be ruthless, she was utterly without sentiment — even worse than herself.

"But this matter — this matter, my mother and I — how do we have any say in it?"

After a long pause, Lu Tangshu finally spoke, her voice slightly unsteady.

Luo Yuehui had also lost her righteous fervour from earlier, mouth closed, no longer calling out.

"And I don't understand those things — it was all He Jianhang who arranged the people—"

"That is your affair."

Lu Huaixi finished speaking and rose.

"I have already extended you one reprieve. If not for that, colluding with criminals would leave He Jianhang with no way out — and the same would apply to you. Though of course—" She looked straight through Lu Tangshu's sudden calculating expression. "— don't think that using this to send him away means you get out of the marriage."

Lu Huaixi smiled.

"Given Third Sister's current circumstances, marrying into the He family is your only way out. Keep a close eye on things and perhaps that He Jianhang will manage to make something of himself — and you can still fight for a better standing."

Without waiting for the mother and daughter of the second branch to say another word, Lu Huaixi turned and walked out.

"Second Uncle has been in officialdom for years. Handling something of this scale will not be too difficult. I don't care what method he uses — only that Xie Yuanjing is kept clear of it.

"I am not a patient person, and I cannot wait too long. Second Aunt and Third Sister had best speak to Second Uncle soon."

The silence behind her said everything. Lu Huaixi knew — this pair of mother and daughter were genuinely afraid.

She walked out of the second branch's quarters without haste.

She had been about to go and say a word to her mother as well, when she noticed someone waiting ahead.

The figure looked rather slight, but was not unfamiliar.

It was Lu Suidong — the one who had aspirations of entering the palace.

Lu Suidong looked over very soon.

"Second Sister."

"Were you waiting for me?"

Lu Suidong nodded and smiled openly at Lu Huaixi.

—

At the Marquis's household, the Xie patriarch made his way to Xie Yuanjing's room.

Seeing that his complexion looked better than it had before, he finally felt some of his worry ease.

"Where is that girl?"

The old man looked around, saw no one, and asked with a straight face.

"Grandfather, she has her own matters."

Xie Yuanjing did not like his tone. He furrowed his brow and let some coldness into his voice.

"She has been taking care of things this whole time without leaving the courtyard more than a handful of times. If Grandfather is going to continue with that sort of temper toward her—"

"Who has the bigger temper here? I only said a few things that day, and she would not even call me Grandfather. She calls everyone else in this whole household by whatever you call them — but for me, she has a formal 'Patriarch Xie'!"

Xie Yuanjing heard this, and the corner of his brow lifted slightly.

"That is not quite true."

He paused, then added: "She only calls the Marquis of Cheng'en 'My Lord' as well."

chapters.title: No Plans for Divorce
chapters.content:
That response from Xie Yuanjing — with its hint of teasing — left the Xie patriarch momentarily at a loss.

He suddenly realised that what he had spoken to this grandson about most was the future of the Xie household, its foundations — and then Xie Yuanjing's own future.

He could not pinpoint exactly when it had begun, but at some point, this grandson had stopped showing genuine emotion.

No matter what happened within the household, no matter whether his father treated him well or poorly, he remained unmoved — accepting it or ignoring it and simply continuing with whatever he needed to do.

At first, the patriarch had not thought this was a problem.

As the First Young Master of the Xie family, it was only right that nothing should distract him.

But now, catching a sudden glimpse of something different, the problem made itself known, piece by piece.

"You certainly protect her."

The patriarch looked at him, his tone unreadable. "If you hadn't been indulging her, would she have developed such a temper?"

"There is nothing wrong with her temper. She does not call him Father because of me. She does not call you Grandfather because you have not been willing to acknowledge her as such."

Xie Yuanjing's voice dropped slightly, his eyes moving to the teacup on the table.

"I was not present to hear what you said to her that day. Since I regained consciousness, she has not mentioned it once. You say I have been indulging her, but before she was married she was the most cherished daughter in the Lu family's main branch. What is there to indulge?"

"When did I ever refuse to acknowledge her? And when did I truly scold her?"

The patriarch was somewhat displeased, but he also knew that what his grandson was saying was true.

The prized daughter of the Lu family's main branch — whatever the household's internal workings — would certainly have been raised with every care and tenderness. That Lu Huaixi was neither haughty nor restless, and had a nature this gentle and obliging, was already rare among noblewomen.

"If it were not for the matter between you and your father — if it were not for the Xie family's reputation — why would I have said those things to her? And I was not blaming her. I was only laying out what was at stake."

The patriarch's manner was no longer what it had been that day.

But his brow was still furrowed — the stubbornness of age, and the pride that refused to bend.

"The two of you are not a true husband and wife as things stand. She has been managing things on your behalf, helping you let off some of that tension, and after that you will dissolve the marriage and she will leave. Is there anyone else who could handle the household with her patience and manner?

"She had the confidence to stand up to your father, yes. But in doing so, she has spread the news of your estrangement from him across the whole capital. When the dust settles, how will you manage the aftermath? Are you planning to give up this Marquis's household?"

Xie Yuanjing waited quietly until the man finished. His expression held very little.

Only after the room had fallen quiet again did he rise.

"Her instructions carried my intention behind them. You must have known that, Grandfather. Your reprimand of her was not really about her actions — it was because you disagreed with my plans, and you wanted to test her."

He paused, as though something had just occurred to him, and gave a sudden quiet laugh.

"You also knew that she wanted to vent anger on my behalf — which means you understood, in your own heart, who was responsible for my injuries. And yet you never once considered standing up for me. You barely offered more than a few words of reproach to that person."

"Are you saying I don't value you?"

"No. On the contrary — it is precisely because you value me so much that even being injured is my fault."

The patriarch seemed stopped by that.

His lips moved, but for a long moment, no sound came out.

Xie Yuanjing was not troubled by it.

He said these things only because he had been thinking of Lu Huaixi — of the emotions she carried because of him, even her displeasure so vivid and alive.

More vivid than anything he had seen before.

Or — perhaps he had seen it. When his younger brother was still alive, his mother had been that way with his brother.

With him, it had been mostly the same strictness as his grandfather's.

Until his brother was gone.

"I bear no resentment toward anyone right now. I am telling you all of this today only because I feel you were unfair to Lu Huaixi — your anger toward her was entirely misdirected. If you are willing to set aside your pride this once, go and speak to her properly. If you are not willing, that is also fine. I will handle the coaxing myself."

"You want me to go and apologise to that girl?"

The patriarch stood in some shock, staring wide-eyed at his eldest grandson.

"Apologise would be too strong a word. But Grandfather, since you yourself said we are not truly husband and wife — then she is not your granddaughter-in-law, and you are not her grandfather. On what grounds did you scold her, and by what right did you tell her she had done wrong?"

"You — the way she acts, so impulsive! The court is a web of competing interests. Even if she were not your wife, a person who acts purely on instinct like this will have no end of hardship ahead. As her elder, what is wrong with me offering her a word or two of caution?"

"There is no need for you to caution her. I will look after her."

"You think you can protect her for the rest of her life?"

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing paid no attention to whether the person before him was flushing with anger. He said it calmly, without hurry.

"I have no plans for divorce. So from now on, she and I are a true husband and wife. My affairs are hers to decide, and she does not need to wonder whether what she does is permissible. If you cannot bring yourself to speak to her with respect, then come and see her less. I made a promise, and I can certainly keep it for a lifetime."

"Are you saying that if I cannot bring myself to speak properly to her, not only have you blocked your father from entering your courtyard — next it will be me you block?"

"That is the second thing I wished to tell you. I am planning to take her and move out of the Marquis's household."

The patriarch's brow gave a single sharp jump, and a bad feeling settled over him.

"Where? To one of the country estates to recover?"

"No. Out of the Marquis's household. To live on our own."

Xie Yuanjing might have been talking about the weather. He even added a line, perhaps worried the man had not quite followed.

"You are no doubt already aware of what happened when he came to my courtyard. I have never been one to say things I do not mean. When I said I would stop managing the Xie household's affairs — I meant it."

"Do you know what you are saying?"

The patriarch's raised hand trembled slightly, his eyes filled with disbelief.

"You have fought every step of the way to get where you are today. You took over the Xie household at great cost, and finally established yourself in the Emperor's trust. And now, after one grievance, you are going to throw all of it away?"

"It is not quite as impulsive as you make it sound. It is simply returning the Marquis's household to him."

Xie Yuanjing was entirely indifferent. "Without the Marquis's title, I am still Xie Yuanjing in the Emperor's eyes. Nothing will be different."

The patriarch was again silent for a long while.

But compared to a moment ago, his complexion had settled slightly — he no longer looked as though he might collapse at any moment.

After some time, he spoke with considerable difficulty.

"If you truly wish to be with that girl, I will not object. A Lu family daughter is a fine match. She may have a spirited temper, but she is more than a match for you. What I said that day — I was impatient. I am used to speaking in that manner. If you want me to speak to her properly, that is not beyond me."

"She does not have a spirited temper. And please do not connect the two matters. It is not because you refuse to speak kindly to her that I am moving out."

"Then why?!"

The patriarch struck the table in frustration. The sound rang out so clearly that those outside could hear it.

Xie Yuanjing barely reacted. He simply poured a cup of tea for the man before him and placed it in his hands.

"Grandfather, mind your health." He said evenly.

"The Marquis believes this identity as the Xie family's First Young Master has brought me every advantage in the world. He also believes He Bingxin lacks nothing but that same identity. Now I have been gravely injured and need time to recover, and I have been punished by the Emperor. Frankly, I am rather weary of it. So I will simply return the Xie family to him."

He did not deny that he had been born to good standing.

He also had never forgotten that he was meant to take over the Xie household and hold it together.

But he had come this far, and the father who was the Marquis of Cheng'en had already faded from the picture, piece by piece.

Wanting the Xie household to be stable was not enough.

As long as his father wanted the person outside to rise to power — to have the influence to stand against him — the Xie household could never truly be stable.

Given that, he might as well let his father try.

"Grandfather knows whose wellbeing he is concerned with right now. And it is certainly not mine."

The patriarch's complexion was, at this moment, genuinely unpleasant.

Restrained — and yet looking as though he might hurl the teacup to the floor at any second.

But he did not move. Only after a long silence did he look once more at the grandson standing before him — visibly tired now, for the first time.

"You don't want the divorce — is it because of the Lu family?"

"No."

At this, Xie Yuanjing's expression finally showed something more.

He lowered his eyes and gave a quiet laugh, his voice unmistakably softer.

"Not the Lu family. I simply want to marry her."

chapters.title: An Exchange of Hearts
chapters.content:
The day passed quickly.

As evening drew near, the wind outside grew pleasantly cool as the sun went down.

Lu Huaixi stood beneath the corridor, looking across at Lu Suidong, while her thoughts quietly calculated whether the worst of the summer heat had finally passed.

By rights, even after the turn into autumn, there were usually still a few hot days to come.

But once those were over, the weather would cool quickly — and she would no longer need to worry about Xie Yuanjing's injuries being aggravated by the heat.

Her thoughts had drifted some distance, but were soon drawn back.

"Second Sister, may I talk with you for a while?"

Lu Huaixi came back to herself. She said neither yes nor no, and simply walked alongside her.

"If you're seen talking with me, what will happen?"

The rift between the two branches had long since gone beyond any possibility of return.

Lu Huaixi herself did not particularly mind.

She understood well that once Lu Tangshu married over, she would still have to rely on the Lu family's name and on the main branch's standing in the outside world. She would not dare do anything against Lu Huaixi — only grovel and yield.

But Lu Suidong was a different matter.

Behind closed doors in the second branch, Luo-shi and Lu Tangshu could vent their rage on whoever they liked, and no one could stop them.

"I am not afraid. After the trouble Third Sister caused, there is no one left to send into the palace in her place."

Lu Suidong said plainly, "My stepmother will not move against me at this time. She will come to me of her own accord."

Lu Huaixi paused, and after a moment, asked a single question.

"Have you truly made up your mind?"

She had not originally intended to say this. She had thought: after today, whatever happened in the second branch, she would not touch any part of it.

But Lu Suidong was standing in front of her, speaking to her as she always had, with that familiar smile at the corners of her mouth. And Lu Huaixi felt it would be wrong to let one Lu Tangshu poison everything.

"Wait a little longer. After a while, no one will be able to use you to let off their frustrations anymore. You don't have to take that path."

Lu Suidong smiled slightly.

She was no longer the timid, fearful girl she had once been. She seemed to have worked something out — or made peace with something. There was a composure about her that surprised even Lu Huaixi.

"No, Second Sister. That is not enough."

She looked steadily at the person before her, and spoke quietly.

"When I was younger and still did not understand things, I sometimes wondered why I was born a concubine's daughter — why my mother was so thoroughly disliked by my stepmother. But then I stopped wondering about that.

"After that, all I thought was: why was I not a daughter of the main branch? Why could my elder sisters not have been First Sister and Second Sister?"

Something pressed in on Lu Huaixi's chest.

But she said nothing, only listened as Lu Suidong continued.

"Then I stopped thinking about those things too. I started thinking instead about how to seem harmless and well-behaved — how to be scolded and punished a little less.

"In those years of keeping my head down, I did actually live a bit better than before. And when I went outside the Lu residence, there were people who wanted to come and talk with me."

Lu Suidong's voice was still quiet, but the tone carried a soft heaviness.

Lu Huaixi looked at her, and suddenly spoke.

"Yes. Whether you are born to a concubine or not, you are a daughter of the Lu family."

Her voice was a little slow — with the usual warmth she carried, but also, somehow, a force behind it.

"The world naturally has people of higher standing than ours. There are noblewomen, county mistresses, princesses — all very fine. But that does not mean we need to feel we are a step below anyone. That includes you."

"Thank you, Second Sister."

Lu Suidong's eyes reddened slightly. She looked as though she wanted to cry, but held it back.

"I know that even as a concubine's daughter, the Lu family has given me more standing than many people will ever have. So I cannot wallow in self-pity. But I am still just a little short on luck — and so I know that what I want, I can only fight for myself."

The wind on the narrow path was stronger than elsewhere.

It rustled through the branches on both sides, and lifted the hems of both their skirts with a soft, swaying motion.

Lu Huaixi stood in the shade of a tree, listening carefully as Lu Suidong laid out what she had thought through: she wanted to enter the palace.

The young girl who had once still carried a childlike quality had grown, without notice, into someone more settled. When she paused in thought, her delicate brows drew slightly together — hesitant and deliberate.

Lu Huaixi simply watched her.

And at last, when Lu Suidong spoke of Luo-shi and her daughter, and the hand at her side clenched involuntarily into a fist, Lu Huaixi reached out and covered it.

"Don't be in a hurry to agree."

She thought for a moment, then said: "Wait for your stepmother to come to you. Let her offer to enter your name under hers. Then say you will consider it."

Lu Suidong blinked, her hand opening as her eyes widened slightly.

"That way, even if you later change your mind about the palace, you will at least have secured another path for yourself."

Lu Huaixi's words still offered her the option of retreating. Lu Suidong understood this.

She was grateful for the kindness — but had no intention of changing her course.

The palace was dangerous. There was no going back. But danger and fortune were two sides of the same coin, and it was the only path she could see that might allow her to gain the upper hand over that mother and daughter.

As for matters like a harmonious marriage — she had never entertained them.

Her stepmother would never allow her to marry someone of her own choosing. She would even use her marriage as a tool to pave the second branch's way.

Given that was the certainty regardless, she would naturally choose the path that offered more.

And besides, she had the Lu family behind her. Even as a concubine's daughter, the Lu family would find ways to protect her.

That was why Lu Tangshu had refused to go — and why she was willing.

Lu Huaixi knew her thinking clearly. But these were not decisions others could make — only the person herself.

She smiled, and did not let what she said carry too much weight.

"I had some watermelon put on ice. Would you like to come and try some?"

Lu Suidong looked as though she genuinely deliberated for a moment, then shook her head.

"Second Sister has come back so rarely. First Aunt must have a great deal she wants to say to you. I won't come along — I'll visit you another time."

Lu Huaixi did not press her, and walked with her a little further.

"Second Sister, if I want to see you in the future — if I enter the palace — would you be willing to come?"

Lu Suidong spoke, then quickly added, "I will make sure it is at a time when I can meet you with dignity. If I have made nothing of myself, I would never put Second Sister in a difficult position."

"I won't be in a difficult position."

Lu Huaixi replied, "If it is not convenient for me to come, I will write back and tell you directly."

Lu Suidong knew that if Second Sister said it that way, she had truly taken the words to heart.

The heaviness from a moment ago lifted, and she pressed her lips together in a small smile.

They walked as far as the fork in the road where their paths diverged. There, Lu Suidong stopped.

She looked at the person before her, thought for a moment, then said with sincerity:

"Suidong wishes Second Sister and Second Brother-in-law continued happiness. If fortune should find me in the future — no matter how things stand with those two — I will look after the Lu family without fail. I will treat Second Sister as my own elder sister, and I will always remember First Aunt's care."

This was an exchange of hearts. It was also a promise. And a reminder.

Along with it came an implicit acknowledgment of her indissoluble bond with the Lu family — that its rises and falls would be hers as well.

Lu Huaixi glanced at her, somewhat surprised by the change in her, yet also feeling it was exactly as it should be.

Wanting a good life for oneself was instinct. So it was for her. It had even been so for Lu Tangshu, once.

But there was a difference between them.

The greatest difference: whether the path toward that better life had been built by stepping on others.

The thought turned briefly in Lu Huaixi's mind, but she did not let it show.

She only smiled and accepted what had been said — and took hold of the branch that had been extended to her.

chapters.title: You've Been Gone from the Residence Too Long
chapters.content:
By the time Lu Huaixi returned to the Marquis's household, even the red clouds on the horizon had faded.

The evening meal had been prepared simply and lightly, but it was mostly the dishes she liked.

She glanced at it briefly, then went into the room first.

But when she drew close to the bed, she found it empty. The covers were laid out neatly, as though someone had risen long ago.

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed. She was about to call someone and ask.

But just as she parted her lips, a warm weight settled against her back.

The movement was familiar, as though it had been done countless times.

Arms wrapped around her waist, a chest pressing snugly against her back, folding her in.

After a moment, the person lowered his head. His chin rested against her shoulder, and he tilted his head to bite lightly at her earlobe.

She felt the place he had breathed over go warm, and Xie Yuanjing felt a ripple of something through him. He let the tip of his teeth trace that soft skin lightly — leaving a sensation that was tingling and faintly dizzying.

Lu Huaixi's legs went a little unsteady. She tried to turn around and push him away, but the moment she moved, she was simply lifted into his arms instead.

When it came to this sort of closeness, she was always at his mercy.

Even sometimes when he was only talking, he would find whatever made her weak and lean against her ear, drawing her in through sound and warmth alone.

If she yielded first, he pressed further — moving from her ear to somewhere else.

If she braced herself and endured the trembling, he laughed and praised her, and said things that made her face flush and her ears burn.

Either way, he would not let go until he had gotten every advantage.

Lu Huaixi thought about it many times, trying to work out how to turn the tables and get the better of Xie Yuanjing. But no matter how she tried, she could never come up with anything.

This was territory she had never set foot in before.

There was no one to teach her, and she did not know who she would even ask.

While she was still thinking, a faint, sharp sensation came from her ear.

Xie Yuanjing had used one of his slightly pointed teeth on her.

"What are you thinking about?"

Lu Huaixi came back to herself, suppressing the warmth in her cheeks and pressing a finger to his chest.

"Don't use things like this to distract me."

She feigned composure and looked at him. "You definitely got up right after I left the residence, didn't you?"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing.

The two of them were face to face now, openly close to each other.

Lu Huaixi waited for a reply that did not come, but she felt Xie Yuanjing tilt his head slightly, his gaze moving to her lips, his eyes growing darker inch by inch.

A nameless tension wrapped itself around her.

Her hand, which had gone still, curled slightly. Even after all the times before, she was still both afraid and drawn in.

But Xie Yuanjing did not kiss her. He only stayed this close, letting the intimacy settle around her.

After a long moment, his lips curved — and then that voice, grown deeply rough, came slowly to Lu Huaixi's ear.

"You have been gone from the residence too long, Lu Huaixi."

This kind of tingling was exactly the kind that made a person's defences crumble.

And he was the sort to press every advantage, making sure to take the upper hand while a young woman's thoughts were scattered.

"I have been wanting to kiss you since the moment you left."

He said quietly. "Just once, and then we eat. All right?"

He seemed to do it on purpose.

A question he had never asked before, asked now with such clarity — with the roguish ease of a scoundrel, and the playfulness of two people in love. It was impossible for Lu Huaixi to counter.

She forced herself to hold on, and wanted to say not all right.

But Xie Yuanjing seemed to anticipate her. He gave a light laugh, and his lips came down to meet hers.

The exhaustion of the day seemed to ease.

He bit down gently and did not press further.

Even so, the warmth of it stimulated him, deepening his gaze and tightening his arms.

He had never denied his desire. But he knew this was not the time, and so he had always kept it in check.

The other closeness, however, he would not give up.

He wanted Lu Huaixi to grow accustomed to his nearness, to his kisses — because beyond that, there were other things he wanted with her.

Things that belonged between a husband and wife.

When the knock at the door came, Lu Huaixi was feeling somewhat lightheaded.

She was drowsy and soft, and had long since forgotten that she had intended to be cross.

Worried that she might not be able to stand on her own, she even lifted her hand, wanting to loop her arms around Xie Yuanjing's neck.

But the sound was too loud, and it stripped some of the warmth from the kiss before it had really begun.

Lu Huaixi instinctively pushed him away, the movement swift.

Perhaps she had caught one of his injuries — she heard Xie Yuanjing give a quiet sound of displeasure.

Lu Huaixi looked over quickly.

She had still been flustered a moment ago, but when she saw his expression shift to something disgruntled, and the faintly aggrieved look in his eyes, she suddenly burst out laughing. For once, she felt she had come out ahead.

"Pushing me away makes you that happy?" Xie Yuanjing asked, his tone unreadable.

"More or less—"

Lu Huaixi nodded instinctively, eyes curving.

Xie Yuanjing responded with a quiet, cold laugh.

Then, the very instant the knock came again, the man in front of her bent forward abruptly, and bit down at the corner of her lips.

"Without my word, who would dare come in."

The tip of his tooth grazed the corner of her mouth.

Then something followed — slow and deliberate, tracing over lips and teeth, soft and insistent.

Lu Huaixi's mind went blank. In the daze that followed, she arrived at one conclusion: she had lost again.

But the conclusion did not last long, and was quickly replaced by another.

Xie Yuanjing really did love to bite.

—

In the end, the kiss was still interrupted.

The knock was followed by Lady Xie's voice from outside, and behind her, the voices of the two other branch wives.

Lu Huaixi startled, feeling as though she had been caught doing something she should not have.

But Xie Yuanjing was perfectly composed.

The door opened, and the women came in.

"What were you doing in there? No sound for so long."

"Changing the dressings."

Xie Yuanjing sat down nearby. His complexion still carried a slight pallor, and he was drinking the herbal medicine a maidservant had just brought in.

The whole room was thick with the smell of medicine. Even if anyone truly suspected something, no one was going to believe it.

Lu Huaixi relaxed, and took a seat beside Xie Yuanjing.

"Your grandmother had a master ask for a peace talisman for you. But she has had a slight cold these past two days and was afraid of passing it to you, so she sent me to bring it."

Lady Xie had the maidservant take it to him, then continued.

"Your two aunts have been worried about you as well, and came along with me to check on you. I noticed just now that you two have not eaten yet?"

Xie Yuanjing replied that they had not.

"This is far too late. Your body still needs to recover — if you eat this late at night, it will keep you up, which will not do."

Lady Xie frowned in disapproval.

She was about to say more, but someone else spoke first.

"Exactly! The whole household has been worried about you, Yuanjing. You have to get better soon."

It was the Third Lady, Zhao-shi.

She picked up the conversation with a look of concern.

"You don't know how many people have been coming to me asking about you and the Marquis. What could I say? Naturally I told them there is no lasting rift between a father and son — not that anyone with sense would believe that."

As she finished, Zhao-shi could not help glancing up, trying to read something from Xie Yuanjing's face.

But Xie Yuanjing said nothing, his expression thoroughly cool. Lady Xie and the second branch's wife also remained silent.

Zhao-shi had talked herself into a wall, but found a way to keep going.

"I have seen no end of people lately. To say nothing of others — I even had someone come to ask about Princess Qinghe, asking what her relationship with you is — oh, I have no other meaning, First Young Mistress Xie, please don't misunderstand."

At the mention of Princess Qinghe, Lu Huaixi showed very little reaction.

Xie Yuanjing, however, furrowed his brow at Zhao-shi's words, then glanced at Lu Huaixi.

Lady Xie could not quite rein Zhao-shi in, but she knew her son's temperament well.

Before he simply showed the guests out, she rose and took the matter into her own hands.

"The hour is getting late. I won't keep you two any longer. Tomorrow evening, don't let the meal drag this late again. Once you are more recovered, I will come with your aunts to see you properly."

After Zhao-shi left, even the smell of medicine in the room seemed more bearable.

Lu Huaixi walked to the table and was about to sit down when she noticed Xie Yuanjing's gaze still resting on her.

"Why are you looking at me?"

She smiled, eyes curved. "Don't start anything. I want to eat."

chapters.title: What Were You Just Thinking
chapters.content:
A few days after that, Xie Yuanjing seemed to grow busier.

He was still recovering, but he would occasionally visit the study for a while.

Lu Huaixi, in turn, went to Shun'an Fang every few days to sit and listen to the various snippets of news the people there gathered through idle chatter.

Most of it was about the Marquis of Cheng'en and his son's estrangement, about Xie the First Young Master being coldly treated by his father, and about He Bingxin's sudden rise to prominence.

But one day, she heard the name Zheng Xiaoqi.

"You're saying the assassins that day were sent by Zheng Xiaoqi?"

Lu Huaixi had not heard from this person since that time.

She only knew his leg had been broken, and that he still could not stand for long.

"Yes, Young Mistress. And more than that — he had a hand in the He Bingxin matter as well."

Jingshuang bowed her head. "He knew that the First Young Master and He Bingxin were at odds, and wanted to use the situation to retaliate against the First Young Master. There were other schemes planned for afterward, but the matter was reported to the palace by Senior Official Xun, and what followed has not yet moved."

Lu Huaixi listened to the summary, and beyond an initial flicker of interest, felt very little by the end.

She had disliked Zheng Xiaoqi from the start. Having sensed that he harboured ill will toward Xie Yuanjing, she had already taken him for someone not to be trusted.

"And what are people saying about He Bingxin now?"

"The news has not fully spread yet. There are those saying he knew nothing about it and speaking up for him, and those saying he deliberately rode the tide and calculated against the First Young Master. But most people are still hedging because of the Marquis and Senior Official Xun, and saying nothing definitive."

"Whether he knew about it or not comes down to how well he acts, and whether the people watching believe it."

"As the Young Mistress says. That He Bingxin has always kept up a good-natured manner. Even if people have their suspicions, they won't show much openly."

Lu Huaixi gave a cold laugh, the contempt in her eyes undisguised.

"Just wait. A person like him — he will probably come to the Marquis's household specifically to apologise in person."

Jingshuang frowned, looking puzzled.

"If he truly does come, that would be shameless beyond measure. He spent all this time manufacturing his own victimhood, got the First Young Master injured, set off a rift between the Marquis and the First Young Master — and now he would actually dare walk into the Marquis's household."

"Why wouldn't he dare? Doesn't he still have the Marquis protecting him?"

Lu Huaixi said coolly.

From the beginning, when news of Xie Yuanjing's punishment first spread, many of those who had been polite to Xie Yuanjing on the surface had turned right around and gone to call on He Bingxin.

Various rumours about the Marquis of Cheng'en also began to circulate in their wake, making that side livelier by the day.

The Marquis had shown some inclination to avoid the appearance of impropriety, but out of concern for He Bingxin's reputation, he neither disputed nor clarified.

And that, in turn, made Xie Yuanjing's position even more passive.

As though he had truly committed some unforgivable wrong and been cast off by his own father in the name of justice.

Yet Xie Yuanjing had never said a single word throughout any of it.

He let the outside world speculate and gossip — call him ruthless and calculating, or laugh at him for being despised by his father, less favoured than He Bingxin.

Lu Huaixi had heard some of it herself.

She had been furious, and had kept every word of it to herself.

All of it was part of their plan.

Neither of them needed to say anything. Not even after the matter was fully resolved — because silence was the most powerful response to any of this.

Once the matter settled, the Emperor would certainly elevate Xie Yuanjing out of guilt over the last round of misplaced anger.

And when he also learned that Xie Yuanjing had been coldly treated by the Marquis of Cheng'en, whatever displeasure he had previously harboured toward the Marquis would transform into regard for Xie Yuanjing.

At that point, regardless of whether He Bingxin had known what was happening, he would once again be surpassed by Xie Yuanjing.

"If he really does come, he would probably use the same trick as before — deliberately provoke the First Young Master the way he did last time. Whether the First Young Master sees him or refuses to, it will probably end up being spread around as the First Young Master being arrogant and dismissive."

Jingshuang paused, then added: "And now that he has more people on his side than before, if he comes again, there will be even more people supporting him."

"He won't."

The music on stage came to an end. Lu Huaixi picked up her slightly cooled tea, took a sip, and let her expression go indifferent.

"He would need an opportunity to actually reach Xie Yuanjing before he could provoke him. But I am here now, and I will not let him get that far."

Jingshuang still had some residual anger and disdain for He Bingxin on her face.

But hearing those words, she paused — and in an instant, forgot everything she had been feeling a moment ago. Something in her settled, as though she had just caught sight of the cornerstone.

Her lips moved. After a long moment, she finally managed to push out the words she had been wanting to say.

"Young Mistress, the First Young Master is so fortunate to have you."

Lu Huaixi's hand stilled for a moment where she held the teacup. Then she could not help a quiet cough, and nodded with practiced composure. "Isn't he."

Proud and self-satisfied, in a way that made one's heart go soft.

Just as they were speaking, Yaoxu came over from the other side, covering her mouth and saying quietly, "Young Mistress, the First Young Master is here. He's waiting for you at the back gate, in the carriage."

"What is he doing outside the residence?"

"This servant doesn't know either. He said he had some things to take care of and came quietly, without letting anyone know."

Shun'an Fang was growing busier. Lu Huaixi did not ask any more questions, and simply closed her mouth and rose.

The sound of the young women's practice drifted through the courtyard from time to time, and whenever the wind passed, it carried the fragrance of the flowers that had bloomed through one season after another in the garden beds.

Lu Huaixi always walked more slowly when she passed this courtyard — but today was the opposite.

She moved through the corridor and out the back gate.

As the door swung open, a wide carriage with no Xie family markings sat parked to one side not far off.

Xie Yuanjing wore a pale ivory robe today — different from usual.

At first glance it took a moment to register: all one noticed was a striking young man, refined and handsome, like clear wind and radiant moon.

He was standing sideways to Lu Huaixi at this moment, with a faint smile toward someone across from him. There was none of his usual reserve, the kind he kept with most people.

His face was still a little pale, but compared to the very beginning he no longer looked weak. If anything, the pallor only added a certain compelling quality to his features.

Lu Huaixi's steps slowed. She looked toward the young woman in fine clothes standing opposite him.

She must have seen her before — the noble air about her was too striking to be easily forgotten.

She did not go any closer, and did not ask.

She simply stood there and watched for a moment, not quite sure what was going through her mind.

Xie Yuanjing finally sensed her presence and turned to look.

As he turned, the smile at the man's lips had not yet faded — it was a gentleness she rarely saw from him, the warmth in his eyes almost spilling over.

"You're here."

He said it, though it was unclear to whom.

The young woman in fine clothes looked over too, her eyes curved pleasantly — charming and noble at once.

Lu Huaixi's stalled steps started again, but Xie Yuanjing was faster, crossing to her side in a few strides.

"That is Princess Qinghe."

He said.

Then, after a thought, he took her hand. "What were you just thinking? Why didn't you call to me?"

chapters.title: Where Are We Going Today
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing asked what she had been thinking. Lu Huaixi did not answer.

In truth, she had not been thinking anything particular. She had simply been a little surprised.

Xie Yuanjing looked at her. The hand within his sleeve held hers, and after a long pause, he gave a quiet laugh beside her ear.

"You are so unconcerned about me — I am going to be unhappy."

"What, do you like me being a jealous wife?"

Lu Huaixi feigned surprise, her clear eyes widening slightly, like a startled rabbit.

Xie Yuanjing considered this for a moment and replied, "If you are a jealous wife, then I like jealous wives. If you are not, then I don't."

Lu Huaixi had never met anyone with a thicker face than this man. She held back what she wanted to say, and then turned to look toward the young woman in fine clothes not far away.

Seeing her gaze shift, Xie Yuanjing added one more line.

"It was a chance encounter. But I arrived first — you can tell from the carriage."

Hearing that kind of explanation — something almost like being well-behaved — come from Xie Yuanjing's mouth, Lu Huaixi could not quite adjust to it, and found herself slightly distracted.

It was only now that she also noticed: not far away, a lavish carriage carved with cloud patterns and cranes stood parked near the corner. It carried no markings, but the opulence was unmistakably that of imperial family.

"This subject-wife greets Princess Qinghe."

Lu Huaixi inclined her head toward the young woman before her, lowering it slightly, then looking back up to reveal her lovely face.

The Princess drew closer.

When she spoke, her tone was warmer than before, and carried a slowness that was difficult to place — one that made Lu Huaixi feel something was slightly off.

"We have met. At one of the palace banquets before."

Qinghe looked at the person before her, her gaze frank and appraising, and then said very earnestly, "You are even more beautiful than the last time I saw you."

Before Lu Huaixi could reply, Qinghe continued, "I only learned today that you are the proprietress of Shun'an Fang. Can you help me find one of the dancers here?"

Lu Huaixi did not answer immediately.

She looked back at Princess Qinghe's expression, and though a few suspicions had arisen, she remained cautious, and simply smiled.

"May I ask what brings the Princess to seek someone here?"

"There is a dance I want to learn."

Qinghe's expression grew serious as she spoke.

Her bright, sharp eyes narrowed very slightly, as though she had been deliberating for a long time before speaking.

"I also heard that a dancer named Chenyue is at Shun'an Fang. I wonder — could you help me arrange a meeting with her? I only want to see her."

She seemed to remember something as she finished, and added: "I am not looking to cause her any trouble. I genuinely just want to see her."

At the name Chenyue, Lu Huaixi instinctively went still for a moment.

She had almost completely forgotten about Chenyue during all of this.

And the person before her was a Princess. Whether she said yes or no, neither was quite appropriate.

Qinghe, thinking she was hesitating, spoke again. "Don't worry — only I will come. For the dancing lessons too. I will not let anyone else know."

"What dance does the Princess wish to learn? The best dancers in the capital have mostly already entered the palace."

"Not all — I like the dancers in your Shun'an Fang very much."

Qinghe said, and then took hold of her hand, blinking with an edge of eagerness. "Are you free today?"

In that open, almost guileless gaze, Lu Huaixi went still — and became more certain that her earlier suspicion had been correct.

She hesitated briefly, thinking perhaps she ought to bring the Princess inside first.

"Today—"

"Princess, my wife and I have plans today."

Before Lu Huaixi could say anything, Xie Yuanjing replied for her. "Another day, perhaps. The Princess's wish to have someone teach her a dance is not so urgent that it cannot wait."

"It is not urgent, but I cannot always find an excuse to leave the palace. And I do not want my mother's consort to find out I have been learning dance."

Qinghe frowned at Xie Yuanjing, looking somewhat anxious.

"You are together with your wife every single day, eyes open and there she is. Could you not lend her to me for just one day?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing replied without a moment's thought. "This subject also has matters today."

"But..."

Qinghe seemed to take a moment to process this. After quite some time she spoke again.

"You owe me from a while ago. Just one day — stop arguing with me. And your wife hasn't even said anything herself yet. For all you know, she would be happy to come with me."

"No. She would not. This subject and this subject's wife truly have matters today. The Princess may treat it as though she does not know that my wife is the proprietress of Shun'an Fang and go in on her own."

"But if I go in, it is still to ask the proprietress."

Lu Huaixi felt a headache coming on.

She looked at Princess Qinghe still holding her hand, and used her free hand to give Xie Yuanjing's sleeve a small tug.

Very quickly, Xie Yuanjing stopped, and changed what he was going to say.

"Today is truly not possible. But if the Princess wishes to come out of the palace in the future, she may send my wife a card directly."

That was his way of offering to serve as a pretext for the Princess's outings.

But having said that, Xie Yuanjing added one more condition.

"However, the Princess may not use my wife's name as an excuse to leave the palace and then go elsewhere. If the Princess has a meeting with my wife, the Princess may only be at the Marquis's household or at Shun'an Fang."

Qinghe's face was still unhappy.

She deliberated for some time, but seeming to understand that this was as far as Xie Yuanjing would yield, she held back and did not push further.

She looked back at Lu Huaixi, and the expression she turned on her held a trace of pity — as though she thought Lu Huaixi was a little unfortunate.

Lu Huaixi was somewhat bewildered by that look.

It took her a moment to realise: Princess Qinghe probably thought she was being kept under tight control, and that she was not having a particularly good time.

She was almost amused, and could not think of what to say, but after a pause she did not go out of her way to explain.

She saw Qinghe inside, then boarded the carriage waiting outside.

The moment she sat down, the wheels began to roll.

"Where are we going today?"

Lu Huaixi looked at Xie Yuanjing, genuinely unable to imagine what their plans were today. "Actually, Princess Qinghe probably won't stay very long — I could have kept her company for a while."

"No need. Wait until she sends you a card next time, and then you can accompany her properly."

"What do you mean?"

Lu Huaixi blinked, then made a soft sound of realisation. "You want people to think that I and Princess Qinghe are on good terms?"

"Not think — genuinely be on good terms."

At this, Lu Huaixi looked at Xie Yuanjing without speaking.

Her eyes were still very bright, but without the smile, there was something more serious in them — more intent — than usual.

Xie Yuanjing reached up and touched her face, pressed a kiss to the tip of her nose, and settled back.

"Why are you looking at me like that?"

Lu Huaixi still did not speak.

Xie Yuanjing held her gaze for a moment, and then it slowly came to him. He gave a quiet laugh.

"You are overthinking this. I simply want you to have another person to be on good terms with — so that moving in court circles will be a little easier for you."

He drew her closer and explained patiently.

"You probably guessed something just now. Princess Qinghe is not quite the same as other princesses. She did fall ill once when she was young and was injured, and for a long time she was unable to speak. It is why the Emperor dotes on her particularly.

"The Princess has recovered now, but she still moves and speaks a little more slowly than most. If one does not know her well, and does not spend too much time chatting with her, there is generally not much of a difference."

"I see. That is why Princess Qinghe rarely appears at banquets, and does not speak much when she does."

Lu Huaixi recalled having heard something, years ago, about Princess Qinghe being injured.

But the news had been suppressed very quickly, and someone had said the injury was not serious, and before long no one spoke of it again.

"Yes. It has been kept quiet within the palace. Very few people know — partly to avoid disrupting her recovery, and partly to prevent anyone from taking advantage of her."

"But I think Princess Qinghe is just like anyone else."

Lu Huaixi said sincerely, "I only noticed because I had heard the rumour before. If I had not, I would simply have thought her candid and straightforward — not that there was anything else."

"As things stand now, that is indeed the case. Several senior physicians in the Imperial Medical Bureau, even Elder Zeng, have said Princess Qinghe is no longer impaired. Only the slight slowness in her speech may take a little more time to fully resolve."

With that said, Xie Yuanjing looked at the person before him.

Recalling what the Third Lady Zhao-shi had said a few days ago, he continued:

"Among all the princesses, Qinghe is the one about whom the least is known — and therefore the most inquired about. But I am not well acquainted with her. The Xie family has had little contact with her mother's consort. The most connection we have is through my paternal aunt, who was acquainted with her — one might say she and I are something like childhood playmates in the loosest sense."

"Then why was she willing to speak up for you — when everyone else was avoiding you?"

Lu Huaixi shifted the subject.

Her voice still sounded clear and pleasant, but listened to carefully, the tone had shifted slightly.

Xie Yuanjing paused for an instant, then broke into a sudden smile.

"So you did care. I thought you truly had not a scrap of concern for me."

Lu Huaixi had been edging slightly toward him, and at his laugh, she stopped and looked away.

She had thought about it before she saw Princess Qinghe, yes. But the thought had only lasted a moment, and so she had not asked.

She should not have asked even now. But the smile on Xie Yuanjing's face just now had been too gentle.

It was the kind of expression that, even when they had been engaged, Lu Huaixi had never managed to see on his face.

So now that he had brought it up, she wanted to know.

"Don't use things like this to brush me off. Just now, in front of Princess Qinghe, you were clearly at ease."

"I was at ease — I was talking about you."

Xie Yuanjing caught her hand and would not let her make mischief with it. His voice grew softer still.

"She was cautioning me at first — she said her palace maids had heard some gossip about my wife being jealous. I asked her about it, and ended up telling her how remarkable you are."

"I don't believe it. What is so remarkable about me? And when was I jealous? When did I ever know about that?"

"You are remarkable in every way."

Xie Yuanjing did not say where that piece of news had come from. It was a small matter, and he would take care of it without needing her involvement.

"As for her speaking up on my behalf — it was not actually because of me. Shen Zhoushu went to find her. Her mother's consort also knew I would not truly be in serious trouble, and let the Princess make the trip, which suited everyone's purpose."

"Shen Zhoushu?"

"Yes. When Princess Qinghe was injured several years ago, it was Shen Zhoushu who rescued her. For a period of time, the Princess only recognised Shen Zhoushu. To put it plainly — those two are the ones who are truly close."

Xie Yuanjing spoke and played with Lu Huaixi's hand at the same time, his eyes full of warmth.

He had never experienced being cared for like this before. In the past, Lu Huaixi would not have had these feelings at all — and the times she had been vexed by someone were always because that person had genuinely annoyed her.

Not this — where she was clearly showing the mild irritation and curiosity that came from something connected to him.

Xie Yuanjing felt something full and spreading in his chest, an inexpressible pleasure, his attention entirely fixed on her.

But he also had no intention of letting her spend time guessing or feeling unsettled. That was never what he wanted.

"I could have Shen Zhoushu come and answer your questions."

"No need."

Lu Huaixi declined. "It's not that I don't believe you."

"You can choose not to believe me, and just keep asking, keep making me prove it."

"Wouldn't that make me unreasonable and demanding?"

"Only when I have no patience does someone become unreasonable and demanding. And I will never lose patience with you."

Lu Huaixi was satisfied with this. Her dark eyes curved into a smile again.

She shifted herself closer to Xie Yuanjing — and then a little closer — like a docile little sheep.

"Then where are we going today? How come there was no word of this before — was it decided on the spur of the moment?"

"Not at all. I have been thinking about it for a while."

"Then where is it?"

Xie Yuanjing teased her and said nothing.

Outside, the sounds went from lively to quiet several times, and after a while, the carriage gradually slowed.

Lu Huaixi had been prying for ages and gotten nowhere, so she gave up and simply lifted the carriage curtain to look out.

It was a residence.

It had none of the imposing authority of the Marquis's household, and none of the grandeur of the Lu residence — but stepping inside, the view that met her was one of quiet elegance, the kind that made a person feel at ease.

Further in, there was a courtyard of the sort Lu Huaixi liked, with flower beds arranged around it. Through the courtyard, a waterside pavilion sat encircled by green water.

"Whose house is this? How did you just bring me straight in?"

Lu Huaixi was absorbed in looking. Not until she was nearly at the pavilion and about to sit down did she suddenly come to herself and grab Xie Yuanjing's arm.

"This isn't a house you've arranged outside, is it?"

"It is. And it's our house."

Xie Yuanjing pinched her cheek lightly, and seeing her stunned expression, led her further in.

The main courtyard was large. Xie Yuanjing did not linger in each room, but went directly toward the back.

"A bathing pool has been built — wider than the one at the household. In a few days I'll have water brought in. Have a look and see if there is anything else you'd like to add."

Lu Huaixi's attention had been on the outside. When she saw the bathing pool — larger than the rooms back at the Marquis's household — she walked around it and shook her head.

"Nothing. Why would I need to come and look at somewhere to bathe?"

She was puzzled.

She did enjoy playing in water, but the pool was already built — it could not be easily altered now.

"If anything, this bathing pool seems a little too large. I'll take a bathing barrel then — and maybe put a daybed at that end. Sometimes after soaking for a while I get tired and need somewhere to rest."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her with a quiet smile, then his gaze passed over the centre of the pool. He gave a nod.

"Yes, one is needed. You will get tired."

Lu Huaixi felt something indefinably off about his tone.

She looked over at him, but could read nothing from Xie Yuanjing's face.

Only the faint curve at the corner of his lips — and those eyes looking back at her, emotions held just below the surface.

Xie Yuanjing remained quietly holding her gaze, then reached out, his thumb pressing lightly at the corner of her mouth, with a meaning that was impossible to put plainly into words.

Lu Huaixi felt a faint itch and tilted her head back slightly.

"What are you doing?"

She asked softly, her ears growing warm.

But no reply came — only at the moment the pressure at the corner of her mouth came again did she sense a familiar, not entirely unfamiliar kind of danger.

Very quickly, something seemed to occur to Lu Huaixi.

She looked past him to the people behind, and lowered her voice. "There are so many people. Don't do anything you shouldn't."

Xie Yuanjing took hold of her with his other hand. His expression was that of a man of perfect propriety, utterly undisturbed — but his voice carried the low, characteristic depth he always had when he wanted to be close to her.

"I'll have them leave."

chapters.title: I Told Them to Leave
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi changed the subject abruptly.

Her voice still sounded sweet and gentle as ever, yet upon closer listen, her tone carried a subtle difference.

Xie Yuanjing froze for a moment, then suddenly broke into a smile.

"So my lady does care after all. I thought you truly didn't mind me in the slightest."

Lu Huaixi had been inching closer to him, but when she heard him laugh, she stopped and turned her head away.

Before she had seen Princess Qinghe, she had indeed thought about this matter. But the thought had only lingered for a fleeting moment, so she hadn't asked.

She shouldn't have asked now either — yet just a moment ago, Xie Yuanjing's smile had been so unbearably warm.

It was an expression she had never once seen on his face, not even back when their engagement had already been settled.

So since he had brought it up himself, she wanted to ask.

"Stop trying to brush me off with words like that. Just now, in front of Princess Qinghe, you were clearly smiling with ease."

"I was at ease — because we were talking about you."

Xie Yuanjing caught her hand to keep her from fidgeting, his tone growing softer by the moment.

"She was warning me at first — her ladies-in-waiting had overheard people gossiping these past few days, saying that my wife was jealous by nature. I asked a few questions, then naturally steered the conversation toward singing your praises."

"I don't believe that. What's so impressive about me? And since when am I the jealous type? I don't even know what they're talking about."

"Everything about you is impressive."

Xie Yuanjing didn't say where the rumors had come from. It was a minor matter — he would handle it quietly without letting her worry about it.

"As for her pleading on my behalf, it wasn't because of me. It was Shen Zhoushu who went to find her. Her mother, the Imperial Consort, also knew I wouldn't really do anything drastic, so she let the princess make the trip — going along with the tide, so to speak."

"Shen Zhoushu?"

"Yes. A few years ago, when Princess Qinghe was injured, it was Shen Zhoushu who saved her. That year, the princess only had eyes for Shen Zhoushu. In other words, he's the one she's actually close to."

As Xie Yuanjing spoke, he idly played with Lu Huaixi's hand, his eyes full of warmth and amusement.

He had never experienced being cared for like this before. In the past, Lu Huaixi would never have worked herself into such moods over him. Occasionally she got annoyed at others, but only when someone had truly gotten on her nerves.

It had never been like this — where she so openly showed her dissatisfaction and curiosity over something that had to do with him.

Xie Yuanjing's heart swelled with a quiet, indescribable joy. His gaze never left her.

But he had no intention of making her guess or feel uneasy again. That had never been what he wanted.

"I can even have Shen Zhoushu come and answer your questions himself."

"No."

Lu Huaixi refused. "It's not like I don't believe you."

"You're allowed not to believe me. You can keep asking, and keep making me prove it."

"Wouldn't that just make me seem unreasonable?"

"You're only unreasonable when I lose patience with you — but I will never lose patience with you."

Lu Huaixi heard that and felt a quiet satisfaction bloom in her chest. Her dark eyes curved into a smile.

She leaned toward Xie Yuanjing, a little closer, then a little closer still — gentle and docile as a lamb.

"So where are we going now? Why wasn't there any word beforehand? Was it a sudden decision?"

"No. I've been thinking about it for a long time."

"Then where?"

Xie Yuanjing teased her and said nothing.

Outside, the sounds of bustle rose and fell several times. A little while later, the carriage gradually began to slow.

Lu Huaixi had been pressing him and gotten nowhere. In the end, she gave up trying to get an answer and simply lifted the curtain to look for herself.

It was a courtyard residence.

It lacked the imposing grandeur of the Marquis's manor and the distinguished elegance of the Lu estate, but stepping through the gate, one was greeted by a serene and refined stillness that made the heart feel effortlessly at ease.

Further inside was a courtyard of the kind Lu Huaixi loved, ringed by garden beds in bloom. Beyond it, a water pavilion sat surrounded by rippling green water.

"Whose home is this? You just walked me right in."

Lu Huaixi had been gazing around in a daze. It was only when she reached the pavilion and was about to sit down that she suddenly caught herself and grabbed Xie Yuanjing's arm.

"Don't tell me this is a house you set up somewhere outside?"

"It is. And it's also our home."

Xie Yuanjing pinched her cheek lightly, and seeing her stunned expression, took her hand and led her further inside.

The main courtyard was spacious. Xie Yuanjing didn't linger in any of the rooms, leading her directly to the rear of the residence.

"The bathhouse has been built with a soaking pool — even more spacious than the one at the manor. In a few days I'll have water piped in. Have a look and see if there's anything else you'd like added."

Lu Huaixi's attention had been on the outer parts of the residence all along. When she saw the bathhouse — larger than even the rooms back at the manor — she walked a full circle around it and shook her head.

"Nothing. Why would I need to come and specially inspect a bathing room?"

She didn't understand.

She did enjoy playing in the water, but the pool had already been built — it wasn't as though it could easily be changed.

"If I had to say something — this pool does seem a bit too large. In that case, I'd also like a bathing tub. And it would be best to put a daybed at that end, so when I've soaked too long and get tired, I can rest on it."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her with a quiet smile and said nothing. Then his gaze swept across the center of the pool, and he gave a small nod.

"Yes, a daybed should go there. You will indeed get tired."

Lu Huaixi felt something vaguely off about that tone.

But when she looked up at him, she couldn't read anything from Xie Yuanjing's expression.

Only the faint curve at the corner of his lips, and the way his lowered eyes met hers — emotions carefully held in check beneath the surface.

Xie Yuanjing held her gaze in silence. Then he reached out, the pad of his finger pressing lightly at the corner of her mouth, carrying an intent that couldn't quite be put into words.

Lu Huaixi felt a little tingle and tilted her head back slightly.

"What are you doing?"

She asked softly, the tips of her ears growing warm.

But she heard no reply. It was only in the moment that pressure fell again at the corner of her lips that she sensed something — a kind of danger that wasn't entirely unfamiliar.

Very quickly, it was as though something had occurred to Lu Huaixi.

She glanced at the people standing behind him and spoke quietly. "There are so many people here. Don't be improper."

Xie Yuanjing held her with his other hand, his outward expression perfectly composed and unreadable — yet his voice carried the low, unhurried cadence it always took on when he wanted to be close to her.

"I'll tell them to leave."

chapters.title: Learn It Later, Practice Some More
chapters.content:
In truth, Xie Yuanjing had no real need to say the words out loud.

The sharp-eyed attendants, noticing that the two of them were lingering in that place with no sign of leaving — as though they had private things to say — had already slipped out quietly and pulled the door shut behind them.

And almost the instant the door closed, Xie Yuanjing wrapped his arms around Lu Huaixi's waist, lifted her, lowered his head, and kissed her.

An unfamiliar place. A wide, private bathing pool.

These things stirred not only Xie Yuanjing — they also seemed to crack open a certain haze in Lu Huaixi, letting in a little more understanding than before.

When a scorching, solid warmth pressed against her, Lu Huaixi suddenly thought of the booklets she had been keeping pressed to the bottom of her storage chest — and the few illustrations she had casually turned past.

She understood, belatedly, why Xie Yuanjing had brought her to look at this pool.

Her face burned, and the nervousness was real — but she still tilted her head back with a kind of quiet compliance, receiving Xie Yuanjing's somewhat forceful kiss, allowing it, and responding as her own heart directed.

The amplified sound of water around them carried a warmth that drew the spirit in.

Lu Huaixi's soft sounds dissolved several times against his lips and each time re-emerged in a register that made her face burn hotter.

She seemed to be beginning to understand what to do — and perhaps was feeling her way toward what made Xie Yuanjing lose his composure.

At the moment he bit down lightly again, Lu Huaixi let the tip of her tongue make brief contact.

Then she opened her eyes and watched the colour in the man's gaze darken in an instant.

In the next breath she was lifted and pressed to the wall beside the door.

At the same time, Xie Yuanjing drew back from her lips by one inch.

"You've learned it?"

He pressed one soft bite after another at the corner of her mouth, his voice a rough, low laugh. "Learn this, and then it's time to learn something else."

"Something else — what?"

Lu Huaixi's breath was also unsteady. Her voice was softer than usual, the syllables unconsciously drawn out — like a cat leaning against someone in a quiet bid for attention.

She did not think anything was wrong with it. But it sent a flush through Xie Yuanjing's gaze, and he immediately changed his mind and kissed her again.

"Learn it later. Practice some more first."

—

When Shen Zhoushu arrived, he wandered around for quite some time before finding anyone he recognised.

"Nice place. It'll be easy for me to visit too — no sneaking around. Like he's keeping a hidden lover here."

He kept talking as he walked.

Noticing that Gong Zhuo and the others had stopped in the courtyard, and that all the room doors stood open but not a single person was inside, he stopped mid-sentence.

"Where are your lord and master?"

"Master Shen, our lord and the Young Mistress are still looking around the residence. Why don't you find somewhere to sit first?"

"Surely looking around doesn't take this long. Fine, I'll go find them myself."

"Master Shen—"

Gong Zhuo called after him, hesitated for quite some time, and said, "Our lord and the Young Mistress likely have private things to say. He deliberately sent everyone away. You might want to wait a while before going."

"They've been together every single day since he was injured. The moment either of them opens their eyes, the other is right there — how much can there be that needs saying out of earshot? I'm the one who has business with him."

Shen Zhoushu waved his hand and went straight ahead. "By the way — did Princess Qinghe have any other business today when she came out?"

"No, she simply went to Shun'an Fang."

"To watch people dance?"

Shen Zhoushu's steps slowed. He turned to look at Jingshuang behind him. "Did your Young Mistress leave someone to keep her company?"

"Master Shen, please don't worry. Shun'an Fang has the Young Mistress's trusted people there, and the First Young Master also left someone. When the time comes, the Princess will be escorted back to the palace. Though the First Young Master did say — if Master Shen's people were also present, then it should be Master Shen's people who escort her back."

Shen Zhoushu heard this, showed no particular reaction, gave a sound of acknowledgment, and did not ask further.

Xie Yuanjing's residence was not among the largest in the officials' district, but even so, Shen Zhoushu walked quite a distance before finding anyone.

The weather had grown less brutal by now, but his forehead still gathered a thin film of perspiration.

"Your lord really knows how to pick a shaded spot."

He looked ahead. "He's not exchanging private words here at all. He just found a cool place and is waiting for sunset."

Gong Zhuo walked alongside him, thinking he might need to intervene at the right moment and give advance notice of their arrival.

But perhaps because they were no longer at the Marquis's household, Shen Zhoushu's voice was considerably louder than usual.

He had no need to say anything — Xie Yuanjing had already heard him approaching.

At this moment, Xie Yuanjing was caught between reason and instinct.

He held her in his arms, using considerable effort to stop himself from taking the hand Lu Huaixi was causing havoc with at his waist and drawing it further down.

Yet he also had no intention of letting go of her.

He measured the distance. Only when the timing was right did he stop the kiss and simply hold her, patting her back gently.

Gong Zhuo's voice came almost exactly at the moment he had calculated. Xie Yuanjing could still feel the small flinch of the person in his arms at the sudden sound.

His patting grew a little softer. His still-uneven breathing stayed measured and soothing throughout.

"It's all right. It is nobody strange. Nobody can see."

Lu Huaixi said nothing. Her face was pressed to Xie Yuanjing's chest — muddled and completely docile.

The gentle patting did not stop, one steady beat after another.

After a while, her eyes slowly gathered focus, clarity returning in small increments.

Once she had come back to herself, she withdrew from Xie Yuanjing's arms, pressed her lips together, and felt the lingering sensation at the corners of her mouth.

Shen Zhoushu's voice rang out again, calling for Xie Yuanjing.

Xie Yuanjing did not answer. His gaze stayed on the person before him.

Seeing the slight redness at the corner of her lips, he touched it gently.

"Does it hurt?"

He had not held back, not once.

But Lu Huaixi did not respond the way she usually would — she did not scold him for not letting go.

And she herself had fanned the flame earlier. To act coy about it now would be a little unreasonable.

It was just that, after all, she was not as bold as Xie Yuanjing, who could emerge from a long stretch of kissing with not a trace of shyness — looking utterly satisfied.

"It doesn't hurt."

Lu Huaixi's voice came out soft and muffled. She said quietly, "Shen Zhoushu is calling you."

"Yes."

"Then go out."

She paused, then added: "By yourself."

"No."

Xie Yuanjing refused at once, drew her in and held her once more, then spoke with resigned helplessness. "I cannot go out right now."

"Why not?"

Why — the reaction had been rather strong, and he had not managed to bring it under control.

"Next time I teach you something new, I'll explain then. You'll understand."

The man's voice carried a thread of laughter. Something in it made Lu Huaixi's ears go inexplicably warm. She had the feeling it was not something easy to speak of out loud.

—

By the time the door finally opened, Shen Zhoushu had been waiting outside for quite a while.

He who had always considered himself the most experienced man in romantic matters stood there — and still had not worked out what exactly he had just interrupted.

"What were you two doing in there? The place is huge — all that space to look at, and you end up tucked away in this corner."

Shen Zhoushu frowned and asked, genuinely puzzled.

Xie Yuanjing ignored him at first. But when the man proved truly unbearable, he stopped and looked at him once.

"I think you ought to consider getting married sooner."

"What? What does that mean?"

Shen Zhoushu blinked, still wanting to ask more — but the other man had already grown tired of talking and walked on ahead.

Gong Zhuo stood to one side watching, and held his tongue.

That was just how this one was. And yet a few days ago he had been trying to teach their First Young Master how to court someone.

chapters.title: The Filth That Clung
chapters.content:
Once Xie Yuanjing confirmed that Lu Huaixi also liked the new residence, he moved quickly.

Furnishings were sent over, and the place changed its appearance almost day by day.

He also made no secret of his intention to move out of the Marquis's household. Everyone in the residence knew, and yet no one dared to ask about it.

Lady Xie sought him out several times with the intention of persuading him, but never managed to change his mind.

In the end, Lady Xie had no choice but to intercept Lu Huaixi the moment she returned from Shun'an Fang — not even waiting for her to step inside the gate before bringing it up.

"I don't know what Yuanjing is thinking. The moment he steps out of the Marquis's household, his father will certainly use it as an opportunity to give He Bingxin free access — let him come calling every day.

"I am not saying anything about the break with his father. That man was never worth it. But what sense is there in simply handing everything over — giving someone else a free advantage?"

Lady Xie had by now completely severed ties with the Marquis of Cheng'en.

She had even blocked his path on several occasions, and never shown He Bingxin a moment of goodwill.

But she had no intention of letting him repudiate her and remarry, and he did not dare truly put her aside.

Right now Lady Xie had no interest in reconciling father and son — but she also had no wish to see her own son make way for someone else.

"You have been spending more time with him lately. Can you try persuading him on my behalf? Doing something like this — what is that if not acting on impulse? And dragging you into hardship along with him — there is simply no justifying that."

Lu Huaixi listened at first without saying anything.

She was not sure whether Lady Xie knew that the new house had been sitting empty this whole time.

"His injuries aren't even fully healed, and he should be recovering properly in the household. But that stubborn temper of his insists on doing things at precisely the wrong moment. He won't trust me, his own mother, and just does as he pleases. Does he think I would harm him — let him suffer this for nothing?"

"Mother, he is not acting on impulse."

Lady Xie finished, and Lu Huaixi waited a beat before speaking.

She had just stepped through the gate, and looking up she could see the servants moving quietly along the corridor in the distance, all of them heads bowed, unhurried and orderly.

And yet in a residence as opulent and imposing as this one, who would ever stop to wonder what rifts lay hidden between its people.

"Whatever he does will have been carefully thought through. And the rumours right now are in his favour. The Emperor has not been able to set aside his pride yet, but his intentions are showing in recent decrees. Mother, it would be better to trust him."

"I want to trust him — for anything else, I would never question him at all. But moving out of the household is no small matter. If he truly leaves, it will require the clan elders to open the ancestral hall."

"Mother is perhaps misreading the situation. He is not separating the family or severing ties. He is simply moving out. To convalesce and carry out his duties."

Lady Xie went quiet for a moment at that, uncertainty crossing her face.

"He said that? Are you sure he isn't keeping something from you?"

"He doesn't need to say it so plainly. What matters, Mother, is not what he says — it is how others see it. Could you not treat it as him going to a country estate to recover? Why force him to put a formal explanation to it?"

Lu Huaixi actually wanted to say that Lady Xie was not thinking clearly.

But she also thought that she and this mother-in-law of hers had perhaps not yet reached the point where such a remark would be taken well.

She also of course understood that Xie Yuanjing genuinely intended to move out. But a father-son estrangement of this kind was best left to live in the realm of rumour — pressing it further into the open would only work against Xie Yuanjing.

She felt that Lady Xie had likely talked herself into a corner and was too turned around to see that there was another path.

"Once a thing is officially named, it becomes difficult to undo. But leaving the household at this moment is not necessarily a bad thing for him. There is no end of visitors coming through, which already disrupts his recovery — and then there is also a Marquis who cannot read the situation—"

Lu Huaixi blinked, realising she had lost track of herself and let the words out unguarded.

But she did not feel too badly about it. She only moved her lips, and added a somewhat perfunctory follow-up.

"I spoke too quickly — it is not proper to be disrespectful to one's elders. But what I mean is: he made the decision to leave the household, which means leaving is better for him."
