Lady Xie was no ordinary woman. Though she had been wound tight with worry over her son, hearing these words, she came back to herself quickly.

After a pause, she said nothing, only looked at Lu Huaixi — and there was something complex in her eyes.

After a long moment, she let out a quiet sigh.

"I was not thinking as clearly as you."

"Not at all — Mother was too worried, and that made it hard to see beyond the immediate."

Lu Huaixi's clear eyes looked at Lady Xie, her lips curving slightly, the sunlight catching her expression — at once bold and charming.

As Lady Xie looked at her, she suddenly laughed.

"In the future, if you don't feel like apologising to me, don't bother. The fact that you clearly can't hide your own unwillingness makes it even more obvious."

Lu Huaixi blinked and offered no explanation on her own behalf.

She returned Lady Xie's smile — a tacit acceptance of the observation that she had not been contrite at all.

Just as they were speaking, the sound of carriage wheels drifted in from outside, growing from distant to near.

Then someone went out and came back in again, stopping before Lady Xie and Lu Huaixi.

"My Lady, Young Mistress — there is someone outside requesting an audience with the First Young Master. He says he has come to offer an apology."

The servant presented a card. Lady Xie accepted it and opened it for a glance.

But in an instant, her expression changed — her brows and eyes going cold and sharp with immediate contempt.

"No audience. Have him driven away."

Lu Huaixi's expression flickered. She instinctively looked over.

"Mother — who is it?"

Lady Xie did not conceal it from her. Her voice came out cold. "He Bingxin."

At the name, Lu Huaixi was not surprised. But her eyes held the same contempt that had flashed through Lady Xie's.

The world would always have people one could not abide. Even among those serving at court, there would always be opposing factions with irreconcilable positions.

But a person who had not quite risen to the level of a smiling fox, and yet habitually played the part of the kind and magnanimous one — always positioning himself in a passive, helpless role to perform his victimhood — was far more nauseating than someone who simply made their enmity plain.

He was like filth that had clung to one. No matter how one dealt with him, he would always find a way to become the one deserving sympathy. Impossible to shake off.

"Don't send him away yet."

Lu Huaixi quickly called the servant back, then looked toward Lady Xie.

"The Marquis is not in the household right now. He has come knowing he cannot get through the gate — he is deliberately hoping to be driven away by Mother's people."

The more forcefully Lady Xie acted right now, the better it would suit He Bingxin's purpose.

He would certainly pin all blame onto her, continuing to play the unknowing party who only wished to seek Xie the First Young Master's forgiveness.

And yet he could not even get through the gate.

Those outside would only feel sorry for him, while the Marquis of Cheng'en would step in to defend him — widening the rift further.

Lady Xie naturally understood this as well. She simply could not swallow the indignity.

"Whatever he has schemed in his heart, I will never allow him to set foot inside the Marquis's household. If he has no fear of people pointing and whispering, he is welcome to have Xie Zizhang personally escort him in."

"Mother, don't be alarmed. I have no intention of letting him in either."

Lu Huaixi took over, her gaze moving to the main gate.

"But Mother, don't play into his hands either. I'll go."

—

Outside the gate, He Bingxin waited to one side, dressed in plain clothes.

Not far away, a carriage sat parked — unremarkable, narrow, and worn.

His lowered eyes concealed calculation, the kind born of long familiarity and certainty of outcome.

He soon heard the sound of the gate opening.

He instinctively looked up, assuming it would be the Xie household's Lady coming out in a fury to send him away.

He had already worked out exactly how he would take a few shoves and bruises to buy himself some sympathy. But when he looked up, he suddenly froze.

The person who had come out was Lu Huaixi — the same Lu Huaixi he had seen twice before. Dark hair, dark eyes, as beautiful as peach blossoms in full bloom.

A pale-coloured skirt, vivid and graceful. Even with a trace of cool composure at the edges of her brows, the effect was still enough to take away one's breath.

She was even more beautiful than the last time he had seen her.

He Bingxin's breath caught for an instant. He simply looked.

In that moment, he could see no one else. He had forgotten entirely why he had come. What showed on his face was the envy of Xie Yuanjing he usually kept buried deep — raw and undisguised.

But not long after, a voice rang out, cold as ice, startling everyone into looking over.

"Look at her one more time, and I will take your eyes."

chapters.title: Warning
chapters.content:
A figure had come out of the household — no one could say exactly when — carrying with them a cold and desolate stillness.

"First Young Master."

The servants nearby bowed their heads.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze did not move.

The moment he saw the look in He Bingxin's eyes, something dangerous had settled into the space between his brows.

He walked directly to Lu Huaixi's side, glanced at her once, and guided the stunned young woman behind him.

He Bingxin lurched back to himself, instinctively flinching at that oppressive force, stumbling back several steps.

But after a moment, he stopped himself, not wanting to appear so clearly at a disadvantage, and forced himself to stand where he was.

The man on the stone steps stood tall and proud, looking down at him with cold contempt.

Within He Bingxin's resentment was mingled humiliation. His fists clenched. He met Xie Yuanjing's gaze — sharp and icy, carrying the force of someone who had never needed to yield.

He opened his mouth, but for a long moment could not produce a sound. He could only watch, helplessly, as the two of them stood together.

He had not expected to run into Xie Yuanjing at all, and had not expected that the Xie Yuanjing before him now would be colder and more imposing than the last time — with a high-born arrogance that no amount of climbing could reach, unsettling him to the core, making it impossible to follow the script he had rehearsed on his way here.

But he knew he could not stay silent.

"First Young Master Xie has misunderstood. I came today—"

He Bingxin finally managed to squeeze out a sound.

He pulled up a smile, trying to appear as guileless and harmless as possible.

"I came today to offer my apologies to the First Young Master. The matter beforehand was my own negligence, and because I was injured I could not explain in time — which led to the First Young Master being implicated without cause."

Xie Yuanjing's eyes held undisguised contempt.

He gave a cold, dismissive sound, withdrew his gaze, and simply ignored the man, turning to look back at Lu Huaixi.

"Why so late getting back?"

He took her hand and drew her forward, positioning her with her back to He Bingxin.

Lu Huaixi finally came back to herself from the shock of his sudden appearance, let him take her hand, and tilted her head up to reply.

"A new dance came in — I stayed to watch. When did you come out? Were you heading somewhere, or did you just get back?"

"I was about to go and meet you. I ran into the gatekeeper."

Xie Yuanjing smiled and raised his hand to tuck a strand of hair at her cheek behind her ear.

As he lowered his eyes, the man across from them remained standing there, his gaze falling on the two of them. The false benevolence he usually wore was absent from his face, replaced by something that was visibly cracking.

Xie Yuanjing looked up, meeting that gaze — full of jealousy and resentment.

He Bingxin was caught in the act and lurched, barely concealing his panic.

Xie Yuanjing gave him one cold, indifferent look. Then he looked away.

"Next time, have someone call for me rather than dealing with these people yourself."

His voice was low but warm — nothing like the Xie First Young Master who had been radiating the will to kill a moment ago.

But his voice was not quiet, either. It carried precisely far enough for He Bingxin to hear.

"It is a waste of your eyes. You will only be in a bad mood after."

Lu Huaixi instinctively wanted to push back on this — she was not so easily put out of sorts, she wanted to say.

But Xie Yuanjing added one more line.

"Though if you are in a bad mood, I will coax you."

Neither of them seemed to be paying He Bingxin the least attention.

But Lu Huaixi still had some sense, and stopped him before he could continue.

"You should not have come out. This is a small matter — I can handle it."

"Even small matters — I will not let you touch them."

Saying this, Xie Yuanjing thought again of the look He Bingxin had directed at Lu Huaixi just now.

Stunned. Hungry. Burning. And envious — so openly covetous that he had forgotten every other person beyond the gate, blatantly trying to lay claim with his eyes alone.

In that instant, violent fury had surged through him. He had almost genuinely wanted to take those eyes, to kill him.

"You need not worry about me. In the past, I could not be bothered and did not care. But now that you are here, I naturally will not be so careless."

"But what can you do? You cannot strike him again."

Lu Huaixi hesitated.

She truly found He Bingxin's methods disgusting, and thought that when it came to dealing with a person like him, she was better suited than Lady Xie.

Her own reputation in the capital's rumour mill was not exactly quiet — but among it all, her appearance was just one unremarkable thread.

In other words, if Xie Yuanjing raised his hand against him, it would not serve him well. But she could.

Even if she hit him, berated him, chased him off — at worst people would say she had a temper, that she was protective of her husband. That was all.

She could even disgust him with it. Everyone already believed she was young and pampered.

Whatever methods he used, she would answer in kind, and they would see who was the sharper one.

But this time, it seemed Xie Yuanjing intended to handle it himself.

Lu Huaixi also thought of He Bingxin's tactics again.

The more she considered it, the more irritated she became, and she instinctively started to turn back toward him.

But Xie Yuanjing was faster, pulling her back and not allowing her to turn.

"Do not look at him."

His voice was low, and he was smiling — but behind it was a forcefulness that did not invite argument. "Go in and wait for me."

"But—"

"Be good."

In the day-to-day, Xie Yuanjing treated Lu Huaixi with patience and gentleness above all else.

But now, with this edge of deep possessiveness and command coming through, Lu Huaixi felt a brief dizziness — and something stirring in her that she could not quite name.

In the end, Lu Huaixi obediently went inside. She even looked up at him as she did, with a tolerant smile, and told him not to let himself be manipulated.

He Bingxin watched their closeness in full.

The hand within his sleeve tightened by degrees. He felt suddenly uncertain — whether, at this rate, he could truly take everything that Xie Yuanjing had.

At last, Lu Huaixi's figure was gone from the gate.

And this time, Xie Yuanjing truly did not raise his hand or have anyone bound.

He stood there, and his gaze lifted. His voice went cold in an instant.

"Seen enough?"

He Bingxin came back fully from the stupor of a moment ago, his heart giving a sudden lurch.

"I — I have no other intention, I—"

"Control your own eyes."

Xie Yuanjing cut him off, voice cold, each word deliberate, carrying a warning. "Otherwise, no one will be able to protect you."

A flash of fear passed through He Bingxin's eyes.

But Xie Yuanjing gave him no time to recover.

He continued very soon, with a touch of contempt.

"With only this much ability, you think you can enter the Marquis's household?"

"No, I never—"

"At this rate, you will never set foot through these doors."

He Bingxin had not expected such bluntness. He was caught off guard, and instinctively moved to explain himself, to beg Xie Yuanjing's understanding once more.

But he had barely twitched the corner of his mouth when he saw Xie Yuanjing's long dark eyes — contempt wrapped in disdain — staring back at him. It was more infuriating than being run through with a blade.

"If I were you, I would first have him acknowledge the name, and then make whatever other plans I wished. Only with that surname would you have the standing to fight me, and the right to claim any of those titles."

"First Young Master Xie has misunderstood — the Marquis's regard for me is simply—"

"Simply out of guilt. Because he will never formally claim you."

chapters.title: Evil Meets Its End
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing cut He Bingxin off with undisguised impatience, yet his lips curved — a faint smile of indeterminate depth.

This was generally how he was with people.

Sometimes cold and distant, sometimes wearing that thin layer of a smile that no one could quite see through.

He Bingxin's colour had visibly worsened by the time Xie Yuanjing finished speaking, and even the false benevolence he habitually maintained had failed to hold.

Xie Yuanjing swept him with a brief, languid look, then lowered his gaze and unhurriedly adjusted his sleeve — his thumb tracing the place Lu Huaixi had just held.

"Do you not understand? From the moment you carried the surname He, he could never acknowledge you. Perhaps he considered bringing you both back to the household — but the name, the identity — never."

"I don't know what the First Young Master is referring to. The Marquis may have misunderstood you because of me this time, but all of it was someone else's scheming — both the Marquis and I were used."

He Bingxin spoke quickly, as though concealing something, his words coming in a rush.

"I know this time the First Young Master has been wronged — caught up in something not of your own making. But the First Young Master should not use these baseless rumours to stir discord between me and the Marquis—"

"You may keep pretending not to understand. But I have no interest in fighting someone with so little to offer. Even now that you have a post and made yourself known in the capital, you are nothing to me. However, I am willing to give you an opportunity."

Xie Yuanjing spoke with complete calm, without hurry.

"I will be moving out of the Marquis's household soon. If you can manage to have him acknowledge you, that will be your best chance to become a recognised son of this household — perhaps even to take my place. You could even contend for my duties, since I am currently 'gravely injured' and in need of recovery."

"First Young Master Xie, I truly had no other intentions. I came today only to offer my apologies."

"As you like."

Xie Yuanjing finally lifted his eyes to look at him one more time.

Before turning away, the corner of his lips moved, his tone detached. "Next time you come to the Marquis's household, send a card first. Come only after the household's master has given approval. That is basic courtesy. And—"

The bluntness of those words had already drained what colour remained from He Bingxin's face.

Xie Yuanjing paid no attention. His gaze stayed cold and dark.

"I will say it once more. Certain people are not to be coveted. One life is not enough to compensate."

—

After that day, He Bingxin went strangely quiet for several days.

Not a single rumour circulated about his visit to the Xie household. What did surface was news that Senior Official Xun had suddenly submitted a memorial, requesting the Emperor once again permit He Bingxin to leave the city and assist with a bandit suppression campaign — so as to make amends through merit.

The place he was being sent to was precisely where Xie Yuanjing had previously been assigned before his injury had prevented him from going.

Lu Huaixi knew that Xie Yuanjing had it all in hand.

She had never asked about any of these matters. These past days she had simply poured herself into furnishing the new residence, going in and out frequently.

Today was no different. Early that morning, Lu Huaixi had gone to the eastern market.

The streets were lively and crowded, and the carriage could not be brought too close — it was left at a spot near the market entrance.

Lu Huaixi stepped down, mentally reviewing the items she had decided last night to look for, and surveyed the shops ahead, deliberating which to enter first.

Just then, a pastry shop nearby was putting out its wares.

Beside the delicate little cakes and pastries sat preserved fruits and candied sweets, and beyond those, a stand selling chilled lychee drink.

Lu Huaixi went over and took a few portions. When she looked up again, she noticed several figures moving in her direction not far away.

At first she paid them no mind, but a moment later she heard a sound and — out of the corner of her eye — caught a thin and familiar silhouette.

"What terrible luck. Making all that fuss over nothing, as if wanting to die, and then of all things someone goes and rescues her — now the whole city knows. What a spectacle."

"All right, she's alive, let it go. Just hurry up and get her fitted with everything she needs. Once she's in the sedan chair, we won't have to look at that wretched face of hers anymore."

What followed the scolding was a string of apologies, low-voiced and deferential.

Once, Lu Huaixi would have been unable to stand by. She would have gone over, called out, stepped in to defend her.

But now she only reached out to take the lychee drink, and after one brief moment of eye contact with the person being berated — turned away expressionlessly and left.

The look on Wu Wenlian's face moved from startled to frightened to utterly grey — and it happened in an instant.

Her lips moved, and the word "Huaixi" rose to the edge of her tongue, only to stop there, held back by the terror left from the day she had been dragged away.

Those who had taken her had come close to cutting out her tongue. They had also almost truly strangled her with a white silk cord.

But in the end, someone had left her with a breath of life and thrown her back at the Wu family's doorstep.

What came back with her was the story: that she had been humiliated by Lu Tangshu, forced to kneel and beg in front of others, and in her grief and rage had attempted to end her own life.

The Wu family felt their face had been lost, yet did not dare truly confront the second branch of the Lu family.

After shutting the doors and giving Wu Wenlian a thorough beating, they had married her off as a concubine to a sixth-rank official who was about to leave the capital.

Not only was returning to the capital unlikely hereafter — a woman who had been the subject of this kind of gossip and was going into a household as a concubine might not even survive that inner courtyard.

Lu Huaixi did not glance back. She had no inclination even to learn what had become of her.

Yaoxu's gaze did linger on Wu Wenlian for a moment, but her eyes were full of undisguised revulsion.

"No wonder those women just now were saying she looks dreadful."

Yaoxu withdrew her gaze and turned to Lu Huaixi. "Her complexion is a sickly yellow, she's bone-thin, her eyes look like they're about to pop out of her head, and her clothes are worse than when she first appeared."

Lu Huaixi said nothing, but she did not stop Yaoxu either.

"This is what she deserves. Evil does meet its end. Though this servant does not believe for one moment that she genuinely tried to take her own life — a woman like her is far more likely to be the one making others' lives miserable."

Lu Huaixi ate a piece of candied fruit and strolled along the edge of the market, not a care for the etiquette her nurses had drilled into her about proper behaviour outside.

Only after Yaoxu had finished did she pass over what she had in her hand, meeting the other woman's gaze — sharp words, but still edged with a faint lingering concern.

"Exactly so — evil does meet its end."

Lu Huaixi smiled, with no sign of being affected.

She even kindly added: "People like that — there's no point talking about them. It ruins the taste of everything."

"The Young Mistress is right. It was this servant's fault for bringing up such unpleasant business. This servant will not mention it again."

Yaoxu exhaled in complete relief.

The words had barely landed when someone called out Lu Huaixi's name from behind.

The group turned. There was Lu Huaixi's elder brother Lu Yuanzhao — and beside him, Zhou Jieyu.

"What are you doing out here? Even after getting married you're always running around outside."

Lu Huaixi heard this and immediately fixed him with a glare.

"Who said a married woman has to stay in the inner courtyard? When you eventually take a sister-in-law, I will personally make sure she talks some sense into that insufferable way of thinking of yours."

Lu Yuanzhao was taken aback, then laughed in exasperation. "Please. Your future sister-in-law will be far more sensible than you, without me having to say a word — she'll be content looking after things inside, unlike you—"

"What's wrong with me? I happen to be doing wonderfully. If anything, I feel deeply sorry for my future sister-in-law, having to deal with someone as rigid and unfeeling as you."

"You have the nerve — now that you're married you've gotten bolder, have you? Openly criticising your own elder brother to his face — all right, Lu Huaixi, I see how it is."

Lu Yuanzhao reached out to rap Lu Huaixi on the head, but she ducked away before he could.

He was about to move to pin her down when Zhou Jieyu beside him gave a quiet laugh, then extended a hand to stop him.

"Lu second daughter is not wrong."

"Brother Zhou, why are you taking this little troublemaker's side?"

Lu Yuanzhao pulled a face. "You don't know her — she is completely unmanageable in private. Always has been, even back at home. And now she dares lecture her own elder brother in the middle of the street."

Zhou Jieyu listened, then looked up and met Lu Huaixi's gaze.

His expression paused for a brief moment, and then he smiled again, warm and even-tempered.

"Even so, Yuanzhao was the one in the wrong first."

He said: "It is true that women are expected to manage the household, but they also have the right to go out and move through the world. There is no hierarchy in that. Yuanzhao should not have said what he said."

"Exactly."

Lu Huaixi felt the vindication and narrowed her eyes further in satisfaction.

She gave Lu Yuanzhao a disdainful huff, then looked back at Zhou Jieyu.

"Don't mind him. Where is Brother Zhou headed? How did you end up with such a tiresome junior?"

"I am going to the Lu residence — to pay my respects to Master Lu."

Having said this, Zhou Jieyu paused, letting her surprise settle, before asking in a gentle voice: "Would the second daughter of the Lu family like to come along? It would be a convenient opportunity to visit."

chapters.title: He Treats Me Very Well
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi naturally wanted to go back to the Lu residence.

The last time she had visited was when she went to deal with the second branch.

After that, she had been preoccupied with Xie Yuanjing's injury, and then with Shun'an Fang, and then with the new residence — there had been almost no time left over.

It was only these past few days, now that Xie Yuanjing had begun to be busy again, spending his days behind closed doors somewhere other than the household, that she had found a little room to go out and take care of things.

Although, she realised, she and Xie Yuanjing had not really talked properly in quite a few days.

Even though the two of them were sleeping under the same roof now, at night she would either fall asleep the moment she lay down, or Xie Yuanjing would come back visibly exhausted — enough that she could not bring herself to bother him.

Xie Yuanjing had perhaps noticed that he had been pushing himself too hard lately, because today when he left he had specifically made plans with her to eat dinner together.

"I suppose I won't, then. I still have things to buy."

Lu Huaixi was somewhat torn.

Going to the Lu residence would still leave her time enough to get back. But if she went, the things she had planned to get today would have to wait until tomorrow.

Beside her, Lu Yuanzhao saw her expression and couldn't resist making fun of her.

"So much for all that swagger — turns out you can't even go back to your own family without permission. Fine, don't come, that's fine with me. I'll have Brother Zhou all to myself over a good drink. No one to bother us."

He grinned. "And I want you to know — this is the finest wine, from a place you can't just go and buy it at any market. I was planning to bury a few jars in your courtyard. Keep them hidden and drink them whenever I felt like it."

Lu Huaixi was not easily baited into things. But the way Lu Yuanzhao said it did make her heart itch, and she found herself more inclined to go after all.

"When are you leaving?"

"What do you care — later, probably."

Lu Huaixi ran a quick calculation in her head, blinked, decided there was probably time for a quick visit, and fell into step behind Lu Yuanzhao.

"Oh — changed your mind?"

"Stop talking so much. Are we going or not?"

Watching the siblings at it again, Zhou Jieyu held a quiet smile and said nothing.

The street was considerably more crowded than when they had arrived. Stalls were not permitted here, so most trade came from the shops themselves, but with people flowing back and forth it was still lively and full of life.

Lu Huaixi had her head tilted to the side.

She was bickering with her brother and walking at the same time, and very nearly collided with someone — only Zhou Jieyu's quick reflexes and a steadying hand saved her from the impact.

She gave Zhou Jieyu a grateful smile, not noticing that he had seamlessly moved to walk on the outside, shielding her from the flow of pedestrians — and in doing so, closing the distance between them.

At first Lu Huaixi noticed nothing. But when she saw a few passers-by glancing over, she began to feel slightly uncomfortable.

She was just thinking that she ought to move on ahead, when she heard Zhou Jieyu speak to her.

"How is First Young Master Xie's injury now?"

At the mention of Xie Yuanjing, her attention shifted immediately.

She gave a small nod. "It is better, but he still has to take care. He cannot walk for too long, cannot use force, cannot exert himself too much."

Xie Yuanjing, of course, had been doing as he liked regardless — but Lu Huaixi was sticking to the official version.

Zhou Jieyu did not ask for details. He only spoke with a note of apology. "I was away from the capital during that time, and was not able to offer any help."

"Brother Zhou, please don't say that — even if you had been here, there would have been nothing you could have done."

"At least there are certain private matters I could have lent a hand with."

"It was truly all right. I did not even ask my father for help — and he did not ask for it either."

Lu Huaixi smiled. "Besides, Xianya sent me a letter at the time, and she asked whether I needed her help. I genuinely felt it wasn't necessary. As long as he came out of the palace and was standing in front of me, I was not so afraid."

Zhou Jieyu acknowledged this with a sound, and did not follow up on it. A brief silence fell.

After a moment, he lifted his eyes to look somewhere in the distance, as though making casual conversation the way an elder brother might.

"So all this time, you have been caring for him yourself?"

"Not really — I was just there. Other people came to apply the medicines. I only helped occasionally."

"Even so, that must have been tiring." Zhou Jieyu said, his tone not quite as composed as before.

Lu Yuanzhao, hearing this, leaned over.

"Oh, don't even start." He cut straight in, without noticing the expression on the person beside him.

"Mother told me everything. She said you sat up through the night, night after night — until Lady Xie grew worried about you specifically, and had someone send word to Mother asking her to come and talk some sense into you."

Lu Huaixi's lips moved, wanting to push back on this, but the words would not come.

She also did not want to say too much in front of other people. She settled for giving her brother a sharp look.

Lu Yuanzhao, completely unbothered, grinned again. "That mother-in-law of yours is quite something — personally writing to your mother's family. Afraid that persuading you herself would not be enough. I have never seen anything like it."

"How many people's mothers-in-law have you seen? Of course it is the first time."

Lu Huaixi replied without patience.

Lady Xie's reason for writing had been twofold: she could not persuade her, and after learning that their marriage was not a true one, she had not known how to approach the subject.

Saying too much would be overstepping. Too little would accomplish nothing.

After thinking it through at length, she had settled on reaching out to her mother.

But she had phrased things delicately, with no mention of anything connected to the nature of their marriage.

Zhou Jieyu's expression throughout had not changed much — but it was plain that the ease he had shown a moment ago was no longer there.

Lu Huaixi had no wish to keep talking about the Marquis's household, and was about to change the subject when Zhou Jieyu, who had been quiet for a while, spoke again.

"To have you look after him so attentively — it seems Xie the First Young Master treats you very well."

Lu Huaixi paused.

It was a thing she had heard said before.

She did not deflect, and felt no need for awkwardness. She nodded openly. "Yes. He treats me very well."

The conversation came to a natural end after those words.

Though Lu Yuanzhao had been running his mouth, hearing his sister say something like that with such seriousness was enough to genuinely reassure him. He did not tease her again.

The group returned to the Lu residence soon after.

Master Lu had official business and would be back late. Zhou Jieyu went first to pay his respects to the Lu patriarch.

Lu Huaixi, naturally, went to her mother's quarters, where they talked at length.

She planned to stay for the midday meal and then leave, so she could still go and pick out a few things, and be back in time to wait for Xie Yuanjing.

Lady Liu was delighted at the prospect of a family meal, and since Zhou Jieyu was also being kept to eat, Lu Huaixi thought about it briefly and did not go to join that side of the table.

Midway through the meal, Lu Yuanzhao came over with a cup of wine — a very small cup, barely three-quarters full.

"Here, just a sip."

Lu Yuanzhao had clearly already had enough and his eyes were going red.

Lady Liu was preparing to say something reproving, but she watched as Lu Huaixi immediately took the cup and raised it to her nose for a sniff.

"It smells wonderful."

"Tastes even better."

Lu Yuanzhao unwisely said this, but retained just enough sense to add quickly, before Lady Liu could scold them: "Don't actually drink it — I was just letting you smell it."

He hiccupped, then got back to the point in a somewhat disjointed way.

"This wine is the absolute finest. Father told me to save a jar — says that since you invited Elder Zeng to the Marquis's household, you should take it back and have someone bring it to him, as thanks for making the trip."

"It is really that good?"

Lu Huaixi looked down at the cup.

If even her father was saying to bring it as a gift, it must truly be something that money alone could not easily obtain.

She was not someone who regularly sought out wine, but occasionally she had a craving.

When something like this was placed right in front of her, she was naturally not going to just look at it and put it back.

With that thought settled, Lu Huaixi promptly raised the cup and drank.

By the time Lady Liu could say anything, she had already taken a sip, pressed her lips together in appreciation, and proceeded to drink the rest clean.

When the dizziness had started, Lu Huaixi could no longer say.

She only remembered her mother alternately lecturing her and scolding Lu Yuanzhao, and herself laughing away and eating a great many things.

Eventually Zhou Jieyu seemed to have come as well, brought something, and asked if she was all right.

Lu Huaixi had said yes, naturally. Only — when she tried to stand up, she pitched forward and went down.

chapters.title: I Did Send a Portrait Once
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing returned to the manor a little earlier than he had promised.

He had bought some of the snacks Lu Huaixi loved — things he didn't usually let her have too much of — along with a few trinkets that had come in from outside.

Shen Zhoushu teased him again about raising a child. Xie Yuanjing smiled and said nothing.

Let him say what he liked. She was his person — of course he was going to keep taking care of her, for as long as it took.

When he entered the room, he saw the new dress that had arrived from Shun'an Fang spread open across the bed, as though Lu Huaixi had looked it over and hadn't asked anyone to put it away.

Xie Yuanjing looked it over. His gaze settled on the waist.

The dress appeared to have been made for dancing — it was different from her everyday clothes.

Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed slightly, but then he recalled the feeling of his hand resting against her waist on those nights when she had rolled into his arms in her sleep.

The darkness in his eyes deepened. He also suddenly remembered that a few days ago, when Princess Qinghe had come out of the palace to visit her, he had heard Lu Huaixi mention she had learned a new dance and offered to show it to the princess to see if she'd like to learn it.

At the time, Xie Yuanjing had thought to himself: he had never seen Lu Huaixi dance.

He wanted to see it. He wanted to see it first. Ideally, he would be the only one who ever got to see it.

After a while, Gong Zhuo called from outside, asking when he'd like dinner served, and whether he should bring a bowl of soup first so he could take his medicine.

Xie Yuanjing didn't respond.

He told the servants to bring the medicine directly, saying he would wait for Lu Huaixi to return before eating together.

But by the time the dinner hour had passed, and even as dusk crept in, the person who had promised to return was still nowhere to be seen.

Only then did Xie Yuanjing know for certain — Lu Huaixi had broken her word.

—

Lu Huaixi woke from a nap.

She came to her senses slowly, and it took her a long while to grasp just how embarrassing it was that half a cup of wine had knocked her out cold.

She clutched the blanket, unable to believe it.

Outside, the sky still held a trace of light, but candles had already been lit inside the room, making the glow feel dim and amber.

Shortly after, Jing Shuang came in carrying a bowl, with Yao Xu following behind, setting a basin of hot water on the stand.

"Does your head hurt, young mistress? This is a hangover remedy — drink a little and you'll feel better."

Lu Huaixi didn't feel a headache, but she took the bowl obediently and drank it down.

Come to think of it, this was the first time she had ever gotten this drunk — and drunk so quickly at that.

But it was also the first time that after drinking too much, she hadn't felt the least bit wretched.

Good wine truly was good wine. She would have to ask Lu Yuanzhao for another jar to bring back for Xie Yuanjing.

A face surfaced in her mind at once. Lu Huaixi immediately sat up in bed, swinging her legs over the side without even stopping to put on her shoes, her bare feet landing straight on the floor.

"What time is it now?"

"To answer you, young mistress — it is already the hour of You."

Hearing that the time they had agreed upon had already passed, Lu Huaixi paused for a brief moment, and then a flicker of urgency crossed her eyes.

"Did anyone send word to the manor? Has Xie Yuanjing come looking for me?"

"When you sat down to eat, you said there was no need to let the young master know — you didn't want him to go out of his way around to come pick you up. So we didn't send word. Then when you fainted from the wine, your servant and Yao Xu were busy wiping you down the whole time and didn't think to ask about the young master."

Jing Shuang took the bowl from Lu Huaixi's hands, and seeing the worry on her face, quickly added:

"The young master most likely already knows you've come to the Lu estate. I'll go send word right now."

"Never mind, it's this late — I might as well just go back myself."

Lu Huaixi got up.

When she thought it over, she figured Xie Yuanjing could probably guess she had come back to the Lu estate. But remembering that the two of them had barely had a proper moment together in the past several days, her movements as she changed her clothes grew even more hurried.

She stepped out of the room. The sky outside still held a faint brightness.

Lu Huaixi went to see her mother first, and learning that her father was still in the front hall, she hurried over to pay her respects there as well.

The carriage was waiting outside before long. She didn't delay any further and made her way toward the main gate.

She was missing Xie Yuanjing. She also wanted to have him smell that wine — she wanted to know if he thought it was as wonderfully fragrant as she did.

As she was thinking this, someone called out to her from behind.

Lu Huaixi was walking along the stone path, some distance from the lantern-lit covered walkway, while the person who had called her stood right beneath the light.

At the same moment, a figure paused outside the main gate.

The shadow cast by the newcomer stretched long across the ground, not quite distinct in the dimness, and soon dissolved into the surrounding dark.

"Miss Lu Huaixi."

Zhou Jieyu had changed how he addressed her.

He stepped down from the veranda and walked toward her, one step at a time. The wind carried waves of wine from his clothes, yet his expression remained composed — not the slightest sign of drunken disarray.

"Elder Brother Zhou."

Seeing that it was him, Lu Huaixi stopped walking. A flash of surprise crossed her face, as though she hadn't expected Zhou Jieyu to still be here at this hour.

He caught her puzzled look and explained with a smile: "I had a bit too much with your brother, so your father suggested I rest here for the afternoon."

"Ah, I see."

Lu Huaixi nodded and glanced past him. "My brother actually left Elder Brother Zhou here alone — I'll have Father give him a talking-to."

"I came over on my own."

Zhou Jieyu looked at her and said: "I heard from a maid that you were about to leave. I just remembered there's something I've been meaning to ask — so I thought I'd come and catch you."

Lu Huaixi lifted her gaze slightly.

The surroundings were dim, but her eyes remained bright and clear, the kind of eyes one could fall into with a single glance.

She seemed to hesitate for a moment, yet still kept her expression agreeable.

"Go ahead and ask, Elder Brother Zhou. Though — are you sure you've sobered up?"

"I have."

After saying this, Zhou Jieyu was quiet for a beat.

Whether to ask, what asking would accomplish, what would come of it — none of that he knew.

Perhaps he didn't need to know.

Compared to other possibilities, this — simply being in each other's lives like this — was already quite good.

But just now, something Yuanzhao had let slip while they were drinking had unsettled something in him.

He had said: how did he never get to see that portrait of his at the time?

Zhou Jieyu had never quite believed that Lu Huaixi and Xie Yuanjing had any real prior engagement. Others might not have known, but he had been waiting for Lu Huaixi to come of age — he couldn't not have known.

So he had made his quiet approaches, his subtle tests.

But in the end, seeing that she truly seemed to be living well, he had thought — perhaps there was no longer any need for him to dwell on it. And so he had let it go.

Yet this recent incident with Xie Yuanjing had set those buried thoughts spreading again.

The Marquis's estate as it stood now was no place for her.

And Xie Yuanjing — cold-blooded, ruthless, and full of hidden schemes — was no match for her either.

If he wasn't suited for her, did that mean there was still room for him to try?

"Elder Brother Zhou?"

Lu Huaixi's voice came again, carrying a faint, barely perceptible urgency.

Zhou Jieyu came back to himself. His gaze returned to the face before him.

"It's nothing of great importance."

He smiled casually, his expression mild.

"I just suddenly remembered — I once sent you a portrait, but I don't think I ever heard you mention it. So I wanted to ask — was it because I'm Xianya's elder brother, and I seem too stern and dull, that you found me less than satisfactory?"

chapters.title: In That Case, Xie Yuanjing Is Still the Best
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi was taken aback. She doubted her own ears, wondering if she had heard him wrong.

Had it been anyone else, she might have suspected an ulterior motive.

Or perhaps teasing, with ill intent behind it.

But this was Zhou Xianya's elder brother — someone she thought of as half a brother herself.

The eldest son of the Zhou family had always been a man of integrity and open character, and the Zhou family itself had always been upright — never fawning, never clinging to power, conducting themselves with honest dignity.

"You — sent me — a portrait?"

It took a long moment before Lu Huaixi managed to squeeze out the words, the disbelief written plainly across her face.

But she quickly found her footing on her own.

She trusted Zhou Xianya far too much to suspect anything. Coming back to herself, she thought only that Zhou Jieyu was a true gentleman — if he was asking this, he must genuinely be curious, nothing more.

"Twice."

Zhou Jieyu's voice was gentle, as though he were making casual conversation.

He didn't say when, and he didn't ask about her and Xie Yuanjing. He simply mentioned it lightly, in passing.

"I assumed you already knew."

"Then perhaps... something went wrong along the way."

Lu Huaixi thought for a moment, without a trace of any hidden meaning, and said plainly: "I never saw Elder Brother Zhou's portrait."

The question Zhou Jieyu had been holding back — "If you had seen it, would you have considered it?" — stopped on the tip of his tongue.

Looking at her clear, unguarded eyes, the way she smiled at him with the same open ease that Xianya had when she looked at him, the last thread of his wine-hazed thoughts finally unraveled.

"I see. I had thought perhaps I wasn't satisfactory — or that Xianya had told you I was dull and uninteresting in private, and that it had made me seem unremarkable."

"No — Xianya has never said a bad word about Elder Brother Zhou. She's never called you stuffy either. And I don't think so either."

"Is that so?"

"It is."

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Elder Brother Zhou is a good person. I've always known that."

Those words were spoken with unmistakable sincerity.

Zhou Jieyu could hear it. And so could the person standing outside the main gate.

He could even picture the expression on Lu Huaixi's face as she said it — her pretty eyes narrowed just slightly, like a crescent moon reflected in a still lake.

The figure outside lingered a moment longer.

But in the end, he did not step over that threshold. Instead, unlike before, he turned and walked away from the Lu estate.

Lu Huaixi didn't hear the movement on that side. She had only just finished replying to Zhou Jieyu when something else suddenly occurred to her.

No matter how close she and Zhou Xianya were, the secret between her and Xie Yuanjing could not be revealed to anyone else.

With that in mind, Lu Huaixi took the initiative and added one more thing.

"I imagine Elder Brother Zhou must have been nudged into it by Xianya back then. That's my fault — I never mentioned that I actually had a prior engagement."

She curved her lips, entirely without embarrassment, and said with a light smile: "So Elder Brother Zhou can rest easy. It isn't that you're not good enough — you're exceptionally good."

"Compared to Xie Yuanjing?"

He couldn't hold it back in the end, and let that slip.

Zhou Jieyu felt a twinge of shame even as the words left his mouth — yet after they fell, his heart climbed into his throat.

Whatever the reply, he told himself — even if she hesitated for just a moment — that would be enough to satisfy him.

But Lu Huaixi suddenly lowered her gaze. Into the clarity of her smile crept a faint girlish shyness — fleeting, gone almost as quickly as it came, yet even in its passing, that gentle tenderness still pierced something in Zhou Jieyu.

Lu Huaixi didn't know this. She only smiled with great warmth and openness, speaking that person's name with the kind of ease that left nothing hidden.

"Well, of course Xie Yuanjing is still the best. Elder Brother Zhou will have to ask someone else."

Zhou Jieyu smiled in the end as well.

His smile was quiet — and seemed to carry within it a layer of quiet sorrow.

A feeling so faint that Lu Huaixi couldn't feel it.

At last, Zhou Jieyu seemed to think of something. He glanced toward the distance, then looked back.

"Just now, outside the main gate — it looked as though someone had come."

Lu Huaixi turned to look, but the space she could see was empty, with no trace of anyone having been there.

"I'll have someone ask around later and find out who it was."

"Go on, then. It was probably someone looking for you."

"Looking for me?"

Zhou Jieyu nodded, a flash of self-mockery and contempt crossing his own eyes.

"I caught a glimpse of a figure just now — but not clearly enough, and he left so quickly, I didn't say anything at the time. But then I suddenly remembered — that figure looked rather like Xie Yuanjing."

Lu Huaixi froze.

Learning that Xie Yuanjing might have come, she could no longer hide the urgency on her face. It came alive all at once.

Yet she was also a little uncertain.

Xie Yuanjing hadn't come inside — that didn't seem like something he would do.

Lu Huaixi had no time to stand on ceremony. She gave Zhou Jieyu a quick wave and was already turning away.

"Elder Brother Zhou, I have to go — tell Xianya I'll invite her out to hear music next time!"

The last word had barely fallen before she was already hurrying out.

Zhou Jieyu watched her go, eyes following the sweep of her hem until it disappeared from view entirely.

—

Lu Huaixi did not find Xie Yuanjing.

He had indeed been there, but by now he was no longer outside the gate.

Lu Huaixi belatedly realized he was truly angry — yet she couldn't understand why, if he had already come to take her home, he had left without a moment's pause.

Jing Shuang stepped forward to console her, saying the young master must have had something sudden come up.

Yao Xu agreed, saying that since the young master had come at all, he clearly knew she had been drinking and would never have simply walked away for no reason.

But Lu Huaixi knew none of this was true.

He was simply unhappy.

And that unhappiness was likely about more than just her breaking her promise.

By the time she returned to the Marquis's manor, every part of her attention was fixed on Xie Yuanjing.

She rushed off the carriage, turning over in her mind what she would say to him when she got back — even if he was angry, he couldn't simply refuse to acknowledge her.

If the fault was hers, she would explain herself. He was allowed to be angry — but he couldn't just vanish without a trace.

Lu Huaixi moved quickly, walking fast enough that her breathing grew slightly unsteady.

Before long, the courtyard came into view.

But before she could get close, she suddenly caught sight of Xie Yuanjing's figure beneath the courtyard wall.

His back was to her. Lu Huaixi couldn't see his expression — but she could see Mu Nianwei kneeling beside him, both hands clutching the hem of his robe, her face streaked with tears.

Lu Huaixi's steps came to a stop.

It was the first time she had ever seen anyone touch Xie Yuanjing like this. And the first time she had seen him allow Mu Nianwei to come so close.

The scene before her didn't look pleasant by any measure — yet the sight of Mu Nianwei sobbing and trembling, so fragile, so helpless, her fingers clenched tight around his robe, filled Lu Huaixi with a sharp, clean anger.

Jing Shuang had also spotted the scene ahead. Without waiting for Lu Huaixi's instruction, she went to find someone to ask.

Lu Huaixi recognized that person — she often brought news to Yao Xu.

"I don't know what happened exactly, but this cousin young miss tried to take her own life. She even had the white silk around her neck. The old madam had someone plead with the young master to come back and speak to her."

The servant kept her voice low.

"All I know is that not long after word was sent out, the young master came back right away. Everyone in the manor was shocked. From what I gather, after a few words were exchanged, this cousin young miss stopped trying to harm herself — but then for some reason, she suddenly ran out to block the young master's path and said... said she wanted to be his."

Jing Shuang glanced at Lu Huaixi, who hadn't said a word, and pressed her lips together. After a long moment she told the servant to step back.

Ordinarily, even if Mu Nianwei had come to make a scene, she shouldn't have been able to get anywhere near him.

And beyond that, Jing Shuang now realized — the young master hadn't left earlier because of official business, but because of another woman.

Jing Shuang didn't know what to say.

Her face held a tangle of conflicting emotions — distress, helplessness, and uncertainty — and she was still trying to work out what words to squeeze out, when she saw the young mistress, who had been standing still, lift her feet and walk forward again.

To enter the courtyard, she would have to pass by that spot. Lu Huaixi had no intention of going around it, nor of pretending it wasn't there.

She would find out why Xie Yuanjing had come back.

If she was in the wrong, she would apologize and make it up to him. But if it was because of Mu Nianwei — then she would not be getting along with him again so easily.

Xie Yuanjing heard the movement quickly. He turned, and his eyes met Lu Huaixi's directly.

"You went to the Lu estate?"

"Yes."

"Then why didn't you wait for me — was it because—"

"Something came up suddenly."

The question was cut off before she could finish.

Her apology died on her lips as well — as though someone had pushed it right back in.

Neither of them spoke again. Beside them, Mu Nianwei gave a slight tremor and tightened her grip on Xie Yuanjing's robe.

Only then did Lu Huaixi lower her eyes to look.

She had been about to say something, but after that glance, she changed her mind.

If Xie Yuanjing hadn't allowed it, she couldn't have touched even the hem of his robe.

With that thought, she suddenly let out a quiet laugh and walked straight past them both.

Xie Yuanjing did not follow. Lu Huaixi heard no further sound from that direction.

It was only after she had entered the courtyard and put some distance between herself and that scene that she finally heard Mu Nianwei's voice break loose in a cry.

"Cousin — you do care about me. I know you do!"

chapters.title: Cold War
chapters.content:
Back in the room, the dress from Shun'an Fang was still spread out where it had been left.

Lu Huaixi hadn't put it away before she went out — she had been thinking it could stand another alteration or two, though she hadn't decided what yet.

Looking at it now, she felt no interest in it at all. She told Yao Xu to put it away.

"Have someone prepare water. I want to bathe."

"Yes, young mistress. And dinner?"

"It's already this late. Don't bother."

Lu Huaixi waved her hand and turned around, her gaze landing on the jar of wine that had been brought up. She paused.

"Set one jar aside and have it buried somewhere. Put the rest away safely — I'll bring it to the old man tomorrow."

Because of Xie Yuanjing's injury, she had kept putting off going up the mountain. Now that he was recovering so quickly and no longer needed her watching over him, she might as well spend a few days up there and get those seedlings she had planted the other day transplanted properly into the ground.

Yao Xu startled slightly at that.

Her eyes instinctively went to Jing Shuang, wondering whether she should ask if any of the wine ought to be set aside for the young master as well.

But Jing Shuang gave a small, quiet shake of her head — this was not the moment to bring that up.

Yao Xu caught the look and held her tongue, murmured her acknowledgment, and retreated from the room.

—

Xie Yuanjing did not come back to the room.

Earlier, his feet had moved almost on instinct to follow Lu Huaixi's retreating figure.

But he had stopped himself cold almost immediately, doing nothing but stare after her as she walked away.

Once the matter was dealt with, Xie Yuanjing went to find Shen Zhoushu and sat down without a word, pouring himself a drink.

Shen Zhoushu's tone shifted from teasing to serious, and when he finally realized something was genuinely wrong, he forced the wine out of reach.

"Are you out of your mind? Your wound isn't even fully healed and you're drinking like this — maybe you're not scared, but I am!"

"What are you scared of? I'm not going to give you any trouble."

"You won't, but that little girl of yours will! She looks soft and delicate, but when she gets angry she's something else — she'll come smash up my room, and I won't even be able to fight back!"

Hearing Shen Zhoushu bring up Lu Huaixi, Xie Yuanjing fell quiet.

He didn't push for the wine again either, just sat there and let Shen Zhoushu talk.

Before long, Shen Zhoushu finally pinpointed what was off. He paused, then asked with some hesitation:

"You and that little girl... have you two fallen out?"

That seemed to bring Xie Yuanjing back to life a little. He looked up.

Shen Zhoushu immediately took it back, saying offhandedly: "Right, right, never — you'd sooner fall out with me than with her. So what's actually going on?"

Xie Yuanjing still said nothing.

What was going on — he didn't know either.

He was new to matters of the heart, just beginning to feel his way through something like love, and he was studious in it but also stubborn.

If it were anyone else, he would never have given them a second glance.

But if the person Lu Huaixi had ever thought of was Zhou Jieyu — then he would find himself wondering where he stood in comparison.

Especially now.

The Marquis's manor had nothing to offer Lu Huaixi, and neither did he.

These past days, she always seemed tired around him — there was so much to manage every day, and each night she fell asleep the moment she lay down.

It felt like a long time since they had talked properly. It had been days since he had seen her smile that easy, unbothered smile.

And then today — she had gone back to the Lu estate on her own. She had eaten, and had wine, and spent time with Zhou Jieyu.

She had forgotten the time they had agreed upon. She had even been on her way out the door when he heard Zhou Jieyu say what amounted to a declaration of feeling.

He hadn't been able to see Lu Huaixi's expression, but from her voice he could tell — she was surprised, yet throughout she had been nothing but open and warm.

So what did that make him — the villain who had barged in and ruined something that might have been mutual?

Xie Yuanjing didn't know. He was unsettled.

Every instinct in him — the deep-seated dominance, the fierce possessiveness — roared at him to go and take her back.

Yet in that moment, the memory of the night on the lake surfaced: the things Lu Huaixi had said to him when she was drunk held him back, kept him from stepping through that gate.

She had said Zhou Jieyu was wonderful. She had said that if his portrait had been among the ones she'd seen, she would have agreed.

Those words had been drawn out by Xie Yuanjing himself — deliberately asked. But the answer had been Lu Huaixi's honest truth.

She had once been willing to marry into the Zhou family. She had once been willing to marry Zhou Jieyu.

And even now, she had never acknowledged him openly in front of the Lu family.

"Can you say something?"

Shen Zhoushu had run out of patience and pressed again.

After a long pause, just as Shen Zhoushu had nearly given up expecting a reply, Xie Yuanjing spoke at last: "What do you think of Zhou Jieyu?"

"That eldest son of the Zhou family?"

Shen Zhoushu answered without thinking:

"Outstanding, honestly. His conduct, his learning — both exceptional. And his appearance is no eyesore either. Among the young men of the capital, he is no less impressive than you."

"Is that so."

Xie Yuanjing replied flatly.

Good. Lu Huaixi thought so too.

"What on earth happened between you two? You're not yourself right now."

"Nothing."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his eyes.

He wasn't himself. That was true enough.

But no matter how exceptional Zhou Jieyu might be, he had no intention of letting him near Lu Huaixi again.

He would give her one night. After tonight, he would not allow her to think of Zhou Jieyu — and he would certainly not allow that man any further quiet moments alone with her.

Xie Yuanjing returned to the manor at first light.

Not wanting to wake Lu Huaixi, he went straight to the bathhouse to wash up and have his wound dressed.

As he was getting dressed, Gong Zhuo came in — drooping eyes, a troubled look on his face.

Xie Yuanjing didn't notice. His thoughts were entirely on Lu Huaixi. It wasn't until he went back to the room that he realized there was no one there.

Gong Zhuo had been bottling things up and finally found his moment. He rushed to report:

"Master — the young mistress paid her respects to the first madam early this morning and then went up the mountain."

He was quietly indignant on the young mistress's behalf, though he didn't dare let it show too plainly.

"The young mistress looked very low in spirits. She didn't say how long she'd be gone, and she didn't ask about where you'd spent the night. She packed her things and left without taking any of your people."

Xie Yuanjing's lips pressed into a thin line. Something clenched in his chest. He turned and walked straight out of the room.

—

Lu Huaixi didn't particularly enjoy climbing mountains, but she refused to let the old man show her up — she wasn't about to hear him say her legs were weaker than his.

Thankfully the mountain wasn't too steep and not overly tall. She walked at a leisurely pace with a few breaks, and before long she could see the old man's bamboo-fenced courtyard on the hillside.

Just beside it ran a small stream, trickling out from between the rocks, deep enough in the gentler slope to make a pleasant sound.

Beyond that were stands of trees and bamboo, lush and green, swaying in the breeze — cool and refreshing.

Lu Huaixi felt a chill from standing in the wind too long, and headed inside.

The old man was feeding the chickens. Lu Huaixi eyed those sharp beaks warily and waited deliberately until he was done before calling out to him.

He turned at the sound, not particularly surprised — but clearly sulking about something.

"So you do remember this stinky old man, do you?"

He gave a light huff, then set down what he'd been holding.

But stepping closer and seeing the faint puffiness around Lu Huaixi's eyes, his tone shifted. He feigned gruffness: "Didn't sleep well, and you come running to me? Think that gets you out of doing any work?"

This time Lu Huaixi didn't talk back.

She had neither the mood nor the energy — climbing up here had genuinely worn her out.

All she wanted was to go inside and sit down with a cup of tea.

"I'm hungry."

"What does that mean? You want this old man to cook for you?"

"No. I brought a cook."

Lu Huaixi shook her head, her gaze drifting to the chickens the old man had just finished feeding.

chapters.title: What Do You Take Me For?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi didn't usually eat chicken legs at home.

The kitchen staff would strip off the tender meat and arrange it neatly for her so she could pick it up easily with her chopsticks.

But up on the mountain, she found that eating it straight from the bone tasted far better.

Ignoring the old man's glowering, she gnawed at it carefully and thoroughly.

By the time Lu Huaixi had eaten her fill, the chickens had lost the nerve to show themselves anywhere near her. Even the ducks beside them had shuffled obediently into a corner of the bamboo-fenced yard.

She patted her stomach and wandered around to the back, decided the ground wasn't right, wandered further out, and found a wider, more open patch of land.

Somewhere nearby, water trickled faintly — not loud, just pleasant enough to be soothing.

Lu Huaixi stood beside the mound of earth, listening to that sound, and idly prodded at the soil that had already been loosened once, dragging a hoe through it.

She had never done any real labor in her life. The only thing she had some practice in was planting flowers, but since growing herbs and growing flowers were much the same, she didn't need to figure it out from scratch.

Lu Huaixi crouched down and, just as she had the last time, dug the holes in rows — one hole, one seedling, moving steadily along.

She didn't need to space them perfectly, but she liked them to line up neatly, and she refused to let anyone else step in.

By the third row and the very last hole, Lu Huaixi was thirsty.

She raised a hand to wipe her forehead — she wasn't sure if it was sweat or a few loose strands of hair — and something about her brow felt itchy.

"Yao Xu, I want water."

Lu Huaixi didn't look up, keeping her eyes on the holes she had dug while calling out for someone.

Before long, a bowl of tea was brought over.

Her hands were dirty with soil, so she didn't reach to take it — she tilted her chin up, ready to drink from the bowl Yao Xu was holding for her.

But the moment she looked up, she found herself looking at Xie Yuanjing, who had not returned the previous night.

Lu Huaixi looked at him for a moment, torn between ignoring him and the very real fact that she was thirsty. After a brief inner struggle, she turned her head away with dignity and chose not to see him.

"Yao Xu!"

She called out again. From inside the small room at some distance away came a reply.

"I want water!"

When Yao Xu came out carrying the bowl and saw the young master standing nearby, she hesitated, not sure whether to step forward.

It was only when Lu Huaixi held out her hand that she placed the bowl into it.

The water was gone in no time.

Yao Xu didn't dare linger and retreated with the empty bowl.

There had still been people keeping watch nearby, but since Xie Yuanjing's arrival, they had all quietly made themselves scarce with an unspoken mutual understanding.

Lu Huaixi still hadn't said anything. She hadn't so much as glanced at him since that first look.

This was also the first time since his injury that she hadn't asked about his wound — as if she had no interest whatsoever in whether climbing this mountain had done him any harm.

It was only when Xie Yuanjing took what was in her hand from her that she finally deigned to look at him again.

But even then, her eyes held no particular feeling — no anger, no displeasure, and no warmth either, none of the fondness he was used to seeing.

Something ached in Xie Yuanjing's chest — a dull, suffocating weight he couldn't name.

"Let me do this."

"I don't need you to."

Lu Huaixi made no move to take anything back, just crouched down and began turning the loose soil over with her hands.

But soon the person beside her crouched down too, and a clean, slender hand closed over hers, keeping it from pressing further into the dirt.

The mountain breeze was cooler than anywhere in the lowlands. A long time in it, and one's fingers began to feel the chill.

When Xie Yuanjing's hand wrapped around hers, the warmth of his palm made her lose her train of thought for a moment.

He was the one who'd been ill, yet somehow it made her feel as though she were the more fragile one.

When Lu Huaixi came back to herself, she tried to pull her hand free, but couldn't.

She couldn't make sense of what this person was doing, couldn't tell what he wanted.

"Can you let me work? I have things to get through."

Her voice held no particular force, but the meaning was clear enough — keep your distance. She didn't want to be near him right now.

But Xie Yuanjing didn't let go.

He looked down at her pale pink fingertips beneath the soil, paying no mind to the dirt on his hands and clothes, and simply held on.

After a long silence, just as Lu Huaixi made another attempt to pull free, he drew her to her feet.

Standing up too quickly made her unsteady. He caught her around the waist and carried her a short distance to a spot not far from the stream, setting her down on a large, flat rock.

That spot had no trees overhead to block the sun. The light was bright and warm — far warmer than in the shade of the trees.

"What exactly do you want?"

Seeing this, Lu Huaixi's irritation finally surfaced. "Weren't you the one with nothing to say to me? Weren't you the one not speaking?"

Yesterday's behavior had made no sense. And then he had been gone the whole night — only to show up today to tease her now that his temper had cooled.

Lu Huaixi frowned, unwilling to be touched.

If the fault was hers, she was willing to admit it. But yesterday, Xie Yuanjing had been more than a little out of line as well.

Thinking of it, a grievance crept up in her chest — her eyes began to sting.

"I don't need you here. I don't want to talk to you right now. If you're upset because I broke my promise yesterday, I'm willing to say I'm sorry — that was wrong of me. But you and that other person, with all your carrying on, and your coldness toward me — that is not my fault."

Lu Huaixi's voice didn't waver much, but it was forthright.

The fact that she could say it out loud meant she genuinely felt wronged, and genuinely believed it wasn't entirely her fault.

Other than not making it back in time, she had no idea what she had done to upset him.

And she had always hated that he said nothing.

"Let go of me—"

"I don't know what to do."

Xie Yuanjing spoke without warning, and Lu Huaixi's struggle stopped in an instant.

"Yesterday I went to the Lu estate. I saw you. I saw Zhou Jieyu. I wanted to go in and take you home — but I didn't know if you would come with me."

Lu Huaixi hadn't expected him to bring up someone else.

She was quiet for a moment, turning back over what Zhou Jieyu had said to her after he'd called out to her that evening.

"Why wouldn't I have gone with you?"

Lu Huaixi didn't understand. "You talked yourself into all of this on your own, then left me there without a word, rushed back to the manor for someone else, got all caught up with her, turned cold toward me, and didn't come home all night?"

As she said it, Lu Huaixi suddenly gave a quiet, cool laugh, her expression going distant.

"Forget it. Just go. I don't want to look at you right now."

"I was genuinely angry that you'd been drinking with someone else. I also didn't know what I could do to show I was better than Zhou Jieyu. But I didn't leave you there — someone came to say that my grandmother had taken a sudden turn and urgently wanted to see me."

Xie Yuanjing explained, his voice carrying an unfamiliar urgency.

"What you saw was me giving the order to have Mu Nianwei removed from the manor. The reason she got close was that I had been lost in thought about you and me and had let my guard down. I stayed out all night because I went to Shen Zhoushu's. I thought giving you one night would let you — calm down."

"Let me calm down? Why would I need to calm down?"

Lu Huaixi caught his meaning immediately, and after a stunned silence, her voice shook — both furious and disbelieving. "So when it comes down to it, you simply don't trust me."

Xie Yuanjing wanted to say that wasn't it, but his expression dimmed in the same instant.

He didn't know what trusting someone was supposed to look like. He didn't know how to do it.

He had heard Lu Huaixi's secret.

If anything, it was himself he didn't trust.

"Is it because you think that after finding out about Elder Brother Zhou's portrait, I'd feel regretful — regret that I didn't marry into the Zhou family, regret that I agreed to you when I did? Is that it?"

Lu Huaixi's face held not a trace of a smile.

The rims of her eyes were faintly red — from anger, or from the effort of not crying, it was hard to say.

But her voice grew colder by the sentence, stripped entirely of the soft pliability she usually carried.

"You think I'd develop feelings for Zhou Jieyu — that after he said what he said, I'd be eager to respond, that I'd want to revisit old times with him, and that the regret would draw me closer and closer to him — is that what you think?"

Lu Huaixi had no intention of waiting for Xie Yuanjing to answer.

She stopped only for a breath, then said: "What do you take me for? Haven't we already made things right between us?"

The last few words had been stained with the faintest hint of tears, even though Lu Huaixi had already held them back with every effort she had.

She didn't want to be here any longer. She shoved him firmly beside his injury, stood up, and walked away.

chapters.title: I Want to Help You Work
chapters.content:
For two full days, Lu Huaixi did not speak to Xie Yuanjing.

She was the same as ever with everyone else — still smiling, still bickering with the old man from time to time. But with Xie Yuanjing alone, there was nothing. No emotion at all.

She wasn't deliberately making things cold. It was simply that whenever their eyes met, anything either of them might have said felt blocked before it could come out.

There were probably still some things between them that needed working through.

Just like in the beginning — Xie Yuanjing had kept too much to himself, and she had told him that wouldn't do. He had said he would change. And he had, for a while. But now he had forgotten again.

These things might not look very serious at first glance. But once they surfaced, they were bound to cut deep.

She didn't want that.

And yet for these two days, Xie Yuanjing had done nothing but follow her in silence. Not a single word of additional explanation.

He gave no response at all to what she had asked of him two days ago. Silence, and only silence.

No matter how hard she tried, Lu Huaixi couldn't make sense of it — how could a man who was so imperious and possessive at his core be so unsettled by someone he had barely interacted with?

But if he refused to say anything, then she had no intention of chasing after an answer anymore.

—

Another day passed.

The sky was overcast. Lu Huaixi had been humming to herself about wanting a hot pot — ideally with a braised chicken to go with it.

The old man was so exasperated he got a headache, and shielded his chickens from her, then banished her to the back to do some work.

Xie Yuanjing, however, was told to stay — the old man said he had brought so many people and was eating his food for free, so he ought to contribute something.

With Xie Yuanjing kept back, Lu Huaixi was relieved but not quite pleased either.

She worked in silence, and even found herself thinking that living up here on the mountain might not be so bad after all.

Gong Zhuo kept watch from a short distance behind her, fretting about one thing and then another, more anxious than anyone. Watching his master grow dimmer by the day, he turned the situation over in his mind and finally decided he couldn't let things go on like this.

Steeling himself, Gong Zhuo waited until his master had been summoned away by the old gentleman, then went to find Lu Huaixi.

"Young mistress, there is something I would like to say to you."

A duck had just run past in front of Lu Huaixi. She watched it for a moment, then turned her gaze to him and listened with a calm expression.

"Say it then. And when you're done, take your master back with you."

Gong Zhuo: "......"

After a long, pained pause, he said carefully: "Young mistress, the master didn't mean to make you angry. The reason he got so tangled up over it is because the other person was Zhou Jieyu."

Zhou Jieyu again.

Lu Huaixi felt a dull ache starting in her head.

"What is it about Zhou Jieyu that makes him so capable? I don't see what's so impressive about him that your master can't stop fixating on him."

She paused, then added: "Fine. If there's something to it, have Xie Yuanjing come and tell me himself. If he's not willing to say anything, then things between us can only stay as they are."

She was not going to spend the rest of her days being the one left to guess.

She had said as much to Xie Yuanjing once before.

"The master may not know how to bring it up."

Gong Zhuo chose his words carefully.

He had never seen his master like this either — stopped in his tracks by a Zhou Jieyu.

In the past, ten Zhou family eldest sons put together couldn't have made his master so much as blink. He wouldn't have given way to any of them for a single moment.

But he knew that if this was never spoken plainly, the young mistress before him would not keep her patience waiting there indefinitely.

With that in mind, Gong Zhuo stopped holding back.

"The truth is — it began when you once mentioned Zhou Jieyu after you'd had too much to drink. That is why, to the master, that name carries a different weight than all the others."

"When did I talk about him while I was drunk... was it the lake outing?"

Lu Huaixi was genuinely surprised.

She put down what was in her hands, both bewildered and intrigued.

"Yes, exactly that time. The master was bringing you home and asked you something, and you answered right away — you said that if you had seen Zhou Jieyu's portrait back then, you would have married..."

Lu Huaixi had no idea this had happened.

She frowned in puzzlement, and after a moment asked: "Did I say anything else?"

"To answer you, young mistress — I don't know the rest. I only heard that one line, and it was by accident. After that the master put you in the carriage, and I believe he asked you a few more things — you seemed quite trusting of the Zhou family's young master at the time... though perhaps that was also because of Miss Zhou..."

Gong Zhuo spoke slowly, his voice low enough that it was sometimes swallowed by the wind.

But Lu Huaixi caught every word of it.

"The master can move against someone like He Jian or He Bingxin at any moment, and he would never give those kinds of people a second thought. But when it comes to the Zhou family's young master — he perhaps has a little more... hesitation."

Lu Huaixi went still.

Xie Yuanjing's words from that day — "I don't know what to do" — echoed in her ears again.

She never would have imagined that something like this had been living in him all along, buried there for so long.

And yet, even knowing, she still felt a swell of frustration.

If Gong Zhuo hadn't happened to overhear, she would never have known any of this.

And the two of them would have gone on — one nursing a quiet grievance, the other carrying a quiet resentment — stumbling along until the misunderstanding deepened beyond mending.

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long time.

When she looked back up, Xie Yuanjing was coming toward her from somewhere.

He stopped in front of her and lowered his eyes. Amid that gentleness was something careful and tentative, an offering. "Can I help you with the work?"

Having learned what she had, Lu Huaixi found she couldn't quite hold onto her anger — yet something still sat heavy in her chest.

She turned her head away and answered coolly: "No. What does my work have to do with you?"

"Haven't we already made things right?"

Xie Yuanjing held her carefully, his voice low and soft against her ear. "I want to help you with the work. And I also want — for you to acknowledge me in front of the Lu family."

chapters.title: Untangling the Knot
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi didn't like misunderstandings.

She liked things open and honest — if she cared for someone, that should be open and honest too. If she was with someone, the same.

But if this could serve as the moment to break Xie Yuanjing of his habit of burying everything inside without a word, perhaps that wasn't entirely a bad thing.

And so Lu Huaixi didn't give him an answer right away.

She heard him ask "haven't we already made things right?" and quote back the words she had said to him, but she didn't soften.

"I thought so too, once. But it doesn't seem like you truly felt that way, Xie Yuanjing."

Lu Huaixi stepped back from his reach and met his gaze.

"So why would I acknowledge you? There is no such thing as a marriage like this — you pin imagined crimes on me, you bottle something up without saying a word, and then your distrust bleeds into how you treat me, and I'm just supposed to quietly endure that treatment for no good reason?"

Lu Huaixi's words came without softening.

But she had decided to be with Xie Yuanjing, and that meant some things had to be laid out in the open, clearly and completely.

"Breaking my promise was my fault. I should not have let myself be tempted by the wine and forgotten what we had agreed upon. But your anger had nothing to do with the broken promise — and yet you said nothing, only left me alone to feel guilty and miserable.

"That day I asked you what you took me for. I asked if we weren't together. You gave me nothing. Today you come and ask me — and I can't give you anything either."

The dark depths of Xie Yuanjing's eyes were already flooded with regret.

He stepped forward.

Seeing the red at the corners of Lu Huaixi's eyes, her beautiful gaze filled with grievance, he felt as though a dull blade were being dragged slowly across his heart.

He had calculated and deliberated, and in the end had chosen the path that upset her most.

In this moment, Xie Yuanjing had only one thought —

He had been utterly wrong.

And only one thing left he wanted to do.

He would make his wife happy again. From now on, no matter who came, Lu Huaixi was his and his alone. He would never let her feel even a moment's unhappiness again.

Thinking it, he did it.

He stepped forward and held her, and even as she struggled, even as the force of her pushing landed against his not-yet-healed wound, he had no intention of letting go.

"It was my fault. I was out of line."

Xie Yuanjing held her close and still, bowed his head, his voice going from urgent to quiet.

"I'm the one who caused you grief, who made you unhappy. That night I was wretched too — I stayed at Shen Zhoushu's the whole night without sleeping, terrified that if I came back to the manor I would find you..."

"Find me what?"

Lu Huaixi stopped struggling, and despite her anger, waited for him to say it himself.

Only if the words came from him could it count as an explanation. Only then could the knot truly be considered undone.

Xie Yuanjing paused for a moment, as if reluctant to say the name aloud.

As if saying it would bring it to life — as if naming it would make her actually think of it.
