But Lu Huaixi didn't waver. She asked again.

"Are you sure you don't want to tell me anything?"

Xie Yuanjing let out a long breath.

He tightened his arms slightly, pulling her closer.

The last sound was a quiet laugh, edged with self-mockery, and then it dissolved into the wind.

"I was afraid of finding you thinking of someone else."

He said it at last. "I have never felt this kind of timidity before. I never imagined that one day I would feel as though I had very little to stand on."

He held her and didn't let go, and having gotten this far, the rest came easier.

"I didn't know what to do to make you feel I was better than him. Perhaps there are things about him that I will never have — but I couldn't bring myself to concede. Lu Huaixi, I couldn't concede."

He had always moved through people and the world with indifference, sometimes coldly, sometimes with calculation. He rarely held anyone in regard.

Ordinarily, a Zhou Jieyu would never have stirred so much as a ripple in him.

But this was no longer about him and Zhou Jieyu. It was about Lu Huaixi learning that someone she had once admired had, in his own time, sent his feelings toward her.

That kind of missed connection held its own quiet ache — the particular kind of wistfulness that existed only between two people who had never crossed paths at the right moment.

He was afraid he couldn't measure up.

"But why Zhou Jieyu specifically? Why have you been so bothered by whether he sent a portrait or not?"

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a while inside his words, and softened for a while too.

Then she asked again: "Why?"

Where Lu Huaixi stood, not far away was a row of vivid wildflowers. When the wind blew, they crowded together, swaying back and forth.

She thought they were beautiful, and the moment she saw them she had wanted to bring Xie Yuanjing over to look at them — even then, even when they had already stopped talking.

So Lu Huaixi had never been able to understand why, when she already liked Xie Yuanjing this much, he still couldn't bring himself to trust her.

And then — just now.

Xie Yuanjing had said he wanted her to give him a place in front of the Lu family. And only then did something suddenly occur to Lu Huaixi.

She liked this person so much. But perhaps she had never really said so.

"Why? Tell me."

Lu Huaixi let her voice go a little softer and asked again.

Xie Yuanjing didn't stay silent for long. Now that he had opened this door, he wanted Lu Huaixi to know.

Before, he hadn't been able to see clearly. But now he seemed to understand — it didn't matter whether he could see it clearly or not. He had only one aim: he wanted Lu Huaixi.

"You said once that you had considered marrying him — that if you had seen his portrait, you would have agreed."

Xie Yuanjing's voice dropped lower still, slow and measured. "You said he was the finest young man you had ever known."

"Did I."

Lu Huaixi didn't deny it. She lifted her gaze and looked at him directly.

"I probably did say something like that."

Watching the shadow move through Xie Yuanjing's dark eyes, Lu Huaixi spoke with deliberate care, word by word, and continued:

"But the 'back then' I meant was before I knew you. I only thought he was good — I never said that because he was good, I would love him."

"Back then, you were probably thinking about who it would be most fitting to marry. And my name — Lu Huaixi — was just one name among many on your long list."

Lu Huaixi continued almost without pause, her voice even and unreadable.

Xie Yuanjing's arms tightened around her, as if he wanted to say something, but Lu Huaixi stopped him.

"Back then, I thought about marriage the same way you did. Though not quite the same, either — you probably had more considerations than I did. I only wanted to avoid being called into the palace, and I wanted the days ahead to be a little quieter. Your reasons were certainly different from mine. But regardless of what they were —"

Lu Huaixi blinked, letting him draw closer by degrees.

"Regardless of what they were — before I knew you, I wanted to marry a good man I already knew something of. What is wrong with that?"

"Nothing. And if anything is wrong, it's on my side."

Xie Yuanjing's voice dropped so low it was barely audible.

His lips brushed against Lu Huaixi's ear, almost imperceptibly. His voice held a rare urgency and regret.

"But you were not one name among many. I had no list. From the beginning, even if it started as an arrangement, it was because I felt you were the right one."

"You could have come to know me earlier."

"Early enough that I'd have known you as a child. Early enough that I would have watched you grow up, then counted the days until your coming-of-age, and come before him — and been the first to fall for you."

chapters.title: Making Up — When Will You Take Me Back?
chapters.content:
In this moment, Xie Yuanjing showed a side of himself that was uncharacteristically reckless and almost boyish.

And the sullenness Lu Huaixi had been carrying for the past few days began to soften in the quiet warmth of his voice.

She still had more to say, but right now she didn't want to interrupt him.

"I would have gone to ask for your hand on the day of your coming-of-age ceremony, and told everyone we were engaged — so you wouldn't have to worry about being called into the palace, and could play to your heart's content at home before happily marrying me."

"How long is 'to my heart's content'?"

"Two years, I suppose. Any longer and I couldn't wait — does that work?"

Xie Yuanjing was actually discussing this with her in complete seriousness. Lu Huaixi didn't stay stunned for long, and laughed into his chest.

"That day I didn't find you waiting, and I was genuinely angry. Then when I went to get you and found out you'd had too much to drink — and that it was with Zhou Jieyu — I felt like I was going mad with jealousy.

"I was afraid you'd smile at him. Afraid that after all the exhaustion of these past days, you'd realize being with me wasn't good at all. Afraid your father and mother would start thinking about your future marriage.

"I was desperate to bring you home and had completely forgotten I was still supposed to be angry with you. But then he said what he said, and I suddenly couldn't figure out what you were thinking anymore."

Xie Yuanjing spoke at unusual length, more than he ever had.

Lu Huaixi felt as though she were catching a glimpse of a different Xie Yuanjing through his words — one stripped of his cold pride and sharp edges, one who could show vulnerability because of her.

She said nothing. She wanted to let him finish.

But Xie Yuanjing suddenly stopped, pulling back just slightly, his gaze dropping to her lips.

"I want to kiss you."

His features were refined and handsome, but the rims of his eyes were faintly red, his gaze deep and laced with something unsteady.

"Lu Huaixi, I'm so afraid of losing you. Both your heart and your person — I'm afraid neither of them is truly mine."

"And after this — are you going to treat me that way again?"

"Never. Not ever again."

Xie Yuanjing murmured it, again and again. "These two days you wouldn't look at me. I felt like my heart was breaking."

Lu Huaixi said nothing more.

But something in her heart had gone soft and warm, and her ears tingled over and over with the sound of his voice.

That face was so close — so beautiful it made her sigh quietly to herself.

The next moment, she rose on her toes and kissed him first.

The mountain chill had faded without her noticing when.

Lu Huaixi was pulled into a tight embrace, and that warmth wrapped around her in layer after layer.

They had been carrying each other in their thoughts all along — making up was easy. But the very depth of that feeling meant the coldness of those two days had cut more deeply than an ordinary quarrel, and needed more tenderness to mend.

But it was Xie Yuanjing who pulled back first.

His eyes were full of restraint — the force of his arms and the flush in his gaze both crying out for closeness.

Lu Huaixi looked up at him, her eyes clouded with a soft bewilderment, not understanding why he had stopped.

She said nothing, only looked at him like that — arms draped over his shoulders, dazed and wanting, like a gentle little creature — and Xie Yuanjing nearly lost his reason all over again.

"We can easily be seen here."

Xie Yuanjing shifted slightly, positioning himself to block the direction from which the old man might appear at any moment. "Your skin is thin — if someone teases you for it, you won't let me kiss you again before we go down the mountain."

"So no more kissing now?"

Lu Huaixi said it softly, and then suddenly remembered — she still hadn't answered what he had said earlier.

Every thread of Xie Yuanjing's reason that had anything to do with Lu Huaixi was fragile.

Hearing her ask like that — guileless, with an unwitting allure she didn't even know she possessed — his mind went blank, and he took her hand and walked straight into the depths of the forest.

Here and there on the ground were thin twigs and branches. Xie Yuanjing had paid them no mind, but thinking of Lu Huaixi's skirts, he turned back and lifted her into his arms.

Only when they were completely clear of where they'd been standing did he stop, pressing her back against a tree.

The sound of water and the rustling of leaves mingled together.

Lu Huaixi's soft, breathless sounds and Xie Yuanjing's unsteady breathing were enough to make anyone flush.

In a brief pause, Lu Huaixi gathered a thread of her senses. Just as he leaned in again, she tilted her head slightly to the side.

"You said earlier you couldn't figure out what I was thinking. What about now?"

Lu Huaixi's arms were still around Xie Yuanjing's waist, her ear still tingling from the graze of his teeth.

Her voice was even softer than before — carrying a faint edge of tears, as though she'd been handled a little roughly.

Xie Yuanjing had been reining himself in from the start. He endured as long as he could, and in the end gave up entirely.

"Now — you're mine. From now on, no matter who comes along, you can only be with me."

He caught her earlobe between his teeth, pressing her closer, the possessiveness and single-mindedness buried in his bones finally surfacing bit by bit.

"And I'm yours. I'll only ever be with you. A single smile from you and I'd give you anything. A single furrow of your brow and my heart aches so much I can't think of anything else. And if you were to act a little spoiled with me, I would—"

"You would what?"

Xie Yuanjing's words stopped there. Only his breathing betrayed his state.

Lu Huaixi was still in a daze, but as his arms drew tighter and tighter around her, she became aware of something different about him.

Almost the moment she felt her face go red with understanding, his voice came again.

"If you so much as hum a note at me, I find I can't hold myself back from wanting you."

—

By the time they emerged from the forest, much of the flush had faded from Lu Huaixi's face.

She looked down at the hand Xie Yuanjing was holding, and suddenly remembered there were still a few unsettled matters left between them.

"What's wrong? Don't want to leave?"

Xie Yuanjing, for his part, looked thoroughly satisfied.

Though things hadn't progressed further, the two of them had just made up and spent a long, unhurried time wrapped up in each other — he was practically glowing, with not a trace of his usual cool composure.

Seeing Lu Huaixi stop, he stopped too.

"I'll carry you back."

"I don't want you to carry me."

Lu Huaixi took a quick step back, then lifted her head to look at him.

"Have you properly explained the business with Mu Nianwei to me?"

Hearing that name, Xie Yuanjing's brow drew together for a fraction of a second.

His instinct was to say it was nothing — that the person had already been driven out and wouldn't be seen again — but remembering the reason Lu Huaixi had been so upset, he stopped himself and changed course.

"She couldn't keep her mouth in check, so I ordered her removed from the manor. My grandmother used her suicide attempt as leverage and interceded for her regardless. She thought I had come back because of her self-harm, and not accepting it, she made a scene."

In the past, Xie Yuanjing's nature would have led him to brush over the whole thing in a single sentence, not wanting Lu Huaixi to worry. But after two days of that aching tightness in his chest, he could no longer bear even a moment of her anger and coldness.

As long as she was still willing to acknowledge him, to talk to him — he would do whatever it took.

"What Princess Qinghe mentioned last time — that came through Mu Nianwei's mouth."

"She was the one who said I was jealous?"

"Yes."

Lu Huaixi showed no particular surprise at this. Instead, she turned the word over — jealous — and found it somehow both unfamiliar and oddly interesting.

"Has she been sent away? If not, go tell her — you're the one who's truly jealous."

Xie Yuanjing paused, then laughed and pulled her back in, pressing a kiss to her lips.

"Yes, I'm very jealous. My lady had better be careful from now on."

"Exactly — and you don't even like to talk about it. You go and sulk in silence with your own feelings, and I have to be careful or I'll end up in the cold again."

Lu Huaixi lifted her chin with a small huff — both petulant and proud — and it made Xie Yuanjing's heart melt completely.

"Yes, all of it was my fault."

He looked down at her, apologizing softly, one sentence after another, with inexhaustible patience.

It was only when he saw the corner of Lu Huaixi's mouth begin to curve upward, fighting back a smile, that he pulled her into his arms and asked earnestly:

"When will you take me back to the Lu estate?"

chapters.title: Lu Tangshu Gets Married
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi hadn't particularly thought about setting a specific day to take Xie Yuanjing back to the Lu estate.

But what had happened this time made her feel suddenly that a visit was overdue.

She was just beginning to think about the timing when Xie Yuanjing spoke first, as though he had been waiting for a very long time.

"How about on the way down the mountain this time? Would that be alright?"

"This time going down?"

"Yes. My grandfather already knows how I feel about you. Once we're down, I'll speak with my mother first, and then the day after we'll go to the Lu estate."

The corner of Lu Huaixi's mouth twitched, and she very nearly nodded along with him.

But then she remembered that Lu Tangshu's wedding was only a few days away, and that the Lu household would be rather tense because of it — so she steeled herself and pushed the date back a little.

"It doesn't have to wait too long — at most half a month. Once she's married and things have settled a bit with my grandfather, we'll go."

Xie Yuanjing wasn't entirely pleased. Half a month was too long.

But seeing the thoughtful sincerity on her face, he agreed to what she'd said.

And even though he hadn't gotten everything he wanted, having Lu Huaixi's promise, and having made up so smoothly, Xie Yuanjing was nothing like the coldness of the previous two days.

For the rest of the day, Xie Yuanjing followed Lu Huaixi around.

Trailing after her, checking on her every so often to make sure she was still there.

He also paid no mind to the old man's jibes and teasing, and dug and turned the earth without complaint — sleeves rolled up, arms working steadily — looking for all the world like a rough mountain laborer.

Lu Huaixi could barely tear her eyes away.

Some people looked beautiful in fine silk robes — but just as beautiful in plain clothes.

Still, when it came to the planting itself, that was still Lu Huaixi's domain. The seedlings still had to be chosen by her.

She didn't dare stare too openly and kept her eyes obediently on what her hands were doing.

The two of them stayed on the mountain for another two days.

By the time Lu Huaixi was starting to feel reluctant to leave, Xie Yuanjing simply carried her down.

Before they left, he also had several dozen chickens and ducks sent up, along with food and various other things, until the small cabin nearby was stacked full.

But Lu Huaixi also pulled up some flowers and herbs to take with her, which left the old man too irritated to even know what to say.

After this, the two were noticeably different from before.

Xie Yuanjing seemed to cling to her a little more than he used to. Though he was still very busy, he would always come home and talk to her at length.

Sometimes it was official business he could share. Sometimes it was things he'd heard about other people. Sometimes it was just him looking for something to say.

At first he talked a little stiffly, as though not quite used to sharing the kind of small, inconsequential details that had little bearing on either of them.

But watching Lu Huaixi occasionally perk up with interest, and sometimes lean over and kiss him when something pleased her, he found himself talking more and more naturally — and grew increasingly skilled at finding things to say when there was nothing to say at all.

He would also hold Lu Huaixi from time to time and say that he used to be too dull, and that he wouldn't be so boring anymore.

A few more days of this sweetness passed, and then came the day of Lu Tangshu's wedding.

Lu Huaixi returned to the Lu estate looking for all the world as though she bore no ill feeling toward the second household.

But seeing Lu Tangshu sitting there in her wedding robes — throwing a tantrum, hurling things, crying and cursing — she still felt a familiar wave of impatience and went cold.

She said nothing and didn't try to console her, leaving that to the distant cousins from the second household who were hovering around her.

But they all knew — the He family and the Lu family had already fallen out, and He Jianhang, a He family son with no real standing, was hardly in a position to give Lu Tangshu the status she wanted.

And beyond that, once Lu Tangshu stepped out of the Lu estate's gates, the comfortable days she'd known were over.

Lu Sueidong also stood silently to one side.

The only thing she said was a quiet word of warning to Lu Huaixi, telling her not to let He Jianhang catch sight of her.

"The other day I overheard He Jianhang and Lu Tangshu quarreling, and your name came up. I don't think He Jianhang is a good person at all — if he sees you later and says something, or gives some sort of telling reaction, people will surely misread it and the gossip will fall on you."

"Mm, I'll stay inside."

Lu Huaixi had no intention of going anywhere near him, regardless of whether He Jianhang had the nerve to try anything.

She had come only to show her face, and to take one last look at Lu Tangshu before she tumbled into the abyss she had made for herself.

Before long, people outside were calling that the He family had arrived to collect the bride — but the sounds that drifted in were sparse and thin, nothing at all like the reception a daughter of a noble family deserved.

Shortly after, a maidservant came looking for Lady Luo, asking her to step out, urgency in her voice.

Lady Luo followed her out. The sound of raised voices carried back, then grew more and more distant.

In the wake of that, the room fell quiet. Someone seemed to overhear a few words and pulled another person outside to whisper.

Lu Tangshu's expression changed in an instant. She called them back, saying they should speak right here.

The person was a young maidservant from Lady Luo's maternal family — confronted by Lu Tangshu's fury, she panicked at once and told everything she had heard.

It was, as it turned out, a humiliation.

He Jianhang had taken a concubine that very day. He hadn't dared make a public spectacle of it, but the news had still reached the second household.

When the second household's master confronted him about it, He Jianhang hadn't even tried to hide it — he said the woman had followed him for years, and he owed her a proper title.

After that first moment, He Jianhang hadn't shown the slightest guilt. On the contrary, he stood up straighter, perfectly certain that Lu Tangshu had no choice but to marry him regardless.

The color drained from everyone's face in the room. Lu Tangshu tore off her wedding veil and threw it to the floor, stamping on it again and again, shouting viciously that she refused to go through with it — that He Jianhang could go and die.

Chaos broke out behind them.

Lu Huaixi and Lu Sueidong stood in the shadows to one side, watching without a word.

In the end the noise carried and several people came — all second household servants.

"Third young miss, the auspicious hour has arrived. You must go out now."

Lu Tangshu's expression was anything but pleasant.

"Get away from me!"

She pointed at the person. "I am not marrying that useless waste! He dares to take a concubine on his wedding day — who does he think he is?! Tell him to get out!"

The servants exchanged uncertain looks, and after a moment someone brought in a length of thick rope.

"We beg your forgiveness, third young miss. The master says there are people watching outside, and you must get into the bridal sedan. But the master also says to tell you — marry first, and after today he will see to justice on your behalf—"

Lu Tangshu stared at them in disbelief.

One by one, the others in the room had already slipped out, unwilling to truly witness the second household's shame.

Lu Huaixi was also preparing to leave, but she caught sight of Lu Tangshu looking at her — rage and resentment in her eyes, but also a flicker of desperate pleading and hope.

"Second Sister, save me!"

She lunged forward. "I don't want to marry that useless man — I know I was wrong! He is not worthy of me, not worthy of the Lu family! Second Sister, give me one more chance. I'll never dare make you angry again — please, Second Sister, save me—"

Lu Huaixi turned and met Lu Tangshu's gaze.

She said nothing. The pleading left her unmoved.

The desperation in the other's eyes turned to frightened fury when help didn't come, and the hatred surfaced again — undisguised.

Lu Huaixi gave a sudden, quiet laugh. But her eyes didn't curve the way they usually did when she smiled. The smile seemed almost like an illusion.

Even now, Lu Tangshu still believed that everything that had happened to her was someone else's fault.

Seeing that no amount of pleading would work, the servants finally stepped forward and bound her.

"Third young miss, the second master says this marriage cannot be changed. If you go out like this, you can at least preserve what's left of your dignity."

Lu Tangshu was soon lifted into the bridal sedan. Beneath the veil her mouth was stuffed to silence, and inside the wide sleeves her hands were tied together.

Lu Huaixi felt not a shred of pity.

She watched until the sedan disappeared from view, waited a moment, then walked out of the courtyard step by step, her face expressionless.

The people outside had no idea what had happened inside — they only knew that this He family young master was evidently of little consequence in his own household, for even coming to collect a noble bride, the procession was remarkably shabby.

Jing Shuang pushed through the crowd and made her way over, lowering her voice: "Young mistress, the young master has come to collect you."

Hearing that Xie Yuanjing had come, the first real smile of the afternoon appeared on Lu Huaixi's face.

She turned. The chill that had settled over her features dissolved, and her eyes curved warmly.

"Where is he?"

"He'll be here very soon — he's just around the corner on the back street. Why don't you go inside and rest first?"

"No rest — I'll go wait for him."

With that, Lu Huaixi gathered her skirts and stepped over the threshold, breaking into a quick run.

Jing Shuang barely had time to follow, catching only a glimpse of the beautiful skirt flying behind the retreating figure — dazzling and bright.

chapters.title: Hard to Say Who's Better Looking
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing arrived even sooner than Jing Shuang had said — almost the moment Lu Huaixi came running out of the crowd, she spotted his horse.

He dismounted, and seeing that she showed no sign of slowing down, he opened his arms and caught her as she ran straight into them.

"Is this happiness or unhappiness?"

Xie Yuanjing looked down at her, paying no mind to the curious glances from passersby.

Lu Huaixi was even more unbothered — especially now, when the two of them were inseparable, and the more she looked at Xie Yuanjing the more she found him impossibly handsome and the more she adored him.

"It was neither, really. But then I heard you'd come to get me, and I was happy."

"You're so good."

A quiet laugh escaped Xie Yuanjing, his voice indulgently gentle. "Then shall we go in now and say goodbye to your parents, or let me hold you a little longer first?"

Lu Huaixi didn't move, only wrapped her arms around him in return.

Xie Yuanjing's arms tightened a little more, and he shifted them a few steps to the side.

Only when they were completely out of anyone's view did he bow his head and press a kiss to her face.

But he also remembered they were still outside, and held himself to just that — only her face.

"Did your elder sister and brother-in-law come today?"

Lu Huaixi shook her head in his arms, then tilted her face up to look at him. "My sister is at home — she's with child, and Mother wouldn't let her come. Why are you suddenly asking about my sister and brother-in-law?"

"Just curious."

After a moment, Xie Yuanjing felt something was a little off and added a follow-up: "I was thinking about how to return a gift to your brother-in-law."

"Return what gift?"

Lu Huaixi didn't understand. Her eyes went wide with puzzlement.

But Xie Yuanjing wouldn't say — he just looked at her with a quiet curl of his lips.

After a long moment, seeing that she was genuinely at a loss, he stopped teasing and lowered his voice. "The booklet. It'll prove very useful."

The moment the words fell, Lu Huaixi's face went red.

She finally remembered — just the other day, this person had been pestering her to look at her practice-dance outfits, and while she was rummaging through them, she had accidentally turned up the booklet her elder sister had gifted her when they married.

Before she could put it away, Xie Yuanjing had already taken it from her.

He was becoming more and more unabashed by the day.

Lu Huaixi's skin was not as thick as his — and while she found it interesting too, she had never once won an argument with him on the subject.

It always ended with her surrendering in embarrassed distress, begging him not to say any more and not to be so fierce about kissing her.

But she also knew that Xie Yuanjing had been holding a great deal back.

He had even mentioned teaching her the next step at some point, yet he had continued to restrain himself and hadn't begun.

"You — stop causing trouble."

Lu Huaixi murmured close to his ear, fighting through her shyness. "What do you mean, returning a gift to my brother-in-law? If you act improperly, I really won't speak to you!"

"And what did you think I meant?"

Xie Yuanjing laughed again, reaching up to pinch her ear.

"When I say return a gift, I naturally mean something in the court — that's your blood sister and her husband, they're family. Do you really think I would do something like send someone else into a household?"

"Well, how would I know."

Lu Huaixi deliberately turned her head away, her voice carrying a slight edge. "It seems someone was asking around just the other day about whether you'd taken any concubines."

"Didn't you hear exactly how I answered that?"

Xie Yuanjing tightened his fingers deliberately, feigning irritation:

"And what about Zhou Jieyu sending tea over — what does that mean? Just because his sister likes it, you're sure to like it too? I can't find tea you enjoy?"

He paused, then added:

"And then there was that day you went to the women's academy — who was that person who came running over to talk to you and ask about you? Did he not see that you were wearing a married woman's hairstyle?"

"And—"

"Alright, I was wrong, I shouldn't have misjudged you — so are you going to return the gift or not?"

Seeing that he was getting more and more worked up in earnest, Lu Huaixi quickly cut him off.

She blinked up at him with genuine sincerity.

Xie Yuanjing could never hold his ground when she looked at him like that — even knowing she was doing it on purpose, he couldn't manage to stay stern.

"I'll return it."

He held her and said: "Whether I saw the booklet or not, I'm returning the gift."

He let the smile settle and grew a little more serious.

"I've heard that your brother-in-law has been declining quite a few duties lately — probably to keep your sister company. He could let that reason stand. If something else comes up later, use that as an excuse to decline, and give himself some extra time to rest."

"Why? Is something happening at court?"

"Mm, a minor matter — but He Bingxin's assignment will likely fall apart, and the longer it drags on, the more tangled things in that region will become. Whoever goes to clean it up afterward will be dealing with double the trouble for the same post. Not worth it."

"But how do you know who they'd choose? If not my brother-in-law, would they come to you?"

"Hard to say who they'd pick. But for something like this, the palace would naturally look to a younger man who's already made himself visible. If your brother-in-law goes, the round trip would take at least a month — and it's more dangerous than it sounds. Though of course, I'm even less able to go right now."

Xie Yuanjing smiled. "I'm still recovering from my injury, after all."

Lu Huaixi took it in and nodded, then nestled back against him with her usual easy compliance. "Then I'll have someone send word to my sister."

"Mm, no rush — He Bingxin will hold out for a while. He won't be back in the capital anytime soon."

"How can you be so sure he'll fail? What if he handles it well and comes back to a commendation?"

Xie Yuanjing lifted a strand of her loose hair and wound it idly around his finger, his attention drifting again to her lips as she spoke.

He couldn't kiss her right now — so he did his best to redirect.

His thoughts drifted toward home as he answered offhandedly: "Because that post was one His Majesty originally planned to send only me to handle."

Hearing this from anyone else might have left them at a loss. But Lu Huaixi understood in moments.

A laugh broke free from her. She wrapped her arms around him and pressed her face to his chest.

"You're so arrogant — just because only you could handle it, does that mean no one else can manage at all?"

"It doesn't mean no one else could manage. But He Bingxin definitely can't."

He also wasn't going to let him manage.

Xie Yuanjing didn't say much more — not because he didn't want to, but because it was still too early to get into it. And compared to this, there was something else he wanted to do far more.

"It's getting late. When are we heading home?"

"It's not getting late at all."

Lu Huaixi looked back at him with a warm, amused smile. "You always seem in such a hurry to get home."

Xie Yuanjing's lips moved slightly.

That he truly couldn't say out loud.

If he said it, she would torture him by delaying their return until the very last possible moment.

He gave a helpless curl of his lips and pulled her close again. "Then let me hold you a little longer."

Lu Huaixi didn't resist.

She loved this — standing somewhere quiet, listening to Xie Yuanjing breathe, holding his hand, letting him hold her.

Something crossed her mind, and she laughed softly.

"What is it?"

His voice was low and warm, and the sound of it made Lu Huaixi feel a faint shyness.

She lowered her gaze and murmured, soft and unhurried: "Nothing. I just think you're really good-looking."

She wondered idly whether, once her parents found out how things stood between them, Xie Yuanjing's face might make them a little more agreeable.

Hearing her say that, Xie Yuanjing smiled too.

He said nothing, only thought to himself — hard to say who's the better-looking one.

chapters.title: Busy Days
chapters.content:
At the Lu estate, Lady Liu watched Lu Tangshu's wedding with a cold and unmoved heart.

She glanced over at the second household mingling with the guests.

Seeing Lady Luo straining to hold back her displeasure and wrenching out the thinnest semblance of a smile, Lady Liu turned away and walked back inside at an unhurried pace.

"Where is Huaixi?"

Lady Liu looked to the maidservant beside her.

There had been a lot of people earlier, and she hadn't spotted her daughter in the crowd. She had assumed the girl found the whole affair too dull — after all, she had no desire to witness anything involving Lu Tangshu and He Jianhang.

But now the guests were dispersing, and she had looked around and still didn't see her.

"To answer the first madam, the second young miss rushed out of the estate just now. She has likely gone to meet someone."

"She went out? How long ago?"

"Your servant saw her leave a little while ago. But the Marquis manor's carriage is still waiting around back and hasn't left — the second young miss should be back before too long."

Lady Liu stopped walking, a small frown crossing her face.

There were a fair number of people outside today, drawn by the spectacle.

Even if this wedding was the second household's own doing, the He family's poor showing and He Jianhang's uselessness would inevitably reflect somewhat on the Lu family name.

And with Huaixi running out like that, she was bound to catch some of the gossip.

If people expected her to speak well of Lu Tangshu, her Huaixi would never stomach that. But if she didn't, people might say she was a cold-hearted elder sister.

Lady Liu had no intention of allowing her daughter to suffer on behalf of that troublesome girl, now that she was finally gone.

With that in mind, Lady Liu headed in the direction the maidservant had indicated.

"The rest of you stay and keep watch here. I'll go and look for her."

"Yes, my lady."

Only one maidservant accompanied her. Lady Liu went out of the estate.

The area was quiet, with no one around.

When she was nearly at the back street, Lady Liu finally spotted Yao Xu and Jing Shuang standing to one side.

She was just about to ask why they were standing there motionless, when she drew closer and caught sight, not far away by the large horse, of her daughter and Xie Yuanjing — standing together in a way that left little ambiguity.

One with his head slightly bowed, saying something, an arm settled around the other's waist.

One with her chin resting against his chest, looking up at him with a smile, occasionally rubbing her face against him — the very picture of a young woman being sweetly affectionate.

Lady Liu stood frozen, convinced she must be seeing things.

She collected herself, then turned to ask Jing Shuang and Yao Xu beside her — and stopped when she saw the matter-of-fact normalcy on both their faces.

They didn't know about the terms of the marriage arrangement.

Which meant that in their eyes, Xie Yuanjing and their young mistress had always been close — which was why neither of them found anything surprising about the scene.

And as though to confirm it, the two figures in the distance embraced again — seemingly even closer than she had first thought.

The impulse Lady Liu had been gathering to speak died away completely.

She stood there in silence for a moment, as though turning something over in her mind.

She had never particularly favored Xie Yuanjing.

This person could be an occasional junior acquaintance, could be a useful ally for the Lu family's main household, could be an admirable young man of talent.

But he could not be her daughter's husband.

Such a husband — her Huaixi might not be able to hold steady.

And a household like his would certainly not remain with only her as the sole noble lady. There would be others — perhaps ones willing to set their pride aside and make themselves smaller.

It all depended on how much ambition this Xie had, and how much weight he placed on his future.

Lady Liu stifled another sigh.

She had not said any of this to anyone yet, and had only been thinking that today she would find a moment — to ask carefully, and properly.

After a long pause, Lady Liu turned around, swallowed those words, and spoke calmly.

"If Huaixi is tired, let her head home and rest early. There's no need to mention that I came by."

—

After that visit, Lu Huaixi did not manage to return to the Lu estate for quite some time.

She had been busy lately.

Xie Yuanjing had truly moved them out of the Marquis's manor, and handed over full management of the new residence to her.

And beyond the residence itself, Princess Qinghe, who had long been in search of reliable news about Chenyue, had persuaded her to take on the task of teaching the princess to dance.

On top of that, she had been inspired by the old shrine guardian from that battered scroll to choreograph a new piece.

Then with autumn arriving, it was time to change wardrobes — and Lu Huaixi had also taken on the task of designing new clothing styles for the seamstresses at Shun'an Fang, wanting to settle it all at once. Free moments were rare.

Xie Yuanjing was the first to lose patience.

He came home before Lu Huaixi several times, and even going to Shun'an Fang to collect her always meant waiting.

Waiting until she had finished with everyone else and finally came to him last.

She had even started teaching Princess Qinghe to dance without once offering to dance for him.

The more Xie Yuanjing thought about it, the more displeased he became. The next time he went to collect her and they had just settled into the carriage, he pulled her over and bit her shoulder in what was very clearly an act of pent-up grievance.

"What are you doing?"

Lu Huaixi hadn't even sat down properly yet, and looked up at him with a glare.

The entire carriage was full of the clean, pleasant fragrance that always clung to Lu Huaixi. Xie Yuanjing couldn't manage a stern face to frighten her with even if he tried.

"What do you think?"

Xie Yuanjing pinched her face and looked down at her with obvious dissatisfaction. "Did you marry me or did you marry Shun'an Fang? Princess Qinghe has been seeing more of you lately than I have, hasn't she?"

"Stop making things up."

Lu Huaixi was laughing at everything he said. "We sleep in the same bed every day — do I see the princess every day too?"

Just as they were talking, a commotion drifted in from outside — someone shouting at someone else, and rather viciously at that.

Lu Huaixi had no interest in listening. She burrowed into Xie Yuanjing's arms and, striking first, began to whine about how exhausted she was.

Xie Yuanjing was powerless against her. Seeing her close her eyes with genuine tiredness, he held her with one arm and raised his other hand.

He started by kneading the back of her neck, then moved slowly downward, his touch settling on her slender back.

Xie Yuanjing expressed his dissatisfaction that she hadn't been eating properly, and then his hand drifted a few inches further down, coming to rest at her waist — pressing and releasing in an idle rhythm.

Lu Huaixi felt a little ticklish, but didn't want to pull away from the warmth.

"If you don't eat properly, I'm forbidding you from going to Shun'an Fang."

"I have been eating properly."

Lu Huaixi was about to argue back, when a voice from outside rose sharply:

"Get lost! Some Lu third young miss — who in the Lu family hasn't heard of her? You think you'd actually ride in this shabby old carriage? You come into my shop to find fault — is it that you look down on my wares, or is it that you simply can't afford them? Look at the fabric you're wearing, and you have the nerve to call yourself a noble lady, coming in here to sneer at my things! Everyone come and look — I could die laughing!"

The words that followed weren't entirely audible. Lu Huaixi listened a moment longer, then finally lifted the edge of the curtain slightly.

Down the street, a small crowd had gathered.

The carriage nearby was indeed inconspicuous — not the kind the He family would typically use — but Lu Huaixi spotted Lu Tangshu's personal maidservant standing beside it.

The person who had been surrounded at the shop entrance was standing there in fury, squaring off with someone.

Yet her arrogance had no backbone to it. She didn't carry herself the way she once had. In the end, she retreated in humiliation, driven back by the shopkeeper's words.

Lu Huaixi took one last look.

As she let the curtain fall, she caught the exact moment Lu Tangshu climbed into her carriage and, without breaking stride, raised her hand and slapped the maidservant who had been waiting for her — as though looking for someone to take her frustrations out on.

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed, a flash of contempt crossing her eyes.

"If it's making you unhappy to look, then don't look. They won't be able to make trouble for long — no need to tire out your eyes."

"Mm, I won't look."

Lu Huaixi closed her eyes and settled back where she'd been.

Xie Yuanjing sheltered her, his fingertips kneading gently once more.

—

Lu Tangshu had no idea that her wretchedness and humiliation had been witnessed in full by Lu Huaixi.

She made it back to the He estate seething, and had barely reached the entrance to her rooms when she heard the sound of a woman's laughter drifting out — cloying and grating.

Then the heavy reek of wine. And He Jianhang's teasing voice.

Lu Tangshu shoved the door open, and the first thing she saw was a maidservant who was supposed to be attending in the courtyard now sitting on He Jianhang's lap.

The moment he saw her, He Jianhang's expression collapsed. Without any attempt to hide it, he told her to get out.

chapters.title: I've Been Waiting a Long Time
chapters.content:
Since she had married into the He household, Lu Tangshu had known nothing but suffering.

And yet, for all her status as a daughter of the Lu family, it counted for nothing here. She couldn't even speak back to that woman they called her mother-in-law. Every day was unbearable.

He Jianhang was beyond redemption.

He had not a scrap of ability, and since he couldn't make a name for himself, he spent his days drinking and indulging himself — taking one concubine after another in quick succession just to humiliate her.

The two of them had not had a single peaceful day since the wedding.

The maidservant in question was even the very one Lu Tangshu had personally struck the day before, and her behavior now was a blatant act of provocation — He Jianhang clearly wanted to make her look foolish.

Lu Tangshu cared nothing for how many women He Jianhang had — but the sight of him disgusted her, and she couldn't bear to see him doing well.

Especially today, when Lu Tangshu was already burning with humiliation. She couldn't hold back. She went straight over and slapped the maidservant hard, then swept every cup and flask of wine from the table and hurled them at He Jianhang.

He Jianhang, of course, was not about to take it.

He had been having a rough time of it lately.

His father's impatience. His elder brother's contempt. And this shrieking woman making his days a misery.

And his resentment of Lu Tangshu had been building for far longer than a day or two.

The moment she started the scene, he struck back — seizing her by the hair.

It ended, naturally, with Lu Tangshu on the losing side.

She sank to her knees on the floor, surrounded by the shards of cups she had smashed and the splashed wine, its foul smell nearly making her retch.

He Jianhang's face bore several fresh scratches, making his already grim expression look even darker.

He pulled the maidservant away with him and, just before he left, stopped and turned back to sneer at Lu Tangshu.

"I forgot to tell you — that complaint you lodged, your father-in-law didn't act on it. He sent word back today telling you to behave yourself in the He household. Stop causing gossip. Otherwise he won't concern himself with your affairs again."

Lu Tangshu glared back with pure venom.

And in that same moment, the reality finally landed — her father would no longer involve himself in her life.

The He and Lu families were at odds. She had shamed the Lu family by marrying into this household. And now, here in this back courtyard, her being dead was more convenient than her being alive.

From this point on, without the Lu family as her backing, she had not a single means of fighting back.

The maidservant on He Jianhang's arm glanced back at her, something like a smirk on her face — as if settling a score.

Lu Tangshu immediately made to call for help.

The maidservant shrank back against He Jianhang in fright. He took it as a challenge and turned back, kicking Lu Tangshu squarely.

"You dare hit me?"

"I hit you — and what of it? Do you still think you're some untouchable noble lady?"

He Jianhang laughed coldly, then grabbed her by the throat with a vicious grip. "Who's the useless one now, Lu Tangshu?"

Through the pain, Lu Tangshu finally felt a shred of genuine regret.

She watched He Jianhang throw her to the floor and walk away with the other woman without a backward glance.

She watched the maidservants slipping in and out, stealing disdainful glances at her — not a trace of deference.

For the first time, she tasted the despair of a door that would never open again.

She was a noble daughter.

She was supposed to have a brilliant future. She was supposed to marry a fine and accomplished young man, to be admired and sought after.

And instead she was tangled up with this worthless, spineless wreck of a man — enduring abuse and humiliation like this!

Lu Tangshu lay shivering on the floor until the cold finally forced her to drag herself up.

Qiao Ling, who had come with her from the Lu estate, came to help her.

Qiao Ling's cheek was still swollen red.

But she wasn't without her own reasons to make a stand. She simply had no one to rely on here and couldn't find a foothold — her only option was to keep depending on Lu Tangshu.

"Young miss, young miss, please bear with it for now."

Qiao Ling had not addressed her as 'young mistress.' She helped Lu Tangshu to a seat and spoke quietly, choosing her words with care:

"Young miss, you mustn't fall into someone else's trap. The master is angry with you right now and won't intercede, but you still have the madam. The madam will help you no matter what. You have to hold on."

Lu Tangshu's expression was dark. Hearing this, she gripped her handkerchief tightly.

Qiao Ling pressed on:

"Even so, you are still the lawful wife this young master married into the household. If you soften toward him a little, once his anger cools — and with the madam finding ways to help from her end — won't you be the one running this back courtyard in time?"

"Soften toward him?"

Something cold and vicious surfaced in Lu Tangshu's eyes.

They had already made enemies of each other. He Jianhang was rotten through — he would never let her live in peace.

If she truly wanted to reach a position of control, there was only one way left.

—

That Lu Tangshu was living miserably struck Lu Huaixi as entirely natural.

She heard about it without mockery and without gloating — just a quiet, indifferent sound of acknowledgment.

This was only the beginning.

But it was a road she had brought herself to.

He Jianhang wouldn't have it easy either. The two of them had a long reckoning still coming — it was only a matter of who cracked first and made a move.

Lu Huaixi heard it once and then put Lu Tangshu entirely from her mind.

When you're busy, the days fly.

By the time word finally came that He Bingxin had indeed run into trouble, Princess Qinghe paid another visit, asking about the Chenyue news she hadn't heard in so long.

Lu Huaixi had no desire to speak of Chenyue anymore — not now, and not in the future.

She had already decided to be with Xie Yuanjing, and Shun'an Fang was thriving.

Xie Yuanjing had also told her she could do whatever she loved, openly and freely — she could keep learning and choreographing dances without needing the so-called mysterious Chenyue as a cover.

That day, Lu Huaixi finally managed to persuade Princess Qinghe, at the cost of one new dance.

The princess was delighted. Before getting into her carriage to return to the palace, she was reluctant to leave and took Lu Huaixi's hands in hers.

"I'll learn the first dance first and perform it for my mother consort at the Mid-Autumn banquet."

Qinghe spoke in her usual unhurried way — a slowness that somehow never felt wrong, carrying instead a kind of warmth that people found easy and pleasant to listen to.

"The one you just danced — I want to learn that one too. I'll perform it for someone else later on. I'm just not sure I'm good enough to learn it."

"Someone else?"

Lu Huaixi's attention sharpened at once.

"A princess cannot dance freely before just anyone. You are royalty — this isn't something to be asked for on a whim."

"Not just anyone."

Qinghe was still gentle. "And not... not an outsider either."

"Then who—"

Lu Huaixi started to ask, but caught herself — this person was a princess. She stopped at once.

"Then when the princess dances, please don't go anywhere unfamiliar, and make sure the people around you always know where you are."

"I will."

Qinghe nodded. After a moment she asked, out of nowhere: "Have you danced for Xie Yuanjing yet?"

"...Not yet."

"Why not? Your dancing is so beautiful."

Lu Huaixi found herself without an answer.

At the same time, an image floated into her mind — Xie Yuanjing watching her dance — and her face suddenly felt warm.

"There... hasn't been the right moment yet."

Lu Huaixi cleared her throat lightly and said, with forced composure: "I'll definitely dance for him eventually."

As she turned to see the princess out, she found Xie Yuanjing standing outside — she hadn't heard him come.

Lu Huaixi startled, but seeing his expression was the same as always, and that he came over to squeeze her hand, she relaxed at once.

The princess was soon in her carriage. Lu Huaixi stood where she was for a moment.

She was just about to go back inside when someone came up from behind and wrapped their arms around her.

"We're still outside."

Lu Huaixi touched him lightly, but the arms only tightened.

"When is eventually?"

The voice that came was low and a little rough, the laughter in it soft and unhurried — quietly captivating.

Lu Huaixi felt it from her ears outward, a spreading warmth that made her head go hazy.

"What eventually?"

"The eventually when you'll dance for me."

Xie Yuanjing kept his voice low, and then, as though carrying a small grievance: "I've been waiting a very long time, my lady. Push me back any further, and I really am going to be unhappy."

chapters.title: I Don't Want to Sleep Alone
chapters.content:
Before Lu Huaixi had a chance to dance for Xie Yuanjing, word arrived from the palace, summoning him inside.

He didn't return until just before the palace gates were locked for the night.

The same pattern repeated for several days running — until at last his complexion went pale again, and the imperial physician said he had a fever. Only then did His Majesty stop summoning him.

That evening, Lu Huaixi stood over him until he finished his medicine, waited for him to get settled, then climbed onto the bed from the far side and lay down beside him — properly, composedly.

Xie Yuanjing heard her give a small, quiet sigh. He set down what was in his hand, turned over, and drew her into his arms.

"What's wrong? Worried about me?"

Lu Huaixi nodded, and looked up at him with something on the tip of her tongue.

Xie Yuanjing couldn't bear to see her looking as though she'd been thinking too much. He laughed softly and rubbed her face. "What are you thinking?"

"I'm thinking about your health."

Lu Huaixi murmured the words. "Your constitution really isn't holding up, is it? Look at your color — from now on you might have to avoid even drafts of cold air. I don't know if this is a lingering effect from the last injury or not. Should I go up the mountain again and ask the old man?"

Xie Yuanjing watched her talk herself through all of this.

At the last word, his laugh suddenly went quieter and deeper.

Lu Huaixi hadn't caught it yet, when the person who had only been holding her a moment ago flipped over and pinned her beneath him.

"What do you mean, my constitution isn't holding up?"

He bent his head and nipped at Lu Huaixi's lip, then pulled back. "You think I'm not up to it?"

Lu Huaixi didn't dare meet his eyes at first — this position was new, and she felt a little nervous.

But the moment she remembered that this person had just finished drinking his medicine, whatever flutter of feeling she'd had dissipated cleanly.

"It's not what I think — it's you yourself. Today, the reason His Majesty sent you home early was precisely because you weren't feeling well."

"If I hadn't found a reason to come back, you'd have had to sleep alone tonight. Is that what you want?"

Xie Yuanjing's breathing grew heavier as he spoke. He turned his head and pressed his lips to Lu Huaixi's ear.

After kissing it, he went ahead and bit down gently.

A soft sound escaped the corner of Lu Huaixi's mouth. Feeling the tingle, she tilted her head to the other side.

"You're just like that little puppy they keep."

"Mm. I am."

Xie Yuanjing answered casually, then asked again: "I asked you — do you want to sleep alone tonight?"

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together. The hand that had been moving to push him away stilled.

"I don't."

Her voice went small, carrying the kind of candor she didn't try to hide. Muffled and earnest: "I don't want to sleep alone."

Xie Yuanjing's laugh was barely a breath — light and weightless where it fell against her ear.

Then he said nothing more, only continuing from where the ear left off — kissing along, and then down the neck, the cheek, the chin, until he stopped at the lips.

With autumn come, even the thin quilt no longer felt hot at night.

But being cocooned the way Xie Yuanjing held her — a furnace of a person — Lu Huaixi found herself squirming, wanting him to move out from under the covers.

Almost the instant she moved, Xie Yuanjing caught her hands.

The kisses came back, tracing the reverse of the path they'd just traveled, fiercer than any time before — and carrying something else beneath them.

Lu Huaixi's instinct was to curl her fingers into a grip, but he opened her hand and laced his fingers through hers.

Xie Yuanjing buried his face in her neck, and then drifted a little lower, a soft bite.

"My health is perfectly fine. There's nothing wrong with me."

He breathed the words unevenly. "But sometimes, it does get a little hard to bear."

Lu Huaixi was drifting in a haze, and hearing him say it was hard to bear, she followed his words without thinking: "Where does it hurt?"

Xie Yuanjing took her hand and moved it downward — but stopped halfway, and with it, his kisses stopped too.

He looked down at Lu Huaixi's cloudy, innocent eyes and gave a helpless quiet laugh.

Then he turned over and pulled her up with him, settling her on top of himself.

Lu Huaixi's vision tilted. She ended up lying against his chest.

Given how they were positioned, there was something impossible to ignore.

"You — you—"

"Hard to bear from waiting for you."

Xie Yuanjing's dark eyes were filled with something languid and wanting, the outer corners lifting slightly — making him look at once unhurried and deeply feeling.

One hand patting Lu Huaixi's back, one arm steadied at her waist — gentle and coaxing, with not a trace of embarrassment.

"Can you feel it? As long as you can still feel it, I'm perfectly fine. But sometimes, when it gets too hard to endure — could you take a little pity on me? Would that be alright?"

Lu Huaixi was genuinely taken aback.

She had, in moments when Xie Yuanjing's face was too beautiful to resist, let some rather unguarded things slip from her own mouth.

She had even run over and kissed him on her own initiative, reached out to hold him herself.

She had thought herself quite bold, all things considered. But compared to the Xie Yuanjing in front of her now — eyes full of something slow and honeyed — she couldn't form a single word.

She couldn't even look at him. Her whole body went stiff.

Xie Yuanjing, having had his fun, finally decided to show mercy.

"So timid. What will you do later on?"

"What do you mean what will I do later — how can someone be this shameless."

Lu Huaixi buried her face in his chest, operating on the logic that if she hid her face, she wouldn't feel embarrassed anymore, and talked to him like that.

Which only made Xie Yuanjing's laughter clearer and deeper, and only made her feel even warmer all over.

She thought to herself, privately — the next time Xie Yuanjing was away, she absolutely had to study those booklets properly. She couldn't keep being left speechless every single time.

She was still plotting how to reclaim the upper hand when Xie Yuanjing shifted her upward slightly.

Moving her away from that particular spot, he tucked the quilt in on both sides.

"A thin-skinned person like you — how did she ever agree to take a wife?"

He said it idly: "Between the two of us, if I had been even a fraction more thin-skinned, this marriage never would have happened."

Lu Huaixi finally managed to lift her head and look at him. She thought about it, then laughed into his ear.

"That's true. If you hadn't come to tell me we'd separate after a year, I never would have dared marry you."

"If you hadn't married me, you couldn't have married anyone else."

Xie Yuanjing said it with an air of subtle meaning. "The portraits that were sent to you — Zhou Jieyu's wasn't among them."

"Why are you still bringing him up."

Lu Huaixi immediately leaned over and bit down on his shoulder.

The candle in the room swayed and flickered. Lu Huaixi's frustration passed, and she lay sprawled on Xie Yuanjing's chest, held by him, drifting toward sleep.

But she still remembered that this person had been going to the palace for several days now, and had fallen ill today — it was probably from the unrelenting strain.

"Do you not have to go out tomorrow? Your last injury had barely healed."

"Mm, I won't be going for the next few days."

Xie Yuanjing patted her back.

Seeing drowsiness settle across her face, he lowered his voice and told her about the past few days.

"He Bingxin pushed too hard and overstepped — he's been detained. Someone needs to go in and take over, clean up the mess he's made. I have no interest in getting involved in his affairs. I find it tedious, so I'll be ill for a few days first."

"So it wasn't for the sake of coming home to sleep next to me."

"Why wouldn't it be?"

Xie Yuanjing was made to laugh by her, and looked down — but she had already closed her eyes and was nearly asleep.

He didn't say anything more, only let his hand on her back keep its slow, quiet rhythm until she was fully asleep.

In truth, it shouldn't be called coming home to sleep next to her.

Now, Lu Huaixi could manage perfectly well on her own. He was the one who couldn't.

So it ought to be said the other way around — it was he who wanted her company.

—

Elsewhere, the Marquis of Chengen had received word from the outer residence since early evening and set out without a moment's hesitation.

He Bingxin had not yet returned to the capital, but several letters had already made their way to the Marquis's hands.

He stepped into the residence, and the woman inside saw him and came out to meet him, eyes already red.

Just as before, she wept as she sank to her knees before him.

"My lord, please, I beg you to save Bingxin — save him!"

chapters.title: No Obsession?
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Chengen had always felt he owed this mother and son a debt. He also believed He Bingxin had been raised well — a match for any son of a respectable family.

He had once truly only had eyes for Xie Yuanjing. And constrained by his wife's standing, he couldn't often come to this household.

But ever since that son had grown more and more set on his own course — more capable and more unyielding — the rift between father and son had widened along with it.

It was around that time that He Bingxin had on several occasions been slighted by others, yet swallowed the humiliation quietly so as not to make things difficult for him.

And each time the Marquis came, He Bingxin looked up at him with undisguised admiration and respect, saying he wanted to earn merit through his own efforts and become his father's right-hand man.

The Marquis had felt increasingly guilty — and increasingly aware that he had someone else worth caring for.

He began offering more support than before. And every time he came, he was met with the mother and son's dependence and reverence — glad to have him and yet anxious for him at the same time.

Over time, this place had begun to feel more like a home to him.

But tonight as he arrived, he couldn't help but notice a tiredness settling in his brow.

The woman saw him and came out crying, sinking to her knees — and after he told her to rise, leaned instinctively toward him.

But the Marquis did not open his arms as he usually had, and went instead directly to sit down.

"My lord..."

"It will still be a while before Bingxin can return. After taking a blow like this, let him follow Master Xun for a proper while — learn what it means to serve as an official. No more rushing to take on assignments."

The woman startled, her crying forgotten for the moment, a trace of panic coming over her.

"Please don't be angry, my lord — Bingxin didn't do well this time, but if — if he can't take on assignments again, people will think he's out of favor, and he had still hoped one day to be of use to you..."

"Becoming useful to me is not something that happens overnight. When he has genuinely built his ability, the court will recognize it on its own, and he will naturally become my right-hand man."

The Marquis spoke directly, a note of barely restrained displeasure entering his voice.

"I advised him at the time not to take this assignment. Even Yuanjing would have found this a difficult task — but he didn't listen. And on top of that, his approach was far too reckless."

"My lord, Bingxin only wanted to..."

The woman didn't dare say much more, afraid a single wrong word might displease the man before her.

She lowered her head and wept softly, then after a long pause said through her tears: "Bingxin has been in the wrong, my lord. Please don't trouble your health on his account. Your wellbeing matters far more than whether he makes an official career."

Seeing her like this, the Marquis softened.

"I don't blame him — but Bingxin's tendency to be soft-hearted is a problem. He trusts the wrong people, again and again — last time, and now this time too."

He said it gravely: "And this time, not only did he walk into someone else's trap, his handling was far too rash. Did he not stop to think — if this assignment had been manageable, how could it possibly have been left undone long enough for him to claim it? He didn't consider it for a single moment."

The woman listened without daring to ask too much.

At the very end, she gave a quiet, choking sigh, and spoke with what seemed like self-reproach:

"It is all my fault. If I had not stubbornly refused to enter the Marquis's household, how could Bingxin have grown up with this kind of character? Even if he were less capable, with the young master Xie Yuanjing to look to, how could he have turned out so poorly? It is all my foolishness."

She paused, then added:

"Now that he has bungled the assignment, whoever is sent to take it over will be full of resentment at the mess Bingxin has left behind. If young master Xie Yuanjing could step in and help smooth things over, perhaps it might ease the situation somewhat..."

She caught herself mid-sentence and stopped, quickly taking it back with an apology.

The Marquis said nothing. His expression was heavy. After a long silence, he waved a hand. "You're right. This matter — I will speak with Yuanjing about it."

The woman's face showed a flash of alarm.

"Would that be appropriate?"

She urged him back: "I only said it out of a moment of panic, speaking without restraint in front of you, my lord. Please don't take it to heart. If Bingxin causes the young master further displeasure and puts you in a difficult position, I would truly be — I would truly—"

Something in the Marquis's expression sank further at those words.

Xie Yuanjing moving out of the manor had, after all, been a mark of humiliation for him. It had the look of Xie Yuanjing being driven out — but in truth it was simply that Xie Yuanjing had not placed him or the Marquis's household in his eyes at all.

And when others brought it up, it only made it more apparent that he had come to fear this son of his, and that his own abilities were increasingly no match for the man's.

"There's nothing inappropriate about it. Wait one more day — if there's no further news about Bingxin, I'll go and personally see to it that Yuanjing takes this assignment."

—

True to his word, Xie Yuanjing's idea of resting meant not dealing with anything at all.

But he had barely rested for a single day when someone arrived from the palace again.

This time it wasn't a summons — instead, they brought a great many gifts, including some fine and valuable medicinal herbs.

Once the visitors left, Xie Yuanjing pushed all of it over to Lu Huaixi and told her this was a fortune for a dance.

The sight of him looking so lavishly generous made Lu Huaixi's eyes curve with laughter, and she couldn't help leaning over to hug him.

"Didn't you say all of this is mine?"

"It is. Gold and silver and treasure are yours. And you are mine."

Xie Yuanjing caught her, and the two of them leaned together against the window frame, letting the warm afternoon sun fall on them, the breeze soft and mild.

"Surely this isn't enough for the proprietress of Shun'an Fang to personally perform one dance?"

"Of course it isn't. Nobody does business like you."

Lu Huaixi smiled, tilting her head up at him. "You're giving me what's already mine and then using my own money to watch my dance — aren't you clever."

Xie Yuanjing found himself at a complete loss for words at her logic, and in the end started laughing too, helplessly pinching her face.

"What if I owe it for now?"

He looked down at her with a coaxing expression. "You dance for me once first, and everything I ever receive from now on goes to you — the silver, the treasures, and myself too."

"You've already been mine for ages. That's not something you can keep putting on the table."

Lu Huaixi turned her head away. "And it's not that I haven't agreed — I did agree. It's just that you weren't free those days."

"Right, it's all His Majesty's fault. So I'm very upset right now — so upset that I refuse to help with his affairs."

Xie Yuanjing said it without a trace of shame and without the slightest concern about being overheard or having it carried back to the palace — his nerve was something else entirely. "I'm even upset enough to have fallen ill. Take a little pity on me and say yes again."

"You—"

Lu Huaixi gave him a sideways look. "Let me think about it."

"How long will you need to think?"

"Until you've fully recovered."

Lu Huaixi learned to stall him with his own methods.

The two of them were going back and forth when a knock sounded at the door from outside.

Xie Yuanjing didn't look up — he kept his eyes entirely on the person in front of him.

It was Lu Huaixi who poked her head out from within his arms to look toward the door.

"Young master, young mistress — the Marquis has come. He is waiting outside to see the young master."

Lu Huaixi blinked, then called toward the door: "Did the Marquis bring anything?"

Jing Shuang was caught off guard for a moment, then answered: "To answer the young mistress — the Marquis appears to have come empty-handed."

"How stingy of him."

Lu Huaixi murmured. "First visit to someone's home, coming to see a sick person no less, and he didn't even think to bring anything. Don't let him in."

For all her words, Lu Huaixi still released Xie Yuanjing, and even straightened his collar for him.

When she finished and stepped back, Xie Yuanjing caught her hand.

"Where are you going?"

"To sit and wait for you inside."

Lu Huaixi pointed toward the inner room. "Don't argue with him. If you get unhappy, come back early. If you fall ill again, I really won't dance for you."

Xie Yuanjing found her concern too disarming for any cool response.

He held her hand and wouldn't let go. He was quiet for a moment, then said: "Come with me."

Lu Huaixi was a little surprised.

"Then the Marquis will say you're obsessed."

"Am I not?"

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet laugh, then looked at her steadily, his voice low and soft, the restraint and intensity in his gaze held carefully in check.

chapters.title: Try Mentioning Someone Else
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing waited for Lu Huaixi to come back to herself, and for the traces of what had just passed to fade from her expression, before walking with her to the front hall.

Along the way, Lu Huaixi refused to speak to him, turning her head aside in silent indignation.

Xie Yuanjing had half expected her to stay silent the entire way.

He was just beginning to think about how to explain that what had happened just now had been entirely beyond his control, when the moment they caught sight of who had come, her expression changed completely.

The bashful sulkiness fell away entirely.

From the moment she stepped into the front hall and stood at his side, it was as though she had built a wall of iron and stone around him.

Something swelled in Xie Yuanjing's chest — tender and at the same time aching.

But naturally he wasn't going to let her walk ahead.

Xie Yuanjing pressed her hand gently and eased her back slightly, keeping her behind him.

"My lord."

He looked toward the person ahead, his tone unhurried and even.

Lu Huaixi followed suit with a bow, then stepped to the side and called out a greeting.

The front hall fell quiet almost instantly. Even the maidservant who had brought tea made not a sound.

The Marquis of Chengen found that "my lord" deeply grating, and was well aware that he was being met with deliberate coldness. Instinctively he wanted to lose his temper.

"You bring her along even for serious matters — is your head full of nothing else? What can the Marquis's manor still count on you for!"

Lu Huaixi's brow furrowed. Her instinct was to step forward and say something.

What did he mean, his head full of nothing else? And what did he mean the manor couldn't count on him — if they couldn't count on him, why come at all? Wanting everything and giving nothing back — insufferable!

But before her words could come out, Xie Yuanjing spoke first, and the hand holding hers gave a light, gentle squeeze — telling her not to be upset.

"What I do is not for you to oversee."

He paused, then let out a short, cold laugh and went still: "It seems the Marquis did not take my words that day to heart. Keep the Marquis's manor for yourself. Gong Zhuo."

The person outside came in immediately, head bowed.

"See the guest out. From now on, if the Marquis of Chengen comes calling, he is not to be let in."

For a man of the Marquis's standing, to be treated this way by anyone — let alone by his own son — was beyond anything he had experienced.

His eyebrows trembled with the force of his rage. He jabbed a finger and after a long, strangled moment managed to squeeze out the word "Insolent."

Yet Xie Yuanjing didn't spare him a glance, only bowed his head and studied the hand he was holding.

"You are perfectly welcome to vent your fury on me — tear down this residence, press the charge of filial impiety, drive me to the wall, and see if I yield. But I am not He Bingxin. Before the Marquis acts, it would be wise to think clearly about what kind of temperament this son of yours once had."

The mention of He Bingxin cooled the Marquis's anger considerably, and reminded him of why he had come today.

He did have something to ask of the person before him. And with the Marquis's manor in the state it was, he was already finding things increasingly difficult to manage alone.

But that phrase — "this son of yours once had" — sent another wave of fury through him. It felt like deliberate provocation.

He couldn't swallow his pride. He could not bring himself to say anything conciliatory.

He didn't want to, either.

He had other sons. Given time, he could raise another Xie Yuanjing. Especially He Bingxin, who in every way held him in regard.

The Marquis's expression shifted through several changes, uncertain how to break the deadlock.

But he knew — the words "see the guest out" from this son of his were never said idly.

Xie Yuanjing truly did not leave half a step of room.

He had said to send someone, and someone had truly come.

Only before the Marquis reached the full height of his fury, Xie Yuanjing suddenly called out to stop them.

The Marquis looked over, the pressure in his chest easing at last.

"Have you come to your senses about the outrage you've been committing? Today, if you—"

"There's something I forgot to mention to the Marquis."

Xie Yuanjing smiled lightly and looked up. "He Bingxin has a younger brother. One who actually bears the He surname."

The Marquis went still. Then Xie Yuanjing continued:

"That man with the He surname was indeed something of a distant maternal cousin to He Bingxin and his mother — but the connection between them is not some pretense they kept up to protect the Marquis's name in front of outsiders, claiming no ties to him. They had known each other long before the mother and son ever knew you."

The Marquis caught his meaning. Something fractured in his expression, his eyes going dark.

Xie Yuanjing showed no fear at all.

Out of the corner of his eye he caught Lu Huaixi's look of stunned disbelief, and suddenly felt that this kind of thing was not so hard to speak of after all — the people in the story had almost nothing to do with him.

He didn't care.

"What nonsense is this?"

It was a long moment before the Marquis managed to force a few words from his throat.

Xie Yuanjing paid it no mind and continued.

"He Bingxin's younger brother did not survive — he was lost in the same year the woman disappeared. Not long after, the man with the He surname also died suddenly, and the woman was found shortly after, saying she did not wish to be a burden on the Marquis — and moved into the outer residence."

Xie Yuanjing spoke of what had once happened to his own father with complete composure.

The person ahead of him had gone pale and then paler still, and looked as though he had already half-believed it.

"This is not difficult to verify. If the Marquis wishes to know, the people who knew what happened at the time — I can have all of them sent to you."

With that said, Xie Yuanjing looked toward the outer door. "As for whether He Bingxin truly carries the He surname — the Marquis will have to look into that himself. Come — see the guest out."

The Marquis had entirely forgotten what he had come to say.

There were many things he hadn't thought through carefully — he had only ever thought of how much the mother and son had suffered, and of the fact that this woman had been the first he had ever been close to.

He could not bear to picture it — in the days when he had been away at war, thinking of their safety with worry, she had been deceiving him.

From the moment she heard the first word, Lu Huaixi had been frozen in place.

Only when the Marquis's figure had completely disappeared from the courtyard did she notice that her hand had gone red from Xie Yuanjing's grip.

She had no thought for anything else. She turned to face him, eyes wide.

"When did you find out? What surname does He Bingxin actually carry?"

"Not long ago."

Xie Yuanjing saw her expression and the corner of his lips curved. "Why so shocked by other people's business?"

"Well, I do enjoy a bit of excitement — but you..."

Lu Huaixi studied the expression on the face before her.

This was the Marquis of Chengen's affair, after all. She wanted to be sure the person in front of her wasn't suppressing something.

Xie Yuanjing noticed, and drew her in.

"What are you looking at? This has nothing to do with me. I'm not going to care."

"But then He Bingxin—"

"That I genuinely don't know."

Xie Yuanjing said it offhandedly, and held her, walking back with her toward the room. "I said it on a whim."

Truly didn't know — and couldn't be bothered to find out.

Either way, the rift was already there, and a rift like that could never fully heal. He Bingxin would not be going back to the life he once had.

"Not that it matters what name he carries — He Bingxin deserves everything coming to him."

Lu Huaixi said with a light huff: "Who told him not to know when to stop — spending his days trying to drive a wedge between you and your father."

Xie Yuanjing smiled but said nothing.

A father-and-son bond wasn't something that could be driven apart so easily. Things being the way they were had more to do with his father's long-standing dissatisfaction with him.

He Bingxin had added fuel to the fire — but he wasn't the most important piece.

They were almost back to the room when Lu Huaixi finally thought of something.

"The Marquis just left like that — then what was he here for? Was he trying to say something on He Bingxin's behalf, but got so angry he forgot to say it?"

"What else would he come for — to see me?"

"True enough — he didn't even bring anything."

Lu Huaixi still remembered the Marquis arriving empty-handed, and after a moment of thought, drifted warmly back toward Xie Yuanjing.

"Do you think He Bingxin is still waiting — waiting for the Marquis to intervene, waiting to come back and move into the manor sooner once he returns? I'd really love to see his face when all his scheming amounts to nothing. I can imagine how satisfying that would be."

Xie Yuanjing was busy straightening her sleeve and didn't respond right away.

Lu Huaixi didn't mind, talking on happily to herself.

"What on earth was He Bingxin thinking — actively going after an assignment like that? He must have had a lot of confidence in himself. He has that scholarly look about him, and he doesn't seem like someone with absolutely no sense—mmph—"

Before she could finish, Lu Huaixi's mouth was stopped.

Xie Yuanjing bit her, then picked her up and set her down on the table nearby.

"Try it."

"Try what?"

Lu Huaixi was startled, and in the split second of being lifted, had grabbed onto his robes and not let go.

"Try saying someone else's name."

chapters.title: Going Back to the Lu Estate Together
chapters.content:
During the days Xie Yuanjing rested at home, Lu Huaixi finally had some breathing room of her own.

In the meantime, the Marquis of Chengen did not come again, nor did he raise the matter of asking his son to help He Bingxin — it was as though he had suddenly gone quiet.

But the Old Marquis did come by once.
