He was not the same cold and distant figure he had been the first time. He arrived without a word of explanation, wandered east and peered west, as though he had come expressly to look over the residence.

Lu Huaixi didn't follow at first.

She had no great grievance against the Old Marquis — at most, they didn't quite know how to talk to each other.

But before long a maidservant came to ask her to join them.

Lu Huaixi had braced herself for another round of things she wouldn't be able to argue back against. But to her surprise, the Old Marquis asked about the flowers and plants in the courtyard, then asked her a few inconsequential questions about daily life — nothing more than idle, easy conversation.

Right up until the Old Marquis was ready to leave, he had not said a word about what had brought him. Only at the very last moment, as he was about to step into the carriage, did he seem to stop and think better of something.

"Old Marquis, is there something you'd like to tell me?"

Lu Huaixi couldn't hold out any longer and asked herself.

She blinked her clear, guileless eyes at the man who looked torn before her.

Mindful of his age after all, Lu Huaixi quietly tugged at Xie Yuanjing's sleeve and gestured for him to ask as well.

But Xie Yuanjing only smiled and said nothing.

Lu Huaixi found it strange, but she couldn't very well glare at him in front of the Old Marquis — so she kept the smile and waited.

After a long pause, during which the great horse ahead finally lost patience and swished its tail, the Old Marquis let out a sigh and turned to get into the carriage.

"Even if you're not living at the manor for now, calling me Old Marquis over and over doesn't sit right. Say it long enough, and what will people think when they hear it."

He stopped, then turned and looked at her. "Or do you plan to go on swallowing your grievance and refuse to call after him your whole life?"

Lu Huaixi blinked, and understood.

"I'm not swallowing any grievance."

She muttered: "It was you who made it clear there was nothing between Xie Yuanjing and me."

"Did anyone tell me what was going on?"

The Old Marquis's voice sharpened. He couldn't help himself and raised his eyes.

"What do I know about any of what happened between you two? I only said what I said that day, and in the end it was you who threw it right back at me. And now here I am, an elder, coming in good grace to say all of this — and I can't even get one word of 'grandfather' out of you?"

Lu Huaixi's eyes went wide too, and her mouth opened, but nothing came out.

What was happening?

The Old Marquis had been steering her through his residence in the cold wind this whole time — and that was his way of making amends?

Lu Huaixi sat with it for a moment without a word, then looked at Xie Yuanjing once, and finally, obediently, called out: "Grandfather."

The Old Marquis was satisfied at last. He lifted the curtain and settled into the carriage.

Back in the room, Lu Huaixi stopped the still quietly smiling Xie Yuanjing and poked him in the chest.

"You knew the Old Marquis was coming to say all of this, didn't you?"

Xie Yuanjing let her finish, then took her fingertips in his hand and smiled: "Why aren't you calling him grandfather now?"

Lu Huaixi gave a small huff, then after a moment said, in a much softer voice: "None of your business."

"It is my business."

Xie Yuanjing drew her back into his arms, his face resting against the side of her neck to gather himself, then said: "Otherwise, who would carry you around and kiss you? Who would kiss you until you almost cry? Who would spend whole nights coaxing you?"

"You—"

Lu Huaixi pushed at him. "How can you say something like that without a trace of shame?"

The only reply was Xie Yuanjing's quiet laughter.

When the two of them were together, Xie Yuanjing was always direct about how he felt, never willing to disguise it.

Almost every day he would tease her once, and tell her once how he felt about her.

"Alright, don't be upset with me. I didn't know at first why grandfather was coming."

"Then once you figured it out, why didn't you warn me?"

"What would warning you have accomplished?"

Seeing that she wasn't truly angry, Xie Yuanjing kissed her twice and watched her. "Last time it was grandfather who spoke out of turn with you. Today, the fact that grandfather was willing to come and talk to you himself means he felt he'd been in the wrong that time too."

Lu Huaixi blinked and was quiet for a moment.

After a little while she looked up and met Xie Yuanjing's gaze.

"Does this also mean the Old Marquis has chosen you over the Marquis?"

"I suppose."

Xie Yuanjing answered without much feeling about it.

Lu Huaixi waited a little longer, not sure what she was thinking, and just as Xie Yuanjing was about to ask, she spoke, her voice quieter.

"It's not really the Old Marquis's fault, actually. He truly didn't know anything at the time — and to him I was practically a stranger."

"No — grandfather would have said what he said even if he had known."

Xie Yuanjing's voice carried a note of apology. "Those words should have fallen on me, but since I was unconscious, you took them instead. Grandfather holds me to a standard unlike anyone else — the more disappointed he is in my father, the less room there is for me to fall short."

"But now — it won't be like that anymore, will it?"

"No. Not in the future either."

Lu Huaixi asked nothing more, and simply held him back quietly.

She had a faint sense of it — the news of He Bingxin and his mother would probably come as a blow to the Marquis of Chengen, and managing the manor was growing more and more taxing for him.

The Old Marquis was also aging, and would find things increasingly beyond his strength.

He would probably come again — hinting, in ways deliberate or not, for Xie Yuanjing to return.

But Xie Yuanjing wouldn't agree.

Lu Huaixi was beginning to know this person's mind well enough to see the fox in him, and she understood — they would be living in this residence for a good while yet.

Still, she was glad. She liked this.

"Let's go back to the Lu estate in a few days."

Lu Huaixi said suddenly: "Not you sending me, and not you coming to collect me — but you and me going back together. Would that be alright?"

Xie Yuanjing was quiet for a moment. Lu Huaixi waited, growing a little puzzled, and looked up.

"Why aren't you saying anything?"

"I've been waiting so long for this — are you really asking if it's alright?"

"You weren't saying anything."

"I was caught off guard."

Xie Yuanjing admitted to a rare moment of vulnerability, then smiled and spoke earnestly: "I don't know how many gifts to bring. If I go by the scale of formal betrothal gifts — would that be enough?"

—

"It will absolutely be enough. You can rest easy, young mistress. The kitchen has already added many more dishes."

A few days later at the Lu estate, Lady Liu had been making preparations since early morning, the moment word reached her that Lu Huaixi would be arriving today.

Lady Liu had been quietly troubled of late.

Her daughter hadn't come back in all this time, and that day's incident wasn't something she could simply send someone to ask about. It had been lodged in her chest ever since — stuck somewhere between up and down.

She had also turned the situation over many times, and found that Xie Yuanjing was both suitable and not.

He was suitable, naturally, for his ability and decisiveness — when everyone had written him off, he had shed his duties without a flicker of change in his face, calm and unhurried.

But that was also precisely why he was unsuitable.

A man like this — it was not certain that Huaixi could keep a firm footing with him.

And in the future, that back courtyard would surely not remain with only one noble lady. There might be others — perhaps ones willing to lower themselves, willing to make themselves less.

It depended entirely on how much ambition this Xie had, and how heavily he weighed his future against everything else.

Lady Liu stifled a few more sighs.

She hadn't breathed a word of any of this to anyone, and was only thinking that today she ought to find a moment — to ask, slowly and carefully.

chapters.title: There Is No Such Thing as Separation
chapters.content:
When Lady Liu went out to receive them, what she saw was her own daughter jumping down from the carriage, and then — in full view of everyone — throwing herself at Xie Yuanjing.

"Was I heavier?"

"You could stand to be a little heavier."

Xie Yuanjing answered her and raised a hand to steady her.

Lady Liu opened her mouth but said nothing. The maidservant beside her stifled a laugh and murmured: "The young miss and the young master really get along well. Before this, your servant thought the young master was difficult and short-tempered."

While she was speaking, the two ahead heard the movement and looked over.

Lu Huaixi caught sight of her mother, her body stiffening for a fraction of a second, a flash of embarrassment crossing her face — followed quickly by shyness.

But it lasted only a moment.

Very soon, she released Xie Yuanjing, cleared her throat with practiced composure, and trotted over to Lady Liu with a smile.

"Mother, how did you end up coming out to meet us?"

She glanced back at the man a step behind her, then looked back at her mother. "Were you missing me?"

Lady Liu swallowed her thoughts and said, helplessly: "Missing you — with no word from you for so long."

"Your daughter has been so busy lately."

As she finished, Xie Yuanjing came up and stopped before Lady Liu.

"Aunt."

He dipped his head slightly, his voice steady.

Lady Liu paused, answered him with some hesitation, then looked up — and stopped herself from saying more.

But right beside her was her daughter's beaming face, and whatever she had wanted to say could only be swallowed back.

Xie Yuanjing was perceptive as always — one look and he could tell something was off with Lady Liu.

Just then, the Lu family's master happened to have a moment away from his duties and returned home. Xie Yuanjing didn't linger, and politely excused himself to follow the man toward his study.

Watching him use such a thoughtful pretense to take himself away, Lady Liu felt something complicated stir in her chest.

"Mother, what are you thinking? You're not even listening to me."

Lady Liu came back to herself, gathered her thoughts, and walked back to the inner courtyard with her daughter.

Only when no one else was nearby did Lady Liu close the door and call Lu Huaixi to come before her.

"Mother?"

"What is the situation between you and Xie Yuanjing?"

Lady Liu asked: "I saw everything just now — you didn't try to hide from anyone at all when you got off the carriage."

Lu Huaixi was caught off guard, and for a moment looked down, twisting the handkerchief in her hands.

She had come back today precisely to lay things out clearly with her family — to make Xie Yuanjing truly become the Lu family's second son-in-law.

But with her mother asking just like this, Lu Huaixi felt a wave of shyness that took quite a while to settle.

Yet the distance between her embarrassment and her honesty was only a moment.

Once her heart landed, she looked up at her mother, eyes curved with warmth, and said with sincerity: "I like him."

Before Lady Liu could compose an expression to respond, Lu Huaixi thought a moment and said it again.

"Mother — I like Xie Yuanjing. And he likes me."

The directness of a young girl's feeling was like light — warm and vivid.

Even with the flush already rising in her cheeks, and the handkerchief crumpled in her hands, she still made her admission with steadiness and boldness.

Lady Liu had already partly guessed — but hearing her own daughter say it like this, without reservation, word after word so open and so sweet, she suddenly didn't know how to reply.

Most of what she had prepared was persuasion.

She was a mother, and also the mistress of the Lu family's main household.

The balance of advantage and risk that she could see would always be far greater than what young Lu Huaixi could see.

But in this moment, she looked at her daughter's eyes.

She looked at the brightness in those dark pupils — the delight reflected there, and the hope stirring in their depths, hoping for approval — and she found herself suddenly uncertain: whether she should say anything at all.

"When did this start?"

"A long time ago."

Lu Huaixi did not receive the response she had been hoping for.

But she wasn't discouraged either. She thought for a moment, then lowered her eyes and said quietly: "I was the one who fell for him first."

The implication being that Xie Yuanjing had not charmed or deceived her into it.

"I don't want to separate from him, Mother."

"You—"

Lady Liu felt an ache beginning at her temple.

Those words, in her ears, sounded rather rash.

"Do you know what you're saying?"

"I know, Mother. I don't want to separate."

"There will be no separation. Huaixi and I — there is no such thing."

In the study, Xie Yuanjing's voice fell.

The Lu family's master frowned slightly, as though not quite following.

He had come home today with legitimate matters to discuss with Xie Yuanjing. Beyond that, he had been weighing whether, when the time came for Huaixi and her husband to go their separate ways, he ought to send her south for a while.

Once she came back to the capital after the journey, the matter of the Lu second young miss's separation would have faded from people's minds.

Even if anyone brought it up again, enough time would have passed for it to lose its bite.

The Lu family's master had even been thinking about looking into suitable young men for his daughter sooner rather than later — and if necessary, he might even ask Xie Yuanjing to take a look. The man knew a great deal and read people well.

But now — he was saying there would be no separation.

"Whose intention is this? Yours, or Huaixi's?"

"It is my intention."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his head slightly, the air of pressure he usually carried softened somewhat.

He looked nothing like the man who sat across a table from you in negotiation — there was a deference and a sincerity to him.

"My feelings for Huaixi are genuine. Although this arrangement was unlike others at the start, I have never treated it carelessly. Since I brought Huaixi into my household, I have never thought of her as someone outside my life. I do not wish to separate, and I do not wish to treat this marriage as a transaction any longer. I hope you will allow it."

"What do you mean, allow it — is Huaixi willing?"

The Lu family's master frowned. He clearly was not in agreement.

If none of the initial circumstances had applied, a marriage like this taking root would naturally have been a good thing.

But both of them had known from the beginning it was an arrangement. It was even Xie Yuanjing who had first proposed making it a partnership.

"I don't want to argue with you about the sincerity of your feelings. All I know is that when things began, you did not treat this marriage as real. I know my daughter's character — she is soft-hearted, and her resolve is easily bent. Having spent so much time with you, it's natural that she would feel some warmth toward you, and be willing to follow your lead. But this marriage—"

"She did not follow my lead. I fell for her first — and at first she did not agree."

Xie Yuanjing's brow drew together, almost imperceptibly.

He didn't like anyone speaking of Lu Huaixi that way. Not even her father.

"In matters that count, she is very clearheaded. I waited for her for a long time before she was willing to give me a chance. She is not as easily swayed as you suggest."

The Lu family's master was momentarily at a loss.

The tone of the man before him was as though he had said something unkind — and this person had begun to take Lu Huaixi's side.

Which was almost laughable. He was her father. No one was less likely to speak ill of his daughter.

"Even so — an arrangement like yours isn't something that can be settled just because you say a few words."

The Lu family's master said: "I know that Xie Yuanjing is capable — many people see you as an excellent match. But I don't need my daughter to marry the most powerful man. I only want her to live peacefully and happily. If the palace matter hadn't pulled her in, I would never have let her go to the Marquis's manor."

"I also want only for her to live peacefully and happily."

Xie Yuanjing's tone remained steady, and he didn't give ground by a single step.

"In my household, she will always be free to do what she wishes — whether at the manor or elsewhere, I, Xie Yuanjing, will never allow her to suffer the slightest grievance, and will do everything in my power to give her the best life I can."

"A few words from you, and I should believe them?"

"I can also show you, with action."

After a beat, Xie Yuanjing lifted his gaze slightly. "You likely already have some sense of how much I have in hand by now. I am willing to give over half of it — as a measure of my sincerity, so that you can set your mind at ease."

That gave the Lu family's master pause.

He studied the person before him, his gaze sharp and assessing.

"With a single sentence of 'half,' I couldn't possibly not take it. You're truly willing?"

"If it were for anyone else, naturally it would be hard to part with. But giving it to you — we are all family."

"You—"

Before long, a knock sounded at the door from outside.

The Lu family's master drew back his words and called out for the person to come in.

"It's nearly time to eat, Father."

The door opened, and Lu Huaixi poked her head in first to have a look.

When she saw that the atmosphere in the room felt a little strange, she stepped fully inside and came to a stop beside Xie Yuanjing.

"What are you two talking about?"

The Lu family's master, seeing his daughter whose loyalties had so obviously already shifted, held his tongue.

Xie Yuanjing also had no desire for Lu Huaixi to know at this moment that her father was not entirely in agreement.

He smiled at her, and reached up to tuck back the loose strands of hair the wind had blown across her face — then, before the Lu family's master had time to look displeased, drew her gently behind him.

The Lu family's master was caught off guard.

In front of his own daughter, he had apparently been treated as a flood requiring a dam.

chapters.title: I Fell First
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi was completely bewildered.

She stood behind Xie Yuanjing, dimly sensing that her father was somewhat displeased.

But why would he be displeased?

Her mother had only just said that her father had deliberately carved out time to come home for this very visit, to see her, discuss proper matters with Xie Yuanjing, and then share a meal together.

Lu Huaixi's delicate brows knit slightly. After a moment, a flash of clarity cut through her mind.

She instinctively reached back and took Xie Yuanjing's hand, forcing herself to remain composed as she looked toward her father.

Sure enough, a flicker of disapproval crossed her father's eyes, and a trace of displeasure was written between his brows.

"Father, you......"

She hesitated before speaking. Though she felt a little uneasy, and though she had no wish to truly anger him, she still did not release Xie Yuanjing's hand.

"Are you angry because I don't want to dissolve the marriage?"

She frowned, genuinely at a loss.

Master Lu's brow twitched. He felt as though whatever he said now would come too late.

But he could not say nothing.

To simply hand his daughter over like this, and to a man who had sought her hand with ulterior motives from the very beginning, was something he could not bring himself to accept.

"Yes."

"But, why?"

"Why? Do you know what sort of man is standing beside you, do you know what intentions he harbored when he first came to seek your hand, do you know how long his promises will hold? And as for all the vexing affairs of the marquis's household, all the dealings of the inner court, how much patience do you honestly think you have for any of it?"

There were things Master Lu left unsaid.

Right now, she did not want to dissolve the marriage simply because there was no one else in that inner courtyard.

Xie Yuanjing, too, did not have much inclination for affairs of the heart, and the two of them got on with an ease that felt novel to them both.

But how long could that ease last? And how many times had she witnessed the cold, ruthless side of Xie Yuanjing?

"You say you don't want to dissolve the marriage out of passing feeling, but have you considered that if you truly don't——"

"But I already knew his reasons for seeking my hand."

Lu Huaixi blinked, picking up where her father had left off with an air of genuine incomprehension.

"I married him with my own agenda as well. When I agreed to marry him, I had no feelings for him either. So the terms on which we began were exactly the same, were they not?"

Master Lu could not find words. Lu Huaixi waited a moment, then continued.

"I don't think it's right to let the uncertainties of the future cast judgment on the present. As for what you say about the inner court, about Xie Yuanjing's faults — if I were to dissolve this marriage and marry someone else, I would still have to get to know that person, still have to judge whether he is good or not, and I would still end up confined to an inner courtyard all the same."

"Your father never said he was not a good man. What your father means is that your temperament does not suit him or the Marquis household."

"Then whose temperament would suit it?"

Lu Huaixi knitted her brows. "Father, I don't feel that we are unsuited. From the very beginning I thought he was wonderful, and wonderful to me."

"I think you've been so thoroughly charmed by him your head has been turned. I say one thing and you give me ten rebuttals. How long have the two of you even been living together? I see him at court nearly every single day. Do you think I don't know whether he is a good man, whether you are suited?"

Master Lu could not argue her down.

He had no wish to truly scold her, yet he could not bring himself to be at ease with Xie Yuanjing, could not simply acquiesce.

He was just about to speak again when Xie Yuanjing chose that moment to break his silence.

He drew Lu Huaixi behind him once more, giving her hand a gentle squeeze to signal her not to speak.

"Father-in-law, what happened today was presumptuous of me. The fault is entirely mine. But even if it were to happen again, this is still something I would want you to know: it is I who first developed feelings for her. Do not fault her. And the promise I made just now still holds——"

"That's not right. I fell first."

Lu Huaixi's voice came from behind him, cutting Xie Yuanjing's words abruptly short.

"Father just said I've had my head turned, but that isn't so. I liked him long before any of this."

Xie Yuanjing forgot there was someone else before them.

He turned, gazing fixedly at Lu Huaixi before him, something stirring and shifting in the depths of his eyes. He said nothing.

Lu Huaixi glanced at him once, then looked away.

She pressed her lips together and did not allow herself to retreat. As she had done before her mother, and with even more conviction this time, she said it again.

"I was the one who fell for him first. So if anyone is to be blamed, it should be me."

Before his two daughters, Master Lu was nothing but a paper tiger.

Even his scolding never lasted long. At most he would raise his voice for a moment or two, then wait for his wife to come and smooth things over, and before long all would be well again.

His wife was not here now. Before him stood only his daughter, looking crestfallen with her head bowed, and beside her, a very capable Xie Yuanjing who had managed to carry his daughter away.

It was as though something was lodged in his throat. He could not get a single word out.

In the end it was Xie Yuanjing who suppressed the turmoil within himself and spoke first to Lu Huaixi, breaking the impasse.

"Weren't you just coming to tell us that your mother wants us to prepare for dinner?"

"Oh, yes."

Lu Huaixi remembered why she had come and nodded quickly. "Mother said she personally made a stew today and has gone to check on it before we eat."

Xie Yuanjing kept his hold on Lu Huaixi's hand, but his gaze shifted to the man before them.

Though still somewhat displeased, Master Lu followed the shift in topic and spoke. "Then let us go to dinner. Don't keep your mother waiting."

"Alright."

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but purse her lips. "Here, Mother always comes first with Father. You're exactly like that yourself, and yet you still scold me."

Master Lu was left speechless by this remark. Too weary to take offense, he flicked his sleeve and walked out of the study.

Behind him, Xie Yuanjing kept his hold on the young woman at his side, his grip growing tighter with each step.

"Not so tight."

"When?"

Suppressing the urge to pull her into his arms, Xie Yuanjing kept his voice low and asked, slowly and deliberately, with complete seriousness: "This falling first that you mentioned. When was it?"

In the courtyard, the autumn wind stirred the slender branches.

Now and then a yellowed leaf was lifted by the breeze, drifting and spiraling in the sunlight.

Lu Huaixi had at first been too shy to look at him, which was why she had turned her eyes to the falling leaves and the gentle wind.

But the autumn day made her heart tremble.

"When they were all still green."

Lu Huaixi laughed suddenly.

Her curving eyes reflected the swaying branches and leaves.

Xie Yuanjing could not kiss her. He stood before her, his dark eyes cast slightly downward, his pupils holding the image of Lu Huaixi's beautiful, clear face.

He was moved, and he regretted.

The regret was a chest full of bitter ache, the knowledge that he had come to understand too late. And the being moved was like tasting a crisp, sweet autumn fruit, like having finally obtained what he had long wished for.

chapters.title: The Ending (Part One): Can We Kiss a Little Longer Tonight?
chapters.content:
That meal passed in the end with a quiet ease.

Doting on their daughter was something Master Lu and his wife had always done naturally and well.

Lady Liu had so much she wanted to say, but none of it could stand against her daughter's ardent and candid declaration: I was the one who fell for him first.

Lady Liu worried more than most, but she was a woman who had lived and learned.

She knew that her reservations could only be answered with time, whether proven right or wrong.

She also quickly recalled the several occasions when Xie Yuanjing had come in person to bring her daughter home, and the attentiveness and care she had sensed in him then, which had exceeded what she had allowed herself to believe.

And compared to the tempered hesitation of Lady Lu, Master Lu was considerably more agitated.

That Xie Yuanjing was willing to relinquish what he held in his hands had indeed surprised him. But what unsettled him now was not a question of ability, or whether this man was capable or not.

What unsettled him was that his daughter had truly begun to speak on someone else's behalf, that the person she now held closest in her heart was someone else.

This was perhaps the common affliction of most fathers.

When this marriage had been nothing more than an arrangement, he had found nothing to fault in Xie Yuanjing. He had even thought on occasion that the Marquis of Cheng'en lacked discernment, overlooking such a fine son in favor of standing up for some unremarkable, obscure scholar.

But now that this marriage looked very likely to endure, Master Lu found no shortage of things to criticize in Xie Yuanjing.

Too overbearing here, too cold-blooded there.

Too decisive in action, too calculating in thought.

All in all there were problems everywhere, and yet none that could actually be said aloud.

Lu Huaixi naturally noticed her father's unhappiness. Before leaving, she deliberately poured him a cup of tea and called out to him, her voice soft with a hint of grievance.

That pitiful tone of hers was enough to make Lady Liu's heart clench as well.

When they finally saw their daughter off, Master Lu still wore a stiff, unyielding expression. Yet he stiffly instructed both of them to come back for dinner next time.

And after all of this, Xie Yuanjing had, in truth, secured his name.

That very evening, he even had the chance to watch a new dance Lu Huaixi had choreographed.

It was the first time he had ever seen Lu Huaixi dance.

Her slender waist was wrapped in gauze that hinted and concealed in equal measure. She dipped down and rose again, appearing fragile at first glance, yet with a resilience quietly held within.

Brilliant long sleeves unfurled with the shifting light, tracing one graceful arc after another. She looked more like a celestial being come to earth than any figure painted on a scroll.

When the music ceased, Lu Huaixi was breathing lightly.

The attendants in the outer room quietly withdrew, leaving the qin behind.

Lu Huaixi went to sit before it, her fingertips drifting between the strings.

Xie Yuanjing had been lost in her dancing at first, and then he was lost in her music.

It was the first time he had seen this side of Lu Huaixi. His heart stirred as though water had been set to a rolling boil, his pulse leaping without rest.

He walked toward her, and at the moment the last note fell, he lifted her into his arms.

Several layers of skirt fanned out and cascaded down, tracing the slender line of her figure.

She instinctively raised her arms to loop them around Xie Yuanjing's neck, and as she shifted in his hold, her fragrance drifted with her.

"Is this what you wear, every time you dance?"

When Xie Yuanjing spoke, his voice was already an extreme rasp. He carried her steadily into the inner room.

Even when he sat down on the bed, his arms did not loosen.

The candlelight in the inner room was somewhat dimmer than that of the outer room.

But this only made the darkness of Xie Yuanjing's eyes more apparent, and cast over the whole of him an air that was difficult to name, dangerous.

"Besides the people in your Shun'an Fang, who else has seen you like this?"

Lu Huaixi looked up at him.

Watching him draw closer, yet deliberately holding himself at three inches' distance as if to torment her, she blinked and thought better of teasing him with a yes.

"This dress is a new alteration I had made a few days ago."

Lu Huaixi said softly, "The original design you've seen before. And the other clothes I wear for dancing, you've seen those too, the last time, in the chest where I keep the albums."

In other words, only this once.

Some of the tension eased from Xie Yuanjing. His arms tightened around her, and his lips pressed close.

But nothing else moved. After a moment, he bit lightly at her lip and asked, "How many people have seen you? Was Shen Yue, the one Princess Qinghe wanted to meet, you?"

"Oh, the people who've seen me, there are really quite a few. Let me count......"

The grip at her waist suddenly tightened again. Lu Huaixi couldn't help laughing, and then she leaned back, slipping out of the way of his mouth at her neck.

"That tickles, stop it."

"Weren't you going to count? Go ahead, let me hear it."

"I was only teasing you, stop biting."

Only when she felt Xie Yuanjing finally stop did Lu Huaixi lean back against him properly. "If you bite me again I won't tell you anything."

"Alright. You talk first."

"There really have been quite a few people, but they were all the young women of Shun'an Fang."

Lu Huaixi spoke as she toyed idly with his sleeve.

"Though not dances like tonight, and not these skirts either, only very ordinary ones. As for Shen Yue, only two senior attendants know, along with two skilled dancers."

"Why?"

"Shen Yue has no need to meet other people. Her dances come from impulse, purely for her own pleasure. When she is willing to teach, she has no need to show her face either."

"So tonight, you prepared it all especially for me. The dance, the dress, the music as well. Didn't you?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing, but the answer was plain.

Xie Yuanjing kissed her again and again, one after another, until he was satisfied. Only then did he hold her close and speak.

"I won't stop you from doing what you love. But I mind others watching you. If it is a woman, I will try to bear it. Anyone else, I cannot."

"What do you mean, anyone else? That just means men."

Lu Huaixi settled into a more comfortable position in his arms, nestling against him, then laughed. "And yet even women you only try to bear. Such a jealous husband."

"Yes, I am. And if you're wearing a dress like this, even women won't do."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his head, and those last words were spoken almost against her lips.

The moment they left his mouth, he parted her lips and swallowed whatever reply she might have given.

His desire was unmistakable. The hand at her waist slid to the small of her back, holding her close against him.

Only when the room was filled with nothing but the sound of their breathing did Xie Yuanjing ease back slightly.

He looked at her lips, then reached up and gently pressed the corner of her mouth for a moment.

"They've gone red."

He murmured, "How do they redden so easily? Your face too, and your skin as well."

Lu Huaixi felt herself go soft all over. Sensing that he would say even more things she would have no defense against, she raised her hand and tried her best to cover his mouth.

Her palm was kissed almost at once. Then Xie Yuanjing's voice came, as though muffled by cotton, low and hushed, even the light laughter in it muffled.

"Can we kiss a little longer tonight?"

He leaned in again, unwilling to be still even with her palm between them. "I want to keep kissing you."

"No——"

Lu Huaixi's refusal was ignored.

As the kissing continued, his voice dropped to something softer. "It's a little uncomfortable. Help me, won't you?"

chapters.title: The Ending (Part Two): I'm Not Going Anywhere
chapters.content:
Ever since the time Xie Yuanjing had said he would teach her certain other things, Lu Huaixi had found herself wondering from time to time what those other things might be.

It was not until today, when he lay holding her and took her hand in his, that she understood what it meant to ease his discomfort.

Even after Xie Yuanjing had personally cleaned her hands for her, and she had bathed and come back, she still could not collect herself from what had just happened.

Nearly every time she so much as glanced at him, Lu Huaixi would involuntarily recall the moment before.

His ragged breathing, the low and hoarse sounds he had murmured against her ear, softer than anything she had ever heard from him, and the words he had said, words that could not be spoken to another soul.

The more Lu Huaixi thought, the hotter she became, her face burning.

Yet she could not stop herself. Whether her eyes were open or closed, all she saw was the image of Xie Yuanjing from moments ago.

A beauty and an allure she had never witnessed before.

Soon Xie Yuanjing drew her back into his arms, carrying with him the freshness that lingered after a bath.

"Are you tired?"

He pressed a kiss to her forehead, not daring to repeat what he had done before. "Don't be angry with me. Alright?"

Lu Huaixi bit his shoulder and made a small sound but said nothing.

The sound was soft and faint, gone almost before it arrived.

But the one beside her was Xie Yuanjing, who had been half-mad with longing for her.

"Don't torment me."

Xie Yuanjing heard the sound and let out a low laugh, drawing her close again and breathing in slowly.

But before long he suddenly sat up.

"Where are you going?"

Lu Huaixi still harbored some lingering displeasure, yet in that moment she instinctively caught his hand. "Are you going out? It's so late."

"I'm not going out."

Xie Yuanjing turned back and kissed her again. "I'm going to pour you some water. You drink a sip, then sleep."

It was the first time he had come to know what it was like to share such moments with Lu Huaixi. The desire he had suppressed for so long had nearly exceeded what he could contain.

But what satisfied him even more deeply was the trust and reliance he saw in Lu Huaixi's eyes.

He could go nowhere now. As long as she was here, he could not possibly leave her side.

When he returned with the water, Lu Huaixi's eyes were heavy with sleep. She looked as though she was forcing herself to stay awake, as though she might drop off at any second.

Xie Yuanjing helped her to a sip, then set the cup aside, and extinguished one of the lamps.

The person in the bed, who had been fighting sleep all along, did not close her eyes until he lay down. She drifted instinctively toward his side of the bed.

She murmured something, her voice small and drowsy.

"Don't go. I don't want to sleep alone."

"Alright."

Xie Yuanjing held her close. "I'll stay right here with you. I'm not going anywhere."

——

The days they spent together passed quickly.

From autumn into winter, Lu Huaixi always felt as though they had barely had any time to simply be close before the weather had turned thoroughly cold.

With it came the liveliness that the approaching New Year brought.

They were still living in the house outside, with no plans to return to the Marquis's estate. The task of seeing to things for the occasion fell to Lu Huaixi.

She loved this sort of thing. Every item she chose well made their home a little more beautiful and a little more festive.

Today was no different. When Xie Yuanjing came home, he found Lu Huaixi smiling as she directed people in hanging lanterns.

Winter darkness fell early, and not long after Xie Yuanjing arrived, the light had already drained entirely from outside.

He gestured for those nearby to withdraw, then came up behind her and wrapped his arms around her, burying his face against the curve of her neck, unwilling to move.

"Today was exhausting."

Xie Yuanjing rarely said he was tired, so whenever he did, Lu Huaixi felt it must be serious.

"Then let's go inside and rest first."

She coaxed him gently and set aside whatever was in her hands, placing it nearby. "Tomorrow is a rest day. We won't go anywhere, we'll just stay home and take it easy."

"Yes. And you're not going anywhere either."

Xie Yuanjing reached out and held her hand, looking down at her soft, pink fingertips. "I'm exhausted. I want to soak in the pool."

Now that winter had come, the pool had become increasingly useful.

Lu Huaixi thought nothing of it and, at his words, instructed someone to prepare towels and heat the water.

"Then I'll wait for you. I bought so many things today, I'll show them to you when you're done."

"Where will you wait for me?"

"In the room, of course."

Lu Huaixi turned her head slightly to look at him, but the moment she moved, he kissed the corner of her mouth.

"No. You're coming with me."

Xie Yuanjing straightened up slightly after the kiss and hooked his arm around her, drawing her back against him and wrapping her entirely inside his crane-feather cloak.

The snow had begun to fall, soft and weightless, drifting into the covered walkway every now and then and settling on the cloak.

Xie Yuanjing blocked the wind and kept her thoroughly warm.

"Come soak with me. Bring the album."

Xie Yuanjing said this without a flicker of self-consciousness. "There is too much I still need to learn in advance. I haven't started on the later sections."

Lu Huaixi shot him a look and said nothing.

The bathhouse that evening was filled with warm mist for a long while.

Sounds rose from the pool that made the heart quiver.

Lu Huaixi's eyes were flushed at the corners as she leaned against him, listening to his coaxing words interspersed with ragged breathing that he could no longer suppress, feeling as though her entire body had been set over a fire to roast.

But she was truly worn out, languid and soft, her hands draped over him, too tired even to form words.

When she did not speak, Xie Yuanjing only continued to coax her.

One phrase after another, with a few improper ones woven in, but far more were tender apologies murmured low against her.

In truth, when it came to restraint, Xie Yuanjing was still holding firmly to it.

After each moment of desire, that look would linger in the depths of his eyes long after, unwilling to fade. Even then, even with the kissing, even with the closeness that went further still, he would ultimately draw it all back into patience and self-restraint.

He wanted more of her, every single day.

But he retained a thread of reason, and had no intention of pressing further just yet.

The next morning, Xie Yuanjing opened his eyes.

The person beside him had not yet woken, curled against him, her thick lashes lowered, showing a curling sweep at the tips.

Below that was the delicate lift of her nose, and her lips, faintly flushed and full. Endlessly lovely.

Xie Yuanjing held her close and felt only that the person in his arms was soft and warm, giving him a steadiness and peace of mind he had never known before.

He looked at her for a long while, and at last lowered his head to kiss her.

Lu Huaixi could not tell whether she was dreaming. She was deeply sleepy and wanted very much to go on sleeping.

But the moment her lips parted, something stole in, and the instant her tongue moved it was caught and held.

The warmth that followed grew.

Lu Huaixi blearily opened her eyes and found Xie Yuanjing before her, his gaze tinged red, desire clearly written in them.

She thought this man was truly insufferable.

Last night, and now again this morning.

But before she could push him away or lose her temper, the moment was interrupted by someone outside.

——

Lu Yuanzhao had come to visit Lu Huaixi, bringing with him some snacks their mother had sent along for her.

Watching her shuffle out, clearly just woken, he was just about to tease her a little when he noticed a Xie Yuanjing following behind her who seemed, to some degree, not entirely pleased.

Lu Yuanzhao felt an inexplicable sense of pressure bearing down on him.

He raised a hand to touch his nose, privately thinking that this second brother-in-law of his really did not seem easy to get along with.

But then it occurred to him that such a formidable person still had to call him brother when standing next to Lu Huaixi, and he suddenly felt as though he were floating on air.

He was very impressive, actually. He wasn't afraid of Xie Yuanjing in the slightest.

He was still thinking this when Lu Huaixi waved a hand in front of his face.

"What's the matter? You come over this early and then just stand there saying nothing."

"I brought things for you."

Lu Yuanzhao quickly came back to himself, and noticing Xie Yuanjing give him a nod, he returned it a little awkwardly.

"Mother had some of your favorite winter snacks made. She also had someone track down the seedlings you mentioned a few days ago. I was coming this way anyway, so I brought them along."

At the mention of these things, Lu Huaixi located a pot sitting in a corner nearby and walked over, crouching down beside it.

"Mother is the best!"

"It's this cold, and you want something like that. I don't know whether you'll be able to keep it alive."

"The book says you can. I'm not sure either."

Lu Huaixi smiled and added, "How is everyone at home? I was meaning to ask Mother, actually, about how you usually manage things for the New Year."

"Isn't that still a ways off?"

Lu Yuanzhao saw that she was in good spirits and smiled along with her, continuing the conversation. "Things at home are fine. I heard Third Uncle may be returning to the capital after New Year's, but Second Branch is not doing so well."

Lu Huaixi had just finished sorting through the soil and was about to stand up.

At those words she turned her head on instinct. The momentary distraction was all it took, and her footing gave way, her body tipping sideways toward the incense table.

Lu Yuanzhao had not yet reacted when Xie Yuanjing, who had been standing there with an unhurried expression, lunged forward in an instant and pulled her into his arms.

"Be careful. You'll knock your head and cry."

"You startled me."

Lu Huaixi patted her chest. "How could I possibly knock my head?"

"You'd cry just the same if you bumped anything else."

Xie Yuanjing finished speaking and looked toward the person outside. "From now on, keep the incense burner further away. Don't put things where my wife walks."

Lu Yuanzhao pressed his lips together.

He looked at the Xie Yuanjing who was supposed to be cold and unreadable, then looked at the increasingly pampered Lu Huaixi, and finally turned his head away.

Out of sight, out of mind.

chapters.title: The Ending (Part Three): That Day, She Said Something to Me
chapters.content:
When Lu Yuanzhao left, the snow outside had just stopped.

Lu Huaixi walked him out, with Xie Yuanjing naturally following the whole way.

Lu Yuanzhao, though a little exasperated by the two of them being so inseparable, could not help standing just a little straighter.

He was the elder brother, after all.

Before long the two of them turned and went back inside.

After seeing her brother off, Lu Huaixi had grown a little quieter, though she was not unhappy exactly, only looking as though she was turning something over in her mind.

"Aside from your parents and me, nothing else in the world is worth spending your thoughts on."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his gaze as he warmed her hands between his. "Whenever you want to go to the Lu family home, I'll go with you."

Lu Huaixi came back to herself and looked at him. Her lips curved, and she said, "But I still have my elder brother and elder sister."

Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed slightly. He said nothing for a long moment, and then finally acquiesced with a single sound. "Then we'll add two more."

Seeing his reluctance, Lu Huaixi found it amusing.

She used to feel that Xie Yuanjing had little in the way of other emotions, and even when he did, they were hidden behind a layer of distance, impossible to read clearly.

But now it was different.

Now she could see every shade of what Xie Yuanjing felt, some things he concealed, others he chose to show her.

Thinking of this, Lu Huaixi felt something soften in her chest, and she flung herself toward him.

"Were you thinking I was in a bad mood? Because of Second Branch, or because you heard about He Jingxing taking his own life?"

Without waiting for Xie Yuanjing to respond, Lu Huaixi continued on her own. "I was surprised, yes. But I'm not in low spirits. As far as I'm concerned, Second Branch stopped being family to me long ago."

When Lu Yuanzhao had mentioned He Jingxing's suicide just now, Lu Huaixi had indeed felt a jolt of shock.

And hearing that Lu Tangshu had not found peace after all, that she had in fact run back to the Lu family home on one occasion seeking help, Lu Huaixi would not be moved to pity, but her emotions were not entirely undisturbed.

The He family had no desire to lose face.

In order to maintain the appearance of propriety, they would naturally leave no visible marks on Lu Tangshu.

But the grinding contempt and quiet persecution would not be spared. After all, the way she and He Jingxing had been seen together had damaged not only her own reputation but the He family's as well.

The mistress of the He household would not easily forgive either of the two people who had brought a stain upon her son's name.

He Jingxing was beyond salvaging, and so next would come Lu Tangshu.

She would not have a good life.

"What your brother told you earlier was not quite complete."

Xie Yuanjing met her eyes and took up the thread of the conversation.

"Your Second Uncle has been impeached several times of late. Neither your grandfather nor your father-in-law has intervened on his behalf. If I have guessed correctly, before your Third Uncle returns to the capital, he will have been stripped of his position and transferred out of the city."

"Will Fourth Sister be affected?"

Lu Suidong had indeed entered the palace, under the identity of a legitimate daughter of the Second Branch. But she kept an extremely low profile, so low that almost no one was even aware a daughter of the Lu family was in the palace.

"She won't be. Your fourth sister is cleverer than you think."

Xie Yuanjing said, "In time, it may even be your Second Uncle who has to rely on her."

"She won't help him."

"No."

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet sound of agreement and had someone add more charcoal to the brazier.

"Either way, it doesn't matter whether she helps or not. You have me, and you need not concern yourself with any of them."

——

A few days later, on the next rest day, Xie Yuanjing brought Lu Huaixi back to the Lu family home.

The moment they stepped through the gate, Lu Huaixi caught sight of Lady Xie.

Lady Xie was chatting leisurely with her mother, both women wearing smiles, and as they walked they had even linked arms.

Lu Huaixi paused, then turned to look at Xie Yuanjing.

He wore an expression of mild helplessness, as though this were equally news to him.

"Huaixi is here!"

Lady Xie caught sight of them as well. She said little to her own son and called Lu Huaixi straight over to her.

"I was just talking with your mother about holding a gathering at the plum garden in the Marquis's estate, a lively occasion for both our families. You've arrived at just the right time to offer some ideas."

This remark likely carried another meaning beneath it.

A celebration for both families together was probably connected to the fact that she and Xie Yuanjing did not intend to dissolve the marriage, bringing the two households closer. And beyond that, it was likely also a way to bring up the matter of Xie Yuanjing returning to the Marquis's estate.

"I can offer ideas for how to make it lively."

Lu Huaixi smiled pleasantly and did not address anything else. "Be sure to send me an invitation when the time comes, both of you."

With that, she made to walk ahead with the others, but something was suddenly draped over her shoulders from behind.

She turned to look. It was Xie Yuanjing, on his way to the study, who had stopped to put a cloak around her.

"I thought you'd already gone."

"Fasten it properly."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his gaze and tied the cloak securely for her, then reached out to feel the hand warmer she was holding to check that it was still hot. Only then did he remember to say in return, "I'm going now."

And with that, he inclined his head slightly toward the two women before them. "Mother, Mother-in-law, I'll go to Father-in-law first."

Lady Xie kept her eyes on her son until he had walked away, and then she let out a quiet sigh and turned her gaze back to Lu Huaixi.

There was some resignation in her eyes, and something like wistfulness, and alongside that, a trace of surprise.

"If not for Huaixi, I would never have known that this son of mine had a side capable of caring so deeply for someone."

"Mother flatters me. He has always been very devoted to you."

Lady Xie shook her head with a smile. "He is considerate, and whenever he comes across something good he remembers to send it my way. But it has always felt more like fulfilling an obligation than anything like this."

Lady Xie could not quite put it into words, but she could feel the change in her son.

This was better. Compared to the Xie Yuanjing of before, who had seemed to have so few vulnerabilities and so little feeling, this version of him felt more like a family member in the truest sense.

"Is he still not planning to come back?"

Lady Xie could not resist asking at last, then added, "If it's possible, Huaixi, could you speak to him on my behalf?"

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together, held back for a moment, and in the end could not hold it in.

"I'm sorry, Mother. I'm afraid I can't help with that."

She met Lady Xie's slightly surprised gaze and spoke sincerely.

"Whatever he decides, I am on his side. I trust him, as I always have. If he doesn't want to go back, I'll stay with him."

Lady Xie stood momentarily at a loss, and then she thought back to when she had first hoped Lu Huaixi might help persuade him.

Perhaps because she had not fared well these years with Xie Zichang, and because it had been so long since she had seen this kind of trust and companionship, Lady Xie found herself unable to speak.

"I was foolish to say such a thing to you."

Lady Xie gathered herself after a moment, and smiled. "You two live well together. Wherever you are, I am your mother."

As the words fell, something settled and cleared in Lady Xie's expression.

She had not married a man who made her happy. But her son had been very fortunate.

——

When Xie Yuanjing arrived at Master Lu's study, he ran into Zhou Jieyu, who had come with Lu Yuanzhao.

Their eyes met and held for a moment. Both wore composed expressions on the surface, yet each carried a quiet weight.

Just then, someone was speaking with Lu Yuanzhao nearby, leaving the two of them standing apart.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze cooled faintly, though the corner of his mouth held a slight curve.

That day, each had been aware of the other's presence, but neither had given it voice.

Zhou Jieyu's expression was somewhat warmer by comparison, though it still carried a strain not present on ordinary days.

He looked at the man before him, gave a slight smile, and spoke first, addressing him as Master Xie.

Without waiting for Xie Yuanjing to respond, he continued in the manner of idle conversation, asking whether Master Xie had come today with the particular purpose of seeing Master Lu.

"Not with any particular purpose."

Xie Yuanjing's tone was mild, neither cold enough to be dismissive nor warm enough to invite familiarity. As his gaze lifted, something in his eyes softened, as it tended to when he spoke of Lu Huaixi.

"Accompanying my wife home for a visit. She misses home sometimes."

A single sentence was enough to make Zhou Jieyu's expression shift slightly.

But he had composed himself well enough not to lose his bearing. He remained where he stood and exchanged a few more pleasantries.

When Xie Yuanjing turned to leave, Zhou Jieyu called after him.

"What happened that day was overstepping on my part."

Upon hearing him dare to bring up that day, Xie Yuanjing's expression turned cold at once.

"But I hope Master Xie will not misunderstand. At the very end of things that day, she said something to me. I feel it is necessary for Master Xie to know."

Xie Yuanjing stood there, looking at the branches bending under the weight of snow.

In the midst of a sky full of swirling snowflakes, he heard Zhou Jieyu speak, lightly and without haste.

"That day she gave me the dignity of a proper farewell. But in the very last moment, she told me most sincerely that Xie Yuanjing was the best of all. That is something Master Xie did not hear for himself."

Zhou Jieyu would never forget that last exchange in the courtyard that day.

"Compared to Master Xie, how does he measure up?"

"Naturally, Xie Yuanjing is still the best."

The wind in his ears fell still.

Xie Yuanjing lowered his eyes, and smiled all at once, with a tenderness that came without warning.

(Main story ends)

chapters.title: Daily Extra 1: The First New Year
chapters.content:
When they returned home that day, Xie Yuanjing asked nothing, and nothing was out of place.

Only that he did not sleep the entire night.

The next morning, Lu Huaixi stirred drowsily awake and found herself held securely in someone's arms, warm as a fire beside her. She nestled contentedly against his chest.

It was still dark outside.

Xie Yuanjing did not tease her as he usually did. He simply lowered his head and pressed a kiss to her forehead.

"Are you about to get up?"

Lu Huaixi closed her eyes again, but still remembered to ask.

Xie Yuanjing said yes, though the arms around her did not let go.

He had spent the whole night thinking.

He had thought back to the very first time he saw Lu Huaixi's name.

Strange, but he remembered clearly the way he had felt when he heard those three characters: he had liked the name very much.

Then he had gone to meet her.

Her every expression was vivid and unguarded, and without any effort at all, she pierced through the stillness of his feelings, which had been like stagnant water for so long.

Later still, he had said that if someone had already captured his heart, then so be it — and yet he had pulled back the carriage curtain anyway, stepped down, walked up to her, and asked her himself.

Xie Yuanjing thought until his chest began to ache.

He held her without releasing her, until the person in his arms, who should have been asleep again, forced her eyes open and looked up at him, dazed and uncomprehending.

"What's wrong with you? Still not getting up?"

"In a moment."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was low and quiet, like something between a lullaby and a comfort. "I've been thinking. Huaixi, I believe that, from the very first glance, I already liked you."

Lu Huaixi was already barely awake, and hearing him say this made her even more blank.

"......You're making that up."

"I'm not. I've been thinking about it all night."

Having said it aloud, Xie Yuanjing suddenly felt as though something had loosened inside him.

He thought of that day when he and Lu Huaixi had returned to the Lu family home, and she had stood before him and said she had fallen for him first.

In that moment his heart had been so entirely full of her that he had forgotten to say otherwise.

But last night it had suddenly come to him, that from the very beginning, she had already occupied a private place in his thoughts.

"You're not allowed to argue with me over this."

Lu Huaixi's eyes welled up at the corners from sleepiness, but she was still forcing herself to stay awake.

"It was me who fell for you first."

"I won't argue. I only——"

Xie Yuanjing let out a quiet laugh and thought for a moment, then continued. "Alright. Let me put it differently. From the first glance I laid on you, I felt you were unlike anyone else."

He patted her gently on the back, signaling her to go back to sleep.

Then he lowered his head, and his kiss landed at the corner of her eye, then on the tip of her nose, and stopped there.

"After that first glance, I never forgot you. I thought you were wonderful, every part of you."

"Then you were......judging entirely by appearances."

Lu Huaixi closed her eyes, let out a small sound, and curled back against him.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing more. He only smiled, and held her a little tighter.

That day, Xie Yuanjing rose earlier than usual.

He went out to a place nearby that sold breakfast foods and chose a few things Lu Huaixi liked, then saw them delivered back before he left for court.

Things cool quickly, and by the time Lu Huaixi woke, the food no longer had the freshness it had just after purchase.

That evening she mentioned this to Xie Yuanjing. He said a few things in response, but the next day he went out again to choose a few items and had them sent back at a carefully calculated time.

On the way he ran into a colleague buying roasted flatbreads.

The colleague was visibly startled to see him, but did not dare let it show.

Xie Yuanjing, for his part, broke with his usual manner and gave the man a nod, and for the first time accepted a casual exchange of words from someone he was not close with.

The man eventually ventured a remark. "I never would have thought Master Xie would come out himself for these kinds of small things."

"I eat very little of it."

Xie Yuanjing said this without thinking much of it. "My wife likes these things in winter. When I have the time, I come to take a look."

Some things are only right to eat on snowy mornings.

But Lu Huaixi woke late, and did not like to send the maids out in such bitter cold. So she had not brought it up much.

Xie Yuanjing had bought things for her on a few occasions before, but not often, not wanting her to eat too much of it.

"Master Xie is truly devoted to his wife," the man said with feeling.

Xie Yuanjing did not respond to this.

But after a moment, just as everyone around them had assumed he would let the comment pass, he offered a reply.

"It is my wife who is too good. She takes care of so much on my behalf every day, thinking of me at every turn. She works herself very hard."

The Lu Huaixi still deep in peaceful slumber had no idea what it was she had worked so hard at.

She only knew that when she opened her eyes, the things she liked to eat were already laid out on the table, still steaming.

——

From that day on, the rumors that had once called Lu Huaixi jealous and spoiled were quietly replaced, one by one, until nothing remained of them.

No one spoke again of the Lu family's pampered young daughter being young and thoughtless. There was only praise and envy.

Praise that she could manage the household and keep Shun'an Fang thriving all the same, so well that even the Princess had given her personal commendation.

And beyond that, envy that she was so deeply cherished by her husband, especially when that husband was the Xie Yuanjing who had once been said to be rather difficult to approach.

By the time Lu Huaixi heard these things being said, the New Year had already arrived.

That day, Xie Yuanjing led her out of the house, saying he wanted to take her somewhere.

Lu Huaixi was bundled thoroughly in her cloak, with only the better half of her face showing, making her dark eyes appear all the more bright and limpid.

"Where are we going?"

"You'll see when we get there."

Xie Yuanjing held her hand and guided her through the crowd.

Both sides of the street were hung with lanterns, as bright as daylight.

The two of them drew attention rather quickly, and the remarks fell one after another into Lu Huaixi's ears.

Lu Huaixi felt a little ill at ease hearing herself praised. She tugged at Xie Yuanjing's hand and asked if they could take a different route.

Xie Yuanjing walked a little further before stopping, and lifted his hands to cover her ears.

"We're here."

"Where is this?"

Along a lively stretch of street, a small building with red silk hung at its entrance stood quietly in the most favorable spot.

Lu Huaixi looked at the closed door ahead and was about to turn around to ask.

But Xie Yuanjing would not let her move.

"You said last time that Shun'an Fang has become a little small, that you wanted to find another space. Is this place good?"

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long moment.

Then she sniffled, and her voice came out muffled, as though she was on the verge of tears.

"When did you find it?"

"Not too long ago. Do you like it?"

"I love it. I love it so much."

After a moment, Lu Huaixi spoke again in a small voice, with a slightly pitiful catch in her nose. "You brought me to see the place, so why did you keep your hands over my ears the whole time?"

Xie Yuanjing thought this person moved him at every turn, and tormented him in equal measure.

Any random thing she said was enough to make him want to bring her home, to coax her and keep her away from every other pair of eyes, so that she would only speak with him.

But he retained enough presence of mind not to forget everything else.

Before long, not far away, a loud boom rang out.

Just as Lu Huaixi was about to turn her head again, fireworks burst upward into the sky, illuminating the whole stretch of it in brilliant, dazzling color.

"This is the first New Year we are spending together."

Xie Yuanjing spoke close against her ear, with a solemnity that was slow and deliberate. "From now on, I will spend every New Year with you. And you must spend every one with me."

chapters.title: Daily Extra 2: My Beloved Wife the Cook
chapters.content:
One day, Lu Huaixi suddenly became captivated by the idea of cooking.

She started with baozi, wanting to steam a basketful for Xie Yuanjing and fold a few dumplings as well.

When Xie Yuanjing came home from court, her face still had dried flour on it and her fingers had lost most of their usual soft pinkness.

But her eyes were bright as anything, and even the fine beads of sweat on her forehead seemed to catch the light with her.

"How did you know I was here?"

When she saw Xie Yuanjing find his way to the kitchen, Lu Huaixi trotted over to him.

She had been about to hug him, then remembered she had not yet washed her hands, and stepped back two paces.

But she had only just moved when someone hooked her by the waist and brought her back.

Both her hands landed flat on Xie Yuanjing's chest, leaving two very visible prints.

"The clothes are dirty now."

"Then I'll change."

Xie Yuanjing looked at the dough and meat filling that had been reduced to a state of some chaos nearby. He let out a small laugh and lowered his head to kiss her on the lips.

There was flour at the corner of her mouth. Xie Yuanjing discovered it, and a touch of white was transferred to his own lips.

"What is all this? Making a mess to show me?"

"I am not!"

Lu Huaixi was displeased. "I'm steaming baozi for you. Tofu and pork filling, you said you liked it!"

Xie Yuanjing did not quite recall having said any such thing. Perhaps he had mentioned it offhandedly on some day when he was coaxing her. But one thing he was certain of was that right now, he absolutely had to nod.

"Yes. And I also like tofu and pork filling in dumplings. Did you make those for me as well?"

"I did!"

Lu Huaixi lifted her chin a little. "Of course I did."

When the baozi arrived, they did not quite look like baozi.

They did not quite taste like baozi either, being a little tough and a little dry.

The filling inside was more like a solid chunk of meat than anything minced, not very well broken up, and the seasoning was a bit thin.

Xie Yuanjing ate three without any change of expression, alongside a bowl of lamb soup from the kitchen.

Beside them sat things that had been called dumplings, bearing no resemblance to their usual half-moon shape. They looked more like baozi themselves, only very small ones.

Lu Huaixi's eyes had lost their earlier brightness and held a trace of disappointment.

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her, then finished every last dumpling and drank down another bowl of soup before setting down his chopsticks.

"Better than I expected."

Xie Yuanjing did not offer her empty flattery, yet his tone was, genuinely, one of satisfaction.

"Next time you make them, I could have one more."

"Let's not make them anymore."

Lu Huaixi took a baozi herself and bit into it, chewed twice, and found she could not quite bring herself to swallow.

But her upbringing at the table was impeccable and would not allow her to react in any obvious way. She paused for a moment, and was preparing simply to force it down.

"Spit it out."

Xie Yuanjing held his hand out toward her.

Lu Huaixi was startled.

She could not possibly spit into his hand.

After a moment of bewildered hesitation, Lu Huaixi forced the mouthful of baozi down.

Xie Yuanjing poured her a bowl of soup and had someone cook her some noodles, then took the baozi she had bitten into from her hands, preparing to finish it himself.

Lu Huaixi did not want him to eat any more, but Xie Yuanjing had the thing down in a few bites.

"What are you doing?"

Lu Huaixi frowned, her heart aching a little. "You don't have to do that. What if it upsets your stomach?"

"It won't upset anything. I genuinely think it's not bad."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her.

The way she frowned was truly endearing. He wanted to kiss her, but remembered they were still at the table.

"Stop coaxing me. I have never eaten baozi this tough in my life."

"I wanted to make you happy about it. I didn't lie to you."

With that, Xie Yuanjing simply rose to rinse his mouth and wash his hands, and when he sat back down he pulled her into his arms.

A wife in low spirits needed coaxing.

A wife who doubted him needed even more coaxing.

"Just keep practicing and it will come right. The first time I made baozi I couldn't even get the folds to close. My beloved wife trying her hand at cooking, and with no small amount of talent."

"Really?"

Lu Huaixi was a little doubtful and looked up at him. "You've made baozi before?"

"I have. When I was young."

Xie Yuanjing held her hands and brushed at the dried flour on them.

"Try something different next time. Though once the weather gets any warmer, stay out of the kitchen."

"But what if I just keep getting better and better?"

"What about it?"

"If I get good enough, I'll become a proper cook."

Xie Yuanjing's hands paused. After a moment, the image of Lu Huaixi spending her days in the kitchen, flushed with the heat, rose in his mind.

"Then you may only ever cook for me alone."

Xie Yuanjing set aside certain thoughts and said plainly, "I'll give you half a month to practice. After that, no more running off to the kitchen. And be careful near the fire, and near the knives."

"Honestly, you're so fussy."

"If you won't listen, you don't get to be this cook anymore."

A beat of silence, and then Xie Yuanjing added, "I won't taste anything you make either."

That last part struck home with Lu Huaixi.

She made a quiet sound of displeasure but did not dare push back.

She was making things for Xie Yuanjing to try. If he wouldn't eat them, what was the point of making them?

While she was still thinking this over, Xie Yuanjing spoke again. "I never actually said I liked tofu and pork filling in baozi. Think carefully. Who did say it?"

Lu Huaixi blinked, and in an instant felt a sense of danger close in.

"What is this, settling scores after the fact?"

She shifted back, trying to climb down from Xie Yuanjing's lap, but the moment she moved, his arm came up and trapped her.

"Who was it. Think carefully, right now."

——

From that day on, Lu Huaixi became more and more interested in cooking.

With Xie Yuanjing's indulgence, which lacked all sense of proportion, she thoroughly transformed from lady of the house into cook.

Xie Yuanjing found himself tasting dishes of a distinctly unique character on a regular basis.

Not exactly bad, but certainly not good.

One day Shen Zhoushu came to visit and, finding himself unwilling to leave when dinnertime arrived, insisted loudly on staying to eat.

The dishes that came out were not many, and appeared thoroughly unremarkable.

Shen Zhoushu was not a person who cared much whether food was a delicacy or not. In his mind, with Lu Huaixi in this household, the kitchen could not possibly be lacking.

He picked up a shrimp and tasted it. Middling.

But shrimp is naturally sweet on its own, which meant middling pointed to a cook with no real skill.

He then tried a piece of the scallion and vinegar chicken, bit into it, and his brow furrowed.

After that he tried a bit of lamb, could not quite chew through it, and swallowed it mostly whole.

"Your kitchen isn't up to much."

Shen Zhoushu set down his chopsticks and reached for the soup that had been prepared nearby, taking a sip.

The soup was decent, actually. Plain-looking as it appeared, it was the best thing on the table by some measure.

"Find someone new. A cook like this wouldn't be tolerated anywhere. I don't know where you found such good nature in yourself, keeping them on until now."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing at first.

He was eating a piece of lamb, unhurried, with none of the difficulty Shen Zhoushu had just experienced.

Only once he finished and swallowed did he set down his chopsticks and speak, slowly.

"Was it bad? I didn't think so."

"Are you alright? That wasn't bad? Where on earth did this cook even come——"

"The cook is my wife."

"......Actually the flavor was quite alright."

Shen Zhoushu fell silent. He lowered his head and drank his soup without further comment.

chapters.title: Daily Extra 3: We Are Husband and Wife Now
chapters.content:
On the second birthday Lu Huaixi celebrated after marrying Xie Yuanjing, Xie Yuanjing drank more than a little.

They had returned to the Marquis's estate some time prior.

This standoff of more than a year had at last reached its conclusion, after the Marquis of Cheng'en severed ties with that mother and son outside, and his health began to fail more and more.

Xie Yuanjing had given his assent at the moment when the estate was at its most precarious.

Old Master Xie had already braced himself for despair, fully expecting that a formal separation between father and son had become unavoidable.

But then, on the occasion when the Marquis of Cheng'en dragged his ailing body to the door one final time and bowed his head, Xie Yuanjing agreed.

Lu Huaixi, as always, did not object.

She had promised she would stay with Xie Yuanjing, and wherever that might be, to her it was all the same.

Only she could not help feeling a certain reluctance about that house.

So much so that even well after they had returned to the Marquis's estate, she would sometimes find herself, in an unguarded moment, thinking of the flowers and plants she had tended there.

Xie Yuanjing felt some guilt, and some remorse.

He promised Lu Huaixi that every year they would go back to stay there for a few months, and promised her as well that back at the Marquis's estate, she would not need to defer to anyone.

The second promise Xie Yuanjing made good on very quickly.

Now that he had returned, the Second and Third Branches greeted him with nothing but smiles and conciliation, especially the Third, which was almost nakedly eager to please.

As for Lu Huaixi, they would sooner risk displeasing Xie Yuanjing than allow the least dissatisfaction to fall on this young lady who had come to them from the Lu family.

So it was that on this birthday of hers, the whole household was livelier than it had been even at New Year's.

Lu Huaixi bathed in a pleasant haze of exhaustion, stifling a yawn as she returned to the room.

Her dark hair was not yet fully dry. But she had smiled the entire day and now felt an ache in her cheeks, and wished for nothing more than to burrow straight into the quilts.

When Xie Yuanjing came into the room, the last of the effort in Lu Huaixi's expression fell away.

She watched him walk to her side, and reached out to wrap her arms around his waist as she sat before the bronze mirror, pressing her face against him.

"I'm so tired. I want to sleep."

Xie Yuanjing stroked her hair, one slow pass after another, then eased back slightly.

When Lu Huaixi looked up in puzzlement, Xie Yuanjing lowered himself into a crouch, so that it was now he who tilted his face up toward her.

"Wait a little longer to sleep. Alright?"

His gentle voice carried something almost like a spell, and the words of refusal on Lu Huaixi's tongue were swallowed back before they could leave.

She had never looked at Xie Yuanjing quite like this before.

Looking down at him now, she found, unexpectedly, that in the candlelight, Xie Yuanjing appeared almost tender in his vulnerability.

"But what for?"

Lu Huaixi asked this without thinking.

The answer was a kiss from him, covering her lips. The two mouths met softly.

After a moment, Xie Yuanjing spoke with his lips still against hers.

"I once said that I wished I could have known you sooner, sooner even than your childhood, watching you grow up, waiting for you to come of age, and then waiting until you had played to your heart's content at home before taking you home as my wife."

Xie Yuanjing's voice was low and unhurried, and in the warmth of the gentle lamplight, the words fell like warmth into Lu Huaixi's heart.

She reached on instinct to catch his lips between her teeth, learning from his closeness, wanting to keep kissing him.

But the man who was usually the most urgent of all held himself back this time.

He drew away slightly and reached out to hold her, looking into her eyes where a film of mist had begun to gather.

"That day you asked me how long was long enough to play to your heart's content, and I said two years. Two years have come now, Huaixi."

Only then did he kiss her again.

More urgent than before.

He kissed her until neither of them could say anything at all, and then he paused, their noses close together.

"Will you?"

The question had no preamble, no context. Yet it made Lu Huaixi's heart give a single, sharp tremble.

A tingling warmth moved through her, starting from her chest and spreading to every corner of her body, out to her hands and feet.

As though something were bursting into small sparks along her skin, both itching and warm.

She understood what Xie Yuanjing meant.

He had been waiting for her all this time.

Lu Huaixi said nothing, only kept breathing, slowly steadying herself.

Xie Yuanjing did not press. He simply stayed, waiting, kissing her softly every now and then, tender and lingering.

In the end it was Xie Yuanjing who broke the quiet first, afraid she was too exhausted.

"It's alright if you don't want to. I can keep waiting. Don't be afraid."

He patted her gently on the back, then rose and lifted her into his arms. "Let's just sleep tonight."

"How long are you willing to wait for me?"

Lu Huaixi gripped the front of his robe and looked up, and the shyness in her eyes set another flame alight in Xie Yuanjing's heart.

Xie Yuanjing's throat moved. He gave a helpless laugh.

"As long as it takes. You are my wife. I may not always be able to help myself, but I will wait until you are willing."

With that, he set her on the bed and turned to extinguish the lamp. "I waited two years. I can wait another two. I don't want you to be afraid."

"How can you be so good to me?"

Lu Huaixi lowered her eyes, her gaze falling on the red bedding between them.

Before long the room dimmed. Xie Yuanjing came close, carrying his own clean, familiar scent.

As always, he kissed her forehead first, then her nose, and finally her lips.

"Alright. Lie down and sleep."

He drew her into his arms and closed his eyes.

The heat had not left him, in truth. His longing had never stopped calling out to him, and it would take more reason than he usually needed to press it down.

Especially now, with her scent so close at his nose, with her breathing in his ear. Xie Yuanjing wanted her near him more than he ever had before.

Even in the way they had grown close before, through other means.

But not this time.

He did not want to frighten her, not now that he had spoken his longing aloud.

Still, he believed he could bear it.

They had so long ahead of them. He could spend a lifetime with Lu Huaixi, and waiting a few more years made no difference.

He was just about to pull the quilt more snugly around her when the person who had been lying quietly beside him stirred.

Then the hand resting at his waist crept slowly upward and tugged, gently, at the front of his robe.

Xie Yuanjing instinctively caught her wandering hand and opened his eyes.

The desire that had never quite left the depths of his gaze was still there, and he could feel it himself.

"What is it?"

He did his best to keep his voice calm, then leaned in and kissed her eyes softly.

But in the moment he drew back, Lu Huaixi surged forward and kissed him herself.

Things came apart almost at once.

Whatever remained of Xie Yuanjing's reason snapped clean in that shy yet reckless kiss.

He wound around her, pulled her close, and kissed her back, fierce and urgent.

Lu Huaixi's broken, breathless sounds only added more fuel to the heat already burning.

It scorched through Xie Yuanjing until nothing of his reason remained, and only instinct drove him, toward possession, toward closeness, toward the one he cherished most.

The inner robes fell somewhere, at some point unknowable. When the bed curtains dropped, the last candle in the corner wavered and let out a faint crackling sound.

A night of pear blossoms and rain, unceasing.

Lu Huaixi only remembered that when she drifted into sleep, the one who had kept her awake all night had risen.

He coaxed her to sleep, then seemed to apply some salve to her somewhere, and then said something in a low voice to someone outside. After that he changed his clothes and left for court.

When Lu Huaixi opened her eyes again, he was already there before her.

"You're awake? Does anything hurt?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing, only blinked, looking at this man she was so very, very fond of.

They were truly husband and wife now.

Lu Huaixi thought this to herself, quietly.

Xie Yuanjing reached out and pinched her nose gently, then lowered his head and pressed kisses across her face.

"Why do you look so dazed?"

He laughed softly and bent to hold her close, as though holding everything that mattered to him.

"From now on, you stay by my side. Don't let anyone take you away."

——

That winter, Lu Huaixi caught sight of a thin, disheveled figure on the street.

Without looking closely, there was no way of knowing this was the He Bingxin who had once been praised to the skies. He could easily have been mistaken for some wandering vagrant.

Lu Huaixi looked for only a moment before looking away. But that person seemed to freeze on the spot, staring at her, an intense and desperate wanting blazing in his eyes.

Xie Yuanjing's expression darkened. He cast a glance at Gong Zhuo, then guided Lu Huaixi back to the carriage.

That was the last time Lu Huaixi ever saw He Bingxin.

She did not even retain a clear memory of him afterward. What she did remember from that day was that in the carriage, Xie Yuanjing had kissed her again and again until her head held nothing but the pleasantly unreasonable warmth of him.

A few days later, Xie Yuanjing took her to see the lanterns.

When they returned home that evening, a potted flower she had started tending that winter was set out in the room.

A very beautiful flower, and the only one she had tended personally that had survived.

That night, lying beside Xie Yuanjing, Lu Huaixi murmured drowsily, "Great-grandfather asked me to come and see the snow. I'll be going in a few days. I want to bring the flower."

"Alright."

Xie Yuanjing answered softly. "I'll come with you."

He watched Lu Huaixi's eyes close, and gently brushed aside the stray hair at her cheek, and said with full sincerity, "Wherever you go, I will go with you."

"Mm......"

The last thread of her wakefulness carried her forward, and she pressed a kiss to Xie Yuanjing's face.

"I'll go with you too."

Wherever he went. Whatever he had to do.

They were husband and wife. They would always be together.

(The End.)
